# Periyalvar Tirumoli

## 1.1.1. Vanna madangal sul

*vaṇṇa mādangaḷ sūḻ tirukkōttiyūrkaṇṇan kēsavan nambi piṟandinileṇṇey suṇṇam edir edir tūvidakkaṇṇan muṟṟam kalandu aḷarāyiṟṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇṇa mādangaḷ – beautiful mansions; sūḻ – surrounded by; tirukkōttiyūr – in the divine abode of tirukkōśtiyūr; nambi – complete with all auspicious qualities; kēsavan – one with commendable locks; in il – in the sweet house (of nandagōpar); piṟandu – mercifully incarnated; eṇṇey – oil; suṇṇam – turmeric powder; edir edir tūvida – sprayed on one another; kaṇ nal muṟṟam – courtyard which was expansive and invigorating to look at; kalandu – due to that mixture \[of oil and turmeric powder\]; aḷaru āyiṟṟu – became muddied

**Перевод:**

**tirukkōttiyūr is surrounded by mansions which are embellished with gemstones. In that divine abode, kriṣṇa mercifully incarnated in the sweet house of nandagōpar. People sprayed a mixture of oil and turmeric powder on each other, in the courtyard, which was beautiful and invigorating to look at. As a result, the courtyard became muddied.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) After emperumān had mercifully incarnated in tiruvāyppādi (śrī gōkulam), the herd-people of tiruvāyppādi celebrated in a grand manner. āḻvār meditates on that and becomes blissful.*

**vaṇṇa mādangaḷ sūḻ tirukkōttiyūr** – just as it has been said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4-4-3 “*vaṇṇa nanmaṇiyum maragadamum aḻutti niḻal eḻum tiṇṇai sūḻ tirukkōttiyūr*” (tirukkōttiyūr, which is surrounded by pials \[raised platforms in the front-yard of houses, called in tamiḻ as *tiṇṇai*\] which shine brightly since gemstones such as carbuncles and emeralds have been embellished in them firmly), in tirukkōttiyūr which is surrounded by mansions which have been embellished with different types of gemstones

**kaṇṇan kēsavan nambi** – kriṣṇa, who had plentiful and beautiful locks and who was complete with all the auspicious qualities. Also, kriṣṇa who had destroyed the monster kēśi.

**piṟandinil** ***–*** this could be considered as *piṟandin-il* which would mean at the time of being born or as *in-il-piṟandu* – born in a beautiful house. Unlike maturā where one could not speak highly of the prison where kriṣṇa was born, in tirukkōttiyūr, he was born in the beautiful house of śrī nandagōpar. Alternatively \[to expand the meaning of *kēśavan* which would mean being the controller of *ka* (brahma) and *īśa* (rudra)\], this could be construed as – being the cause for the birth of brahmā, rudra et al, having auspicious qualities in full, emperumān incarnated as kriṣṇa.

**eṇṇey suṇṇam edir edir tūvida** – being in total bliss \[the people in tiruvāyppādi\], mixed oil and turmeric powder and sprayed on one another as an outlet for that happiness.

**kaṇṇan muṟṟam** – since nandagōpar considered that henceforth kaṇṇan will be the controller of his house, the courtyard would be called as kaṇṇan’s courtyard. Alternatively,

**kaṇ nal muṟṟam** – courtyard which was expansive and invigorating

**kalandu aḷaṟāyiṟṟē** – the oil and turmeric powder mixed together and became muddy.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.1.2. Oduvar viluvar

*ōduvār viḻuvār ugandālippārnāduvār nambirān enguṟṟān enbārpāduvārgaḷum palpaṟai kotta ninṟuāduvārgaḷum āyiṟṟu āyppādiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āyppādi – śrī gōkulam; ōduvār – (herd-people) will run, in a bewildered way; viḻuvār – they will slip in the muddied place; ugandu ālippār – they will let out a loud cry, out of bliss; nāduvār – they will search for the infant \[who has been born in nandagōpar’s mansion\]; nam pirān – kriṣṇa, who is our benefactor; enguṟṟān enbār – they will wonder as to where he is; pāduvārgaḷum – those who sing, out of happiness; pal paṟai – various musical instruments; kotta – even as they are played; ninṟu – in syncronisation with the music; āduvārgaḷum – those who dance; āyiṟṟu – entire \[śrī gōkulam\] became like this

**Перевод:**

**On hearing about the birth of kriṣṇa in nandagōpar’s divine house, the herd-people will run in bewilderment. They will slip in the muddy place \[muddied as a result of spraying oil and turmeric, as seen in the first pāsuram\] and will let out a cry in sheer happiness. They will search out as to where the infant has been born and go looking for him. Even as different musical instruments are played out, they will sing and dance in syncronisation with that music. Entire śrī gōkulam was like this.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) – Not only that, since the covherd people of tiruvāyppādi show affection towards kriṣṇa in line with the thinking in his divine heart, āḻvār praises them.*

**ōduvār** – upon hearing about the news of kriṣṇa having been born, the people of śrī gōkulam will run in happy bewilderment

**viḻuvār** – even as they run, they will slip in the muddied place and fall down.

**ugandu ālippār** – they will be very blissful and as an outlet for that happiness, will let out a loud cry.

**nāduvār** – they will search out “Where is the infant? Where is the infant?”

**nam pirān enguṟṟān** – even as they see the little kaṇṇan, realising that he is the son of their leader, nandagōpar, bringing out happiness in their voice, they will ask “Where is our *svāmy* (leader, lord)?”

**pāduvārgaḷum** – those who sing as an outlet for that happiness

**palpaṟai kotta ninṟu āduvārgaḷum** – even as many people start playing on various instruments, people will dance, syncronising their movements with that music. Alternatively, some people will play instruments, as they like, without any proper musical tunes and some people will dance, as they like, without any syncronisation with that music. All the activities listed above are to be considered as taking place simultaneously. Thus, some people will run, some people will slip and fall down, some people will search out  etc

**āyiṟṟu āyppādiyē** – Among the five lakh homes in tiruvāyppādi, there was none who was not affected in any way due to the birth of kriṣṇa. All of them were engaged in one or more of the above-mentioned activities.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.1.4. Uriyai murrattu

*uṟiyai muṟṟattu urutti ninṟāduvārnaṟu ney pāl tayir nanṟāgat tūvuvārseṟi men kūndal aviḻat tiḷaittu engumaṟivaḻindanar āyppādi āyarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āyppādi āyar – the herd-people in tiruvāyppādi \[śrī gōkulam\]; uṟiyai – vessels containing milk and curd, hung from the ceiling, through a network of ropes; muṟṟattu urutti ninṟu – bring them down and roll them over, on the courtyard; āduvār – they will dance; naṟu ney pāl tayir – fragrant ghee, milk and curd; nanṟāga – without leaving behind anything; tūvuvār – will offer to others as a gift \[to celebrate kriṣṇa’s birth\]; seṟimen – being close together and soft; kūndal – locks; aviḻa – to be diśevelled; tiḷaittu – break in to a dance; engum – throughout śrī gōkulam; aṟivaḻindanar – lost their senses, not knowing as to what they should do and what they śouldn’t

**Перевод:**

**As a result of their ecstasy on knowing about the birth of kriṣṇa, the herd-people in śrī gōkulam would lose their senses, not knowing what they should and what they śouldn’t do. They would bring down vessels containing milk, curd etc which have been suspended from ceiling through a network of ropes, on to the courtyard and roll them on the floor. They would dance in joy. They would offer the fragrant ghee, milk, curd etc as gifts to others, without leaving behind anything. In their frenzied dancing, they would not even notice that their dense, soft locks had got untied.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**uṟiyai muṟṟattu urutti ninṟu āduvār** – as an outlet for their happiness, they would bring down the fragrant ghee, milk, curd etc, not considering their immense value, which have been suspended from the ceiling in pots, through a network of ropes. They would roll the pots on their courtyards, spilling their contents and dance in unbounded joy.

**naṟu ney pāl tayir nanṟāgat tūvuvār** – praying that their svāmy \[lord\] kriṣṇa should get all benefits, they will offer the fragrant materials such as ghee, milk, curd etc as gifts to others.

**seṟi men kūndal aviḻat tiḷaittu** – they would dance in such a frenzied manner that their dense, soft locks would get diśevelled completely

**engum aṟivu aḻindanar āyppādi āyarē** – thus, the herd-folk in śrī gōkulam, with happiness going over their heads, would lose their sense of what is the correct action to be done and what is not to be done. Some will dance on their courtyards, after bringing down vessels containing milk, curd etc. Some others will gift fragrant ghee etc to others, as a result of their happiness. Some others will not even know that their locks, which are dense and soft, have got diśevelled and continue to dance. All these are due to their loss of senses on what is to be done and what is not to be done.

They were herd-folk not because of their adoption or profession, but because of their birth \[Hence they were in a celebratory frame of mind on knowing about kriṣṇa’s birth\].

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.1.5. Konda taluri

*koṇḍa tāḷuṟi kōlak kodumaḻuttaṇḍinar paṟiyōlaic cayanattarviṇḍa mullai arubu anna pallinaraṇḍar miṇḍip pugundu neyyādinār*

**Пословный перевод:**

koṇḍa tāḷ – densely woven, through the network of ropes; uṟi – vessels containing curd etc, suspended from ceiling through the network of ropes; kōlam – beautiful; kodu – sharp; maḻu taṇḍinar – those who were holding axe, a weapon and sticks \[to protect the infant kriṣṇa\]; paṟiyōlai – woven into a mat with fragrant screw-pine leaves; sayanattar – as their mattress; viṇḍa – blossomed; mullai arumbu anna – similar to buds of jasmine flower; pallinar – those who were having teeth; aṇḍar – celestial entities; would also refer to herd-people; miṇḍip pugundu – entering, in a crowded manner \[many people entering together\]; neyyādinār – were dancing with pots containing ghee

**Перевод:**

**Herd-people \[on hearing about the birth of infant kriṣṇa in śrī nandagōpar’s mansion\], who hold weapons such as axe and sticks, who sleep on mats woven with screw-pine leaves and who have teeth which are similar to a just-then blossomed jasmine bud, entered his house in a crowded manner, held the lengthy pots which contained ghee, curd etc and danced with those pots.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**koṇḍa tāḷuṟi … –** herd-people, having pots with closely strung ropes, axes which were sharp, sticks which are typical of their clan \[as an instrument for grazing cows as well as a weapon\] and who sleep on mats woven with the leaves of screw-pine plant. Since they are happy, they smile, manifesting their teeth which are like jasmine buds which had just then blossomed. They entered śrī nandagōpar’s mansion, in a crowded manner and danced with their pots, till late in the night, debating amongst themselves in a happy manner, about the beautiful features of infant kriṣṇa. If the text were *viṇḍin mullai*, the term *viṇḍu* would refer to hill; the herd-people had teeth which were bright like a cluster of jasmine flowers which had blossomed on a hill. Their teeth were also similar to a line of bottle-gourd seeds, which had been kept side by side. The term *aṇḍar* would refer both to celestial entities and to herd-folk. Here it refers to the herd-folk.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.1.6. Kaiyum kalum

*kaiyum kālum nimirttuk kadāra nīrpaiya āttip pusum siṟu manjaḷālaiya nā vaḻittāḷukku angāndidavaiyam ēḻum kaṇḍāḷ piḷḷai vāyuḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaiyum kālum – the divine hands and the divine feet; nimirttu – to stretch them out; kadāra nīr – warming up water in a vessel; pasum siṟu manjaḷāl – with fresh piece of turmeric; paiya – aptly, for the divine form of kriṣṇa; ātti – giving him a divine bath; aiya – tender; nā vaḻittāḷukku – to yaśōdāp pirātti, who gently cleansed kriṣṇa’s tongue with the fresh piece of turmeric; angāndida – kriṣṇa, who opened his divine mouth \[to enable her to clean his tongue\]; piḷḷai vāyuḷ – inside the divine mouth of her son, kriṣṇa; vaiyam ēḻum – all the seven worlds; kaṇḍāḷ – she saw

**Перевод:**

**In order to give her infant kriṣṇa a divine bath, yaśōdāp pirātti stretched out his divine hands and divine feet. She warmed up water in a vessel. She took a piece of fresh turmeric and dipped it in that vessel. She took another piece of turmeric in order to cleanse his divine tongue. When she opened his divine mouth for that, little kriṣṇa showed her all the seven worlds inside his divine mouth and made her see them.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kaiyum kālum nimirttu** – stretching his divine hands and divine feet, apt for his soft divine form \[being an infant\]

**kadāra nīr paiya ātti** – she added healthy herbs and fragrant materials which are apt for his divine form, to the warm water taken in a vessel; she poured water on his divine form gently such that his divine form was not roughed up.

**pasum siṟu manjaḷāl** – this turmeric has to be added to both the previous term and the succeeding term. It was with a piece of turmeric which had small nodes that she gave kriṣṇa the divine bath.

**aiya nā …**– she cleaned his soft, divine tongue with another piece of turmeric. When kriṣṇa opened his divine mouth to enable her to clean his divine tongue, she saw all the worlds inside his divine mouth. Just as kriṣṇa \[during the mahābhārata war, in later years\] granted divine eyes to arjuna in order to enable him to see his virātrūpam (his form encompassing the entire universe), he gave yaśōdāp pirātti too divine eyes, to enable her to see all the worlds inside his small mouth. She saw inside his divine stomach, the *aghatitagatanā sāmartyam* (ability to carry out impossible tasks) of *vatapatra śāyi* (emperumān who was lying as an infant atop a tender banyan leaf) when he hid all the worlds inside his small divine stomach.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.1.7. Vayul vaiyagam

*vāyuḷ vaiyagam kaṇḍa mada nallārāyar puttiran allan arum deyvampāya sīrudaip paṇbudaip pālaganmāyan enṟu magiḻndanar mādarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāyuḷ – inside the divine mouth of infant kriṣṇa; vaiyagam – worlds; kaṇḍa – those who saw; mada nallār – herd-women who have the qualities of simplicity and obedience; mādar – herd-women; āyar puttiran allan – “he is not a herd-boy; arum deyvam – the most-difficult-to-attain deity; pāya sīr udai – having many auspicious qualities; paṇbu udai – having the quality of simplicity; pālagan – (this) little infant; māyan enṟu – one with amazing activities”, saying so; magiḻndnar – became delighted

**Перевод:**

**The women folk in the herd clan, who had the qualities of simplicity and obedience and who saw the worlds exhibited by infant kriṣṇa \[as in the previous pāsuram\] said, among themselves, of kriṣṇa “He is not a herd-boy; he is a very-difficult-to-attain deity, who has many auspicious qualities and who has simplicity too. He is one with amazing activities” and were delighted.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vāyuḷ vaiyagam kaṇḍa mada nallār** – the women folk in the clan of herd-people, who had the qualities of obedience and simplicity, who saw several worlds displayed by infant kriṣṇa in his divine mouth. In the previous pāsuram, it was mentioned that only one person \[yaśōdā\] had seen several worlds inside infant kriṣṇa’s divine mouth. However, in this pāsuram, since it is clearly mentioned in plural number \[*mada nallār*\], it is evident that several women among the herd-folk, apart from yaśōdā, had seen those worlds inside his divine mouth. In other words, after seeing several worlds inside his divine mouth, yaśōdā would have called the women in her proximity to share with them the amazing sight that she had seen. In order to make others too to know of his greatness, he would have granted them too, the divine vision to see the worlds inside his divine mouth.

**āyar puttiran allan arum deyvam** – he is not the son of śrī nandagōpar, the head of herd-clan. He is the most-difficult-to-attain sarvēśvaran \[lord of all\].

**pāya sīrudai paṇbudaip pālagan** – he is a little boy with many auspicious qualities, and is simplicity personified. By manifesting the worlds inside his divine mouth, he revealed his auspicious qualities and by showing it to the simple herd-folk women, he displayed his quality of simplicity too.

**māyan** – one with amazing activities

**enṟu magiḻndanar** – the herd-women shared their happiness with each other, in this manner. They were happy that since he has amazing activities \[*māyan*\], he will be the cause for us to get liberated from this world.

The pāsuram should be rearranged as *vāyuḷ vaiyagam kaṇḍa mada nallārāna-mādar-pāya sīruaip paṇbudaip pālagan-āyar puttiran allan arum deyvam-māyan enṟu magiḻndanar* to get the sequential meaning.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.1.8. Pattu nalum

*pattu nāḷum kadanda iraṇḍā nāḷettisaiyum sayamaram kōdittumatta māmalai tāngiya maindanaiuttānam seydu ugandanar āyarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pattu nālum kadanda – after ten days had passed; iraṇḍām nāḷ – and another two days \[viz. twelve days from birth\]; ettisaiyum – in all directions; saya maram – staffs to signify victory; kōdittu – carrying out decorations by planting; matta mā malai – the hill gōvardana, which had many exulting elephants; tāngiya – one who held; maindanai – kaṇṇan, one who had the strength; āyar – herd folk; uttānam seydu – carrying him in their arms; ugandanar – were blissful

**Перевод:**

**On the twelfth day from his \[kriṣṇa’s\] birth, the herd-folk planted decorative flag-staffs in all directions, announcing to all, their victory \[of having the great kriṣṇa amidst them\]. They carried in their arms the infant kriṣṇa, who, in later years, will hold aloft the gōvardana mountain which had many elephants which were in exultation. They displayed their bliss in this manner.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**pattu nāḷum kadanda iraṇḍā nāḷ** – on the day of *puṇyāhavacanam* \[the day when the new-born child is given a name\], which falls on the twelfth day after birth. Since āḻvār is totally engaged with carrying out *mangaḷāśāsanam* \[praising and protecting\], he does not wish to reveal the details of kriṣṇa’s birth and says – the twelfth day from birth \[hiding from entities such as kamsan et al\].

**ettisaiyum saya maram kōdittu** – planting decorative flag-staffs in all four directions, to signify their victory \[of having attained kriṣṇa\]

**matta māmalai tāngiya maindanai** – the powerful child who held aloft the huge mountain that had many elephants which were in exultation. Since āḻvār incarnated in the period much after the birth of kriṣṇa, he has the liberty to identify the activities of kriṣṇa which he carried out much later, with the child who had been born only twelve days earlier.

**uttānam seydu ugandanar āyarē** – due to overflowing affection for kriṣṇa, the herd-folk carried the infant kriṣṇa, individually, in their hands, and became happy.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.1.9. Kidakkil tottil

*kidakkil tottil kiḻiya udaittidumeduttuk koḷḷil marungai iṟuttidumodukkip pulgul udarattē pāyndidummidukku ilāmaiyāl nān melindēn nangāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

nangāy – Oh women, who are complete with all the auspicious qualities!; kidakkil – if laid down (on the cradle); tottil – cradle; kiḻiya – to break up; udaittidum – he starts kicking; eduttuk koḷḷil – if he were kept on the waist \[since he doesn’t like to be put inside the cradle\]; marungai – waist; iṟuttidum – he breaks; odukki – such that he cannot do any anything; pulgil – if he were kept close to the chest; udarattu – in the stomach; pāyndidum – he kicks; midukku – strength to put up with these activities; ilāmaiyāl – since \[this child\] does not have; nān – I (his mother); melindēn – have become very thin

**Перевод:**

**yaśōdā tells the ladies among the herd-folk “Oh ladies who have all the auspicious qualities! If I have to put down the infant kriṣṇa in the cradle, he kicks it such that it would break. If I hold him on my waist, since he does not like being put inside the cradle, he breaks my waist with his kicks. If I hold him tight to my chest such that he could not engage in any activity, he kicks the stomach region. Since the little kriṣṇa does not have the strength to put up with his activities \[of kicking hard objects\], I have become thin”**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In the previous pāsuram, āḻvār mentioned about kriṣṇa’s activity which he carried out years later \[of holding the mountain with his hand\]. In this pāsuram, he recalls the activities which are not appropriate for a child of that age, by recounting them in the pathos of yaśōdā, to women who are in her proximity.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kidakkil** – if the infant kriṣṇa were laid down in the cradle, he will keep kicking it until the cradle would break into pieces.

**eēduttuk koḷḷil marungai iṟuttidum** – thinking “Kicking like this would not be apt for the softness of his divine legs”, if I pick him up and keep him on my waist, he will keep kicking my waist until the waist itself would break.

**odukkip pulgil udarattē pāyndidum** – thinking “Even this is not apt for his soft, divine form”, if I keep him close to my chest such that he cannot engage in any activity, he would still slip a bit and start kicking my stomach.

**midukku ilāmaiyāḷ nān melindēn nangāy** – I became very thin after thinking “This infant does not have the strength in him to put up with his activity of kicking repeatedly with those soft, divine feet”. The term *nangāy* refers to a group of women who were near yaśōdā, even though it appears to address a single person. She appears to be hinting that they have all the auspicious qualities in them since they have sired children who act according to their age and have nurtured them that way, and not like kriṣṇa, who is acting beyond his age.

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.1.10. Sennelar vayal

*sennelār vayal sūḻ tirukkōttiyūrmannu nāraṇan nambi piṟandamaiminnu nūl vittu cittan viritta ippannu pādal vallārrku illai pāvamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sem nel – reddish paddy; Ar – being dense; vayal – by fields; sūḻ – surrounded; tirukkōttiyūr – in the divine abode, tirukkōttiyūr; mannu – one, who resides forever; nāraṇan – one who is referred to as nārāyaṇan; nambi – kaṇṇan, one who is complete will all the auspicious qualities; piṟandamai – the manner in which he incarnated; minnu nūl – having the sacred thread which shines brightly; vittu cittan – bhattar pirān, also known as viṣṇu cittar \[periyāḻvār\]; viritta – explained in a detailed manner, the activities performed at the time of \[emperumān’s\] incarnation; ip pannu pādal – these pāsurams, which are meditated upon by wise people; vallārkku – those who are capable of learning; pāvam illai – sins will not come near

**Перевод:**

**periyāḻvār, who wears a splendorous sacred thread, has described in a detailed manner, in his pāsurams, the activities performed at the time of incarnation of emperumān, as kriṣṇa, in the divine abode of tirukkōttiyūr, which is surrounded by fields which have dense reddish paddy cultivated in them. Sins will not come anywhere near those who are capable of learning these pāsurams.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In the final pāsuram, āḻvār mentions about the benefits that one would get by reciting these pāsurams and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**sennel …..** – in tirukkōttiyūr which is surrounded by fields in which densely grown paddy crop is cultivated, śrīman nārāyaṇan, who has a unique form lying atop ādiśēśan and who is complete with all auspicious qualities, is residing permanently. He incarnated in this divine abode. periyāḻvār had started the decad with the words “*tirukōttiyūr kaṇṇan kēsavan nambi*” and ended the decad with the words “*mannu nāraṇan nambi*”. Through these, he has mercifully spoken about the qualities of emperumān which are different from his general qualities \[such as being present everywhere, being permanent etc\] and which are different from his distinguished qualities \[such as not changing ever, having knowledge which is unbounded and inestimable, not being contained within an entity, space or time\]. In other words, he has described about the qualities of his divine form, which are referred to in the *vākhya dvayam* \[the esoteric hymn of dvaya mahāmantram in which we hold on to the divine feet (form) of emperumān through the first line and seek to carry out servitude to that divine form, through the second line\].

**minnu nūl vittu cittan viritta** – Since he is bhattar pirān (benefactor, who carries out the activities of a brāhmaṇa), he has the sacred thread which is shining brightly on his chest. He is also known as viṣṇu cittan since he keeps that emperumān, who has pervaded everywhere, in his divine mind. Such periyāḻvār has explained in a detailed manner, the divine incarnation of emperumān in that divine abode, tirukkōttiyūr.

**ip pannu pādal vallārkku illai pāvamē** – these pāsurams, composed by periyāḻvār, are such that people, with distinguished knowledge, will keep reciting them because of their sweetness. For those who are capable of reciting these pāsurams, knowing the meanings of the pāsurams, sins, which are a hurdle in enjoying emperumān, will not approach anywhere near them.

We shall next consider the pravēsam of the second tirumoḻi of this centum.

## 1.2.1. Sidak kadal

*sīdak kadal uḷḷamudanna dēvakikōdaik kuḻalāḷ asōdaikkup pōttandapēdaik kuḻavi pidittuc cuvaittu uṇṇumpādak kamalangaḷ kāṇīrē pavaḷa vāyīr vandu kāṇīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sīdak kadal ūl amudu anna – like pirātti (śrī mahālakśmi) who was born as the inner nectar in cool ocean; dēvaki – dēvakip pirātti; kōdai – decorated with flowers; kuḻal āḷ – one who has locks; asōdaikkup – to yaśōdāp pirātti; pōttanda – allowing \[her child, kriṣṇa\] to go; pēdaik kuḻavi – ignorant child; pidittu – holding (with his divine hands); cuvaittu – tasting; uṇṇum – feeding with his divine mouth; pādak kamalangaḷ – divine feet which are like lotus; kāṇīrē – look; pavaḷa vāyīr – oh women, who have coral-like reddish mouth!; vandu kāṇīrē – come (at once) and look at his divine feet

**Перевод:**

**dēvakip pirātti, who is like śrī mahālakśmi, who in turn is like the nectar inside the cool ocean, sent her child, kriṣṇa, to yaśōdāp pirātti. That ignorant child is holding his divine feet in his divine hands and is feeding on them. yaśōdāp pirātti is calling out to herd-women, who have coral-like reddish lips, telling them to come and look at his divine feet which are like lotus.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**sīdak kadal uḷḷamudanna dēvaki** – the ocean is cold because it is very deep. The \[initial\] nectar which came out of that ocean was the one which was offered to celestial entities to grant them long lives \[so that they could fight with the demons and monsters for long periods of time\]. The nectar which was inside that cold ocean was as mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 6-1-2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/05/periya-thirumozhi-6-1-2/) “*amudil varum peṇṇamudu*” (śrī mahālakśmi who was the essence of that nectar\]; dēvakip pirātti was similar to śrī mahālakśmi, who was the *uḷḷamudu* \[inner nectar\]. śrī mahālakśmi is one who constantly helps others by forgiving their offences and uniting them with emperumān through her recommendatory role. dēvakip pirātti too was helping others by giving birth to kriṣṇa and offering him to the world such that he would help all.

**kōdaik kuḻalāḷ asōdaikkup pōttanda** – yaśōdāp pirātti has decorated her fine locks with flowery garlands. dēvakip pirātti allowed kriṣṇa to come to śrī gōkulam. *pōttanda* refers to allowing kriṣṇa to go to śrī gōkulam. It is considered as a single word.

**pēdaik kuḻavi** – just as it has been mentioned mercifully by kūrattāḻvān in atimānuśa stavam 14 “*mugda śiśu vatadaḷē śayisa*: *ati tanvā tanvā jaganti bibruśē sa vikāsamēva* l *iśīm imām tu tava śaktim atarkitavyam avyājata*: *pratyasē ki miha avatīrṇa*:” (You were lying on a tender banyan leaf, keeping all the worlds inside your stomach, as a little innocent child. kūrattāḻvān is wondering as to how to explain the reason for emperumān’s arrival here \[samsāram\]. Is it to prove to the world your unmatched ability and your being the reason for the creation of all the worlds?) The samskruta term *mugda śiśu* aptly explains the tamiḻ term *pēdaik kuḻavi* \[an ignorant child\]. Not having the knowledge apt for its age.

**pidittuc cuvaittuṇṇum** – Holding \[the divine foot\] in his divine hands and relishing the taste \[of his divine foot\]. parāśara bhattar has mercifully said in his śrī rangarāja stavam uttara śatakam 54 “*vatadaḷa madi śayya rangadāman*! *śayita ivārṇavatarṇaka*: *padābhjam* l  *atimukhamudarē jaganti mātum nidatika vaiṣṇava bhōjñalipsayā vā* ll” (śrīvaiṣṇavas apply the divine mark of emperumān’s divine feet on their foreheads \[as tirumaṇ kāppu\] since it is enjoyable. It appears that you wanted to ascertain whether it is indeed so and hence you have put your divine foot inside your divine mouth). śrī viṣṇu sūktam says “*viṣṇō*: *padē paramē madva utsa*:” (honey is dripping from the divine foot of viṣṇu); [tiruvāimoḻi 1-5-5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-5-5-maney-nokki/) says “*tēnē malarum tiruppādam*” (your divine foot is blossoming with honey). emperumān wanted to check the veracity of these verses and hence relished his divine foot with his divine mouth, acting in the way an ignorant child would act by putting its foot in its mouth. Another explanation – in an earlier pāsuram (1.1.6) it has been said “*vaiyam ēḻum kaṇḍāḷ piḷḷai vāyuḷē*” (yaśōdāp pirātti had seen all the worlds in his divine mouth). Since he has captured the worlds and kept them imprisoned in his stomach, he had to feed the people who are inside the prison; hence, he kept his divine foot in his divine mouth.

**pādak kamalangaḷ kāṇīrē** – yaśōdā is beseeching the herd-women to look at his divine feet which are like lotus. Reference to lotus implies the colour, coolness, softness, fragrance etc of his divine feet.

In the svāpadēśam for this pāsuram, tiruvāimoḻippiḷḷai brings out the following explanation –  Just as nammāḻvār had mentioned mercifully in [tiruvāimoḻi 4-6-8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/03/thiruvaimozhi-4-6-8-vedham-vallargalai/) “*vēdam vallārgaḷaik koṇḍu viṇṇōr perumān tiruppādam paṇindu*” (surrendering to the enjoyable, divine feet of emperumān who is vorśipped by nityasūris \[permanent dwellers of śrī vaikuṇṭam\] through the *puruśakāram* (recommendatory role) of those who are experts in vēdam), other herd-women have to look at and enjoy the divine feet of kriṣṇa, only when shown by yaśōdāp pirātti.

**pavaḷa vāyīr vandu kāṇīrē** – yaśōdāp pirātti is calling the attention of other herd-women who have their lips similar to coral and who were also keen to enjoy the divine features of child kriṣṇa, just like she was, by praising them \[through the term *pavaḷa vāyīr*\].

In his svāpadēśam, tiruvāīmoḻip piḷḷai says the following: just as the reddish lips are covering the whitish teeth inside the mouth, devotion (which is denoted by *rāga* or reddish colour) is covering *prapatti* (surrendering to emperumān, which is denoted by whiteness). After surrendering to emperumān, one should be fully devoted to emperumān and carry out *mangaḷāśāsanam* to him \[praising him\] constantly, in order to carry out kainkaryam to him. The herd-women have both the devotion towards emperumān and the quality of obedience towards yaśōdāp pirātti \[who is like an ācāryan\]. Hence, yaśōdāp pirātti is urging them to come and witness the divine feet of emperumān so that they could pass through the stages of *parabhakti, parajñānam* and *paramabhakti* \[knowing about emperumān, envisioning emperumān and inability to sustain oneself in the absence of emperumān, respectively\].

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.2.2. Muttum maniyum

*muttum maṇiyum vayiramum nanponnumtattitip padittut talaippu eydāṟpōl engumpattu viralum maṇivṇṇan pādangaḷottittu irundavā kāṇīrē oḷ nudaleer vandu kāṇīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

muttum maṇiyum – pearls and rubies; vayiramum – diamonds; nan ponnum – pure gold; tattitp padittu – arranged in a disorderly way \[and not in the order in which they are normally arranged while making a necklace or ring by a goldsmith\]; talaippu eydāṟpōl – embellished together; engum – everywhere; pattu viralum – all the ten toes; maṇivaṇṇan – kriṣṇa, who has the complexion of a bluish gemstone; pādangaḷ – present in his divine feet; ottittu irunda A – being present together \[without any gap\]; kāṇīrē – have a look; oḷ nudaleer – Oh, ones who have beautiful foreheads

**Перевод:**

**yaśōdāp pirātti tells the herd-women, who have beautiful foreheads, to come and have a look at the divine toes and nails which are present in the divine feet of kriṣṇa. She is comparing his toes and nails with gemstones. Just as toes are disorderly, varying in size from one another, the gemstones such as pearls. rubies, diamonds and pure gold are placed in a disorderly way. They have been embellished together in a necklace or ring, just like the ten divine toes of little kriṣṇa are seen together, without any gap.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In the earlier pāsuram, āḻvār enjoyed the beauty of kriṣṇa’s feet, on the inner side. In this pāsuram, he enjoys the ten divine toes along with their divine nails.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**muttum …** – while applying decorative colours to the toe-nails, different colours are applied to various nails, to give contrasting colours. In a similar way, the nails on the toes of kriṣṇa appear to be of different hues. The big toe appears like golden hue, the next appears like a pearl, the one next to that like ruby, the one next to that like diamond etc. They appear to complement the complexion of kriṣṇa which is like a bluish gemstone. They are without any shortcoming in their *sāmudrikālakśaṇam* (physiognomy) and appear to be together. yaśōdāp pirātti is inviting her friends, who have beautiful, shiny foreheads, to come and witness the divine nails and toes. Reference to pearls, rubies etc is indicative of all the gemstones.

In his svāpadēśam, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that addressing the herd-women as *oṇṇudaleer* is indicative of the fact that they have control over their five senses just like *prapannars* (those who have surrendered to emperumān) have control over their senses.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.2.3. Panaittol ilavaycci

*paṇaittōḷ iḷavāycci pāl pāynda kongaiaṇaittāra uṇḍu kidanda ippiḷḷaiiṇaikkāḷil veḷḷittaḷai ninṟu ilangumkaṇaikkāl irundavā kāṇīrē kārigaiyīr vandu kāṇīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paṇai – like bamboo; tōḷ – having shoulders; iḷa āycci – yaśōdāp pirātti, who is youthful; pāl pāynda kongai – bosom which is secreting milk; aṇaittu – hugging, with divine hands; Ara – such that the divine stomach is full; uṇḍu – drinking that milk; kidanda – lying happily \[due to fullness in his stomach\]; ip piḷḷai – this infant, kriṣṇa; iṇai – having beauty in being together; kālil – divine feet; veḷḷit taḷai ninṟu – silver anklets, firmly; ilangum – shining brightly; kaṇaikkāl irunda A – the way his divine shin is present; kāṇīr – have a look; kārigaiyīr – Oh beautiful women!; vandu kāṇīr – come and have a look

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa was hugging the divine bosom of yaśōdāp pirātti, who is youthful and who has bamboo-like shoulders. He drank milk from her bosom and was lying happily, due to filled-up stomach. On his divine pair of feet, he has silver anklets on the shin region, shining brightly. yaśōdāp pirātti is calling her friends who are beautiful, to look at his divine shin.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) After enjoying the divine feet in the previous pāsuram, āḻvār is enjoying the divine shin \[portion of the leg between the ankle and knee\] in this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**paṇaittōḷ iḷavāycci** – yaśōdāp pirātti has her shoulders which are like bamboo, being fresh, well rounded and beautiful. She is also youthful. The reason for describing her this way is not because of her being an enjoyable person due to her beauty and age, but because of her affection for kriṣṇa and her desire to protect him constantly.

**pāl pāynda kongai** – her bosoms will start secreting milk, the moment kriṣṇa becomes hungry and desires to have milk. He does not even have to bring his mouth near them.

**aṇaittu Ara uṇḍu kidanda ippiḷḷai** – hugging her bosom with his divine hands, imbibing her milk till his stomach became full, kriṣṇa lay happily. Such kriṣṇa’s …

**iṇaikkālil …** – In the two divine feet, which are having beauty countering each other. Those who are qualified to enjoy this, look at the beauty of shins which are shining brightly with silver anklets.

**kārigaiyīr vandu kāṇīrē** – since you \[referring to the herd-women\] are beautiful, you know the distinction of beauty. Hence, you should come and look at his beautiful shins.

In his svāpadēśam, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that the reason for their being beautiful is because they are totally devoted to emperumān and are fully dependent on them.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.2.4. Ulandal naruney

*uḻandāḷ naṟu ney ōrō tadā uṇṇaiḻandāḷ erivināḷ īrttu eḻilmattinpaḻandāmbāl ōccap payattāl tavaḻndānmuḻandāḷ irundavā kāṇīrē mugiḻ mulaiyeer vandu kāṇīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uḻandāḷ – with effort \[accumulated\]; naṟu ney – fragrant ghee; ōrō tadā – each vessel, sequentially; uṇṇa – as he ate; iḻandāḷ – thinking that she had lost the child; erivināl – due to anger; īrttu – pulling him (by his hand); eḻil mattinn – with a beautiful churning staff; paḻam tāmbāl – with an old rope; ōcca – as she \[yaśōdāp pirātti\] raised it, to hit him; payattāl – out of fear; tavaḻndān – one, who crawled; muḻandāl – divine knees; irundavā – the way they were; kāṇīrē – look; mugiḻmulaiyīr – Oh those with bosoms which are like buds!; vandu kāṇīr – Come and have a look

**Перевод:**

**yaśōdāp pirātti had accumulated ghee, with effort, over a period of time, and stored them in vessels. Little kriṣṇa ate the ghee from each vessel. Fearing that she would lose her child if he ate so much of ghee, in order to warn him, yaśōdāp pirātti caught hold of his divine arm, pulled him, and raised an old rope \[which was used for making butter by churning the staff with it\], as if to strike him with that rope. kriṣṇa crawled away from her, out of fear for her. Looking at him crawl like that, yaśōdāp pirātti called her friends, whose bosoms were like buds, to come and have a look at his divine knees.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) After enjoying the beauty of the divine shin, āḻvār enjoys the beauty of kriṣṇa’s divine knees*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**uḻandāḷ** – yaśōdāp pirātti had taken lot of efforts to get the ghee – she had to milk the cows, then heat the milk and set it to become curd; then she had to churn the curd, in order to get butter from it. She then had to heat the butter and convert it into ghee. Thus, she had to take plenty of efforts in order to get each vessel of ghee.

**naṟu ney oṟo tadā uṇṇa** – kriṣṇa ate the fragrant ghee from one pot after another, without leaving anything behind.

**erivināl īrttu** – out of fear whether the little infant would be able to digest all the ghee which he had eaten, she pulled him roughly, with anger.

**eḻil mattin paḻam tāmbāl ōcca** – she tried to hit him with an old rope which was coiled around a beautiful churning staff.

**payattāl tavaḻndān** – out of fear that she would hit him, little kriṣṇa crawled away from her, to escape from her.

**muḻandāḷ irundavā kāṇīrē** – she is beckoning her friends to look at his beautiful, divine knees as he crawled away from her.

**mugiḻ mulaiyīr vandu kāṇīrē** – Oh ladies who have bosoms which are like buds! Come and have a look at his divine knees.

In his svāpadēśam, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that their bosoms indicate devotion. The reference to bud-like bosom is to indicate that their devotion is just then sprouting.

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.2.5. Pirangiya peycci

*piṟangiya pēycci mulai suvaittu uṇḍittuuṟanguvānpōlē kidanda ippiḷḷaimaṟangoḷ iraṇiyan mārvai mun kīṇḍānkuṟangugaḷai vandu kāṇiṟē kuvi mulaiyīr vandu kāṇīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mun – in an earlier time; maṟam koḷ – having hatred; iraṇiyan – hiraṇya kaśyap’s \[a monster\]; mārvai – chest; kīṇḍān – tore; piṟangiya – having a splendour (born out of cruelty); pēycci – pūtanā’s; mulai – bosom; suvaittu – tasting in such a way that all the life was removed from it; uṇḍittu – one who consumed her milk; uṟanguvān pōlē – one who slept, as if he did not know anything; kidanda – one who was lying; ippiḷḷai – this kriṣṇa (his); kuṟangugaḷai – divine thighs; kāṇīr – have a look; kuvi mulaiyīr! – Oh ladies who have rounded bosoms! Come and have a look \[at his divine thighs\]

**Перевод:**

**In an earlier time \[kruta yugam\], emperumān had torn the chest of monster hiraṇya kaśyap, who had only hatred. Such emperumān \[in dvāpara yugam\] incarnated as kriṣṇa and suckled on the bosom of pūtanā, who had a splendour about her as a result of her cruelty, so hard, that her life itself got removed. Such kriṣṇa, after drinking her milk, slept as if he did not know anything about what had happened. yaśōdāp pirātti is calling her friends, who had well-rounded bosoms, to come and have a look at the divine thighs of kriṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) After enjoying the beauty of kriṣṇa’s divine knees, āḻvār next enjoys the beauty of his divine thighs.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**piṟangiya pēycci mulai suvaittu uṇḍittu** – pūtanā had a splendour about her, which came about, not because of her beauty or her good thoughts, but because of her cruelty. kriṣṇa suckled hard on her bosom such that along with her milk, her life too came out of her bosom. The term *uṇḍittu* is to be treated as a single word and not as a compounded form of *uṇḍu* and *ittu*.

**uṟanguvān pōlē kidanda ippiḷḷai** – this little infant kriṣṇa is lying as if he did not know about the valorous deed which he had carried out in killing that pūtanā.

**maṟangoḷ …** – during kruta yugam, the monster hiraṇya kaśyap had hatred for his son, prahlādan \[since prahlādan showed his devotion towards emperumān\]. emperumān \[as narasimha\] kept hiraṇyan on his thighs and tore the chest of that monster. Such emperumān, who is lying now as kriṣṇa, carries resemblance to that act, in his thighs. Come and have a look at such divine thighs.

**kuvi mulaiyīr vandu kāṇīrē** – Oh women who have well rounded bosoms! Come and have a look at his divine thighs.

In his svāpadēśam, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that when yaśōdāp pirātti is calling her friends to come and have a look at kriṣṇa’s divine thighs, it appeared that those thighs still carried blood stains \[formed when he, as narasimha, had kept the monster hiraṇya on his lap and torn his chest\]. The reason for recalling that incident now is because of exhibiting ability to eliminate enemy \[hiraṇya kaśyap for narasimhan and pūtanā for kriṣṇa\] and also because both are incarnations of the same śrīman nārāyaṇa. Alternatively, when yaśōdāp pirātti was hugging kriṣṇa as her nature, since she admired his divine thighs, she was calling other herd-women to come and have a look at his thighs. The reason for describing their bosoms as well rounded is because bosoms represent devotion towards emperumān and when they are well rounded, the devotion is being nurtured well.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.2.6. Mattak kalirru

*mattak kaḷiṟṟu vasudēvar tammudaicittam piriyāda dēvaki tan vayiṟṟilattattin pattā nāḷ tōnṟiya accudanmuttam irundavā kāṇīrē mugiḻ nagaiyīr! vandu kāṇīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

matta kaḷiṟu – one who has elephants which are in rut; vasudēvar tammudai – śrī vasudēvar’s; cittam piriyāda – never separating from his heart; dēvaki than – dēvakip pirātti’s; vayiṟṟil – in her stomach; attattin pattānāḷ – on the divine day of tenth day from the star hastam; tōnṟiya – one who incarnated; accudan – kaṇṇan, who does not let go of others; muttam – the manner his cannam is (it is customary to refer to the male genital organ with words such as cannam, muttam, mottu); kāṇīr – see; mugiḻ nagaiyīr – Oh, women, who have gentle smile! Come and see

**Перевод:**

**dēvakip pirātti, consort of śrī vasudēvar who has elephants in rut, never leaves his heart. kaṇṇan, who does not let go of others, incarnated from the stomach of such dēvakip pirātti, on the tenth day of the star hastam. yaśōdāp pirātti is calling the attention of women, who have gentle smile, to come and have a look at his divine loin region.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) After enjoying the beauty of kriṣṇa’s divine thighs, āḻvār is enjoying the beauty of his divine loin region.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**matta …** – from the stomach of dēvakip pirātti, who always acts as per the heart of śrī vasudēvar who has elephants which are in rut.

**attattin …** – on the tenth day from the day of star *hastam*. Since āḻvār is a mangaḷāśāsanaparar (one who constantly carries out mangaḷāśāsanam for emperumān), to prevent enemies from knowing the precise day of birth and carrying out wrongful deeds, he hides the divine day when emperumān incarnated and mentions this way.

**tōnṟiya …** – just as it has been mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5.3.2 “*acyuta bhānunā dēvakīpūrva sandyāyām āvirbhūtam*” (kriṣṇa, who is the sūryan \[sun\], appeared in the east direction, dēvaki), he incarnated without the fault of having resided inside a womb. Look at the divine loin region of such kriṣṇa, who does not ever let go of his followers.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that unlike *cētanas* (souls having ability to think) who reside inside a womb due to compulsion of *karma* (past deeds), kriṣṇa incarnated due to his mercy.

**mugiḻ nagaiyīr! vandu kāṇīrē** – Oh, you all, who have a budding gentle smile! Come and have a look.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.2.7. Irungai madakaliru

*irungai madakaḷiṟu īrkkinṟavanaiparungip paṟittukkoṇḍu ōdum paraman tannerungu pavaḷamum nēr nāṇum muttummarungum irundavā kāṇīrē vāṇudaleer! vandu kāṇīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

irum kai – having a huge trunk; mada kaḷiṟu – kuvalayāpīdam, the elephant in rut; īrkkinṟavanai – the mahout \[controller of the elephant\], who was controlling it; parungi – killed; paṟittuk koṇḍu – snapping (the tusks of that elephant); ōdum – one who ran; paraman than – kaṇṇan, who is the supreme entity; nerungu pavaḷamum – coral chain, which had been strung closely; nēr nāṇum – excellent waist cord; muttum – pearl chain (together with all these); marungum – divine waist; irunda A – the manner in which it is; kāṇīr – have a look; vāḷ nudaleer – oh women, who have radiant foreheads! Come and have a look

**Перевод:**

**kaṇṇan, the supreme entity, killed the mahout who was controlling elephant kuvalayāpīdam, which had huge trunk and which was in rut. He snapped the tusks of kuvalayāpīdam and ran with them. Look at that kaṇṇan’s divine waist, which is decorated with closely strung chain of coral, excellent waist-cord and pearl chain. Oh women, who have splendorous foreheads! Come and have a look.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) After enjoying the beauty of kriṣṇa’s divine loin region, āḻvār next enjoys his divine waist.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**irungai …** – killing the mahout, who had under his control the elephant kuvalayāpīdam, which had huge trunk and which was rutting. *parungudal* – to kill

**paṟittu …** – supreme entity who snapped the tusks of that elephant and ran towards king kamsan, who was sitting on a high land and jumped before him. Alternatively, the herd-boys who were playing in tiruvāyppādi made an elephant doll with the materials which they had and were roaming around, saying that it was a huge elephant. kriṣṇa, the supreme entity, controlled them and ran with the tusks of that elephant doll.

**nerungu …** – look at his divine waist which is decorated with densely strung coral chain, with golden waist cord and with a pearl chain.

**vāṇudaleer vandu kāṇīrē** – oh, you women, who have radiant foreheads! Come and have a look at his divine waist. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says in his svāpadēśam that the term *vāṇudaleer* refers to the radiance of mind control of those who have surrendered.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.2.8. Vanda madalai

*vanda madalaik kuḻāttai vali seydutandak kaḷiṟu pōl tanē viḷaiyādumnandan madalaikku nanṟum aḻagiyaundi irundavā kāṇīrē oḷi iḻaiyīr! vandu kāṇīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vanda – those who came to play with him; madalai kuḻātti – group of little children; vali seydu – forcing (himself) on them; tanda kaḷiṟu pōl – like a little elephant which has (converging) tusk; tanē – he himself (as the primary person); viḷaiyādum – one who played; nandan madalaikku – for kaṇṇan, nandagōpar’s son; nanṟum aḻagiya – very beautiful; undi – divine navel; irunda A – the manner in which it is; kāṇīr – have a look; oḷi iḻaiyīr – Oh women, who have radiant ornaments! Come and have a look

**Перевод:**

**kaṇṇan, the son of śrī nandagōpar, forces himself on the group of children who come to play with him, to assert that he is the best among them. Look at his divine navel. Oh, women, who have decorated yourselves with radiant ornaments! Come and have a look at his divine navel.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) After enjoying kriṣṇa’s divine waist, āḻvār enjoys his divine navel.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vanda …** – when a group of children came to play with him \[kriṣṇa\], just as it has been said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3-1-1 “*tannērāyiram piḷḷaigaḷōdu*” (along with a thousand children \[in tiruvāyappādi\] who are like he is), even as he is as child-like they are, he will make them all to be on one side while he alone will be on the other side, and win against them by force, just like a young elephant will break tree branches. He wanted to dominate over all the other children.

**nandan …** – even while he will roam around like this \[in a dominant fashion\], in the presence of śrī nandagōpar, he would behave like a very obedient child.

**nanṟum …** – look at his very beautiful divine navel. Oh women, who are having splendorous ornaments! Come and have a look at his divine navel.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that the term *oḷi iḻai* \[shiny ornaments\] refers to *ātma bhūśaṇam* \[ornament for the soul, such as bliss, knowledge, being a servitor to emperumān etc\].

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.2.9. Adirum kadalnira

*adirum kadal niṟa vaṇṇanai āyccimadura mulai ūtti vanjittu vaittupadarap padāmē paḻandāmbāl ārttaudaram irundavā kāṇīrē oḷi vaḷaiyīr! vandu kāṇīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

adirum kadal niṟa vaṇṇanai – one who has the colour of uproarious ocean; āycci – yaśōdāp pirātti, his divine mother; madura mulai ūtti – feeding him sweet milk from bosom; vanjittu vaittu – thinking of deceptive act; padarap padāmē – without losing her thought; paḻam tāmbāl – with an often-used rope; ārtta – tied; udaram – divine stomach; irunda A – the way it is; kāṇīr – have a look; oḷi vaḷaiyīr – oh, women with splendorous bangles! Come and have a look

**Перевод:**

**The divine mother yaśōdāp pirātti, while feeding her son kriṣṇa, who has the complexion of an uproarious ocean, with her bosom milk, thought of a deceptive act. Without losing track of her thoughts, she tied kriṣṇa with an often-used rope. She calls her friends who are wearing radiant bangles to come and have a look at kriṣṇa’s divine stomach.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) Subsequent to enjoying kriṣṇa’s divine navel, āḻvār enjoys his divine stomach.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**adirum kadal niṟa vaṇṇanai** – one who has the attractive complexion of an uproarious ocean. While it was sufficient to say “One who has the complexion of an ocean”, the mention of “uproarious ocean” is to refer to his uncontrollable behaviour.

**āycci madura mulai ūtti vanjittu vaittu** – yaśōdā, his mother, even while suckling him with her sweet milk, had thought of a deceptive plan to tie him, without kriṣṇa being aware of it. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that since she had planned to tie him, until she unties and releases him, to provide him sustenance, she suckled him. Since she wanted kriṣṇa to enjoy the taste of her milk, she had eaten tasty food items, as a result of which her milk became sweet.

**padara …** – without losing track of her thoughts, she tied him with a rope which was used often to tie cows and calves. She calls her friends to come and have a look at his divine stomach which carries the mark of the rope, which she had used to tie him.

**oḷi vḷaiyīr vandu kāṇīrē** – oh, you all, who are wearing radiant bangles! Come and have a look at his divine stomach. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *oḷi vaḷai* is symbolic of belonging only to emperumān and to none else.

We shall next consider the 10<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.2.10. Peruma uralil

*perumā uralil piṇippuṇḍu irundu anguirumā marudam iṟutta ippiḷḷaikurumā maṇippūṇ kulāvit tigaḻumtirumārbu irundavā kāṇīrē sēyiḻaiyīr! vandu kāṇīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

peru mā uralil – with a huge mortar; piṇippuṇḍu irundu – being tied down; angu – in that state; iru mā marudam – two huge maruda trees \[Indian laurel\]; iṟutta – one who snapped; ippillai – this child’s; kurumā maṇippūṇ – kaustuba chain, the most eminent ornament; kulāvit tigaḻum – swaying radiantly; tiru mārbu irunda A – the way his divine chest is; kāṇīr – have a look; sē iḻaiyīr – oh women, who are wearing reddish ornaments! Come and have a look

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa was tied down with a huge mortar. In that state itself, he went in between two huge marudam trees, snapping them. Look at his divine chest, on which the divine ornament kaustubam is swaying. Oh, women, with eminent ornaments! Come and have a look.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) After enjoying kriṣṇa’s divine stomach, āḻvār enjoys his divine chest.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**peru mā …** – even as he was tied down to a huge mortar, kriṣṇa crawled in that state itself and went in between two *marudam* trees, which had united to kill him. When he went between the two trees, with the mortar, the two trees snapped and fell down. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says in his svāpadēśam that kriṣṇa gave an understanding smile after seeing the twin *maruda* trees snapping and falling down \[two demons had pervaded the trees and were planning to kill kriṣṇa\]. yaśōdāp pirātti points out to such kriṣṇa and says “*ippiḷḷai*” (this child). Such kriṣṇa’s …

**kuru mā …** – look at his divine chest on which the eminent, renowned śrī kaustubam ornament is swaying \[śrī kaustubam is symbolic of all the jīvātmās\]. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that śrī kaustubam ornament is a bluish gemstone. He further says that whatever ornament is worn by kriṣṇa, will shine in blue colour due to the rays from his bluish divine form.

**sēyiḻaiyīr vandu māṇīrē** – Oh those who are wearing reddish ornaments! Come and have a look at his divine chest. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *sēyiḻai* refers to ornament of the soul which is full of devotion \[towards emperumān\].

We shall next consider the 11<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.2.11. Nalgal or

*nāḷgaḷ ōr nālaindu tingaḷ aḷavilētāḷai nimirttuc cagadattaic cādippōyvāḷkoḷ vaḷai eyiṟṟu āruyir vavvināntōḷgaḷ irundavā kāṇīrē suri kuḻaleer! vandu kāṇīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nāḷgaḷ ōr nālaindu tingaḷ aḷavilē – About four, five months (after his divine incarnation); sagadattai – the monster śakatāsuran; tāḷai nimirttu – lifting his foot; sādip pōy – kicked him; vāḷ koḷ – having radiance; vaḷai – curved; eyiṟu – pūtanā, who had teeth like that, her; Ar uyir – dear life; vavvinān – one who usurped; tōḷgaḷ irunda A – the way the shoulders are; kāṇīr – have a look; suri kuḻaleer – oh, women, who have curly locks! Come and have a look

**Перевод:**

**Four, five months after he incarnated, kriṣṇa lifted his divine foot and kicked the monster śakatāsuran, killing him. He usurped the precious life of pūtanā, another monster, who had shiny, curved teeth and killed her. Oh women, who have curly hair! Look at the divine shoulders of such kriṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) After enjoying the beauty of kriṣṇa’s divine chest, āḻvār enjoys his divine shoulders.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**nāḷgaḷ ōr** – About four five months after his divine incarnation. Since āḻvār is a mangaḷāśāsanaparar (one who is constantly engaged with carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam (praising and wishing) for emperumān), he does not specify the exact month after birth, but gives a vague period which could be construed as four months or five months or (four plus five) nine months or (four times five) twenty months etc, as a means for removing evil eyes cast on kriṣṇa.

**tāḷai …** – a monster, *śakatan*, had pervaded a wheel with the intention of killing kriṣṇa, when kriṣṇa was sleeping alone in a place, kicking his legs since he was feeling hungry and could not feel yaśōdāp pirātti’s bosom. The monster got caught between the kicking feet of kriṣṇa and got annihilated. The term *sādip pōy* refers to kicking.

**vāḷ koḷ …** – he also usurped the life of pūtanā, another monster, who had shiny, curved teeth, whose life was difficult to be usurped.  This is in line with tirumangai āḻvār mercifully saying in [periya tirumoḻi 1-3-1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/02/periya-thirumozhi-1-3-1/) “*pēycci perumulaiyūduyirai vaṟṟa vāngi uṇḍa vāyan*” (emperumān, who has a divine mouth through which he drank, without leaving anything, the life of pūtanā through her huge bosoms). While pūtanā was killed first and only after that was *sakatāsuran* killed, the reason for changing the sequence here is not due to any uncertainty but due to overflowing enthusiasm \[that kriṣṇa had been able to destroy his enemies). tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the reason for āḻvār changing the order of annihilating pūtanā and sakatāsuran is because of his ability to see the earlier *yugams* \[epochs\] too \[the events in each epoch get repeated; hence āḻvār, who has been mercifully granted knowledge with devotion, without any trace of doubt by emperumān, has seen all the killing of enemies\]. Alternatively, he has composed the events in the order in which emperumān had manifested the events to him.

**tōḷgaḷ …** – yaśōdāp pirātti wants her friends to see the beauty of kriṣṇa’s divine shoulders which he contracted when he drank the milk from pūtanā’s bosom. Oh, women who have curly locks! Come and have a look at his divine shoulders. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *suri kuḻal* refers to the act of surrendering to emperumān, controlling one’s mind.

We shall next consider the 12<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.2.12. Maittadam kanni

*maittadam kaṇṇi asōdai vaḷarkkinṟaseyttalai neela niṟattuc ciṟuppiḷḷaineyttalai nēmiyum sangum nilāviyakaittalangaḷ vandu kāṇīrē kananguḻaiyīr! vandu kāṇīre*

**Пословный перевод:**

mai tadam kaṇṇi – one who has dark, expansive eyes; asōdai – yaśōdāp pirātti; vaḷarkkinṟa – nurturing; talai sey – in eminent field; neelam niṟattu – having the complexion of blue water lily; siṟu piḷḷai – small child’s; ney – sharp; talai – having edge; nēmiyum – divine disc and; sangum – divine conch; nilāviya – dwelling; kaittalangaḷ – divine palms; vandu kāṇīr – come and have a look; kanam kuḻaiyīr! – Oh women, who have golden ear-rings! Come and have a look

**Перевод:**

**yaśōdāp pirātti, who has dark, expansive eyes, is nurturing kriṣṇa who has the complexion of blue lilies which are cultivated in eminent fields. Come and have a look at his divine palms which are holding the divine disc, with sharp enges, and the divine conch. Oh, women who have golden ear rings! Come and have a look.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) Subsequent to enjoying kriṣṇa’s divine shoulders, āḻvār enjoys his divine palms.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**maittadam kaṇṇi** – this refers to yaśōdāp pirātti’s eyes which are dark and expansive. This could also mean that her eyes have become wide after she applied black pigment to her eyes to decorate them. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that her eyes are symbolic of her entire decoration \[she has decorated herself fully and āḻvār is mentioning only her eyes, as symbolic of that\].

**asōdai vaḷarkkinṟa** – yaśōdāp pirātti, who was like this, nurtured kriṣṇa by constantly looking after him with her eyes. Though there were many people to nurture him, instead of leaving him with them, she nurtured him herself. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that though yaśōdāp pirātti has seen his amazing activities which are beyond the realm of human beings, she still considers him as *siṟu piḷḷai* \[a little child\].

**seyttalai …** – kriṣṇa was like a little child with the complexion of blue lily, which has just then blossomed in a plant which was growing on its fertile land. All the earnestness which she had showed in her nurturing him, manifested in his divine complexion.

**neyttalai nēmiyum sangum nilāviya** – this refers to the divine disc with sharp edges. Alternatively, since weapons are applied with ghee \[to prevent rust\] this refers to divine disc which is immersed in ghee. Another explanation – just as tirumangai āḻvār had mentioned in periya tirumoḻi 10-7-3 “*kaiyellām ney*” (emperumān’s divine hands are full of ghee) \[consumed as kriṣṇa\], the ghee from his divine hands have got transferred to the divine disc too. While the divine disc is like this, having to go out of emperumān’s divine hand to annihilate his enemies, just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 10-6-8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/02/thiruvaimozhi-10-6-8-meynninru/) “*karudumidam porudu*” (the divine disc will go to the place thought of by emperumān to destroy his enemy and return to his divine hand to stay there)  the divine conch is such that without having to leave emperumān’s divine hand, it would annihilate the enemies by its mere roaring sound. It is possible that kriṣṇa has shown his divine disc and divine conch to yaśōdāp pirātti on a few occasions, for her to sing this way. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa would have shown her his divine weapons for her to say this, just as embār had mentioned while araiyar was performing for the pāsuram verse in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2.1 padigam “*appūcci kāttuginṟān*” \[we shall consider this in detail during the vyākhyānam translation of 2.1 padigam\]. *nilāvudal* – to dwell.

**kaittalam …** – Come and have a look at his divine palms. Oh, women who hare heavy ear rings! Come and have a look. *kanam* would also refer to gold. Thus, it would mean women who have worn golden ear rings. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *kanam kuḻaiyīr* refers to surrendered people listening to the activities of emperumān, with involvement.

We shall next consider the 13<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.2.13. Vandamar pungulal

*vaṇḍamar pūnguḻal āycci maganāgakkoṇḍu vaḷarkkinṟa kōvalark kuttaṟkuaṇḍamaum nādum adanga viḻungiyakaṇḍam irundavā kāṇīrē kārigaiyīr! vandu kāṇīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇḍu amar – settled upon by beetles; pū kuḻal – having locks which are decorated with flowers; āycci – yaśōdāp pirātti; maganāga – as (her) son; koṇḍu – accepting; vaḷarkkinṟa – nurtured; kōvalar kuttaṟku – for the son of herd-clan; aṇḍamaum – all the galaxies; nādum – cētana and acētana entities (entities with and without the ability to think, who are inhabiting those galaxies); adanga – completely; viḻungiya – swallowed; kaṇḍam – divine neck; irunda A – the way it is; kāṇīr – have a look; kārigaiyīr – Oh, beautiful women! Come and have a look

**Перевод:**

**yaśōdāp pirātti has locks decked with flowers, on which beetles have settled. She nurtures kriṣṇa, the child of the entire herd-clan, as her son. Have a look at his divine neck which has swallowed \[at the time of deluge\] all the galaxies along with the inhabiting entities, both with and without the ability to think. Oh, beautiful women! Come and have a look.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) Subsequent to enjoying the divine palms of kriṣṇa, āḻvār enjoys his divine neck.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vaṇḍamar …** – mothers would decorate themselves such that the children will not feel distressed. In line with this, since yaśōdāp pirātti too has decorated herself with seasonal flowers, beetles would come and settle on them in order to imbibe honey in those flowers. The son of śrī nandagōpar, who she considers as her son, and nurtures. Since āḻvār knows the fact \[that kriṣṇa is dēvakip pirātti’s son\], he says “considers as her son”; as far as yaśōdāp pirātti is concerned, kriṣṇa is her son.

**aṇḍam …** – this refers to emperumān swallowing all the galaxies along with the *cētanas* and *acētanas* who inhabit those galaxies such that they remain in a small corner of his divine stomach. He had swallowed everything, without leaving out anything.

**kaṇḍam …** – Look at the beauty of his divine neck. Oh, beautiful women! Come and have a look at his divine neck. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *kārigaiyīr* refers to those who are completely devoted to emperumān.

We shall next consider the 14<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.2.14. Endondai vayccingam

*endoṇḍaivāyc cingam vā enṟu edutukkoṇḍuandoṇḍai vāy amudu ādarittu āycciyartandoṇḍai vāyāl tarukkip parugum iccendoṇḍai vay vandu kāṇīrē sēyiḻaiyīr! vandu kāṇīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

toṇḍai vāy – having divine mouth which is like kovvaip (kōvaip) paḻam (type of berry); en singam! – oh my son, who is like a lion cub!; vā enṟu – saying “Come”; eduttuk koṇḍu – taking him on their waists; āycciyar – herd-women; am toṇḍai – like beautiful kovvaip paḻam; vāy – (secreting) in the divine mouth; amudu – nectar; ādarittu – desirously; tam – their; toṇḍai vāyāl – mouths, which are like kovvaip paḻam; tarukki – pressing; parugum – drinking; iccem toṇḍai vāy – this divine mouth which is like reddish kovvaip paḻam; vandu kāṇīr – come and have a look; sē iḻaiyīr – Oh women, who have reddish ornaments! Come and have a look

**Перевод:**

**Herd-women carry on their waists kriṣṇa, who has divine mouth like kovvaip paḻam and who is arrogant like a lion cub. They press their kovvaip paḻam like mouths against his divine mouth and take in the nectar which secretes from his divine mouth. yaśōdāp pirātti calls her friends, who are wearing reddish ornaments, to come and have a look at his divine mouth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) After enjoying the beauty of kriṣṇa’s divine neck, āḻvār enjoys his divine mouth.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**en toṇḍai …** – kriṣṇa had his mouth reddish like *kovvaip paḻam* and had a pride, like a lion cub. The herd-women carried him on their waists, saying ”He is my son”. Desiring his saliva, which is like nectar, coming from his divine mouth, they press their mouths against him and imbibe that. t*harukkip parugum* – would also mean that they drink it with pride.

**ic cendoṇḍai …** – even after they keep drinking the saliva from his mouth, the divine mouth looks reddish. yaśōdāp pirātti calls her friends, who are wearing reddish ornaments, to come and have a look at his divine mouth. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his *svāpadēśam*, says that *sēyiḻai* refers to ornament for the soul, which is reflective of devotion.

We shall next consider the 15<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.2.15. Nokki asodai

*nōkki asōdai nuṇukkiya manjaḷālnākku vaḻittu nīrāttum innambikkuvākkum nayanamum vāyum muṟuvalummūkkum irundavā kāṇīrē moy kuḻaleer! vandu kāṇīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

asōdai – yaśōdāp pirātti; nōkki – confirming (that it is apt for his divine form); nuṇukkiya – ground; manjaḷāl – with turmeric; nākku vaḻittu – cleansing his divine tongue; nīrāttum – giving a divine bath; innambikku – for this kaṇṇan, who is complete with all the auspicious qualities; vākkum – words; nayanamum – divine eyes; vāyum – divine mouth (or, the way it is); muṟuvalum – gentle smile; mūkkum – divine nose; irunda A – the way they are; kāṇīr – have a look; moy kuḻaleer – Oh women, who have dense locks! Come and have a look

**Перевод:**

**yaśōdāp pirātti selects turmeric and grinds it such that it would be apt for kriṣṇa’s divine form. She cleanses his divine tongue with that turmeric and gives him a divine bath. kriṣṇa is complete with all the auspicious qualities. yaśōdāp pirātti calls her friends to have a look at his divine words, divine eyes, divine mouth, divine smile and divine nose. Oh, women, who have dense locks! Come and have a look.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) Subsequent to enjoying his divine mouth, āḻvār enjoys the overall beauty of his divine face.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**nōkki …** – yaśōdāp pirātti understands the tenderness of kriṣṇa’s divine form. She selects turmeric which will be apt for that form and grinds it. She cleanses his tongue with that turmeric powder, and uses that powder for giving him a divine bath too. He, who is complete with all the auspicious qualities, is obedient to her during all these activities.

**vākkum …**  – Have a look at the divine words with which he calls mother and others, the divine eyes with which he showers his grace on those who tell him “Look at me” ”Look at me”, the divine lips which separate in order to break into a divine smile, the divine smile which results from opening of those lips, the divine nose which is spoken of by nammāḻvār in [tiruvāimoḻi 7-7-2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/10/thiruvaimozhi-7-7-2-attiyum-thurriyum/) “*māttuyar kaṟpagattin valliyō koḻundō aṟiyēn*” (I do not know whether it his divine nose or the creeper from the *kaṟpaga* tree (a celestial tree) or its tender shoot) making one doubt all the time. Oh women, who have dense locks! Come and have a look. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that the term *moy kuḻaleer* refers to those who have surrendered and who are praying to him, just prior to the stage of carrying out servitude to him.

We shall next consider the 16<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.2.16. Vinkol amarargal

*viṇkoḷ amarargaḷ vēdanai tīra munmaṇmoḷ vasudēvar tam maganāy vandutiṇkoḷ asurargaḷ tēya vaḷarginṟānkaṇgaḷ  irundavā kāṇīrē kanavaḷaiyīr! vandu kāṇīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

viṇkoḷ – having worlds such as svargam \[heaven\] etc as their habitats; amarargaḷ – celestial entities such as indra et al; vēdanai – distress; tīra – to be eliminated; mun – earlier; maṇkoḷ – having earth as his dwelling place; vasudēvar tam – as vasudēvar’s; maganāy vandu – incarnating as \[his\] son; tiṇkoḷ – having strength; asurar – monsters; tēya – to be destroyed; vaḷarginṟān – kaṇṇan, who is growing up, his; kaṇgaḷ irunda A – the way his divine eyes are; kāṇīr – have a look; kanam vaḷaiyīr – oh, women, who have golden bangles! Come and have a look

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa incarnated earlier, as the son of vasudēvar, who has earth as his habitat, in order to eliminate the distress of celestial entities such as indra et al who have heaven etc as their habitats. He is growing up \[in śrī gōkulam\] such that monsters would get annihilated. Have a look at his divine eyes. Oh, women, who are wearing golden bangles! Come and have a look at his divine eyes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) While āḻvār was enjoying the overall beauty of the divine face of kriṣṇa, the divine eyes secured his attention, as a result of which he enjoys their beauty again. While it was the divine nose which he enjoyed the last, among the divine organs on the divine face of kriṣṇa, there is a commonality between these two \[while the divine eyes are like lotus flowers, the nose is like the stalk of that lotus\].  Also, when he is enjoying the beauty of kriṣṇa from his divine foot to his divine crown, the eyes come in that order of sequence and are like a vortex, pulling āḻvār towards them.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**viṇkoḷ …** – Since the purpose of emperumān’s incarnation is to protect the noble ones etc, in order to eliminate the distress of celestial entities such as indra et al, who inhabit worlds such as *svargam* etc, coming from monstrous entities, he incarnated earlier as the son of vasudēvar, who inhabits earth. Since vasudēvar was imprisoned, since kriṣṇa was going to be born as his eighth son, kriṣṇa incarnated as his son first, to eliminate vasudēvar’s distress before eliminating the distress of celestial entities, just as tirumangai āḻvār has mentioned in his periya tirumoḻi 8-5-1 “*tandai kālil vilangaṟa vandu tōnṟiya tōnṟal*” (the lord who incarnated in order to break the chains from his father’s feet). tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that he could eliminate the distress of celestial entities only if he removes the distress of vasudēvar.

**tiṇkoḷ …** – the one who was growing up in order to annihilate the monsters who had physical as well as mental strength. As kriṣṇa’s legs grew \[as he was growing up\], the monsters’ position was decaying. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that he grew up in tiruvāyppādi in order to get rid of his distress \[he considers the distress of his favourable ones as his own\]. For the monsters, *tiṇmai* \[strength\] refers to the pain in the hearts of kriṣṇa’s followers due to the monstrous nature of kamsan et al and their birth. In other words, without considering that they are his parents or relatives, kamsan imprisoned them all; without considering that they are his nephews, he hit them against rock as soon as they were born. kriṣṇa grew up in tiruvāyppādi in order to burn the stomachs of such monsters and to annihilate them.

**kaṇgaḷ …** – since he has come to help the noble ones and to destroy the enemies, he was showering his mercy on the favourable ones such that they would be protected. Look at his divine eyes. Oh, women who are wearing golden bangles! Come and have a look. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *kanavaḷai* \[golden bangles\] symbolises the total dependence of the surrendered entities’ possessions.

We shall next consider the 17<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.2.17. Paruvam nirambame

*paruvam nirambāmē pārellām uyyatiruvin vadivu okkum dēvaki peṟṟauruvu kariya oḷi maṇivaṇṇanpuruvam irundavā kāṇīrē pūṇ mulaiyīr! vandu kāṇīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paruvam – age; nirambāmē – before reaching maturity; pār ellām – all the world; uyya – to get uplifted; tiruvin vadivu okkum – matching the nature of periya pirātti \[śrī mahālakśmi\]; dēvaki – dēvakip pirātti; peṟṟa – gave birth to (after observing penance); uruvu kariya – dark in his form; oḷi – splendorous; maṇi vaṇṇan – having a form like that of a gemstone; puruvam – divine eyebrows; irunda A – the way they are; kāṇīr – have a look; pūṇ mulaiyīr – Oh women, who have adorned your bosoms with ornaments! Come and have a look

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa, even before he reached the age of maturity, had carried out activities which uplifted all the worlds. Look at the divine eyebrows of that kriṣṇa, who has a form which is dark and radiant like a gemstone, and who was given birth to by dēvakip pirātti, after she had carried out penance. Oh, women, who have adorned your bosoms with ornaments! Come and have a look at his divine eyebrows.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) Subsequent to the divine eyes, āḻvār enjoys the beauty of the divine eyebrows.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**paruvam …** – unlike cakravartit tirumagan \[śrī rāma, the divine son of emperor daśarata cakravarti) who killed his enemies after he had grown up beyond the age of maturity, and uplifted the world, since kriṣṇa was, just as it has been said in the previous pāsuram “*tiṇkoḷ asurarait tēya vaḷarginṟān*”, growing up to annihilate monsters to enable the worlds to get uplifted, he destroyed monsters such as pūtanā, śakata et al even when he was in the cradle-stage.

**tiruvin vadivu okkum dēvaki peṟṟa** – dēvakip pirātti, who has the nature of periya pirātti, had observed penance in order to give birth to kriṣṇa. Since it has been mentioned as *tiru vadivu okkum*, the meaning meant in the first pāsuram, *uḷ amudu anna dēvaki*, has been explicitly mentioned here. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the term *tiruvin vadivu okkum* refers to their having matching quality in one aspect amidst different qualities \[the quality of assisting in uplifting the world – periya pirātti, through her quality of *puruśakāra bhūtai* (recommendatory role) helps in uplifting the world while dēvakip pirātti, by giving birth to kriṣṇa, uplifted the world through him\].

**uruvu …** – one who has a dark form which was shining like a gemstone.

**puruvam …** – look at the beauty of his divine eyebrows, which appear like the sugarcane bow of *madanan* \[kāman, deity for love\]. Oh women, who have your bosoms decorated with ornaments! Come and have a look. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *pūṇ mulaiyīr* refers to decoration for the soul, manifesting devotion. This is taught lucidly by one’s ācārya \[spiritual teacher\].

We shall next consider the 18<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.
