## 1.2.18. Mannum malaiyum

*maṇṇum malaiyum kadalum ulagēḻumuṇṇum tiṟattu magiḻndu uṇṇum piḷḷaikkuvaṇṇam eḻil koḷ magarak kuḻai ivaitiṇṇam irundavā kāṇīrē sēyiḻaiyīr! vandu kāṇīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṇṇum – earth; malaiyum – mountains; kadalum – oceans; ulagu ēḻum – seven worlds; uṇṇum tiṟattu – with respect to keeping them in the divine stomach; magiḻndu – feeling happy; uṇṇum – keeping in the divine stomach; piḷḷaikku – for the little child; eḻil vaṇṇam koḷ – having a beautiful complexion; magarak kuḻai – divine ear rings; ivai – their; tiṇṇam – sturdiness; irunda A – the way they are; kāṇīr – have a look; sē iḻaiyīr – oh, women who have beautiful ornaments! Come and have a look

**Перевод:**

**emperumān keeps earth, mountains, oceans and all the seven worlds in his divine stomach, with happiness. yaśōdāp pirātti wants the herd-women, who are wearing beautiful ornaments, to come and have a look at the sturdiness of his divine ear rings which have a beautiful complexion.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) After enjoying the beauty of kriṣṇa’s divine eyebrows, āḻvār enjoys his divine ear rings \[could also be taken as divine ears\]*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**maṇṇum …** – to prevent deluge from swallowing earth, which is the support for all, anchoring mountains, which support earth, oceans, which protect earth and all the worlds, emperumān kept them in his divine stomach. He felt happy that he had been able to protect them. For the child \[kriṣṇa\] who kept these as his sustenance… tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that he kept the seven worlds above the earth and seven below the earth in his divine stomach.  For the term *uṇṇum tiṟattu magiḻndu uṇṇaum piḷḷiakku*, he says that emperumān was happy that he was able to protect all the worlds in his divine stomach. His happiness came about because he felt that since their sensory organs have been kept in abeyance during the time that they spend in his divine stomach, the jīvātmas \[all the souls\] would be prevented from indulging in sinful activities.

**vaṇṇam …** – his divine ear rings have a complementary complexion to that of his divine form and due to differences in their shapes, they have a beauty about them. Come and have a look at these divine ear rings which attract the eyes and hearts of those who see them, on account of their sturdiness. Oh women, who have adorned yourselves with beautiful ornaments! Come and have a look at his divine ear-rings. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *sēyiḻai* refers to ornaments for the soul \[knowledge about emperumān, total bliss, being a servitor etc\]

We shall next consider the 19<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.2.19. Murrilum tudaiyum

*muṟṟilum tūdaiyum mun kaimmēl pūvaiyumsiṟṟil iḻaittut tiri taruvōrgaḷaipaṟṟīp paṟittuk koṇḍu ōdum paraman tanneṟṟi irundavā kāṇīrē nēr iḻaiyīr! vandu kāṇīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

siṟu il – small houses \[made of sand\]; iḻaittu – building them; tiri taruvōgraḷai – little girls who roam around; muṟṟilum – small winnow (for sifting sand); tūdaiyum – small pots (for making food, out of sand); mun kai mēl – playing on the forearm; pūvaiyum – bird, myna; paṟṟi – grabbing the hand; paṟittuk koṇḍu – stealing them; ōdum – one who is running; paraman than – lord (of mischievous activities); neṟṟi – divine forehead; irunda A – the way it is; kāṇīr – have a look; nēr iḻaiyīr – oh, women who are wearing eminent ornaments! Come and have a look

**Перевод:**

**While girls in tiruvāyppādi were playing with sand, building houses, using small winnows and small pots, keeping their pet bird, myna, on their forearms, kriṣṇa will grab their hands, steal all these from them and run away. Oh, women who are wearing eminent ornaments! Come and have a look at his divine forehead.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) Subsequent to enjoying the divine ear rings, āḻvār now enjoys kriṣṇa’s divine forehead.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**muṟṟilum …** – little girls in tiruvāyppādi are playing, building small houses with sand, using winnows and small pots. They are also playing with myna birds, their pets, speaking with them.

**paṟṟi …** – kriṣṇa catches their hands, stealing the winnows, pots and myna birds, and runs without getting caught. He is the lord of indulging in misciefs.

**neṟṟī …** – look at the beauty of his divine forehead, on which little droplets of sweat have formed, on account of this exertion. Oh, women, who are donning subtle ornaments, come and have a look at his divine forehead. Subtlety for ornaments comes on account of making them with subtle hands and minds; they are apt for the softness of the women who wear them. In his svāpadēśam, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that the term *nē riḻaiyīr* refers to ornaments which need not be removed even during union. In other words, this term refers to ornament for the soul which deals with subtle knowledge about emperumān.

We shall next consider the 20<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.2.20. Alagiya paimbonnin

*aḻagiya paimbonnin kōl angaik koṇḍukaḻalgaḷ sadangai kalandu engum ārppamaḻa kanṟu inangaḷ maṟittut tirivānkuḻalgaḷ irundavā kāṇīrē kuvi mulaiyīr! vandu kāṇīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aḻagiya – being beautiful; paim ponnin – made of pure gold; kōl – staff; am kai – with beautiful hand; koṇḍu – holding; kaḻalgaḷ – the valorous anklets donned on the divine feet; sadangai – string of small metal bells tied to the divine anklet; kalandu – together; engum ārppa – to make a sound, everywhere; maḻam – youthful; kanṟu inangaḷ – herd of calves; maṟittu – restraining; tirivān – one who roams; kuḻalkgaḷ – divine locks; irunda A – the way they are; kāṇīr – have a look; kuvi mulaiyīr – oh, women, with globular bosoms! Come and have a look

**Перевод:**

**Holding a staff made of pure gold in his divine hand, with the valorous anklets and string of bells which decorate his divine feet making sound everywhere, kriṣṇa will restrain the herd of youthful calves and roam around. Oh, women with globular bosoms! Come and have a look at the divine locks.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) Subsequent to enjoying the beauty of kriṣṇa’s divine forehead, āḻvār enjoys the beauty of his divine locks.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**aḻagiya …** – holding a staff made of pure gold, which looks beautiful to beholders, in his beautiful, divine hands which are such that evil eyes have to be warded off, and his valorous anklets and string of metal bells which he has worn on his divine feet, kriṣṇa restrains the herd of youthful calves, roaming everywhere. Oh, women, with globular bosoms, come and have a look at his divine locks.

**kaḻalgaḷ …** – since he has to run with heavy steps, in order to restrain the calves from running astray, the valorous anklets and the string of bells tied to his divine feet, in a harmonious way, will make sound everywhere. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that the calves which go astray from the herd, will find their way back, from the sound of his anklet and string of bells.

**maḻa kanṟu …** – ensuring that the herds of young calves do not escape from him, by restraining them with the staff in his hand, and roaming with them.

**kuḻalgaḷ …** – just as it has been said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2-6-3 “*neṟitta kuḻalgaḷai nīnga munnōdi …*” (running ahead of the calves such that his dense locks will break into two sides …), since he is running with heavy steps to control the calves, his locks will sway on either side. Have a look at those divine locks. Oh, women, who have rounded bosoms, come and have a look at his divine locks! tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that his divine locks are long. The reason for describing the bosoms of herd-women as *kuvi mulaiyīr* \[being well rounded\] is because bosoms represent devotion towards emperumān and when they are well rounded, the devotion is being nurtured well. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai further explains here that while periyāḻvār enjoys the divine limbs of kriṣṇa, just as nammāḻvār had enjoyed in his tiruvāimoḻi 3-1-1 “*mudiccōdi*” padigam \[ten pāsurams\], nammāḻvār started with emperumān’s divine locks and ended with his divine feet while periyāḻvār started with his divine feet and ended with his divine locks. The reason for periyāḻvār calling the herd-women twice “*kāṇīr*” “*kāṇīr*” \[to come and have a look\] is due to the fact that they \[the herd-women\] knew that their *svarūpam* \[basic nature of ātmā, which is *śēśatvam*, servitude to emperumān\] should be aligned to their *prāpyam* \[end-goal, which is attaining emperumān\] and that their *prāpyam* \[end-goal\] should be aligned to their *svarūpam* \[being a servitor\]. It could also be said that they knew emperumān’s *upēyabhāvam* \[that he is the ultimate goal for them\] and his *upāyabhāvam* \[that he is the means for attaining him\]. Only if periyāḻvār shows this way, would *mangaḷāśāsanam* \[protecting and praising emperumān\] get fulfilled.

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.2.21. Suruppar kulali

*suruppār kuḻali yasōdai munsonnatiruppāda kēsattait ten puduvaip pattanviruppāl uraitta irubadōdu onṟumuraippār pōy vaigundattu onṟuvar tāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

surumbu Ar – beetles settling on; kuḻali – having locks; asōdai – yaśōdāp pirātti; mun – at the time of \[kriṣṇa’s\] incarnation; sonna – told \[the herd-women by calling them\]; tiruppāda kēsattai – describing \[kriṣṇa’s\] limbs from divine foot to divine locks; then puduvai – controller of beautiful villibuttūr (śrīvilliputtūr); pattan – bhattar pirān; viruppāl – with plenty of affection; uraitta – mercifully said; irubadōdu onṟum – all the twenty-one pāsurams; uraippār tām – those who learn; pōy – go (past prakruti maṇḍalam, the region of primordial matter); vaigundattu – in śrī vaikuṇṭam; onṟuvar – will dwell aptly

**Перевод:**

**yaśōdāp pirātti, who has locks on which beetles settle, had called and told herd-women, during the time of kriṣṇa’s incarnation, about his divine limbs. bhattar pirān \[periyāḻvār\], the controller of beautiful śrī villibuttūr, with plenty of affection, had mercifully stated those in twenty-one pāsurams. Those who learn these pāsurams, will go past the region of primordial matter and dwell aptly in śrī vaikuṇṭam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In this last pāsuram, āḻvār mentions the benefit which will accrue to those who learn these pāsurams and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**suruppār kuḻali …** – the word *surumbār* has got transformed as *suruppār*. s*urumbu* – beetles. To imbibe the honey which drip from the flowers donned by yaśōdāp pirātti, beetles settle on her locks. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that she decorated herself with flowers constantly so that kriṣṇa will come to her, without getting angry. Since she was having flowers constantly, beetles were also settling on her hair all the time, to drink the honey from the flowers.

**mun sonna tiruppāda kēsattai** – the divine foot to divine locks, which she had enjoyed during the time of kriṣṇa’s incarnation, and which she showed to others. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as kriṣṇa had incarnated in śrī madurā and shifted to tiruvāyppādi, periyāḻvār too, after his birth in śrī villibuttūr, shifted to the mansion \[nācciyār tirumāḷigai}.

**then …** – mercifully composed, with overflowing affection, by periyāḻvār, a brāhmaṇa and controller of śrī villibuttūr. Here, maṇavāḷa māmunigaḷ, in his vyākhyānam, compares the affection between yaśōdāp pirātti and periyāḻvār towards kriṣṇa.

His affection is not like hers. He had described yaśōdāp pirātti through pāsurams such as (1) 1.2.1 “*kōdaikkuḻalāḷ aśodai*” (2) 1.2.3 “*paṇaittōḷ iḷavāycci*”, (3) 1.2.12 “*maittadam kaṇṇi yasōdai*” etc; he had described kriṣṇa’s divine activities through pāsurams such as (1) 1.2.4 “*uḻandāḷ naṟuney*”, (2) 1.2.9 “*adirum kadalniṟa vaṇṇanai*”, (3) 1.2.15 “*”nōkki yasōdai*” etc; he had described kriṣṇa’s activities which are outside of this incarnation, such as 1.2.5 “*maṟam koḷ mārvai munkīṇḍān*” as well as activities which occurred in the later stages of this incarnation itself, such as (1) 1.2.10 “*irumāmarudam iṟutta ip piḷḷai*”, (2) “*sagadattaic cādippōy vāḷ koḷ vaḷai eyiṟṟu āruyir vavvinān*”. He was able to talk about these divine activities of emperumān since he had been granted knowledge with devotion, without any trace of doubt, by emperumān himself such that all the events which happened even in earlier times and in later times were vividly seen by him.

He enjoyed these events with the same passion with which yaśōdāp pirātti had enjoyed them. Seeing the events just as she had seen and speaking about showing the events to her friends are the features where he shared commonality with yaśōdāp pirātti. Hence, he was able to mercifully mention about “*asōdai mun sonna tiruppādakēsattait tenpuduvaip pattan viruppāl uraitta*”. This feature is applicable to similar events which will be mentioned in the other padigams which will follow this.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *pattan* refers to eminent brāhmaṇa.

**irubadōdu onṟum uraippār** – this would refer to those who are able to recite these with the same pathos with which periyāḻvār had composed them; it would also refer to those who, even if they do not have periyāḻvār’s pathos, could recite them as mere words.

**pōy …** – they will be able to go to śrī vaikuṇṭam and live there without ever separating from there, carrying out *mangaḷāśāsanam* to emperumān, just as it has been mentioned in [tiruppallāṇḍu 12](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/11/thiruppallandu-12-pallandu-enru/) “*sūḻndirundu ēttuvar pallāṇḍu*” (they will carry out *mangaḷāśāsanam* by being with emperumān at all times), enjoying emperumān to completion.

This brings us to the end of the second padigam of first centum.

We shall next consider the pravēśam \[introduction\] of the third tirumoḻi \[decad\].

## 1.3.1. Manikkam katti

*māṇikkam katti vayiram idai kattiāṇip ponnāl seyda vaṇṇac ciṟut tottilpēṇi unakkup piraman vidu tandānmāṇīk kuṟaḷanē tālēlō vaiyam aḷandānē! tālēlō*

**Пословный перевод:**

māṇikkam – rubies (on either side); katti – stringing them; idai – in the centre; vayiram – diamonds; katti – stringing them; āni ponnāl – with pure gold; seyda – made; vaṇṇam – beautiful; siṟu tottil – small cradle; piraman – brahmā; pēṇi – joyously; unakku – to you; vidu tandān – sent; māṇi – as a bachelor; kuṟaḷanē – oh, one who is vāmana \[dwarf form\]; tālēlō – may you sleep well; (tālēlō – tāl + ēl + O; tāl – tongue; ēl and O are metrical syllables. When women lay down their infants in cradle, move their tongues and make a sound to put them to sleep, it is called as tālēlō); vaiyam – all the worlds; aḷandānē – oh, one who measured as trivikrama! tālēlō \[in our translation, we shall use the words “May you go to sleep” to refer to tālēlō)

**Перевод:**

**brahmā, with joy, made and sent for you, a beautiful, small cradle, made of pure gold and embellished on either side with ruby stones and with diamond stones in the centre. Oh, one who incarnated as a dwarf, vāmana, as a bachelor! May you go to sleep. Oh, one who measured all the worlds as trivikrama! May you go to sleep.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) This pāsuram speaks about the servitude carried out by brahmā, the head of all he worlds, appropriate to kriṣṇa’s age.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**māṇikkam …** – embellished on either side with rubies and with diamonds in the middle, with all he gems arranged in a proper manner, brahmā made the little cradle with the purest form of gold, making their colours to complement one anote; it was beautiful, being apt for your age. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that brahmā had embellished diamonds and rest of the nine gems in a proper manner, on a base of gold. brahmā allowed that cradle with happiness. It is said that he had allowed it to be sent. Why did brahmā himself not carry the cradle with him and personally give it to kriṣṇa? Unless they are invited and given honours, it is rare for them to come. For those through whom he had sent the cradle, they could come when they carry the gift. This shows the eminence of their subordinates \[through whom the cradle was sent\] over entities such as brahmā who desire independence \[not being dependent on emperumān\].

**pēṇi …** – with affection, brahmā allowed it \[to be sent\] for you. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *vidu tandān* refers to brahmā removing his ownership over that cradle and letting it to be sent to kriṣṇa.

**māṇi …** – Oh, one who took the form of a dwarf in order to obtain through alms, your own possessions and went seeking alms as a bachelor for whom seeking had become such a habit that scars had formed on your divine form! May you go to sleep. Oh, one who grew up as trivikrama, as an outlet for the happiness of having been given alms, and measured all the worlds! May you go to sleep. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the terms *māṇi* and *kuṟaḷan* refer to smallness in stature. The reason for using both instead of only one of them is to emphasise that emperumān took such a small form that the dwarfs in the world could be termed as being tall. One can feel honourable only till the time that one goes seeking alms. Once the person goes to seek alms, honour disappears first \[emperumān did not mind seeking his possession through alms since he wanted to make his followers to be happy\]. When trivikrama measured the worlds, his divine foot had reached brahmā’s world too. It is due to remembering this act that brahmā sent the gift to kriṣṇa, since that act removed his thought of being independent and reminded him that he is a servitor to emperumān.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.3.2. Udaiyar kanamaniyodu

*udaiyār kanamaṇiyōdu oṇmādaḷam pūidai viravikkōtta eḻil teḻginōduvidaiyēṟu kābāli īsan vidutandānudaiyāi! aḻēl aḻēl tālēlō ulagam aḷandānē! tālēlō*

**Пословный перевод:**

udai Ar – apt for the divine waist; kana maṇiyōdu – with golden bells; idai – in-between; viravi – mixed; kōtta – strung; eḻil – being beautiful; teḻginōdu – with knives; oṇ – beautiful; mādaḷam pū – waist cord with several figurines of flowers; vidai ēṟu – one who has bull as his vehicle; kābāli – one who dons a skull; īsan – one who is the controller of his followers; vidu tandān – sent; udaiyāy – oh, one who has everything!; aḻēl aḻēl – do not cry; do not cry; may you go to sleep; ulagam aḷandānē! – oh, one who measured all the worlds! May you go to sleep

**Перевод:**

**rudra, who has bull as his vehicle, who dons a skull and who is the controller of his followers, sent a waist cord, apt for kriṣṇa’s divine waist, with golden bells, strung in-between with figurines and knife. Oh, one who has everything! Do not cry; do not cry. May you go to sleep. Oh, one who measured all the worlds! May you go to sleep.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) This pāsuram mentions about the servitude carried out by rudra, who is counted next to brahmā in the order of importance and who prides himself as īśvaran \[controller of all\]. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that it was not only this \[referring to the servitude of brahmā\], even rudra sent something to him.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**udai …** – waist-cord, strung with golden bells, with figurines in between and knives, apt for the divine waist. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that apart from gems such as golden bells etc, other materials which are both decorative and splendorous have been strung in that waist cord. *eḻil teḻgu* refers to a beautiful knife which is placed in that waist cord.

**vidai …** – rudran, who has bull as his vehicle, who has skull as his identity and who is the controller of his followers, sent.

**udai …** – even if someone were to say \[claiming some possession as\] “It is mine”, oh, one who has everything including those people \[who had said “It is mine”\] and their possessions! Do not cry; do not cry; may you go to sleep. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that even before these entities had sent those materials as their servitude, emperumān had these entities and he materials sent by them, as his possession.

**ulagam …** – Oh, one who lay claim to everything through your action of measuring all the worlds! May you go to sleep. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when emperumān measured the worlds, none said “Do not step on my head”. If they had known that emperumān was going to step on their heads, they might have stood on their heads.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.3.3. En tambiranar

*en tambirānār eḻil tirumārvarkkucandam aḻagiya tāmarait tāḷarkkuindiran tānum eḻil udaik kiṇkiṇitandu uvanāy ninṟān tālēlō tāmaraik kaṇṇanē tālēlō*

**Пословный перевод:**

en – for me; tambirānār – as svāmy \[lord\]; eḻil – beautiful; tiru mārvarkku – one who has divine chest; aḻagiya candam – having a beautiful complexion; tāmarai tāḷarkku – for you, having lotus-like divine feet; indiran tānum – dēvēndran \[lord of celestial entities\]; eḻil udai – having beauty; kiṇkiṇi – anklet; tandu – proffered; uvanāy ninṟān – stood, neither near nor far. May you go to sleep; tāmaraik kaṇṇanē – oh, one who has lotus-like divine eyes! May you go to sleep

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is my svāmy, having beautiful, divine chest and reddish divine feet with the co,plexion of a lotus flower. indran, who is the head of celestial entities, brought a beautiful anklet, proffered it to you and stood at a distance, which was neither near nor far. May you go to sleep. Oh, one who has lotus-like divine eyes! May you go to sleep.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) This pāsuram mentions the servitude carried out by indran who comes after brahmā and rudran, in the list of prominent entities.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**en tambirānār eḻil tirumārvarkku** – *eḻil* – beauty; the term *en tambirānār* indicates that āḻvār had lost out to kriṣṇa’s divine chest.

**candam …** – one who has divine feet which are like reddish and blossomed lotus flower. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that emperumān’s divine feet are like fresh lotus, apt for the overall beauty of his divine limbs.

**indiran …** – indran, who gains prominence as the lord of three worlds, came and proffered a beautiful anklet, stood at a distance which was neither near nor far, manifesting his humility. May you go to sleep. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the anklet was beautiful and making a \[harmonious\] noise.

**tamarai …** – Oh, one who has divine eyes which are like lotus flower, and with which you shower your mercy on those who carry out servitude to you! May you go to sleep.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.3.4. Sangin valamburiyum

*sangin valamburiyum sēvadik kiṇkiṇiyumangaic carivaḷaiyum nāṇum araittodarumangaṇ visumbil amarargaḷ pōttandārsengatkarumugilē! tālēlō dēvaki singamē! tālēlō*

**Пословный перевод:**

sangil – eminent among the conces; valam puriyum – conch, curved on the right side; sē adi – apt to be adorned on the reddish, divine feet; kiṇkiṇiyum – anklet; am kai – decorative for the beautiful divine hand; sari vaḷaiyum – bracelet on the divine forearm and rings, on the divine shoulders; nāṇum – golden cord, apt to be adorned on the divine chest; arait todarum – cord on the divine waist (all these); am kaṇ – being beautiful and expansive; visumbil – inhabiting worlds such as svargam \[heaven\] etc; amarargaḷ – celestial entities; pōttandār – sent; sem kaṇ – one who has reddish, divine eyes and; karumgilē – oh, one who has the form of a dark cloud! May you go to sleep; dēvaki – one who was born from dēvakip pirātti’s stomach; singamē – oh, one who is like a lion cub! May you go to sleep

**Перевод:**

**Celestial entities who inhabit worlds such as svargam etc, which are beautiful and expansive, sent \[1\] a conch curled on the right side which is the most eminent among conces, \[2\] an anklet which is apt for the reddish, divine feet, \[3\] bracelets which are decorative for the divine forearms and rings, for the divine shoulders, \[4\] golden cord which is apt for the divine chest and \[5\] waist cord. Oh, one who has reddish, divine eyes and who has the form of a dark cloud! May you go to sleep. Oh, one who was born from dēvakip pirātti’s stomach, and who is like a lion cub! May you go to sleep.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) This pāsuram mentions about the servitude carried out by a group of prominent celestial entities, who are under indran. In his svāpadēśam, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says: Is it only this much? \[in continuation of the previous pāsuram where indran had sent his gifts\] All the celestial entities too came with materials in their hands, just as it has been said “rikta pāṇistu nōpēyāt rājānām divatam gurum” (one should not go empty handed when visiting a king or deity or ācārya \[teacher\]). kriṣṇa himself is all of these; hence they went with several gifts.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**sangu …** – conch which is curled on the right side, which is the most eminent among conces and which is full of auspiciousness, anklets which are apt to be adorned on the reddish, divine feet; since the verse is “*sēvadik kiṇkiṇiyum*”, the term *kiṇkiṇi* refers to anklet.

**angaic cari …** – bracelets, which are most apt for the divine forearms and rings for the divine shoulders, cord which is apt to be adorned on the divine chest and string of beads around the waist. Alternatively, since it is together with the *araittodar*, the term *nāṇ* could refer to waist cord.

**angaṇ …** – celestial entities who inhabit beautiful and expansive worlds such as *svargam* etc, sent these materials as their servitude.

**sengaṇ …** – Oh, one who is together with the divine reddish eyes and a dark form which appears like a dark cloud which has blossomed lotus flower, such that your form does not need any decorative ornaments! May you go to sleep.

**dēvaki …** – due to having been born from the stomach of dēvakip pirātti, one who has the arrogance of a lion cub! May you go to sleep. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa is well known as the son of dēvaki. This is also mentioned in vēdas \[mahānārāyaṇōpaniśat\]. The eminence for this is that this has been mercifully mentioned by āḻvār.

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.3.5. Elilar tirumarvukku

*eḻilār tirumārvukku ēṟkum ivai enṟuaḻagiya aimbadaiyum āramum koṇḍuvaḻuvil kodaiyān vaiccirāvaṇantoḻudu uvanāy ninṟān tālēlō tūmaṇi vaṇṇanē! tālēlō*

**Пословный перевод:**

eḻil Ar – “with beauty overflowing; tiru mārvukku – to adorn on the divine chest where pirātti \[śrī mahālakśmi\] resides; ivai ēṟkum – these will be apt”; enṟu – thinking this way; aḻagiya – being beautiful; aimbadaiyum – ornament having replicas of the five divine weapons; āramum – pearl chain; koṇḍu – taking them; vaḻu il – without having any fault; kodaiyān – one who donates; vayiccirāvaṇan – vaiśravaṇan; toḻudiu – performing anjali (to accept these mercifully in the divine mind); uvanāy – stood, neither near nor far; may you go to sleep; tū – being pure; maṇi vaṇṇanē – oh, kaṇṇa, who has the complexion of bluish gemstone! May you go to sleep

**Перевод:**

**One who is magnanimous without any fault, vaiśravaṇan (kubēran), thinking “These ornaments will be apt for the divine chest which is overflowing with beauty and where pirātti is residing” took the beautiful ornament with \[replicas of\] five divine weapons and pearl chain. He stood at a distance, neither too near nor too far, after proffering his gifts. May you go to sleep. Oh kaṇṇa, who has the complexion of pure, bluish gemstone! May you go to sleep.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) This pāsuram mentions the servitude carried out by vaiśravaṇan \[kubēran\], who is the lord of northern direction and who is magnanimous.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**eḻil** … – kriṣṇa’s divine chest was such beautiful that one has to ward off evil eyes from it. Thinking that for such s divine chest, these will be apt …

**aḻagiya …** – the ornament of śrī pancāyudam \[five divine weapons\] which was beautiful, and a pearl chain, just as it has been mentioned in amalanādipirān 9 “*kōla māmaṇi āramum*” (beautiful, eminent chain made with nine gems). tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says here that the pearl chain was apt for the divine neck.

**vaḻuvil** …- vaiśravanan, not having the fault of accepting something in return for giving something or the fault of being reluctant to give. The short syllable in vaiśravaṇan has got lengthened to vaiccirāvaṇan

**toḻudu …** – proffering these, he stood at a distance which was neither near nor far, cupping his palms together in *anjali* pose, beseeching kriṣṇa to accept them. May you go to sleep. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that emperumān is not the entity through whom a task could be accomplished by offering some gift to him. It is only through performing an anjali that he would be pleased.

**tūmaṇi …** – Oh, one who has the form of a faultless blue gemstone, which does not require any ornament! May you go to sleep. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that once vaiśravaṇan performed the anjali, after knowing that emperumān is not one who would be pleased with any other offering, the radiance in emperumān’s divine form was manifested.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.3.6. Odak kadalin

*ōdak kadalil oḷi muttin āramumsādip pavaḷamum sangin valamburiyummādakka enṟu varuṇan vidu tandānsōdic cudar mudiyāy! tālēlō sundarat tōḷanē tālēlō*

**Пословный перевод:**

ōdam – throwing out waves; kadalil – formed in the ocean; oḷi – having radiance; muttin – strung with pearls; āramum – chain, and; sādi – made from high purity; pavaḷamum – coral chain; sandam – being beautiful; sari – bracelet for the forearm; vaḷaiyum – rings for the shoulders; mādakka enṟu – thinking “These are highly valuable and apt”; varuṇan – varuṇadēvan \[lord of ocean and rain\]); vidu tandān – sent; sōdic cudar – oh, one who has a radiant crown! May you go to sleep; sundarat tōḷanē – oh, one who has beautiful shoulders! May you go to sleep

**Перевод:**

**varuṇan, the lord of oceans, sent a chain of pearls which had high radiance, and which had formed in the ocean with agitating waves, another chain made with highly pure corals, beautiful bracelets for the divine forearms and beautiful rings for the divine shoulders, thinking “These are of high value and would be apt \[for kriṣṇa\]” Oh, one who has an effulgent crown! May you go to sleep. Oh, one who has beautiful shoulders! May you go to sleep.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) This pāsuram mentions the servitude carried out by varuṇan, who is the deity of western direction and is the lord of ocean.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**ōdam …** – chain strung with pearls obtained from ocean with agitating waves, along with a chain made with eminent corals, instead of artificial ones, to complement it. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the chain was made with pearls which had resplendence and high quality, obtained from unfathomable ocean which had agitating waves. For *sādip pavaḷamum*, he says that they have been strung in-between the pearls in such a manner that their shadow will fall on the pearls.

**sandac carivaḷaiyum** – beautiful bracelets and rings, apt for the divine hand.

**mādakka …** – varuṇan sent these, which are very expensive, and which “Will be apt for him”.

**sōdi …** – Oh, one who has the effulgent crown, which subtly hints that you are the supreme entity! May you go to sleep. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: “Oh, one who has divine crown which is hinting about your supremacy, manifesting that you are the lord and is resplendent and one who has beautiful divine shoulders apt for that supremacy!”

**sundarat tōḷanē** – Oh, one who has beautiful shoulders such that ornaments are superfluous for them! May you go to sleep.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.3.7. Kanar narundulay

*kānār naṟum tuḻāy kai seyda kaṇṇiyumvānār seḻum sōlaik kaṟpagattin vāsigaiyumtenār malar mēl tirumangai pōttandāḷkōnē! aḻēl aḻēl tālēlō kudandaik kidandānē! tālēlō*

**Пословный перевод:**

tēn Ar – full of honey; malar mēl – dwelling atop a reddish lotus flower; tiru mangai – periya pirāttiyār (śrī mahālakśmi); kān Ar – cultivated in the forest; naṟu tuḻāy – with fragrant, divine tuḷasi; kai seyda – manifesting the handicraft with which it was strung; kaṇṇiyum – garland, and; vān Ar – as if filling up the entire sky; seḻum – full of excellence; sōlai – formed as a garden; kaṟpagattin – strung with kaṟpaga (a celestial tree) flowers; vāsigaiyum – garland for the divine forehead; pōttandāḷ – sent; kōnē – oh, one who is the lord of all!; aḻēl aḻēl – do not cry; do not cry. May you go to sleep; kudandaik kidandānē – oh, one who is mercifully reclining in tirukkudandai (present day kumbakōṇam)! May you go to sleep

**Перевод:**

**periya pirāttiyār, who resides on a reddish lotus flower, which is full of honey, sent a garland which was handcrafted with fragrant tuḷasi, cultivated in the forest and garland for the divine forehead made from kaṟpaga flowers, which had been plucked from kaṟpaga trees which had grown in a garden filling up the entire sky. Oh, one who is the supreme entity! Do not cry; do not cry. May you go to sleep. Oh, one who is mercifully reclining in tirukkudandai! May you go to sleep.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) This pāsuram mentions about the gift sent by pirāttiyār, the prominent among his divine consorts.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kānār …** – garland made by handcrafting tuḷasi which had grown in its fertile land, due to which it was flourishing and fragrant.

**vānār …** – garland for the divine forehead strung with *karpaga* flowers which had grown in a tree that had filled up the entire sky as if it were a garden. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that though there were many *kaṟpaga* trees in the ethereal region, each tree appeared as if it were a garden by itself.

**tēnār …**– the garlands were sent by periya pirāttiyār who dwells on the lotus flower from which honey will never stop dripping. She is always with the age of *yuvatiśca kumāriṇi* (about 16, between the stages of adolescent and adult). tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that whatever periya pirāttiyār sends is *aprākrutam* \[not seen in samsāram, the materialistic realm\]. She sends them through entities who are also *aprākrutar* \[those who do not dwell in samsāram\].

**kōnē …** – Oh, one who is the lord of everyone such that everyone desires to carry out servitude to you! Do not cry; do not cry. May you go to sleep. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: Oh, one who is the controller of both vibhūti \[nitya vibhūti, the spiritualistic realm and samsāram, the materialistic realm\]! This implies that he is the head of the clan of herd-folk.

**kudandai …**– Oh, one who is mercifully reclining in tirukkudandai, to manifest a simplicity which is the exact opposite of the eminence which was just seen! May you go to sleep. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that by reclining in the third vibhūti \[divyadēsam or divine abode\] he administers the other two vibhūtis.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.3.8. Kaccodu porcurigai

*kaccodu poṟcurigai kāmbu kanaga vaḷaiuccimaṇic cutti oṇṭhāḷ nirap poṟpūaccudanukku enṟu avaniyāḷ pōttandāḷnaccu mulai uṇḍāy! tālēlō nārayaṇā! aḻēl tālēlō*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaccodu – along with kaccu (a cloth) which is donned over the divine waist cloth; pon – attractive; curigai – knife; kāmbu – a type of sari, with short border and figurines; kanagam – made of gold; vaḷai – rings for the divine shoulders; ucci – apt to be adorned on the divine crown; maṇi – embellished with rubies; cutti – the ornament which is adorned on the divine forehead; oṇ tāḷ – having a shiny stalk; nirai – properly set; pon pū – golden flower; accudanakku enṟu – saying “for one who does not let go of anyone”; avaniyāḷ – śri bhūmip pirātti; pōttandāḷ – sent; nanju – applied with poison (on pūtanā’s bosom); uṇḍāy – oh, one who consumed! May you go to sleep; nārāyaṇa! aḻēl – Oh, nārāyaṇa! Do not cry. May you go to sleep

**Перевод:**

**śrī bhūmip pirātti sent the divine cloth which is worn on top of the dress which is worn on the divine waist, an attractive knife, a sari with narrow border, golden rings for the divine shoulders, cutti, an ornament which is worn on the divine forehead, a golden flower with a shiny stalk which is adorned on the divine crown, for the one who does not let go of others. Oh, one who consumed the poisoned bosom of pūtanā! May you go to sleep. Oh, nārāyaṇa! Do not cry. May you go to sleep.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) This pāsuram mentions about the gift sent by śrī bhūmip pirātti who is reckoned as next only to periya pirāttiyār.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kaccodu …** – along with the dress which is worn over the dress which adorns the divine waist and a knife which can be inserted in that dress, sari with short border carrying patterns, golden rings which are applied to the divine shoulders, *cutti*, an ornament for the forehead, which is embellished with rubies, golden flowers with stalks, which is adorned on the divine crown. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that the term *oṇḍāḷ niraippoṟpū* refers to the beautiful golden flower apt to be adorned properly on the divine feet; alternatively, it could refer to a flower with a stalk. If the text were *oṇḍār* (instead of *oṇḍāḷ*), it would refer to the golden flower with a stalk, apt to be adorned properly on the divine crown.

**accudan** **…** – śrī bhūmip pirātti sent these gifts for *acyutan*, one who will never let go of his followers. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *accudan* refers to one who does not let go of his follower; one who does not let go of his eminence.

**naccu mulai …** – Oh, one who consumed the poisoned bosom of pūtnā, in order to annihilate her, as the starting point of reducing the load on earth! May you go to sleep.

**nārāyaṇā …** – Oh, one who has the divine name of nārāyaṇa, which is symbolic of your being the lord of both vibhūtis, such that people in both the vibhūtis would carry out servitude!  Do not cry. May you go to sleep. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that it is because he is nārāyaṇa that entities such as brahmā, īśan \[rudra\] et al came and carried out servitude.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.3.9. Mey timirum

*mey timirum nānap podiyōdu manjaḷumseyya tadam kaṇṇukku anjanamum sinduramamveyya kalaippāgi koṇḍu uvaḷāy ninṟāḷayyā! aḻēl aḻēl tālēlō arangattu aṇaiyānē! tālēlō*

**Пословный перевод:**

mey – on the divine form; timirum – apt to be applied; nānap podiyōdu – along with fragrant powders such as musk, medicated camphor, sandalwood powder etc; manjaḷum – turmeric powder too; seyya – being reddish; tadam – being expansive; kaṇṇukku – apt to be applied on the divine eyes; anjanamum – black pigment and; sinduramum – vermillion too; veyya – cruel; kalai – male deer; pāgi – durgai, who has as her vehicle; koṇḍu – taking these; uvaḷāy ninṟāḷ – stood, neither near nor far; ayyā! – oh, one who is the lord! Do not cry; do not cry. May you go to sleep; arangattu aṇaiyānē! – oh, one who is reclining on the serpent mattress! May you go to sleep

**Перевод:**

**durgai, who has a cruel male deer as her vehicle, took a mix of powders made of musk, medicated camphor and sandalwood powder, apt to be applied on the divine form \[of kriṣṇa\], along with turmeric powder, as well as black pigment for the reddish, expansive divine eyes and vermillion, for the divine forehead. After proffering these, she stood neither near nor far. Oh, one who is the lord! Do not cry; do not cry. May you go to sleep. Oh, one who is reclining on the serpent mattress at śrīrangam! May you go to sleep.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) This pāsuram mentions the servitude carried out, with affection, by durgai, who was born during the time of incarnation of kriṣṇa, protecting him at the time of his birth \[by exchanging places with him\], as a result of which she was different from all the other entities mentioned this far.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**mey …** – apt to be applied on the divine form \[of kriṣṇa\], to a mixture of musk, sandalwood powder and medicated camphor, turmeric powder was added to provide the desired colour; black pigment, apt to be applied to the divine eyes which are reddish, expansive and extending to the ears and vermillion, apt to be applied on the divine forehead.

**veyya …** – durgai, who has a cruel male deer as her vehicle, brought all these, and stood at a distance, neither far nor near. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says here that this term \[*kalaippāgi*\] refers to sarasvati, who has arts, which are the cause of *svātantryam* \[being independent of emperumān\], under her control. The term *vemmai* refers to *svātantryam*. Alternatively, this verse could refer to durgai, who has a cruel male deer as her vehicle. Here, *vemmai* refers to being cruel.

**ayyā …** – Oh, one who is the lord of all! Do not cry. May you go to sleep.

**arangattu …** – Oh, one who is reclining mercifully on the serpent mattress in kōyil \[in our sampradāyam, the term *kōyil* refers to śrīrangam\], in order to carry out that lordship! May you go to sleep. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that śrīrangam is the origin of all incarnations and emperumān is reclining mercifully here, just as it has been mentioned in [mūnṟām tiruvandādi pāsuram 62](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/05/munram-thiruvandhadhi-62/) “*tēnār tiruvarangam tenkōtti*”(śrīrangam which is surrounded by gardens with overflowing honey, tirukkōttiyūr etc are divine abodes of emperumān\].

Alternatively, for *veyya kalaippāgi*, since the term *vemmai* refers to desire, this verse \[*veyya kalaippāgi*\] would refer to sarasvati \[deity for arts and education\] having attractive arts in her tongue and controlling them. Earlier \[in the very first pāsuram of this decad\], brahmā was mentioned as the servitor. Now, his primary consort, sarasvati, is mentioned as carrying out servitude. In line with this, the meanings of the verses will undergo a change.

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.3.10. Vanjanaiyal vanda

*vanjanaiyāl vanda pēycci mulai uṇḍaanjana vaṇṇanai āycci tālāttiyasenjol maṟaiyavar sēr puduvaip pattan solenjāmai vallavarkku illai idar tānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vanjanaiyāl vanda – coming in the form of mother, hiding her \[original\] fiendish form; pēycci – pūtanā’s; mulai – bosom; uṇḍa – one who consumed such that her life perished; anjana vaṇṇanai – kaṇṇan, who has a dark form; āycci – yaśōdāp pirātti, the mother; tāl āttiya – the manner in which she sang the lullabies; sem sol – having eminent words; maṟaiyavar – those who have vēdams \[sacred texts\] as their identity; sēr – residing together; puduvai – one who incarnated in śrī villibuttūr; pattan – mercifully composed by periyāḻvār, the eminent among brāhmaṇas; sol – pāsurams; enjāmai – without any shortcoming; vallavarkku – those who are capable of reciting; idardān – distress; illai – is not there

**Перевод:**

**yaśōdāp pirātti sang lullabies to put to sleep kaṇṇan, who consumed the \[milk from\] bosom of pūtanā such that she perished, and who has a dark, divine form. periyāḻvār, who incarnated in śrī villibuttūr, and who is the most eminent among brāhmaṇas, who have vēdams, which have eminent words, as their identity and living together in śrī villibuttūr, composed those lullabies mercifully into pāsurams. Those who are capable of reciting these pāsurams, without any shortcoming, will not have any distress.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In this last pāsuram, āḻvār mentions the benefits which will accrue to those who learn this decad and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vanjanai …** – just as it has been said in [periya tirumoḻi 1-5-6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/04/periya-thirumozhi-1-5-6/) “*tāyāy vanda pēy*” (the fiend who came as mother), pūtanā came, hiding her fiendish form and came in the form of yaśōdāp pirātti, kriṣṇa’s mother. Just as she came as a mother, kriṣṇa too, like her son, drank milk from her bosom such that she perished.

**anjana vaṇṇanai** – this verse mentions about the radiance which came to his divine form, on knowing that the enemy \[of his followers\] \[pūtanā\] has been annihilated.

**āycci …** – the manner in which yaśōdāp pirātti, his mother, sang lullabies.

**senjol …** – since those who live in śrī villibuttūr speak only truth, they have vēdams, which speak only truth, as their identity. periyāḻvār, who is the leader of brāhmaṇas in śrī villibuttūr, mercifully composed \[yaśōdāp pirātti’s words into\] pāsurams. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that after periyāḻvār had established the true supreme being, all the meanings in vēdams, which were hitherto hidden, became clear to the brāhmaṇas residing in śrī villibuttūr, as a result of which they entered the divine mind of periyāḻvār. For this reason, they are referred to as *senjol maṟaiyavar*. He further says that *pattan sol* refers to the words of a favourable person.

**enjāmai …** – there is no distress for those who are capable of reciting these pāsurams, without any shortcoming. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that for those who are capable of reciting these pāsurams with the pathos of periyāḻvār, there is no distress. Instead of saying *idar illai*, āḻvār says *illai idar*, similar to saying *druśtā sītā* (saw sītā, as revealed by hanuman to śrī rāma) and *na ma*: (not mine, as mentioned in ntirumantram). i*dar* refers to not taking refuge under periyāḻvār’s affection. Since that *idar* will disappear on its own, he says *illai idar*.

We shall next consider the pravēśam of next tirumoḻi.

## 1.4.1. Tan mugattu

*tan mugattuc cutti tūngat tūngat tavaḻndu pōypon mugak kiṇkiṇi ārppap puḻudi aḷaiginṟānen magan gōvindan kūttinai iḷamāmadi!nin mugam kaṇ uḷavāgil nī ingē nōkkippō*

**Пословный перевод:**

than mugattau – on his face (shining); cutti – ornament cutti \[worn from head, hanging on the divine forehead\]; tūngat tūnga – swaying many times over; pon mugam – having a beautiful face; kiṇkiṇi – chain on the divine waist; ārppa – to make a sound \[like kaṇa kaṇa\]; tavaḻndu pōy – crawling; puḻudi – dirt on the floor; aḷaiginṟān – he is playing with; en magan – my son; gōvindan – gōvindan’s; kūttinai – beautiful activities; mā – to a great extent; iḷam – being youthful; madī! – oh, candran!; nin mugam – on your face; kaṇ – eyes; uḷa āgil – if they are present; nī ingē nōkkip pō – look here and proceed

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa is crawling, with the ornament on his face, cutti, swaying from side to side, repeatedly and the chain on the divine waist making a sound. He is playing with dirt on the floor. Oh candran, who is youthful! If you have eyes on your face, look in this direction, at the activities of my son, gōvindan, before proceeding.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, says in his svāpadēśam: when yaśōdāp pirātti told kriṣṇa “I will get you ambuliyammān \[candran\]” and took him to the courtyard, he saw the dirt there. He indulges in activities such as playing in that dirt, asking for candran, remembering that yaśōdāp pirātti had told him that. āḻvār mercifully recounts these activities in this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**than mugam …** – kriṣṇa’s divine face, even without any decoration is such that people will have to perform *ālatti* to ward off evil eyes \[*ālatti* is a practice, performed to ward off evil eyes\]. A beautiful ornament, *cutti*, is hanging on his forehead, with one end tied to his divine hair. As he crawls, the ornament, due to the movement of the hair on his head, is swaying repeatedly. The ornament, tied to his waist and hanging up to his divine ankles, is making a noise. With all these, he is playing with dirt \[in the courtyard\]. *pon mugak kiṇkiṇi* could also refer to the anklets, adorned on the divine ankles. When he crawls, these would be lot of making noise.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that with the *cutti* swaying on his forehead, and the *kiṇkiṇi* adorned on the divine waist making a noise as kriṣṇa crawls, seeing kriṣṇa playing with mud, yaśōdāp pirātti, feeling affectionate towards him, tells candran to look at this, if he had been provided with eyes on his face. Since candran is not looking in kriṣṇa’s direction, she says that he is not looking because of his childishness. Just as it has been said in [tiruvāimoḻi 6-2-8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/11/thiruvaimozhi-6-2-8-pinakki-yavaiyum/) ”*kadir jñāna mūrttiyanāy*” (Oh, one who has your form, the knowledge of carrying out your will!) and in [tiruvāimoḻi 6-2-5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/11/thiruvaimozhi-6-2-5-kazharel-nambi/) “*unakku onṟu uṇarttuvan nān*” (I wish to tell you something; please listen), since the knowledge available both in *nitya vibhūti* (spiritualistic realm) and in *tritīyā vibhūti* (a third divine abode) are under his \[periyāḻvār’s\] control, he is calling that and indicating that to kriṣṇa. The term “calling here” refers to the activities taking place there, which he is able to see in his divine mind, and informing that to kriṣṇa. Alternatively, this would refer to the activities indulged in by kriṣṇa, true to his having incarnated in human species, which āḻvār celebrates through his pāsurams.

**en magan …** – the activity of my son, gōvindan, which steals the mind

**iḷa mā madi** – Oh, ignorant candran, who, instead of stopping in order to see these divine activities, are proceeding on your journey! The term *iḷa māmadi* refers to candran who is young.

**nin mugam …** – if you have eyes on your face, to realise the benefit of having been provided with eyes, see in this direction and then proceed.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.4.2. En sirukkuttan

*en siṟukkuttan enakkōr innamudu empirāntan siṟuk kaikaḷāl kātti kātti aḻaikkinṟānanjanavaṇṇanōdu ādal āda uṟudiyēlmanjil maṟaiyādē māmadī! magiḻndu ōdi vā*

**Пословный перевод:**

enakku – to me; ōr – unique; in amudu – like sweet nectar; em pirān – as my benefactor; en siṟuk kuttan – my little child; than – his; siṟu kaikaḷāl – little hands; kāttik kātti – repeatedly pointing out to you; aḻaikkinṟān – is calling; anjana vaṇṇanōdu – with this little boy, who has a dark form; ādal Ada – to play; uṟudiyēl – if you consider; mā – one who is eminent in terms of coolness and greatness; madī – oh, candra!; magiḻndu – manifesting your happiness; ōdi vā – come fast

**Перевод:**

**This little child, who is my unique, sweet nectar and who is my benefactor, is calling out to you repeatedly, with his little hands. If you consider to play with him. who has a dark, divine form, oh, candra, having eminence in terms of your coolness and greatness! Come fast.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram. pāsuram*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**en siṟukkuttan** – my little child

**enakkōr innamudu** – through his age and his activities, he is a unique, sweet nectar. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that this differentiates from the other nectar \[which was distributed among the celestial entities for immortality\]

**empirān** – he is my benefactor, having been born as my son and through making me enjoy his divine activities. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that he is my benefactor since he incarnated as my son, removing my barrenness.

**than …** – he is calling you repeatedly, with the little hands, which are apt for his age.

**anjanam …** – if you wish to play with him, who is having the divine complexion of darkness like a dark pigment, which is invigorating to his beholders…

**manjil …** – do not hide yourself behind clouds. Oh, candra, who is famous for your form and coolness! Come fast, with joy, displaying your affection, saying “It is my fortune that I have been invited”. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that in the previous pāsuram, āḻvār had referred to candran as *iḷa madi*; here, he is referring to him as *māmadi*, manifesting the growth in his form over time. āḻvār tells candran to come running joyously, just as one goes with joy in desirous matters.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.4.3. Surrum olivattam

*suṟṟum oḷivattam sūḻndu sōdi parandu engumettanai seyyilum en magan mugam nēr ovvāyvittagan vēngadavāṇan unnai viḷikkinṟakaittalam nōvāmē ambulee! kadidu ōdi vā*

**Пословный перевод:**

ambulee – oh, candran!; oḷi – having splendour; vattam – region; suṟṟum – on all the four sides; sūḻndu – whirling; engum – in all directions; sōdi – with radiance\|; parandu – pervading; ettanai seyyilum – even if everything is done; en magan – my son’s; mugam – for the divine face; nēr ovvāy – you will not be a match; vittagan – one who is amazing; vēngadam – in the divine abode of tirumalai; vāṇan – one who has mercifully taken residence; unnai – you; viḷikkinṟa – calling, joyously; kai talam – divine hand; nōvāmē – such that it does not pain; kadidu – immediately; ōdi vā – come running

**Перевод:**

**Oh, candran! Even if your radiance swirls around in all the four directions and pervades everywhere, you will not match the divine face of my son. One, who is amazing and has mercifully taken residence in tiruvēngadam is calling you. Come fast, running, such that his divine hand does not pain.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says in his svāpadēśam that candran’s coolness is not a match for the coolness on the child’s face.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**suṟṟum …** – even if the region, which has splendour, swirls on all the sides, without any reduction in its intensity, and without any blemish, pervades everywhere… tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that even if candran travels at a height, in the sky

**en magan …** – you will not be a match in any way for the splendour and perfectly circular face of my son. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that candran will not match the coolness and cheerfulness on kriṣṇa’s face.

**vittagan …** – being amazing in his beauty and auspicious qualities, disregarding proud entities such as you, respecting forests and monkeys just as it has been mentioned in [nānmugan tiruvandādi 47](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-47/) “*kānamum vānaramum…*” (desiring forests and monkeys…), he resides mercifully in tiruvēngadam. Oh, ambulee! Come running, fast, such that the hand which is beckoning you, does not pain. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *vittagan* refers to kriṣṇa’s capability and being the reason for everything. For the term *vēngadavāṇan* he says that he is the easily approachable entity who has taken residence in tirumalai. He further says that giving respect to forest and monkeys, and disregarding you \[referring to candran\], kriṣṇa is not speaking anything. Even after such an entity calls you, you are not coming.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.4.4. Cakkarak kaiyan

*cakkarak kaiyan tadam kaṇṇal malara viḻittuokkalai mēl irundu unnaiyē cuttik kāttum kāṇṭhakkadu aṟidiyēl candirā! salam seyyādēmakkaḷ peṟāda maladan allaiyēn vā kaṇḍāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

candirā! – oh, candran!; cakkaram – divine disc; kaiyan – one who has in his divine hand; tadam – extending up to the ears; kaṇṇāl – with divine eyes; malara viḻittu – seeing widely; okkalai mēl irundu – sitting on my waist; unnaiyē – only you; cutti kāttum kāṇ – will point at, you could see; takkadu – apt for you; aṟidiyēl – if you understand; salam seyyādē – do not deceive; makkaḷ peṟāda – not having sired children; maladan – barren; allaiyēl – if you aren’t; vā kaṇḍāy – come and stand here

**Перевод:**

**Oh, candran! Having the divine disc on his divine had, looking with wide eyes, sitting on my waist, kriṣṇa is pointing at you only. If you know as to what is apt for you, do not indulge in deceptive acts. If you aren’t a barren person, not having sired children, come at once and stand here.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**cakkarak kaiyan** – he has in his divine hands, the divine disc, just as it has been said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10-6-8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/02/thiruvaimozhi-10-6-8-meynninru/) “*karudumidam porudu*” (proceeding to the place which emperumān thinks of). The implied meaning here is – if you do not come, he has the necessary implement to punish you.

**tdam kaṇ …** – looking at you, affectionately, with his divine eyes which have enough space.

**okkalai mēl irundu** – from my waist

**unnai …** – only pointing at you, without looking at anything else

**takkadu aṟidiyēl** – if you know as to what is proper for you. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that the purpose of having been provided with eyes is only to look at kriṣṇa.

**candirā salam seyyādē** – you, who are cool towards everyone else, do not indulge in deceptive act towards him.

**makkaḷ …** – if you aren’t barren, who has not given birth to a child, come at once and stand here. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here – if you are not barren or a eunuch, come. It appears that even those who have sired only one child could be termed as barren \[candran has only one son, *budan*, mercury\].

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.4.5. Alagiya vayil

*aḻagiya vāyil amuda ūral teḷivuṟāmaḻalai muṟṟāda iḷam sollāl unnaik kūvuginṟānkuḻagan sirīdaran kūvak kūva nī pōdiyēlpuḻaiyila āgādē nin sevi pugar māmadī!*

**Пословный перевод:**

pugar – radiance and; mā – having generosity; madī – oh, candran!; aḻagiya – beautiful; vāyil – in the divine mouth; Ural – secreting; amudam – along with saliva, which is like nectar; teḷivu uṟā – without clarity; maḻalai – gibberish; muṟṟāda – not matured enough; iḷam sollāl – with tender words; unnai – you; kūvuginṟān – is calling; kuḻagan – one, who is with all; sirīdaran – he, who is having pirātti \[śrī mahālakśmi\] on his divine chest; kūvak kūva – even as he calls repeatedly; nī pōdiyēl – if you keep going; nin sevi – your ears; puḻai ila – being without holes; āgādē – will they not be?

**Перевод:**

**Oh, candran who has radiance and generosity! kriṣṇa, with saliva, which is like nectar, secreting from his divine mouth, is calling you with gibberish, tender words which are not clear and which are not matured. Even as he is calling you many times, if you keep going, will it not tantamount to saying that your ears are without holes?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**aḻagiya …** – with saliva, which is like nectar, secreting from his divine mouth, kriṣṇa is calling you with gibberish, tender words, which are not matured and which lack clarity.

**kuḻagan …** – he is one who mixes with people, such as those who gave him their bosoms to feed him and those who carried him, aptly going with them.

**sirīdaran** – he has an eminence which is the exact opposite of the simplicity mentioned just now. *śrīdaratvam* (quality of having śrī mahālakśmi) is symbolic of supremacy.

**kūvakkūva nī pōdiyēl** – Even as he is calling you many times, if you keep going, as if you did not hear him…

**puḻai …** – will it not be considered that your ears lack holes in them? *puḻai* – hole. It will be tantamount to saying that there is no purpose to your sense of hearing.

**pugar māmadī** – is this apt for your radiance and your eminence? tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says in his svāpadēśam – isn’t your radiance famous throughout the world?

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.4.6. Tandodu cakkaram

*taṇḍodu cakkaram ēndum tadakkaiyankaṇ tuyil koḷḷak karudik kottāvi koḷginṟānuṇḍa mulaippāl aṟa kaṇḍāy uṟangāvidilviṇ tanil manniya māmadī! viraindōdi vā*

**Пословный перевод:**

viṇ tanil – in the sky; manniya – being present; māmadī! – oh, candran, who has eminence in your form!; taṇḍodu – along with the mace (called as kaumōdaki); cakkaram – divine disc and; sārngam – bow (called as śrī śārngam); ēndum – one who is holding; tadam – expansive; kaiyan – he, who has divine hands; kaṇ tuyil koḷḷa – to recline; karudi – considering; kottāvi koḷginṟān – \[he\] is yawning; uṟangāvidil – if he does not rest; uṇḍa – consumed; mulai pāl – milk from bosom; aṟā kaṇḍāy – will not digest, you see. (Hence, you); viraindu – hurriedly; ōdi vā – come running

**Перевод:**

**Oh, candran, who is present in the sky! kriṣṇa, who is holding the divine mace, the divine disc and the divine bow, is yawning, since he is considering to take rest. If he does not take rest, the bosom milk, which he has consumed, will not get digested. Hence, you come running, immediately.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**taṇḍu …** – mentioning mace, disc and bow is symbolic of the other two divine weapons too \[divine conch and divine sword\].

**ēndum tdakkaiyan** – he has divine hands with which he holds these weapons, all the time, as if he were holding flowers. These will be part of his weapons as well as his decorative ornaments \[for the favourable devotees, they will be ornaments and for the unfavourable enemies, they will be weapons\]. With this, āḻvār tells candran that instead of enjoying this beauty and continuing to live, do not become a target of their \[divine weapons’\] valour and perish. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that usage of the term *ēndum* \[holding\] indicates that the divine weapons are being held like flowers.

**kaṇ tuyil …** – considering that he should take rest, as a hint to that, he is letting out a yawn. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that sleep, which disturbs the considerations of everyone, is under his \[kriṣṇa’s\] control. His activities are all like this only \[whatever impacts the rest will have no impact on him\].

**uṇḍa …** – Note that if he does not take rest, the bosom milk consumed will not get digested. Hence …

Here, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says: If you \[referring to candran\] think “Until I come, could he not remain awake?” understand that when a child has consumed bosom milk, the child has to sleep for the milk to get digested. Here, digestion refers to a change of state. When samsāris \[those who dwell in the materialistic realm\] do not carry out his orders and live as they like, emperumān considers that as a loss and loses his desire. Hence, he decides “Let them lie in inactive state \[just as they are, during deluge\]” and changes their state from one of being active to one of being inactive. Sleep refers to his state of not having to support anyone when the samsāris are engaged in their worldly engagements. Does emperumān eat \[for the food to get digested\]?  śvētāśvatara upaniśat says that emperumān does not eat; when that is the case, how could he consume bosom milk here? In [śrī bhagavat gītā 9-26](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/9-26/), emperumān had said “*aśnāmi*” (I eat). If anything is offered to him with devotion and affection, he will take that \[just as he takes when yaśōdāp pirātti gives him her milk with affection\].

**viṇ tanil manniya māmadī viraindōdi vā** – Oh candran, who has the eminence of being in a high place!  In line with your high level of inhabitation and completeness, come fast. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: just as emperumān has given the samsāris sensory organs to let us enjoy worldly pleasures, āḻvār is calling those who are in *tripādvibhūti* \[śrīvaikuṇṭam or nitya vibhūti which is three times as large as leelā vibhūti\] to come and enjoy kriṣṇa’s enjoyable activities in leelā vibhūti. The term *māmadi* refers to *bhakti* \[devotion\]. Devotion is matured state of *jñānam* \[devotion\]. Hence, āḻvār calls people with devotion to come and see kriṣṇa’s activities. Would devotion refer to knowledge? In śrīrangam, during rāmānujar’s time, people such as embār would refer to piḷḷai uṟangāvilli dāsar as *māmadigaḷ* due to his devotion towards rāmānujar. Why is āḻvār calling people with the singular number *māmadi* \[when it should have been in plural number *māmadiyīr*\]? This is because he is calling a group of people and there is a rule  known as *jātyēkavacanam*, in which, a word, to refer to a group, is used in singular number.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.4.7. Palagan enru

*pālagan enṟu paribavam seyyēl paṇḍoru nāḷālin ilai vaḷarnda siṟukkan avan ivanmēl eḻap pāyndu pidittuk koḷḷum veguḷumēlmālai madiyādē māmadī! magiḻndōdi vā*

**Пословный перевод:**

māmadī! – oh, candran who is dignified!; pālagn enṟu – thinking “He is a little child”; paribavam – contempt; seyyēl – do not indulge in; paṇḍu oru nāḷ – at an earlier point in time; ālin ilai – on a tender banyan leaf; vaḷarnda – one who reclined; siṟukkan avan – one who was a little child; ivan – understand that it is this child; veguḷum ēl – if (he} becomes furious; mēl eḻap pāyndu – jumping up; pidittuk koḷḷum – he will catch (you). (hence); mālai – in matters regarding an eminent person; madiyādē – without being indifferent; magiḻndu – come joyously (thinking “How fortunate are we to be called by him!”)

**Перевод:**

**Oh, candran, who is dignified! Do not think contemptuously that “He is a little child”. He is the same child who, at an earlier point in time, reclined on a tender leaf. If he were to become furious, he will jump up and catch you. Without being indifferent towards an eminent entity like this, come with joy, at once.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) As kriṣṇa considered to sleep, he realised that yaśōdāp pirātti had told him that she will get him candran and asks her again to get him candran. After calling candran several times, since he did not come, she tells him that kriṣṇa will get angry and asks him to come soon.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**pālagan …** – do not make the mistake of being contemptuous, thinking “He is, but a little child”. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: do not get distressed by followers of viṣṇu, after thinking “He is, but a child”. At many places, he had removed insults heaped on you. Even if he incarnates in a lowly form in any birth, he is such an eminent entity that brahmā, īśan et al, who you worship, will have to come hurriedly, if he were to beckon them.

**paṇḍu oru …** – realise that he is the same entity who, at an earlier point in time, had kept in his divine stomach, all the worlds and reclined on a tender banyan leaf. This underlines the fact that he has the capability of carrying out *aghatitaghatanā* (ability to bind together entities which can never be bound together).

**mēl eḻa …**– if he were to become furious, he is capable of jumping up and catching you. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that this child, should he get angry, would jump above you and catch hold of you. There is no doubt in this. Just as tirumangai āḻvār had mercifully said in [tirunedundāṇḍagam pāsuram 5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thirunedunthandakam-5/) “*oṇmidi…*”, when emperumān took the form of trivikrama, he had stepped on the heads of all entities. If his foot could touch you, vouldn’t the hand!

**mālai ,,,** – Oh, candran, who is eminent! Do not underestimate an eminent entity as a little child.  In line with your eminence, come immediately, manifesting your joy that “We have been fortunate to be beckoned by him”. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: instead of looking at his infatuation \[for you\], thinking “Since I am carrying out the orders of emperumān \[in travelling around the skies providing light and coolness to the people of the world\], I will come a bit later”, in line with his infatuation, come immediately, manifesting the joy “We have been fortunate to be beckoned by him”.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.4.8. Siriyan enru

*siṟīyan enṟu en iḷam singattai igaḻēl kaṇḍāysiṟumaiyin vārttaiyai māvali idaic cenṟu kēḷsiṟumaip piḻai koḷḷil nīyum un tēvaikku uriyai kāṇniṟaimadī! nedumāl viraindu unnaik kūvuginṟān*

**Пословный перевод:**

niṟai madī! – Oh, candran, who is complete!; en – my; iḷam singattai – son, who is like a lion cub; siṟiyan enṟu – saying, a little child; igaḻēl kaṇḍāy – do not be derisive; siṟumaiyin – regarding his child-like form; vārttaiyai – distinguished activities \[as vāmana\]; māvali idai – with mahābali; senṟu kēḷ – go and ask; siṟumai – thinking mean (in such an entity’s matter); piḻai koḷḷil – if you think that it is an offence (then); nīyum – you too; un tēvaikku – servitude towards him; uriyai kāṇ – you would qualify; nedumāl – he, who is the lord of all; viraindu – with an urge; unnai – you; kūvuginṟān – is calling you

**Перевод:**

**Oh, candran, who is complete! Do not be derisive towards my son who is like a lion cub. Go to mahābali and listen to him about kriṣṇa’s activities as a child. If you think that thinking mean about kriṣṇa is an offence, then you too would qualify to be his servitor. He, who is the lord of all, is calling you with an urge.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**siṟiya …** – Do not think about my son, who is like a lion cub in his valour and pride, despicably, by looking at his age and considering him as “a little child”. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam: candran has a doubt – “Are you thinking whether anyone, who is a child, had jumped up before?” In that case, you have not heard about the eminence of his \[kriṣṇa’s\] small form. mahābali has got rid of his pride of being magnanimous, which he had got due to his pathos of carrying out his deeds constantly, and is now in the pathos of meditating about the supreme being, in the nether world. You could go there and listen to him. Do not despise my little child who is like a lion cub.

**saiṟumai …** – go to mahābali and hear from him about the distinguishing activity of my son, who went to mahābali as vāmana, seeking three seps of land, charmed him, measured all the worlds with two steps and imprisoned him with the third.

**siṟimai\[piḻai koḷḷil\] …** – if you realise that it was an offence thinking lowly about such an entity, then you would also qualify for carrying out servitude towards him. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here – If you \[referring to candran\] consider that “emperumān had to go in the form of vāmana \[dwarf form\] because of our offences, due to our pride”. If you think “Am I too required?” realise that for you too, being dependent on emperumān, while carrying out your duty \[of rising in the evening and setting in the morning\] which has been ordained, even that has been done through emperumān’s divine mind.

**niṟai …** – Oh, candran who is complete! He, who is the lord of all, is calling you, with an urgency. The opinion here is that in line with his quality of being complete, candran should come at once. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: āren’t you one with full knowledge? Is there anything which you do not know about duty ordained through his divine mind? Just as it has been said in taittirīya upaniśat śīkśāvalli that various celestial entities such as *vāyu* \[wind\], *sūrya* \[sun\], *agni* \[fire\], indra et al carry out their duties out of fear of emperumān, one has to carry out an errand out of fear too. *nedumāl viraindu unnaik kūvuginṟān* – he \[emperumān\] is not limited, like you. His infatuation towards you now is coming out of his independence. In line with that infatuation, come immediately.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.
