## 1.4.9. Taliyil venney

*tāḻiyil veṇṇey tadam kaiyāra viḻungiyapēḻai vayiṟṟu empirān kaṇḍāy unnaik kūvuginṟānāḻi koṇḍu unnai eṟiyum aiyuṟavu illai kāṇvāḻa uṟudiyēl māmadī! magiḻndōdi vā*

**Пословный перевод:**

mā madī! – Oh, eminent candran!; tāḻiyil – collected in pots; veṇṇey – butter; tada – expansive; kai Ara – with the hand full; viḻungiya – one, who scooped and consumed; pēḻai – stout; vayiṟu – having divine stomach; empirān – realise that he is the benefactor for our clan; unnai – you; kūvuginṟān – \[he is\] calling; unnai – upon you; āḻi koṇḍu – with the divine disc; eṟiyum – he will fling; aiyuṟavu – any doubt in this; illai kāṇ – there is none; vāḻa uṟudi ēl – if you desire to live; magiḻndu – with joy; ōdi vā – come running

**Перевод:**

**Oh, eminent candran! With his huge, divine hands, kriṣṇa, who has a stout divine stomach, has scooped fully, butter which had been collected in tall jars, and consumed it. He is the benefactor for our clan. He is calling you. If you do not come, he will fling his divine disc upon you; there is no doubt in this. If you wish to exist, come at once, with joy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tāḻi …** – with overflowing affection, with hands which grow expansively upon seeing butter such that it could be said that the “Hands are apt for his age”, kriṣṇa scoops butter in his hand fully and consumes. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam: If you \[referring to candran\] think that the infatuation with which emperumān is calling you is on account of his *nirankuśa svātantryam* (uncontrollable independence), then, realise that this is not his infatuation.  What, then, is his infatuation? *tāḻiyil veṇṇey tadangaiyāra viḻungiya pēḻai vayiṟṟu empirān kāṇ unnaik kūvuginṟān*. This is his actual infatuation. The term *tāḻiyil veṇṇey* refers to the greatness on account of physical \[relating to one’s form\] qualities. Just as it has been said in [tiruvāimoḻi 8-10-3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/05/thiruvaimozhi-8-10-3-urumo-paviyenukku/) “*siṟumāmanisar*” (being small in physical form and eminent in knowledge\], the smallness which is attached to the physical form since it is dependent on food, water etc, is converted to eminence on account of the eminent qualities of *ātmā* \[such as total dependence on emperumān, servitude etc\], which will match the eminence of nityasūris \[permanent dwellers of śrī vaikuṇṭam\]. Since these people get such eminence even while they are living in samsāram, they are said to be superior to even nityasūris, just as it has been said in [tiruviruttam 79](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/03/thiruviruththam-79/) “*viṇṇūḷārilum sīriyarē*”. The term *veṇṇey* in this verse \[*tāḻiyil veṇṇey*\] refers to such people \[those whose supreme knowledge overshadows their physical form\]. The container in which such *veṇṇey* is kept, becomes *tāḻi*. In other words, if the supremely knowledgeable people are termed as *veṇṇey*, their physical forms will be *tāḻi*. For samsāris \[those who live in the materialistic realm, and go after the worldly pleasures\], their *ātmaguṇam* \[qualities of ātmā\] will follow their *dēham* \[in other words, since their *dēham* desires worldly pleasures, their *ātmaguṇam* will also go after lowly features\]. For *mumukśus* \[samsāris who desire to get liberated from samsāram and attain emperumān\], their *dēhaguṇam* will follow their *ātmaguṇam*. Though āḻvārs are like *mumukśus*, since they have been showered with knowledge and devotion without any shortcoming, their *ātmaguṇam* will follow *dēhaguṇam* \[here, the term *dēhaguṇam* does not refer to āḻvārs’ dēhaguṇam but to emperumān’s *dēhaguṇam*, viz. qualities of his divine form such as the beauty of his individual limbs, overall beauty of his divine form, his softness etc\]. Thus, the term *tāḻiyil veṇṇey* refers to āḻvārs whose *ātmaguṇam* follows their *dēhaguṇam*. Desiring these āḻvārs is the real infatuation which emperumān has.

**pēḻai …** – he has a divine stomach which will expand, to accommodate the material which has gone in. He is also the benefactor for our clan. ṟealise that such an entity is calling you. Through this, it is hinted that the one, who desirously swallowed butter, in line with his age, is calling you \[with the same desire which he had towards butter\]. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that this is not like digesting bosom milk \[as seen in the sixth pāsuram\]. Unlike periya tirumoḻi 11.6.9 pāsuram “*uṇḍotta tiruvayiṟṟin..*” (despite swallowing all the worlds, his divine stomach was like before) and like periya tirumoḻi 10.7.3 “*vayiṟū piḷḷai param anṟu*” (his divine stomach is not apt for his age), his stomach will show, appropriate to the material that he has consumed \[butter, here\]. *pēḻai* – huge. *empirān* – a great benefactor for our clan. His calling you loudly is not for overcoming any shortcoming with him, but to remove your shortcoming. If your shortcoming is removed, he will feel that his shortcoming has been overcome.

**āḻi …** – If the jar, inside which butter is stored, were kept high, outside his reach, just as he breaks the jar with a stone, if you do not come when he calls you, he will fling his divine disc and sever your head; realise this. Have no doubt in this. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that emperumān had changed daytime to night \[during mahābhārata war\] by using his divine disc. Do not be under the impression that he will not change night time to day time. Think of your status when the day was decided for starting of the war \[kriṣṇa had advanced amāvāsyai by one day to ensure that the kauravas will get defeated\]. Do not think “That was done once, in order to achieve a specific objective. Does that reason apply to me too?” That incident happened because the kauravas did not listen to what emperumān said \[to share their kingdom with pāṇḍavas\]. That is applicable to you too \[since you too are not listening to him\]. ṟealise this.

**vāḻa …** – If you desire to be alive, instead of perishing on account of his anger, oh, candran, who is eminent, come running, with joy, in line with your eminence! tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: For you \[referring to candran\], to live is to tell emperumān, just as arjuna had told him in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18-74](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-74/) “*kariśyē vacanam tava*”(I will do as per what you had told me\]. emperumān had said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18-66](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66/) “*sarva darmān parityajya …*” (letting go of all the other means …). If emperumān, after removing all your previous hurdles, puts you back in that state, would it be same for you? \[it would be worse than that previous state itself\]. Once you agree to do as per his bidding, if he tells you to do some tasks, you have to carry out that order. If you are in the old state \[of not carrying out emperumān’s order\], he will not say “*mā śuca*:” (do not grieve), just as he had told arjuna in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18-66](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66/). The term *māmadī* refers to all those who have intelligence, to come running with happiness of being a servitor, when emperumān beckons.

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.4.10. Maittadam kanni

*maittadam kaṇṇi yasōdai tan maganukku ivaiottana solli uraitta māṟṟam oḷi puttūrvittagan vittucittan viritta tamiḻ ivaiettnaiyum solla vallavarkku idar illaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mai – black; tadam kaṇṇi – one who has large eyes; asōdai – yaśōdāp pirātti; than maganukku – for him, her son; ottana – consistent between thought and word; ivai solli – saying these; uraitta – spoken, looking at candran; māṟṟam – pāsurams; oḷi – having splendour; puttūr – incarnating at śrī villibuttūr; vittagan – capable of mangaḷāśāsanam; vittucittan – periyāḻvār; viritta – mercifully composed, in a detailed manner; tamiḻ – in the form of drāvida bhāśai (tamiḻ language); ivai – these ten pāsurams; ettanaiyum – in any manner; solla vallavarkku – those who are capable of reciting; idar – sorrow; illai – there is none

**Перевод:**

**yaśōdāp pirātti, who has black, large eyes, had spoken these pāsurams to her son, consistent between his thoughts and words, looking at candran. periyāḻvār, who is capable of carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam to emperumān, who incarnated in the splendorous śrī villibuttūr, mercifully composed these ten pāsurams in tamiḻ language in a detailed manner. Those who are capable of reciting these, in any manner, will not have any sorrow.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In this last pāsuram, āḻvār mentions the benefits which will accrue to those who recite these ten pāsurams of this decad and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**maittadam kaṇṇai** – yaśōdāp pirātti, who has black, large eyes. Her eyes have become large due to application of black pigment. Alternatively, since she keeps looking at kriṣṇa, who is dark, constantly, her eyes have become black. The eyes have become large since they expand with affection for him. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that speaking about her eyes is indicative of her overall decoration.

**than …** – saying these, which are consistent between kriṣṇa’s thoughts and words, to him. about candran who manifests both softness and toughness. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that having assured kriṣṇa that she will get him candran, though getting candran is impossible for her, she kept calling him to come, in every pāsuram.

**oḷi …** – śrī villibuttūr is such a noble place that if one steps on to that land, he would get knowledge and love towards emperumān. periyāḻvār, who incarnated in that place and who is an expert in carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam to emperumān, composed these ten pāsurams in tamiḻ language, in a detailed manner. There will be no sorrow to anyone who is able to recite these pāsurams in some manner or the other. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that nācciyār \[āṇḍāḷ\] tirumāḷigai \[divine house\] is called as śrī villibuttūr. *vittagan* – *samarttan* (one who is skilful or is capable). Even before he was showered with knowledge and devotion, without any trace of doubt, by emperumān, āḻvār was carrying out *puśpa kainkaryam* (offering garland to emperumān) by nurturing a garden, plucking divine tuḷasi and stringing garlands. Thus, he was skilful always. Alternatively, he had desire in his divine mind, for carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam. *vittucittan* – his standing was such that he was always in the divine mind of *vataperum kōyil udaiyān* \[the divine name of emperumān in śrī villibuttūr\]. Alternatively, just as he had mercifully said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5-4-11 “*aravattu amaḷiyinōdum…*” (with the divine mattress of ādiśēśan …), emperumān was constantly in āḻvār’s divine mind. *viritta tamiḻ ivai* – considering the pāsurams of yaśōdāp pirātti as a pretext, he explained the meanings of śāstrams (sacred texts) to carry out mangaḷāśāsanam to emperumān. Mercifully composing them in tamiḻ was due to his mercy \[so that we could understand the meanings of sacred texts\]. *ettanaiyum solla vallavarkku* – people may have distress that they have not been able to recite vēda śāstrams and understand their meanings. If such people are able to recite these pāsurams, taking refuge under periyāḻvār’s affection, with his pathos, there will be no such distress.

We shall next consider the pravēśam of the next tirumoḻi.

## 1.5.1. Uyya ulagu

*uyya ulagu padaittu uṇḍa maṇi vayiṟā!   ūḻi tōṟūḻi pala ālin ilai adanmēlpaiya uyōgu tuyil koṇḍa param paranē!   pangaya neeḷ nayanattu anjana mēniyanē!seyyavaḷ ninnagalam sēmam enak karudic    celvu poli magarak kādu tiganḻndu ilagaaiya! enakku oru kāl āduga sengīrai    āyargaḷ pōrēṟē! āduga ādugavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uyya – for uplifting ātmās (souls); ulagu – worlds; padaittu – creating them; uṇḍa – later, keeping them inside and protecting them; maṇi vayiṟā! – oh, one who has a beautiful, divine stomach!; pala ūḻi ūḻi tōṟu – for many kalpams \[a kalpam is one day in the life of brahmā, equivalent to 4.32 billion earth years\]; ālin ilai adan mēl – on top of a tender banyan leaf; paiya – slowly (such that the banyan leaf does not move); uyōgu tuyil koṇḍa – one who mercifully carried out yōga nidrā (reclining with total awareness); param paranē! – oh, who is the most supreme!; pangayam – resembling a lotus flower; neeḷ – being long; nayanam – having divine eyes; anjanam – like black pigment \[used for applying to eyes\]; mēniyanē – oh, one who has a divine form!; nin agalam – your divine chest; sēmam ena – that it should be well protected; karudi – thinking; selvu poli – symbolic of abundant wealth; magaram – being together with divine ear rings; kādu – divine ears; tigaḻndu ilaga – to shine well; aiya – oh, lord!; enakku – for me; oru kāl – one time; sengīrai āduga – you should perform sengīrai (sengīrai – a type of dance where mothers will move their children’s limbs to make it appear that the children are dancing); āyargaḷ – being obedient to the herd-folks; pōr – ready for battle; ēṟē! – oh, one who is like an arrogant bull!; āduga āduga – you should dance; you should dance

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who has a beautiful, divine stomach in which you have kept the worlds in a protective manner, after creating them earlier for uplifting ātmās! Oh, one who is the most supreme entity who is meditatively reclining on a tender banyan leaf for many kalpams! Oh, one who has long, divine eyes which are like lotus flower and who has dark divine form! Oh, lord, you should perform sengīrai once for me, such that the divine chest on which pirātti, who was born on a reddish lotus, is dwelling, is well protected and the divine ears with the divine ear rings shine well! Oh, one who is obedient to the herd-folk and who has the arrogance of a bull which is battle-ready! You should dance; you should dance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**uyya …** – During *prākruta praḷayam* \[ultimate deluge when it destroys all the worlds\], the ātmās are lying without form or senses, like *acit* \[those entities which are without knowledge\], not in a position to either enjoy worldly pleasures or be in a position to reach *mōkśam* \[getting liberated from samsāram and attaining śrī vaikuṇṭam\].  In order to uplift them, emperumān starts creation afresh. During *avāntara praḷayam* \[deluge during which only the first three worlds are destroyed\], emperumān protects these three worlds by keeping them in his stomach. Oh, one who has a beautiful, divine stomach where you keep the ātmās and protect them, such that they do not get destroyed! tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that jīvātmās were in the state as mentioned in taittirīya upaniśat śeekśāvalli “*asannēva sa bhavati*” (like acit, without knowledge). In order to enable them to indulge in either enjoying worldly pleasures or to seek liberation from samsāram and to attain śrī vaikuṇṭam, when the worlds were created, they \[ātmās\] started indulging in excessive offences. While they were fit to be destroyed, instead of that, since emperumān kept them safely in his divine stomach, āḻvār says mercifully “*uyya ulagu padaittu uṇḍa maṇi vayiṟā*”.

**ūḻi tōṟ …** – Oh, the most supreme entity, who lies down on a tender banyan leaf, after protecting all the worlds in your divine stomach, during every *kalpam* \[one day of brahmā, when *avāntara praḷayam* sets in\] and engages in *yōga nidra* \[reclining, thinking of how to uplift all the jīvātmās\]. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *ūḻi tōr ūḻi* reflects the fact that many kalpams pass in this status. Instead of mentioning only *ālilai* \[banyan leaf\], since āḻvār has qualified that with *adan mēl*, this refers to the tenderness of the banyan leaf. The term *paiya* \[slowly\] denotes that he was mercifully reclining on the tender banyan leaf, which was just then sprouting, meditating on how to protect and uplift the ātmās, such that the banyan leaf did not even move. This itself indicates his supremacy.

**pangayam …** – symbolic of that supremacy, oh, one who has divine eyes which are like a blossomed lotus, but much longer than the lotus, and who has a dark form to complement the colour of the divine eyes! By calling him as one who has a dark form, āḻvār is cautioning that the one \[śrī mahālakśmi\] who is residing on his divine chest should not be disturbed.

**seyyavaḷ …** – pirātti resides forever on your divine chest. When you engage in *sengīrai*, nothing untoward should happen to her due to your movement. Oh, one who has divine ear rings which hint at your abundant opulence and which shine well! tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that since periya pirāttiyār is residing on his divine chest, nothing should happen to her when he performs *sengīrai*. Unlike people who make an issue of carrying an object \[on their heads or back\] and keep saying “*sem sem*” \[a sound made\] to indicate that they are carrying excessive weight, emperumān is carrying his beloved one, without any effort. The divine ear rings are much enjoyable for pirātti, and they are also indicative of his abundant opulence.

**aiya …** – Oh, my lord! For my sake, you should engage with *sengīrai*, once. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that children are called as *aiya, appā* etc. *enakku …* – you have danced for your sake as well as for her \[pirātti’s\] sake. āḻvār requests kriṣṇa to dance once for his sake. His desire is that if kriṣṇa dances, the food which he has consumed will get digested due to tiredness \[of dancing and that he will go to sleep\].

**āyargaḷ …** – Oh, one who is obedient towards herd folk such that they could be proud saying “He is ours”, due to which you are arrogant like a bull which is ready for battle! You should mercifully engage with *sengīrai*; you should mercifully engage with *sengīrai*.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.5.2. Kolari innuruvam

*kōḷariyin uruvam koṇḍu avuṇan udalam    kurudi kuḻambi eḻak kūr ugirāl kudaivāy!meeḷa avan maganai meymmai koḷak karudi    mēlai amarar padi mikku veguṇḍu varakāḷa nan mēgam avai kallodu kāl poḻiyāk    karudi varaik kudaiyāk kāligaḷ kāppavanē!āḷa enakku oru kāl ādugai sengīrai    āyargaḷ pōr ēṟē! āduga ādugavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōḷ ariyin – with the strength of a lion; uruvam koṇḍu – having the disguise; avuṇan – hiraṇyāsuran’s \[monster hiraṇya kaśyap\]; udalam – body; kurudi – blood; kuḻambi eḻa – to rise up, thick; meeḷa – again; avan – that monster; maganai – his son, prahlādan; meymmai koḷa – to consider as “satyavādi” (one who always speaks truth); karudi – thinking, in his divine mind; kūr ugirāl – with sharp nails; kudaivāi! – oh, one who tore (that monster’s body); mēlē – distinguished; amarar padi – dēvēndran (the head of celestial entities); mikku veguṇḍu vara – when he came angrily; kāḷam – dark; nal – benefical (to coklete the task given by lord); mēgam avai – clouds; kallodu – together with hail; kār poḻiya – as they rained; karudi – considering (what he had said earlier “This mountain is yur protector; provide it with food”); varai – that gōvardana hill; kudaiyā – holding as an umbrella; kāligaḷ – cows; kāppavanē! – oh, one who protected!; āḷa! – oh, the one with masculinity to protect like this!; enakku – for me; oru kāl – one time; sengīrai āduga – you should perform sengīrai; āyargaḷ – being obedient to the herd-folks; pōr – ready for battle; ēṟē! – oh, one who is like an arrogant bull!; āduga āduga – you should dance; you should dance

**Перевод:**

**Two narratives are mentioned in this pāsuram – the first about emperumān, incarnating as narasimha, destroying the monster hiraṇyan and the second, emperumān incarnating as kriṣṇa, protecting cows.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

Oh, one who tore the body of monster hiraṇyan with sharp nails, taking the guise of a powerful lion, in such a manner that the monster’s blood rose up thick, flowing over. In the bargain, emperumān considered in his divine mind that prahlādan, the son of hiraṇyan, should be spoken of as *satyavādi* \[one who speaks only truth\]. Oh, one who lifted the hill gōvardana as an umbrella and protected cows when dēvendran, the eminent head of celestial entities, came angrily and ordered black clouds to rain excessively, with hail, on the cows and herd-folk. Oh, one who is obedient to the herd-folk and who has the arrogance of a bull which is battle-ready! You should dance; you should dance.

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kōḷariyin uruvam koṇḍu** – taking over the guise of strong narasimha \[human body, with the head of a lion\], without compromising on the boons granted to the monster by celestial entities, to annihilate the monster. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that emperumān decided to take the disguise of narasimha, tear the body of hiraṇyan, which had been nurtured like the body of a wild pig, such that the blood spilled over and he bled from his mouth. Since he could not use his weapons \[on account of the boons granted to the monster by celestial entities\], emperumān used his sharp, divine nails as weapon. He also considered to make the monster’s son as one who speaks only truth.

**avuṇan …** – the monster hiraṇyan had arrogance resulting from the strength of the boons which he had been granted \[by brahmā et al\] and the strength of his shoulders. He was confident that emperumān was not present inside a pillar which he had built, when his son, prahlādan, told him that emperumān exists everywhere. In order to destroy that monster such that his blood rose up from his body, spilling over, and to prove the words of prahlādan, emperumān incarnated as narasimha, without carrying any weapon, and with sharp nails. Just as it has been said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4-9-8 “*oḷḷiya mārbu uṟaikka ūnṟik kudaindavanē*” (Oh, one who tore completely the well decorated chest of the monster!) oh, one who tore the chest of that monster! The term *meeḷa* refers to emperumān knowing the mind of the monster that emperumān does not exist and the term *meymmai koḷa* refers to considering prahlādan as speaking only truth. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *kudaivāy* refers to letting blood to flow out from all the regions where they were stagnant. The term *meymmai* refers to emperumān’s *bhāgavata śēśatvam* – emperumān carrying out servitude to his followers \[due to their overflowing affection towards him\]. This meaning is manifested in the first *rahasyam* \[*tirumantram* or the divine hymn which describes the relationship between emperumān and ātmās\]. Even if prahlādan had only said the name \[nārāyaṇaya\], emperumān considered it as having been said with the full meanings \[including carrying out servitude to emperumān’s followers\].

\[Now, we move to the second part, when dēvēndran’s arrogance was subdued\].

**mēlai …** – celestial entities are those who have much higher wealth and longevity than people who inhabit earth. dēvēndran is the head of such celestial entities. He became angry when he found that the food, meant for him, was consumed by someone else. With hunger driving him, he came angrily, asking “Who consumed the food meant for me?” Clouds had become very dark since they had imbibed water from ocean such that the ocean had dried up. They had the benefit \[for indran\], of obeying his command and started raining heavily, along with fierce wind. This meaning holds good when the verse is *kallodu kāl poḻiya* \[*kāl* refers to wind\]. If, on the other hand, the verse had been *kallodu kār poḻiya* \[*kār*– dark clouds puring rain\], the meaning will change as: raining with hail. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the celestial entities are called as *amarars* \[those without death\] since they live for a few days more than those who live on earth. indran, being the head of the thirty-three main entities and a crore other entities, is called as *amarar padi* \[chief of the celestial entities\]. Further, he says that the clouds are called as *nan mēgam* \[beneficial cloud\] since they carried out the discordant task set out for them by indran, their head. Earlier they used to carry out beneficial work \[of providing rains to people on earth for their sustenance\]. Now, fearing his anger, they are torturing them, by pouring hailstorm with heavy winds.

**karudi …** – kriṣṇa had earlier told the herd-folk “This mountain \[gōvardana\] is your protector. Offer your food to it”. Recalling those words, oh, one who lifted that mountain as an umbrella and protected the cows! Instead of saying that he protected the herd-men and herd-women, why is āḻvār saying “*kāligaḷ kāppavanē*” (one who protected cows)? The reason for this is that he wanted to make sure that cows are prominent as the class to be protected. Also, only these know precisely, the help rendered. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa had already decided that he was going to eat all the food, meant to be offered to indran. Considering that he had told the herd-folk “Offer the food to this mountain. It will protect you”, he now lifted that mountain as an umbrella and protected them.

**āḷa …** – this speaks about the masculine power that emperumān has, in protecting. Also, it refers to – fulfilling my \[reference is to yaqśōdāp pirātti’s\] desire and making me your servitor. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here “If you wish to rule over me, you should perform *sengīrai* for me”. Alternatively, “If you want me to control you and rule over you, you should perform *sengīrai* for me” \[since it is normal for a mother to control her child\].

**enakku …** – for my sake, you should perform *sengīrai*, once.

**āyargaḷ …** – Oh, one who is obedient towards herd folk such that they could be proud saying “He is ours”, due to which you are arrogant like a bull which is ready for battle! You should mercifully engage with *sengīrai*; you should mercifully engage with *sengīrai*.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.5.3. Nammudai nayagane

*nammudai nāyaganē! nānmaṟaiyin poruḷē!    nāviyuḷ naṟkamala nānmuganukku oru kāltammanai ānavanē! taraṇi talam muḻudum   tāragaiyin ulagum tadavi adan puṟamumvimma vaḷarndavanē! vēḻamum ēḻ vidaiyum    viraviya vēlai tanuḷ venṟu varum avanē!amma enakku oru kāl āduga sengīrai    āyargaḷ pōrēṟē! āduga ādugavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nammudai – our; nāyaganē! – oh, one who is the lord!; nāl maṟaiyin – in the four vēdas \[sacred texts\]; poruḷē! – oh, one who is the meaning!; nābi uḷ – formed in the divine navel; nal kamalam – born in the eminent lotus; nān muganukku – for brahmā, who has four faces; oru kāl – during the time when he lost the four vēdams; tammanai ānavanē! – oh, one who was affectionate, like a mother!; taraṇi talam muḻudum – all the worlds; tāragaiyin ulagum – the galaxy of stars; tadavi – feeling with your divine feet; adan puṟamum – in the worlds outside those; vimma – to be filled; vaḷarndavanē! – oh, one who grew as trivikrama!; vēḻamum – elephant, called as kuvalayāpeedam; ēḻ vidaiyum – seven bulls; viraviya – when they came together, to torture you; vēlai tanuḷ – at that time; venṟu – winning against them; varum avanē – oh, one who came!; amma – oh, my lord!; enakku – for me; oru kāl – one time; sengīrai āduga – you should perform sengīrai; āyargaḷ – being obedient to the herd-folks; pōr – ready for battle; ēṟē! – oh, one who is like an arrogant bull!; āduga āduga – you should dance; you should dance

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who is our lord! Oh, one who is the meaning of the four vēdas! Oh, one who was like an affectionate mother to brahmā, who was born in the beautiful lotus flower which formed in your divine navel! Oh, one who grew up as trivikrama, to fill up all the worlds, the galaxies of stars and the worlds outside of those, feeling them with your divine feet! Oh, one who won over the elephant, kuvalayāpeedam and the seven bulls when they charged at you together, to torture you! Oh, one who is our lord! Oh, one who is obedient to the herd-folk and who has the arrogance of a bull which is battle-ready! You should dance; you should dance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**nammudai nāyaganē**– Oh, one who is our controller! tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that it was only after emperumān became āḻvār’s lord that he became the meanings of vēdams. *nārāyaṇa anuvākam* \[this is a part in vēdam which praises emperumān as the supreme entity\] became prominent only after this.

**nān maṟaiyin poruḷē** – Oh, one who is explained primarily, in the four vēdas! kaṇṇan himself has said in [bhagavat gītā 15-15](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/15-15/) “*vēdaiśca sarvair ahamēva vēdya*:” (only I am known through all the vēdams). tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that vēdas are innumerable.

**nābiyul …** – on a distinguished lotus which formed inside the divine navel, brahmā appeared. Oh, one, at one point of time, was affectionate towards brahmā, like a mother!

**tammanai …**– mother. brahmā lost vēdams to two monsters, madu and kaitabha and started lamenting “*vēdāmē paramam cakśur vēdāmē paramam danam*” (vēhdam is my most eminent eye; vēdam is my most eminent wealth) saying “I have lost my eyes; I have lost my wealth”. Since emperumān redeemed the vēdams from the monsters and returned them to brahmā, protecting him, he is referred to as brahmā’s mother. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that he was the abode of birth for both brahmā, who appeared on a blossomed lotus, and for the lotus itself. Alternatively, *tammanai* could be considered as *than anai*, thus, becoming mother of brahmā.

**taraṇai talam …**– Oh, one who grew, filling up all the worlds, including the galaxies of stars and other worlds outside of those galaxies, like a cool breeze and cool moon, touching them with your divine feet! This narrates the divine activity of emperumān to fulfil the desire of his follower, indra, who had lost all his three worlds to mahābali. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that emperumān touches all the worlds here, where people are subservient to other deities, and all the galaxies of stars which have entities thinking that they are totally independent, with his divine feet, like a gentle breeze and like moon. Since emperumān became happy that his task had got fulfilled, he was elated with joy.

**vēḻamum …** – Oh, one who came out victoriously, when kuvalayāpeedam and the seven bulls came charging at you, in order to harm you! While kuvalayāpeedam and the seven bulls were destroyed at different points of time, the reason for making them appear that kriṣṇa had killed them together is because of āḻvār’s overjoy that kriṣṇa’s enemies have been killed. Through these two events, the divine activities carried out by emperumān to make happy the women of maturā and nappinnaip pirātti, have been mentioned.

**amma!** – Oh, my lord! tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that periyāḻvār says *amma* since he considered destruction of enemies of emperumān’s followers \[through the killing of elephant kuvalayāpeedam\] and of his consort, nappinnaip pirātti \[through the killing of seven bulls\] as his own benefit. Alternatively, it could be construed as periyāḻvār’s fear about kriṣṇa undertaking some other activity after this where he would be exposed to other dangers.

**enakku …** – for my sake, you should perform *sengīrai*, once.

**āyargaḷ …** – Oh, one who is obedient towards herd-folk such that they could be proud saying “He is ours”, due to which you are arrogant like a bull which is ready for battle! You should mercifully engage with *sengīrai*; you should mercifully engage with *sengīrai*.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.5.4. Vanavar tam magila

*vānavar tām magiḻa van sagadam uruḷa    vanja mulaippēyin nanjamadu uṇḍavanēkānaga valviḷavin kāy udirak karudik    kanṟadu koṇḍu eṟiyum karu niṟa en kanṟētēnuganaum muranum tiṇ tiṟal ven naragan    enbavar tām madiyac ceru adirac cellumānai! enakku oru kāḷ āduga sengīrai    āyargaḷ pōrēṟē! āduga ādugavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vānavar tām – celestial entities; magiḻa – to feel joyous; val sagadam – śakatāsuran, who is strong; uruḷa – to roll; vanjam – deceitful; pēyin – pūtanā \[fiend\]; mulai – atop her bosom; nanju – poison; amudu – as nectar; uṇḍavanē – oh, one who consumed!; kānagam – in the forest; val – strong; viḷavin – wood apple; kāy – raw ones; udira – to fall down; karudi – thinking; kanṟu – in the form of calf; adu – that vatsāsuran \[a monster\]; koṇḍu – holding in the hand; eṟiyum – one who threw; karu niṟam – having a dark complexion; en kanṟē! – oh, one who is my calf!; dēnuganum – monster dēnukāsuran; muran – monster murāsuran; tiṇ tiṟal – known well as having strength; vem – cruel; naragan – monster narakāsuran; enbavar tām – these monsters; madiya – to die; seru – in the battle; adira – having strength; sellum – one who went; ānai! – oh, one who is like an elephant!; enakku – for me; oru kāl – one time; sengīrai āduga – you should perform sengīrai; āyargaḷ – being obedient to the herd-folks; pōr – ready for battle; ēṟē! – oh, one who is like an arrogant bull!; āduga āduga – you should dance; you should dance

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who made the strong śakatāsuran to roll \[down to his death\] such that the celestial entiti4s were joyous and one who consumed the poison applied on top of pūtanā’s bosoms, as if it were nectar! Oh, my dark-complexioned calf, who threw a calf in which the monster vatsāsuran had pervaded, to hit against a wood apple raw fruit \[inside which another monster had pervaded\] such that wood apples would scatter down \[and killing both the monsters\] inside the forest! Oh, one who is like an elephant going mightily in the battlefield such that monsters such as dēnukāsuran, murāsuran and the cruel and strong narakāsuran died! Oh, one who is obedient to the herd-folk and who has the arrogance of a bull which is battle-ready! You should dance; you should dance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vānavar …** – celestial entities prayed to you to incarnate on earth such that the excessive load on earth, on account of monstrous entities, would get reduced. Oh, one who made those celestial entities to be joyous by annihilating the monstrous entities even before reaching the age which is fit to fight with them! When śakatāsuran, a monster, pervaded a wheel near you, to harm you, due to delay in being fed bosom milk, you were kicking your legs, to draw attention. That monster got caught between your legs such that your kick made him roll down to his death. When pūtanā, another monster, came in the guise of your mother, applying poison on her bosoms in order to kill you, oh, one who consumed her life along with that poison! When the text is *nanjamudu uṇḍavanē*, it would mean one who consumed that poison as nectar. harivamśam viṣṇu parvam 6-39 says “*stanyam tat viśasammiśram rasyamāsījjagad gurō*:” (That bosom milk, which had been mixed with poison, was sweet for kriṣṇa, who is the lord of all the worlds). tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that it was due to my \[reference here is to āḻvār\] fortune that the poison became nectar-like. This refers to the auspicious time when kriṣṇa was born.

**kānagam …** – when kriṣṇa went to the forest to graze calves, two demons had pervaded a calf and a wood apple raw fruit, in order to harm him. This part of the pāsuram narrates the incident when kriṣṇa threw one entity against the other, killing both of them. Oh, one who stood like a dark-complexioned calf, who threw a calf on a few wood-apple raw fruits to make them fall down, in the forest! Through this narration, the way his divine form became splendorous on account of killing the enemies of his followers and the way he was obedient towards his followers are mentioned.

**dēnukan …** – Oh, one who is like a powerful elephant, entering a battlefield, and destroyed monsters such as dēnukāsuran, murāsuran and the strong, cruel narakāsuran!

**enakku …** – for my sake, you should perform *sengīrai*, once.

**āyargaḷ …** – Oh, one who is obedient towards herd folk such that they could be proud saying “He is ours”, due to which you are arrogant like a bull which is ready for battle! You should mercifully engage with *sengīrai*; you should mercifully engage with *sengīrai*.

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.5.5. Mattalavum tayirum

*mattaḷavum tayirum vār kuḻal nanmadavār    vaittana ney kaḷavāḷ vāri viḻungi orunguotta iṇai marudam unniya vandavarai    ūru karattinodum undiya vem tiṟalōy!muttin iḷa muṟuval muṟṟa varuvadan mun    munnam mugattu aṇiyār moy kuḻalgaḷ alaiyaatta! enakku oru kāl āduga sengīrai    āyargaḷ pōrēṟē! āduga ādugavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vār kuḻal – having lengthy locks; nal madavār – women who have virtue and simplicity; vaittana – saved and kept; mattu – with churning staff; aḷavum – apt to be churned; tayirum – curd, and; ney – ghee, obtained by melting butter; kaḷavāl – through stealing; vāri – scooping with the hand; viḻungi – eating such that the stomach is filled; unniya – having the thought to harm you; orungu – focussed; otta – minds syncronised; iṇai marudam – as twin maruda trees \[Indian laurel tree\]; vandavarai – monsters who pervaded and stood; ūru karattinodum – with divine thighs and divine hands; undiya – one who pushed such that \[the two trees\] slid and fell down; vem tiṟalōy! – oh, one who has great strength!; atta! – oh, one who is like my father!; muttu – such that the divine pearls showed (divine teeth); in – sweet; iḷa muruval – gentle smile; muṟṟa – completely; varuvadan mun – before it comes; munnam mugattu – on the front side of the face; aṇi Ar – being beautiful; moy – being dense; kuḻalgaḷ – divine locks; alaiya – to sway, in a lowered manner; enakku – for me; oru kāl – one time; sengīrai āduga – you should perform sengīrai; āyargaḷ – being obedient to the herd-folks; pōr – ready for battle; ēṟē! – oh, one who is like an arrogant bull!; āduga āduga – you should dance; you should dance

**Перевод:**

**Women, who have lengthy locks, who have virtue and simplicity, have saved and kept curd, which is apt to be churned with a churning staff, along with ghee. You stole those materials, by scooping them with your hands and eating till the stomach became full. Two monsters had planned to harm you, pervaded two marudam \[Indian laurel\] trees and stood, waiting for an opportunity. Oh, one who has great strength, with which you pushed with your divine thighs and divine hands in such a manner that the twin trees snapped and fell down on either side! Oh, one who is like my father! Before one could see the gentle smile breaking out completely to show your divine pearls \[teeth\], the dense locks come on to the front side of the face and sway, in a lowered manner. Oh, one who is obedient to the herd-folk and who has the arrogance of a bull which is battle-ready! You should dance; you should dance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vār kuḻal nan madavār vaittana** – saved properly by women who have lengthy locks along with virtue and simplicity.

**mattaḷavum tayirum – neyyum kaḷavāl vāri viḻungi** – without the knowledge of those who had kept \[them\], stealing \[them\], scooping with his \[kriṣṇa\] hands and eating curd which was apt for being churned with churning staff, ghee which had been prepared from butter which had been churned earlier itself, to fulfil his desire for eating them.

**unniya – orungotta iṇai marudam – vandavarai** – two monsters who had thought of harming you, syncronising their minds to carry out such an act, hiding their real forms and standing as two *marudam* trees.

**ūru …** – Oh, one who has the great strength to go between the two trees, knocking them down with your divine thighs and divine hands by crawling between them!

**muttu …** – in such a manner by which the dense and beautiful locks on the front side would come down and hide the gentle smile which would have broken out to reveal the divine pearls \[divine teeth\], just as it has been said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1-8-2 “*pangigaḷ vandu un pavaḷavāy moyppa*” (such that the curly locks would swarm around your divine lips which are like coral). *aṇi*– beauty; *moy* – dense; *atta* – father!

**enakku …** – for my sake, you should perform *sengīrai*, once.

**āyargaḷ …** – Oh, one who is obedient towards herd folk such that they could be proud saying “He is ours”, due to which you are arrogant like a bull which is ready for battle! You should mercifully engage with *sengīrai*; you should mercifully engage with *sengīrai*.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.5.6. Kayamalr nirava

*kāyamalar niṟavā! karumugil pōl uruvā!    kānagamāmaduvil kāḷiyan ucciyilētūya nadam payilum sundara en siṟuvā!    tunga madakkariyin kombu parittavanē!āyam aṟindu poruvān edir vanda mallai    andaram inṟi aḻittādiya tāḷ iṇaiyāy!āya! enakku oru kāḷ āduga sengīrai    āyargaḷ pōr ēṟē! āduga ādugavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kāya malar – like kāyām pū (dark-purple coloured flower); niṟavā! – oh, one who has the divine colour!; karu mugil pōl – like bluish clouds; uruvā! – oh, one who has the divine form!; kānagam – in forest; mā maduvil – in a huge river; kāīiyan – kāḷiyan’s \[a snake\]; ucciyilē – on his head; tūya – pleasing to the mind; nadam – dance; payilum – carried out; sundara – having beauty; en siṟuvā! – oh, my son!; tungam – very tall; madam – being in rut; kariyin – elephant, known as kuvalayāpeedam; kombu – tusks; paṟittavanē! – oh, one casually plucked!; āyam aṟindu – knowing the nuances of wrestling; poruvān – to engage in fight; edir vanda – those who came opposing; mallai – wrestlers; andaram inṟi – without any danger to yourself; aḻittu – destroyed; ādiya – one who roamed around, asking “Is there anyone else who wishes to come for a fight?”; tāḷ iṇaiyāy! – oh, one who has divine feet!; āya! – oh, one who tends to cows!; enakku – for me; oru kāl – one time; sengīrai āduga – you should perform sengīrai; āyargaḷ – being obedient to the herd-folks; pōr – ready for battle; ēṟē – oh, one who is like an arrogant bull!; āduga āduga – you should dance; you should dance

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who has the divine colour of a dark-purple flower! Oh, one who has the form of bluish cloud! Oh, my beautiful son, who danced on the head of snake kāḷiyan in a huge river such that it was pleasing to the mind! Oh, one who effortlessly plucked the tusks of elephant kuvalayāpeedam which was eminent and in rut! Oh, one who has divine feet, and who, without any danger to yourself, destroyed the wrestlers who knew the nuances of wrestling! Oh, one who tends to cows! Oh, one who is obedient to the herd-folk and who has the arrogance of a bull which is battle-ready! You should dance; you should dance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kāya …** – The flower is called as *kāyām* pū. The long syllable in *kāyā* has got shortened to the short syllable *kāya*. Owing to the shine and the dark-purple colour, oh, one who is like the dark-purple flower!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says: Oh, one who has the divine colour of a dark-purple coloured flower and who has a divine form which is like a cloud which has imbibed water to its neck \[fully imbibed with water\]!

**karu mugil …** – Owing to the darkness and coolness, oh, one who has the form of a rain-filled cloud!

**kānagam …** – Oh, my beautiful son, who danced in a pleasing way, on the expanded hoods of snake kāḷiyan who became angry, while lying down inside a large river, and who drove the snake away from the river! *sundaram* – beauty; *siṟuvan* – son.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that in the middle of the orchard on the bank of river yamunā, in a large river, kāḷiyan had spread his hoods. Oh, one who danced on that kāḷiyan’s head, in line with *bharata śāstram* \[treatise on bharata nātyam\]! The term *tūya nadam* refers to compliance with *bharata śāstram*. s*undara* … – Oh, my little son, who is such beautiful that I could proudly say “He is mine”! While I am your servitor, your activities are such that you are my servitor.

**tunga …** – Oh, one who effortlessly plucked the tusks of elephant kuvalayāpeedam, which was very tall and which was in rut!

**āyam …** – the wrestlers \[appointed by king kamsan to destroy you\] knew the nuances in the art of wrestling. Without giving them scope, oh, one who went hurriedly towards them and killed them, roaming around \[in the wrestling arena\], asking “Is there anyone else who is willing to fight?”! Alternatively, the word *andaram inṟi* would refer to absence of any space between the bodies of two wrestlers when they are engaged in wrestling.  Also, *andaram* would refer to danger; here it would mean that kriṣṇa destroyed the wrestlers without any danger to himself.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that without giving time to the wrestlers to present themselves \[to the spectators\] speaking highly of their achievements, kriṣṇa immediately broke their bones with his divine feet in such a way that they were lifted like a plough. *āyam* – nuances in wrestling. *andaram* – interval \[time\]. kriṣṇa destroyed the wrestlers without giving them any time.

**āya** – Oh, one who tends to cows!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *āya* would refer to “for”. While I exist for you, you should perform *sengīrai* for me. Alternatively, *āya* would refer to one who tends to cows.

**enakku …** – for my sake, you should perform *sengīrai*, once.

**āyargaḷ …** – Oh, one who is obedient towards herd-folk such that they could be proud saying “He is ours” due to which you are arrogant like a bull, which is ready for battle! You should mercifully engage with *sengīrai*; you should mercifully engage with *sengīrai*.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.5.7. Tuppudai ayargal

*tuppudai āyargaḷ tam sol vaḻuvādu oru kāl    tūya karum kuḻal nal tōgai mayil anaiyanappinnai tan tiṟamā nal vidai ēḻu aviya    nallatiṟal udaiya nādanum ānavanē!tappina piḷḷaigaḷait tana migu sōdi pugat    tani oru tēr kadavit tāyodu kūttiya enappa! enakku oru kāl āduga sengīrai    āyargaḷ pōrēṟē! āduga āugavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tuppu udai – having strength; āyargaḷ tam – herd-folk’s; sol – word; vaḻuvādu – without going back; oru kāl – at one point of time; tūya – being beautiful; karu kuḻal – having dark locks; nal tōgai – having eminent feathers; mayil anaiya – having the appearance of a peacock; nappinnai than tiṟamā – with nappinnaip pirātti as the reason; nal – being accomplished in cruelty; vidai ēḻ – seven bulls; aviya – to be killed; nalla tiṟal udaiya – having great strength; nādanum ānavanē! – oh, one who became the lord of those herd-folks!; tappina – slipping out of hands; piḷḷaigaḷai – the brāhmaṇa’s children; tana – his \[emperumān’s\]migu sōdi – in paramapadam which is having infinite brilliance; puga – to enter; tani – separately; oru – a unique; tēr – chariot; tāyodu – \[with their\] mother; kūttiya – one who united; en appa! – oh, one who is like my father!; enakku – for me; oru kāl – one time; sengīrai āduga – you should perform sengīrai; āyargaḷ – being obedient to the herd-folks; pōr – ready for battle; ēṟē – oh, one who is like an arrogant bull!; āduga āduga – you should dance; you should dance

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who became the head of herd-folks, by fulfilling their words, after killing seven cruel bulls for the sake of nappinnaip pirātti, who had beautiful, dark locks and who had the appearance of beautiful peacock with eminent feathers! Oh, one who is like my father, who united the children of a brāhmaṇa who came and complained to you about his children who slipped out of his hands, by conducting a chariot, going to your effulgent abode of śrī vaikuṇṭam, bringing back the brāhmaṇa’s children and united them with their mother! Oh, one who tends to cows! Oh, one who is obedient to the herd-folk and who has the arrogance of a bull which is battle-ready! You should dance; you should dance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tuppu …** – *tuppu* – *midukku*; having strength; this refers to the skill in controlling bulls. Alternatively, this would also refer to the mental strength by which the herd-folks asked kaṇṇan to win over the seven bulls, without considering the cruelness of the bulls and the softness of kaṇṇan’s divine form. Without going against the words of such herd-folks, at one point of time …

**tūya …** – keeping nappinnaip pirātti, who has beautiful, dark locks as a result of which she has the appearance of a peacock with eminent features as the reason, and considering that in order to unite with her, “It will be good to listen to anyone’s words”, kriṣṇa listened to the words of herd-folk, without going back on those words.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that *tūymai* \[purity of yaśōdāp pirātti’s locks\] is that kriṣṇa desires her locks. He further says that the term *tuppu* would also refer to firmness in heart. In other words, without looking at the cruel nature of the bulls and the softness of kriṣṇa’s divine form, the herd-folks were firm in their minds that he should win over them in order to marry nappinnaip pirātti.

**nal vidai …** – You had destroyed the seven cruel bulls as if they were vheatvorms. Oh, one who has that strength such that herd-folk would celebrate saying “You are the head of our clan” and became their head! The term *nalvidai* \[good bull\] is similar to saying *nalla pāmbu* \[good snake, cobra\], referring to their cruel nature \[in a tone of sarcasm\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that in the term *nalla tiṟal* \[beneficial skill\], the benefit for his skill was that the activity was undertaken for the sake of others \[his followers. Here, the act of winning over the seven bulls was undertaken to satisfy the herd-folk\].

Is it only this much? āḻvār mercifully mentions emperumān being the lord of both *vibhūtis* \[realms\], by narrating about how he went to śrī vaikuṇṭam in order to fulfil the wish of someone in samsāram.

**tappina …** – the children of the brāhmaṇa who disappeared, soon after their birth, even before their mother could see them. Just as it has been said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3-10-5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/11/thiruvaimozhi-3-10-5-idar-inriye/) “*tannudaic cōdi*” (his effulgent divine abode of śrī vaikuṇṭam), emperumān went in a unique chariot, made it to stop on this side of primordial region, entered his divine abode, retrieved the children, gave them back to their mother who hugged them and exclaimed “My children!” Oh, one who became my benefactor, by carrying out your followers’ task!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai adds here that āḻvār says *en appa* \[my father\] considering the benefit which emperumān carried out for the mother as one which was done for āḻvār himself.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.5.8. Unnaiyum okkalaiyil

*unnaiyum okkalaiyil koṇḍu tam il maruvi    unnodu tangaḷ karuttāyina seydu varumkanniyarum magiḻak kaṇḍavar kaṇ kuḷirak    kaṟṟavar teṟṟī varap peṟṟa enakku aruḷimannu kuṟungudiyāy! veḷḷaṟaiyāy! madiḷ sūḻ    sōlaimalaikku arasē! kaṇṇapurattu amudē!en avalam kaḷaivāy! āduga sengīrai    ēḻulagum udaiyāi! āduga ādugavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mannu – lasting such that it would not be destroyed even during deluge; kuṟūngudiyāy! – oh, one who has mercifully taken residence in tirukkuṟungudi! \[a divine abode\]; veḷḷaṟaiyāy! – oh, one who is dwelling in tiruveḷḷaṟai! \[another divine abode\]; madiḷ sūḻ – surrounded by fortified walls; sōlai malaikku – for the hills of tirumālirum sōlai \[another divine abode\]; arasē! – oh, one who is the head!; kaṇṇapurattu – one who is residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram \[another divine abode\]; amudē! – oh, one who is enjoyable like nectar!; en – my; avalam – distress; kaḷaivāy! – oh, one who removes!; unnaiyum – you (who steal our hearts); okkalaiyil – on the waist; koṇḍu – taking; tam il – to their houses; maruvi – reaching with you; unnodu – with you; tangaḷ – their; karuttu āyina seydu – playing with you as per their desires; varum – and bringing you back; kanniyarum – young girls; magiḻa – to feel happy after seeing this; kaṇḍavar – those who saw; kaṇ – eyes; kuḷira – to feel cool \[comfortable\]; kaṟṟavar – those who could speak a few words; teṟṟi vara – to string garlands of nuanced poems; peṟṟa – one who sired you; enakku – in my matter; aruḷi – having mercy, perform sengīrai; ēḻ ulagum – for all the seven worlds; udaiyāy – oh, one who is the lord!; āduga āduga – you should dance; you should dance

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who has mercifully taken residence in tirukkuṟungudi, which does not get destroyed even during deluge! Oh, one who is dwelling in tiruveḷḷḷaṟai! Oh, one who is the head of tirumālirum sōlai, which is surrounded by fortified walls! Oh, one is enjoyable like nectar, residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram! Oh, one who removes my distress! You should perform sengīrai such that young girls, who take you on their waists, reach their homes and play with you as they please, feel happy; you should perform sengīrai such that those who see you dance, would have cool and comfortable eyes; you should perform sengīrai such that those who speak a few words, are able to compose nuanced poems; you should perform sengīrai such that you shower your grace on me, who had given birth to you. Oh, one who is the lord of all the worlds! You should dance; you should dance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**unnaiyum …** – Keeping you who steal, through your qualities such as beauty etc, the eyes and minds of those who see you, on their waists, they \[the young women in śrī gōkulam\] reach their respective home. The opinion given here is: How strange that even after keeping you on their waists, the girls are such conscious that they are able to reach their homes without losing their way.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam: you, who are capable of stealing the eyes and minds of people by their merely seeing you.

**unnodu …** – young girls, who play with you, who are like this \[as stated in the previous verse\], to their hearts’ content, will bring you back \[to my house\]. Such youngsters should see \[you performing *sengīrai*\] and feel joyous. Through this, the meaning hinted is that the girls would feel happy that one, who, when he is alone with them, is behaving like a youth, is behaving like a child when he is with his mother and carrying out activities accordingly.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: bringing you back \[to yaśōdāp pirātti’s mansion\] is even rarer than taking you to their houses without losing their way. *kanniyarum magiḻa* – apart from mother, even those who desire him to be happy. Happiness for those who leave is due to innocence of not knowing the sorrow of leaving him behind and going.

**kaṇḍavar kaṇ kuḷira** – if someone were to see this \[your performing *sengīrai*\], their eyes would feel cool, as if tender coconut water had been poured into their eyes.

**kaṟṟavar teṟṟi vara** – those who are capable of stringing a few words into verses would be capable of composing nuanced poems such as *piḷḷait tamiḻ* \[a class of tamiḻ poems focussing on activities of children\] if they see your divine activities as a child.

**peṟṟa enakku aruḷi** – showering your grace on me, who had given birth to you. This is to be read with the final verse.

**mannu kuṟungudiyāy** – tirukkuṟungudi is such a divine abode that even deluge cannot destroy it, just as it has been said in śrī bhāgavatam 5-38-9 “*na plāvayati sāgara*:” \[ocean cannot drown it). Oh, one who has mercifully taken residence in such tirukkuṟungudi!

**veḷḷaṟaiyāy** – not only that, oh, one who is permanently dwelling in tiruveḷḷaṟai!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that tiruveḷḷaṟai is the divine abode for which āḻvār has carried out mangaḷāśāsanam in a distinguished manner.

**madiḷ sūḻ sōlai malaikku arasē** – oh, one who is ruling over as the king in *tirumalai* \[divine mountain\] which has fortified walls as protection, avoiding rule by two kings! \[meaning hinted here is that emperumān has come down from paramapadam, won over tirumālirunjōlai through his divine qualities of beauty, simplicity etc and ruled over it, without a second king lurking anywhere\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the divine fortified walls of tirumālirunjōlai would make āḻvār to be without any stress.

**kaṇṇapurattu amudē** – Oh, one who is like a nectar in tirukkaṇṇapuram, to be enjoyed by all the people \[unlike the nectar which was exclusively consumed by celestial entities\]!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kaṇṇapuram is such that just as it has been said in [perumāḷ tirumoḻi 8-6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/08/perumal-thirumozhi-8-6/) “*kaṟṟavar tām vāḻum…*” (the divine abode of tirukkaṇṇapuram is inhabited by wise people…), it is apt to carry out mangaḷāśāsanam there.

**en avalam kaḷaivāy** – Oh, one who removes my distress! The meaning conveyed here is: by being obedient to me, you have removed my distress which I would have felt if you had been uncontrollable.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: āḻvār is saying “*en avalam kaḷaivāy*” because there is no shortcoming in his knowledge that he \[āḻvār\] is the protector and kriṣṇa is protected. Distress for him will occur if kriṣṇa were not protected. āḻvār has told emperumān that he should reside permanently in these divine abodes and has made him to reside in those places as per his \[āḻvār’s\] desire.

**āduga sengīrai** – You, who are like this, should perform *sengīrai*.

**ēḻulagum …** – Oh, one who is the lord of all the worlds! You should mercifully perform dance. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here – only if emperumān is controlled by āḻvār could he \[emperumān\] become the controller of all the worlds. āḻvār says “You look after your possession” \[and let me look after you, since he is mangaḷāśāsanaparar\].

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.5.9. Palodu ney

*pālodu ney tayir oṇ sāndodu seṇbagamum    pangayam nalla karuppūramum nāṟi varakōla naṟum pavaḷac cenduvar vāyin idaik   kōmaḷa veḷḷi muḷaip pōl sila pal ilaganeela niṟattu aḻagār aimbadaiyin naduvē   nin kanivāy amudam iṟṟu muṟindu viḻaēlu maṟaip poruḷē! āduga sengīrai    ēḻulagum udaiyāy! āduga ādugavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pālodu – along with milk; ney – ghee, and; tayir – curd (consuming all these for a long time); oṇ sāndodu – with beautiful sandalwood paste; seṇbagamum – \[fragrant\] flowers such as campaka etc (applying these for a long time); pangayam – lotus flower; nalla – most eminent; karuppūramum – medicated camphor, all these; nāṟi vara – to emit a fragrance together; kōlam – beautiful; naṟu pavaḷam – like eminent coral; sem – being beautiful; tuvar – being reddish; vāyin idai – inside the divine lips; kōmaḷam – tender; veḷḷi muḷaip pōl – like silver buds; sila pal – a few divine pearls (divine teeth); ilaga – to shine; neelam niṟattu – with blue colour; aḻagu Ar – overflowing beauty; ai padaiyin naduvē – amidst the divine pancāyudam (five divine weapons); nin – your; kani vāy – secreting in the divine mouth which is like kovvaikkani (type of berry); amudam – the water of nectar; iṟṟu muṟindu viḻa – exuding and dripping down; ēlum – apt; maṟai – vēdam’s; poruḷē! – oh, one who is the meaning!; āduga sengīrai – you should perform sengīrai; ēḻ ulagum – for all the seven worlds; udaiyāy – oh, one who is the lord!; āduga āduga – you should dance; you should dance

**Перевод:**

**Owing to consuming milk, ghee and curd over a long period of time, owing to applying sandalwood paste and campaka flower over a long period of time, with lotus flower and medicated camphor emitting an eminent fragrance together, with a few divine teeth, which are like tender, silver buds, shining inside your divine mouth which is beautiful and reddish, amidst the figurines of five divine weapons which are beautiful with a bluish colour, nectar like saliva secreting from your divine mouth which is like kovvaikkani dripping, oh, one who is the meaning of the apt vēdams! You should perform sengīrai. Oh, one who is the lord of all the worlds! You should dance; you should dance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**pāl …** – Since you have been consuming materials obtained from cows, such as milk, ghee and curd, since materials such as beautiful sandalwood paste and campaka flower have been applied on your divine form, when your divine form moves, they too move; due to your happiness \[that you have been asked to dance by your mother\] since your divine lips, which are described by āṇḍāḷ in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 7-1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/08/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-7-1/) as “*karuppūram nāṟumō kamalappū nāṟumō*” (will \[the divine mouth\] have the sweet fragrance of medicated camphor or will it be fragrant like a lotus flower?), have blossomed, the naturally fragrant smell of lotus and medicated camphor come mixed with the earlier mentioned fragrances.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that due to consuming milk, ghee and curd, by stealing within and outside the house, he has a fragrance. Also, fragrance coming out of materials such as sandalwood paste, campaka flower etc which are applied by those who are affectionate towards him, gets emitted.

**kōlam …** – a few divine pearls which are like silver buds are shining inside the divine mouth which is like fragrant coral which is pleasing to look at.

**neelam …** – your divine lips are like matured *kovvaikkani* fruit, complementing the bluish colour of your divine form. The divine nectar, secreting from that divine mouth is dripping amidst the figurines of \[your\] five divine weapons, which are strung in a chain.

**ēlum …**– Oh, one who is the apt meaning of the vēdams \[sacred texts\]! Just as it has been mentioned in bhagavat gītā 15-15 “*vēdaiśca sarvair ahamēva vēdya*:” (Only I am known through all the vēdams), he is the most fitting meaning of all the vedams. You should perform *sengīrai*.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: *ēlum* – apt; only that entity who is the apt meaning of all the vēdams is the lord of the seven worlds.

**ēḻulagum …** – Oh, one who is the lord of all the worlds! You should mercifully perform dance.

We shall next consider the 10<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.5.10. Sengamalak kalalil

*sengamalak kaḻalil siṟṟidaḻ pōl viralil     sēr tigaḻ āḻigaḷum kiṇkiṇiyum araiyiltangiya pon vadamum tāḷa nan mādaḷaiyin    pūvodu pon maṇiyum mōdiramum kiṟiyummangala aimbadaiyum tōḷ vaḷaiyum kuḻaiyum    magaramum vāḷigaḷum cuttiyum ottu ilagaengaḷ kudikku arasē! āduga sengīrai     ēḻulagum udaiyāy! āduga ādugavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sem kamalam – matching a reddish lotus; kaḻalil – in the divine feet; siṟu idaḻ pōl – like contracted petals (inside that lotus flower); viralil – in the divine toes; sēr – together; tigaḻ – shining; āḻigaḷum – divine rings; kiṇkiṇiyum – divine anklet; araiyil – on the divine waist; tangiya – donning; pon vadamum – golden waist-cord; tāḷa – having a stalk; nal – eminent; mādaḷaiyin pūvodu – with mādaḷam flower; pon maṇiyum – strung in-between with golden spheres; mōdiramum – finger rings; kiṟiyum – bracelet with small corals applied on the divine wrist; mangalam – being auspicious; ai padaiyum – divine five weapons on a chain; tōḷ vaḷaiyum – rings on the divine shoulder; kuḻaiyum – divine ear ornaments; magaramum – divine ear rings; vāḷigaḷum – ornaments over the divine ears; cuttiyum – the ornament, cutti on the divine forehead; ottu – matching well; ilaga – to shine; engaḷ – our; kudikku – for the clan; arasē! – oh, one who is the king!; āduga sengīrai – you should perform sengīrai; ēḻ ulagum – for all the seven worlds; udaiyāy – oh, one who is the lord!; āduga āduga – you should dance; you should dance

**Перевод:**

**The divine rings are shining on the divine toes which are on the divine feet, appearing like the inner petals of a reddish lotus flower; divine anklets, divine golden waist, golden spheres strung in-between mādaḷam flowers, rings on the divine fingers, bracelet made of small corals on the divine wrist, figurines of the five divine weapons on a chain, rings on the divine shoulders, ornaments on the divine ears, divine ear rings, cutti on the divine forehead, are fitting well and shining. Oh, one who is the king of our clan! You should perform sengīrai! Oh, one who is the head of all the worlds! You should dance; you should dance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**sengamalam …** – on the divine feet which are like reddish lotus, the divine toes are like the inner petals of that lotus flower. On these toes, rings, which are shining well, have been adorned, fitting so well with the toes that it would appear that the rings were there on the toes from birth itself. On the divine waist, *kiṇkiṇi* \[divine waist chain\] is adorned; alternatively, *kiṇkiṇi* would refer to the anklet on the divine ankles, to go with the toe rings. This is the *sēvadik kiṇkiṇi* seen in the second padigam.

**araiyil tangiya pon vadamum** – the golden cord which is always adorned on the divine waist.

**tāḷa nan mādaḷaiyin pūvodu pon maṇiyum** – just as it has been mentioned in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1-3-2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/07/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-1-3-2/) “*udaiyār kaṇamaṇiyōdu oṇmādaḷam pū*” (along with the golden waist cord, the cord with *mādaḷam pū*), the eminent *mādaḷam* cord with golden spheres strung in-between.

**mōdiramum kiṟiyum** – the golden rings adorned on the divine fingers on the divine hand and the bracelet on the divine wrist, with small corals.

**managala aim padaiyum** – the auspicious śrī pancāyudam (figurines of the divine five weapons), adorned on the divine chest.

**tōḷ vaḷaiyum** – complementing that, the rings adorned on the two divine shoulders

**kuḻaiyum** – the divine ear ornaments \[on the lower portions of the divine ears\]

**magaramum** – the divine ear rings \[on the middle portions of the divine ears\]

**vāḷigaḷum** – the divine ear ornaments \[on the upper portions of the divine ears\]

**cuttiyum** – fixed on one side to the divine locks, hanging on the divine forehead, the ornament *cutti*

**ottu ilaga** – since these are hanging on either side, swaying \[when he dances\], they shine brightly; this implies that they shine apt for the splendorous divine form

**engaḷ kudikku arasē!** – Oh, one who is the head of our clan! You should perform *sengīrai*.

**ēḻulagum …** – Oh, one who is the lord of all the worlds! You should mercifully perform dance.

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.5.11. Annamum minuruvum

*annamum mīn uruvum āḷariyum kuṟaḷum    āmaiyum ānavanē! āyargaḷ nāyaganē!en avalam kaḷaivāy! āduga sengīrai    ēḻ ulagum udaiyāy! āduga āduga enṟuanna nadai madavāḷ asōdai uganda parisu    āna pugaḻp puduvaip pattan uraitta tamiḻinnisai mālai ip pattum vallār uloagil    eṇ disaiyum pugaḻ mikku inbam adu eyduvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

annamum – “swan; mīn uruvum – fish; āḷ ariyum – narasimha \[lion face and human body\]; kuṟaḷum – vāmana \[dwarf\]; āmaiyum – tortoise \[thus, in all these forms\]; ānavanē! – oh, one who incarnated!; āyargaḷ – for the herd-folk; nāyaganē! – oh, one who is the head!; en avalam – my distress; kaḷaivāy! – oh, one who removed!; sengīrai āduga – \[you\] should mercifully perform sengīrai; ēḻ ulagum – for the seven worlds; udaiyāy! – oh, one who is the lord!; āduga āduga enṟu – you should dance; you should dance” saying so; annam – like a swan; nadai – having the beauty of gait; madavāḷ – having simplicity; asōdai – yaśōdāp pirātti; uganda – saying with happiness; parisu – manner; Ana – with abundance; pugaḻ – having fame; puduvaip pattan – bhattar pirān, who incarnated in śrī villibuttūr; uraitta – mercifully said; in isai – having sweet tune; tamiḻ mālaigaḷ – garlands of tamiḻ \[words\]; ippattum – these ten pāsurams; vallār – those who are capable of reciting; ulagil – even as they live in this world; eṇ disaiyum – in eight directions; pugaḻ – fame; mikku inbam adu – lot of comfort \[bhagavat anubhavam, experiencing emperumān\]; eyduvar – will attain

**Перевод:**

**yaśōdāp pirātti, who has the gait of swan and who has simplicity, had said with happiness “Oh, one who incarnated as swan, as fish, as narasimha, as vāmana and as tortoise! Oh, one who is the lord of herd-folk! Oh, one who removed my distress! You should mercifully perform sengīrai. Oh, one who is the lord of seven worlds! You should dance; you should dance”. bhattar pirān, who has abundant fame and who incarnated in śrī villibuttūr, had mercifully composed that yaśōdāp pirātti’s words as garlands of tamiḻ, with sweet tunes. Those who are capable of reciting these ten pāsurams, will attain fame in the eight directions and experience emperumān, even as they live in this samsāram.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In this last pāsuram, āḻvār mentions the benefit which will accrue to those who learn this decad and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**annamum …** – Oh, one who incarnated as *hamsa* \[swan\], which instructed vēdam, as *matsya*, \[fish\] which was the support during deluge, as *narasimha* \[lion head with human body\], who destroyed the monster hiraṇya kaśyap, as *vāmana* \[dwarf\] who fulfilled the desire of indran \[head of celestial entities\] and as *kūrma* \[tortoise\] which was the support for mantara mountain \[when the milky ocean was churned\]! Through all these, it is explained that emperumān transforms himself from his most distinguished, auspicious divine form, for the sake of his followers, to lowly forms and protects his followers in line with the activities of the species in which he has incarnated.

**āyargaḷ nāyaganē** – Unlike those incarnations \[where he protected a few entities\], incarnating to reduce the excess load on earth, one who became the head of herd-folk!

**en avalam kaḷaivāy** – oh, one who removed my distress of “What will befall you?” in all manner, by protecting yourself!

**āduga sengīrai** – You should mercifully perform *sengīrai*.

**ēḻulagum …** – Oh, who is the lord of all the worlds! You should dance; you should dance. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *adu* \[*inbam adu*\] indicates that those who learn these pāsurams will get to carry out mangaḷāśāsanam for emperumān in śrī vaikuṇṭam.

**annam …** – the manner in which yaśōdāp pirātti, who has the beauty of swan’s gait and obedience, had told.

**Ana …** – born as a brāhmaṇa, āḻvār took over the pathos of herd-folk, enjoyed the experience of yaśōdāp pirātti in her time, at a much later point of time, with a fame which was more abundant than hers. Those who are able to learn these pāsurams which were mercifully composed by periyāḻvār, who was the controller of śrī villibuttūr, in tamiḻ language, with sweet tunes…

**ulagil …** – even as they live in this world, they will attain fame transcending the eight directions and will attain the eminent comfort of *bhagavat anubhavam* \[experiencing emperumān\] in a vibhūti where even nityasūris cannot enjoy \[viz. in samsāram\].

We shall next consider the pravēśam of the next tirumoḻi.

## 1.6.1. Manikkak kinkini

*māṇikkak kiṇkiṇi ārppa marungin mēlāṇip ponnāl seyda āy pon udai maṇipēṇip pavaḷa vāy muttu ilangap paṇḍukāṇi koṇḍa kaigaḷāl cappāṇi karunguḻal kuttanē! cappāṇi*

**Пословный перевод:**

āṇi – of highest purity; poṇṇal – with gold; seyda – having been made of; āy – without any fault; pon – attractive; udai maṇi – having waist cord; marungin mēl – on the waist; māṇikkam – made of carbuncle; kiṇkiṇi – girdle of tinkling bells; ārppa – as it makes a noise; pēṇi – desirously; pavaḷam – like coral; vāy – divine mouth; muttu – divine pearls \[teeth\]; ilanga – to shine (the opinion is that he should smile\]; paṇḍu – earlier; kāṇi – earth; koṇḍa – taking (from mahābali), symbolically through water; kaigaḷāl – with divine hands; cappāṇi – you should carry out cappāṇi (cappāṇi – a type of dance, while clapping the hands); karum kuḻal kuttanē! – oh, little child, having dark locks! You should clap your hands

**Перевод:**

**You are donning the waist cord, which is made of the purest gold, without any fault, and which is attractive, on your divine waist. You are having a girdle of tinkling bells, made of carbuncle, over it. Even as it makes a noise, and you smile desirously such that the divine pearls \[teeth\] inside your divine mouth, which is like coral, shine, you should clap your hands, with which you had earlier taken earth from mahābali, symbolically through water. Oh, little child, who has dark locks! You should clap your hands.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**māṇikkam …** – On top of the cord, made of faultless pure gold, worn on the divine waist, is a girdle, with its carbuncle bells tinkling. In the verse “*āy pon udai maṇi*”, the term *āy* refers to being visible, and without any fault. Since *āṇip ponnāl seyda* has been said first, where the term *pon* has been taken to mean gold, the term *pon* \[in the verse *āy pon udai maṇi*\] is taken to refer to beauty. Will a carbuncle tinkling bell make a noise? If the clapper \[bell’s tongue\] is made of carbuncle and the bell, outside, is also made of carbuncle, it will not make a noise. However, if the clapper is made of carbuncle and the outside bell is made of gold or any other metal, it will make a noise.

**pēṇi …** – instead of clapping due to my compulsion, you should clap with your desire, with your divine mouth, which is like coral, and the divine pearls, whose colours complement each other, shining. Alternatively, the term *pēṇi* would also refer to protection. kriṣṇa should protect his divine form, such that it does not become tired.

**paṇḍu …** – At a previous point of time. Just as it has been said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4-3-9 “*kudam kaiyil maṇ koṇḍu*” (taking the land in your divine, cupped hands \[through water, symbolically\]), with the divine hands with which you had taken water as a symbol of having been granted three steps of land when you had gone to mahābali. This conveys the meaning – for the sake of your followers, without considering your eminence, you are willing to transform your divine form and carry out their task.

**cappāṇi** – you should clap.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the action *cappāṇi* highlights performing *anjali* \[cupping the hands together, in salutation\]. He says further that since āḻvār is asking for performing *cappāṇi* twice, he is highlighting, through kriṣṇa, that we should have nothing in our hands while considering emperumān as both *upāyam* (means to attain emperumān) and as *upēyam* (carrying out servitude to emperumān, after attaining him). The reason for saying *kāṇi* is that while many say proudly, while referring to their land etc as “This is mine” and gift that to others too, the term says that this earth \[samsāram\] is his. It is this that he had to take through alms.

**karum kuḻal …** – Oh, one who has dark locks and childishness! You should clap.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.6.2. Ponnarai nanodu

*ponnarai nāṇodu māṇikkak kiṇkiṇitannarai ādat tanic cutti tāḻndādaennarai mēl ninṟu iḻindu ungaḷ āyar tammannarai mēl kottāy cappāṇi māyavanē! kottāy cappāṇi*

**Пословный перевод:**

pon – made of gold; arai nāṇodu – together with the cord on divine waist; māṇikkam – made of carbuncle; kiṇkiṇi – girdle of tinkling bells; than – its dwelling place; arai – in the divine waist region; Ada – as it makes a noise; tani – unique; cutti – \[ornament\] cutti \[on the divine forehead\]; tāḻndu – lowering on the forehead; Ada – as it sways; en arai mēl ninṟu – from my waist; iḻindu – getting down; ungaḷ – as your father; āyar tam – for the herd-folk; man – king, śrī nandagōpar’s; arai mēl – from lap, clap \[your divine hands\]; māyavanē! – oh, one who is amazing! You should clap

**Перевод:**

**Even as the girdle with tinkling bells made of carbuncle, which is together with the golden waist cord, makes a sound on its dwelling place of waist, and the unique cutti ornament lowers down on the divine forehead and sways, you should get down from my waist, get on to the lap of śrī nandagōpar, who is your father and the chief of herd-folk, and clap your divine hands. Oh, one who is an amazing entity! You should clap.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**pon …** – even as the girdle bells, made of carbuncle, staying together with the golden waist cord, make a sound on their dwelling place…

**than …** – even as the ornament *cutti*, which is hung from the divine locks, lowers on to the divine forehead and sways…

**en …** – you should get down from my lap, get on to the lap of your father, śrī nandagōpar, who is also the head of herd-folk and clap your hands. Through this, yaśōdāp pirātti says that since she enjoys his clapping his hands from nandagōpar’s lap rather than from her lap, she is requesting him to carry that out mercifully.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that just as śrī nandagōpar is happy when kriṣṇa is on yaśōdāp pirātti’s lap, she is happy when kriṣṇa is on nandagōpar’s lap. Hence, she tells him to clap, while sitting on his lap.

**māyavanē!** – Oh, one who is an amazing entity!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *māyavanē* refers to kriṣṇa having amazing powers.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.
