## 1.6.3. Panmani muttu

*panmaṇi muttin pavaḷam padittu annaen maṇi vaṇṇan! ilangu poṟṟōttin mēlnin maṇi vāy ilanga ninnammai tanammaṇi mēl kottāy cappāṇi āḻiyam kaiyanē! cappāṇi*

**Пословный перевод:**

en – as mine; maṇi vaṇṇan! – oh, one who has the form of a bluish gemstone!; pal maṇi – different types of gems; muttu – along with pearls; in – enjoyable; pavaḷam – coral too; padittu – embedded; anna – having well spread-out beauty; ilangu – shining; pon tōttin mēl – more than the beauty of golden ear rings; nin – your; maṇi – beautiful; vāy – in the divine mouth; muttu – divine pearls \[teeth\]; ilanga – to shine; nin – one who bore you; ammai than – mother yaśōdāp pirātti’s; ammaṇi mēl – from her lap, clap; āḻi – divine disc; am kaiyanē! – oh, one having in your divine hand! Clap

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who is mine, who has the form of a bluish gemstone and who has on his ear rings, embedded gemstones of different types! With the beauty of your divine teeth inside your divine mouth shining more than that golden ear ring, you should clap your divine hands from your mother, yaśōdāp pirātti’s, lap. Oh, one who has the divine disc on your beautiful hand! You should clap.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that since playing from the lap of yaśōdāp pirātti is causing happiness for him, śrī nandagōpar tells kriṣṇa to play from her lap, again.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**en maṇivaṇṇan** – Oh, one who is obedient towards me such that I could take pride that you are mine and who has the form of a bluish gemstone!

**pan maṇi …** – surpassing the beauty of the golden ear ring embedded with gemstones such as carbuncle, emerald, topaz, diamond, sapphire, onyx and cat’s eye as well as with pearl and sweet coral…

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that all the gems were equal, without any difference among them. He further says that śrī nandagōpar is proud that kriṣṇa is his son since he is obedient while he \[nandagōpar\] belongs to kriṣṇa and that the divine ear rings are shining bright because they are adorning kriṣṇa’s ears.

**nin …** – the divine pearls \[divine teeth\] in your beautiful, divine mouth to shine

**ninnammai …** – you should clap from the lap of yaśōdāp pirātti who is fortunate to have given birth to you. *ammaṇi* – lap. Through this, it is clear that śrī nandagōpar desires to see kriṣṇa clap from the lap of yaśōdāp pirātti rather than from his lap.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: āḻvār says “*ninnammai*” just as it has been said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2-2-9 “*ivanaippeṟṟa vayiṟu udaiyāḷ*” (one who was fortunate to have the stomach which gave birth to him) and as in sahasranāmam “*sukhatātam*” \[while recounting the greatness of sage vyāsa, the importance arising out of being the father of sage sukhar is mentioned\].

**āḻi am kaiyanē** – this refers to one who has the divine disc on his divine hand. It would also refer to one having ring on his divine finger.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when kriṣṇa claps his hand, the divine disc and the divine conch, knowing kriṣṇa’s divine mind, would leave his divine hand, stand at a distance and feel happy looking at kriṣṇa clapping with his divine hands.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.6.4. Tunila murratte

*tūnilā muṟṟattē pōndu viḷaiyādavānilā ambulee! candirā! vā enṟunī nilā nin pugaḻā ninṟa āyar tamkōnilāvak kottāy cappāṇi kudandaik kidandānē! cappāṇi*

**Пословный перевод:**

vān nilā – roaming in the sky; ambulee! – oh, ambulee! \[moon\]; candirā! – oh, candran! \[moon\]; pōndu – coming; tūnilā – having beautiful moon; muṟṟattē – in the courtyard; viḷaiyāda – for playing; vā enṟu – saying “Come”; nin – you; pugaḻā ninṟa – praising; āyar tam – for the herd-folk; kō – nandagōpar, who is their head; nilāva – to feel happy, clap your hands; kudandai – in tirukkudandai; kidandānē! – oh, one who is reclining!; nī nilā – you should stand and clap

**Перевод:**

**Oh, candran, who is moving about in the sky! Herd-folk are praising you, calling you to come and play in the courtyard. nandagōpar is the head of such herd-folk. You \[addressing kriṣṇa\] should clap your hands so that nandagōpar is happy. Oh, one who is reclining in tirukkudandai! You should stand and clap your hands.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tū nilā …** – come to the courtyard which has moon.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that yaśōdāp pirātti carried kriṣṇa on her waist to the courtyard, calling candran “Oh ambulee, who is roaming about in the sky! Oh, candran! Come”, calling candran as *ambulee* too, in the way a child would call him.

**viḷaiyāda …** – calling candran too “Oh, ambulee who is moving about in the sky! Oh, candra! Come and play”

**nī nilā** – you should stand.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *nilāva* refers to nandagōpar and that yaśōdāp pirātti is asking kriṣṇa to clap his hands such that nandagōpar exists.

**nin …** – You should clap your hands such that nandagōpar, who is delighted with your activities and who praises you, and who is the leader of herd-folks, becomes happy and shines.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that nandagōpar praises kriṣṇa for both his eminence and simplicity. He further says that nandagōpar, through his qualities, has controlled and ruled the herd-folk who are ignorant and are individualistic.

**kudandai …** – Oh, one who is reclining in tirukkudandai, being under the controller of your followers!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: Oh, one who is reclining in tirukkudandai just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 5-8-1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/08/thiruvaimozhi-5-8-1-aravamudhe/) “*tigaḻak kidandāy kaṇḍēn*” (I am seeing you, in the lying posture, shining) and in [tiruccanda viruttam 61](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/01/thiruchchandha-viruththam-61/) ”*kidandvāṟu eḻundirundu pēsu*” (you should speak to me, getting up from your posture of lying down).

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.6.5. Puttiyil serum

*puttiyil sēṟum puḻudiyum koṇḍu vanduatti amukki agam pukku aṟiyāmēcattit tayirum tadāvinil veṇṇeyum uṇpattikkanṟē! kottāy cappāṇi paṟpanābhā! kottāy cappāṇi*

**Пословный перевод:**

puttiyil – in the divine waist; sēṟum – mud; puḻudiyum – and dirt; koṇḍu vandu – bringing them; atti – applying; amukki – such that it is felt; agam pukku – entering inside; aṟiyāmē – without anyone knowing; catti – saved in pots; tayirum – curd, and; tadāvinil – saved in large pots; veṇṇeyum – butter too; uṇ – as one who had consumed in large quantities; patti – roaming; kanṟē! – oh, one who is arrogant like a calf! You should clap; paṟpam – divine lotus flower; nābhā! – oh, one who has in the divine navel! You should clap

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa applied mud and dirt on his divine waist, embraced yaśōdāp pirātti such that she felt the mud and dirt on her. He then entered the house without anyone knowing and consumed curd and butter, saved and kept in pots. Oh, one who roams around like a calf which eats food unknown to the farmer! You should clap your hands. Oh, one who has the divine lotus \[with brahmā on it\] which created the worlds! You should clap.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**putti …** – bringing mud and dirt on his waist. Since there is water on some parts of his divine form just as it has been mentioned in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1-9-1 “*cottuccottu ennat tuḷikkat tuḷikka*” (with droplets of water from inside the body coming out and dripping), when he rolls on dirt, that which sticks to that part of his divine form which has water, becomes mud and that which sticks to that part of his divine form, which does not have water, becomes dry dirt.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that in order to make it real when he incarnates in various species, his activities in such species will correspond to those species. Thus, fluid from inside the body coming out is in line with that. The fluid could be sweat or other fluid coming out from inside the divine form.

**atti amukki** – since he comes in with his divine form like this and hugs yaśōdāp pirātti firmly, the mud and dirt transfer on to her such that she feels them well.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that if she had prevented him from applying the mud and dirt on her, he would have got furious. Hence, she allows him to do that, with a smile.

**agam pukku …** – running inside the house, without me, who had kept them, knowing about it, eating curd and butter kept in pots.

**patti …** – oh, one who roams around like a calf which steals and eats, making it appear that stealing is your full-time work! You should clap.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that a farmer would have kept hay etc, outside the fence, safely. The calf would go there, without the farmer knowing about it and eat that hay. In a similar fashion, kriṣṇa enters the house without yaśōdāp pirātti knowing about it and eats curd and butter, kept there by her. Hence, āḻvār calls him as *pattikkanṟē*.

**paṟpanābhā** – Oh, one who has the divine lotus \[with brahmā on it\] which is the reason for the creation of all the worlds, in your divine navel!

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.6.6. Tarittu nurruvar

*tārittu nūṟṟuvar tandai sol koḷḷādupōruyttu vandu pugundavar maṇṇāḷapāritta mannar padap panjavarkku anṟutēruytta kaigaḷāl cappāṇi dēvaki singamē! cappāṇi*

**Пословный перевод:**

tandai – one who is the father of all the worlds, your; sol – word; tārittu koḷḷādu – not tolerating; pōr – war; uyttu – to conduct; vandu – came as arrogant people; pugundavar – those who entered the battlefield; maṇ āḷa – to rule the entire earth (after destroying the pāṇḍavas); pāritta – those who thought deep; mannar – kings; nūṟṟuvar – all the hundred persons; pada – to be killed; panjavarkku – for the five pāṇḍavas; anṟu – on that day when they prayed to you; tēr – chariot; uytta – conducted; kaigaḷāl – with the divine hands, clap; dēvaki – born from dēvakip pirātti’s stomach; singamē! – oh, one who is proud like a lion cub! Clap your hands

**Перевод:**

**The hundred kings \[kauravas, starting from duryōdana\] did not listen to your words, you being the father of all the worlds, when you told them to share their kingdom with pāṇḍavas. They thought that they could kill the five pāṇḍavas and rule the entire world themselves. They entered the battlefield with arrogance. To kill them, you had conducted the chariot for the pāṇḍavas, when they prayed to you to help them. Clap, with those divine hands, with which you conducted the chariot. Oh, one who was born from the stomach of dēvakip pirātti, as a proud lion cub! Clap your hands.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tārittu** – the short syllable in the word *tarittu* has got lengthened as *tārittu*. *tarittu* refers to tolerating. It also refers to listening, with intelligence.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says: thinking with pride “Where is their existence? We are a hundred; they are only five” without fulfilling the words of one who is *nirupādika pitā* (father without any cause, viz. emperumān)

**nūṟṟuvar** – this is to be combined with the next term.

**tandai sol koḷḷādu** – just as it has been said in mahābhāratam āraṇya parvam 192-56 “*sarvēśāmēva lōkānām pitā mātā ca mādava*:” (only the divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi is the father and mother of all entities in the worlds), since you are the father of all, you had gone as a messenger \[to the court of dritarāśtra\] in order to unite the two sides \[kauravas and pāṇḍavas\]. You had said “pāṇḍavas and you need not have enmity towards each other; both of you have a right to enjoy the kingdom; hence, divide the kingdom into two and enjoy your share; if you are not willing to do that, give to each of the five pāṇḍavas, two villages; if even that is not agreeable, give one village each to them so that they could reside”. Without accepting any of your words …

**pōr uyttu …** – just as it has been said in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam “*vīra bhōjñā vasundarā*” (one who is valorous will enjoy the earth), deciding to wage a war, they entered the battlefield with arrogance. The hundred kings\[kauravas\] wanted to destroy pāṇḍavas in the war and rule over the entire earth. To ensure that all the hundred, without leaving behind anyone, get killed…

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: \[the kauravas\] entered the battlefield with their armies and weapons, against those who are favoured by kriṣṇa. *maṇṇāḷa* – kings who thought that they alone will rule the entire earth, perished, just like a flowering tree withers and falls down.

**panjavarkku …**  – pāṇḍavas felt isolated, without any help other than you. With the divine hands with which you had conducted the chariot for them such that you had, without holding any weapons during the war, annihilated the opponents \[hundred kauravas\] through your expertise in conducting the chariot, you should clap. While the term *mannar* \[kings\] is in plural, the term *pada* \[died\] is in singular. Instead of saying “That person died; this person died; he died etc”, this term establishes that all of them died. He \[āḻvār\] did not see anyone remaining with life.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the reason for saying *panjavar* \[five persons\] instead of pāṇḍavar is because āḻvār had said *nūṟṟuvar* \[hundred people\] earlier and he wants to maintain the count. *uyttal* – to conduct. āḻvār says that just as kriṣṇa had shown *āśrita pāratantryam* (fulfilling desire due to dependence on his followers) in the battlefield, he should fulfil his \[āḻvār’s\] desire too here \[by clapping his hands\].

**dēvaki singamē** – Oh, one who is arrogant like a lion cub, having incarnated from the stomach of dēvakip pirātti! You should clap.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the arrogance results from being born in a royal clan. He says further that if the term had been *tāruytta* \[instead of *tēruytta*\] the term *tār* would refer to parade; marching with the army in a parade.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.6.7. Parandittu ninra

*parandittu ninṟa padu kadal tannaiiranditta kaimmēl eṟi tirai mōdakarandittu ninṟa kadalaik kalangasaram totta kaigaḷāl cappāṇi sārngaviṟ kaiyanē! cappāṇi*

**Пословный перевод:**

parandittu ninṟa – being expansive; padu – being deep; kadal – ocean (on the southern side); tannai – regarding it; iranditta – one who carried out śaraṇāgati (surrendered); kai mēl – on the divine hands; eṟi – throwing up droplets; tirai – waves; mōda – flung; karandittu ninṟa – hiding, not showing the face; kadalai – on varuṇan, who is the lord of oceans; kalanga – such that his intestine churned; saram – arrows; totta – one who shot; kaigaḷāl – clap, with those divine hands; sārngam – known as “śrī śarngam”; vil – bow; kaiyanē! – oh, one who holds in the divine hand! Clap with those divine hands

**Перевод:**

**Ocean is expansive and deep. On the divine hands of the entity who surrendered to it, the \[king of\] ocean flung droplets through its waves, by blowing, and hid himself, without showing his face. You should clap with the divine hands with which you had prepared to shoot arrows on that varuṇan. Oh, one who holds the divine bow, śrī śārngam! You should clap.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**parandu …** – Just as it has been mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 19-31 “*apramēyō mahōdadi*” (this ocean, which cannot be measured), the ocean is such expansive that its boundary cannot be seen and its depth cannot be estimated. The term *padu* refers to depth. Also, it refers to gems such as rubies which are available in abundance.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that the ocean was such expansive that its length, breadth and depth could not be estimated.

**tannai …** – Just as it has been mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 21-1 “*anjalim prāngmukha*: *krutvā pratiśiśyē mahōdadē*” (emperumān, looking at the eastern direction, performed *anjali* (cupping hands together in salutation) towards the ocean), śrī rāma had surrendered to the ocean, saying “You should provide a way to reach lankā”. The ocean flung droplets of water on his divine hands.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here, for the term *ittu ninṟa padu kadal tannai* – the ocean gave rubies and other gems to those who attained it, without drying up. The term *padu* would refer both to gemstones such as rubies and to depth. For the term *irandu* … he says – considering the ocean’s magnanimity earlier \[in giving gemstones etc\], and as per vibhīśaṇa’s instruction as mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 19-21 “*samudram rāghavō rājā śaraṇam kartum \[gantum\] arhati*” (the ocean is apt to be surrendered to by king śrī rāma\], śrī rāma surrendered to the ocean. Though one could surrender, the act will fructify only if the entity to whom one has surrendered has the requisite qualities \[of accepting and granting refuge\]. On the hands which sought alms from it, the ocean flung droplets of water through its waves.

**karandu …** – the \[lord of\] ocean had hidden, without showing the face. Becoming furious, śrī rāma told lakśmaṇa, as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 21-21 “*cāpamānaya saumitrē*! *śarāmścāsi viśōpamān*” (Oh, lakśmaṇa! Bring bow and arrows which are like the poison of snake) and placed the arrows on the bow such that the ocean, becoming bewildered and in fear, threw up the sand from the bottom of the ocean to top in an agitated way. You should clap with those divine hands, which had touched the bow.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *kadal* refers to varuṇan who is its controller and representative lord.

**sārngavil kaiyanē** – Oh, one who had the beauty then, holding the bow and arrow! Alternatively, this shows the valour even as he held the bow then.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.6.8. Kurakku inattale

*kurakkinattālē kurai kadal tannainerukki aṇai katti neeḷ nīr ilangaiarakkar aviya adu kaṇaiyālēnerukkiya kaigaḷāl cappāṇi nēmi am kaiyanē!cappāṇi*

**Пословный перевод:**

kurai kadal tannai – ocean, which was resounding; kurakku inattālē – with the troop of monkeys; nerukki – such that water would be stagnant on either side; aṇai katti – building a bridge (in between); neeḷ nīr – having the expansive ocean as a moat; ilangai – present in lankā; arakkar – demons; aviya – to be annihilated; adu – torturing; kaṇaiyālē – with arrows; nerukkiya – closely combating; kaigaḷāl – with the divine hands, clap; nēmi am kaiyanē – Oh, one who has the divine disc in the divine hands! Clap

**Перевод:**

**With the help of monkey troops, you had built a bridge across the resounding ocean such that water was stagnant on either side \[allowing the entire army to pass through the ocean\]. You should clap with your divine hands with which you had tortured demons who were inhabiting lankā, for which the ocean was functioning as a moat, annihilating them. Oh, one who holds the divine discus in your divine hands! You should clap.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kurakku** – monkeys are fearful of water and live on high lands. With such monkeys, you had built a bridge across the ocean which, due to its expansive and deep nature, was resounding in its agitation, in such a manner that water on either side of the bridge was stagnant.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that while monkeys live on mountain tops and caves, without any connection with ocean, if he \[emperumān\] decides, there is nothing which cannot be connected.

**neeḷ nīr …** – just as it has been said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1-6-7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-6-7-nil-kadal/) “*neeḷ kadal sūḻ ilangai*” (lankā, surrounded by expansive ocean), since demons were having lankā, surrounded by expansive ocean which was functioning as a moat for them, as their dwelling place, they thought “When we have this protection, there is no shortcoming for us”. With your arrows, which have the quality of eliminating your enemies, you had annihilated the demons. Clap with the divine hands, which had killed the demons.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the demons, due to their arrogance of having ocean as their protection, were inhabiting lankā, showing their fire of independence through their enjoyment. śri rāma, through his arrows, made that fire as vheatvorms \[*viḷakkup piṇam* or *vittil pūcci*\], annihilating them, keeping that fire in their stomachs. Through monkeys, he created islands in ocean. Through torturing arrows, he fought and annihilated demons. When he takes aim, we do not see any distinction between “monkey” and “arrow”. Since āḻvār says *arakkar aviya* (annihilate demons) with *adu kaṇai* (torturing arrows), the arrows act like water for fire; since śrī rāma had earlier said “*sāgaram sōśayiśyāmi*” (I will dry up the ocean), the arrows had acted as fire for water. Since he had killed a vāli, a kara, a dūśaṇa, a mārīca et al, it is called as *adukaṇai* (torturing arrow).

**nēmi am kaiyanē cappāṇi** – Oh, one who has the beautiful, divine disc in your divine hands! Clap. Since arrows were there for annihilating enemies, the divine disc was present as a decorative ornament.

Here, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that the divine disc is termed beautiful since arrow has finished the work of annihilation. Alternatively, when it comes to *karudumidam porudu* (waging a war at the place which he thinks of), there is no difference among disc, arrow and monkey.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.6.9. Alanditta tunai

*aḷanditta tūṇai avan tatta āngēvaḷarndittu vāḷugirccinga uruvāyuḷandottu iraṇiyan oṇmārvu agalampiḷanditta kaigaḷāl cappāṇi pēy mulai uṇḍānē! cappāṇi*

**Пословный перевод:**

aḷandu itta – constructed by hiraṇyan, after measuring; tūṇai – pillar; avan – he himself; tatta – kicked furiously; āngē – in that pillar itself (at the place where he hit); vāḷ – cruel, like a sword; ugir – having nails; singam uru āy – in the form of narasimha \[lion face and human body\]; vaḷarndittu – growing up; uḷam – his heart; tottu – analysing (would he have become favourable, at the least, now?); iraṇiyan – hiraṇyan’s; oḷ – shiny; agalam – being broad; mārvu – chest; piḷanditta kaigaḷāl – with the hands, which tore, clap; pēy – pūtanā’s; mulai – (poisoned) bosom; uṇḍānē – oh, one who consumed (along with her life)! Clap

**Перевод:**

**hiraṇyāsuran (monster, hiraṇyan) had himself measured and constructed a pillar. When he hit that pillar, while ascertaining the existence of emperumān, you had grown inside that pillar itself, as narasimha, with nails as sharp and cruel as a sword. You should clap with the hands with which you had analysed the heart of hiraṇyan and tore his broad and shiny chest. Oh, one who had consumed the milk from pūtanā’s bosom, along with her life! You should clap.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**aḷandu …** – it was a pillar which he had measured to ensure that it was appropriate for him, and erected by hiraṇyan, lest someone say that “It was built with narasimha inside”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that hiraṇyan, who considers that there is no deity other than himself, had erected that pillar on a day which was fitting \[auspicious\] for him, grouting it well

**avan tatta** – if someone had hit that pillar, it could have been said that “Someone had hidden narasimha inside the hand and thrust narasimha inside that pillar”. Instead, hiraṇyan, unable to bear the words of prahlādan \[his son\] who had sworn, as in [tiruvāimoḻi 2-8-9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-8-9-engumulan-kannan/) “*engum uḷan*” (he is omnipresent), that emperumān was present everywhere, he became furious with his son, just as it has been said in [periya tirumoḻi 2-3-8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/08/periya-thirumozhi-2-3-8/) “*piḷḷaiyaic cīṟi veguṇḍu pudaippa*” (hitting (the pillar) after becoming very furious with his son), and due to excess of that fury, hit the pillar saying “But, the one, who you are referring to, is not present here”.

**āngē** – If emperumān had manifested himself in a place other than where hiraṇyan had hit, he would have said that his solemn declaration that “He is not here” is true. Hence, in that pillar, in the same place where hiraṇyan hit …

**vaḷarndittu** – narasimha grew huge such that hiraṇyan, who was said to be huge as said in periya tirumoḻi 9-4-4 “*pariya iraṇiyan*” (hiraṇyan who was huge), appeared like a dwarf.

**vāḷ ugirc cinga uruvāy** – hiraṇyan had obtained boons from brahmā, rudra et al, by which he could not be killed by weapons known, by any of the four species such as dēva, manuśya et al \[celestial, human et al\] etc. Ensuring that these boons were not compromised, emperumān appeared in the form of narasimha, with splendorous nails.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: emperumān appeared with lion on top. śrī gajēndran \[elephant which was caught by a crocodile in a pond when the elephant had entered to pluck a lotus flower in order to offer to emperumān\] had cried out, as mentioned in siṟiya tirumadal “*nārāyaṇā*! *vārāy*” (Oh, nārāyaṇa! Come). While emperumān is pervading everywhere, inside any object, at all times, prahlādan saying that nārāyaṇa is present everywhere is similar to gajēndran saying “*maṇivaṇṇā nāgaṇaiyāy*” (Oh, one who has a divine form like a gemstone! Oh, one who is lying on the mattress of ādiśēśan!). There \[in the case of gajēndran\] there was no doubt about emperumān’s existence. However, here hiraṇyan had that doubt. Hence, considering the all-pervading concept of “*engum uḷan*”, since there was a reason required for demonstrating that, since hiraṇyan was torturing emperumān’s follower, unable to tolerate that, while he had tolerated the offences of hiraṇyan doubting his existence earlier, now, he appeared in the same place and at the same time when hiraṇyan hit the pillar. Thus, in the [tiruvāimoḻi pāsuram 2-8-9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-8-9-engumulan-kannan/) “*āngē appoḻudē avan vīya…*” (there itself, at the same time (when hiraṇyan hit the pillar) and to destroy that hiraṇyan …), through the term *angu*, contrast with some other place \[he appeared at the same place\], through the term *appoḻudē* contrast with some other time \[he appeared at the same time\] and through the term *avan vīya*, contrast with any other form have been indicated. In the same manner, *avan tatta āngē* also indicates the same. In order to prevent appearance of his divine weapons, he appeared with *vāḷugir* (shiny nails).

**uḷam tottu** – prahlādan had said \[that emperumān is\] “present everywhere”. In the place where hiraṇyan had declared “He is not present here”, emperumān had appeared. Also, he had appeared in a form which was not included in any of the forms that he had taken exceptions from.  Just as it has been said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4-9-8 “*siram paṟṟi mudi idiyak kaṇ pidunga vāy alaṟat teḻittān*” (holding hiraṇyan by his head, emperumān tore his hair such that his eyes popped out, he cried out aloud), each of emperumān’s strikes was severe on hiraṇyan. emperumān thought that with all these, hiraṇyan, out of fear, would have softened his stand and would have become favourable towards him. Hence, he analysed hiraṇyan’s heart for any softness …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that emperumān examined the heart of hiraṇyan to see if there was any change in his stance: (1) Despite all the torment which hiraṇyan meted out to prahlādan, since prahlādan was not affected, he could have let go of his arrogance and become favourable. (2) When prahlādan told him “At least now, perform an anjali to emperumān”, he could have recalled his earlier offences and become favourable. (3) When hiraṇyan had denied emperumān’s existence and when emperumān appeared as narasimha, hiraṇyan could have thought of emperumān’s omnipresence, and due to his shame, could have become favourable. (4) After seeing the fierce form of *ugram* (fury) *vīram* (valour) etc of emperumān’s as narasimha, out of fear, he could have become favourable. (5) Unlike rāvaṇa, who, after losing his bow to śrī rāma, had to return to his palace empty handed, just as mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 59-140 “*cacāla cāpam ca mumōca vīra*:” (with his bow having fallen, he appeared like a valorous person), hiraṇyan did not have that opportunity to go back and come for another day’s battle. Due to lack of power, he could have become favourable. (6) After being hit by narasimha, as brought out by pāsurams such as periya tirumadal 35 “*vāy tagarttu*” (his mouth getting torn), [tiruccanda viruttam 25](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/10/thiruchchandha-viruththam-25/) “*urattinil karattai vaittu*” ((emperumān) kept his divine hand on (hiraṇyan’s) chest) and [periya tirumoḻi 2-3-8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/08/periya-thirumozhi-2-3-8/) “*ugirttalattai ūnṟināy*” ((you) firmly anchored your divine nails), hiraṇyan, due to sadness over all these, could have become favourable.

**iraṇiyan oṇ mārvu agalam** – hiraṇyan’s chest which was shiny and broad. *oḷ* – shiny; hiraṇyan’s chest was shiny due to the fire from narasimha’s anger and the fire of fear in hiraṇyan’s blood. The resultant heat made his chest to be shiny just as gold, melting in the presence of fire, would shine. This \[heat\] made it easy for narasimha’s divine nails to tear hiraṇyan’s body effortlessly. The term *agalam* \[broad\] suggests that due to the strength of his boons as well as the strength of his shoulders, hiraṇyan’s chest had become expansive, making it an apt prey for the divine nails of narasimha.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that hiraṇyan’s chest was such broad that there was sufficient space for emperumān to keep all his ten finger nails \[while tearing his chest\].

**piḷandu …** – just as it has been said in [periya tirumoḻi 5-3-3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/08/periya-thirumozhi-5-3-3/) “*udalagam irupiḷavāk kaiyil neeḷ ugirp padaiyadu vāyttavanē*” (Oh, one who had the army of long nails with which you had torn the body into two pieces!), you should clap with your divine hands, with the divine nails, with which you had torn the body of hiraṇyan into two pieces.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that emperumān tore his chest such that periya pirāttiyār was worried as to what will befall emperumān if his divine hands hit hiraṇyan’s hard bones just as it has been mentioned in [mudal tiruvandādi 23](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/07/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-23/) “*pūngōdaiyāḷ veruva*” (periya pirātti feared as to what will happen to the world). He further says that if kriṣṇa now claps his hands, āḻvār could see is there are any blood stains on his divine fingers.

**pēy mulai …** – pūtanā did not come in an unfavourable form, like hiraṇyan. She came deceitfully, in the form of (kriṣṇa’s) mother, as mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 1-5-6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/04/periya-thirumozhi-1-5-6/) “*tāyāy vanda pēy*” (the fiend who came as a mother). Oh, one who consumed her milk along with her life! You should clap.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that for one who had consumed the poisoned milk of the fiend, would any pain come when he tore the chest of hiraṇyan?

We shall next consider the 10<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.6.10. Adaindittu amrargal

*adaindittu amarargaḷ āḻkadal tannaimidaindittu mandaram mattāga nāttivadam suṟṟi vāsugi van kayiṟāgakadainditta kaigaḷāl cappāṇi kār mugail vaṇṇanē! cappāṇi*

**Пословный перевод:**

amarargaḷ – celestial entities; adaindittu – when they surrendered; āḻ – deep; kadal tannai – milky ocean; midaindittu – closely; mandaram – the mountain mantara; mattāga – as churning staff; nātti – anchoring; vāsugi – snake, vāsuki; val vadam – strong rope; kayiṟāga – as churning rope; suṟṟi – coiling it; kadainditta – clap with the hands which mercifully churned (such that amrut, nectar, came; kār mugil – like a dark cloud; vaṇṇanē – oh, one who has the complexion! Clap

**Перевод:**

**When the celestial entities surrendered to emperumān, the mountain mantara was anchored closely, as the churning staff, in the milky ocean which was deep. Snake vāsuki, which was like a strong rope, was coiled around the mountain as the churning rope. You should clap with those divine hands. Oh, one who has the complexion of dark cloud! You should clap.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**adaindu …** – having been cursed by sage durvāsa, losing all their wealth as a result of that, with their dwelling places seized by monsters and driven away, due to which desiring *amaratvam* (state of living forever, without death), celestial entities came and surrendered, as mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 1-9-65 “*śaraṇam tvām anuprāptā*: *samastā dēvatāgaṇā*:” (All the celestial entities came and surrendered to you). The word *adaindittu* has got shortened to give the meaning of *adaindida*, just as the word *vaṇangi* in [tiruvāimoḻi 1-3-8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/07/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-8-nalum-ninradu/) pāsuram “*nalam kaḻal vaṇangi*” has got shortened to give the meaning of the word *vaṇanga*.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, rearranges the verse as *amarargaḷ midaindu adainditta* which would mean that the celestial entities came crowding and surrendered to you. To help them, you had added a few herbs to make the milky ocean as curd and anchored mountain *mantara* in it, just as it has been mentioned in [nāṇmugan tiruvandādi 49](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-49/) “*malai āmai mēl vaittu*” (keeping *mantara* atop tortoise).

**āḻkadal …** – Not considering the unfathomable milky ocean as his mattress, crowding it \[with the mountain, tortoise, rope etc and the celestial as well as monstrous entities to churn\].

**mandaram …** – just as it has been mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 1-9-84 “*mandānam mantaram krutvā*” (using the mountain *mantara* as churning staff), anchoring the great mountain mantara as the churning staff.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the word *nātti* refers to – to anchor the mountain well on the back of tortoise which was supporting it, since curd was preventing the mountain to rest on the tortoise’s shell owing to its thickness.

**vadam …** – just as it has been mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 1-9-84 “*yōgtram krutvāca vāsukim*” (utilising snake vāsuki, who is like a strong rope, as the churning rope), utilising the strong vāsuki as the churning rope and coiling it around the mountain *mantara*.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that vāsuki was like a long rope used for pulling chariots during utsavams \[temple functions, for carrying the idols of emperumān and ubhayanāccimārs\].

**kadainditta …** – you had made the celestial and monster entities to churn initially; when they became tired and stepped out, you took their place and churned the ocean, just as it has been said in [tiruvāimoḻi 8-1-1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/01/thiruvaimozhi-8-1-1-dhevimar-avar/) “*alaikadal kadainda appan*” (the lord who churned the ocean with waves), until nectar ebbed out. You should clap with the hands with which you had churned the milky ocean.

**kār mugil …** – Oh, one whose form became śiningly dark due to the happiness of fulfilling the desire of your followers! You should clap.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that his form was like a dark cloud which was going to help the people of the world \[through rains\].

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.6.11. Atkollat tonriya

*ātkoḷḷat tōnṟiya āyar tam kōvinainātkamaḻ pūmboḻil villibuttūrp pattanvētkaiyāl sonna cappāṇi īraindumvētkaiyināl solluvār vinai pōmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ātkoḷḷa – to make everyone as servitor; tōnṟiya – one who incarnated in tiruvāyppādi \[śrī gōkulam\]; āyar tam – for the herd-folk; kōvinai – one who is the head; nāḷ – everyday; kamaḻ – emitting fragrance; pū – having flowers; poḻil – surrounded by gardens; villibuttūr – the controller of śrī villibuttūr; pattan – bhattar pirān (periyāḻvār); vētkaiyāl – with desire; sonna – mercifully composed; cappāṇi – regarding cappāṇi; iraṇḍu aindum – these ten pāsurams; vētkaiyināl – with desire; solluvār – those who recite; vinai – all their sorrows; pōmē – will leave, on their own

**Перевод:**

**emperumān incarnated in tiruvāyppādi, in order to make everyone as his servitor. bhattar pirān, who is the controller of śrī villibuttūr, which is surrounded by gardens having flowers which emit fragrance every day, mercifully and desirously composed pāsurams regarding kriṣṇa performing cappāṇi. For those who recite these ten pāsurams with desire, all their sorrows will leave on their own.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In this last pāsuram, āḻvār mentions the benefit which will accrue to those who learn this decad and brings it to an end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**ātkoḷḷat tōnṟiya** – emperumān who came and incarnated, in order to make everyone as his servitor. This conveys the meaning that the purpose of his incarnation is to correct the *cētanars* (those with ability to think) in leelā vibhūti (materialistic realm) and to make them as his servitors. Instead of saying *piṟanda* (born) the reason for saying *tōnṟiya* (incarnated) is to manifest the fact that emperumān came and incarnated, without the fault of being inside a womb, as mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5-3-2 “*dēvakī pūrva sandyāyām āvirbhūtam*” (he appeared in the eastern direction which is dēvaki).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that emperumān incarnated in tiruvāyppādi in order to make everyone as his servitor, instead of in vadamadurai (śrī maturā, in the north), which is inhabited by those who are a burden on earth and who were not willing to be his servitors. When asked “Here (in tiruvāyppādi), are there people who were willing to be his servitors?” he responds saying as mentioned in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2-5-1 “*ennaiyum engaḷ kudimuḻudu ātkoṇḍa mannan*” (he is our lord who made me as well as our clan to be his servitors). udaiyavar \[rāmānujar\] mercifully referred to arjunan as “*kriṣṇa dāsan*” (servitor of kriṣṇa) only after he had said, as in [bhagavat gītā 18-73](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-73/) “*kariśyē vacanam tava*” (I will do as per your bidding). Similarly, hanuman was called as “*rāma dāsan*” (servitor of śrī rāma) only after he had said, as in śrī rāmāyaṇam uttara kāṇḍam ślōkam “*bhāvō nānyatra gaccati*” (At the end of his incarnation, when śrī rāma was taking all the entities in ayōdyā to mōkśam, he called hanuman too, to accompany him. At that time, hanuman told him that his *bhāvam* (pathos) will not go to any other entity, viz. his eyes will constantly look at only śrī rāma and will not look at paramapada nātan, in śrī vaikuṇṭam). *dāsatvam* (being a servitor) was present in both the entity who said that he will do \[arjuna\] and the one who said that he will not do \[hanuman\], based on the quality of the *śaraṇyan* \[entity to whom they surrendered\]. For hanuman, not being satiated with śrī rāma’s qualities was due to śrī rāma’s fortune \[Had hanuman been satiated with śrī rāma’s auspicious qualities, he would have been probably willing to go to mōkśam\]. Instead of saying “*nānyatra*” (my pathos will not gravitate towards anyone else) if hanuman had been willing to go along with śrī rāma to śrī vaikuṇṭam, the divine mind of śrī rāma would have been sorrowful \[since hanuman would have been satisfied with seeing śrī rāma and enjoying his qualities and would have been ready to enjoy someone else’s \[paramapadanātan’s\] qualities\]. It is through carrying out servitude that one makes others as servitors. This is aptly brought out in [periya tiruvandādi pāsuram 32](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/11/periya-thiruvandhadhi-32/) “*tamakku adimai vēṇḍuvār dāmōdaranār*” \[*dāmōdaran* refers to kriṣṇa being tied down to a mortar by yaśōdāp pirātti; in letting her to tie him up, he allowed himself to be enslaved by her, becoming her servitor; through that quality, he made everyone to become his servitor\]. Those who seek to be servitors, would say, as mentioned in [nānmugan tiruvandādi 50](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-50/) “*māyan uraik kidakkum uḷḷattu enakku*” \[the divine words of kriṣṇa, *caramaślōkam*, by which emperumān tells his followers to surrender to him, that he would remove all their hurdles, and that they do not need to grieve, would always remain in my heart\].

**āyar tam kōvinai** – even though he had incarnated in śrī maturā, it was in tiruvāyppādi that it \[his incarnation\] shone and it was there that the purpose of his incarnation was fulfilled. He lowered himself \[from his eminent status\], carrying out the errands of herd-folk, attracted them through his simplicity, made them as his servitors and became their controller.

**nātkamaḻ …** – periyāḻvār, controller of śrī villibuttūr, which is surrounded by flower gardens, which emit fragrance, through all the time.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that unlike śrī rāmāyaṇa ślōkam “*akālapalinō vrukśā*:” (trees started flowering and yielding fruits at unseasonal time when śrī rāma returned to ayōdyā after fourteen years’ exile), the gardens in śrī villibuttūr were constantly yielding flowers which were fragrant all the time since there was no concept of “This is not the season for flowering” in śrī villibuttūr.

**vētkai …** – with a desire towards enjoying the activities in emperumān’s incarnation, periyāḻvār had mercifully composed these ten pāsurams, regarding emperumān’s activity of carrying out *cappāṇi*. All the sins of those who recite these ten pāsurams, with desire, will leave on their own.

Here, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that these ten pāsurams were mercifully composed by periyāḻvār with overflowing desire and which were shining with the concept of *ākincanyam* (not having anything in our hands to attain emperumān; he alone is the means to attain him). *vētkaiyināl solluvār vinai pōmē* – even if one does not have the pathos and the relationship which periyāḻvār had \[with emperumān\], if that person recites these ten pāsurams, with only the words being recited, taking refuge under periyāḻvār’s affection, the sin that “We are not able to carry out *mangaḷāśāsanam* like periyāḻvār” will leave on its own.

We shall next consider the pravēśam of the next tirumoḻi.

## 1.7.1. Todar sangiligai

*todar sangiligai salar bilār ennat tūngu pon maṇi olippappadu mummadap punal sōra vāraṇam paiya ninṟu ūrvadu pōludan kūdik kiṇkiṇi āravārippa udai maṇi paṟai kaṟangatadam tāḷiṇaik koṇḍu sārngapāṇi taḷar nadai nadavānō*

**Пословный перевод:**

sārngapāṇi – one who has śrī śārngam (divine bow) in his divine hand; sangiligait tudar – the series of chains; salār bilār enna – as it was making a noise “salār bilār”; pon tūngu – hanging from the golden cord; maṇi – bell; olippa – as it makes a sound; padu – created; mum (mūnṟu) – two cheeks and the reproductive organ, from these three places; madam punal – rutting fluid; sōra – to flow in abundance; vāraṇam – elephant; paiya ninṟu – standing slowly; ūrvadu pōl – just as it walks; kiṇkiṇi – anklets on the divine feet; udan kūdi – together; āravārippa – as it makes a noise; ūdai maṇi – bell adorned on the divine waist; paṟai – like a drum; kaṟanga – as it makes a noise; tada – stout; tāḷ iṇai koṇḍu – with the two divine feet, which match each other; taḷar nadai nadavānō – will he not take tender steps?

**Перевод:**

**An elephant, which has snapped from its chains, walks unsteadily, since it is in rut, with the chains making a noise as it walks, with the bell tied to a golden cord on its back making a noise, with the rutting fluid flowing copiously from its two cheeks and its reproductive organ. Similar to this, will one, whose anklets on the divine feet are making a noise, the bell from whose divine waist is making a noise like that of a drum, not take tender steps with his divine, stout legs?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār compares kriṣṇa’s tender steps to an elephant which is in rut.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tudar …** – An elephant, since it is rutting, has snapped from its chains, with which it had been tied. As it walks, dragging the chain with it, the chain makes a noise *salār bilār*. *tudar* – shackles; for an elephant, the shackles are normally chain. The term *salār bilār* merely indicates the sound made by the chain and does not have any meaning.

**tūngu …** – the bell, hanging from a gold cord, from the elephant’s back, making a sound. The term *pon* in *ponmaṇi* indicates golden cord.

**padu …** – the rutting fluid, created from three places, flowing down like a stream. The three places are: two cheeks on the face and the reproductive organ.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the three regions from where the rutting fluid secretes are: the two ears and head.

**vāraṇam …** – due to the burden of the rutting fluid, the elephant was walking, without being under its control, slowly. In a similar vein…

**udan …** – just as it has been mentioned in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.3.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/07/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-1-3-4/) “*sēvadik kiṇkiṇi*” (anklets on the divine feet), the anklets adorning the divine feet were making a sound together. Alternatively, the waist cord with chain adorned on the divine waist, slipped from the waist, got caught in the feet and, being dragged \[when kriṣṇa walked unsteadily\], the bells in that cord made a noise.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that in the case of kriṣṇa too, fluid from his mouth, from his eyes and other limbs were flowing, just like the elephant.

**udai …** – the bell tied to the cord on the divine waist was making a noise like a drum.

**tadam tāḷ …** – with the divine feet, which had grown stout, matching his age and which were matching each other.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that since kriṣṇa’s divine feet were such that they could bear his walking strides, they were stout. āḻvār prays that he wishes to see kriṣṇa walk with the two divine feet, which did not have any equivalent other than themselves, both with and without his control.

**sārngapāṇi** – one who has the divine bow, *śrī śārngam*. Reference to śārngam is symbolic of all the divine weapons, indicative of his being the supreme entity. Even as he incarnated, he had all the divine weapons on his divine form.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that since āḻvār knows the *avatāra rahasyam* (secret behind kriṣṇa’s incarnation – that he is śrīman nārāyaṇa), he prays that just like śārngam, kriṣṇa should also be capable of eliminating his enemies.

**taḷar nadai nadavānō** – *taḷar nadai* indicates walking in a tottering manner with the divine feet, unlike the age when one walks with firm steps.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.7.2. Sekkaridai nuni

*sekkar idai nunik kombil tōnṟum siṟu piṟai muḷai pōlanakka senduvar vāyt tiṇṇai mīdē taḷir veṇ pal muḷai ilagaakku vadam uduttu āmaittāli pūṇḍa ananta sayanantakka māmaṇi vaṇṇan vāsudēvan taḷar nadai nadavānō*

**Пословный перевод:**

akku vadam – chain made of beads from shell; uduttu – donning on the divine waist; āmaittāli – ornament representing the form of tortoise; pūṇḍa – donning on the divine neck; ananta sayanan – one who has reclined on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan); takka – apt; māmaṇi – like a bluish gemstone; vaṇṇan – having the form; vāsudēvan – kaṇṇan, who is the divine son of śrī vasudēvar; sekkar idai – in the reddish sky; nunik kombil – on a tender branch; tōnṟum – appearing splendorously; siṟu piṟai – nascent moon’s; muḷaip pōla – like a bud; nakka – when he smiles; sem tuvar – being dark reddish; vāy – of the divine mouth; tiṇṇai mīdu – on a high location; naḷir – being cool; veṇ – being white; pal – having divine pearls \[teeth\]; muḷai – buds; ilaga – to shine; taḷar nadai nadavānō – will he not take tender steps?

**Перевод:**

**Reclining atop ādiśēśan, having the form of an apt bluish gemstone, being the divine son of śrī vasudēvar, kriṣṇa has donned a chain made of conch beads on his divine waist. He has donned an ornament with the form of tortoise on his divine neck. With his shining, cool, white divine teeth which are like buds and which appear on a high location when he smiles with his divine reddish mouth, just like the bud of nascent moon appearing on a tender branch in the reddish sky, will he not take tender steps?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**sekkar …** – just like the bud of the eminent nascent moon \[sprouting moon\] which appears on a tender branch on the reddish sky.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the sky was such reddish that the tender branch of a tree was also reddish.

**nakka …** – with kriṣṇa smiling, on the high location of his divine lips which are reddish, the bud of a single tooth, which is cool and white, is shining splendorously.

**akku vadam uduttu** – donning the chain of beads, made out of conch, on his divine waist.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that this could also be silver chain, since the term *akku* also refers to silver.

**āmaittāli pūṇḍa** – donning the distinguished ornament, which is in the form of tortoise, on the divine neck.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that this ornament was appropriate for his herd-clan.

**ananta sayanan** – this is being mentioned, considering the root of incarnation, just as it has been mentioned in harivamśam 113-62 “*nāgaparyankam utsrujya hyāgata*:” (coming, after getting up from the mattress of ādiśēśan).

**takka māmaṇi vaṇṇan** – having the divine complexion of an apt blue gemstone.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa had the complexion of a splendorous bluish gemstone which was most apt to his divine form. Both the object of comparison and the entity which it is compared with are exactly alike, without any distinction between them.

**vāsudēvan …** – will not the divine son of śrī vāsudēvar, take tender steps?

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that this would also refer to one who is residing, everywhere. He further says that this entity is also the one mentioned as the divine son of śrī vasudēvar.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.7.3. Minnuk kodiyum

*minnuk kodiyum ōr veṇ tingaḷum sūḻ parivēdamumāypinnal tulangum arasilaiyum pīdagac ciṟṟādaiyodumminnil polindadu ōr kār mugil pōlak kaḻuttinil kāṟaiyodumtannil polinda irudīkēsan taḷar nadai nadavānō*

**Пословный перевод:**

min kodiyum – streak of lightning; ōr – unique; veṇ – being white; tingaḷum – region of moon; sūḻ – surrounding it; pari vēdamumāy – the penumbra region of moon; pinnal – golden plaits donned in the waist region; tulangum – strung into it, and shining; arasu ilaiyum – string of peepal tree leaves; pīdagam – with golden colour; siṟu ādaiyodum – with a short garment; minnil – in lightning; polindadu – being resplendent; ōr – as unique; kār – being dark; mugil pōla – like a cloud; kaḻuttinil – donned on the divine neck; kāṟaiyodum – with an ornament called as kāṟai \[like a necklace, worn by boys\]; tannil polinda – being self-illuminating; irudīkēsan – will kaṇṇan, who steals the senses of beholders, not take tender steps?

**Перевод:**

**Just like a lightning streak with unique moon region, which is white in colour and its penumbra, kaṇṇan has adorned with golden chain on his divine waist, a string of peepal leaves strung onto that golden chain and a small golden garment over the waist. Along with these, he has adorned himself with an ornament kāṟai \[necklace\], shining like a unique cloud in lightning. Will such kaṇṇan, who is self-illuminating and who steals the senses of those who see him, not take tender steps?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**min …** – like a streak of lightning, together with unique moon region which is without any fault and its associated penumbra region.

**pinnal …** – golden chain which is donned on the divine waist, the golden peepal leaves which have been strung to it and the golden small garment which has been donned over that; along with these

**minnil …**– having an ornament *kāṟai* which he has donned on his divine neck, which is similar to a dark cloud illuminated by lightning

**tannil …** – being full and beautiful, even without these decorations, as a result of which he keeps the senses of his beholders under his control; will such kaṇṇan not take tender steps?

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that apart from the shining beauty which he has, which is similar to the analogies mentioned earlier, kaṇṇan has beauty from his quality of self-illumination, just as it has been mentioned in [mūnṟām tiruvandādi 38](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/04/munram-thiruvandhadhi-38/) “*tānē tanakkuvaman*” (he alone is the analogy for himself).

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.7.4. Kannal kudam

*kannaṟkudam tiṟandāl ottūṟik kaṇakaṇa sirittu uvandumun vandu ninṟu muttam tarum en mugil vaṇṇan tirumārvantannaip peṟṟēṟkut tan vāy amudam tandu ennait taḷirppikkinṟāntanneṟṟu māṟṟalar talaigaḷ mīdē taḷar nadai nadavānō*

**Пословный перевод:**

kannal kudam – pot with sugan cane juice; tiṟandāl ottu – like its mouth a little opened; ūri – secreting nectar from the divine mouth; kaṇakaṇa sirittu – laughing with the sound “kaṇa kaṇa”; uvandu – being happy; mun vandu ninṟu – coming forward and standing; muttam tarum – offering his juice from the divine mouth; en – being obedient to me; mugil – like a bluish cloud; vaṇṇan – having the divine complexion; tiru – periya pirāttiyār \[śrī mahālakśmi\]; mārvan – having on his divine chest; tannai – him; peṟṟēṟku – me, who gave birth to; than – his; vāy amudam – nectar, secreting from his divine mouth; tandu – offering; ennai – me, his mother; taḷirppikkinṟān – he, who is making to flourish; than eṟṟu – those who opposed him; māṟṟalar – enemies’; talaigaḷ mīdē – on top of their heads; taḷar nadai nadavānō – will he not take tender steps?

**Перевод:**

**Just as a pot, containing juice of sugar cane, opens, letting out the juice from inside, with the nectar secreting from his divine mouth, laughing with the sound kaṇa kaṇa, feeling happy, kriṣṇa comes forward, offering his juice from the divine mouth. He is obedient to me, with the divine complexion of bluish cloud, having periya pirāttiyār on his divine chest. Will this kriṣṇa, who is offering nectar from his divine mouth to me, who gave birth to him, making me flourish, not take tender steps on the heads of his enemies, who oppose him?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, is wondering whether he would walk with tender steps, on the heads of his enemies who are unfavourable towards him.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kannal …** – just like a pot having sugar cane juice opens a little bit for the juice to drip and flow out, with water secreting and coming out from his \[kriṣṇa’s\] divine mouth, laughing with the sound *kaṇa kaṇa*, feeling joyous. *kaṇa kaṇa* – refers to the sound which is made when one laughs with a gap in between.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *kaṇa kaṇa* also indicates warmth, implying that the nectar, drooling from his divine mouth, was warm and he laughed with that warmth.

**mun …** – coming forward and offering the flavour of his divine lips.

**muttam** – divine lips

**en …** – being obedient to me, having the form of a dark cloud and having connection with lakshmi, as the reason for that obedience.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that he is obedient to me such that I could proudly say that “He is mine”. The basis for his obedience is that śrī mahālakśmi is always residing on his divine chest, just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāīmoḻi 6-10-10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/06/thiruvaimozhi-6-10-10-agalagillen-part-1/) “*alarmēl mangai uṟai mārbā*” (Oh, one who has śrī mahālakśmi, who is atop a lotus, residing constantly on your divine chest!)

**tannai …** – he offers the nectar of his divine mouth to me, who is fortunate to give birth him, making me flourish \[from my earlier state of withering, before his birth\]. Since it has been mentioned here that “He is offering nectar from his divine mouth, making me flourish”, in the present tense, the term mentioned earlier “*muttam tarum*” implies that giving his  divine nectar is his nature, which takes place often.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the verse mentioned earlier “*muttam tandu aruḷum*” was periyāḻvār’s prayer and the term ”*vāyamudam tandu ennait taḷirppikkinṟān*” refers to fulfilment of his wish. *ennait taḷirppikkinṟān* – kriṣṇa’s nectar like drooling is the water for nurturing crops, and periyāḻvār exists because of that.

**taneṟṟu …** – will he not take divine steps on the heads of enemies who oppose him?

Here tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that asking kriṣṇa to take tender steps on the heads of his enemies is āḻvār’s prayer or his affirmation that he would certainly walk on their heads or his fear as to what will happen if kriṣṇa were to walk on their heads.

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.7.5. Munnal or

*munnal ōr veḷḷip perumalikkuttan modu modu viraindu ōdapinnait tudarndu ōr karumalaik kuttan peyarndu adi iduvadu pōlpanni ulagam paravi ōvāp pugaḻp paladēvan ennumtannambi ōdap pinkūdac celvān taḷar nadai nadavānō*

**Пословный перевод:**

mun – ahead; nal – distinguished; ōr – unique; peru veḷḷi malai – given birth to, by a huge silver mountain; kuttan – a small one; modu modu – making a noise such as “didu didu”; viraindu ōda – even as he ran fast; pinnai – behind that small one; todarndadu – followed; karu – dark; malai – yielded by a mountain (created by a mountain); kuttan – a small one; peyarndu – slowly; adi iduvadu pōl – just as taking a step; ulagam – eminent people; panni – analysed; paravi – praised; ōvā – indeterminable limit; pugaḻ – having fame; baladēvan ennum – having the name “baladēvan” (balarāman); than nambi – his elder brother; ōda – as he ran ahead; pin – following him; kūda – to join with him; selvān – one who goes rapidly; taḷar nadai nadavānō – will be not take tender steps?

**Перевод:**

**A distinguished, unique, child, given birth to by a huge silver mountain, ran ahead, making a sound such as “didu didu”. Another child, given birth to by a dark mountain, followed the earlier child, with small steps, slowly. Even if eminent people in the world, after analysing, praise him, they cannot ascertain the limit of his fame. Even as such baladēvan \[balarāman\], was running in front \[like the child of the silver mountain\], kriṣṇa, his younger brother \[who was like the child given birth to by a dark mountain\], ran behind him, to join with him. Will such kriṣṇa not take tender steps?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that āḻvār is enjoying the manner in which kriṣṇa was following his elder brother nambi mūtta pirān \[balarāman\], which was similar to a child of a mountain chasing another child of a mountain.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**munnal …** – a child, distinguished, unique, given birth to by a huge silver mountain, was running in front, with arrogance, with his steps making a noise “*didu didu*”.

**pinnai …**– behind that child, with his arrogance, to catch him, another child, given birth to by a dark mountain was running, in line with its quality of childishness, with small steps. Similar to this …

**panni …** – Even if all the eminent people in the world, with all the power of their knowledge, analyse and praise, they cannot see the limit of baladēvan’s fame. Even as such baladēvan, his elder brother, was running in front, to catch up with him, kriṣṇa was running behind him with small steps. Will not such kriṣṇa take tender steps?

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that even if the people of the world analyse various śāstras \[sacred texts} and stōtrams \[hymns in praise\] through their ācāryans \[preceptors\], and praise without any interval, they cannot complete their praising of baladēvan; such was his fame.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.7.6. Oru kalil sangu

*oru kālil sangu oru kālil cakkaram uḷḷadi poṟittu amaindairu kālum koṇḍu angu angu eḻudināṟpōl ilaccinai pada nadanduperugā ninṟa inba veḷḷattin mēl pinnaiyum peydu peydukaru kārkkadal vaṇṇan kāmar tādai taḷar nadai nadavānō*

**Пословный перевод:**

karu – being dark; kār – being cool; kadal – like an ocean; vaṇṇan – having the divine complexion; kāmar tādai – one who is the father of manmatan \[deity of love\]; oru kālil – on one divine foot; sangu – śrī pāncajanyam \[divine conch\]; oru kālil – on the other divine foot; cakkaram – śrī sudarśana āḻvān \[divine disc\]; uḷ adi – on the inner divine feet \[divine soles\]; poṟittu – engraved like lines; amainda – to be present; iru kālum koṇḍu – with both divine feet; angu angu – in all the places where he had taken a step; eḻudināṟ pōl – as if it had been written; ilaccinai – the signs; pada – to form; nadandu – walking; perugā ninṟa – with happiness overflowing; inba veḷḷattin mēl – on that flood of happiness; pinnaiyum – repeatedly; peydu peydu – raining happiness; taḷar nadai nadavānō – will he not take tender steps?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān has a divine complexion which is like that of a dark and cool ocean. He is the father of manmatan. On one divine foot, he has śrī pāncajanyam and on the other divine foot, he has śrī sudarśana āḻvān, engraved as lines on the soles. With those two divine feet, will he not take tender steps such that the signs of those divine lines are formed, creating on overflowing flood of happiness?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that while he walks, kriṣṇa should leave behind the impressions of his divine feet.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**oru kālil …** – with the two divine feet, of which on one divine foot, śrī pāncajanyam and on the other divine foot, śrī sudarśana āḻvān have been engraved as lines.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that on the inner sides of the unique divine feet \[where one divine foot matches the other, and none to match them\], just as it has been said in [periya tiruvandādi 31](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/11/periya-thiruvandhadhi-31/) “*adi tāṟum*” (the lines on the inner sides of the two divine feet), śrī pāncajanyam and śrī sudarśana āḻvān are shining brightly. *iru kālum* – in the earlier part of the pāsuram, āḻvār had said “*oru kāl oru kāl*” denying anything else which was a match for each of those two divine feet. Now, when he says *iru kālum* he says that these two divine feet match each other.

**angu angu …** – on each place where he had taken a step, making a sign \[with those lines of divine conch and divine disc\] similar to painting with a brush.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that during the *kōdait tirunāḷ utsavam* (function in śrī rangam temple), when namperumāḷ went out during the *utsavam*, ācāryas (preceptors) saw his divine feet on the path and their happiness was overflowing like a flood.

**perugā …** – looking at the beauty of his gait and his divine form, with overflowing ocean of happiness, creating more and more of happiness

**karu kār …** – having a divine complexion similar to a dark, cool ocean; *karumai* – darkness; *kār* – coolness. Alternatively, *karumai* could refer to greatness and *kār* could refer to darkness. Also, *kār* could refer to cloud, with kriṣṇa having a divine complexion similar to that of a dark cloud and like a dark ocean.

**kāmar tādai** – father of *kāman* \[manmatan\] who goes around, frightening people with his beauty. emperumān is referred to as in [tiruvāimoḻi 10-2-8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/10/thiruvaimozhi-10-2-8-kadu-vinai/) “*kāmanaip payanda kāḷai*” (one who sired *kāman*). Unlike the saying “*prasavāntanca yauvanam*” (youthful state is only until one gives birth to a child), for emperumān, after siring *kāman*, his age started decreasing.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that for *kāman*, qualities of beauty, tenderness and winning the minds of beholders came about because he was sired by emperumān. *kāmar tādai pinnaiyum peydu peydu taḷar nadai nadavānō* – will he, who is the father of *kāman*, raining more and more happiness, not take tender steps?

The verse should be rearranged as “*kāmar tādai inba veḷḷattin mēl pinnaiyum peydu peydu – taḷarnadai nadavānō*” to obtain sequential meaning.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.7.7. Padar pangayam

*padar pangaya malar vāy negiḻap pani padu siṟu tuḷi pōlidam koṇḍa sevvāy ūri ūri iṟṟiṟṟu vīḻa ninṟukadum sēkkaḻuttin maṇikkural pōl udai maṇi kaṇa kaṇa enatadam tāḷiṇai koṇḍu sārngapāṇi taḷar nadai nadavānō*

**Пословный перевод:**

padar – spread; pangaya malar – lotus flower; vāy negiḻa – as it blossoms; pani padu – cool honey; siṟu tuḷi pōl – just as it drips a little bit; idam koṇḍa – expansive; sem – being reddish; vāy – nectar in the divine lips; ūṟi ūṟi – secreting permanently; iṟṟu iṟṟu vīḻa – as it breaks down and falls; ninṟu – remaining; kadum – cruel; sē – bull’s; kaḻuttil – tied to its neck; maṇi – bell’s; kural pōl – like its sound; udai maṇi – bell tied to the divine waist \[cord\]; kaṇa kaṇa ena – as it makes a sound “kaṇa, kaṇa”; tada – stout; tāḷ iṇai koṇḍu – with the two divine feet which match each other; sārngam – the divine bow, śrī śārngam; pāṇi – will the one, who has in his divine hand, not take tender steps?

**Перевод:**

**When a lotus flower just blossoms, the honey present inside the flower will drip a little bit at a time. Similar to that, the divine nectar is breaking and dripping from kriṣṇa’s divine lips which are expansive and reddish. With the bell tied to his divine waist making a noise “kaṇa kaṇa”, similar to the noise made by a bell tied to the neck of a cruel bull, will not kriṣṇa take tender steps?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that kriṣṇa should take tender steps with the bells on the waist cord making a sound.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**padar …** – a lotus flower, which has spread, unlike a bud \[where its mouth is closed\], is just blossoming. From inside its mouth, which is cool, honey is dripping.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the lotus, due to the quality of the mud in which it is growing, is spreading well. p*ani* – coolness.

**idam koṇḍa …** – nectar from the divine mouth, which is expansive and reddish, is permanently secreting. As it secretes, a few drops break and fall down.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *idam koṇḍa* refers to the expansive mouth within which yaśōdāp pirātti had earlier seen seven worlds. emperumān is referred to as “*ulagam uṇḍa peru vāyan*” (one who has a huge mouth with which he had swallowed all the worlds) by nammāḻvār in his [tiruvāimoḻi 6-10-1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/06/thiruvaimozhi-6-10-1-ulagam-unda/).

**kadum sēkkaḻuttu …** – just like the sound made by a bell tied to the neck of a cruel bull, the bell tied to the divine waist of kriṣṇa should make a sound “*kaṇa kaṇa*”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the sound *kaṇa kaṇa* refers to making a noise such as *kaṇār kaṇār*.

**tadam tāḷ …** – will not kriṣṇa, who has stout, divine feet which match each other \[in their eminence etc\] and who has the divine bow śrī śārngam on his divine hand, take a few tender steps?

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa should walk with his beautiful divine feet, planting them firmly on the ground.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.7.8. Pakkam karum

*pakkam karum siṟuppāṟai mīdē aruvigaḷ pagarndu anaiyaakku vadam iḻindēṟit tāḻa aṇiyalgul pudai peyaramakkaḷ ulaginil peydaṟiyā maṇik kuḻavi uruvintakka māmaṇivaṇṇan vāsudēvan taḷar nadai nadavānō*

**Пословный перевод:**

karu – dark; siṟu pāṟai – of a small mountain; pakkam mīdu – on the slope; aruvigaḷ – streams; pagarndu anaiya – just as \[they\] emit a radiance; akku vadam – the chain made of beads from shell stones (donned on the divine waist). It could; iḻindu – lowering; ēṟi – rising; tāḻa – as it hangs; aṇi algul – beautiful, divine waist region; pudai peyara – as it moves on the sides; ulaginil – in the world; makkaḷ – people; peydu aṟiyā – not having been sired by; maṇi – stealing the mind; kuḻavi uruvin – having the form of a small child; takka – apt; mā maṇi – like a blue gemstone; vaṇṇan – one who has the divine complexion; vāsudēvan – will not the divine son of śrī vasudēvar take tender steps?

**Перевод:**

**Just as streams coming down the slopes of a dark, small mountain emit a radiance, the chain made with beads from shell stones, donned on the divine waist would rise and lower, hanging down, as kriṣṇa moves. With the divine, beautiful waist region moving on the side, and having a form of a little child which steals the minds of beholders, will the divine son of śrī vasudēvar, who has a divine complexion like a bluish gemstone, not take tender steps?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**pakkam …**– just like small streams, which are at higher and lower altitudes, flowing down the slopes of dark, small mountain, shine brightly… *pagar* – radiance.

**akku …** – the beads made of shells, donned on the divine waist, rise and fall, hanging down. *akku vadam* could also refer to a chain made of silver.

**aṇi …** – with the divine waist region swaying on the two sides

**makkaḷ …** – a beautiful child, who has not been sired by anyone in the world, his

**takka …** – will the divine son of śrī vasudēvar, who has the divine complexion of an apt bluish gemstone, not take tender steps?

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *māmaṇi vaṇṇan* refers to the divine complexion of an eminent bluish gemstone. *vāsudēvan* – he too {vasudēvar himself\] would have grown up like this, just as it has been said in mantra praśnam cauḷa kaṇḍam “*ātmāvai putranāmāsi*” (a person himself is born as the son). The pāsuram should be rearranged to read as *māmaṇitakka vaṇṇan vāsudēvan – ulaginil makkaḷaip peydu aṟiyā maṇik kuḻavi uruvil – karum siṟuppāṟai mīdē aruvigaḷ pagarndu anaiya akku vadam iḻindu ēṟit tāḻa aṇi algul pudai peyara – taḷar nadai nadavānō* in order to get the sequential meaning.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.7.9. Ven puludi

*veṇ puḻudi mēl peydu koṇḍu aḷaindadōr vēḻattin karum kanṟu pōlten puḻudi ādit tirivikkiraman siṟu pugar pada viyarttuoṇ pōdu alar kamalac ciṟukkāl uṟaittu onṟum nōvāmētaṇ pōdu koṇḍa tavisin mīdē taḷar nadai nadavānō*

**Пословный перевод:**

veṇ puḻudi – white dust; mēl peydu koṇḍu – spraying on its top part; aḷaindadu – mingling with \[the dirt, with its trunk\]; ōr – a; karu – dark; vēḻattin kanṟu pōl – like a baby elephant; teḷ – clean \[white\]; puḻudi – in dirt; ādi – playing; tirivikkiraman – one who measured the worlds with three steps; siṟu pugar pada – just as the form appears resplendent, a little bit; viyarttu – sweating; oṇ – being beautiful; pōdu – at the appropriate time; alar – blossomed; kamalam – like a lotus; siṟu – little; kāl – divine feet; uṟaittu – where \[he\] stepped firmly; onṟum nōvāmē – without any pain; taṇ – cool; pōdu koṇḍa – having flowers; tavisin mīdu – on the mattress, will he not take tender steps?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, as trivikraman, had measured all the words with three steps of his divine feet. Just as his divine form has appeared radiant, kriṣṇa is playing with dirt, like a dark, baby elephant which sprays white dirt all over its body and plays with its trunk. Will not that kriṣṇa, whose divine form is shining with the dirt sticking to places where he is sweating, take tender steps on to a matress of lotus flowers, such that his divine feet do not pain where he steps on?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that āḻvār desires that kriṣṇa should walk like a little elephant which roams around on its own.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**veṇ puḻudi …** – just like a dark, baby elephant, which sprays white dirt on itself, swinging its trunk

**teṇ …** – applying clean \[white\] dirt on his divine form

**trivikraman** – without considering the softness of his divine feet, emperumān measured the worlds to fulfil the desire of his follower, indran.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as āḻvār saw trivikraman during the incarnation of vāmana, due to matching nature of quality, he sees kriṣṇa also as trivikrama.

**siṟu pugar pada viyarttu** – on those places on his divine form where there are droplets of sweat, the dirt which he had applied, appears a bit shiny

**oṇ pōdu …** – his divine, little feet appear like a beautiful lotus flower which has blossomed at the appropriate time. Without causing any pain to those divine feet at the places where he has stepped onto firmly.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that his feet are tender just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 6-2-10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/11/thiruvaimozhi-6-2-10-ninrilangu-mudiyinay/) “*maṟṟai nilamagaḷ pidikkum melladi*” (the tender, divine feet which are gently massaged by śrī dēvi and bhū dēvi, who themselves have very tender divine hands).

**taṇ …** – will he not take tender steps on a mattress of lotus flowers? *tavisu* – mattress

We shall next consider the 10<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.7.10. Tirai nir

*tirai nīrc candira maṇḍalam pōl sengaṇ māl kēsavan tantiru nīr mugattut tulangu cutti tigaḻndu engum pudai peyaraperu nīrt tirai eḻu gangaiyilum periyadu ōr tīrtta balamtaru nīr siṟuc caṇṇam tuḷḷam sōrat taḷar nadai nadavānō*

**Пословный перевод:**

tirai – tossing waves; nīr – appearing as moving in the midst of ocean \[its shadow\]; candira maṇḍalam pōl – like the region of moon; sem kaṇ – with reddish divine eyes; māl – having a dark complexion; kēsavan – he \[kriṣṇa\] who has eminent locks; than – his; tiru – being splendorous; nīr – having coolness; mugattu – on his divine face; tulangu – being radiant; cutti – ornament cutti (suspended from the lock and hanging on the forehead); engum tigaḻndu – shining everywhere; pudai peyara – swaying between left and right; peru – being the most eminent among all the sacred waters; nīr tirai eḻu – tossing white coloured waves; gangaiyilum – more than the river gangā; periyadu – being eminent; ōr – being without a match; tīrtta balam – strength of sacred water; tarum nīr – having water which is capable of giving; siṟu saṇṇam – small saṇṇam (saṇṇam – hidden part; here, this refers to the male reproductive organ); tuḷḷam sōra – even as it drips, will he not take tender steps?

**Перевод:**

**Just like the lunar region appears moving in the middle of the ocean \[the reference here is to the shadow of the moon\], which is tossing waves, kriṣṇa has reddish eyes, dark complexion and eminent locks. He has the ornament cutti, which is radiant, on his divine face. gangā river, which is tossing white coloured waves, has water which is the best among all the sacred waters. Will kriṣṇa not take tender steps such that the cutti sways between left and right sides, emitting radiance, and with water dripping from his private part, the water which is without a match, which has the strength of sacred waters and which is more eminent than the water flowing in river gangā?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that kriṣṇa should walk with a decoration, just like candran appears amidst ocean.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tirai nīr …** – just like the lunar region \[whose shadow\] in the ocean, which has agitating waves, appears to move.

**sengaṇ māl …** – having reddish eyes, and as a complement to it, a dark divine form, and having eminent locks. *māl* – one who has a dark complexion.

**than …** – with the ornament *cutti*, which is shining on the divine face which is beautiful and cool, emitting radiance everywhere as it sways between left and right sides.tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that on the divine face of emperumān, which is cooler than candran, the divine ornament *cutti* is resplendently reflecting, shining everywhere.

**peru nīr …** – river gangā is the most eminent among sacred waters, throwing up waves, with its flow never changing. Will kriṣṇa not take tender steps such that water, which is more eminent than the waters of that gangā and which gives unique strength, drips from his private part?

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that while āḻvār continues to be emperumān’s servitor and to be completely dependent on him, this water dripping from his private part gives āḻvār the strength to carry out mangaḷāśāsanam for him such that the relationship of protector-protected changes whereby, he, out of concern for kriṣṇa \[when he is vulnerable as a child\] takes on the role of the protector of emperumān, who is now protected. The meaning for *gangaiyilum periyadu* is that this water is the sustenance for the entire universe \[while ākāśa gangā is exclusively for the celestial entities\].

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.
