## 1.7.11. Ayar kulattinil

*āyar kulattinil vandu tōnṟiya anjanavaṇṇan tannaitāyar magiḻa onnār taḷarat taḷar nadai nadandadanaivēyar pugaḻ vittu cittan seerāl virittana uraikka vallārmāyan maṇivaṇṇan tāḷ paṇiyum makkaḷaip peṟuvargaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āyar kulattinil – in the clan of covherds; vandu tōnṟiya – one who came and incarnated; anjana vaṇṇan tannai – kaṇṇan, who has a divine form like black pigment; tāyar – yaśōdā, who gave birth to him and other women, who had similar affection towards; magiḻa – to be happy; onnār – enemies such as kamsan et al; taḷara – to shrivel in their minds; taḷar nadai nadandadanai – the manner in which he took tender steps; vēyar – brāhmaṇas; pugaḻ – to be praised \[by them\]; vittucittan – periyāḻvār; seerāl – with eminence; virittana – mercifully and expansively composed these pāsurams; uraikka vallār – those who are capable of reciting; māyan – one who has amazing power; maṇivaṇṇan – emperumān, who has the complexion of bluish gemstone; tāḷ – in the divine feet; paṇiyum – apt to carry out servitude; makkaḷai – children; peruvargaḷ – will sire

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, who has a dark complexion like that of a black pigment, incarnated in the clan of covherds. He took tender steps which made his mothers happy and his enemies, such as kamsan et al, shrivel in their hearts. periyāḻvār, who is praised by brāhmaṇas, expansively and mercifully composed these pāsurams, about those tender steps. Those who are capable of reciting these pāsurams, will sire children who will carry out servitude at the divine feet of one, who has amazing power and who has the complexion of blue gemstone.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In this last pāsuram, āḻvār mentions the benefit which will accrue to one who recites the decad, and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**āyar …** – one who incarnated in the clan of covherds. ḍidn’t kriṣṇa incarnate in the clan of kings? Only a few people know about that, while everyone knows that he incarnated in the clan of covherds.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that only those who had seen his birth in the royal clan and those who had read about it in śāstrams \[such as śrī bhāgavatam, mahābhāratam etc\] know about his birth in royal clan. All the others, whether with or without knowledge, know that he incarnated only in the clan of covherds.

**anjanavaṇṇan tannai** – one who has the divine complexion like a black pigment, which makes the eyes of his beholders to be cool.

**tāyar …** – yaśōdāp pirātti, who gave birth to him and other women who were friendly towards him like her, were happy; inimical entities such as kamsan et al, who knew the annihilation of monsters such as pūtanā, śakata et al, right in the state when kriṣṇa was in the cradle, were in a state of fear as to what further harm kriṣṇa will do, now that he has started taking tender steps.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *tāyar* refers to the favourable mothers and periyāḻvār. kamsan, who is an unfavourable entity, not only did not wish to see kriṣṇa, but had fire burning in his stomach when he heard that kriṣṇa had started taking tender steps. While he had sent pūtanā, śakata, yamāḷārjuna et al, upon hearing that they were annihilated, just as it has been mentioned in [tiruppāvai 25](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/01/thiruppavai-25-oruththi-maganai/) “*kanjan vayiṟṟil neruppu*” (like a fireball in kamsan’s stomach), he thought “We did not get to win with any of the inimical entities who we had sent; those who spoke valorously that they will kill him, did not return; we are waiting here with drawn sword, even before he was born; there appears to be no alternative; let us send our minister akrūrar and see if we can get him \[kriṣṇa\] through the bridge of relationship”. Upon calling akrūrar, the words mentioned by akrūrar \[“nothing will happen other than your death”\] was also not pleasant. For the unfavourable entities too, while death would be a welcome event, even that was not happening. For the favourable entities, even when they were worried, through carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam, as to ”What will befall him?” they were happy, more than being worried, with his tender steps.

**vēyar …** – since periyāḻvār appeared in the clan of brāhmaṇas, just as it has been mentioned in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5-4-11 “*vēyar tangaḷ kulattu uditta …*” (one who was born in the clan of brāhmaṇas), others in that clan praised him.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that since he was born as a brāhmaṇa, he has to be mentioned as *vēyar*. Alternatively, just as carrying out *sandyāvandanam* \[an activity carried out three times in a day, propitiating water, with hymns to various celestial entities\] is an identity for brāhmaṇas and tending to cows with their flutes is an identity for herd folk, since periyāḻvār desired to be a herd-person, he had twin-births \[as a brāhmaṇa by birth and as a herd person by desire\], just as kriṣṇa too had twin births \[royal and herd folk\]. *vittucittan* – just as he had said *vāsudēvan*, he says *vittucittan* too \[the term *vāsudēvan* refers to one who is present in all the places; one of those places is in the mind of periyāḻvār too, which is the meaning of the term *vittucittan*\]. If it is not in this way, then identifying a person through an identity \[*vāsudēvan*\] and the ability to attain an entity \[attaining emperumān\] will be negated \[if emperumān has to be identified as the supreme entity, he has to be omnipresent; one of those places where he resides is in the mind of *vittucittan*\]. Even for *vyāpaka mantrams* \[the three esoteric mantrams \[Om namō nārāyaṇāya, Om namō viṣṇavē and Om namō bhagavatē vāsudēvāya\] which signify the all-pervasive characteristic of emperumān\] without the praṇava \[Om\] and nama: \[namō\] terms, there will be no significance \[the mantrams will only say that emperumān is all pervasive. It is only with *Om* and  *nama*: added at the beginning and end respectively, would it mean that he is all pervading and that ātmās have to attain him and carry out kainkaryam to him.

**seerāl …** – those who are capable of reciting these pāsurams, in any manner, which have been expansively and mercifully composed.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *seerāl virittal* refers to envisioning the entity \[kriṣṇa\] in whom the auspicious qualities are present, the reason for that quality to shine \[āḻvār -being endowed with devotion and knowledge by emperumān, without any trace of doubt\] and the benefit for those qualities to shine \[attaining emperumān\]. *uraikka vallār* – even if they do not recite the pāsurams with the pathos of periyāḻvār, if they merely recite the words which āḻvār had mercifully composed, taking refuge under his affection

**māyan …** – they will sire children who carry out activities in line with their *svarūpam* \[basic nature, which is carrying out servitude\] at the divine feet of one who has amazing qualities and who has the beautiful, divine form of a bluish gemstone. Since it has been mentioned in a generic term as *makkaḷ*, this refers to children who come through their learning \[as disciples of such people\] and through their clan.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *paṇiyum* refers to the fact that they \[children\] will carry out servitude for ever. It would also refer to the prayer made in the *uttara vākhyam* \[second line of dvaya mahāmantram in which one prays for being granted servitude\]. *makkaḷ* – this term refers to disciples who are considered as children; it also refers to those who carry out servitude and are considered as children. Is it enough if one were to merely recite the words of the pāsuram? If one were to take refuge under āḻvār’s affection and recite the words, and teach others to recite the words, it would be enough. How is this so? The thoughts of the disciples who have been taught the words of the pāsuram would bring the benefits. As examples. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai quotes from śrī viṣṇu sahasranāmam “*sukhatātam*” (father of sage sukhar, while referring to sage vasiśta), periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2-2-4 “*ivanaip peṟṟa vayiṟudaiyāḷ*” (yaśōdāp pirātti, who has the divine stomach from which she gave birth to kriṣṇa) and [perumāḷ tirumoḻi 7-3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/08/perumal-thirumozhi-7-3/) “*nandanan peṟṟanan*” (nandagōpar sired kriṣṇa). \[In the last two cases, yaśōdāp pirātti and śrī nandagōpar brought up kriṣṇa as their own child and were considered as his parents\]. He also quotes the example of kūrattāḻvār \[father of kūrattāḻvān, rāmānujar’s disciple\]. After kūrattāḻvār’s bhāryāḷ \[his wife\] nangai, attained paramapadam, he wanted to remarry. Looking at kūrattāḻvān’s śrīvaiṣṇavatvam (the quality of being emperumān’s servitor\], he decided that kūrattāḻvān should not be subjected to *anyaśēśatvam* (being a servitor to someone other than emperumān) and decided against marrying again. This is the result of getting a child who is a servitor of emperumān. If this is the benefit of merely reciting the words in the pāsuram, should one state the benefits when one is to recite with the pathos of āḻvār?

We shall next consider the pravēśam of the next tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 1.8.1. Ponniyal kinkini

*ponniyal kiṇkiṇi cutti puram kattittanniyal ōsai salan salan enṟidaminniyal mēgam viraindu edir vandāṟpōlennidaikku ottarā accō accō emperumān! vārā accō accō*

**Пословный перевод:**

ponniyal – coated with gold; kiṇkiṇi – anklet; cutti – cutti, an ornament, worn on the divine forehead; puṟam katti – donning them in their respective place; than – that anklet’s; iyal ōsai – natural sound; salan salan enṟida – as it makes a sound “salan salan”; min iyal – having lightning as its nature (or), being beautiful with lightning; mēgam – cloud; viraindu – hurriedly; edir vandāṟpōl – just as it comes opposite; en idaikku – for my waist; ottarā – coming fast; accō accō – you should come and embrace me (since the word accō is repeated, the overflowing affection is evident); em perumān! – oh, one who is my lord!; vārā – come and embrace me

**Перевод:**

**The ornaments kiṇkiṇi (anklet) and cutti (worn on the forehead) should be donned on their respective location. They should make a noise, which is natural for them. Just like a cloud comes rapidly opposite with lightning, and with those ornaments making noise, you should come fast and hug my waist. Oh, my lord! You should come and hug me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that āḻvār is asking kriṣṇa to come and hug him, just like a cloud comes with lightning.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**ponniyal kiṇkiṇi** – made with coated gold. In order to look beautiful, these ornaments, which are not of pure gold, have been given a coating of gold, to make a noise. Ornaments made with pure gold will not make a perceptible noise while those which are not made of gold, will make a noise.  In order to make them look attractive, they have been given a coating of gold. Alternatively, this could refer to bells which have been suspended from a gold cord. Since these make a noise “*salan salan*”, the ornament *kiṇkiṇi* could refer to the ornament adorning the waist or the anklet worn on the ankles.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that bells (*kiṇki*) have been strung on a golden cord, adorned on the waist and kept on the back side, with *cutti* being on the front side.

**cutti** – ornament worn on the divine forehead. *puṟam katti* – this refers to adorning the ornaments in their respective place. The words *kaṇ, kāl, puṟam, agam* refer to the same meaning – place.

**tanniyal …** – the waist cord as well as the anklet make a natural noise *salan salan*. The word *salan* does not have a meaning on its own. It refers to a noise made, when the ornaments move \[when kriṣṇa comes running to hug her\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when allowed to play, the ornament *kiṇkiṇi* (bells) will make a noise.

**minniyal …** – just like a cloud, which has lightning as its nature, develops feet and comes running from the opposite side. The ornaments *kiṇkiṇi* and *cutti* mentioned here are symbolic of all the ornaments which are donned on the divine form of kriṣṇa, complementing his dark complexion. This example \[of cloud with lightning\] has been mercifully mentioned to show the desire \[of yaśōdāp pirātti\] that he should come with the radiance of all these ornaments \[like lightning streaking across a cloud\].

**en idaikku …** – you should come running and hug me, in order to get on to my waist and remain there.  Repeating the word \[*accō*\] indicates overflowing affection.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār is praying to see kriṣṇa running in towards him while emperumān is praying to get on to the waist \[of āḻvār who is with the pathos of yaśōdāp pirātti\]. You should come such that I could lift and hug you. While āḻvār’s *hastamudra* (keeping the palms together, cupped to perform *anjali*\] extends up to seeking *paramabhakti* \[the situation where he could exist only if he is together with emperumān and would perish otherwise\], emperumān’s expectation is *apradiśēdam* (non-avoidance when he comes towards his followers).

**emperumān …** – After yaśōdāp pirātti told him to come and hug her, since there was a delay, she tells him “Oh, my lord! You should come and hug me”. The term *accō* refers to the act of hugging.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *emperumān* refers to my lord, my benefactor, who is waiting to hear “When will he call me?”  The term *vārā* refers to his \[āḻvār’s\] distress. The term *accō* refers to the word said with joy by people who are desirous of uniting with children.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.8.2. Sengamalap puvil

*sengamalap pūvil tēn uṇṇum vaṇḍē pōlpangigaḷ vandu un pavaḷa vāy moyppasangu vil vāḷ taṇḍu cakkaram ēndiyaangaigaḷālē vandu accō accō ārat taḻuvā vandu accō accō*

**Пословный перевод:**

sem kamalap pūvil – in the reddish lotus flower; tēn uṇṇum – drinking honey; vaṇḍu pōl – like the beetles; pangigaḷ – curly locks; vandu – coming on to; un – your; pavaḷa vāy – mouth, which is like coral; moyppa – to throng; sangu – śrī pāncajanyam; vil – the bow, śrī śārngam; vāḷ – sword, śrī nandakam; taṇḍu – mace, śrī kaumōdakī; cakkaram – śrī sudarśanāḻvān; ēndiya – one who is holding; am kaigaḷālē – with the beautiful hands, come and hug; Ara – completely; taḻuvāy – you should mercifully embrace; vandu accō – you should come and embrace

**Перевод:**

**Just like beetles which drink honey from reddish lotus flowers, your curly locks should throng your divine lips, when you come running \[to embrace me\]. With the divine hands, in which you are holding your divine weapons, conch, bow, sword, mace and disc, you should embrace me. You should embrace me completely.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār tells kriṣṇa to come fast such that the divine locks cover his divine face.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**sengamalam …** – just like beetles which imbibe honey from reddish lotus flower.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that beetles throng the lotus flowers which are growing on their own fertile lands.

**pangigaḷ …** – curly, divine locks should come and throng your divine lips

**sangu …** – your divine hands are holding the divine weapons such as pāncajanyam et al, which are present both for annihilation of your enemies and for providing beauty. Your hands are such beautiful, even without these, that one has to ward off evil eyes. You should embrace me with such beautiful hands.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that with the divine hands which are holding śrī pancāyuda āḻvārs (the five divine weapons), who are mangaḷāśāsanaparars (they keep praising and wishing well for emperumān), you should embrace me. *ārat taḻuvāy* is being said due to excessive affection.

**Ara …** – Instead of being incomplete, your embrace should be complete.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the contact for āḻvār with emperumān \[when he embraces āḻvār\] is similar to youths embracing bosoms of their beloved such that, due to the excessive enjoyment, they would sing pāsurams as an outlet for the joy.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.8.3. Panjavar tudanay

*panjavar tūdanāyp pāradam kai seydunanju umiḻ nāgam kidanda naṟ poygai pukkuanjap paṇattin mēl pāyndittu aruḷ seydaanjana vaṇṇanē! accō accō āyar perumānē! accō accō*

**Пословный перевод:**

panjavar tūdanāy – as the messenger of pāṇḍavas; bāradam – in the mahābhāratam battle; kai seydu – providing help; nanju umiḻ – spitting poison; nāgam – the snake, kāḷiyan; kidanda – dwelling; nal poygai – in the cruel river; pukku – entered; anja – to be fearful; paṇattin mēl – on the spread hoods of that kāḷiyan; pāyndittu – went and jumped (with that, kāḷiyan surrendered); aruḷ seyda – oh, one who has a dark complexion, who showered mercy on him! You should embrace me; āyar perumānē! – oh, one who is the king of herd clan! You should embrace me

**Перевод:**

**You had gone as a messenger of pāṇḍavas and helped them during the mahābhāratam battle. You had jumped on to the spread hoods of snake kāḷiyan, who was residing in the cruel river and spitting poison, in such a manner that he surrendered to you, and you had showered your mercy on him. Oh, one who has a dark form! You should embrace me. Oh, one who is the king of the herd clan! You should embrace me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār had told kriṣṇa to come hurriedly in the previous pāsuram such that his dress and locks were diśevelled. In this pāsuram, he tells kriṣṇa to come such that his divine form is not disturbed.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**panjavar …** – after having been troubled by duryōdana et al, pāṇḍavas lost their kingdom and wealth. They did not have any support other than you \[reference here is to kriṣṇa\]. Being dependent on them completely, you had gone as their messenger, to the court of duryōdana et al, and tried to bring about a compromise between the two sides. When the kauravas refused to accept your proposals, you had said “If that is the case, engage in battle such that the winner gets to rule the kingdom”. Later, during the battle, you had sided with the pāṇḍavas, conducting the battle for them, by arranging their armies in various formations.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that it was kriṣṇa’s prayer that the pāṇḍavas should pray to him to go to the kauravas as their messenger.  It is said that parāśara bhattar \[son of kūrattāZhvān\] had told his disciple nanjīyar, just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 2-2-3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/08/periya-thirumozhi-2-2-3/) “*munnōr tūdu vānarattin vāyil moḻinḻu – avanē – innār tūdan ena ninṟān*” (during śrī rāmāvatāram, śrī rāma had sent hanuman as his messenger to rāvaṇa; the same śrī rāma, in kriṣṇāvatāram, was ready to go as the messenger of pāṇḍavas). kriṣṇa went in as a mediator between pāṇḍavas and kauravas, wondering “Could we make these people \[kauravas\] to accept the peace proposals?” Not finding even an iota of sympathy in their hearts, he had to help the pāṇḍavas in the battle which ensued, by arranging the army formations etc.

**nanju …** – the poisonous snake, kāḷiyan, was dwelling in the cruel pond. Without any regard for him, you had entered the pond. The reason for calling the pond as *nal poygai* (good pond) is the result of contrarian indication, with the snake spitting poison in that pond.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai rearranges the verse as *nal poygai pukku – kidanda – nanjumiḻ nāgam – anjappaṇattin mēl – pāyndittu* to get cogent meaning. It was because of the entry of kāḷiyan that the pond, which was earlier like nectar, became mixed with poison now.

**anja …** – all the friendly people such as the women of the herd clan as well as the menfolk were frightened when they heard this narrative, just as it has been mentioned in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 4-4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/07/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-4-4/) “*āyccimārgaḷum āyarum anjida*” wondering “What will happen, now that he has entered?” Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruppallāṇḍu 10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/11/thiruppallandu-10-ennal-emperuman/) “*aindalaiya painnāgattalaip pāyndavanē*” (Oh, one who jumped on the spread hoods of the five-headed snake kāḷiyan!) you had jumped on the spread hoods of kāḷiyan and danced on his heads, weakening him, such that he surrendered to you, to save his life and prayed, as mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5-7-70 “*krupā mātra manō*: *vrutti prasīda mē*” (you should shower only your mercy on me, thinking of me in your divine mind). You too had showered your mercy on him after he had surrendered to you. The verse “*anjap paṇattin mēl pāyndittu*” would also indicate that kriṣṇa had jumped on to the spread heads of kāḷiyan such that kāḷiyan was scared.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that all the people in tiruvāyppādi (śrī gōkulam) and those who saw the event were frightened for kriṣṇa’s safety when he jumped onto the spread hoods of kāḷiyan. Also, āḻvār, who was feeling knots in his stomach for an event which had happened much earlier in the past, was afraid. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that āḻvār thinks that kāḷiyan surrendering to kriṣṇa and being showered with his mercy were due to his \[āḻvār’s\] fortune

**anjana vaṇṇanē** – Oh, one whose divine form became cool and radiant, since you had protected an entity who had surrendered! You should embrace me.

**āyar perumānē** – Oh, one who has the simplicity of being the lord of herd folk, as opposed to the eminence of being the lord of nityasūris \[permanent dwellers of śrī vaikuṇṭam\]! You should embrace me.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa is the controller of both those who were scared \[when kriṣṇa jumped on kāḷiyan\] and those who were not scared \[since they didn’t see the event\] and protected them all.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.8.4. Nariya sandam

*nāṟiya sāndam namakku iṟai nalgu ennatēṟi avaḷum tiru udambil pūsaūṟiya kūninai uḷḷē odunga anṟuēṟa uruvināy! accō accō emperumān! vārā accō accō*

**Пословный перевод:**

namakku – “apt for our form; nāṟiya – being with fragrance; sāndam – sandalwood paste; iṟai – a little bit; nalgu enna – you must give” saying these words, when you asked the hunchback; avaḷum – that hunchback too; tēṟi – comforting her mind; tiru udambil – on the divine form; pūsa – when she applied eminent paste; anṟu – at that time; ūṟiya – sprouting from her back; kūninai – hunchback; uḷḷē odunga – to disappear inside her body; ēṟa uruvināy – oh, one who straightened it, with your divine hands! You should embrace me; emperumān! – oh, one who is the king of our clan! You should come and embrace me

**Перевод:**

**When you had asked a hunchback lady, who was selling sandalwood paste in maturā, “You should give us a little bit of your eminent sandalwood paste, apt for our divine form”, she had applied the paste on your divine form. At that time, oh, one who had pushed her hunch, which had sprouted from her back, into her body such that it disappeared! You should embrace me. Oh, one, who is the king of our clan! You should come and embrace me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār is asking kriṣṇa to come with the fragrance of sandalwood paste, applied on him by the hunchback lady, kubjā.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**nāṟiya …** – when kriṣṇa and his elder brother balarāma killed the vaśerman, donned new dresses and roamed in the streets of śrī maturā, they came across a hunchback lady, *kubjhā*, who was taking sandalwood paste to be given to kamsan. When kriṣṇa told her “Are you capable of giving sandalwood paste for our elder brother and us?” unable to refuse his request and thinking “Will these people, who are used to the smell of butter, know the distinction of sandalwood paste?” she offered them sandalwood paste of poor quality. Just as it has been mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5-20-6 “*sugantam ētat*” (this appears to be with artificial and not natural fragrance), kriṣṇa refused all those offers. As mentioned in continuation of the same ślōkam “*āvayōr gātra sadruśam dīyatām anulēpanam*” (Look at our divine forms and give sandalwood paste which will be the most appropriate for them), he told her “You should give a little bit of fragrant sandalwood paste which is apt for elder brother’s and our forms”. Feeling happy with way in which he rejected the lowly pastes, the eminence with which he sought the high-quality paste and his beautiful form, the hunchback, without fearing “What shall I do if kamsan punishes me for giving them the high-quality paste that I am taking for him?” consoled her mind and applied the best sandalwood paste which she had, on the divine forms of kriṣṇa and balarāma.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *tēṟik koduttal* (comforting her mind and offering them sandalwood paste) refers to giving them sandalwood paste with affection, without fearing about the torture that kamsan would mete out to her once he comes to know of this incident. This indicates that she had applied the paste on their divine forms with pathos and affection. It would also mean that she offered them the paste so that they could apply it themselves.

**ūṟiya …** – Feeling affectionate towards her since she served him a little bit without expecting anything from him, kriṣṇa mercifully thought in his divine mind “Let us straighten her hunchback”. Oh, one who had pushed back, at that time, the hunch which appeared as if it had taken root on her back, into her body, with your divine hands! You should embrace me. Oh, one who is the king of our clan! You should come and embrace me.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here for the term *uḷḷē odunga* – he had pulled her jaws and pushed her hunch such that it would get hidden inside her body. The purpose of his straightening her hunch was to indicate to us to get rid of our crooked thoughts and follow him. *anṟu* – at the same time when she applied sandalwood paste on him, he removed her hunchback.

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.8.5. Kalal mannar

*kaḻal mannar sūḻak kadir pōl viḷangieḻal uṟṟu mīṇḍē irundu unnai nōkkumsuḻalaip peridu udait tuccōdananaiaḻala viḻittānē! accō accō āḻiyangaiyanē accō accō*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaḻal mannar – kings who were wearing valorous anklets; sūḻa – as they were paying their obeisance, around\|; kadir pōl – like sūryan (sun); viḷangi – being radiant; eḻal uṟṟu – attempting to get up; mīṇḍē – again; irundu – hiding it, by wrath, sat down; unnai – you; nōkkum – looking, as if to harm; peridu – mostly; suḻalai udai – indulging in conspiracies; duccōdananai – duryōdana; aḻala – with intense anger; viḻittānē! – oh, one who looked at! You should embrace; āḻi am kaiyanē – oh, one who is holding the divine disc in your beautiful, divine hand! You should embrace

**Перевод:**

**duryōdana, son of dritarāśtra, was sitting radiantly like sūryan, in his court, surrounded by kings, who were wearing valorous anklets. Upon seeing you, entering the court, he attempted to get up from his throne. Again, hiding that act through his wrath, he sat down, looking at you as if to harm you. Oh, one who looked at that duryōdana, who was indulging in conspiracies, with intense anger! You should embrace me. Oh, one who is holding the divine disc in your beautiful, divine hand! You should embrace.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) āḻvār desires that kriṣṇa should come with the divine disc in his divine hand.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kaḻal …** – upon getting to know that kriṣṇa was coming as the messenger of pāṇḍavas, all the kings in neighbouring countries, wearing their valorous anklets, came to the royal court of duryōdana, sat around him, in a servile manner. duryōdana was sitting on his throne, being radiant like the sun, on account of his crown and other ornaments which he had worn, as well as his due to his power. He had told the kings “When kriṣṇa comes, don’t get up or enquire about his well-being”. He had laid a false throne, by digging a pit under it so that when kriṣṇa sat on it, it would break and kriṣṇa would be carried down below. He had organised wrestlers in the pit, below the false throne, so that when kriṣṇa falls into the pit, the wrestlers would punch him and maul him. However, when kriṣṇa entered the court, all the kings, not being under their control, got up and offered salutations to him, just as it has been mentioned in mahābhāratam sabhā parvam 75 “*avaśā*: *pratibhēdirē*” (they carried out, obediently). duryōdana too, out of fear, attempted to get up from his throne, upon seeing kriṣṇa, but sat again, hiding his wrath towards kriṣṇa.

tiruvāimoḻi piḷḷai says here that the kings in the neighbourhood were powerful too and sat around duryōdana. After seeing the kings getting up from their respective seat and paying obeisance to kriṣṇa, despite his order not to do that, duryōdana too attempted to get up and thought “This is the time for seeing the result of the earlier planned conspiratorial acts” and remembered ordering his wrestlers to wait for kriṣṇa to fall down from the false throne that he had laid out for him.

**unnai …** – duryōdana was looking at you with the intention of harming you through the false throne etc, carrying out conspiratorial activities. Oh, one who looked at that duryōdana with the fury in your divine mind appearing blatantly in your eyes! You should embrace me.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa too, aware of the hints, made the conspiracies hatched by duryōdana, to turn on him by looking at him widely, with intense anger in his divine eyes.

**āḻi am kainyanē …** – Oh, one who is holding the divine disc on your divine hand! You should embrace.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the divine disc was more like an ornament on the divine hands of kriṣṇa, since he had already looked at duryōdana with intense anger. By calling duryōdana as *duccōsana*, āḻvār says that he has a heart which cannot be corrected by anyone.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.8.6. Porokkap panni

*pōr okkap paṇṇi ip pūmip poṟai tīrppāntēr okka ūrndāy! seḻum tār visayṟkāykār okkum mēnik karum perum kaṇṇanē!ārat taḻuvāy vandu accō accō āyargaḷ pōrēṟē! accō accō*

**Пословный перевод:**

ip pūmi – this earth’s; poṟai – burden; tīrppān – to reduce; pōr okkap paṇṇi – making duryōdana et al to engage in war; seḻum – excellent; tār – having tumbai garland \[a kind of flowery garland worn by valorous warriors in battle\]; visayaṟku – for arjuna, who is called as “vijayan” \[victorious\]; āy – standing as his support; tēr – his chariot; okka – matching the enemies’ chariots; ūrndāy! – oh, one who conducted!; kār okkum – similar to cloud; mēni – having a divine form; karu – black; peru – extending up to the ears; kaṇṇanē – oh, one who has eyes!; vandu – coming in \[my\] proximity; Ara – completely; taḻuvāy – you should mercifully embrace me; āyargaḷ – having incarnated in the clan of herd-folk; pōr – ready to fight; ēṟē – oh, one who is arrogant like a bull! Embrace me

**Перевод:**

**In order to reduce the burden of this earth, you had made duryōdana et al to engage in a war. Oh, one who stood by arjuna, who wears a tumbai garland, by conducting his chariot, matching the chariots of enemies! Oh, one who has a complexion similar to cloud and dark, expansive eyes, extending up to the ears! You should come near me and embrace me. Oh, one who is like an arrogant bull ready for battle! You should embrace me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**pōr …** – this refers to waging a battle with the five pāṇḍavas and their army of about seven *akśauhiṇis* (each *akśauhiṇi* consists of 21,870 elephants, 21,870 chariots, 65,610 horses and 1,09,350 foot soldiers) opposing an army of eleven *akśauhiṇis*, a hundred kings, great warriors such as bhīśma, drōṇa et al. After duryōdana had curtly said that “We will not give even that much of land on which a stick could be pushed in, for the pāṇḍavas” kriṣṇa made duryōdana et al to engage in a war.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that kriṣṇa was firm that he would oppose the eleven *akśauhiṇis* of enemy camp, which had a hundred kings and eminent warriors such as karṇa, bhīśma, drōṇa et al with the seven *akśauhiṇi*s and five kings (on the pāṇḍavas’ side) on equal footing. This is not only due to their \[kauravas’\] unfavourable posture and pāṇḍavas’ favourable posture. It was also due to removal of earth’s burden. Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 9-1-10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/06/thiruvaimozhi-9-1-10-kannan-allal/) “*maṇṇin bāram nīkkudaṟkē vadamaduraip pirandān*” (emperumān incarnated in northern maturā only to reduce the load on earth) and the saying of bhūmip pirātti “*nabhāram saptasāgara*:” (the seven oceans, the anchoring mountains etc are not a burden to me) who had said “Oceans and mountains are not a burden for me; without acknowledging the help rendered by emperumān continuously from the time that he had provided the ātmās with a form and senses, there are people who, due to their ego and possessiveness, behave in a thankless manner. It is these people who are a burden to me”. To remove that burden, he conducted his chariot as an equivalent of many chariots on the other side.

**ippūmip poṟai tīrppān** – the purpose of bringing about this war was to annihilate all those who were not following the path of righteousness and who were having the behaviour of monsters. Just as it has been mentioned in tiruvāimoḻi 9-1-10 “*maṇṇin bāram nīkkudaṟkē vada maduraip piṟandān*”, this was also the purpose of his incarnation.

**tēr …** – arjuna had donned garlands made of flowers of *tumbai*, *vāgai* etc as an indication of engaging in war and emerging victorious. Just as it has been mentioned in mahābhāratam “*yasya mantrīca gōptāca*” (kriṣṇa remains as the minister and protector) etc, oh, one who remained as everything \[during the war\] and conducted the chariot matching all the chariots of all the enemies! Since kriṣṇa had taken a vow “I will not wield a weapon”, conducting the chariot \[of arjuna’s\] he had annihilated the armies of enemies with the chariot wheels. He had reduced the burden of earth merely by ably conducting the chariot, as mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 3-2-3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-2-3-kolla-makkol/) “*kollā mākkōl*” (the eminent stick with which he guided the horses of chariot and which did not directly kill anyone).

**kār okkum …** – Oh, one who has the form of rain bearing clouds and eyes which are wide, as mentioned in amalanādipirān 9 “*kariyāvāgip pudai parandu*” (being dark and expansive)! This states the happiness resulting from the effect of removing the burden on earth and making arjuna, his follower, as victorious.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa’s eyes widened and became huge upon seeing āḻvār \[when he came to embrace\]. Hence, āḻvār is addressing him as one who has expansive eyes.

**Ara …** – you should embrace me fully such that my desire is satiated.

**āyargaḷ …** – Oh, one who is obedient towards the herd-people, as result of which one who is arrogant like a bull which is battle-ready! You should embrace me.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.8.7. Mikka perum

*mikka perum pugaḻ māvali vēḷviyiltakkadu idu anṟu enṟu dānam vilakkiyasukkiran kaṇṇait turumbāl kiḷaṟiyacakkarak kaiyanē! accō accō sangam idattānē! accō accō*

**Пословный перевод:**

mikka peru – being huge; pugaḻ – having fame (due to his magnanimity); māvali – mahābali’s; vēḷviyil – in his ritual (when emperumān, as vāmana, went to seek three steps of land); idu – “donating to him; takkadu anṟu enṟu – is not proper” saying this; dānam – donation of land; vilakkiya – one who prevented; sukkiran – śukra, the ācārya \[teacher\] of monsters; kaṇṇai – eyes; turumbāl – with the edge of pavitram \[bunch of sacred grass\] worn on his divine finger; kiḷaṟiya – one who poked; cakkarak kaiyanē – oh, one who holds the divine disc on your divine hand! You should; sangam – śrī pāncajanyam \[divine conch\]; idattānē – oh, one who is donning on the divine left hand! You should embrace me

**Перевод:**

**emperumān had gone \[in the guise of a dwarf, vāmana\] to the ritual arena of mahābali, who was famous for being magnanimous, with the intention of seeking three steps of land. śukrācārya, the guru \[teacher\] for the clan of monsters, attempted to prevent mahābali from donating the land sought, saying “Donating to him is not proper”. Oh, one who holds the divine disc on your divine hand! You should embrace me with the hand with which you had poked the eye of that śukrācārya, with the tip of the divine grass which you were wearing on that hand. Oh, one who holds the divine conch on your left hand! You should embrace me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that āḻvār wants kriṣṇa to come with the disguise which he had taken on, when he went to the ritual arena of mahābali, donning all the divine weapons.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**mikka …**– mahābali, a monster \[grandson of emperumān’s follower, prahlādan\] was famous for being magnanimous. When he was conducting a ritual, emperumān went to that arena, for the sake of indran \[who had lost his kingdom to mahābali\], disguising himself as vāmana, a dwarf. He told mahābali, as mentioned in [tiruvāīmoḻi 3-8-9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-9-kolvan-nan/) “*koḷvan nān māvali mūvadi tā*” (give me three steps of land, mahābali; I will accept), to give him three steps of land. Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 1-8-6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-8-6-kalanthu-ennavi/) “*pulan koḷ māṇāy*” (having a form which attracted the senses of all), due to the beauty of vāmana, which was stealing all the senses of beholders as well as the childishness with which vāmana had demanded fulfilment of his wish, mahābali, with his heart stolen by vāmana, agreed to grant him that which he had sought. śukrācārya, his guru, analysed from the form, the gait and the way in which he demanded, that the visitor is not any ordinary human personality. He warned mahābali “He is the lord of all; he has come on behalf of celestial entities, to rob you of all your possessions. Thus, it is not proper on your part to donate him like this”. Rejecting his words, when mahābali attempted to offer water on the hands of vāmana (symbolic of acceding to vāmana’s request for three steps of land), śukrācārya took the form of a beetle and lodged himself at the entrance of the vessel through which water was to be poured as a symbolism, blocking the flow of water. vāmana, with the edge of the *pavitram* (sacred grass) worn on his finger, poked the hole as if testing it. The grass pierced the eye of śukrācārya, blinding him and making him to fall out. Oh, one who has the divine disc on your divine hand!  Since the verse states “*turumbāl kiḷaṟīya cakkarakkaiyan*” it appears that it was the divine disc which went in the form of the grass and poked the eye of śukrācārya, just as it has been said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10-6-8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/02/thiruvaimozhi-10-6-8-meynninru/) “*karudum idam porum tiruvāḻi*” (divine disc goes to the place where emperumān thinks of, to engage in battle).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that śukrācārya told mahābali “His seeking alms and your giving alms are both incorrect”. He ordered mahābali not to accede to vāmana’s request. mahābali, instead of listening to his ācārya’s words, attempted to offer water as symbolic of fulfilling vāmana’s request. periyavāccān piḷḷai, one of our preceptors and who had mercifully given the vyākhyānam for all the pāsurams of *nālāyira divya prabandam*, asked nampiḷḷai, who was his ācārya (guru, teacher) “One who fulfilled the wish of an alms-seeker, a worthy recipient, was punished and imprisoned. One who warned him, saying ‘This is a deceptive person; do not fulfil his request’ speaking the truth, lost his eye. Is this proper?” \[the reference here is to mahābali who had to be pushed down into the nether world by emperumān after he had measured all the lower worlds with one step and all the upper worlds with the second step, and asked mahābali as to where he should keep the third; mahābali told him to put his third step on his head, thus pushing him to the nether world; śukrācārya lost his vision in the eye which was poked by the edge of the sacred grass\]. nampiḷḷai told periyavāccān piḷḷai “mahābali did not heed the words of his ācārya; hence he was punished. śukrācārya prevented a righteous act \[donation to a brāhmaṇa\] being performed; hence he too was punished”. When asked: just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 5-1-2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/07/periya-thirumozhi-5-1-2/) “*kaḷḷak kuraḷāy māvaliyai*” (with a deceptive disguise, cheating mahābali) and in [tiruvāimoḻi 4-8-6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/04/thiruvaimozhi-4-8-6-arivinal-kuraivilla/) “*kodum kōḷāl nilam koṇḍa*” (reclaiming earth through a cruel path, by deceiving mahābali), could emperumān demonstrate a dishonest activity and break established lawful traditions? The response was: just as it has been said in [tirumālai 15](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thirumalai-15/) “*poyyarkkē poyyanāgum*” (emperumān will act deceptively with those who act in a deceptive manner) and in [tiruvāimoḻi 1-4-3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/07/thiruvaimozhi-1-4-3-vidhiyinal-pedai/) “*madiyināl kuraḷ māṇāy*” (through his intelligence, taking the form of a dwarf and seeking alms), for emperumān this conduct is acceptable. Moreover, when such acts are carried out for the sake of his followers, everything is valid only. He did not do these for fulfilling his desire.

**sangam idattānē** – there is never a separation between the divine disc and *śrī pāncajanyam* (divine conch). Thus, when the divine disc appears on emperumān’s divine right hand, the divine conch will have to appear on his divine left hand.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when a hurdle in the form of a block is noticed in the vessel, first it has to be blown away. For this purpose, emperumān was carrying the conch.

**accō accō** – she tells kriṣṇa to come with his divine hands and the āḻvārs \[divine weapons are referred to as āḻvārs in our traditional custom\], and to hug her.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 1.8.8. Ennidu mayam

*ennidu māyam en appan aṟindilanmunnaiya vaṇṇamē koṇḍu aḷavāy ennamannu namuciyai vānil suḻaṟṟīyaminnu mudiyanē! accō accō vēngadavāṇanē! accō accō*

**Пословный перевод:**

idu – “the way you are doing; en māyam – appears to be illusory; en appan – my father; aṟindilan – did not know (earlier, that you would do like this). (Hence); munnaiya vaṇṇam – the state you were earlier in, when you sought alms; E koṇḍu – taking the same form; aḷavāy – you should measure”; enṟa – the one who said this; mannu – one who remained steadfast in his position; namuciyai – (mahābali’s son) namuci; vānil – in the sky; suḻaṟṟiya – one who swirled and threw him; minnu – shining radiantly; mudiyanē! – oh, one who has divine crown! You should embrace me; vēngadam – on the hills of tiruvēngadam; vāḻ nanē – oh, one who is dwelling! You should embrace me

**Перевод:**

**namuci, the son of mahābali, upon seeing that emperumān was growing rapidly with his divine feet and was going to measure the worlds with those feet, said “What an illusion is this! My father had not known earlier that you would do this way. You should take the form which you had, when you sought alms and measure land with those steps only”. Oh, one, who swirled and threw that namuci in the sky! You should embrace me. Oh, one who is dwelling in the divine hills of tiruvēngadam! You should embrace me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that āḻvār wants kriṣṇa to come with the shiny crown.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**en …**– as soon as droplets of water fell on his divine palm (symbolic of mahābali accepting his request for three steps of land), emperumān stared lengthening his feet to measure the worlds. namuci, the son of mahābali, came running, trying to prevent the growing of the divine feet, saying “What is this?” emperumān asked him “Why are you preventing the growth of my feet? Should I not measure that which was offered through water?” namuci responded, saying “īsn’t your action deceptive?” emperumān asked him back “Who are you to say that it is deceptive? Looking at my form of being a bachelor and acceding to my request, your father granted me my wish, through the medium of water. Was that false?” namuci replied “My father was caught in the web of your deception and did not know any of your methods”. emperumān queried him further “How did you conclude that my action is deceptive?” namuci said “If it is not deceptive, measure with the form with which you had sought alms” Even when emperumān told him “Is it possible to measure with the previous form? ḍoesn’t the form change constantly?” namuci was firm in his view. Oh, one who swirled that namuci and threw him in the skies, and one, who has an effulgent crown! His crown became effulgent after he had removed the *anyaśēśatvam* (being servitors of other entities) of all the ātmās \[souls\] and their *svasvātanryam* (being dependent only on themselves and not dependent on emperumān).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: emperumān, after removing the hurdle created by śukrācārya, thought “His disciples may start taking inimical actions” and hence started growing up, to measure the worlds. namuci, son of mahābali and disciple of śukrācārya, trying to prevent this, asked him “What is this?” emperumān asked him “Why are you preventing this?” namuci replied “You are changing your form. What did you seek and what are you doing?” emperumān said “I have carried out all the activities without any violation to my state of being a bachelor. I am qualified in vēda śāstrams (sacred texts\]. Should I not complete the measurement of the land given by your father?” namuci said “My father does not know. Without consulting me, who is fully matured, did he act properly?” emperumān responded saying “Is one, who did not listen to his guru, going to ask you prior to donating?” namuci said “If there is a hurdle to the donation, should one not revert to the original status?” emperumān said “What did you say? It is only after knowing the hurdle which would come through you that I had accepted this with the fiat that no objection would be entertained after a moment of getting the donation, instead of the usual limit of ten days”. namuci again said “You should measure with the form with which you had sought the alms” emperumān replied “Is that possible? It is that time in my life when the body keeps changing every moment”.  namuci replied “Why can’t you grow at the rate at which people grow in this world?” emperumān said “Will growth be uniform for all?” namuci then said “I have to hate only my father. There is no point in faulting you” to which emperumān asked “Why should you hate your father? Just as it has been mentioned in mantra praśnam ‘*ātmāvai putranāmāsi*’ (father is born as the son), when you are not in favour of his donation, \[it is evident that\] you have been born in the wrong way. You are not his son. You have despised him in my presence, saying that he does not know anything. You cannot call him as your father. Even though he has sired you, he will not recognise you anymore as his son and will consider you as one who had been born the wrong way”. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai now asks in his svāpadēśam “Was there enough time for asking all these questions and counter questions, more and more?” He gives the response himself quoting [mudal tiruvandādi pāsuram 79](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/08/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-79/) “*oṇḍārai nīrangai tōya nimirndilaiyē neeḷvisumbil ārangai tōya aduttu*” (the moment water fell on his divine hands, he grew up rapidly to reach the ethereal layer). emperumān grew the moment water fell on his divine hand. However, he had sufficient time before that to engage in conversation with namuci. hanuman was flying towards lankā, in search of sītāp pirātti. While flying, *maināka parvatam* \[a huge mountain\] stood in his way and asked him several questions. While he was hurrying towards his destination, he still found time to respond to its questions. Further on the way, *nāga mātā* \[a deity for snakes\] came in his way and told him that she wanted to swallow him. He entered her mouth, converting his *stūla* (gross) form into *sūkśma* (subtle) form, and came out in a moment with his *stūla* form and reached his destination. When it is possible for hanuman to do these, when he was in a hurry to complete his task, would it not be possible for the omnipotent entity to raise and answer questions? Further on, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that when a muktātmā \[one who is liberated from samsāram, the materialistic realm\] gets liberated and goes to śrī vaikuṇṭam in a moment, in the path of light (*arcirādi mārgam*), he accepts the honours given to him by various entities enroute.

**vēngadam …** – Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 3-3-8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-3-8-kunram-endhi/) “*anṟu jñalam aḷanda pirān – senṟu sēr tiruvēngadam māmalai*” (the place where our benefactor, who measured all the worlds at that time, went and resided is the great hill of tiruvēngadam), oh, one who is standing in tiruvēngadam as its controller, after completing your activity of measuring all the worlds! You should embrace me.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: After swirling and throwing out namuci in the ethereal layers, after getting rid of *anyaśēśatvam* \[servitors to other deities\] and *svasvātantryam* \[being dependent only on self and not on emperumān\] of samsāris, his crown became effulgent. That feature took root when he became vēngadavāṇan, residing in tirumalai. However, that was established only when he hugged āḻvār. The term *minnu mudiyan* became a reality only after kriṣṇa embraced āḻvār.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.8.9. Kanda kadalum

*kaṇḍa kadalum malaiyum ulagu ēḻummuṇḍattukku āṟṟā mugil vaṇṇā ō! enṟuiṇḍaic cadai mudi īsan irakkoḷḷamaṇḍai niṟaittānē! accō accō mārvil maṟūvanē! accō accō*

**Пословный перевод:**

iṇḍai – being dense; sadai mudi – having matted hair; īsan – rudran; kaṇḍa – “those which are seen; kadalum – oceans; malaiyum – mountains; ēḻu ulagum – seven worlds (even if all these are attempted to fill-up); muṇḍattukku – for the cranium which is in my hand; āṟṟā – are insufficient; O! mugil vaṇṇā! – oh, one who is like a cloud when it comes to being magnanimous”; enṟu – crying out like this, in line with his grief; irak koḷḷa – as he sought; maṇḍai – (that) cranium; niṟaittānē! – oh, one who filled it! You should embrace me; mārvil – on your divine chest; maṟuvanē – oh, one who has śrīvats (divine mole)! You should embrace

**Перевод:**

**rudran, who has densely matted hair and who was carrying a begging bowl, in the shape of cranium, lamented “Even if the oceans, mountains, all the worlds, which are seen, are attempted to fill-in, the cranium in my hand is not getting filled up.” Looking up to emperumān, he pleaded “Oh, one who is like the cloud in your magnanimity! You should help me”. Oh, one who filled up that cranium! You should embrace me. Oh, one who has a divine mole on your divine chest! You should embrace me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that kriṣṇa should come with the divine mole on his divine chest.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kaṇḍa …**– even if I attempt to fill the cranium in my hand with the oceans, mountains and the seven worlds which are seen, they are not sufficient to fill it up.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 3-2-1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-2-1-munnir-gyalam/) “*munnīr jñālam padaitta mugil vaṇṇanē*” (Oh, one, who is having the divine complexion similar to a cloud! You had created the world with oceans), the oceans, mountains and the worlds which you had created.

**muṇḍam** – cranium. This implies that despite roaming around, seeking alms, he is unable to fill up the cranium. Alternatively, even if he went around seeking alms in all these places \[oceans, mountains, worlds\], he was unable to fill up the cranium.

**mugil vaṇṇā** – Oh, one who has the magnanimity of cloud which pours rain without distinction between ocean and land! This implies that apart from emperumān, there is none who is capable of filling up the cranium.

**O! enṟu** – calling, manifesting his grief

**iṇḍai …** – rudran, who has densely plaited, matted hair and who has the ego of being *īśvaran* (one who controls everything). This speaks about the fact that his *īśvaratvam* (the quality of being *īśvaran*) came about due to the power of his penance \[only people who carry out penance will have matted hair\] and his egoistic nature.

**irakkoḷḷa** – just as it has been mentioned in mātsya purāṇam 182-87 “*tatra nārāyaṇa śrīmān mayā bhikśām prayāsita*:” (nārāyaṇan, who was with pirātti \[śrī mahālakśmi\], was beseeced by me for alms), rudra sought for alms, from emperumān, with sorrovfulness. The term *irakkoḷḷa* is considered as a single word.; to seek alms.

**maṇḍai niṟaittānē** – rudran tells his consort, pārvati, as mentioned in mātsya purāṇam – 182 “*viṣṇu prasādāt suśrōṇi kapālam tat sahasratā – sputitam bahudāyātam  svapna labdam danam yatā*” (just as wealth seen in one’s dream disappears when the person wakes up, the cranium, which I had in my hand, with the mercy of viṣṇu, broke into a thousand pieces and disappeared), the cranium broke into smithereens, without anyone knowing the way in which it disappeared. Just as it has been said in [tiruccanda viruttam 42](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/11/thiruchchandha-viruththam-42/) “*ūṟu senguridiyāl niṟaitta*” (filling up with secreting reddish blood), oh, one who filled up that cranium with reddish blood!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 2-2-2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/01/thiruvaimozhi-2-2-2-epavam-parame/) “*araṟkup piccai pey gōpāla kōḷari*” (Oh, one who is like a lion among the covherd people, who offered alms to rudran), oh, one who filled the cranium held by rudran!

**mārvil maṟuvanē** – Oh, one who has the divine mole on your divine chest, as an indication of your being the supreme lord of all! You should embrace me. Alternatively, instead of *muṇḍattukku āṟṟā*, if the text had been *uṇḍattukku āṟṟā*, for the term *kaṇḍa kadalum …* – the meaning would be: after being cursed by brahmā, rudran had gone wandering around the oceans, mountains, various worlds etc in order to get the cranium on his hand to be filled up. Just as it has been mentioned in irāmānusa nūṟṟandādi “*mudaittalai Un*” (eating from the foul-smelling cranium), in order to rid himself of eating from the foul-smelling cranium, rudran, who has matted hair and the pride that he is *īśvaran*, appealing to emperumān’s quality of magnanimity, cried out *mugil vaṇṇā O*. Since you \[referring to emperumān\] knew that there was none other than you who would be a refuge for such rudran, you filed up his cranium out of your mercy, just as it has been mentioned in tiruvāimoḻi 2-2-2 “*ararkkup piccai pey gōpāla kōḷari*”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the pāsuram has to be rearranged as *iṇḍaiccadai mudi īsan āṟṟādu irakkoḷḷa, kadalum malaiyum uṇḍa kadal vaṇṇā O enṟadukku – maṇḍai niṟaittānē* to get the correct sequence of meaning. He further explains this saying that the garb of carrying out penance, with the hair matted, and being the lord of all would not syncronise in one form \[the form of rudran\]. rudran had been sorrowful for a long time, after thinking through his vanity that he was the controller of all. He went to emperumān and pleaded with him “No one supports me”. It was after this that he was told as in “*mōha śāstrāṇi kāraya*” (you could attract people through the text of bewilderment). Through that, with the divine will of emperumān, he started controlling those who became followers of that text, and that he would remain as īśvaran \[one who controls his followers\] until his matted hair loosens up \[until deluge\].

*āṟṟādu irakkoḷḷa* – apart from seeking alms everywhere and finding that the cranium in his hand was not getting filled-up, during the time that emperumān swallowed the oceans, mountains and the seven worlds, he \[rudran\] too went into emperumān’s divine stomach and got spat out during the next cycle of creation. Since he was one inside the divine stomach of emperumān and had been spat out, isn’t it strange that his name is *Sivan* (that which is auspicious)? Feeling embarrassed with his deed of destruction, he calls emperumān as *mugil vaṇṇā O*, in order to get liberated from his form. It was for this reason that emperumān filled up his cranium, since he would not be a protector if he had not protected rudran. The term *adu* in *muṇḍattukku* has got changed to *attu* (*muṇḍhattu*). Both *attu* and *ku* (the last syllable in *muṇḍattukku*) are fillers and express outwardly the sympathy inside the heart. emperumān’s act of filling up the cranium indicates that the seeking of alms by rudran was not the means to get the cranium to be filled up, but it was emperumān’s mercy. This is brought out clearly in tiruvāimoḻi 2-2-2 “*aruḷāl aḷippār Ar*” (Who will give, out of mercy?) Just as gajēndrāḻvān had appealed to emperumān when caught by the crocodile, as mentioned in siṟiya tirumadal “*nārāyaṇā O*” since he did not know of any other means by which he could overcome his sorrow, rudran is calling out to emperumān as *mugil vaṇṇā O*.

We shall next consider the 10<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.8.10. Tunniya perirul

*tunniya pēriruḷ sūḻndu ulagai mūdamanniya nānmaṟai muṟṟum maṟaindidapinivvulaginil pēriruḷ nīnga anṟuannam adu ānānē! accō accō arumaṟai tandānē! accō ahcō*

**Пословный перевод:**

tunniya – permanent; pēr iruḷ – the huge darkness of ignorance; sūḻndu – pervading; ulagai – world; mūda – to envelop; manniya – eternal; nāngu maṟai – four vēdams; muṟṟum – fully; maṟaindida – as they disappeared; pin – later; ivvulaginil – formed in this world; pēr iruḷ – huge darkness; nīnga – to be removed; anṟu – during that time; annam adu ānānē – oh, one who incarnated as a swan! You should embrace; aru maṟai – rare vēdam; tandānē! – oh, one who mercifully gave! You should embrace

**Перевод:**

**The four vēdams (sacred texts) disappeared such that permanent, huge darkness of ignorance pervaded and enveloped the world. Oh, one who incarnated subsequently during that time, as a swan, so that the huge darkness would be removed! You should embrace me. Oh, one who mercifully gave the rare vēdam! You should embrace.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that āḻvār desires that kriṣṇa should come with the disguise which attracted him.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tunniya …** – just as in the absence of light darkness spreads everywhere, when vēdams (sacred texts), which reveal the *karma svarūpam* (basic nature of deeds) and *brahma svarūpam* (basic nature of supreme being), disappear, the darkness of ignorance spreads throughout the world and hides everything.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that vēdams are innumerable, as mentioned in “*anantāvai vēdā*:”. They could disappear either when monsters steal them from brahmā or during total deluge. Then, they will not have the distinction between the *pūrva bhāgam* (former part), which deals with carrying out *karmas* (deeds) and the *uttara bhāgam* (latter part), which deals with *brahmam* (supreme being). When vēdams, which are permanent, without fault and self-illuminating, disappear, just like darkness envelops when light is absent, darkness of ignorance spreads. This darkness is composed of two parts – an inner darkness and an outer darkness. Inner darkness is the absence of light which comes from *uttara bhāgam* (dealing with supreme being) and outer darkness is the absence of light which comes from *pūrva bhāgam* (dealing with karmas).

**manniya …** – vēdams, which are permanent and are composed of four parts such as rig etc disappear.

**pin …** – subsequently, in order to remove the huge darkness which had enveloped the world.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that after the vēdams have disappeared and both the inner darkness and outer darkness have enveloped the world. āḻvār says *ivvulagu*, specifically *bhārata varśa*, the peninsular region among the three oceans, since it is here that *śruti* (vēdams, sacred texts), *smriti* (remembering and recalling the sacred texts), *itihāsa* (great epics of śrī rāmāyaṇa and mahābhāratam) and *purāṇas* (narratives about emperumān, mainly, and some of the celestial entities) happen without any shortcoming. Since this is the primary land, leaving aside the other worlds, he refers to this land as *ivvulagu*.

**anṟu …**– Oh, one who incarnated as *hamsa* (swan) bird, which is capable of distinguishing between the essence (useful) and the non-essence (useless)! You should embrace.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when brahmā et al cried out “We have lost our eyes; we have lost our wealth” \[after the vēdams were stolen by monsters\], emperumān incarnated in the form of a swan, which is capable of distinguishing between the essence and the non-essence. Since he instructed celestial deities such as brahmā et al, sages such as sanaka et al, without their asking for it, āḻvār says *annam adu*, to refer to emperumān’s giving them the vēdams, on his own. Even if they had asked for it, he would have given them the vēdams, using their asking for it as a pretext. Instead of saying *āgiṟān* (he becomes) the reason for saying *ānān* (became) is that he had instructed them vēdams in the form of a swan, such that it was firmly established in their minds. Since the instructions were given by swan, there is no hurdle in saying that it was an ācārya (guru, or teacher). āḻvār considers the beneficial acts of emperumān, carried out to those celestial entities and sages, as his benefit, as a result of which, he says *accō*, in amazement.

**arumaṟai …** – Oh, one who gave the vēdams, which are rarer to get, than even you! You should embrace.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār is qualifying the vēdams as *arumaṟai* (rare to get vēdams) because he is, as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi “*vēdap payan koḷḷa valla vittucittan*” (viṣṇu cittar who is capable of taking in the benefit of vēdam) one who knows the benefit of vēdam and that the most secretive instruction of vēdams is to carry out mangaḷāśāsanam (praising emperumān and wishing well for him). By saying “*tandān*” (he gave), āḻvār says that it was not limited to *śāstrajanyajñānam* (knowledge gained by reading śāstrams) or to *upadēśajñānam* (knowledge gained by listening to an ācārya’s instructions). He says that it was given by emperumān directly, through his physical proximity, with knowledge and devotion, without any trace of ignorance. Who gave this, without expecting anything? āḻvār says that it is the one who is distinct from the form of a swan, the benefactor who is donning the yellow-coloured divine dress and who is residing sweetly in śrī villibuttūr, the *vataperum kōyil udaiyān* \[this is the divine name of emperumān who is dwelling in śrī villibuttūr, for whom periyāḻvār was carrying out *puśpa kainkaryam*, carrying out servitude through flowers and garlands\].

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 1.8.11. Naccuvar munnirkum

*naccuvār munniṟkum nārāyanan tnnaiaccō varuga enṟu āycci uraittanamaccaṇi mādap puduvaik kōn battan solniccalum pāduvār neeḷ visumbu āḷvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

naccuvār – those who desire to see him; mun niṟkum – one who is coming in front; nārāyaṇan tannai – śrīman nārāyaṇan; accō varuga enṟu – asking him to embrace; āycci – yaśōdāp pirātti, his mother; uraittana – the pāsurams which she said, calling out to him; maccu aṇi mādam – having mansions with several layers; puduvai – for śrī villibuttūr; kōn – one, who is the controller; battan – periyāḻvār, who is eminent among the brāhmaṇas; sol – mercifully composed pāsurams; niccalum – all the time; pāduvār – those who are capable of reciting, with affection; neeḷ visumbu – parama padam, which is known as parama ākāśam; āḷvar – they will be capable of controlling

**Перевод:**

**yaśōdāp pirātti, the mother, had called out to śrīman nārāyaṇa, who stands in front of those who desire to see him, and asked him to embrace her. periyāḻvār, who is eminent among brāhmaṇas, and who is the controller of śrī villibuttūr, which has mansions with several layers of construction, composed these pāsurams mercifully. Those who are capable of reciting these pāsurams, all the time, will be capable of controlling parama padam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In the end, āḻvār mentions the benefit which will accrue to one who learns this tirumoḻi and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**naccuvār …** – nārāyaṇan, who comes in front of those who desire him, without looking at differences in their birth, conduct etc, with the form which they desire to see.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *nārāyaṇa* could refer to the meaning derived from *yaugikam* (this is the meaning derived from the root of the word. Here, it refers to one who is the abode for all the ātmās and one who resides inside all the ātmās) or to *rūdyartam* (the meaning which is widely known to all). He says that though the *yaugika* meaning may appear to be true here, it is the *rūdyartam* which is more prominent. The term *tannai* is *vastu nirdēśam*, viz. pointing out to the entity who is indicated. Here, it is nārāyaṇan. *accō varuga* refers to *prāpya nirdēśam*, viz. pointing to the activity which is to be carried out. Here, it is embracing nārāyaṇan. This holds good for those who are *naccuvār*, viz. those who are desirous of seeing him. The meaning conveyed here is that if the desire is there, he \[emperumān\] appears in front of the person. Through the verse *naccuvār munniṟkum*, emperumān’s *āśrita pāratantryam* is manifested, viz. his dependence on his followers. Through the verse *accō*, the deep affection which is the *svarūpam* (basic nature) of the *adikāri* (one who is qualified to attain emperumān) as well as the *sauśeelyam* (simplicity) of emperumān are indicated.

**accō …** – pāsurams said with the pathos of yaśōdāp pirātti, his mother, where she is desiring to affectionately embrace him, when he comes in the form of a child, in line with the characteristics of his incarnation \[as a human entity\] and calling out to him as “*accō accō*” and ”*varuga*”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti has spoken these words since emperumān is showing his activities in line with the species in which he has incarnated (here, it is kriṣṇa, as a human entity) and since she has a deep affection towards him, born out of the fact that he is her child. periyāḻvār, considers this \[her singing these pāsurams\] as his fortune. Just like her, āḻvār is also stretching his hands to embrace emperumān \[kriṣṇa\] as he comes running towards him. The term *accō* is the *rūdyartam* (meaning known to all) of embracing emperumān through his divine shoulders and expansive chest.

**maccaṇi …** – these pāsurams mercifully composed by periyāḻvār, who is the most eminent among brāhmaṇas and who is the controller of śrī villibuttūr which has mansions built with several storeys.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just like periya tirumoḻi 8-2-2 “*neeṇilā muṟṟam*” (the expansive courtyard in tirukkaṇṇapuram), this term *maccaṇi* refers to the mansions of śrī villibuttūr. This will also refer to the mansion \[temple\] where *vataperum kōyil udaiyān* is residing. Through these terms, the eminence of emperumān and the boundary of the followers of emperumān are indicated \[emperumān’s temple in śrī villibuttūr shows his eminence and the mansions of the śrī vaiṣṇavas there (*maccaṇi*) show that they are superior to all\]. The term *puduvai* has the same meaning as the verse “*nātkamaḻ pūmboḻil villibuttūr*” as in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1-6-11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/09/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-1-6-11/). Thus, the verse “*puduvaik kōn battan*” refers to āḻvār being the controller of śrī villibuttūr, with is mansions, kōyil and nācciyār tirumāḷigai. The term *battan* refers to āḻvār being a *satyavādi*, one who always speaks only truth. Those who recite these pāsurams, taking refuge under āḻvār’s affection, even if they do not have his pathos and his connection with emperumān, without looking at anything else \[focussing only on his words\] …

**niccalum pāduvār** – those who recite these, with affection, and with the intention of enjoying these, will get to rule over parama padam, which is called as *parama ākāśam*, viz. they will be the controller of all the enjoyments there.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 10-9-10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/03/thiruvaimozhi-10-9-10-vidhi-vagai/) “*ānmingaḷ vānagam*” (rule over śrī vaikuṇṭam), such people will rule over parama padam forever. Even though āḻvār has called his verses as *āycci uraittana* (spoken by yaśōdāp pirātti), those who are desirous of ruling over *tripād vibhūti* \[nitya vibhūti or śrī vaikuṇṭam, which is three times as big as leelā vibhūti\] will not recite anything other than that which has been mercifully composed by periyāḻvār.

We shall next consider the pravēśam of the ninth tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 1.9.1. Vattu naduve

*vattu naduvē vaḷarginṟa māṇikkamottu nunaiyin muḷaikkinṟa muttē pōlcottuccottu ennat tuḷikkat tuḷikka enkuttan vandu ennaip puṟam pulguvān gōvindan ennaip puṟam pulguvān*

**Пословный перевод:**

vattu naduvē – between the two round objects which are like bluish gemstone; vaḷarginṟa – having grown; māṇikkam – made of carbuncle; mottu – bud’s; nunailyil – at the tip; muḷaikkinṟa – sprouting; muttu pōl – like pearls; cottuccottu enna – making a sound “cottu cottu” \[dripping noise\]; tuḷikkat tuḷikka – as they keep dripping for a long time \[drops of liquid coming out of the divine form\]; en – one, who is obedient to me; kuttan – one, who is my child; vandu – coming on his own; ennai – me; puṟam pulguvān – let him embrace my back \[or, stood embracing my back\]; gōvindan – one, who incarnated to graze cows, will embrace my back

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa’s private part is like a bud made of carbuncle, growing between two round objects made of bluish gemstones. With water sprouting at the tip of the limb and dripping continuously, making a noise “cottu cottu”, my little child will come on his own and embrace me on my back. One, who incarnated to tend to cows, will embrace my back.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār wants kriṣṇa to come with water dripping and embrace his back.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vattu …** – like pearls which appear at the tip of a bud made of bluish gemstone, which has formed between two round objects made of bluish gemstone. Mentioning it as bluish gemstone is with reference to both the colour and the object.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the pearl drops are most eminent and are invaluable. He says that kriṣṇa is wearing a golden cord around his waist, on which carbuncle pendants are hanging. Reflection from the carbuncle pendants is making the drop of water also to shine like carbuncle gem. Just as it has been said in [tiruvāimoḻi 8-9-1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/05/thiruvaimozhi-8-9-1-karu-manikka-malai/) “*karumāṇikka malai mēl maṇittadam tāmaraik kādugaḷ pōl*” (just like a forest of beautiful, large lotus flowers on top of a dark carbuncle mountain), since the form of emperumān in kutta nāttut tiruppuliyūr \[a divine abode in present day kēraḷam\] has been mentioned as being similar to dark carbuncle, there is no shortcoming in mentioning the limb here as being like a bluish carbuncle stone.

**cottu …** – water drops, which come out of the inner parts of the divine form, gather at the tip of the hidden limb and keep dripping. *cottu cottu* – mere sound made; does not have any specific meaning

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here – in the court of a king, when this pāsuram was being discussed, the king was very happy, saying “How well has the activity of a child been described here”. A person, ignorant of āḻvār’s pāsurams, said “Is this word about a child worth celebrating?” Hearing this, the main person who was responding about these, asked him “Have you heard that this āḻvār has also composed a pāsuram ‘*adir mugam udaiya valam puri kumiḻtti*’?” \[reference here is to periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4-7-3\] (keeping the resounding śrī pāncajanyam, the divine conch, on his divine lips and blowing it). The king was pleased with the response and said encouragingly “That is the way to respond”.

**en kuttan …** – One, who is simple, will embrace my back. *puṟam* – back of the body; p*ulgudal* – to embrace. The desire is that he should embrace. Alternatively, the term *pulguvān* would refer to a person who is embracing. In this case, instead of a desire from this side (yaśōdāp pirātti or periyāḻvār), kriṣṇa would embrace on his own. This meaning would syncronise with the term “*āḻip pirān puṟam pulgiya*” which is seen in the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: *en kuttan* – my son. *ennaip puṟam pulguvān* – this indicates āḻvār’s prayer to kriṣṇa to embrace his back. This also refers to kriṣṇa embracing his back. Just as kriṣṇa had embraced āḻvār’s chest \[in the previous decad\], only if he embraces āḻvār’s back too, would he be able to carry out mangaḷāśāsanam with this body. If this does not take place, he too would say, just like nammāḻvār had said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4-8-9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/04/thiruvaimozhi-4-8-9-megalaiyal-kuraivilla/) “*udambināl kuṟaivilamē*” (we do not desire this body which has not been desired by emperumān). *gōvindan* – one who is simple.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.9.2. Kinkini katti

*kiṇkiṇi kattik kiṟi kattik kaiyinilkangaṇam ittuk kaḻuttil todar kattitan gaṇattālē sadirā nadandu vanduen kaṇṇan ennaip puṟam pulguvān empirān ennaip puṟam pulguvān*

**Пословный перевод:**

kiṇkiṇi – anklet \[chain\]; katti – donning it on the divine waist; kiṟi – small chain made of coral; katti – wearing it on the forearm; kaiyinil – on the shoulder; kangaṇam – divine shoulder ring; ittu – adorning it; kaḻuttil – on the divine neck; todar – necklace; katti – donning it; than gaṇanttālē – with those divine ornaments; sadirā – beautifully; nadandu vandu – coming towards me, walking; en – my; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa will embrace my back; empirān – one, who is my svāmy \[lord\], will embrace my back

**Перевод:**

**Wearing the chain on the divine waist, the small coral chain on the forearm, the divine shoulder ring on the divine shoulder, necklace on the divine neck, my kriṣṇa, with all those divine ornaments, will come walking towards me and embrace my back. He, who is my svāmy, will embrace my back.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār says that kriṣṇa should come will all the ornaments and embrace him.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kiṇkiṇi …** – donning the chain in the divine waist and the small chain made of coral, on the forearm. *kiṟi* – small coral chain.

**kangaṇam …** – wearing shoulder rings on the divine shoulders and necklace on the divine neck.

**than gaṇattālē** – with the entire set of divine ornaments. Since the context here is the divine ornaments, it implies that he was also wearing ornaments which were not appropriate. The entire mass of ornaments is referred to under the term *gaṇam* – set. Alternatively, it could be referring to kriṣṇa, showering his mercy through his divine eyes. The term *attu* \[in *gaṇattālē*\] is a filler, without a specific meaning.

**sadirā nadandu vandu** – walking, without my knowing about it. Alternatively, walking beautifully.

**en kaṇṇan** – one, who is easily approachable for me, will embrace my back.

**empirān** – one, who is my lord, will embrace my back.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.
