## 1.9.3. Kattak kadittu

*kattak kadittuk kidanda perum selvamottup porundikkoṇḍu uṇṇādu maṇṇāḷvānkottut talaivan kudi kedat tōnṟiyaattan vandu ennaip puṟam pulguvān āyargaḷ ēṟu en puṟam pulguvān*

**Пословный перевод:**

kattak kadittu kidanta – due to abundant ego and possessiveness; perum selvam – huge wealth; ottu – agreeing with pāṇḍavas; porundik koṇḍu – accepting with his heart; uṇṇādu – without living; maṇ – throughout earth; āḷvān – one who thought of ruling by himself; kottu – for the gathering of brothers such as duśśāsana et al; talaivan – duryōdana, who is the first among them; kudi keda – such that his clan was totally obliterated; tōnṟiya – one, who was resplendent as the charioteer; attan – one, who is my svāmy, will come and embrace my back; āyargaḷ – for the clan of herd folk; ēṟu – one who is the leader, will embrace my back

**Перевод:**

**duryōdana, who is the first among the hundred brothers, thought that he alone should rule the entire earth, instead of sharing the abundantly available huge wealth with pāṇḍavas. My svāmy, who was resplendent as the charioteer, and who made sure that duryōdana was obliterated with his entire clan, will embrace my back. kriṣṇa, who is the leader of the herd folk, will come and embrace my back.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that āḻvār wants kriṣṇa to embrace his back, displaying his quality of being biased towards his followers.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**katta …** – fighting for the huge wealth, because of ego and possessive nature, saying that this is for me and this is for you. k*adippu* – having fat layers. Alternatively, just like saying “*takkattadittu*” and “*pakkapparuttu*” the verse “*kattakkadittu*” could be taken as a single word, referring to a huge opulence.

**ottu …** – unable to live together with the pāṇḍavas, who are close relatives, since their \[duryōdana and his brothers\] hearts were not accepting any agreement with the pāṇḍavas.

**maṇṇāḷvān** – expecting anxiously to rule over the entire world, himself \[duryōdana\]

**kottut talaivan …** – duryōdana, who is the first and who is the controller of the assembly of brothers starting with duśśāsana.

**kudi keda …** – to be annihilated with the entire clan

**tōnṟiya** – just as rāmānujar had said in the avatārikai \[introduction\] of śrī gītā bhāśyam “*pārtam ratim ātmānam ca sāratim sarva lōkam sākśikam cakāra*” (kriṣṇa made sure that the entire world saw that arjuna was the head of the chariot and that he was the commander of that chariot), he was the lord who shone as the charioteer for pārta \[arjuna\]. That lord will come and embrace my back.

**āyargaḷ …** – The one, who is the head of herd-folk, will embrace my back.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa had the pride of being the controller of the herd-folk by being under their control.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.9.4. Nandagam endiya

*nāndagam ēndiya nambi caraṇ enṟutāḻnda dananjeyarkāgit taraṇiyilvēndargaḷ utka visayan maṇit tiṇ tērūrndavan ennaip puṟam pulguvān umbar kōn ennaip puṟam puḷguvān*

**Пословный перевод:**

nāndagam – the divine sword known as nāndakam; ēndiya – holding in his divine hand; nambi – kaṇṇan, who is full of auspicious qualities; caraṇ enṟu – that you should be the protector; tāḻnda – one who surrendered; dananjayaṟku āgi – for arjuna; taraṇilyil – those who are on earth; vēndargaḷ – kings; utka – for their hearts to be distressed; visayan – arjuna’s; maṇi – stealing the hearts; tiṇ – firm; tēr – chariot; ūrndavan – one, who conducted it, will embrace my back; umbar kōn – one, who is the lord of celestial entities, will embrace my back

**Перевод:**

**arjuna surrendered to kriṣṇa, saying “Oh kaṇṇa, who is holding the divine sword in your divine hand! You should be my protector”. One who conducted the attractive, firm chariot for arjuna such that the hearts of the kings on earth became distressed, will embrace my back. One, who is the lord of celestial entities will embrace my back.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār wants kriṣṇa to come, manifesting his eminence.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**nāndagam …**– holding the short dagger, called as *nāndakam*, all the time, as if holding a flower in your divine hand, so that there is no delay when it comes to protecting the followers. You, who are complete with all the auspicious qualities for protecting your followers, should be my protector.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just like *sārngavil* (divine bow called as “*śārngavil*”), the dagger, called as *nāndakam* is a *tirukkuṟṟudaivāḷ*, a short dagger, a unique type of sword. *ēndiya* – one who holds it as if it were a flower; *nambi caraṇ* – being biased towards arjuna who took refuge under you saying “oh, one who has completeness of qualities such as valour etc! You should protect me”

**tāḻnda …**– as one who is biased towards arjuna, who took refuge under you

**daraṇi …** – all the kings who were on earth, were distressed seeing you being biased towards arjuna and conducting his chariot skilfully, wondering “Is there anything now by which we could survive?”

**visayan …** – one, who conducted the beautiful, firm chariot of arjuna, as his charioteer, will embrace my back.

**umbar kōn …** – celestial entities had desired that you should incarnate and reduce the excessive burden on earth; by annihilating the evil forces, you had become the controller of those celestial entities. Such an entity will embrace my back.

We shall next consider the 54<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.9.5. Venkalap pattiram

*veṇ kalap pattiram katti viḷaiyādikaṇ pala seyda karum taḻaik kāvin kīḻpaṇ pala pādip pallāṇḍu isaippap paṇḍumaṇ pala koṇḍān puṟam pulguvān vāmanan ennaip puṟam pulguvān*

**Пословный перевод:**

veṇ kalam – made of veṇ kalam \[bronze, an alloy of copper and tin\]; pattiram – leaf; katti – wearing it on the divine waist \[appropriate for the clan of herd-folk\]; viḷaiyādi – playing; pala kaṇ – many feathers of peacock; peyda – strung together; karu – being eminent; taḻai – as an umbrella; kāvin kīḻ – under the shade of a garden; pala paṇ pādi – singing many tunes; pallāṇḍu isaippa – (the favourable ones) to carry out mangaḷāśāsanam (praising emperumān); paṇḍu – during the time when he went with the form of a dwarf, to mahābali’s arena; maṇ pala – all the worlds such as earth etc; koṇḍān – one, who measured with his divine feet, will embrace me; vāmanan – who was a dwarf, before measuring, will embrace me

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa was wearing a cord on his divine waist, which had bronze leaf tied to it, typical of his clan of herd folk. Holding an eminent umbrella made with many feathers of peacocks strung together, like being under the shade in a garden, with followers singing in many tunes, carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam to him, kriṣṇa, who earlier went to the ritual arena of mahābali as a dwarf and measured all the worlds with his divine feet, will embrace my back. With the form of one before he measured the worlds, viz. vāmana, he will embrace me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār wants kriṣṇa to come with the disguise of vāmana.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**veṇkalam …** – tying a cord with bronze leaf strung in it, on his divine waist and playing.

**kaṇ pala …** – under the shade of a huge umbrella strung with peacock feathers, like a garden. *kaṇ* – peacock feathers. *peydal* – stringing. This speaks about stringing the peacock feathers together. k*arumai* – eminence.

**taḻai** – umbrella. Referring that to a garden is to manifest the coolness brought about by the peacock feathers. Alternatively, if the text had been *kaṇ pala peydu* (instead of *kaṇ pala peyda*), the words should be rearranged as *karum taḻai – kaṇ pala peydu* – the meaning would be that many feathers were donned on the divine locks as a decorative feature. *karum taḻai* – bunch of peacock feathers. *kaṇ* – refers to the eye seen on the feather of a peacock. Donning peacock feathers on the locks is apt for his clan of being a covherd.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *karum taḻai* will also refer to the bunch of peacock feathers and to the eyes of his friendly \[women\] followers who would be looking at him constantly with their eyes. His divine form was such that even men would lose out their hearts and eyes to him, as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 3-29 ślōkam “p*umsām druśti citta apahāriṇim*” (śrī rāma would steal the hearts and vision of men)

**kāvin kīḻ** – decorating himself with peacock feathers like this and playing, in the shade of a garden.

**paṇ …** – just as it has been said in śrī viṣṇu darmam māngalyastavam “*sangais surāṇām*” (group of celestial entities) and in [tiruvāimoḻi 7-4-1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/thiruvaimozhi-7-4-1-azhi-ezha/) “*tisai vāḻi eḻa*” (people in every direction praising emperumān), all the favourable entities \[emperumān’s followers\] were singing in many tunes, carrying out *mangaḷāśāsanam* (praising emperumān and wishing him well).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that they were carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam to the divine feet which went up to measure the worlds, just as it has been said in [mudal tiruvandādi 1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-1/) “*sūttinēn solmālai*” (strung garlands of words for emperumān).

**paṇḍu …** – during that time when emperumān went to mahābali and received water on his hand \[as token of taking three steps of land with his divine feet\]. One, who measured all the worlds with his divine feet, will embrace my back.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that while emperumān went to mahābali in the form of a dwarf, he measured all the fourteen worlds.

**vāmanan …** – one who was in the form of vāmanan (dwarf) before he measured the worlds, will embrace my back.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that while the reference \[when measuring the worlds\] is to trivikrama, āḻvār’s divine heart is focussed on his form of vāmana only.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.9.6. Cattiram endi

*cattiram ēndit tani oru māṇiyāyuttaravēdiyil ninṟa oruvanaikattiriyar kāṇa kāṇi muṟṟum koṇḍapattirāgāran puram pulguvān pāraḷandān en puṟam pulguvān*

**Пословный перевод:**

cattiram – umbrella; ēndi – holding it; tani – without any support; oru – as unique; māṇi āy – as a bachelor (going to the vicinity of mahābali’s ritual arena); uttara vēdiyil – in the northern side where the sacred fire is lit; ninṟa – one, who stood; oruvanai – mahābali, who is without any match, among magnanimous people; kattirivar – kśatriyas (people in the class of warriors); kāṇa – to see; kāṇi muṟṟum – all the worlds such as earth etc-; koṇḍa – one who accepted, after receiving water \[symbolically\]; pattiram – auspicious; āgāran – \[tamiḻ version of samskruta word, ākāram\] one, who has form, will embrace my back; pār aḷandān – one, who measured this earth (which he sought as alms earlier), with his divine feet, will embrace me

**Перевод:**

**vāmana went, holding an umbrella, to the arena where the rituals were being held, without anyone to accompany him. mahābali, who has no match among those who are magnanimous, was standing near the sacred fire, on the northern side. One, who took the land from mahābali, with all the kings looking on, and has an auspicious form, will embrace my back. One, who measured the worlds, will embrace my back.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār, even as he was envisioning vāmanāvatāram \[emperumān’s incarnation as vāmana, the dwarf\], recalls trivikramāvatāram \[his incarnation as trivikrama\].*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**cattiram …** – being without any support, holding an umbrella along with wearing deer skin, sacred thread and girdle made of divine grass on the divine waist, going in the guise of a unique vāmana with humility and beautiful form, to the arena where the rituals were being conducted. With the kings of the world looking, vāmana took water, as a symbol of accepting three steps of land from mahābali. That vāmana, who has an auspicious form, will embrace my back. One, who measured all the worlds, will come and embrace my back.

**uttara vēdi …** – mahābali, who was without a match in his quality of magnanimity, was standing on the northern side of the arena where sacred fires were lit.

**kattiriyar …**– as the kings of the earth \[who had assembled at that place\] were looking on, vāmana claimed the worlds, which mahābali was thinking were his, by taking them as alms, after accepting water as a symbol of that.

**pattirākāran** – one, who has an auspicious form. This implies that he had a distinguished form. [tiruvāimoḻi 1-8-6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-8-6-kalanthu-ennavi/) says “*pulan koḷ māṇāy*” (one who had the form of a brahmacāri (bachelor) that was stealing our senses).

**pār aḷandān** – one, who had measured this earth which he had taken as alms, with his divine feet, will embrace my back.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that even as vāmana was taking water poured on to his hands by mahābali, āḻvār became happy since he knew what was running in emperumān’s divine mind and said that *pār aḷandān* (one who measured the worlds). That happiness in āḻvār’s mind was the watering required for vāmana to grow into the form of trivikrama. indra felt happy that he had got back his worlds. mahābali felt happy since he was able to give what vāmana wanted, retaining his quality of magnanimity.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.9.7. Potta uralai

*potta uralaik kaviḻttu adan mēl ēṟitittitta pālum tadāvinil veṇṇeyummettat tiruvayiṟu āra viḻungiyaattan vandu ennaip puṟam pulguvān āḻiyān ennaip puṟam pulguvān*

**Пословный перевод:**

potta uralai – with a mortar which had a hole at the base; kaviḻttu – inverting it (under the uṟi); adan mēl ēṟi – standing atop that mortar; tadāvinil – kept safely inside pots; tittitta – being sweet; pālum – concentrated milk; veṇṇeyum – and butter; tiru vayiṟu – divine stomach; metta Ara – to be completely filled up; viḻungiya – one who ate; attan – one, who is my svāmy, will embrace my back; āḻiyān – one, who is fully immersed in mischievous activities, will embrace my back

**Перевод:**

**Keeping a discarded mortar, which had a hole at the base, under the hooped network of ropes, kriṣṇa got on top of that mortar. He ate the sweet milk concentrate as well as butter such that his divine stomach was completely full. Such kaṇṇan, who is my lord, will come and embrace my back. One, who is immersed in mischievous activities, will embrace my back.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(īntriduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that tiruvāyppādi \[śrī gōkulam} was agitated that butter was getting stolen. When the herd-folk complained to yaśōdāp pirātti, she told them, without blaming the child, “Keep your respective material safely, in your houses, inside pots kept in an uṟi \[uṟi is a network of ropes, suspended from a hook in the ceiling\], out of his reach”. Guessing that he could steal the materials using a mortar, they hid the mortars too, safely. Looking everywhere for the mortar, a discarded mortar with a hole at the bottom, got caught in his fortunate vision. Such svāmy will come and embrace me, says āḻvār.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**potta …** – kriṣṇa entered houses with the intention of stealing materials such as milk, butter etc. People in those houses, thinking “Let us keep them safely, outside his reach”, kept them inside pots, in hooped network of ropes. Sighting a mortar, which had a hole at its base, which had been discarded by all since it was of no use, kriṣṇa rolled it under the *uṟi* upside down and got on top of that mortar. Thinking that people would come looking for it if he had taken a good mortar, he located the mortar with a hole.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *potta* would refer to a hole; it would also refer to one which is apt. That mortar would be apt for kriṣṇa. He says that the term mortar here refers to *prapannars* \[those who have surrendered to emperumān\]. Just as the mortar would be of use only to kriṣṇa and to no one else, *prapannars* would be *ananyārha śēśabhūtars* \[servitors only for emperumān and not for anyone else\]. For such people, who exist only for emperumān and do not having any desire for anything other than emperumān, the divine feet of emperumān will be attained. Just as his divine feet came on their own, on top of the mortar with the hole, for these *prapannars* too, emperumān’s divine feet will come on their own, without their expressing any desire for those divine feet. Even if they have other *abhimānam* (pride) \[for example, making someone to become emperumān’s follower through one’s effort and feeling proud about it\], but are without *svābhimānam* (pride in themselves, coming out of *ahankāram* (ego), *svātantryam* (depending on oneself and not on emperumān) and d*hēhātbimānam* (mistaking body for self)), they will be *bhōjñabhūtars* for emperumān (enjoyable entities).

**tittitta …** – Tasteful, sweet milk, which had been concentrated and kept inside pots, and butter, which too had been kept inside pots. The term *tadā* (pot) should be added to both the terms \[milk and butter\]. Since the term *viḻungiya* (swallowed) has been used \[and not *kuditta*, which would refer to the action of drinking\], the milk should be considered as concentrated milk and not normal, liquid milk.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *veṇṇey* refers to one who knows *śēśatvam* (being a servitor to emperumān) and is willing to attain mōkśam (śrī vaikuṇṭam); the term *tittitta pāl* refers to one who is without *svābhimānam* and other avenues of desire (desiring anything other than emperumān). Just as it has been said in [tiruviruttam 71](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/03/thiruviruththam-71/) “*nāḻ ivaḷō ennum*” (this girl is clever) and in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3-7-4 “*seyda sūḻcciyai yārkku uraikkēn*” (to whom would I tell the mischief carried out), this type of pride is acceptable to emperumān and he recognises such a person. This pride is a cause for his *angīkāram* (recognition). Those who desire to have darśan of emperumān in śrī vaikuṇṭam are more distinguished than all the others and are referred to as *veṇṇey*. Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 2-8-8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-8-8-kanbar-ar/) “*ellā ulagum ōr tuṟṟāṟṟā* ”(even if he consumes all the worlds, emperumān’s divine stomach will not get filled up), his stomach will get filled up and he will feel happy only if he sees such an entity \[as described here\]. In caturti \[the hidden fourth case *āya* which is present on the first syllable *a* of tirumantram\], though *śēśabhūtan* (being a servitor to emperumān) is evident, emperumān desires only *ananyārha śēśabhūtan* (one who is servitor only to emperumān and not to anyone else) which is present in the middle term *u* of *praṇavam* (first syllable of tirumantram). It is this person, who is referred to as *veṇṇey* here. prapannan should be like *acit* (one without any thinking power), like the mortar.

**metta …** – when he went to consume these, due to his overflowing desire to eat, he consumed them such that his divine stomach was completely filled up.

**attan** – one, who is my *svāmy* \[lord\]. It is a word mentioned out of happiness of the activity narrated above. He will come and embrace my back.

**āḻiyān** – one, who is fully immersed in mischievous activities. This would also refer to one who has the divine disc in his divine hand. The meaning implied here is that one, who is holding the divine disc in his divine hands, is the one who engaged with such a lowly act of stealing. He will embrace my back.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.9.8. Muttavai kana

*mūttavai kāṇa mudu maṇal kunṟu ēṟikūttu uvandu ādik kuḻalāl isai pādivāytta maṟaiyōr vaṇanga imaiyavarētta vandu ennaip puṟam pulguvān empirān ennaip puṟam pulguvān*

**Пословный перевод:**

mūttu avai – assembly of aging herd-folk; kāṇa – to see; mudu – tall; maṇal kunṟu ēṟi – getting on top of a sand hill; kuḻalāl – with the bamboo flute; isai pādi – playing tunes; uvandu – displaying his happiness; kūttu ādi – dancing; vāytta – those who took refuge under his divine feet; maṟaiyōr – sages who follow vēdams \[sacred texts\]; vaṇanga – such that they bow down to him; imaiyavar – celestial entities; ētta – to praise; vandu – with the freshness of this dancing, he will come and embrace my back; empirān – one, who is my svāmy \[lord\], will embrace my back

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa got on top of a tall sand dune such that old people among the herd-folks could see him. With the flute, which he had, he played nice tunes and exhibiting his happiness, he danced too. That kriṣṇa, vorśipped by sages who follow vēdas and praised by celestial entities, will come and embrace my back. One, who is my lord, will embrace me**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**mūttavai kāṇa** – matured herd-folks, matured due to their 1) age, 2) knowledge appropriate for their clan and 3) qualities, to see the essence of his activities. Alternatively, the term *mūttu* (old age) with the last syllable having got reduced, and the term *avai*, meaning assembly, would refer to the assembly of old people among the herd-folks.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the old people among the herd-folks came and sat, to hear the flute recital of kriṣṇa, and locked up their girls in cellars such that they could not see this. The term *avai* refers to pointing out to these old people with distaste since they did not allow the girls too to come and engage with this activity. Alternatively, *avai* would also refer to an assembly; here, it would refer to the assembly of old people.

**mudu maṇal …** – getting on top of a tall sand hill, such that everyone could see him. Here, the term *mudu* refers to a raised place.

**kūttu …** – he danced in such a way that girls, who are inside cellars, would come out of their cellars and see him dance. Manifesting that happiness, he danced.

**kuḻalāl isai pādi** – playing tunes through the flute kept on his divine mouth. The old people would only hear the tune that he was playing. However, through those tunes, he was calling out to the girls who he desired to see and kept back the girls, who he did not wish to see, in their respective cellar. Only the girls who move with him would understand the distinctions in the tunes which he was playing. The verse should be rearranged as “*kuḻalāl isai pādi kūttu uvandu ādi*”. Through the songs which he was playing on the flute, he would call out to those who he desired to see, and feeling happy “We are fortunate to have seen them” he would dance. Since the type of dance has not been specified as dancing with false legs, dancing with pots etc, we should consider this as one of those dances.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the aged herd-folks would only know the music played out by kriṣṇa on his flute. It is only the youngsters (girls in their cellars) who would understand the call of kriṣṇa as he played out various tunes. They would know the regret that he was expressing through his music, for the delay in calling out to them; they would think of his soft feet and how those divine feet would be placed on their heads.

**vāytta …** – desiring to see his distinguished activities, eminent sages who follow him, would lose out to this activity and worship him. Celestial entities, engaging with his activities, would praise him. Alternatively, *vāytta* would transform as *vāynda*, and *maṟaiyōr* would refer to girls who are hiding in their cellars and who came out because of the tunes which he played on his flute. These girls would think of the softness of his divine feet and would worship him since he was dancing for their happiness. The old herd-folks, mentioned earlier, out of amazement, would praise him.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the girls, who are mangaḷāśāsanaparars, would know the softness of his divine feet and would praise him, saying “May you live long! May you live long!” Since the young girls have been kept hidden in the cellars \[in tamiḻ, *maṟaidal* refers to hiding\], they could be termed as *maṟaiyōr* \[those who have been hiding\]. The old herd-folks, engaging with kriṣṇa’s singing and dancing, would forget to bat their eyelids and praise him. Alternatively, this term \[*maṟaiyōr*\] would refer to celestial entities, who wish to see the divine activities of kriṣṇa in his incarnation and come down to tiruvāyppādi, hide their forms and see his activities of singing and dancing. *mūttavai* refers to nityasūris and muktātmās in śrī vaikuṇṭam, who have matured knowledge; *mudu maṇal* refers to those who control their senses such that they do not flow into worldly pleasures and stand atop those senses, exhibiting their control over their senses. *kuḻalāl isai pādi* refers to *ācārya vacana pāratantryam* – listening to the words of ācāryan and being a servitor to him. *imaiyavar ētta* refers to those who, forgetting even to bat their eyelids, engage deeply with the auspicious qualities of emperumān and look at the divine form of emperumān in divyadēsams as their nurturing entity.

**vandu …** – he will come with the freshness of his dance and embrace my back.

**empirān** – one, who is a great benefactor for us, would embrace my back.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 1.9.9. Karpagak kavu

*kaṟpagak kāvu karudiya kādalikkkuippoḻudu īvan enṟu indiran kāvinilniṟpana seydu nilāttigaḻ muṟṟattuḷuyttavan ennaip puṟam pulguvān umbar kōn ennaip puṟam pulguvān*

**Пословный перевод:**

indiran – dēvendran’s; kāvinil – being in his garden; kaṟpagak kāvu – kaṟpaga tree (wish-fulfilling tree); karudiya – one who desired (that it should be planted in the backyard of her house); kādalikku – satyabhāmā, who is dear to kriṣṇa; ippoḻudu – immediately; Ivan enṟu – I will bring it, saying so; nilāt tigaḻ – radiant due to moonlight; muṟṟattuḷ – in her backyard; niṟpana seydu – planting (by uprooting the tree from heaven); uyttavan – one, who nurtured that kaṟapaga tree, will embrace my back; umbar – for nityasūris \[permanent dwellers of śrī vaikuṇṭam)kōn – one, who is the lord, will embrace my back

**Перевод:**

**kaṟpaga tree is a wish-fulfilling tree, growing only in celestial region. satyabhāmā, kriṣṇa’s dear consort, desired that the tree should be planted in the backyard of her house \[in dvārakā\]. kriṣṇa assured her that he will immediately give that to her. The one, who planted that tree in her backyard, which is shining with moonlight, and nurtured it, will embrace my back. The one, who is the lord of nityasūris, will embrace my back.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kaṟpagam …** – satyabhāmā, kriṣṇan’s consort, desired to have the kaṟpaga tree (wish-fulfilling tree which grows only in celestial region) planted in her backyard, in dvārakā. indran’s consort, śaśi, insulted her saying that these trees grow only in celestial region and not on earth. kriṣṇa, instead of telling her “I will bring this tomorrow” or “We will see this later”, told her that he would plant it immediately in dvārakā and uprooted the tree. indran, who was affectionate towards kriṣṇa until then, was upset that a blade of grass had been uprooted from his backyard and went after kriṣṇa with his vajrāyudam \[a weapon\] to get back the tree. After being subdued by kriṣṇa, he realised his mistake and praised him. kriṣṇa told him, as his pledge, “Let this remain in dvārakā for some time and then, come back here”. Just as it has been mentioned in periya tirumoḻi 6-8-7 “*vaṇṭhuvarai nattavan*” (one who planted in the fertile dvārakā), he planted the tree in the backyard of satyabhāmā’s house in dvārakā, which was radiant with moonlight. Since the pāsuram says *uyttavan* \[one who nurtured\], it is evident that the tree, after being transplanted in dvārakā, was growing abundantly, with tender leaves, flowers and branches.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that karpaga tree will grow only in celestial regions and nowhere else. “*nīyatām pārijātōyam kriṣṇa dvāravatīm purīm* I *martya lōkē tvayā muktē nāyam samstāsatē bhuvi* ll (Let this kaṟpaga tree come with you to dvārakāpuri. Àfter being liberated by you from *manuśyalōkam* (earth), let it return to celestial region as it will not be able to grow on earth). Knowing that if he had told her “I will do it tomorrow” she would feel hurt and he could not postpone it to a later time due to his affection for her, he decided to fulfil her desire immediately. indra was feeling proud that this tree would be nurtured only in their lands, for their women and that they would protect the tree.  Feeling angry that kriṣṇa had uprooted the tree to take it with him to dvārakā, indra took his vajrāyudam and followed kriṣṇa to fight with him. Since he failed in his activity, he bowed down to kriṣṇa and prayed to him saying that the tree could be in dvārakā till kriṣṇa desires and then it could come back to the celestial region.

**ennai** – one, who is a servitor to his consort, will come and embrace my back.

**umbarkōn …** – losing out to kriṣṇa’s quality of carrying out a task for his dear consort, nityasūris gave in writing that they have lost out to his nature of fulfilling her desire. One, who is the controller of nityasūris, will embrace my back.

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi as well as this centum.

## 1.9.10. Aycci anru

*āycci anṟu āḻip pirān puṟam pulgiyavēyttadam tōḷi sol vittu cittan magiḻnduītta tamiḻ ivai īraindum vallavarvāytta nan makkaḷaip peṟṟu magiḻvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vēy – like bamboo; tada – being well-rounded; tōḷi – having shoulders; āycci – (mother) yaśōdāp pirātti; anṟu – during that time; āḻi – having the divine disc in his divine hand; pirān – kaṇṇapirān (kriṣṇa); puṟam pulgiya – manner of embracing the back; sol – words; vittu cittan – periyāḻvār; magiḻndu – with happiness; ītta – mercifully composed; tamiḻ – drāvida (language of tamiḻ); ivai iraṇḍu aindum – these ten pāsurams; vallavar – those who are capable of reciting; vāytta – apt to sing pallāṇḍu to emperumān; nal makkaḷai – distinguished disciples, children; peṟṟu – getting; magiḻvar – they will be happy

**Перевод:**

**yaśōdāp pirātti, kriṣṇa’s mother, who has bamboo-like, well-rounded shoulders, at that time, spoke words about kaṇṇapirān, who has the divine disc in his divine hands, regarding his embracing her back. periyāḻvār mercifully composed those words in drāvida language, with happiness. Those who are capable of reciting these ten pāsurams, will get distinguished disciples and children, who are apt to carry out mangaḷāśāsanam to emperumān and will be happy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In this last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi, āḻvār mentions the benefit to those who recite these pāsurams and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**āycci …**– *vēyttadam tōḷi āycci* – yaśōdāp pirātti has broad shoulders which are like bamboo, with freshness, well-rounded, long features.

**anṟu** – sarvēśvaran (emperumān, the lord of all), who has the divine disc in his divine hands, had incarnated as kriṣṇa. In order to follow the age-related activities of his incarnation, he, as a child, indulged in the activity of embracing yaśōdāp pirātti’s back. The words through which she described this activity…

**vittu cittan …** – periyāḻvār became happy, enjoying as if he were enjoying during yaśōdāp pirātti’s time. Those who are capable of reciting these ten pāsurams, which periyāḻvār had mercifully composed in drāvida language to make these known to all, such that everyone could recite them, with his pathos …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that periyāḻvār received emperumān’s divine glance and became happy. The term *viṣṇu cittan* is in line with his pāsuram 5-2-10 “*aravattu amaḷiyinōdum*” (emperumān, who was reclining on top of ādiśēśan in tiruppāṟkadal, the milky ocean, entered the divine mind of periyāḻvār, along with śrī mahālakśmi).

**vāytta …** – will get distinguished disciples or children, who are apt to carry out mangaḷāśāsanam (praising emperumān and wishing him well), and will be as a result of that.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *vāytta makkaḷ* refers to children and *nanmakkaḷ* refers to disciples. Just as disciples have a right over carrying out exclusive servitude to their ācāryans (teachers) as brought out by the term *āya* which is the hidden fourth case over the first syllable *a* in tirumantram, both children and disciples have a right over being protected by ācāryan, as brought out by the first syllable *a* in tirumantram (the term *āya* is referred to as *pratyayam* by our preceptors and the syllable *a* is referred to as *prakruti*). While the saying “*putrān santyajya*” (denouncing children) would appear to run contrary to this explanation, it should be recalled that there, the relationship between a father and son happens due to *kāraṇa kārya bhāvam* (cause and effect condition, viz. due to a *karma* \[past deed\], the child is born as a person’s son\]) whereas here, it is not due to that. Hence, there is no discordance between the quoted ślōkam and the benefit mentioned in the pāsuram. That emperumān is the protector and we are all the protected will be well understood only when the meaning of the hidden fourth case (*āya*) is clear, viz. that we exist only for carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam to emperumān and that he is the protector.

We shall next consider the pravēśam of the first tirumoḻi of second centum

## 2.1.1. Meccudu sangam

*meccūdu sangam idattān nalvēyūdipoyccūdil tōṟṟa poṟai udai mannarkkāypattūr peṟādu anṟu bāradam kai seyduattūdan appūcci kāttuginṟān ammanē! appūcci kāttuginṟān*

**Пословный перевод:**

mecca – to celebrate; ūdu – blow; sangam – śrī pāncajanyam \[divine conch\]; idattān – having in the divine left hand; nal – having a sweet musical note to hear; vēy – flute made of bamboo which is played by kriṣṇa; poy – dishonest; sūdil – in gambling \[play of dice\]; tōṟṟa – having lost; poṟai udai – having the nature of patience; mannarkku āy – as a support for the pāṇḍavas; pattu Ur – even ten villages; peṟāda – not attained; anṟu – during that time; bāradam – in the mahābhāratam war; attūdan – that messenger \[kriṣṇa\]; appūcci kāttuginṟān – is showing appūcci; (showing appūcci – to frighten the children sitting on the opposite side, flipping the eyelids, to expose the inner, reddish, fleshy portion, covering the face with the hair and creating a scare etc); ammanē! – oh, my! (this is the word mentioned to express fear on seeing that appūcci). He is showing appūcci

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa has the divine śrī pāncajanyam on his divine left hand, which he blows, leading to celebration. He plays on the divine flute which gives out a sweet musical note, to hear. Such kriṣṇa supported the pāṇḍavas when they lost out in a dishonest game of dice, having only patience with them. He, who assisted them during the mahābhārata war when they could not get even ten villages for themselves, is showing appūcci. Oh, how frightening! He is showing appūcci.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**meccūdu sangam idattān** – he has the divine śrī pāncajanyam on his divine left hand such that everyone would celebrate, saying “He, who is dependent on his followers, is biased towards pāṇḍavas”. The word *mecca* \[to celebrate\] has got shortened as *meccu*. He blows the divine conch such that everyone celebrates. The sound of śrī pāncajanyam makes the unfavourable entities to feel defeated and the favourable ones to feel sustained, just as it has been mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5-21-29 “*yasya nādēna daityānām balahānirajāyata* l *dēvānām vavrutē tēja: prasādāścaiva yōginām* ll” (Through the sound of which pāncajanyam the monsters felt weakened, the celestial entities’ splendour got enhanced and the mercy on sages increased….).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that kriṣṇa’s divine left hand was the identity for śrī pāncajanyam and when he blew it, people on both sides (pāṇḍavas and duryōdana et al) knew that he is biased towards pāṇḍavas. He further says that apart from śrī pāncajanyam being the identity for his divine left hand, kriṣṇa also made it known that his divine left hand was the identity for śrī pāncajanyam, making it a distinct identity.

**nalvēyūdi** – this is the necessary identification for his incarnation \[as kriṣṇa\]. One who plays on the flute such that the favourable entities feel happy. What is beneficial for the flute? \[*nal* – beneficial\] Just as it has been mentioned in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3-6-5 “*nannarambudaiya tumburuvōdu nāradanum tandam vīṇai maṟandu*” (upon hearing the sweet notes from the flute, played by kriṣṇa) entities such as tumburu, nārada et al, who possess instruments which have eminent strings, forgot about their vīṇa (a stringed instrument)) and in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3-6-10 “*marangaḷ ninṟu madu tāraigaḷ pāyum*” (upon hearing the musical notes from kriṣṇa’s flute, streams of honey will flow out from trees), he would engage both the *cētana* (those with thinking power) and *acētana* entities (those which cannot think), without any distinction, to fully engage with his playing. In this incarnation, kriṣṇa was constantly in touch with both śrī pāncajanyam and the divine flute. During the time when he would go behind the cows for the purpose of grazing, just as it has been mentioned in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3-4-3 “*āniraiyinam meeḷak kuṟitta sangam*” (kriṣṇa would blow the śrī pāncajanyam in order to get the cattle to flock back to him) and in [tiruvāimoḻi 6-4-2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/01/thiruvaimozhi-6-4-2-keyath-thinguzhal/) “*kēyattīnguḻal ūdiṟṟum niraimēyttadum*”  (kriṣṇa played sweet songs with the flute to herd the cattle together), he was constantly using śrī pāncajanyam and the divine flute.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as *śikha*(tuft), *yajñōpavīdam* (sacred thread) and *sandyāvandanam* (paying obeisance to various celestial entities at three specified times in a day) are identities for a brāhmaṇa, flute and playing the flute are identities for the herd-clan people. More than kriṣṇa’s basic identities \[of having the divine weapons, of having śrī mahālakśmi on his divine chest, of having ādiśēśan as his mattress etc\], since the flute, as his distinct identity, was dominant, āḻvār terms it as *nalvēy* (beneficial flute)

**poyccūdil tōṟṟa** – losing their entire wealth after being defeated in the dishonest game of dice. There was no possibility \[for duryōdana et al\] to defeat \[the pāṇḍavas\] through honest means; hence they were defeated through dishonest means.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that while playing the game of dice was meant to be a flavour of one’s playing ability, since duryōdana et al used it as a pretext for carrying out evil intentions, āḻvār calls it as *poyccūdu* (dishonest game of dice).

**poṟai udai mannarkkāy** – for the kings \[the five pāṇḍavas\] who retained their quality of tolerance, without showing any anger, despite knowing that they were defeated through dishonest means. Though duryōdana et al seized all the wealth of the pāṇḍavas, they were unable to steal their quality of patience. Hence, the term *poṟaiyudai mannar* is being used to identify them.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that while duryōdana et al seized the wealth of pāṇḍavas, if pāṇḍavas had given them a part of their quality of patience too, duryōdana et al would not have accepted that, with their forms. When yudiśtira and his brothers left the court of dritarāśtra \[duryōdana’s father and pāṇḍavas’ paternal uncle\] after the game of dice was over, dritrāśtra, expecting that they would have left in anger, asked people nearby “When darmaputra \[yudiśtira\] and others left, did they leave in anger?” they responded saying “We saw only happiness on the faces of pāṇḍavas; there was no trace of anger” dritarāśtra lamented “The great sinner did not show any anger or did not cry, ensuring that not one of my hundred sons will survive in future; a great evil he is” since his inner eye too was blind, just as his external eyes. Even if duryōdana et al had returned the wealth of yudiśtira et al, which he had usurped through dishonest means, along with his share of the wealth, yudiśtira et al would not have accepted them. What is the reason for this? Is it that they did not want to live with duryōdana et al, sharing the total wealth? No, this is not the reason, as we could see from the narration about the way gandarvas \[a class of celestial entities\] insulted duryōdana et al, in the forest, when there was none to help duryōdana et al, and hearing their outcry, yudiśtira sent his younger brothers to help them. Thus, people will seek wealth; for yudiśtira et al, tolerance was their wealth and hence, they did not separate from it. For īśvaran (kriṣṇa, pāṇḍavas were the wealth and hence, he joined with them.

**mannarkkāy** – just as it has been mentioned in mahābhāratam āraṇya parvam ślōkam “*yasya mantrīca gōptāca suhruccaiva janārdana*:” (janārdana, who is the lord of the three worlds, is the minister, protector and friend of darmaputra), kriṣṇa was their support in all ways, being their *paratantran* (being dependent on them).

**pattūr …** – for the sake of pāṇḍavas, kriṣṇa went as their divine messenger and told duryōdana et al “Instead of displaying enmity, pāṇḍavas and you could pool in your respective wealth, apportion them appropriately and live together for a long time”. When they refused, he told them “Even if you wish to reduce their share, it is acceptable; I will make them to accept it”. When they did not agree to this too, he told them “Give each of them two villages, thus ten villages in all”. They said “We will not give them any of these; isn’t *vasundarā vīrabhōjñai*?” (earth belongs to the winner). Then kriṣṇa said “Let it be that way”; he made yudiśtira et al too, to engage in war, and helped the pāṇḍavas through conducting the chariot, counselling the pāṇḍavas in the formation of the army etc; he was the messenger who was biased towards his followers.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa was the messenger who was the charioteer for the pāṇḍavas during the war, conducting the chariot  and arranging the army formations; he was the messenger who could not get ten villages for the pāṇḍavas; while being neutral between the two sides as a messenger, he made it known to duryōdana et al that he was biased towards pāṇḍavas, who had taken refuge under him, by saying, as in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam “*mama prāṇāhi pāṇḍavā*:” (pāṇḍavas are my life).

**appūcci** – one that created fear among the children who were sitting opposite him. There is a narrative here about kriṣṇa displaying the symbols of his being the lord of all to frighten children who were considering him as “One among us”, looking at his simplicity. There was an *araiyar* \[*araiyar* is a title given to certain prople who are experts in singing nālāyira divya prabandam with musical tones and through fluid movements of their forms, enact the narration in the prabandam), by the name of *uynda piḷḷai* in śrīrangam, during the time of rāmānujar. One day, he was demonstrating the movements for this pāsuram, in the presence of rāmānujar and other preceptors. When it came to the term *attūdan* he pointed out to namperumāḷ, who was seated in that assembly. When it came to *appūcci*, he flipped his eyelids, and came around the dais. embār, rāmānujar’s younger brother as well as his successor to the head of śrīvaiṣṇava assembly in śrīrangam, who was seated much behind rāmānujar, indicated to the *araiyar* with his divine hands and divine shoulders joined together. *araiyar* understood the meaning conveyed by embār, and demonstrated the same during the second time when he showed the meaning for the terms. rāmānujar, wondering “What is the reason behind this?” understood the sequence, by turning back mercifully and said “śrī gōvindap perumāḷ! Were you present!” \[gōvinda perumāḷ was another name by which embār was known\]. The term *appūcci* refers to the two āḻvārs \[śrī sudarśana āḻvār, the divine disc, and śrī pāncajanyam āḻvār, the divine conch\]; *ammanē* is the world expressed with fear, upon seeing kriṣṇa with the divine āḻvārs on his divine hands.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa showed *appūcci*, manifesting his bias towards pāṇḍavas, who had taken refuge under him. He further says that āḻvār refers to the two āḻvārs \[divine disc and divine conch\] in his two divine hands as *appūcci*. If the identity for an entity \[kriṣṇa\] is simplicity \[since he went as a messenger to the court of dritarāśtra\], then eminence could be termed as *appūcci* \[here, the word eminence refers to divine disc and divine conch\]. This is unlike bhagavat gītā ślōkam 18-66 when kriṣṇa said “*mām vraja*” (take refuge under me\]. The reason for this is that there, he said this as a charioteer and his eminence was not seen. It is only when he said further in the same ślōkam that “I will liberate you from all your hurdles” that his eminence was clear. However, here, though he went in as a messenger, signifying his simplicity, for *appūcci* he manifested his eminent symbols of divine disc and divine conch, making it very clear that he is an eminent entity.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.1.2. Malaipurai tol

*malaipurai tōḷ mannavarum māradarum maṟṟumpalar kulaiya nūṟṟuvarum pattaḻiya pārttansilai vaḷaiyat tiṇ tēr mēl mun ninṟa sengaṇalaivalai vandu appūcci kāttuginṟān ammanē! appūcci kāttuginṟān*

**Пословный перевод:**

malai purai – firm, like a mountain; tōḷ – having shoulders; mannavarum – kings; mā radarum – mahā ratas (great warriors) such as bhīśma et al; maṟṟum palar – and other eminent and great warriors; kulaiya – to tremble; nūṟṟuvarum – the hundred people, including duryōdana; pattu aḻiya – to be destroyed like an uprooted tree; pārttan – arjuna, his; silai – bow, known as gāṇḍīvam; vaḷaiya – to be drawn; tiṇ tēr mēl – on top of his firm chariot; mun ninṟa – one who stood as the charioteer; sem kaṇ – one, who has reddish eyes; alai valai – kaṇṇan, who was praising arjuna’s victory, is showing appūcci; ammanē! – oh, my! He is showing appūcci

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa stood on the chariot of arjuna, as his charioteer. kriṣṇa made arjuna to draw his bow, gāṇḍīvam such that kings, who had shoulders like firm mountains, great warriors such as bhīśma et al as well as other eminent warriors trembled, the hundred brothers starting with duryōdana got destroyed like uprooted trees. That kriṣṇa, who has reddish eyes, is showing appūcci. Oh, how frightening! He is showing appūcci.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that the one, who did not say words based on the qualification of the listener, is showing appūcci.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**malai …**– kings, who had shoulders which were like mountains not movable by anyone. Through this, it is indicated that they were fearless, due to their immense strength.

**māradarum** – great warriors such as bhīśma, drōṇa et al. bhīśma, drōṇa, karṇa et al were such eminent warriors that they would not fear any enemy.

**maṟṟum palar** – since they could not be counted individually, āḻvār is clubbing them together, along with these eminent warriors. Since the kauravas army had eleven akśauhiṇī \[one akśauhiṇī comprises 21,870 elephants, 21870 chariots, 65610 horses and 1,09,350 foot soldiers\], there would have been countless eminent warriors. Hence, they could be combined together under this term.

**kulaiya** – they were trembling in fear, thinking “Is there any meaning to the words that we are alive?” upon hearing “kriṣṇa has got on to the chariot as charioteer”. While earlier they were identified as great warriors, eminent warriors et al, once they started trembling, it is implied that there is no distinguishing feature to any of them.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the reason for their trembling is the sound of the conch which kriṣṇa had blown at the start and the valorous ankles which he had worn on his divine feet.

**nūṟṟuvarum pattaḻiya** – earlier the term *mannavarum* was used, to denote kings. Since these hundred brothers have been separately mentioned now, it is clear that through the *gobaleevarda nyāyam* \[citing a separate entity within a major group; example, speaking about a bull after cattle had been mentioned; this would mean that the bull is different from the earlier mentioned cattle\], these hundred people are not part of the earlier mentioned kings. They had planned ruling over the entire country after defeating pāṇḍavas in the mahābhārata war. Now, they are getting destroyed. Just as it has been mentioned in [bhagavat gītā 11-33](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/11-33/) “*mayaivētē nihatā*: *pūrvamēva*” (they have been already killed by me), they had been killed like uprooted trees when kriṣṇa took a pledge to kill them.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that these hundred people \[duryōdana et al\] had already been included in the verse *palar kulaiya*. The reason for mentioning them separately is due to their excessive, fiery ego. These hundred people got destroyed just like huge trees, losing out their green nature, get burnt to dryness due to fire and fall down.

**pārttan silai vaḷaiya** – as the bow *gāṇḍīva*, in arjuna’s hand, was drawn. In other words, it was because of the strength of kriṣṇa’s support that arjuna became capable of waging the war, not considering the presence of great warriors such as bhīśma et al on the opposite side.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the effort which kriṣṇa had taken to fell the hundred kauravas was nothing compared the effort that he had to take to make arjuna to draw his bow again. arjuna had got onto the chariot with lot of efforts \[in the past\], being ready for the battle. However, he thought that protecting relatives, even if they are opponents, is proper and what had been ordained for him \[as a kśatriya, belonging to the clan of warriors, it was his duty to engage in a fight for a just cause\], as unjust, due to fear of friendliness, compassion, killing etc. He said, as in [bhagavat gītā 1-32](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/1-32/) “*kinnōrājyēna gōvinda kim bhōgair jīvitēnavā*” {Oh, one who tends to cows! What is the purpose of ruling a kingdom and of enjoying pleasures?\] She \[draupadi) had let loose her hair, taking a pledge \[that she will plait her hair only with the blood of duśśāsana\], with pride, based on the fruition of her surrendering to kriṣṇa. kriṣṇa thought “I have to bring in clarity to his mind, make him draw his bow and make her to plait her hair”.

**tiṇ tēr mēl mun ninṟa** – the chariot, because of its connection with kriṣṇa’s divine feet, did not burn down due to the impact of weapons such as *āgnēyāstram* (weapon of fire) shot at by great warriors such as bhīśma et al, and stood firm. Just as it has been mentioned in mahābhāratam drōṇa parvam 33-18 “*urasā dārayāmāsa pārtam sanjātya mādava*:” (mādava, the consort of śrī mahālakśmi, bore (the weapons) on his chest, shielding arjuna), when critical weapons, which could not have been taken by arjuna, came their way, kriṣṇa bore them all, on himself and stood at the front, as the charioteer.

**sengaṇ alaivalai** – due to the skilful way in which he conducted the chariot, kriṣṇa was able to defeat the opponents; he gave the credit for that victory to arjuna, showering his grace on him due to his motherly forbearance. He praised arjuna for the way in which arjuna was able to win the war \[though it was he who was the cause for that victory\]. Unlike the cāndōjña upaniśat ślōkam 3-14-2 “*avākyanādara*:” (one who does not speak and does not support), kriṣṇa, keeping that aside, kept talking in praise of arjuna, just as it has been mentioned in [nānmugan tiruvandādi 24](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-24/) “*pugaḻndāy sinap pōrc cuvēdananaic cēnāpadiyāy manappōr mudikkum vagai*” (in order to bring to an end the war that you \[reference is to kriṣṇa here\], as the commander, had planned in your divine mind, you had praised arjuna, who had his chariot drawn by white coloured horses). In other words, through the verse *pārttan silai vaḷaiyat tiṇ tēr mēl min ninṟa sengaṇ alaivalai*, the following is being pointed out to: arjuna with a confused mind, as mentioned in āḷavandār’s gītārta sangraham “*astānasnēha kāruṇya darmā adarma diya ākulam*” (arjuna had misplaced friendliness, mercy, just and unjust activities, due to confused intelligence), had told kriṣṇa, as mentioned in [bhagavat gītā 1-32](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/1-32/) “*na kānkśē vijayam kriṣṇa*” (Oh, kriṣṇa! I do not desire victory), rejecting victory and kingdom \[since his opponents were related to him\] and sat on the chariot, dropping his bow, as mentioned in [bhagavat gītā 1-47](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/1-47/) “*ratōpasta upāviśat… visrujya sacaram cāpam śōka samvigna mānasa*:” (with grieving mind, (arjuna) dropped his bow and arrows and sat on the chariot). Such arjuna, who did not wish to engage in war, finally said, as in [bhagavat gītā 18-73](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-73/) “*kariśyē vacanam tava*” (I shall do as per your words) with a clarity of mind which was brought about by kriṣṇa, who, starting with distinction between *prakruti* (primordial matter) and *ātmā* (soul), ending with the most esoteric meaning of *paramabhakti* (inability to survive if emperumān were not attained) and *prapatti* (surrendering to emperumān), instructed arjuna about various meanings, making him to take up the bow again. All these instructions are covered under the term *alaivalai*. This term refers to a person who speaks the words which come to his mind, not considering the deep meanings of the words spoken and the qualification of the person to whom they have been said. Since it aptly fits the situation here, kriṣṇa could be termed as *alaivalai*. The reason for his giving all these instructions was to make the lady who surrendered to him \[draupadi\] to plait her locks.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the reason for āḻvār to refer to kriṣṇa as *alaivalai* is: arjuna is unable to come out of the illusion that his *darmam* \[duty of engaging in war with opponents\] is *adarmam* \[unjust, since he had to kill his relatives\]. For him, engaging in battle has become *adarmam* \[unjust\]. kriṣṇa decided to make arjuna accept what he classified as *adarmam* by making him to qualify for carrying out *karma yōgam* \[path of carrying out deeds\]. Even then, arjuna was not willing to do his *karma yōgam*, which is engaging in battle. kriṣṇa then decided that there was no option other than telling arjuna the most esoteric concept \[act of surrendering\] and hence told him to give up all the *darmams* without any exception and surrender to him \[once he surrenders, he has to carry out what the entity to whom he has surrendered, tells him to do\]. It is due to all these conversations which kriṣṇa had with arjuna that āḻvār calls him as *alaivalai.* When arjuna refused to act on a particular feature \[engaging in battle\], did he accept that it is *darmam*? Yes, he did accept it. How did he accept it? He said that it is *darmam*; since it is part of his *karma yōgam*, he accepted that it is his *darmam*. However, since it has the fault that it is impossible for him to do it, and since he accepted that he is emperumān’s *paratantran* (being totally dependent on emperumān, implying that he cannot act on his own on anything\], he could not act in anything which is against his nature of *pāratantryam*. He was in grief, saying “I cannot carry out this; I do not see any other means too”. To overcome his grief, when kriṣṇa asked him to give up all his *darmams* and when it was beyond his power to do it, it was his *darmam*, due to his bewilderment. Did he become bewildered after seeing the fault of inability etc to carry out the *darmam*? He was bewildered that he had to engage in yuddam if he had to follow his *karma yōgam*. Since that was impossible for him to do, he was bewildered. He had set out to engage in battle at the beginning, since it was within his power and it was also ordained for him as per his *varṇa darmam* (as a kśatriya). At an earlier point of time, when the celestial entity *ūrvasi* expressed her desire to embrace him, he had refused. Thus, he had control over his senses and was carrying out his *karma yōgam* properly. He had also heard from kriṣṇa, as in [bhagavat gītā 3-35](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/3-35/) “*śrēyān svadarmō viguṇa*:” (It is the best to follow one’s *darmam*). He had to give up his *darmam* due to his bewilderment of harming his relatives in the war. He did not have any other means too such as residing in a *divyadēśam* (noble dwelling place of residence for emperumān), he had not recited the divine names of emperumān, he had not lit lamps or adorned emperumān with garland etc. When this is his case, how does the command of kriṣṇa “Let go of all *darmams*” apply to him \[since he doesn’t have any *darmam*\]? kriṣṇa became *alaivalai* in order to remove arjuna’s *alaivalaimai* \[he was constantly speaking about what to do since he was not keen on engaging in the battle). He revealed esoteric meanings for the sake of arjuna, who is not apt for it \[tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai refers to him as *erukkilai*, leaf of a wild plant which has no significant use\]. If he had revealed like this, how does it relate to her \[draupadi’s\] pledge \[of plaiting her hair only after the death of duśśāsana\]? If arjuna had done earlier what he ultimately said, the bow would have been drawn much earlier and she could have platted her hair. Even otherwise, if he had done that before he got bewildered, there would not have been a necessity to tell him, as in [bhagavat gītā 18.66](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66/) “*sarva darmān parityajya…*” (renounce all your *darmams*). Through all these, since her pledge had to be fulfilled, even though he said “*sarva darmān parityajya*” as a universal rule of sacred texts, just as it was a pretext for fulfilling her pledge, there was one feature in arjuna too for which it became a pretext. What is that feature? Just as it has been said in [bhagavat gītā 2-7](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-7/) “*kārpaṇya dōśōpahata svabhāvam*: …” (I am besieged with anxiety), “*darmasammūdacētā*:” (I am confused about my duty), not knowing what is *darmam* and what is *adarmam*, feeling repentant. He asked kriṣṇa to give him good counsel, treating him as his disciple, as one who is controlled by him and as one who has surrendered to him. When arjuna asked kriṣṇa to ascertain that which is proper for him and to tell him that, the pretext had been revealed. arjuna had given up his *darmam* of engaging in battle, which was doable for him, due to misplaced thought of compassion, friendliness etc. kriṣṇa had analysed arjuna’s heart in between, to ascertain if he really had misplaced sense of friendliness, compassion etc. This was the reason for instructing arjuna with the entire bhagavat gītā. While īśvaran \[kriṣṇa\] was not *alaivalai*, it was āḻvār’s considered opinion due to which he referred to him that way. What is his opinion? Just as he had said in tiruppaḷḷāṇḍu, he had invited those who were interested in wealth and in *kaivalyam* (ātmā enjoying itself, instead of being subservient to emperumān\] to carry out mangaḷāśāsanam in leelā vibhūti, and in nitya vibhūti, he had said that everyone will praise emperumān, by surrounding him and saying “*pallāṇḍu*” (may you live forever with all auspiciousness!). For such a person, the focus is only *mangaḷāśāsanam*. Anything else will appear as *alaivalai* only. His divine daughter, āṇḍāḷ, who had said in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 11-10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/10/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-11-10/) “*meymmaip peruvārttai vittucittar kēttiruppar*” (periyāḻvār would have listened to carama ślōkam of emperumān (sarvadarmān parityajya ….) and would have conducted himself accordingly) had said that periyāḻvār would have changed his stance if he had come to hear about the misciefs which kriṣṇa was indulging in, with her. sītāp pirātti too, in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 30-3 “*striyam puruśa vigraham*” (If my father, king janaka, had come to know that you \[śrī rāma\] are leaving me \[sītāp pirātti\] behind in ayōdyā, he would have thought that he had given his daughter in marriage to a person in the garb of a lady). She told śrī rāma “I couldn’t have heard it. That is my anxiety. If I stay back, hearing your words, that sin will not befall me. I know that you will not leave me and go. When such is the case, why do you wish to indulge in such long talk \[*alaivalaimai*\]?” In the same way, kuṟumbaṟutta nambi \[a potter in tiruvēngadam\] also asked the king toṇḍaimān whether “tiruvēngadam udaiyān \[divine name of emperumān in tiruvēngadam\] indulged in *alaivalaimai* and revealed the truth about me”. It was only after arjuna had heard words such as “*tyajya*”, “*vraja*”, “*mā śuca*:“ that arjuna said, as in [bhagavat gītā 18-73](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-73/) “*stitōsmi gatasandēha*: *kariśyē vacanam tava*” (I am now without any doubt; I will do as per your command) and drew his bow, and subsequently, the hundred persons were killed. arjuna had lost his firmness, had let go of his bow and arrows and was overtaken by grief. He sat on the chariot. However, even then, the chariot was firm only. This was made possible, since kriṣṇa was standing on the chariot, in the forefront. Just as it has been mentioned in mahābhāratam “*urasā pratijagrāha*” (he took the arrows shot by the opponents on his divine chest), while arjuna was on a higher level in the chariot, kriṣṇa sat at a lower level and took all the intimidating arrows on himself. That *alaivalai* is showing *appūci*. *sengaṇ* – kriṣṇa’s eyes became reddish, since he was constantly looking to see if arjuna would run away from the battlefield, after jumping off the chariot. His eyes were red since he was furious with the opponents. Also, the eyes were red, due to the natural quality of being *īśvaran* (one who is opulent and controls everything).

**vandu …** – the one, who has the qualities of destroying the enemies of his followers and who carries out the tasks of those who attained him, by standing at the forefront of the chariot as its charioteer, making the enemies to tremble, uprooting them, by making some to draw their bows etc is showing *appūcci*.

**ammanē!** – *ammanē* is the world expressed with fear, upon seeing kriṣṇa with the divine āḻvārs on his divine hands.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.1.3. Kayunir pukku

*kāyu nīr pukkuk kadambēṟik kāḷiyantīya paṇattil silambu ārkkap pāyndādivēyin kuḻal ūdi vittaganāy ninṟaāyan vandu appūcci kāttuginṟān ammanē! appūcci kāttuginṟān*

**Пословный перевод:**

kāyum – boiling due to the fire of kāḷiyan’s \[a snake’s\] poison; nīr – water in the river; pukku – entered; kadambu ēri – got atop a kadamba tree \[Indian oak\] nearby; kāḷiyan – the snake, kāḷiyan’s; tīya – cruel; paṇattil – on the hoods; silambu – anklets on the divine feet; ārkka – to make a resounding noise; pāyndu – jumped; ādi – indulged in dance; vēyin kuḻal – bamboo flute; ūdi – played; vittaganāy ninṟa – one who stood as an amazing entity; āyan – kaṇṇan, who was born in the clan of herd-folk, is showing appūcci; ammanē! – oh, my! He is showing appūcci

**Перевод:**

**kāḷiyan, a poisonous snake, had taken residence in a river. With the fire of his poison, he had made the water in the river to boil. kriṣṇa got atop a nearby Indian oak tree and jumped onto the cruel hoods of kāḷiyan and danced such that the ankles on his divine feet were making a resounding noise. That kriṣṇa, who was born in the clan of herdfolk, and an amazing person, is showing appūcci. Oh, my, he is showing appūcci.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the one, who is the reason for the sustenance of herd-folk, is showing appūcci.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kāyu nīr pukku** – kriṣṇa entered the river, not considering that it was boiling due to the effect of snake kāḷiyan’s poison, which was making nearby trees and hovering birds to fall down dead. Just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 4-10-3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/06/periya-thirumozhi-4-10-3/) “*kaduvidam udaiya kāḷiyan tadattaik kalakki*” (agitating the waters where kāḷiyan, with cruel poison, was resting), he agitated the water such that kāḷiyan came out in anger.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the river water was like nectar, earlier. It was after the entry of kāḷiyan, due to fear of garuda, that the water became poisonous like this.

**kadambēṟi** – a nearby oak tree had become withered due to the effect of that poison. With his glance, kriṣṇa made that tree to become verdant and got atop it.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the oak tree was earlier cool and verdant; however, due to the effect of kāḷiyan’s poison, it had withered. nanjīyar, one of our preceptors, asked his ācāryan \[preceptor\], parāśara bhattar, “If it had withered, how did it tolerate when kriṣṇa stepped on it?” bhattar responded, saying “Since the one who climbed on it had looked at it with his merciful glance, it got rid of the fault that it had to endure on account of the poison, and returned to its verdant state”. For one who converted a forest of thorny bushes into meadows for grazing cows, is this a hurdle?

Again, periyavāccān piḷḷai used to quote the following, having been mercifully said by his ācāryan, nampiḷḷai – “His divine feet gave life to the lifeless form of uttarā’s son \[abhimanyu’s son and arjuna’s grandson\]. With those divine feet, if he were to climb a tree, vouldn’t a withered tree turn back to its previous verdant form?” Those divine feet had given life to a stone, converting it to a lady \[reference is to ahalyā, wife of sage gautama, who came out of her curse when śrī rāma’s divine feet stepped on her\]. For such feet, is this a wonder? It could be said that it was after looking at the way that kriṣṇa danced that the rules and regulations of bharata śāstra \[art of dancing\] were framed.

**kāḷiyan …** – the hoods of kāḷiyan had become cruel on account of the poison which they contained. kriṣṇa jumped onto those hoods \[from the oak tree\] and danced on them to such an extent that the hoods cracked, blood started coming out of mouth due to which he became wizened and he surrendered to kriṣṇa.

**vēy …** – people in tiruvāyppādi, on seeing and hearing about this, started running towards the river, many of them falling in fear on the wayside, due to their affection for kriṣṇa. kriṣṇa played on the flute in his divine hands, made these people to get up in comfort and live in joy. Due to this superhuman activity \[of dancing on the cruel hoods of snake kāḷiyan\], he stood as an amazing entity.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that it was after listening to his playing the flute that not only the herd-women and herd-men regained consciousness, even āḻvār regained his consciousness. Not only they, even those who were wondering “Who is he?” also came back to life. *vittaganāy ninṟa* – this refers to kriṣṇa being the cause for the clan of herd-folks. It refers to one, who had the skill to drive away kāḷiyan from the river such that cows, calves, herd-men, herd-women, without fear, could go and drink water from that river, whenever they wanted.

**āyan** – irrespective of whatever he does, he does not sway from his quality of being a herd-clan person. Such a person is showing *appūcci.*

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that despite carrying out all the activities, it is because he did not deviate from the appropriate qualities of the herd-clan that instead of calling him by his name \[kaṇṇan\], āḻvār is referring to the clan \[*āyan*\]. Alternatively, it could be considered as *vāyan*, the divine mouth which played on the flute.

**ammanē!** – *ammanē* is the world expressed with fear, upon seeing kriṣṇa with the divine āḻvārs on his divine hands.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan
