## 2.1.4. Iruttil pirandu

*iruttil piṟandu pōy ēḻai vallāyarmaruttait tavirppittu van kanjan māḷappuratti annāḷ engaḷ pūmbattuk koṇḍaarattan vandu appūcci kāttuginṟān ammanē! appūcci kāttuginṟān*

**Пословный перевод:**

iruttil – in pitch darkness; piṟandu – mercifully incarnated; pōy – (then) went to tiruvāyppādi \[śrī gōkulam\]; ēḻai – those, having deep affection towards him; val – having strength due to attaining kriṣṇa; āyar – herd-folk; maruttai – words of delusion; tavirppittu – avoiding those; van kanjan – hard-hearted kamsan; māḷa – to die; puratti – seizing him by his locks and turning him over; annāḷ – that day when the ladies had bath in the cold river yamunā; engaḷ – our; pū pattu – beautiful silk dresses; koṇḍa – one who scooped and went; arattan – mischievous person; appūcci kāttuginṟān – is showing appūcci; ammanē! – oh, my! He is showing appūcci

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa mercifully incarnated in utter darkness. In that darkness itself, he left for tiruvāyppādi. He made the herd-folk, who were affectionate towards him, and who were strong since they had taken refuge under him, to avoid speaking words in delusion. He had pulled kamsan by his locks and turned him over such that kamsan died. During that time, when we had gone to yamunā river to have bath in its cold eater, he had stolen our beautiful, silk dresses. Such a mischievous person is showing appūcci. Oh, my, he is showing appūcci.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that āḻvār is saying that the mischievous person is showing appūcci.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**iruttil piṟandu** – Just as it has been mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5-3-7 “*ardarātrē akhilādārē jāyamānē janārdanē*” (janārdana \[kriṣṇa\], who sustains everything, incarnated in the middle of night) kriṣṇa incarnated, without being seen by evil entities such as kamsan et al, in utter darkness, when even those nearby could not see him. kamsan, who was standing with drawn sword to harm him when he was born, vouldn’t have spared him if kriṣṇa had been seen. dēvakip pirātti too said “*jānātumāvatārantē kamsōyam ditijanmaja*:” (This kamsan, who was born in the clan of diti, as a monster, not knowing about your divine incarnation…).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa incarnated in utter darkness so that he would not be seen by kamsan who was standing with drawn sword, to kill him. Having incarnated in darkness, he could have taken his mother’s milk and slept. But, knowing the consequence if kamsan had come to know of his incarnation, he had to mercifully leave for tiruvāyppādi, not minding the forest and darkness enroute.

**pōy** – leaving for tiruvāyppādi, with dēvakip pirātti crying out, catching hold of vasudēvar’s and kriṣṇa’s feet, with the pangs of separation, in that pitch darkness, as mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 6-4-5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/01/thiruvaimozhi-6-4-5-vendith-thevar-irakka/) “*vīngiruḷvāy anṟannai pulambappōy*” (leaving for tiruvāyppādi, during that night of expanding darkness, when dēvakip pirātti was crying).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that he had to leave, as soon as he incarnated.

**ēḻai vallāyar maruttait tavirppittu** – herd-folk were deeply affectionate towards kriṣṇa. Just as it has been said in mahābhāratam drōṇa parvam 18-3-24 “*kriṣṇāśrayā*: *kriṣṇa balā*:” (they took refuge under kriṣṇa; they derived strength from kriṣṇa), whenever herd-men, who had attained kriṣṇa, said out of arrogance they had attained him, that they are capable of killing kamsan, kriṣṇa would tell them “Does this require you people? I will do that myself”; he would counsel them through his distinguished plans, to avoid any indiscrete action.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *vallāyar* \[strong herd-folk\] refers to their strength in ignorance \[sarcasm\]. While they look up to fresh water, through rains, and wooden utensils for keeping their food, they were talking among themselves, while playing with the sticks which they use for grazing cows “We are so many here; we have these sticks too in our hands. Why should we pay any tax to kamsan? Let us kill kamsan with these sticks in our hands”. Hearing this, kaṇṇan got up to tell them “Are all of you required for this task? Wouldn’t I myself pull him down and kill him?” Many herd-folk got up, once kriṣṇa said these words. kriṣṇa again told them “Do not speak like this again. Get rid of your delusion that you are capable of completing what you had told”. He told them further “Elder brother \[balarāman\] and I are enough for this task” and prepared to leave for śrī maturā. akrūrar came with a chariot saying “You should mercifully come”, speaking about their relationship. When kriṣṇa was ready to mercifully leave, the capable herd-folk, with total affection for him and all the herd-women, who were friendly with kriṣṇa, also came in a large assembly. They despised akrūrar saying that “*akrūra*: *krūra hrudaya*:” (akrūrar has a cruel heart \[*krūra* in samskrutam refers to cruelty\]. They blocked the chariot and told kriṣṇa and balarāma “If you go, all of us will kill ourselves”*.* kriṣṇa told them “This is not your mouth speaking these words. Is it possible for you to end your lives whenever you think of? Do not create any delusion in me by saying that you would all die”. With the help of *nambi mūtta pirān* (balarāma, his elder brother), kriṣṇa removed their delusion. Here, their friendliness is termed as *maruttu*. How did he prevent their delusion?

**van kanjan māḷap puratti** – instead of letting what he had said to disappear as a mere strategy, kriṣṇa implemented what he had said. He mercifully went to śrī maturā, when akrūra came, having been sent by kamsan to bring kriṣṇa there with the pretext of attending a bow festival. On the way, kamsan had arranged for killing kriṣṇa through his elephant, kuvalayāpeedam, and his chosen wrestlers. The hard-hearted kamsan had sat on a throne, at a high level, watching these, just as it has been mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5-20-26 “*tunga manjē vyavastita*:” (he was seated on a high-level throne). kriṣṇa destroyed the elephant and the wrestlers initially. Then, he jumped onto the high pedestal, just as it has been said in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5-20-84 “*kēśēśvā kruśya vigaḷat kirītam avaneetalē sa kamsam pātayāmāsa tasyōpari papādaca*” (with a loud cry, that kriṣṇa pulled the locks of kamsan such that kamsan fell on the ground with his crown and jumped on top of that kamsan), pulling kamsan by his locks, making his crown to fall down and jumped over him, as mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 3-10-3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2022/11/periya-thirumozhi-3-10-3/) “*kanjan kunji pidittu aditta*” (one who hit kamsan by pulling him by his locks).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that they \[kriṣṇa and balarāma\] said that they will return after seeing their maternal uncle, kamsan. The ladies felt sorrowful, saying “Is that \[your returning to tiruvāyppādi\] possible? If you see women in the city \[of śrī maturā\] will you return to us, who are lowly, rural people?” Hoping that kriṣṇa will take pity on them \[and decide against going to maturā\] they immersed themselves deeper and deeper into their delusion. In order not to get trapped in their delusion and to rid them of their delusion, he told them “Are we princes? Is it that we are going to establish a great relationship with them? Go, look after your chores”. It was saying this way that he entered maturā. Since they saw kamsan’s deceptions there, kriṣṇa destroyed those also. He then jumped on to the high pedestal, where kamsan was sitting, pulled him down such that his head fell on earth. Since that hard-hearted kamsan \[*vankanjan*, as seen in the pāsuram\] did not die, he pulled him again by his hair, and hit him hard such that kamsan’s life ebbed. What then is *pūmbattukkoṇḍu*?

**annāḷ …** – the mischievous person, who took away all our beautiful silk dresses on that day when we had gone to yamunā river for having a bath, early in the morning, in its chill water. *arattu* – mischief; it would also refer to strength. He is showing *appūcci*.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that it is only after the enemy was destroyed that āḻvār could enjoy kriṣṇa’s activity of stealing the herd-women’s clothes. Hence, āḻvār speaks about that activity, after kamsan had been done with. Since āḻvār has mercifully said “*engaḷ pūmbattukkoṇḍa arattan*”, periyāḻvār has joined the ranks of the herd-women and enjoys this activity. When balarāma is not around, since kriṣṇa gets caught in certain confusions, in order to ensure that there is no controversy here, āḻvār went to the banks of yamunā, when kriṣṇa had stolen the dresses of herd-girls; when the girls claimed “These are ours”, kriṣṇa said “No, they are not yours”. When they again said “These are ours”, āḻvār joined them, saying that they are ours \[“*engaḷ pūmbattu*”\]; he gave back their dresses, after getting them from kriṣṇa and put an end to the confusion. But, when āḻvār goes in their assembly, will they not object to his presence? Even if they accept balarāman, will they accept āḻvār? They will accept. When sage śri vēda vyāsa was coming their way, the girls jumped into the river; however, after he had passed them and his son, sage śrī sukhabrahma came that way, they came out of the water without any sense of shyness. That sage \[śrī sukhabrahma\] and āḻvār celebrate kriṣṇa’s activities. āḻvār’s immersion in kriṣṇa’s activities is not limited to sage śrī sukha brahmam’s. When describing dirt and mud on kriṣṇa’s divine form \[in pāsuram 1.9.1\], āḻvār had used certain terms such as water droplets dripping from his divine form. Not considering rules of hiding certain words, āḻvār had openly mentioned about secretions from kriṣṇa’s divine form \[This shows how deeply involved he is in kriṣṇa’s activities\]. Hence, the girls will accept him to mediate. Alternatively, āḻvār would have made himself as one among the herd-women and to ensure that kriṣṇa’s heart did not get hurt, engaging with his activity, would have said *engaḷ pūmbattu* (our dress), to make kriṣṇa happy. He too has all rights with kriṣṇa. Just as it has been mentioned in [mudal tiruvandādi 53](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/08/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-53/) “*senṟāl kudaiyām*” (ādiśēśan engages in all types of servitude with emperumān, being his umbrella when emperumān walks, etc), śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 12- “*yadā yadā hi kausalyā*” (just as kausalyā is daśarata’s friend, minister etc) and [stōtra ratnam 41](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/sthothra-rathnam-41/) “*dāsassakā*” (garudan is emperumān’s servitor, friend etc), when they had been servitors to emperumān in whichever state they were in, periyāḻvār too showed his affection towards kriṣṇa in various states. *arattu* – mischief; strength. Through the verse “*annāḷ avanai māḷap puratti, innāḷ engaḷ pūmbattuk koṇḍa arattan*” āḻvār treats their term “*engaḷ*” (our) as his own benefit and follows their pathos. His action is also similar to bhagavat gītā ślōkam “*sambhavāmi yugē yugē*” (I make myself incarnate in every epoch to establish *dharma* (righteousness)…). Just as emperumān incarnates in every epoch to establish righteousness etc, āḻvār incarnates in all those epochs to carry out mangaḷāśāsanam to emperumān. This is his *darmam*.

**ammānē** – Oh, my! He is showing *appūcci.*

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.1.5. Seppundu sadu

*sēppūṇḍa sādu sidaṟi tirudi neykkuāppūṇḍu nandan manaivi kadai tāmbālsōppūṇḍu tuḷḷit tudikkat tudikka anṟuāppūṇḍān appūcci kāttuginṟān ammanē! appūcci kāttuginṟān*

**Пословный перевод:**

sē pūṇḍa – drawn by bulls; sādu – wheel \[cart, permeated by śakatāsuran, a monster, sent by kamsan to kill kriṣṇa\]; sidaṟi – kicked; neykku – desiring ghee; tirudi – stole it; āppu uṇḍu – tied down by herd-women; nandan – nandagōpālar’s; manaivi – yaśōdfhāp pirātti, his consort; kadai tāmbāl – with the rope used for churning \[curd\]; tuḷḷi tudikka tudikka – jumping and trembling; sōppu uṇḍu – getting beaten; anṟu – at that time; āppu uṇḍān – one, who was tied down, is showing appūcci; ammanē! – oh, my! He is showing appūcci

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa kicked a wheel, part of a cart which was drawn by bulls, in which a monster had pervaded. He was desirous of ghee and stole it to consume. He was caught and got tied down by herd-women. Subsequently, he was beaten by yaśōdāp pirātti, consort of nandagōpar, even as he jumped and trembled. The one, who was tied down, is showing appūccī. Oh, my! He is showing appūcci.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the one, who was tied down by his mother, is showing appūcci.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**sēppūṇḍu …** – just as it has been mentioned in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3-1-2 “*van bārac cagadam*” (the wheel which was strong and heavy), it was a wheel \[part of the cart\], which was very heavy, drawn by bulls. The wheel was pervaded by śakatan, a monster, sent by kamsan to kill kriṣṇa. kriṣṇa was crying for milk, kicking his divine feet. The wheel, which came rolling towards him to harm him, got caught between kriṣṇa’s kicking feet. The kick, delivered by kriṣṇa, destroyed the wheel in such a way that it could not even be identified as a wheel.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti had nurtured kriṣṇa under the wheel, which couldn’t be moved even by strong bulls. It was such an auspicious time when the child \[kriṣṇa\] was born that anyone, who comes within his proximity, with the intention of harming him, gets destroyed.  Thus, since it was its time to go, the wheel too got disfigured completely into pieces. It is not only that it could not be moved easily, the huge wheel, tied to pole, broke into smithereens, when it got caught between the divine feet which kriṣṇa was kicking since there was a delay in feeding him when he was hungry.

**tirudi …** – desirous of consuming ghee, he went \[to others’ houses\] to steal it. He was caught by those who had the material \[ghee\], in the act of stealing.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that many people came and complained to yaśōdāp pirātti “Ghee is getting stolen in the village”. She told them “You are blaming this child without any reason. If you indeed find him stealing, as you say, bring him to me, tying the vessel from which he had stolen, to his neck”. With anger she told them “You people too have given birth to children, just like him and are nurturing them”. Hearing her words, they started spying on him, when he went out to steal and consume ghee. Since they are herd-women, without understanding the meaning of yaśōdāp pirātti’s words \[she was scoffing at them for complaining about such small things\], not considering that he is a prince \[as the son of vasudēvar\], they brought him to her, with the vessel, from which he had consumed ghee, tied to his neck, telling everyone “We have found out the thief who had stolen ghee”. They brought through the streets, where girls, who were charmed by kriṣṇa, were living. They considered that it was their fortune to have seen him walk through their houses.

**nandan manaivi …** – yaśōdāp pirātti had earlier told the herd-women “Do not blame my son for stealing. If he had stolen, tie him to the vessel from which he has stolen and bring him to me”.  Since they brought kriṣṇa with the vessel from which he had stolen and eaten ghee to yaśōdāp pirātti, she hit herself on the head and said “The way nandan’s consort has given birth to a child and nurtured him is indeed great” \[sarcasm\]. In their presence, manifesting her anger, she beat him with a rope used for churning curd, even as kriṣṇa was jumping and trembling due to her beating.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here – Once the herd-women brought kriṣṇa to yaśōdāp pirātti’s house, she took out a rope, used for churning curd, and in their presence said “What a great way that nandan’s wife \[referring to herself\] is bringing up this child”, angrily beating kriṣṇa, such that he was jumping and trembling. She tied him such that they could see, telling him “Until your father \[nandagōpar\] comes, stay like this, without quivering”.

**anṟu …** – apart from beating him, she tied him such that he couldn’t move anywhere. Such a person, who was tied down, is showing *appūcci*. The short syllable in words such as *sōppuṇḍu, āppuṇḍu* etc have got transformed to the long syllables *sōppūṇḍu, āppūṇḍu* etc.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the one, who was tied down like this, on that day, instead of remaining there, is showing *appūcci* here. *āppūṇ* – to be tied down.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.1.6. Seppila menmulai

*seppiḷa menmulait tēvaki nangaikkusoppadat tōnṟīt toṟūppādiyōm vaittatuppamum pālum tayirum viḻungiyaappan vandu appūcci kāttuginṟān ammanē! appūcci kāttuginṟān*

**Пословный перевод:**

seppu – having the appearance of copper; iḷa – youthful; mel – soft; mulai – having bosoms; dēvaki nangaikku – for dēvaki who is complete with ātma guṇas \[qualities of soul sucas being subservient to emperumān, being dependent on him etc\]; soppada – very well; tōnṟi – shining; toṟuppādiyōm – we, who are in tiruvāyppādi; vaitta – saved and kept; tuppamum – ghee; pālum – along with milk; tayirum – and curd too; viḻungiya – one who mercifully consumed; appan – kriṣṇa, who is our benefactor, is showing appūcci; ammanē! – Oh, my! He is showing appūcci

**Перевод:**

**dēvakip pirātti has her bosoms which are having the appearance of copper, and which are youthful and tender. Instead of taking milk from that dēvaki, who is complete with the ātma guṇas, kriṣṇa is consuming ghee, milk and curd, which we have saved and kept safely in tiruvāyppādi. Such kriṣṇa is showing appūcci. Oh, my! He is showing appūcci**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that one, who is the protector of all, is showing appūcci.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**seppu …**– dēvakip pirātti, who was complete with noble qualities, had her bosoms with the appearance of copper, being soft and tender. The purpose of describing now bosoms is – these are the bosoms which kriṣṇa should have suckled on; however, due to fear of kamsan, she had to allow him to go to another place.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the reason for describing her bosoms here is because they were the ones from which he had mercifully taken milk. The reason for using the metaphor *seppu* is because, with aged bosoms, the milk will not have strength and, sustenance for the infant will be an issue; hence, he calls them as youthful bosoms. When kriṣṇa holds on to the bosoms while taking in milk, since they would melt in his hands, āḻvār calls them as tender.

**nangai** – dēvakip pirātti had the qualities of knowing the events which would unfold, having the affection with which she could see the situation of her just-born son, letting others to enjoy and nurture themselves \[reference to people in tiruvāyppādi – śrī gōkulam\] etc.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here, for the term *dēvaki nangaikku* – even though she had missed out on suckling kriṣṇa, as mentioned in [perumāḷ tirumoḻi 7-7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/08/perumal-thirumozhi-7-7/) “*oḻugu pēreḻil*” (bosoms which have beauty, but from which you had not consumed milk), just as it has been said in [perumāḷ tirumoḻi 7-5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/08/perumal-thirumozhi-7-5/) “*ellām deyva nangai yasōdai peṟṟāḷē*” (yaśōdāp pirātti, the celestial mother, had the fortune of experiencing all the joys of nurturing you), since she considered the benefit which yaśōdāp pirātti had obtained by nurturing kriṣṇa as her own, āḻvār refers to dēvakip pirātti as *nangai* – one who is complete with all the auspicious qualities of soul. When kriṣṇa incarnated, he came with his four shoulders, along with the divine weapons, displaying his total supremacy. Looking at his divine form, dēvakip pirātti told him “Oh, my lord! We are residing under the shadow of kamsan’s turret. He is one, who would not tolerate even words such as sages, celestial entities etc. If he sees you like this, he will not leave you. After killing six and losing the seventh, he has been waiting, wondering ‘When will the eighth child arrive?’ Please hide this divine form; Take the form of a normal child, don’t stay anywhere around me and hide in some place, in some manner”. Since she prayed this way and hid his incarnation, āḻvār considers these as benefits for him, enjoins her with him as a mangaḷāśāsanaparars \[one wishing well for emperumān\] and refers to her as *nangai*, one who is complete in auspicious qualities of the soul.

**soppadat tōnṟi** – incarnating well. In other words, when she had carried out penance in order to give birth to the lord of all, just as it has been mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam5-3-10 “*jātōsi dēva dēvēśa śankhacakragadādara*” (being the controller of nityasūris, you incarnated with your divine weapons of conch, disc, mace etc) you incarnated with the symbols which explicitly mention that you are the lord of all. You had fulfilled dēvakip pirātti’s wish, as mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5-3-14 “*sapalam dēvi sanjātam jātōham yat tavōdarāt*” (Oh dēvaki! The reason for which I had incarnated through your stomach…). Instead of saying “being born” the reason for saying “incarnated” is to be in line with the śrī viṣṇu purāṇam ślōkam 5-3-2 “*dēvakī pūrvasandyāyām āvirbhūtam*” (rising from the eastern direction, which is dēvaki) \[just as sun rises from the eastern direction, emperumān rose from dēvaki’s stomach\], without the fault of having stayed inside a womb. This is also congruent with mahābhāratam sabhā parvam 62-35 “*naiśa garbhatva māpēdē nayōnyām avasatprabhu*:” (this kriṣṇa did not have the quality of staying in a womb; he did not stay in any other womb too).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: *soppada* – very well. Incarnating, without any shortcoming in his qualities of either eminence or simplicity. Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 3-5-5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-5-5-sadhu-sanaththai/) “*ādi am sōdi uruvai*” (incarnating here with the same effulgent, primordial form which he has in śrī vaikuṇṭam), he hid that divine form in order to fulfil the words of his mother \[dēvakip pirātti\].

**toṟuppādiyōm** – *toṟu* – cow; *toṟuvar* – herd-folk; *toṟuppādiyōm* – we, who reside in āyppādi.

**vaitta** – saved and kept

**tuppam …** – *tuppam* – ghee. One who consumed ghee, milk, curd etc. After mentioning the materials, since āḻvār had used the term *viḻungiya* (swallowed), the terms *tuppam* and *pāl* (milk) refer to ghee which had solidified and milk, which had been concentrated, respectively. Alternatively, the term *viḻungiya* could refer to consuming, based on the qualities of the materials consumed.

**appan** – one who is the benefactor. It refers to one who consumed all these materials and created a benefit for us \[that he had consumed them\].

**vandu appūcci kāttuginṟān** – such kriṣṇa coming and showing *appūcci.* Oh, my! He is showing *appūcci*.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.1.7. Tattuk kondal

*tattuk koṇḍāḷ kolō tanē peṟṟāḷ kolōcittam anaiyāḷ asōdai iḷam singamkottārk karum kuḻal gōpāla kōḷariattan vandu appūcci kāttuginṟān ammanē! appūcci kāttuginṟān*

**Пословный перевод:**

tattu – as adopted son; koṇḍāḷ kol O – did she nurture? (ōr); tanē – she herself (with her body going through pain); peṟṟāḷ kol O – did she give birth to?; cittam anaiyāḷ – one who acts as per his thoughts; asōdai – having been born from the stomach of yaśōdāp pirātti; iḷam singam – one who remained as the cub; kottu – with bunches of flowers; Ar – being filled; karu – being black; kuḻal – having plenty of locks; gōpālar – for the herd-folk; kōḷ – having strength; ari – one who is like a lion; attan – one who is the lord, is showing appūcci; ammanē! – oh, my! He is showing appūcci

**Перевод:**

**Did yaśōdāp pirātti adopt kriṣṇa as her son or did she give birth to him? He is the cub and yaśōdāp pirātti acts as per his thoughts. He is having bunches of flowers, which are completely filled on his dark locks. He is like a lion, having great strength, for the herd-folk. Such kriṣṇa is showing appūcci. Oh, my! He is showing appūcci.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that kriṣṇa is showing appūcci displaying the strength of his divine form of narasimha (lion head and human body)*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tattu …** – Did yaśōdāp pirātti nurture kriṣṇa as her adopted son or did she give birth to him, after enduring pain, in her form? He is known as yaśōdāp pirātti’s young lion. We \[herd-women\] have not seen her adopting him as her son. We had been focussed on her well-being at the time that she gave birth to him, but we did not see her giving birth to him. We had become tired and slept off. We had only heard from her that she had given birth to him. Just as it has been mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5-3-22 “*dadarśaca prabhuddāsā yaśōdā jātam ātmajam*” (yaśōdāp pirātti, who was sleeping, woke up after remaining unconscious, and found the son who was born), it was only after she had regained consciousness that she saw the infant \[kriṣṇa\]. After seeing kriṣṇa’s divine form, auspicious qualities and activities which are beyond this world, it could be only said that “He is not her son”. She too says, as mentioned in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3-1-3 “*immāyam valla piḷḷai nambi unnai en maganē enbar ninṟār*” (Oh, one who is complete in your auspicious qualities as a child! Seeing your amazing activities, people, who are neutral, will say that you are my son only) that neutral persons would say that he is her son only, while most of the others would say, after seeing your activities which are beyond this world, that you could not have been my son.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that in the first line of the pāsuram, the herd-ladies are asking whether yaśōdāp pirātti had adopted kriṣṇa as her son initially, and only after that, they are asking whether she had given birth to him. Normally, those who are conversant with śāstrams (sacred texts) will say that the eminence should be for the son who was given birth to and only after that, one asks about the son who was adopted. However, here, āḻvār, who knows the ultimate benefit of vēdams, as mentioned in *vēdap payan koḷḷa valla* (one who knows the benefit of vēdams) is accepting the herd-ladies’ order of adoption initially and giving birth to, subsequently. When there are two *darmams* \[accepted principles\] such as *sāmānya darmam* (normal principle) and *viśēśa drmam* (distinguished principle), the former will come under the latter while the latter will never go under the former \[in other words, distinguished principle will get precedence over the normal principle\] \[it goes without saying that when there is no *viśēśa darmam*, only the *sāmānya darmam* will be followed\]. Why is the *viśēśa darmam* given priority? Those who are conversant with śāstrams will relegate the adoption process to the background since it has the fault of selective *muhūrtam* (auspicious time for carrying out the function of adoption), unlike the natural birth which happens automatically, without selecting any auspicious time. In kriṣṇa’s case, no function was held when he had incarnated since no one knew that he had been born. Apart from the fault coming from forefathers’ *karmas* \[deeds\], the fault of union between a man and a woman also gets attached to the one who is born as a natural child. Also, any fault due to union between man and woman belonging to different *varṇas* (divisions) will also come to the naturally born child. These faults are not seen in the case of the child who is taken through adoption. Faults due to not practicing ordained activities as well as following the ordained activities in the wrong manner also will not come to the child taken through the adoption process. On the other hand, atonements carried out for overcoming faults at various points of time when the child is naturally born \[and not adopted\] will lessen the affection towards the child, to an extent. These faults are not seen in the case of the adopted child. Will these faults come to the naturally born child? Just as it has been mentioned in mantra praśnam “*ātmāvai putranāmāsi*” (father is born as the child), the faults will come onto the child. Due to these faults, the faults of *ruci* and *vāsanā* (impressions from previous births and repeated taste in carrying out wrong deeds) also will get attached. While these faults will go off, to an extent, by following vēdāntams and being together with noble people, it is not easy to remove them fully. However, will not those faults come to the adopted child through the original father’s deeds? Only the fault due to lineage \[clan\] will come. The faults due to *ruci* and *vāsanā* will not come. Due to the earlier mentioned following of vēdāntam and being with noble people, following their activities, faults due to the original father’s deeds will also disappear. Hence, the prominence is more to the adopted child than to the naturally born child. What are these differences? In vihagēndrasam 22 the order of importance is mentioned as “*putrān dārān bandūn sakīn gurūn*” (sons, wives, relatives, friends, teachers) and as “*pitaram mātaram dārān*” (father, mother, wives). When these relationships are renounced at the time of surrendering, these differences will not exist anymore. However, *putran* (son) has to be mentioned before *pitaram* (father). Only if there is a son, will the father exist. Even when *pitaram mātaram* (father, mother) are mentioned, they have to be identified as “this person’s father, this person’s mother”. Only in order to manifest the needlessness of these relationships were the words *pitaram mātaram* mentioned. This is the reason for giving prominence to adopted son over naturally born son. More than all these arguments, for the one who did not know that she only had given birth to the son \[yaśōdāp pirātti\], when she nurtures the child \[kriṣṇa\] with complete affection and esteem, should one talk about the differences in affection and esteem for those who had adopted and who had given birth to, as a result of ignorance?

**cittam …**– yaśōdāp pirātti is such that even when she sees your mischievous activities, she doesn’t control you. She acts in line with your thoughts. You are like a young lion, uncontrolled by her. She controls him in the other way \[giving him more opportunities to indulge in misciefs\] by saying, as in periya tirumoḻi 10-7-11 “*anganam tīmai seyvargaḷō nambī*! *āyar madamakkaḷai*” (Oh, kaṇṇapirān! Against the women who are obedient towards herd-folk, is it apt to carry out such misciefs?) by making him indulge in more misciefs. This is also mentioned in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 3-9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/07/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-3-9/) “*anja urappāḷ asōdai āṇāda vittirukkum*” (yaśōdāp pirātti vouldn’t say any harsh word which would frighten him; she would allow him to indulge in misciefs). He is being referred to as a young lion since he had the pride and there was none who could control him.

**kottār …** – his locks were completely decorated with flowers, donned with love by those who were affectionate towards him. Just as kūrattāḻvān had mentioned in varadarāja stavam 23 “*anjanapunjaśyāma kundaḷam*” (locks which were dark like the dark bluish clouds), he had dark locks; he could not be controlled by herd-folk; he had strength and he was like a lion, being prideful. *asōdai iḷanjingam – gōpāla kōḷari* – one who does not obey his mother, will not obey the words of those who are in the town. *kōḷ* – strength. *attan* – lord. This is the word uttered, after losing out to the qualities and activities mentioned earlier.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.1.8. Kongai van

*kongai van kūni soṟkoṇḍu kuvalayattungak kariyum pariyum irācciyamumengum baradaṟku aruḷi van kānadaiangaṇṇan appūcci kāttuginṟān ammanē! appūcci kāttuginṟān*

**Пословный перевод:**

kongai – appearing as if a bosom had come up on her back; van – strong; kūni – mantara, who had a hunch back; sol koṇḍu – considering her words; kuvalayam – among the elephants in the world; tungam – being the tallest; kariyum – elephants; pariyum – and horses; irācciyamum – as well as kingdom; engum – the forest where he was mercifully stepping into; baradarṟku – to bharatāḻvān; aruḷi – offered; van – difficult to enter for anyone; kān – forest; adai – one who attained; am – beautiful; kaṇṇan – one, who has eyes, is showing appūcci; ammanē! – oh, my! He is showing appūcci

**Перевод:**

**Considering the words of mantara, who had a huge hump on her back, which appeared like a bosom on the back, śrī rāma offered the tallest among the elephants in the world, along with horses, the kingdom and the forest which he was going to enter, to bharatāḻvān. He entered the forest, which is difficult to enter. Such an entity, who has beautiful eyes, is showing appūcci. Oh, my! He is showing appūcci.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that the entity, who is simple, is showing appūcci.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kongai …**– mantara had a strong hump on her back which appeared as if a bosom had arisen on her back. Considering the words of such kūni… While śrī rāma had gone to the forest in order to fulfil the words of his father, why is the pāsuram saying that he went as per the words of kūni? Just as bharatāḻvān had said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam “*na mantarāyā na māturasyā dōśōnurājña*:” (It was not the fault of kūni’s, it vasn’t mother kaikēyi’s neither was it daśarata’s), among the reasons for śrī rāma to enter the forest, the first mentioned name was that of kūni’s. It was due to her words that kaikēyi’s mind got confused and because of that, cakravarti (emperor) had to ask śrī rāma to go to the forest. Thus, since she was the root of all these, the pāsuram says that considering her words, śrī rāma went to the forest.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kūni’s intelligence too was crooked, just like her form.

**kuvalayat tungak kariyum** – śatrunjayan, which was the tallest among all the elephants on earth, and elephants which were similar to it

**pariyum** – horses, which were eminent, like those elephants.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the horses in the kingdom were similar to uccaiśravas (horse seen in celestial world).

**irācciyamum** – expansive kingdom, which did not have any enemies in between

**engum** – just as it has been mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 18-6 “*ikśvākūṇām iyam bhūmi: saśailavanakānanā*” (earth, with its mountains, woods and forests, belongs to ikśvāku kingdom), even the forest to which śī rāma was about to mercifully go to, belonged to ikśvāKu kingdom.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai asks here: Did śrī rāma give the forest too, which he was going to enter, to bharata? He answers this question in the following way: After śrī rāma had felled vāli with his arrow, vāli took that arrow and asked śri rāma many questions, of which one was “What benefit would you attain by killing me?” to which śrī rāma said “In the kingdom of bharata, would you covet your brother’s wife?” vāli then asked śrī rāma “Did he \[his brother, sugrīva\] not commit the same offence?” śri rāma told him “If you speak this way, I will hurt you in such a way that you would feel that you have been kept on top of a totem pole” \[In śrī rāmāyaṇam, śrī rāma had told vāḷi that sugrīva had taken vāli’s wife to offer her protection, since everyone had thought that vāli was dead. However, vāli had seized sugrīva’s wife, even when sugrīva was alive\]. It is due to this reason that śrī rāma said that the forest too belonged to bharatāḻvān. Alternatively, it could be said that śrī rāma had told bharata that through righteousness and through valour, he had offered bharata whatever he desired. perumāḷ \[śrī rāma\] had said “I have given you” when it should have been “Father has given you”. Why did he say this way? Even if cakravarti \[daśarata\] were to give it, he needed śrī rāma’s permission. Absence of objection is equivalent to granting permission. Hence, it could be said that śrī rāma had given the forest too, to bharata.

**baradaṟku aruḷi** – śrī rāma gave all these to bharatāḻvān, in line with the boons asked for by kaikēyi, and as accepted by emperor daśarata.

**van kān adai …** – the one, who is beautiful and simple, who attained the forest, which could not be entered into, by anyone. When śrī rāma was asked to leave for the forest, with the *kāppu* \[protective sacred thread\] around his wrist, his face did not darken \[viz. he did not become sorrowful that he had to go to the forest when he was to be coronated the next day as the king of ayōdyā\]. He removed the crown, plaited his hair into matted hair and set for the forest, leaving the kingdom. Considering these aspects, śrī rāma is being referred to here as one with beauty and simplicity. Alternatively, the term *am kaṇṇan* would refer to one who has beautiful, divine eyes, as mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 66-8 “*rāma*: *kamalapatrākśa*:” (śrī rāma who has his eyes like the petals of lotus flower). This describes the happiness in the eyes of śrī rāma, reflecting the state of his mind, instead of having any distress that he was leaving the wealth of kingdom and entering forest.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that after sending off sumantran \[daśarata’s minister\] and the chariot, śrī rāma entered the forest. where the small stones were hot due to the scorching sun and with his feet burning and paining, knowing the way to enter the forest but not the way to come out.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.1.9. Padaga mudalai

*padaga mudalai vāyppatta kaḷiṟukadaṟik kaikkūppi en kaṇṇā! kaṇṇā! ennaudavap puḷḷūrndu angu uṟu tuyar tīrttaádagan vandu appūchi kāttuginṟān ammanē! appūcci kāttuginṟān*

**Пословный перевод:**

padagam – being cruel; mudalai – crocodile; vāy – in its mouth; patta – got caught; kaḷiṟu – śrī gajēndrāḻvān \[elephant\]; kadaṟi – uttering a loud cry; kai kūppi – performing anjali (salutation); en kaṇṇā! kaṇṇā! enna – as it called out many times “Oh, one who is my controller!”; udava – to help during that time of danger; puḷ – garuda; ūrndu – conducting him to go fast; angu – in that pond; uṟu – suffering of śrī gajēndran in the mouth of the crocodile; tuyar – sorrow; tīrtta – one who removed; adagan – one who is strong, is showing appūcci; ammanē! – oh, my! He is showing appūcci

**Перевод:**

**Elephant śrī gajēndrāḻvān was caught by the cruel crocodile in its mouth. He cried out aloud, saying “Oh, one who is my controller!”, saluting emperumān. In order to help him, emperumān rode on garuda rapidly to that pond and removed the sorrow of śrī gajēndran who suffered inside the mouth of the crocodile. Such kriṣṇa is showing appūcci. Oh, my! He is showing appūcci.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the one with great strength is showing appūcci*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**padagam** – cruelty of the crocodile, as mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 5-8-3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/02/periya-thirumozhi-5-8-3/) “*kodiya vāy vilangu*” (animal with a cruel mouth). This mentions about the cruelty by hurting śrī gajēndrāḻvān, as mentioned in [tiruppaḷḷiyeḻucci 2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2014/12/thiruppalliyezhuchchi-2-kozhungodi/) “*adan vidattinukku anungi aḻungiya ānai*” (gajēndrāḻvān who was hurt by the crocodile’s poisonous teeth). Alternatively, the long syllable in *pādagam* has got shortened as *padagam*. This then refers to the crocodile which had grievous sin. In other words, this crocodile, being stricken with a curse, was lying in the pond. Since it knew that the elephant was the one which will liberate it from its sin, it gripped the elephant’s leg firmly, without letting go of it, in order to fulfil its wish.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that śrī gajēndran is a follower of emperumān. Which is the grievous sin for the crocodile? Is it catching hold of śrī gajēndran’s leg or is it the curse of the sage due to which the crocodile has taken its present form? He says that it is the original curse of the sage due to which the crocodile was in its present form and to clear which it had to hold the foot of the elephant, which was the grievous sin for the crocodile. Otherwise, the grievous sin would get transposed to the sage since the crocodile grabbed the divine foot of emperumān’s follower \[which is the antidote for the curse\].

**vāyp patta kaḷiṟu** – the elephant, which got caught in the mouth of the crocodile. Since water is not its natural habitat, it got caught by the worm in the water. Had it been its natural habitat of land, the crocodile vouldn’t have come anywhere near the elephant.

**kadaṟi …** – once the elephant got caught by the crocodile, it thought “I can reach the bank on my strength itself”, as mentioned in viṣṇu darmam 69-46 “*gaja ākarśatē tīrē grāha ākarśatē jalē*” (śrī gajēndrāḻvān was pulling the crocodile towards the bank and crocodile was pulling towards water). The crocodile was trying to pull the elephant towards water while the elephant was trying to pull the crocodile towards land. This went on for a thousand celestial years \[one earth year is one day for celestial entities. Thus, 360 earth years will be one celestial year\]. Since water is natural habitat for crocodile, since its desire \[of getting liberated\] was going to be fulfilled, just as it has been mentioned in periya tirumoḻi 5-8-3 “*muḻuvali mudalai*” (crocodile with its full strength), the strength of crocodile was waxing, while for the elephant, since water was not its habitat, since its desire was not getting fulfilled, its strength was waning. Its trunk was almost getting into water. The elephant thought “There is nothing that we could do now”. Just as it has been mentioned in viṣṇu darmam 69-47 “*paramāpadamāpannō manasā cintayat harīm*” (having been caught in critical danger, elephant thought of hari, emperumān), it thought of *sarvēśvaran* \[lord of all\] as its protector. It took out its hand \[trunk\], performed *anjali* and manifesting its anguish, called out several times to emperumān “Oh, one who is my controller!” tirumangai āḻvār, in his siṟiya tirumadal said “*nārāyaṇā*! *O*! *maṇivaṇṇā*! *nāgaṇaiyāy*! *vārāy*!” (Oh, nārāyaṇa! Oh, one who has a divine complexion like a gemstone! Oh, one who is reclining on ādiśēśan! Come immediately). periyāḻvār says in this pāsuram that gajēndrāḻvān called out to emperumān as “*en kaṇṇā*! *kaṇṇā*!”. *paurāṇikars* \[those who are experts on purāṇams\] said that gajēndran had called out to emperumān as “*mūlēti mukta padamālāpati dvipēndrē*” (during the time when gajēndran had called out to emperumān as *mūlamē* (one who is the origin of all)). What is common among all these? Since gajēndran had thought of emperumān who is together with distinguished form, āḻvārs had referred to him with similar meaning terms; hence, all these refer to the same.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai asks here: why is it said “*kadaṟi*”? \[the elephant had cried out emperumān’s divine name\]. The elephant is not qualified to recite emperumān’s divine name. What is its qualification? It should call out to the dēvatā \[divine entity\] which is residing in its heart and through that dēvatā, the *antaryāmi* \[indvelling soul, emperumān\]. ōr, *svāntaryāmi* – emperumān who is residing as the indvelling soul inside every entity. Since the elephant called out to emperumān directly, āḻvār refers to it as *kadaṟi.* Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 3-1-9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-1-9-mazhungadha/) “*maḻungāda jñānamē padaiyāga nīngum*” (If you had removed the distress of śrī gajēndran through your *sankalpam* (divine will) would that action not have reduced your great radiance?), not wishing to use your divine will, you were waiting for a long time \[for the elephant to realise its *pāratantryam* (being totally dependent on you) and to call you out). Sage viśvāmitra had realised that his strength as a king was inferior to the strength of sage vasiśta when he had waged a battle on vasiśta \[when viśvāmitra was still a king) by saying “*dikbalam kśatriya balam*” (the strength of a king is inferior). In a similar manner, considering that *bhakti mārgam* (attaining emperumān through the path of devotion) is inferior to *prapatti mārgam* (the path of attaining emperumān through the act of surrendering), even before the cry of *kaṇṇā kaṇṇ*A \[by the elephant\] could be completed, emperumān showed himself up, before the elephant, rejecting the supporting hand of *sēnai mudaliyār*, making his divine consorts to wonder as to what had happened, not considering the umbrella and *covry* \[fly-flapper\], sandals etc, not waiting for garuda to decorate himself, imploring garuda to go faster, and upon reaching the bank of the pond, he took the flower from the hand of elephant and accepted it, making the *pūrva bhakti* \[devotion shown by śrī gajēndran\] as *sādya bhakti* \[carrying out kainkaryam \[servitude\] as the benefit of having surrendered.

**udava …** – As soon as emperumān heard this cry of anguish from gajēndrāḻvān in his divine ears, he got out of his divine mattress in a flurry, did not hold the hand of *sēnai mudaliyār* (viśvaksēnar) when he tried to give his hand, as mentioned in śrī rangarājastavam uttara śatakam 57 “*atantrita camūpati prahitahastam*” (not considering the helping hand of sēnai mudaliyār), did not put on his divine sandals too and took steps on the floor. Seeing this, his divine consorts were perplexed wondering “What has happened?” He did not wait for garuda to prepare himself for carrying emperumān through decorations, focussing on “We should help for that anguish”, imploring garuda to go even faster. Once he reached the bank of the pond, he removed the sorrow of śrī ganjēndran. What was gajēndran’s sorrow? Just as it has been mentioned in viṣṇu darmam ”*nāham kaḷēparasyāya trnārtam madusūdana*! *karasta kamalānyēva pādayōrarpitum harē*:” (Oh, madusūdana! It was not for protecting my physical form, but I am calling in order to proffer the reddish lotus flower in my hand at the divine feet of hari), it was for proffering the fresh lotus flower in his hand at the divine feet of emperumān that gajēndrāḻvān called out.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that for the verse “*angu uṟu tuyar tīrtta*”, the term *angu* refers to the place where the crocodile had grabbed. *uṟu tuyar* – the sorrow of the elephant as well as his \[emperumān’s\] sorrow. Even when the elephant’s trunk was getting drowned, emperumān came there and touched his divine disc, as mentioned by tirumangai āḻvār in his [periya tirumoḻi 2-3-9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/08/periya-thirumozhi-2-3-9/) “*niṇru āḻi tottān*” (emperumān reached the pond and touched his divine disc), wondering whether the elephant would go back to its previous state of choosing the path of devotion \[over *śaraṇāgat*i, act of surrendering\]. Even in the act of surrendering, if one does not remove the thought that it was due to the act of surrendering that they had attained emperumān, it would cause immense sorrow. The strength which the elephant had all along, had to be destroyed for him to surrender today. If emperumān had to offer a benefit for the act of surrendering, a miniscule part of his *sankalpam* (divine will) was sufficient. However, he came in person to the pond, making \[parāśara\] bhattar to mercifully say “*bhagavatastvarāyai nama*:” (I bow down to the speed with which you came to the bank of the pond). If he had not come to the pond with such urgency, as confirmed by a disciple *siṟṟātkoṇḍār*, his radiance would have got diminished \[reference here is to nammāḻvār’s tiruvāimoḻi pāsuram 3-1-9 when nammāḻvār had asked whether his radiance would not have lessened if he had removed the elephant’s distress through his *sankalpam*\]. *uṟutuyar tīrtta adagan* – the hugely powerful entity who removed the sorrow through the proper means. Alternatively, by making his mercy to take precedence \[by going in person to the pond and removing the elephant’s sorrow\] and his *svātantryam* supported by his *sankalpam* to lie low, he is the powerful entity who came and showed *appūcci*.

**adagan** – one who is powerful. This speaks about the distinguished power with which he protected his follower. With such divine hand, he is showing *appūcci*. Oh, my! He is showing *appūcci.*

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.1.10. Vallal ilangai

*vallāḷ ilangai malangac caram turandavillāḷanai vittu cittan virittasollārnda appūccip  pādal ivai pattumvallār pōy vaigundam manni irupparē*

**Пословный перевод:**

val āḷ – having strong entities; ilangai – lankāpuri; malanga – to become bewildered; saram – arrows; turanda – one who shot; vil āḷanai – one who was controlling the bow; vittu cittan – periyāḻvār; viritta – mercifully explained; sol ārnda – filled with words; appūcci – regarding the activity of appūcci; pādal – pāsurams \[songs\]; ivai pattum – these ten; vallār – those who are capable of reciting; pōy – going beyond prakruti maṇḍalam (the region of primordial matter); vaigundam – in śrī vaikuṇṭam; manni iruppar – will remain fittingly

**Перевод:**

**emperumān shot arrows at lankāpuri, which had many strong entities, such that all the people became bewildered. vittu cittan had mercifully composed pāsurams regarding the matter of appūcci indulged in, by that emperumān. Those who are capable of reciting these ten pāsurams will go beyond the region of primordial matter and fit aptly in śrī vaikuṇṭam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In this last pāsuram, āḻvār mentions the benefit which will accrue to one who recites all the ten pāsurams of this decad and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vallāḷ ilangai** – lankā had strong people and the means as a result of which no one could attack it. It is inhabited by demons who are respected by rāvaṇa.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai summarises the fear of āḻvār from the first to the last pāsuram of this decad. In the first pāsuram, when he said “*bāradam kai seyda attūdan*” he was fearful as to “What will happen?” In the second pāsuram, when he said “*nūṟṟuvar pattaḻiyat tiṇ tēr mēl munninṟa …*” he was fearful about *alaivalai* (one who speaks or does a lot); in the third pāsuram “*kāyunīr kadambēṟit tīya paṇattil pāyndādi* ” he was fearful that kriṣṇa had jumped on top of the hoods of the snake kāḷiyan. In the fourth pāsuram, “*iruttil piṟandu..*” he was afraid of darkness; in the fifth pāsuram, he was afraid of the favourable entities turning into unfavourable \[kriṣṇa used to sleep under a cart; a monster pervaded that card and came rolling towards kriṣṇa with the intention to kill him\]. In the sixth pāsuram, since kriṣṇa was consuming ghee, curd, milk etc, āḻvār was afraid as to whether his stomach would be able to digest all these. In the seventh pāsuram, “*asōdai iḷam singam – gōpālak kōḷari*” he was afraid of kriṣṇa’s activities due to his arrogance of being a young lion. In the eighth pāsuram, in line with the activities of his incarnation, emperumān had to go to forest. āḻvār was afraid of that. In the ninth pāsuram, he was afraid that kriṣṇa had to go on top of garudan to save an elephant from a crocodile. In this \[tenth\] pāsuram, he was afraid of the danger from demons when he went with his bow to destroy lankā. In order to remove āḻvār’s fear, emperumān showed him the divine āḻvārs \[divine disc and divine conch\] which he constantly held in his divine hands. Since the girls in tiruvāyppādi and āḻvār too were afraid of enmity of monsters such as pūtanā, śakata, yamaḷa, arjuna et al towards emperumān, the āḻvārs showed by emperumān in his divine hands increased the fear of young girls in tiruvāyppādi as well as āḻvār himself. This showing of divine disc and divine conch in his hands is referred to as *appūcci* \[if āḻvār had got consoled after seeing the divine disc and divine conch in emperumān’s divine hands, he would have said ‘divine disc, divine conch’; however, he said *appūcci*, again expressing fear\]. If the herd-girls had been scared on seeing divine disc and divine conch, it is understandable \[since they vouldn’t have known about the divine āḻvārs on emperumān’s divine hands\] and their friendliness towards emperumān is admixed with fear. Though they had seen the divine weapons in many places, as in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1-2-12](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/07/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-1-2-12/) “*neyttalai nēmiyum sangum nilāviya*”, they might have forgotten these \[or, they would have been made to forget by emperumān\] and might have realised now, after seeing them on his divine hands. However, periyāḻvār had moved with the divine āḻvārs on emperumān’s divine hands, as in [tiruppallāṇḍu pāsuram 1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-1-pallandu/) “*valattuṟaiyum sudar āḻiyum pallāṇḍu*” etc, why should he then say *appūcci* \[as if he too had been scared\]? This is because, he being a mangaḷāśāsanaparar \[one who praises and wishes well for emperumān\], it is his nature to be like this. While āḻvār might have composed these pāsurams under the pretext of herd-women saying *appūcci*, for periyāḻvār, this is his nature \[being fearful of what would befall emperumān and carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam\]. Even if this *appūcci* pāsuram had not been there, he had still expressed his fear through pāsurams, as in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.3.6 – “*vayiṟum maṟūkkināy*” (why did you make my stomach feel churned, in fear?). This is his habit. In situations where he had mercifully composed such pāsurams, this sense of fear would be always present in his divine mind.

Since lankā was seized \[from kubēra\] through show of strength \[in a battle\], āḻvār says *vallāḷ ilangai*.

**malanga** – lankā was bewildered such that the sandals of demons and the \[idols of\] deities vorśipped by the demons got scattered in various directions, looking for a safe place.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai asks here whether celestial deities are present in lankā. Just as it has been mentioned in the ślōkam “*agnihōtrāśca vēdāśca rākśasānām gruhē gruhē*” (in every house of the demons, the sounds of rituals and reciting of vedams are heard), they are there. Alternatively, whatever \[or whosoever\] they liked, is their deity.

**saram totta villāḷanai** – one who had the divine bow, with which the divine arrows were shot. It is implied through this that instead of destroying lankā with the greatness of being īśvaran (controller of all), in line with the species \[human\] in which he had incarnated, śrī rāma, with arrows, as a symbol of his masculinity, destroyed that place. While this tirumoḻi (divine verses of 2<sup>nd</sup> centum, 1<sup>st</sup> decad) deals with emperumān’s incarnation as kriṣṇa, mercifully speaking this way about śrī rāmāvatāram in the final pāsuram of this tirumoḻi is to bring in the unity between the two incarnations \[both have same root, śrīman nārāyaṇan\]. This unity was mentioned in the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this decad too, “*vankānadai am kaṇṇan*”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *rāmacaram* \[arrows of śrī rāma\] is famous. This is evidenced in pāsurams such as [tiruvāimoḻi 7-4-7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/thiruvaimozhi-7-4-7-maru-niraiththu/) “*māṟu niraittu iraikkum*” (the arrows released by śrī rāma would make great sounds) and  in [tiruvāimoḻi 8-6-3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/04/thiruvaimozhi-8-6-3-oruvar-iruvar/) “*oruvar iruvar ōr mūvar*” (depending on the pace with which he released the arrows, śrī rāma would appear as a single entity or two persons or three persons; if the intensity is high, he would move so fast that it would appear as if he had disappeared).

**viṣṇu cittan viritta** – mercifully composed by periyāḻvār, in a detailed manner.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that based on the valour etc shown in this \[śrī rāma\] avatāram which āḻvār explained in a detailed manner, the valour in other incarnations too was explained . Even when he started composing prabandams, as in [tiruppallāṇḍu 3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-3-vazhatpattu/) “*ilangai pāḻāḷgap padai porudānukku*” (one who fought along with the army of monkeys such that everyone in lankā was annihilated), he had explained this in a detailed manner.

**sollārnda …**– those who are capable of reciting these ten pāsurams, which are composed with words which are full of meanings, on the activity of *appūcci*. Due to the usage of the term *sollārnda*, it is opined that those who recite these pāsurams need not take efforts to know their meanings. The flavour of the words itself is enough for them to recite these.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that śāstrams \[sacred texts\] such as *śruti, smruti, itihāsas* and *purāṇas* became complete with words only after these *appūcci* pāsurams were composed. This activity of *appūcci* is such that the one who shows it, is fearless and the one, who sees it \[āḻvār\], is fearful.

**vallār** – this would refer to those who are capable of reciting the pāsurams with the pathos of periyāḻvār.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *vallār* refers to those who recite with the pathos of āḻvār. Alternatively, it refers to those who take refuge under āḻvār’s affection, recite these with only the words \[without knowing even the meanings\] and make others to recite, making this as a habit.

**pōy …** – mere reciting of the pāsurams will enable them to go through the path of *arcis* \[the path of light which leads a soul to śrī vaikuṇṭam\], enjoy emperumān there and carry out mangaḷāśāsanam forever.

We shall next consider the pravēśam of the next tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.2.1. Aravanaiyay! ayarere!

*aravaṇaiyāy! āyarēṟē! ammam uṇṇat tuyil eḻāyēiravum uṇṇādu uṟangi nī pōy inṟum ucci koṇḍadālōvaravum kāṇēn vayiṟu asaindāy vana mulaigaḷ sōrndu pāyatiru udaiya vāy maduttu tiḷaittu udaittup parugidāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aravu – tiruvanantāḻvān; aṇaiyāy – oh, one who has as mattress!; āyar – for the herd-folk; ēṟē – oh, one who is the head!; ammam uṇṇa – to consume the milk from bosom; tuyil – from divine sleep; eḻāy – should get up; nī – you; iravum – last night too; uṇṇādu – without consuming milk from bosom; uṟangi pōy – apart from sleeping; inṟum – today also; ucci koṇḍadu – it has become noon; varavum kāṇēn – (in order to have milk, getting up from the bed) I haven’t seen you coming; vayiṟu asaindāy – (not indicating that you don’t desire) your stomach is languishing; vanam mulaigaḷ – beautiful bosoms; sōrndu pāya – such that milk is flowing out; tiru udaiya – having beautiful; vāy – divine mouth; maduttu – keeping; tiḷaittu – with pride; udaittu – kicking my form with your divine feet; parugidāy – you should imbibe

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who has ādiśēśan as your mattress! Oh, one who is the head of herd-folk! You should get up from your divine sleep in order to consume milk from my bosom. You had gone to bed last night, without consuming milk. It is already noon time, today. I haven’t seen you getting up from the bed, in order to have milk. Your stomach is languishing from want of milk. You should take milk from my beautiful bosoms which are overflowing with milk, by keeping your divine mouth on them, with the pride of consuming from them, and kicking my stomach, even as you consume the milk.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**aravaṇai …** – having ādiśēśan, who has softness, coolness, fragrance etc as his nature, as the mattress, oh, one who got out of that, as mentioned in harivamśam 113-6-2 “*nāgaparyankam utsrujya hyāgata*:” (getting out of the mattress of tiruvanantāḻvān \[ādiśēśan\] and reaching maturā) and who became lord of herd-folk! Is it the flavour of having reclined on that mattress as a habit that you are still sleeping? Even after becoming the head of herd-folk, kriṣṇa doesn’t want to get out of the bed. When emperumān incarnates in various species, just as it has been mentioned in [mudal tiruvandādi 53](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/08/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-53/) “*senṟāl kudaiyām*” (when emperumān walks, ādiśēśan becomes his umbrella etc), tiruvanantāḻvān, in line with his nature of carrying out servitude, could have taken the form of a mattress for emperumān to recline upon, knowing the divine mind of emperumān. Thus, the comfort which emperumān had enjoyed there, is continuing here too, for the one who is reclining.

**ammam uṇṇat tuyil eḻāyē** – the reason for using the term *ammam* instead of saying *mulai uṇṇa* (consume milk from the bosom) is to make him understand the simple word used for a child, in line with his incarnation in the human species. *tuyil* – sleep. *eḻugai* \[getting up\] refers to that sleep getting broken and getting up. The term *eḻāy* refers to the prayer \[of yaśōdāp pirātti\] to get up.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says here that kriṣṇa may not realise the meaning of words such as *sōṟu* (food), *prasādam* (divine food which had been offered to the lord) and hence āḻvār says *ammam* \[a term which he would be familiar with, being a child\].

**iravum …** – you had slept off last night, without consuming milk from me. Not only that, it is already noon time now. Even if you had slept off last night due to excessive weariness \[due to wandering all the time\], once the morning has broken out, should you not have taken milk? Is it that it has dawned only now? It is noon time already. The two syllables, *Al* and *O* \[as in *koṇḍadālō*\] have been used as poetic metrics and do not carry any meaning.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that those who have had food in the noon time, may forget to eat during night. But, would those, who haven’t had food in the noon time too, forget to eat during night? \[implies that kriṣṇa had not taken milk the previous day afternoon too\]. In the night, when you were asleep, I \[reference is to āḻvār\] tried to wake you up. Since you did not get up, I did not want to disturb you further. Now, with dawn breaking out, āḻvār says that it is noon time.

**varavu …** – I have not seen you getting up on your own in order to have food. Your stomach also appears to be languishing due to lack of food, negating any impression that you are not desirous of food.

**vana mulaigaḷ sōrndu pāya** – *vanappu* – beauty and eminence. My bosoms, due to affection towards you, are secreting milk on their own, looking at you. The implied meaning is that “While you are hungry, this milk is getting wasted, without being consumed”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here – if you decide not to have food, śouldn’t you have come and told me that you don’t need food? When he gets up to inform her that he doesn’t need milk, looking at him, she realises that his stomach is languishing from hunger and his face is drooping. Hence, milk automatically started flowing out of her bosoms.

**tiru udaiya vāy maduttu** – keeping the beautiful divine mouth. *tiru* – beautiful. Keeping your divine mouth on these beautiful bosoms, manifesting your desire to consume milk.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: this implies that emperumān’s divine mouth is specific for pirātti (śrī mahālakśmi). This would also mean that for the herd-women in tiruvāyppādi, as mentioned in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3-1-6 “*suruttār menkuḻal*” (women with curled, soft locks decorated with flowers), his divine mouth was the source for imbibing nectar. This would also refer to beautiful divine mouth

**tiḷaittu …** – you should consume milk, manifesting your happiness such that with pride, you kick me on my form. *parugudal* – to imbibe.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.2.2. Vaitta neyyum

*vaitta neyyum kāynda pālum vadi tayirum naṟu veṇṇeyumittanaiyum peṟṟaṟīyēn empirān! nī piṟanda pinnaiettanaiyum seyyap peṟṟāy ēdum seyyēn kadam padādēmuttu anaiya muṟuval seydu mūkku uṟinji mulai uṇāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

em pirān! – oh, one who became my lord!; nī piṟanda pinnai – after you were born as my son; vaitta neyyum – ghee, which has been melted; kāynda pālum – milk, which has been heated; vadi tayirum – curd, which is hard; ittanaiyum – even one among these; peṟṟu aṟiyēn – I have not got; ettanaiyum – in the manner that it is acceptable to you; seyya peṟṟāy – you may do; ēdum seyyēn – I will not run after you or tie you up; kadam padādē – do not be angry; muttu anaiya – like pearls; muṟuval seydu – smiling; mūkku uṟinji – rubbing your nose; mulai uṇāyē – you should consume milk from my bosoms

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who became my lord! After you were born as my son, I have not seen ghee, which has been melted, or milk, which has been heated, or curd, which is solid or butter, which is fragrant. You can do whatever you wish to. I will not chase you or tie you up. Do not get angry. Smile such that the pearls \[divine teeth\] are visible, rub your nose and consume milk from my bosoms.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vaitta …** – ghee, which had been melted without any fault, milk, which had been heated to a concentrated stage, curd from which water has been removed by straining and fragrant butter, which has been prepared from fresh curd.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that the ghee has been obtained by melting fragrant butter, which had no fault in it. Curd was such that if tilted, the entire curd would slide. It was that solid \[had it been having any water in it, when tilted, the water / curd would have flowed down the container, instead of sliding\]. *naṟu veṇṇey* – fragrant butter, which had been obtained by churning fresh curd, knowing the stage until when it had to be churned.

**empirān nī pṟanda pinnai – ittanaiyum peṟṟaṟiyēn** – oh, my lord! After you were born, I had not known of any of these materials. Alternatively, the term *ittanaiyum* would refer to even a little bit of any of these materials. kriṣṇa became angry on hearing this. He said “You are making me out as a thief. āren’t you saying all these things in order to catch me and to beat me?”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār hadn’t known anything about any of these materials. Even the containers, in which these had been kept, did not have a trace of any of the materials. When āḻvār \[in the pathos of yaśōdāp pirātti\] said that he had not known about any of these materials, kriṣṇa responded saying “Someone would have taken it”. When he said “*empirān*”, there was a change in his \[kriṣṇa’s\] facial expression and when he said “I have not known any of these after your birth”, kriṣṇa became angry, saying “āren’t you saying all these, blaming me?” and started to leave the place. āḻvār told him “Come to me” to which he responded, saying “āren’t you calling me in order to catch me and to beat me?”

**ettanaiyum seyyap peṟṟāy** – you could do whatever you wish to.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here – āḻvār tells kriṣṇa “You could do whatever you wish to”; kriṣṇa replies “Now, you are saying this. But aren’t these your words? \[indicating that in the past, āḻvār had called kriṣṇa to him, like this, and once he went to āḻvār, he had beaten him\].

**ēdum seyyēn kadambadādē** – I will not catch you or beat you. You need not get angry.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here – āḻvār tells him “I will not beat you or be angry with you; you come to me, without getting angry”. Upon hearing this, kriṣṇa smiled, displaying the divine pearls \[his divine teeth\]. āḻvār went to him, took him in his arms, forgetting all thoughts of punishing him, and tells him “With that smile, hit me with your divine nose, rubbing your face and nose against my bosoms and consume my milk”

**muttanaiya …** – smile, displaying your pearl-like divine teeth; in other words, get rid of your anger and smile.

**mūkkurinji mulai uṇāyē** – hitting against the base of my bosom, rubbing your nose against it, consume the milk from my bosoms.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says at the end – through all these, with the term *vaitta ney*, mukttātmā has been spoken of \[muktātmā is one who has got liberated from the material realm, samsāram and reached the spiritual realm, śrī vaikuṇṭam\]. The term *kāynda pāl* refers to those who recite emperumān’s divine names, as mentioned in [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 26](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/10/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-26/) ”*mādavan pēr solluvadē ōttin surukku*” (reciting the divine name of emperumān is the essence of vēdams) and in the verse “*nāma niśtōsmi aham harē*:” (through recitation of emperumān’s divine names, I remain deeply engaged with the divine names). The term *vadi tayiṟu* refers to those who are clear about the distinction between *prakruti* and *ātmā* (body and soul, respectively) and who are clear about *caturti* and *ukāram* \[these refer to tirumantram, in which *caturti* refers to the hidden fourth case over the first syllable *a* in praṇavam, indicating relationship (being a servitor) with emperumān and *ukāram* refers to the *ananyārha śēśantvamī* (being a servitor only to emperumān and to no one else)\]. Finally, the term *naṟu veṇṇey* refers to those who have learnt the distinction between *prakruti* and *ātmā* and who are complete with auspicious qualities of ātmā \[such as being *ananyārha śēśan* to emperumān, being totally dependent on emperumān etc\], without any trace of *ahankāram* \[ego\] or *mamakāram* \[possessiveness\] and being desirous of *mōkśam* \[in other words, *mumukśus*, those who desire to attain śrī vaikuṇṭam\].

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.2.3. Tandam makkal

*tandam makkaḷ aḻudu senṟāl tāymār āvār tarikka killārvandu nin mēl pūsal seyya vāḻavalla vāsudēvā!undaiyār un tiṟattarallar unnai nān onṟu urappa māttēnnandagōpan aṇi siṟuvā! nān suranda mulai uṇāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tam tam – their; makkaḷ – children; aḻudu senṟāl – if they go, crying; tāy mār āvār – their mothers; tarikka killār – cannot tolerate; vandu – people in the town, will bring their children; nin mēl – upon you; pūsal seyya – to complain; vāḻa valla – making this as your life; vāsudēvā! – oh, kaṇṇā, the divine son of śrī vasudēvar!; undaiyār – your father; un tiṟattar allar – does not have the capability to look at your misciefs; nān – I, on the other hand; unnai – you, a hugely mischievous child; onṟu – in any manner; urappa māttēn – not capable of controlling you (while all these remain this way); nanda gōpan – nandagōpar’s; aṇi siṟuvā! – oh, beautiful child!; nān suranda – secreted by me; mulai uṇāyē – you should consume milk from bosom

**Перевод:**

**When children go to their mothers crying, the mothers will not be able to tolerate that crying. They will bring their children and fight with you. Oh, the son of vasudēvar! You are having this as your way of life. Your father does not have the quality of looking at your misciefs. I am not capable of controlling such a mischievous child as you. Oh, the beautiful child of śrī nandagōpar! You should now consume the milk, secreted by my bosoms.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tandam …** – while children in the village start playing, unlike other children, you beat them, punch them etc. Could you do like this? When their children go to them crying, their mothers will not tolerate.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam – many, including the children playing in the street, complain “Your son beat us”. When yaśōdāp pirātti brought those children to kriṣṇa, who had played mischief with them, he said, in fear, at the point of breaking out into a cry “Mother, I did not do anything. They only did all these”. Instead of comforting the children who came crying to her or punishing kriṣṇa, she started blaming herself. After hearing her say “Will their mothers tolerate if their children are beaten up like this?” the mothers too went their way. When yaśōdāp pirātti started searching for him to punish him, she saw him crying. “Everyone is blaming you and finding fault with you. This has become your nourishment”.

**vandu nin mēl pūsal seyya** – when they come with their children, and complain about you, angrily

**vāḻa valla** – instead of feeling sad about it, you appear to be enjoying this, with desire.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here – yaśōdāp pirātti became angry with kriṣṇa, saying “You are like a tiger cub, which came out of the stomach of a cow”

**vāsudēvā** – Oh, one who is the son of vasudēvar! You are like a tiger cub born to a cow.

**undaiyār …** – your father \[nandagōpar\] is not looking at your misciefs. She implies that he is not punishing kriṣṇa.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here – your father śrī nandagōpar, is not having your skills, He is not nurturing you, by punishing you on occasions.

**unnai …** – I, who am weak, cannot control you, who are a mischievous child.

**nandagōpan aṇi siṟuvā** – Oh, one who came as the son of śrī nandagōpar! *aṇi* – beautiful. This is the word being spoken of by her, due to anguish at his misciefs.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here – yaśōdāp pirātti became angry with kriṣṇa, saying “You happen to be the son of śrī nandagōpar”.  Forgetting that too, she prays to him to consume the milk secreted by her bosoms.

**nānsuranda mulai uṇāyē** – Let all those things remain. Now, consume the milk secreted by my bosoms.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.2.4. Kanjan tannal

*kanjan tannāl puṇarkkappatta kaḷḷaccagadu kalakkaḻiyapanjiyanna melladiyāl pāyndapōdu nondidum enṟuanjinēn kāṇ amarar kōvē! āyar kūttattu aḷavanṟu ālōkanjanai un vanjanaiyāl valaippaduttāy! mulai uṇāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

amarar kōvē – oh, dēvādirāja! (king of all the celestial entities); kanjan tannāl – by kamsan (who was rankling on you); puṇarkkappatta – instructed (to harm you); kaḷḷam – deceptive; sagadu – śakatam (wheel); kalakku aḻiya – to be destroyed completely, including its joints and spokes; panji anna – like cotton; mel – soft; adiyāl – with divine feet; pāynda pōdu – during the time you kicked; nondidum enṟu – thinking that it would hurt; anjinēn kāṇ – I was scared, you would see; āyar kūttattu aḷavu anṟu – my fear was not like the fear felt by the assembly of herd-folk; Al O! – Oh, my!; kanjanai – kamsan, who was carrying out deceptive deeds against you; un vanjanaiyāl – through your deceptive deeds; valaip paduttāy! – Oh, one who destroyed him such that he couldn’t escape! You should consume milk from my bosoms

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who is the king of all the celestial entities! kamsan had instructed a monster to harm you, in a deceptive manner, by pervading a wheel. When you kicked the wheel with your soft, like cotton, divine feet, such that the wheel got destroyed including its joints and spokes, I was scared that your divine feet would have got hurt. My fear was not like the fear felt by the assembly of herd-folk. Oh, one who destroyed that deceptive kamsan through your deceptive activities! You should consume milk from my bosoms.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kanjan …** –  \[monster who pervaded\] the deceptive wheel was sent by kamsan, who had been rankling \[from the time of your birth\], in order to hurt you. Since the wheel, which was kept as a protective entity, was pervaded by the monster, it is referred to as *kaḷḷaccagadu* (deceptive wheel).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kamsan has been waiting since the incarnation of kriṣṇa, in order to destroy him. If he comes to know “He \[kriṣṇa\] is growing up in tiruvāyppādi”, with the thought of killing in his mind, he will not let go of the opportunity. He would consider in his mind “This person is apt for this task”. With such deceptive thoughts in his mind, he had instructed śakatāsuran to harm kriṣṇa. The deception in the case of śakata was larger than the case with pūtanā \[another monster sent by kamsan, earlier\] since śakata pervaded a wheel \[which was meant as a protective entity for kriṣṇa\].

**kalakkaḻiya …** – just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 6-9-4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/06/thiruvaimozhi-6-9-4-thalarndhum-murindhum/) “*taḷarndum muṟindum sagada asurar udal vēṟāgap piḷandu vīya*” (the body of the monster śakatan was broken into two and destroyed such that it broke up into smithereens), the wheel was destroyed beyond recognition.

**panji …**– I was frightened that the divine feet, which were soft, like cotton, which kicked the wheel, would have got hurt.

**amarar kōvē** – Oh, one who is the controller of celestial entities! It is their fortune that they are getting rid of their enemies through you. It is implied that no harm came kriṣṇa’s way.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa escaped due to the fortune of celestial entities \[only if he escapes every time could he carry out similar tasks for them again and again\]. Alternatively, it could refer to the auspicious time when kriṣṇa incarnated such that those who came to him with enmity in their minds would perish. Even if āḻvār sees such activities which were supposed to remove his fear, he would still get frightened.

**āyar kūttattu aḷavu anrālō** – My fear was not similar to the fear felt by the assembly of herd-folk. Syllables such as *Al, O* etc are sounds which express the anxiety of the mind.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here – āḻvār is concerned as to how he was going to bring up kriṣṇa \[in the pathos of yaśōdāp pirātti\] with his fear being much higher than that of the five-lakh herd-folk. Seeing his worry, kriṣṇa tells him “Haven’t you seen how we destroyed kamsan?” āḻvār says “ḍidn’t kamsan suffer due to the sin of carrying out deceptive deeds against you?”

**kanjanai …** – Oh, one who destroyed kamsan through your deceptive deeds such that he could not escape with the deceptive deeds which he had indulged in.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār saying “*kanjanai nī valaipopaduttāy*” was only a pretext. On that day, it was due to my good fortune that you escaped. Alternatively, he consoles himself saying “I breathed comfortably after seeing you imprisoning kamsan through deception and killing him”. With that, āḻvār asks kriṣṇa to come and consume milk from bosoms.

**mulai uṇāyē** – you should now consume the milk from my bosoms.

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.
