## 2.2.5. Tiyabundik kanjan

*tīya bundik kanjan unmēl sinam udaiyan sōrvu pārttumāyam tannāl valaippadukkil vāḻa killēn vāsudēvā!tāyar vāyc col karumam kaṇḍāy sāṟṟic connēn pōga vēṇḍāāyar pādikku aṇi viḷakkē! amarndu vandu en mulai uṇāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāsudēvā! – oh, the son of vasudēvar!; tīya bundi – one who has wicked reasoning; kanjan – kamsan; un mēl – on you; sinam udaiyan – is having anger; sōrvu pārttu – when you are roaming around, alone; māyam tannāl – through deceptive deed; valaip padukkil – if he catches you (such that you cannot escape); vāḻa killēn – (subsequently) I will not live; tāyar – mothers’; vāy sol – spoken through their mouths; karumam kaṇḍāy – has to be necessarily followed by children; sāṟṟic connēn – I have said such that everyone will know clearly; pōga vēṇḍā – do not go alone, even if you desire to go for playing; āyar pādikku – for tiruvāyppādi; aṇi viḷakkē! – oh, one who is like an auspicious lamp!; amarndu vandu – fitting aptly, come and consume my milk

**Перевод:**

**Oh, the son of vasudēvar! kamsan, who has wicked intelligence, is angry with you. When you are alone, he will catch you such that you would not be able to escape from him. After that, I will not live. Words spoken by mothers have to be necessarily followed by children. I have said this such that everyone would know about it. Even if you have to go for playing, do not go alone. Oh, one who is like an auspicious lamp for tiruvāyppādi! Come and consume milk from my bosoms.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tīya bundik kanjan** – kamsan has a malignant attitude. He is a killer of children. Just as it has been mentioned in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5-3-1 “*makkaḷ aṟuvaraik kallidai mōda*” (hitting the six children born ahead of you against rock and destroying them), kamsan is a great sinner who had killed six children born before kriṣṇa by hitting their heads against rock.

For the verse **tīyabundi …**, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says: for innumerable births, due to carrying the effects of past deeds, due to friendship with people of poor conduct, due to listening to the counsel of wicked ministers, due to not listening to the wise words of minister akrūrar, not having a knowledge of his own, despite having been born in the clan of kings, due to not having the fortune of seeing emperumān until then, due to not going in the path of righteousness, which results in harming everyone, due to having stayed in his mother’s womb as a result of all these faults, āḻvār refers to kamsan as *tīyabunddik kanjan*. *tīya bundi* – being firm in following the path of destruction for self, due to his ego and possessiveness. Such a person, with all these characteristics, is having anger towards you, without any reason. He has as his followers, those who follow the path of wrongful methods, and who take bewildering forms \[such as animals, plants etc\]. kamsan lets these followers to enter places where you go alone. If you get caught in their net of deception, I \[referring to yaśōdāp pirātti\] will not survive; I will perish. *sōrvu* – to go alone.

**un mēl sinam udaiyan** – Since he had heard the voice of an *aśarīri* \[one without any form\] that “the one conceived \[by dēvakip pirātti and vasudēvar\] on the eighth occasion is your enemy” and subsequently since durga \[the girl child who exchanged places with kriṣṇa\] had also confirmed it, kamsan thought “Our enemy has escaped from us and has entered a place where we cannot enter. We should somehow harm him” and was very angry towards you.

**sōrvu pārttu** – waiting for a time when you are without anyone to come with you, viz. when you are roaming alone.

**māyam tannāl valaip padukkil** – if he catches you by sending monstrous entities with deceptive forms such as animals or as botanical entities, in order to harm you, to places where you normally go to, in such a manner that you could not escape.

**vāḻa killēn** – I will be unable to live after that; I will perish.

**vāsudēvā** – even a gentle person such as vasudēvar had to undergo imprisonment because of you \[since the *aśarīri* said that the person conceived on the eighth occasion by dēvakip pirātti and vasudēvar would kill kamsan\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kamsan is harming gentle people such as vasudēvar on account of kriṣṇa. If they see you, will the monsters let loose by kamsan leave you harmlessly?

**tāyar …** – you should behave in line with the words of your mother. In other words, due to being apt and being spoken with affection, the words of a mother are to be necessarily followed.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: Earlier, āḻvār had referred to kriṣṇa as a lion cub, who had been sired by dēvakip pirātti. Now āḻvār says that he is the son of yaśōdāp pirātti. He cites a few *pramāṇams* (authentic texts) such as śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 58-31 “*pitrutvam nōpalakśayē*” \[lakśmaṇa tells minister sumantran to inform emperor daśarata that he does not consider daśarata as his father\], [perumāḷ tirumoḻi 7.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/08/perumal-thirumozhi-7-3/) “*undaiyāvan enṟuraippa*” (when asked as to who was his father, kriṣṇa pointed out to nandagōpar) and “*nandagōpan maindan*” (the son of nandagōpar), to show that kriṣṇa indicated subtly as to who his father was. Just as kriṣṇa had listened to the words of dēvakip pirātti on the day that he incarnated \[by hiding his divine weapons, crown, four hands etc\], āḻvār tells kriṣṇa that he should listen to his words too \[in the pathos of yaśōdāp pirātti\]. I had mentioned these on several occasions, for many people to know \[instead of saying them in secret\]. He tells kriṣṇa not to venture alone, even if it is for playing with friends.

**sāṟṟic connēn pōga vēṇḍā** – these words were not mentioned in any secretive manner. I had said this openly such that everyone would know about it. Even for the purpose of playing with your friends, do not go alone.

**āyar pādikku aṇi viḷakkē** – Oh, one who is like an auspicious lamp for tiruvāyppādi! *aṇi* – beauty. Through this, it is emphasised that it is not only for her \[yaśōdāp pirātti\], but the entire tiruvāyppādi will be plunged into darkness if anything untoward happens to you \[kriṣṇa\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: āḻvār queries kriṣṇa whether harm would come only to āḻvār should anything untoward happen to kriṣṇa. Oh, one who shines with your auspicious qualities such as beauty etc such that you are the object of intense focus for those in this town, like an auspicious lamp! Is there such a lamp which does not require inducing it and which does not perish? In actual practice, such a lamp is present amidst the herd-folk. While guessing something requires that the particular object had to have been seen at some point of time \[in the past\], seeing in reality \[seeing the object right in front of one’s eyes\] does not require any guesswork. Thus, since kriṣṇa has been seen right in front of their eyes, by the herd-folk, with both conditions of no inducement and non-perishing being present in one divine form \[of kriṣṇa\], he is referred to as the *aṇiviḷakku* \[the beautiful lamp\] for tiruvāyppādi.

**amarndu —** – leaving aside your hastiness, come securely and consume this milk which has got secreted only for you.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that while kriṣṇa may scurry to one place or the other for his regular activities, when invited to consume milk from the bosoms, he should let go of all his hurriedness and come slowly, at normal pace. Now, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai raises a query as to what is bosom milk for āḻvār. It is the flow of knowledge which is admixed with devotion, which enables carrying out apt *mangaḷāśāsanam* at all places, at all times and in all situations. For emperumān who cultivates the crop of devotion, the sustenance, nurturing and enjoyment are all this devotion only, which has matured from knowledge.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.2.6. Minnanaiya nunnidaiyar

*minnanaiya nuṇṇidaiyār viri kuḻal mēl nuḻainda vaṇḍuinnisaikkum villibuttūr inidu amarndāy! unnaik kaṇḍārenna nōnbu nōṟṟāḷkolō ivanaippeṟṟa vayiṟu udaiyāḷennum vārttai eyduvitta irudikēsā! mulai uṇāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

min anaiya – like lightning; nuṇ – being subtle; idaiyār – women, who have waists; viri – spread out; kuḻal mēl – on their locks; nuḻainda – settled on, in order to imbibe honey; vaṇḍu – beetles; in isaikkum – singing sweet songs; villibuttūr – in śrī villibuttūr; inidu – with the divine mind fitting; amarndāy! – 0h, one who is residing!; unnaik kaṇḍār – those who saw you; ivanai – he, who is “distinguished from the world; peṟṟa vayiṟu udaiyāḷ – one, who has the stomach which gave birth to; enna nōnbu – what sort of penance (for getting this); nōṟṟāḷ kol O – she did”; ennum vārttai – words, spoken in praise; eyduvitta – one who made out for me; irudīkēsā! – oh, hriśīkēśa! Consume milk from my bosoms

**Перевод:**

**śrī villibuttūr is a place where beetles, for the purpose of imbibing honey and for singing, settle down on the spread-out locks of women who have slender waists, matching lightning. Oh, one, who is residing in such śrī villibuttūr, with your divine mind accepting! Oh, hriśīkēśa! You made out the words from people who, after seeing you, said “What penance did the one, who has the divine stomach which gave birth to him, who is distinguished in this world, carryout?” You should consume milk from my bosoms.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**min …** – those who have their waists which are slender, like lightning. Alternatively, those who have subtle waists \[it could not even be seen; one has to assume that it exists; it is that slender\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that lightning could, in a way, be compared to their waists. However, since the waists of these women are thinner than even lightning, the pāsuram refers to them as *nuṇṇidaiyār* \[those with slender waists\].

**viri kuḻal mēl nuḻainda vaṇḍu** – on the expansive locks, beetles have settled down in order to drink in the honey \[from the flowers which the women have donned on their locks\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *viri kuḻal* refers to locks which are long, expansive, dark, curled and shiny.

**innisaikkum …** – the beetles will sing, as an outlet for the pride of having imbibed honey. Oh, one who is dwelling in such śrī villibuttūr, fitting here more than in paramapadam \[śrī vaikuṇṭam\]! Since it is the divine abode where you show your divine face to even lowly people, your divine mind is fitting better here than in śrī vaikuṇṭam. In paramapadam, you manifest yourself only to those who have attained equivalence to you in eight divine qualities. However, it is only here that you are manifesting yourself to both the lowly people and the eminent nityasūris, who dwell in śrī vaikuṇṭam.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *vataperum kōyil udaiyān* \[the divine name of emperumān who has taken residence in śrī villibuttūr\] prefers to reside in śrī villibuttūr, in order to listen to the songs sung by the beetles, after drinking honey from flowers, donned on their locks by women in śrī villibuttūr. vēdams are considered as \[a\] being permanent, \[b\] being without any fault \[c\] giving out the meanings of its content, by themselves, without the need for any other text, \[d\] not having been written by people and \[e\] establishing only one truth, that emperumān is supreme. periyāḻvār established that carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam is the ultimate benefit of vēdams and came to be famously known as “*vēdap payan koḷḷa valla vittu cittan*” (vittucittan who knows the ultimate benefit of vēdams). Such periyāḻvār decided that while emperumān has distinguished divine names such as “*viṣṇu, vāsudēvan, nārāyaṇan*” as *vyāpaka mantrams* (the esoteric hymns in which emperumān is shown as all-pervading), which are different from the names of other entities, being the most distinguished, he should be identified as one who resided in śrī villibuttūr through the verse “*villibuttūr inidu amarndāy*”. This is the reason for *sākśātkāraparars* (those who have seen emperumān \[āḻvārs\]) to celebrate emperumān in divyadēśams, similar to *prāmāṇikars* (those who are experts in pramāṇams such as vēdams etc).

**unnaik kaṇḍār** – Unlike children in the world, you are distinguished from them in your divine form, your auspicious qualities and your amazing activities. Those who saw such a child like you would say “There are fortunate women who give birth to distinguished children; unlike those children, you are highly distinguished; what penance did one, who has the stomach which gave birth to this child, carry out?” Oh, one who brought out such appreciative words for me!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that people used to celebrate vyāsar that he was śukhatātam (the father of *sukhar*). Unlike the quality of devotion which people such as vēdavyāsa et al had, people became amazed at seeing yaśōdāp pirātti and celebrated her as having been fortunate to have given birth to kriṣṇa from her divine stomach. One, who brought out such fame for yaśōdāp pirātti.

**irudīkēsā** – Oh, one who has the distinction of controlling the senses of those who see you, by making them not to let their senses to go on to anyone else! Consume milk from my bosoms.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa is one who stole the hearts of everyone through his qualities of beauty etc such that the sensory organs of his beholders will not go towards other entities. He further explains the reason for usage of specific terms in the pāsuram. The term *idai* \[in *nuṇṇidai*\] refers to detachment from everything; the waist is becoming slender because the bosoms are growing large; viz. bosoms refer to devotion and hence, with deeper devotion towards emperumān, one’s detachment from other entities would gain; *virikuḻal* refers to ācārya \[spiritual teacher\] who, having a good heart, makes all those who surrender for different reasons to focus on one divine form \[of emperumān\]; *mēl nuḻainda vaṇḍu* refers to the *prapannan* (one who surrenders to emperumān), who has all these qualities; *innisai* refers to the ability of the *prapannan* to sing about the qualities of knowledge, devotion and detachment of ācāryan. Seeing and listening to all these refers to the supreme entity who is residing in *tirumāḷigai* \[the divine mansion, which is emperumān’s divine abode\] in śrī villibuttūr.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.2.7. Pendir valvar

*peṇḍir vāḻvār ninnoppāraip peṟudum ennum āsaiyālēkaṇḍavargaḷ pōkku oḻindār kaṇ iṇaiyāl kalakka nōkkivaṇḍu ulām pūnguḻalinār un vāy amudam uṇṇa vēṇḍikoṇḍu pōvān vandu ninṟār gōvindā! nī mulai uṇāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

peṇḍir – being wives to their respective husband; vāḻvār – living like this; kaṇḍavargaḷ – those who saw you; nin oppārai – sons, who are like you; peṟudum ennum – of giving birth to; āsaiyālē – with the desire; pōkku oḻindār – remained, without moving further; vaṇḍu ulām – with beetles settling down; pū – decorated by flowers; kuḻalinār – those, having locks; kaṇ iṇaiyāl – with their eyes; kalakka nōkki – looking at the overall beauty of your divine form; un vāy amudam – the nectar from your divine mouth; uṇṇa vēṇḍi – desiring to drink that; koṇḍu pōvān – in order to take you; vandu ninṟār – they came (Hence); gōvindā! – oh, kaṇṇa, who is simple to approach for everyone! You should consume milk from the bosoms

**Перевод:**

**Women, who are wives to their respective husband, living in order to give birth to sons like you, remained, without moving further. With beetles settling down on flowers with which they have decorated themselves, looking at the overall beauty of your divine form, and in order to drink the nectar which is coming from your mouth, they came in order to take you with them. Oh, kaṇṇa, who is the simplest entity to approach for everyone! You should consume milk from my bosoms.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**peṇḍir …**– women, who are wives to their respective husband, who saw you, could not move on further, desiring to give birth to sons like you.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says here that women, who are desirous of giving birth to children, lose out their minds to you, after seeing you. Thinking “We are not able to give birth to a son like him. Is this possible for us?”, they are unable to engage with any other work.

**vaṇḍulām pūm kuḻalinār kaṇ iṇaiyāl kalakka nōkki** – just like people standing at the shore instead of getting into the gutsy wind, beetles were roaming over the honey which was flowing heavily from flowers with which women have decorated themselves. Such women were looking at the overall beauty of your divine form. *kalakka nōkkudal* refers to looking at the overall beauty of the divine form instead of focussing at the beauty of each limb. Earlier, through the term *peṇḍir vāḻvār*, the pāsuram mentioned about women, who were wives to their respective husband, and who looked at you with the desire of giving birth to sons who are like you. Here, through the term *vaṇḍulām pūnguḻalinār*, it refers to young women, waiting to enjoy the pleasures.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that there are other young girls, with locks decorated with garlands, in which beetles would immerse themselves, who stood looking at you with all their affection, looking at your overall beauty with their eyes, standing in order to take you with them and drink the nectar flowing from your divine mouth. You too appeared to be focussed on going with them.

**un …** – they came in order to take you with them and to drink the nectar flowing from your divine mouth.

**gōvindā** – Oh, one who is the easiest to approach for all! This \[your refusing to go with them\] is not appropriate for your easy approacability.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that since you \[referring to kriṣṇa\] are gōvinda, you have to go with those young girls. āḻvār tells him that before he goes with them, he should consume milk from the bosoms and then go.

**nī mulai uṇāyē** – let that be their wish. You should consume milk from my bosoms.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.2.8. Irumalai pol

*iru malai pōl edirnda mallar iruvarangam eri seydāy! untirumalindu tigaḻ mārvu tēkka vandu en algul ēṟioru mulaiyai vāy maduttu oru mulaiyai nerudikkoṇḍuiru mulaiyum muṟai muṟaiyā ēngi ēngi irundu uṇāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

iraṇḍu malai pōl – similar to two mountains; edirnda – opposed, in order to wrestle; mallar iruvar – two wrestlers, cāṇūra and muśtika; angam – forms; eri seydāy! – oh, one who made them to be burnt by the fire of fear; un – your; tiru malindu – overflowing with beauty; tigaḻ – being radiant; mārvu – divine chest; tēkka – to be filled up, by milk from bosoms; vandu en algul ēṟi – coming and getting onto my lap; oru mulaiyai – one bosom; vāy maduttu – keeping inside your divine mouth; oru mulaiyai – the other bosom; nerudikkoṇḍu – holding with the divine hand and twisting; iraṇḍu mulaiyum – both the bosoms; muṟai muṟaiyā – alternately; ēngi ēngi irundu – taking rest, now and then; uṇāy – you should consume

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who burnt down the two wrestlers, cāṇūra and muśtika, who appeared like mountains, through the fire of their fear of you! You should consume milk such that your divine, radiant chest is filled up with milk, by coming and getting up onto my lap, keeping your mouth on one bosom while twirling the other bosom with the other divine hand, and consuming milk from both bosoms alternately, taking rest in between, now and then.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**irumalai …** – due to the eminence of their forms and their firmness, the two wrestlers, cāṇura and muśtika, looked like two mountains. Oh, one who burnt down their bodies through the fire of their fear \[of you\]!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, says in his svāpadēśam that āḻvār is referring to the two monsters, madu and kaitaba, who went to *tiruppāṟkadal* \[milky ocean\] in order to harm emperumān and who were burnt down by *tiruvanantāḻvān* (ādiśēśan) such that their forms were destroyed beyond recognition. Alternatively, this would refer to the two wrestlers arranged by kamsan to harm you but who were burnt down due to the fire of their fear about you.

**un …**– your divine chest, which is very beautiful and radiant. *malidal* – excessive. Alternatively, the term *tiru* could be considered as referring to pirātti \[śrī mahālakśmi\] and due to her presence, your divine chest is radiant.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the phrase could be *un tiru malindu tigaḻ mārvu tērkka vandu en algul ēri* \[instead of *tēkka vandu …*\]. He says that *malidal* refers to emperumān’s divine chest which is radiant, being identified by periya pirātti \[śrī mahālakśmi\] who is referred to as *sarva bhūtānām īsvari* \[controller of all the creations\], being distinct from everyone starting with the controller of village level to the lord of all the universes which are covered under the expansive area of 50 crore miles and those who are in nitya vibhūti. *tērkka* refers to the identity provided by such periya pirāttiyār, due to which your divine chest is radiant. He is *śriya:pati*, because of her. *malidal* – abundance; *tērkkai* – identity. Alternatively, if the text were *tēkka vandu en algul ēṟi*, it would refer to consuming milk from my bosom such that it fills up to the level of your divine chest.

**tēkka** – to stagnate. To be filled-up with bosom-milk.

**vandu en algul ēṟi** – getting up onto my lap.

**oru mulai …** – keeping one bosom in your divine mouth and twirling the other bosom between your fingers, you should consume milk from both bosoms, taking rest now and then, due to excessive flow of milk from the bosoms.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār is telling kriṣṇa that he should twist his body in between, while consuming the milk from bosoms. He should sit on the lap and consume milk.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.2.9. Angamalap podagattil

*angamalap pōdagattil aṇi koḷ muttam sindināṟpōlsengamala mugam viyarppat tīmai seydu im muṟṟattūdēangamellām puḻudi aḷaiya vēṇḍā amma! vimmaangamararkku amudu aḷitta amarar kōvē! mulai uṇāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

amma! – oh, lord!; am – beautiful; kamalap pōdu agattil – inside a lotus flower; aṇi koḷ – having beauty; muttam – pearls; sindināl pōl – as if scattered; sem kamalam – like a reddish lotus; mugam – face; viyarppa – budding with little drops of perspiration; im muṟṟattūdē – standing inside this courtyard; tīmai seydu – carrying out misciefs; angam ellām – throughout the divine form; puḻudi āga – to be with dirt; aḷaiya vēṇḍā – do not mingle with dirt; vimma angu – during the time when they were sorrowful due to \[sage\] durvāsa’s curse; amararkku – for the celestial entities; amudu aḷitta – one who churned nectar and gave them; amarar kōvē! – oh, one who is the head of all celestial entities! Consume milk

**Перевод:**

**Oh lord! Just like pearls appear scattered on a beautiful lotus flower, little droplets of perspiration are showing up on your beautiful face, when you play with dirt inside this courtyard and carry out misciefs. Do not play with dirt. Oh, the head of all the celestial entities, who churned and gave nectar to the celestial entities during the time when they were in agony due to the curse of sage durvāsa! You should consume milk.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that āḻvār desires that kriṣṇa, with perspiration due to the tiredness of playing in dirt, should come and consume milk.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**angamalam …** – in a lotus flower which is beautiful due to its colour, fragrance, freshness and blossomed nature.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that beetles have drunk honey from inside the blossomed, beautiful lotus and the excess honey has got splattered over the lotus petals. Similar to that, on the divine face of kriṣṇa, which is like a reddish lotus, drops of perspiration have formed. Alternatively, *angamalam* would refer to beautiful water. *am* – beautiful; *kamalam* – water. On that beautiful water, reddish lotus has blossomed. Similar to pearls which have got scattered on that lotus, droplets of perspiration have formed on kriṣṇa’s face, which looks like a reddish lotus.

**pōdu** – flower

**agam** – inside

**aṇi** – just as pearls, which are beautiful with beauty and simplicity, have got scattered

**sengalam …** – on the divine face, which is like a reddish, blossomed lotus flower, droplets of perspiration have formed

**tīmai …** – do not remain inside this courtyard and play with dirt such that your divine form is full of dirt

**amma** – refers to kriṣṇa being the lord. Alternatively, refers to amazement induced by his activities.

**vimma …** – celestial entities, under the curse of sage durvāsa, were harassed by monsters. Looking for a medicine to live forever, to overcome their ills, they came to you. Oh, one who gave them nectar such that their stomachs were filled up, and who became their controller!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *vimma* refers to being full.

**mulai uṇāyē** – just as you had fulfilled their \[celestial entities’\] desire then, you should fulfil my desire and consume milk from my bosoms

We shall next consider the 10<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.2.10. Odavodak kinkinigal

*ōda ōdak kiṇkiṇigaḷ olikkum ōsaip pāṇiyālēpādip pādi varuginṟāyaip paṟpanāban enṟu irundēnādi ādi asaindu asaindu ittu adanukkēṟṟa kūttai ādiōdi ōdip pōyvidādē uttamā! nī mulai uṇāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uttamā! – oh, puruśōttamā (the most eminent among all the souls)!; ōda ōda – even as you run in a flurry; kiṇkiṇigaḷ – anklets on the divine feet; olikkum – making a sound; ōsai – the sound; pāṇiyālē – due to that noise; pādip pādi – singing constantly; adanukkēṟṟa – appropriate to those songs; kūttai – dance; asaindu asaindu ittu – swaying in a grand manner; ādi ādi – dancing; varuginṟāyai – you, coming towards me; paṟpanāban enṟu – saying “īsn’t he padmanābhan!”; irundēn – I was amazed (hence); ōdi ōdip pōy vidādē – instead of running away, you should consume milk

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who is the most eminent among all the souls! With your anklets, worn on the divine feet, making a noise, you are singing, and dancing, swaying from side to side, appropriate to that singing, while you are running in a flurry, typical of your childhood. When you come towards me like that, I was amazed thinking “īsn’t he padmanābhan!” Instead of running away from me, you should consume milk.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**ōda ōda …** – Instead of walking softly, with a pride typical of childhood, as you run in an excited manner, with the anklets on the divine feet making a sound.

**pādip pādi – adanukkēṟṟa kūttai asaindu asaindu ittu – ādi** – through your gait, swaying from left to right, dancing in line with the song. He is mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 10-1-6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/10/thiruvaimozhi-10-1-6-kuththan-kovalan/) as “*kūttan kōvalan*” (one who walks beautifully like an expert dancer and who protects those who need protection), one who walks as if he is an expert dancer. Thus, when he comes in a flurry, the sounds from the anklets would appear like a song and his gait would appear like a dance. Alternatively, considering the noise made by the anklets as the base notes for music, kriṣṇa would sing himself and dance to that song, by swaying from side to side.

**varuginṟāyaip paṟpanāban enṟu irundēn** – while you were coming towards me in this manner, looking at the divine navel on your form, as mentioned in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 11-2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/10/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-11-2/) “*koppūḻil eḻu kamalap pūvahagar*” (the beautiful entity who has the lotus flower springing out of his beautiful divine navel), would your divine navel not appear like an ornament such that there was no necessity for any other decoration for your divine form! Does he require any other singing and dancing? yaśōdāp pirātti was in amazement, thinking “How do the sound of the anklet and the beauty of the gait appear like singing and dancing!” She was thinking “īsn’t the one, who creates from destruction, coming towards me, to make me exist!” \[implying that by consuming her milk, he would make her exist\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār says “*paṟpanāban enṟu irundēn*” recalling his earlier pāsuram 1.6.5 “*paṟpanābā cappāṇi*”. āḻvār had thought of kriṣṇa’s eminence of being the cause for the creation of universe. āḻvār said “Instead of manifesting the simplicity of your childhood in line with your incarnation as a human being, is it required to manifest this eminence? Come to me” upon hearing which, he started running away from āḻvār.

**ōdi ōdi …** – Instead of comprehending the meaning of her utterances, kriṣṇa thought “Instead of speaking about my simplicity, she is talking about my eminence which is reflective of my independence” and started running away from her. She tells him not to run away from her like this whereby she would not be able to reach him. Since he is *puruśōttaman* \[most eminent among all the souls\], she tells him that in line with his quality of *āśrita pāratantryam* \[dependence on followers\], he should come under her control and consume her bosom milk.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār tells kriṣṇa “Do not run away. āren’t you *uttaman* \[most eminent among all\]? Come and consume my bosom milk”. The quality of being *puruśōttaman* is to manifest his *āśrita pāratantryam*. Through this, it appears that just as it has been said in taittirīya upaniśat ānandavalli *apprāpya manasā saha* \[emperumān is beyond one’s words and mind\], kriṣṇa would run away from āḻvār, who is the best among those who follow vēdams. The pāsuram should be read as *ōsaik kiṇkiṇigaḷ ōda ōda ādi ādi olikkum pāṇiyālē pādip pādi adanukkēṟṟa kūttai asaindau asaindu ittu ādi ādi varuginṟāyai, paṟpanāban enṟu irundēn, ōdi ōdip pōy vidādē uttamā* in order to get the sequential meaning.

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.2.11. Varaninda kongai

*vār aṇinda kongai ācci mādavā uṇṇenṟa māṟṟamnīr aṇinda kuvaḷai vāsam nigaḻa nāṟum villibuttūrpār aṇinda tol pugaḻān battar pirān pādal vallārsīr aṇinda sengaṇ māl mēl senṟa sindai peṟuvar tāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vār aṇinda – decorated by bodice; kongai – having bosoms; ācci – yaśōdāp pirātti, the mother; mādavā! – “Oh, one who is śrīya:pati! \[consort of śrī mahālakśmi\]; uṇ – consume milk”; enṟa māṟṟam – the words mentioned by her; nīr aṇinda – blossomed, as a decoration for waters; kuvaḷai – red water-lily flower’s; vāsam – fragrance; nigaḻa – without interruption; nāṟum – emitting fragrance; villibuttūr – as controller of śrī villibuttūr; pār – throughout the world; aṇinda – spread; tol – having as nature; pugaḻān – having fame; battar pirān – mercifully composed by periyāḻvār, the most eminent among brāhmaṇas; pādal – pāsurams; vallār tām – those who are capable of reciting; sīr aṇinda – being decorated with groups of qualities; sem kaṇ – having reddish eyes; māl mēl – in matters concerning emperumān, who is infatuated with his followers; senṟa sindai – mind, going towards; peṟuvar – will have

**Перевод:**

**yaśōdāp pirātti, having bosoms decorated with bodice, told kriṣṇa “Oh, śrīya:pati! You should consume milk”. periyāḻvār, who is the most eminent among brāhmaṇas, who is the controller of śrī villibuttūr, which has the uninterrupted fragrance of red water-lilies which are a decoration for the waters there, and who has a fame which has spread throughout the world, had composed those words \[of yaśōdāp pirātti\] into pāsurams. Those who are capable of reciting these pāsurams will have a mind which will go towards emperumān, who has reddish eyes and who is infatuated with his followers**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) āḻvār brings the tirumoḻi to its end by mentioning the benefit which will accrue to those who recite the pāsurams in this tirumoḻi.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vār …** – just like servants of kings tie the favourite materials of kings, seal them and carry with them wherever the kings go, yaśōdāp pirātti has tied her bosoms, which are kriṣṇa’s favourite, with bodice, keeping them safely. Hence, āḻvār appreciatively says that yaśōdāp pirātti has bosoms which have been decorated with bodice.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that regal service has to be shown in a situation where there is love towards son \[such a son has to be treated like a king\]

**mādavā uṇ enṟa māṟṟam** – Since he is *śrīyapati* (consort of śrī mahālakśmi), he is without any unfulfilled desire. However, to align himself with the species in which he has incarnated, she is asking kriṣṇa to come and consume milk.

**nīr …** – controller of śrī villibuttūr, which shines with the uninterrupted fragrance from red lilies, which are a decorative feature for the waters there.

**pār …**– Apart from śrīvallabhan (the pāṇḍiya king) who is the most eminent among all the kings in the world, and selva nambi, who is the most eminent among all the wise people in the world, periyāḻvār is celebrated by all the people in the world due to his fame which is an innate quality for his soul and not one which came in-between. Those who are capable of reciting the pāsurams composed by such periyāḻvār, who is the most eminent among brāhmaṇas.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that periyāḻvār has the eminence of being a *mangaḷāśāsanaparar* for a long time. *battar pirān* refers to his being the benefactor for brāhmaṇas, who speak only the truth all the times and who are eminent. *pādal vallār* – even if they do no not have āḻvār’s pathos or his relationship with emperumān, if people merely recite the words composed by him…

**sīr …** – emperumān has noble qualities which are a decoration for him; he has reddish eyes, which are the predominant among all his limbs. He is infatuated with his followers, enabling them to enjoy these. In matters related to such emperumān… Alternatively,

**sīr …** – being decorated with the quality of being dependent on his followers, having reddish eyes which shine due to his eminence and simplicity and being superior to everyone else. In matters related to such emperumān…

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *sīr* refers to *āśrita pāratantryam* (being infatuated with his followers). *sem kaṇ* is an identity for his being the lord of both leelā vibhūti (materialistic realm) and nitya vibhūti (spiritualistic realm).

**senṟa …** – those who are capable of reciting these pāsurams will have their minds going towards emperumān, uninterruptedly.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that through red lilies which are constantly with abundant water, āḻvār refers to the noble hearts \[people\] who are constantly carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam and through the term *nigaḻa nārum* he refers to their eminence on account of that.

We shall next consider the pravēśam of the next tirumoḻi.

## 2.3.1. Poyppadu udaiya

*pōyppādu udaiya nin tandaiyum tāḻttān poru tiṟal kanjan kadiyankāppārum illai kadal vaṇṇā! unnait taniyē pōy engum tiridipēyppāl mulai uṇḍa pittanē! kēsava nambī! unnaik kādu kuttaāyppālar peṇḍugaḷ ellārum vandār adaikkāy tirutti nān vaittēn*

**Пословный перевод:**

pādu udaiya – having affection towards protecting his people; nin tandaiyum – your father too; pōy – going for grazing cows; tāḻttān – delayed in returning; poru – to wage a war; tiṟal – having the strength; kanjan – kamsan; kadiyan – remained as being cruel towards you; kadal vaṇṇā – oh, one who has the invigorating complexion like an ocean!; unnai – you; kāppārum – capable of protecting; illai – none (here); taniyē – without anyone accompanying; engum pōy – going everywhere; tiridi – are roaming, as you please; pēy – pūtanā’s; mulai pāl – bosom milk; uṇḍa – consumed; pittanē – oh, one who is loony!; kēsava! – oh, one who killed \[monster\] kēśi!; nambī! – oh, one who is an expert in misciefs!; unnaik kādu kutta – to pierce your ears; āy – in āyppādi; pālar – children; peṇḍugaḷ – herd-women; ellārum – all these persons; vandār – have come; adaikkāy – areca nut etc; nān tirutti vaittēn – I have kept ready

**Перевод:**

**Your father, who has affection towards protecting his people, has gone to graze the cows and has delayed in returning home. kamsan, who has strength in engaging in war, is cruel towards you. Oh, one who has the invigorating complexion of an ocean! There is none to protect you. On the other hand, you are roaming as you please, alone. Oh, one who is like a loony person, who consumed milk from the bosoms of monster pūtanā! Oh, one who killed the monster kēśi! In order to attend the function of piercing your ears, children and herd-women have come to our house. I have kept ready materials such as areca nut etc, in order to honour them.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**pōyp pādudaiya nin tandaiyum tāḻttān** – your father, who is engaged with protection of you and his people in his heart, had said “I would go behind the cows, to graze them. You look after our son”. He has delayed in returning home. Alternatively, the term *pōy* would also refer to being in excess; thus, your father is deeply \[excessively\] thinking about protection of those to be protected. Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruppāvai 1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2014/12/thiruppavai-01-margazhi-thingal/) “*kūrvēl kodum toḻilan*” (nandagōpar would wield a sharp spear in his hand in order to protect infant kriṣṇa), right from the day when you were born, he would wield the radiant spear and would attack an ant which was crawling below your cradle as if it were a lion. Such nandagōpar, who had gone out on an errand, has not returned.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa tells āḻvār \[who is with the pathos of yaśōdāp pirātti\] that he wants to go before nandagōpar arrives. Since kriṣṇa said that, āḻvār tells him about kamsan.

**poru tiṟal kanjan kadiyan** – kamsan, who is strong in waging a war, is cruel towards you. Since you are roaming around, in order to harm you at suitable places, I do not know as to “Who he would send and what he would do”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kamsan had become arrogant since he had won over indra et al. Hence, he would be very cruel towards you.

**kāppārum illai** – There is none who knows the appropriate means in order to protect you \[from kamsan’s cruel plans\]. The one who is expected to protect you \[nandagōpar\] has not returned; I am a lady without any strength. Who will protect you?

**kadal vaṇṇā** – Just as it has been mentioned in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3-1-1 “*tannēr āyiram piḷḷaigaḷ*” (kriṣṇa would go around with a thousand children who were like him), do not think “I will roam around like the other children in this place. Will they \[those sent by kamsan\] know as to who I am, among those children?” Will your divine form, which is invigorating like the ocean, not reveal you to them? The implied meaning is that there is none who would be able to protect kriṣṇa, knowing these nuances. Even if there is no enemy, you, for whom mangaḷāśāsanam has to be carried out due to misplaced sense of fear, there is none to protect you here which is teeming with enemies.

**taniyē pōy engum tiridi** – you are wandering alone in all the places, such that we cannot even think that you are safe with other children. What is the benefit even if you go along with other children?

**pēyppāl mulai uṇḍa pittanē** – aren’t you the bewildered one, who drank milk from a fiend who came in the form of a mother, thinking her to be your real mother? The meaning conveyed here is that if the monstrous entities come in the form of one of his friends, he would mingle with such entities and play with them \[thinking of them as his real friends\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when kriṣṇa tells āḻvār that he would play along with the children in tiruvāyppādi, āḻvār tells him that kriṣṇa doesn’t know the difference between the fiend pūtanā’s bosoms and real milk. How then would he be able to distinguish between his real friends and the monsters who come in the form of his friends? He further tells kriṣṇa “Ever since you had consumed pūtanā’s milk, your intelligence has dullened a bit. Hence, you may mistake the monsters for your friends and play with them”.

**kēsava nambī…** – when kriṣṇa manifested the completeness of his valour, saying “For what are your frightened like this? Am I not *kēśava nambi*? Have you not heard about how kēśi suffered at my hands?” yaśōdāp pirātti left that subject and focussed again on the subject that she had initially broached upon. She tells him “It is not only me. In order to witness the function of piercing your ears, all the children and ladies from tiruvāyppādi have come. In order to honour the visitors, I have kept ready materials such as areca nut, betel leaves etc. You have to come now so that your ears could be pierced”.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.3.2. Vannap pavalam

*vaṇṇap pavaḷam marunginil sātti malarp pādak kiṇkiṇi ārppanaṇṇit toḻuvar sindai piriyāda nārāyaṇā! ingē vārāyeṇṇaṟku aṟiya pirānē! tiriyai eriyāmē kādukku iduvankaṇṇukku nanṟum aḻagum udaiya kanagak kadippum ivaiyā*

**Пословный перевод:**

naṇṇi – approaching you; toḻum avar – those who worship; sindai – remaining in their minds; piriyāda – without separating; nārāyaṇā! – oh, nārāyaṇa!; vaṇṇam – having good complexion; pavaḷam – coral cord; marunginil – on the divine waist; sātti – donning; malar – like lotus flower; pādam – adorning the divine feet; kiṇkiṇi – anklet; ārppa – to make a sound; ingē – to the place where I am calling you; vārāy – you should mercifully come; eṇṇaṟku – even to think “emperumān is like this”; ariya – remaining as unapproachable \[for those who are inimical towards you\]; pirānē! – oh, one who is the benefactor!; kādukku – for your ears; tiriyai – \[cotton\] thread; eriyāmē – without causing pain; iduvan – I will apply; kaṇṇukku – to behold; nanṟum – to a great extent; aḻagu udaiya – being beautiful; kanagam – made of only gold; kadippu ivai – these ear ornaments; A – are amazing (implying that you should see these)

**Перевод:**

**Oh, nārāyaṇa, who remains in the minds of those who approach and worship you, without ever separating! You should mercifully come to this place where I am calling you, with the coral chain, which has a beautiful complexion, donned on your divine waist and the anklet, on your divine feet which are like lotus flowers, making a sound. Oh, the benefactor, who could not be even thought of as “He is like this” by those who are not favourable to you! I will apply the cotton thread to \[the holes on\] your divine ears, without causing any pain to you. These ear ornaments, made of pure gold, are amazing to look at.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vaṇṇam …** – having formed in its place \[ocean\], the corals have a beautiful complexion. Donning a chain of those corals on his divine waist such that the corals gain beauty.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the corals are without any fault.

**malar …** – with the anklets, adorning the divine lotus-like feet, making a sound. The implied meaning here is that he should come with the beauty of the divine waist together with the coral chain, along with the sound made by the anklets donning the divine feet.

**naṇṇi …** – without moving away from you due to ego etc, with the absence of such ego, approaching you, and vorśipping you as their pastime on account of their servitude. Oh, nārāyaṇa, who resides in the hearts of such followers without ever leaving, as mentioned in [periya tiruvandādi 35](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/11/periya-thiruvandhadhi-35/) “*ninṟum irundum kidandum tiri tandum*” (standing, sitting, reclining and walking (in various divine abodes in order to attain me))! Come to this place, where I am calling you.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that those who approach emperumān do so out of affection for him as well as due to their belief that attaining emperumān is good for them. *naṇṇugai* (approaching) refers to going to him until attaining his divine feet \[attaining mōkśam\]. emperumān remains forever in the hearts of those who are like this. āḻvār’s meaning for nārāyaṇa is only this \[nārāyaṇa would refer to one who is the abode for everyone / everything and who treats everyone / everything as his abode; in other words, all-pervading entity. For such an entity, there is no scope for going or coming from one place to another, as he is present everywhere\]. In śāstrams, there is no question of going or coming, no question of attainment, none of emperumān coming within us and none of our controlling him. It is valid only in mangaḷāśāsanam and āḻvār’s pāsurams.

**eṇṇaṟku ariya pirānē** – Oh, one who is the benefactor, who is difficult even to think of for those who are not affectionate towards you! For those who are fully engaged with carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam, being easy to approach for those who attain and being difficult to even think of for those who do not attain, this is considered as their benefit. When kriṣṇa asks her whether she is calling out in order to apply the cotton thread to his ears, she says …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that emperumān will not be attained by those who think that for each of their efforts, there will be benefits and with their own efforts, they will be able to reach emperumān. āḻvār considers that emperumān remaining in the hearts of those who are favourable to him and being beyond the thoughts of those who are unfavourable to him, are both his benefits.

**tiriyai eriyāmē kādukku iduvan** – I will apply the cotton thread carefully, without making it painful for your ears.

**kaṇṇukku …** – If the holes in the ears are made bigger by inserting the cotton thread, then I will adorn your ears with these golden ear rings which are beautiful to look at. Through the words “*nanṟum aḻagum udaiya*” and “*kanagak kadippu*”, the handiwork in making the ornament and the material with which the ornament has been made, have been indicated.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *kanagam* refers to gold and *A* (as in *ivaiyā*) refers to celebration.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.3.3. Vaiyam ellam

*vaiyam ellām peṟum vār kadal vāḻum magarak kuḻai koṇḍu vaittēnveyyavē kādil tiriyai iduvan nī vēṇḍiyadu ellām taruvanuyya ivvāyar kulattinil tōnṟiya oṇ sudar āyar koḻundē!maiyanmai seydu iḷa āycciyar uḷḷattu mādavanē! ingē vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

uyya – to enable everyone to get uplifted; ivvāyar kulattinil – in this cow-herd clan; tōnṟiya – one who incarnated; oṇ sudar – having huge splendour; āyar – for herd-folk; koḻundē – oh, one who became the lord!; vaiyam ellām – throughout the earth; peṟum – having a value which will get earth; vār kadal – in the expansive ocean; vāḻum – inhabiting; magaram – like crocodiles; kuḻai – ear rings; koṇḍu vaittēn – I brought; kādil – in the ears; tiriyai – cotton thread; veyyavē – a little bit warm; iduvan – I will apply; nī vēṇḍiyadu ellām – all the eatables such as appam, vadai, fruits etc, which you desire; taruvan – I will give; iḷa āycciyar – cow-herd girls; maiyanmai seydu – making them to be infatuated, through your divine form; uḷḷattu – one who remains forever in their hearts; mādavanē – oh, one who is the consort of śrī mahālakśmi! Come here

**Перевод:**

**I have brought invaluable crocodile-shaped ear rings with which one could buy all the things on earth. I will apply the cotton thread when it is a bit warm, so that it will go in easily. I will provide you with whatever eatables etc which you desire. Oh, one who is highly splendorous and who incarnated in this clan of covherds, to uplift them and who became their leader subsequently! Oh, one who is the consort of śrī mahālakśmi, who made the covherd girls to become infatuated with you and who lives in their hearts forever! You should come here.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār says that it is not only golden ear ornaments, he has kept crocodile-shaped ear-rings too, which are of high value, for kriṣṇa, if he allows the holes in the ears to be made bigger.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vaiyam …** – yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa “It is not only the golden ear rings. I have also kept ear rings which look like crocodiles living in the vast ocean, with which the entire earth could be bought; they are that expensive”. kriṣṇa asks her “āren’t you saying this in order to apply the cotton thread to my ears? Even as you apply the cotton thread, my ears will pain. I do not want that”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *vār kadal* refers to the length, surrounding nature and fullness of water.

**veyyavē kādil tiriyai iduvan** – even when she tells him that she will apply the cotton thread with a little bit of warmth such that the pain in the ears will be reduced, he does not agree. To make him agree, she tells him…

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the long syllable *E* (as in *veyyavē*) should be transposed to *veyyat tiriyaiyē* \[warm cotton thread only\]. If the text had been *meyyavē* \[instead of *veyyavē*\], it would refer to kriṣṇa accosting her “You would show something and apply something else” to which yaśōdāp pirātti would respond, saying “You would see that my words bear only truth”

**nī vēṇḍiyadu ellām taruvan** – I will give you the eatables which you like such as *māśā bhūpam* (vadai), *gudā bhūpam* (appam), fruits etc. Since he did not come even after this, she tells him …

**uyya ivvāyar kulattinil tōnṟiya oṇ sudar āyar koḻundē** – you incarnated in this clan of cow herds such that we, who too were born in this clan, could get uplifted, making that to be the reason for your splendorous radiance. Oh, one who became the leader of this clan subsequently, since your face would wither away if anyone in the clan became sad, just like the tender leaf would start withering if anything happens to the root!

**maiyanmai seydu iḷa āycciyar uḷḷattu mādavanē** – You made the young girls in the covherd clan to become infatuated with you, due to your qualities of beauty etc. You remained in their hearts forever. Oh, one who became dear to pirātti (śrī mahālakśmi) who stole your heart!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that while kriṣṇa makes the girls in the herd-clan to think constantly about him, śrī mahālakśmi, who stays in his heart all the time, makes him to think of her constantly.

**ingu vārāy** – She calls him, by praising him.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.3.4. Vana nanrudaiya

*vaṇa nanṟudaiya vayirak kadippu ittu vār kādu tāḻap perukkiguṇa nanṟu udaiyar ikkōpāla piḷḷaigaḷ gōvindā! nī solluk koḷḷāyiṇai nanṟu aḻagiya ikkadippu ittāl iniya palāp paḻam tandusuṇa nanṟu aṇi mulai uṇṇatt taruvan nān sōttam pirān! ingē vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

nanṟu – good; va(N)Nam udaiya – having complexion; vayirak kadippu – diamond ear-rings; ittu – donning; vār kādu – long ears; tāḻa – to come down to the shoulders; perukki – nurturing (the ears); ikkōpāla piḷḷaigaḷ – these covherd boys; nanṟu guṇam udaiyar – (listening to the words of their mothers et al) remain with good qualities; gōvindā! – oh, one who is easy to approach!; nī – you, desiring to join with those boys; sollu – my words; koḷḷāy – are not listening to; iṇai – matching each other; nanṟu aḻagiya – being beautiful; ik kadippu – these ear-rings; ittāl – if you wear; iniya – being tasteful for you; palāp paḻam – jack fruit; tandu – giving; suṇa(ngu)m – having light-coloured spots; nanṟu aṇi – being very beautiful; mulai – bosom; uṇṇa – for you to consume; nān taruvan – l will offer; pirān! – oh, one who is the benefactor!; sōttam – I am vorśipping you. Come here

**Перевод:**

**These herd-boys are wearing diamond ear rings, which have a good complexion, such that their long ears come down to their shoulders. They listen to their mothers and have good qualities. Oh, one who is easy to approach! You desire to join with these herd-boys, but you aren’t listening to my words. If you don these two ear-rings which match each other in their beauty, I will give you sweet jack fruit which you like, as well as my beautiful bosoms which have light-coloured spots, to consume milk from. Oh, one who is the benefactor! I am vorśipping you. Come here.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār tells kriṣṇa that covherd boys, who are of his age, are roaming around, after increasing the size of the holes in their ears.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vaṇam …** – Despite praying to him like this, since kriṣṇa did not come, yaśōdāp pirātti wonders “Will he come if I tell him these?” She tells him that these cow-herd boys are wearing diamond ear-rings, which have a good complexion, such that their long ears come down to their shoulders. They listen to their mothers et al and remain with good qualities. Should you too not be like them?

**gōvindā! nī solluk koḷḷāy** – you, having the name *gōvinda* in order to reflect your easy approacability, are not listening to my words. kriṣṇa asks her “If I wear these ear rings listening to your words, what will you give me?”

**iṇai nanṟu aḻagiya ikkadippu ittāl** – If you wear these ear-rings, which match each other in their beauty and appear beautiful …

**iniya palāp paḻam tandu** – I will give you jack fruit, which you like

**suṇa nanṟu aṇi mulai uṇṇat taruvan nān** – I will give you my beautiful bosoms, which have light spots on them, for you to consume milk from. *suṇangu* – the light-coloured spots which appear over the bosoms. *nanṟu* – remaining soft; *aṇi* – distinction, due to the location.

**sōttam pirān ingē vārāy** – Since he did not come, despite telling him all these, yaśōdāp pirātti now tells him “Oh, pirān! I am offering you anjali \[cupping the palms together\] with my hands. You should come now”. The term *sōttam* refers to the word mentioned by those who, to express their lowly state, make an *anjali* with their hands and bow down.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa remains as a simple person and as a great benefactor to those who perform the act of vorśipping.

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.3.5. Sottam piran

*sōttam pirān! enṟu irandālum koḷḷāy suri kuḻalārodu nī pōykōttuk kuravai piṇaindu ingu vandāl guṇam koṇḍu iduvanō nambī!pērttum periyana appam taruvan pirānē! tiriyida ottilvēyt tadam tōḷār virumbu karum kuḻal vittuvē! nī ingē vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

pirān! – “Oh, one who is the benefactor!; sōttam enṟu – I worship you” saying this; irandālum – even if prayed; koḷḷāy – you are not accepting that; nambī! – oh, one who is an expert in indulging in misciefs!; nī – you; suri kuḻalārodu pōy – going with girls who have curly locks; kōttu – joining with their hands; kuravai piṇaindu – if you carry out the dance of kuravai (kuravai is a type of dance where kriṣṇa appears between two herd-girls and dances with them; it is also called as rāsakrīdai); ingu vandāl – if you come here; guṇam koṇḍu iduvanō – would I accept that as a good quality?; pirānē! – oh, one who is the benefactor!; tiri ida ottil – if you allow me to apply the cotton thread to your ears; pērttum – subsequently; periyana – being large; appam – appams \[a sweet dish made with jaggery and wheat flour\]; taruvan – l will give; vēy – like bamboo; tada – being huge; tōḷār – girls who have shoulders; virumbu – such that they desire; karu – being dark; kuḻal – having locks; vittuvē! – oh, viṣṇu! You should come

**Перевод:**

**Even if I prayed to you saying “Oh, the benefactor, I worship you”, you are not accepting that. Oh, one who is indulging in misciefs! If you come here, after joining hands with herd-girls who have curly hair, and perform kuravai dance with them, will I accept that as a good quality? Oh, the benefactor! If you allow me to apply the cotton thread to your ears, I will subsequently give you huge appams. Oh, viṣṇu, who has dark locks desired by girls who have huge, bamboo-like shoulders! You should come here.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**sōttam …** – Since he did not come, even after she had called out to him saying “*sōttambirān ingē vārāy*” \[as seen towards the end of 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram\], yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa “Oh, my benefactor! Even when I pray to you telling you that I am vorśipping you, you are not coming”. He responds saying “When I came near you, upon hearing you calling out to me, didn’t you beat me yesterday, instead of praising my good quality?” She tells him “Oh, are you talking about that one?”

**suri kuḻalārōdu nī pōy kōttuk kuravai piṇanindu ingu vandāl guṇam koṇḍu iduvanō nambī** – “When you return here after going to uninhabited places with girls who have curly locks, joining hands with them and indulging in the dance *kuravai*, will I consider that as a good quality, instead of finding fault with you?” Upon hearing this, he did not have a proper answer. ūtilising that as an opportunity, when yaśōdāp pirātti tried to apply the cotton thread to his ears, he refused.

**pirānē! tiriyida ottil – pērttum periyana appam taruvan** – “Oh, one who is the benefactor to me in all manner! If you allow me to apply this little bit of cotton thread, I will give you bigger and bigger appams, even if you keep rejecting them saying that they are small”. Since he did not come, even after that…

**vēy …** – you have dark, lengthy locks which are desired much by the herd-girls who have big shoulders which appear like bamboo, in terms of their freshness and roundedness. Oh, viṣṇu! You should come here.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that yaśōdāp pirātti is calling kriṣṇa by his distinguished name of viṣṇu, and attempts to apply the thread. She calls kēśavan as viṣṇu. Since she had addressed him as *kēśava* in the first pāsuram, recalling that, she is calling him as *viṣṇu*. Due to his curly locks, she is recalling his abundant locks now.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.3.6. Vinnellam ketka

*viṇṇellām kētka aḻudittāy! un vāyil virumbi adanai nān nōkkimaṇṇellām kaṇḍu en manattuḷḷē anji madusūdanē enṟu irundēnpuṇṇēdum illai un kādu maṟiyum poṟuttu iṟaippōdu iru nambī!kaṇṇā! en kārmugilē! kadal vaṇṇā! kāvalanē! mulai uṇāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

viṇṇellām – throughout the sky; kētka – to hear; aḻudittāy! – oh, one who cried!; un – your; vāyil – in the mouth; virumbi – desiring (“let us see if there is any sign of having eaten sand”); adanai – that; nān nōkki – even as I saw; maṇ ellām – all the earth; kaṇḍu – seeing, inside your divine stomach; en manattuḷḷē – inside my heart; anji – fearing (thinking “We beat him thinking that he is our son”); madusūdanē enṟu – thinking “He is none other than the lord of all who had annihilated madu”; aṟindēn – I knew; puṇ ēdum illai – there is no abscess; un kādu – your ear; maṟiyum – will get twisted; iṟaippōdu – a little bit of time; poṟuttiru – bear; nambī – oh, one who is complete!; kaṇṇā – oh, my kaṇṇan!; en – for me; kār mugilē – one who is magnanimous, like the monsoon cloud!; kadal vaṇṇā – oh, one who has the complexion of the ocean!; kāvalanē – oh, one who is my protector! Consume milk

**Перевод:**

**When I beat you \[after hearing from various people that you had eaten sand\], asking you to open your mouth, you cried in such a manner that your cry was heard all over the sky. When I desired to see if there is any trace of sand in your mouth, I saw the entire earth inside your divine stomach. I was frightened in my mind that you are not my son, but the lord of all, who had annihilated the monster madu. There is no abscess in your ear. It would get twisted. Bear with me for a moment. Oh, one who is complete with all the auspicious qualities! Oh, one who is easy to approach! Oh, one who is magnanimous towards me like the dark cloud! Oh, one who is my protector! You should consume milk.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that yaśōdāp pirātti is calling viṣṇu as “madusūdanan”*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**viṇ …** – when I \[yaśōdāp pirātti\] beat you, saying “You had eaten sand”, you opened your mouth crying out “*Ah*”. The cry reverberated throughout the expansive sky. Even as you cried, I wanted to see “If there is any sign of sand in your mouth”. When I saw the entire earth inside your mouth, I was frightened in my mind thinking “We had hurt him thinking that he is our son”. I thought “He is not our son. He is *sarvēśvaran* (the lord of all)”. Since kriṣṇa is of the type as said in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5-13-13 “*ahamvō bāndavō jāta*:” (I have been born as your relative), he was unable to tolerate her words which made him feel that he is alien to their clan. To make her forget that, he came near her such that she could hug him. When she tried to insert the cotton thread into the hole in his ears, he said “My ears will get hurt and form an abscess. I do not need that”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti thinks that if she saw any remnants of sand in his mouth, she would brand him. When he said that he had not eaten sand, she wanted to see his mouth. Though he had desirously eaten sand, he said that he had not eaten. When he opened his mouth, she looked at his mouth and tongue keenly. When she saw the worlds in his mouth, she became fearful in her mind thinking that she had mistaken him for her son while he was the lord of all. Since kriṣṇa didn’t want to be isolated, he made her forget all these, just as it has been said in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1-1-7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/06/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-1-1-7/) “*āyar puttiran allan; arum deyvam*” (he is not the son of a cow-herd person; he is emperumān, the difficult-to-see supreme entity).

**puṇṇēdum illai** – “There will be no abscess. Your ear will get twisted \[If I don’t apply the thread\]. Oh, one who is complete with all auspicious qualities! Bear with me for a moment”. Since he was patient, she became joyous.

**kaṇṇā** – Oh, one who is easy to approach, for me!

**en kār mugilē** – Oh, one who is a benefactor for me, by being like a monsoon cloud which pours out water irrespective of whether it is sea or land!

**kadal vaṇṇā** – Oh, one who has the complexion of an ocean, which is enjoyable for me!

**kāvalanē** – Oh, one who is my protector! Praising him in all these ways, she desires that he should consume milk.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār says through the verse *kāvalanē* that kriṣṇa is his protector, after becoming protected by āḻvār.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.3.7. Mulaiyedum venden

*mulai ēdum vēṇḍēn enṟu ōdi nin kādil kadippaip paṟittu eṟindu ittumalaiyai eduttu magiḻndu kal māri kāttup pasu nirai mēyttāysilai onṟu iṟuttāy! tirivikkiramā! tiruvāyarpādip pirānē!talai nilāp pōdē un kādaip perukkādē vittittēn kuṟṟamē anṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mulai – “the bosom which you offer; ēdum – and other eatables; vēṇḍēn – I do not desire”; enṟu ōdi – saying this, getting out of my hand; nin – your; kādil – applied to your ears; kadippai – ornament; paṟittu eṟindu vittu – plucked it out and threw it (and after that, when indran, out of his anger due to his hunger, made rains to come down heavily); malaiyai – gōvardana hill; eduttu – lifted as an umbrella; magiḻndu – feeling happy, without showing any sign of tiredness; kal māri – from that hailstorm; kāttu – protecting the cow-herd people and the cows; pasu nirai – herd of cows; mēyttāy! – oh, one who made the herd-people to graze them!; onṟu – unique; silai – rudra danus (bow, once used by rudra) which was used as a stake during sītāp; iṟuttāy! – oh, one who broke it!; tirivikkiramā! – oh, one who mercifully measured the worlds, by stretching your divine feet!; tiru āyarpādi – for the people in śrī gōkulam; pirānē! – oh, one who is the lord!; talai – head; nilā – not stable; pōdu – at a young stage; un kādai – your ears; perukkādu – without piercing the holes; vittittēn – my not having done; kuṟṟam anṟē – is it not a fault?

**Перевод:**

**Saying “I do not desire the bosom and other eatables which you are offering”, you plucked out the ear ornaments and threw them away. When indran, due to his anger of having been denied food, forced rain to wreak havoc, you lifted the gōvardana hill like an umbrella and protected the cow-herd folks and the cows from the hailstorm, becoming joyous, without showing any sign of ennui. Oh, one who enabled the cow-herd folks to graze the herds of cows! Oh, one who broke the unique rudra’s bow which was kept as a wager for winning sītāp pirātti during her marriage! Oh, one who measured the worlds by lengthening your divine feet! Oh, one who is the lord of the people in śrī gōkulam! Is it not my mistake that I had not pierced the holes in your ears even at the stage when you were young with your head not being stable?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**mulai …** – even as yaśōdāp pirātti praised kriṣṇa, asking him to consume milk \[as seen in the previous pāsuram\], kriṣṇa started consuming milk. When she tried to adorn his ears with ear rings, he became furious.

**muiai ēdum vēṇḍēn enṟu** – saying “I do not want your bosom or the other eatables such as appam, vadai etc”

**ōdi** – slipping out of my hand and running such that I would not be able to catch you. When I ran behind you, to make me feel terrible

**nin kādil kadippaip paṟittu eṟindu ittu** – plucking out the ear rings which I had adorned on your ears and throwing them down, in front of me. During that time, indran, out of his anger of having been denied food, started a hailstorm to punish the herd-people. In order to ensure that they were not harmed …

**malai eduttu** – lifting the gōvardana hill itself, which kriṣṇa had earlier referred to as the protector, as an umbrella.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that kriṣṇa, while running away from yaśōdāp pirātti after throwing down his ear-rings, said “Am I not the protector? Would I remain silently when those who are to be protected suffer?”

**magiḻndu** – without showing any sign of tiredness due to lifting the mountain, feeling happy that “We have been able to protect those who were to be protected”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa lifted the gōvardana hill, feeling happy “We got hold of a good mountain”. He further quotes an incident which happened during the time of bhattar \[son of kūrattāḻvān and one of our preceptors\]. bhattar would say that kriṣṇa lifted a stone \[mountain\] since it was raining stones \[hailstorm\]. Had it been raining water, he would, perhaps, have lifted the ocean itself.

**kal māri kāttu** – protecting them such that not a drop of water fell either on any of the cow-herd people or on any of the cows

**pasu nirai mēyttāy** – just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 7-4-10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/thiruvaimozhi-7-4-10-mey-nirai/) “*ina ānirai pādi angē odunga*” (such that the herds of cows and cow-herd people in śrī gōkulam took shelter), oh, one who made the cow-herd people to graze their cows by making the mountain cover all the areas where the cows would graze!

**silai onṟu iṟuttāy** – the unique bow, belonging to rudra, was kept as the wager for marrying sītāp pirātti. Oh, one who snapped that bow, which could not be moved or lifted by anyone!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that this \[breaking the bow\] could refer to maturā \[when kamsan had invited kriṣṇa to the ritual of bows, with the intention of killing him\] or it could refer to mitilā \[where śrī rāma snapped the bow\]

**tirivikkiramā** – Oh, one who measured all the worlds in order to redeem the land lost by indra, just like those who walk along the boundaries of their land, to proclaim possession!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that emperumān, as trivikrama, removed the *anyaśēśatvam* \[being servitor to deities other than emperumān\] and *svasvātantryam* \[being dependent on oneself and not on emperumān\] when he kept his divine feet on all the people in samsāram.

**tiru āyarpādip pirānē** – Oh, one is the benefactor in all manner for the people who live in śrī gōkulam! Thinking “Just like you fulfil the desires of everyone by being their benefactor, you should fulfil my desire too”, when yaśōdāp pirātti attempted to put back the ear rings, which he had thrown earlier, he refused to listen to her.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār calls kriṣṇa as tiruvāyarpādip pirān since he acted as their benefactor by protecting them from the hailstorm.

**talai nilā …** – yaśōdāp pirātti says “I should have done this when you were still young, with your head still not being stable enough; it was my mistake. There is no sense in finding fault with you”, blaming herself for this.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that she blames herself for not piercing his ears before he put his head up and started arguing with her for everything.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.3.8. En kurrame

*en kuṟṟamē enṟu sollavum vēṇḍā kāṇ ennai nān maṇ uṇḍēnāgaanbuṟṟu nōkki adittum pidittum anaivarkkum kāttiṟṟilaiyēvan puṟṟu aravin pagaikkodi vāmana nambī! un kādugaḷ tūrumtunbuṟṟana ellām tīrppāy! pirānē! tiriyittuc collugēn meyyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en kuṟṟam enṟu – “It is my fault”; sollavum vēṇḍā kāṇ – there is no need for you to say this; see this; nān maṇ uṇḍēnāga – thinking that I have eaten sand; anbuṟṟu – having affection; nōkki – seeing if there were any trace of having eaten sand, in my mouth; ennai pidittum – holding me, as if traces had been seen; adittum – beating me; anaivarkkum – to all the people; kāttiṟṟilaiyē – have you not shown “Look at the way he has eaten sand” (when kriṣṇa said all these); van puṟṟu aravin – of the snake which is hiding inside a strong anthill; pagai – garuda, who is the enemy; kodi – having that as the flag; vāmana nambī! – oh, one who went as a bachelor with a dwarf form and who became; un kādugaḷ – your ears; tūrum – \[the holes in them\] will get blocked; uṟṟana – endured by your followers; tunbu ellām – all the sufferings; tīrppāy! – oh, one who removes!; pirānē – oh, one who is the benefactor!; tiri ittu mey sollugēn – let me speak only the truth, after applying the cotton thread to your ears; When the text is tiri ittuc cellugēn meyyē \[instead of sollugēn meyyē\], the meaning would be – let me go about my task, after applying the cotton thread to your ears

**Перевод:**

**\[kriṣṇa tells yaśōdāp pirātti\] There is no need for you to say “It is all my fault”. Have you not looked inside my mouth to check for traces of sand, thinking that I have eaten sand, and shown that to all the people? yaśōdāp pirātti tells him “Oh, one who became complete after getting that which you had desired when you went as a bachelor with the form of a dwarf, carrying garuda, who is the enemy of snake hiding inside a strong anthill, as your flag! The holes in your ears will get blocked. Oh, one who removes the distress endured by your followers! Let me speak only the truth, after applying the cotton thread to your ears”**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**en kuṟṟam …** – kriṣṇa tells yaśōdāp pirātti “The reason for your telling dejectedly that it is your fault is because you feel that I am not doing that which you want me to do and that it is my fault. There is no need for you to say also ‘It is my fault’” When yaśōdāp pirātti asks him “Whose fault is it then?” kriṣṇa tells her “Is it not your fault?” yaśōdāp pirātti asks him, in turn “What did I do to you?”

**ennai nān maṇ uṇḍēnāga** – When I had not eaten sand, you had thought that I had eaten sand.

**anbuṟṟu nōkki** – looking at my mouth and hands in a friendly manner, to see if there were traces of sand.

**adittum pidittum anaivarkkum kāttiṟṟilaiyē** – did you not catch hold of me, as if you had seen trace of sand, not stopping with that, beat me too, and show to everyone “All of you, look at the way that he has eaten sand”?

**van puṟṟu aravin pagaikkodi vāmana nambī** – snake hides inside a strong anthill, fearing that if it goes out, it will be harmed. Having garuda, who is the enemy of such snakes, as the flag, oh, vāmana nambī, who measured and seized lands in a cruel manner and became prominent! Through this, it is implied that since emperumān is the one who has ādiśēśan as his mattress and garuda as his flag, he is capable of uniting entities which cannot be united anywhere else in the world and after carrying out unjustifiable acts, he would justify such acts too.

**un kādugaḷ tūrum** – \[yaśōdāp pirātti tells him\] if we keep debating like this, with each saying something and the other, saying something else, wasting time, your ears would get blocked, you would see that.

**tunbuṟṟana ellām tīrppāy piurānē** – when yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa “Oh, one who is the benefactor who removes all the sufferings of your followers!” kriṣṇa repartees “There is no need for you to praise me like this. You say one true word ‘Hereafter I will not catch you or beat you like before’ such that I will agree to have the cotton thread inserted in my ear”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that it is only when kriṣṇa allows yaśōdāp pirātti to insert the cotton thread in his ears would all her suffering get eliminated. She tells him “It is only if you allow me to insert the thread would I speak with you, who are presently without the completeness of your good qualities. īsn’t it only then that my suffering would get eliminated?”

**tiri ittuc collugēn meyyē** – she tells him that she would speak only the truth after inserting the cotton thread.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan
