## 2.3.9. Mey enru

*meyyenṟu solluvār sollaik karudit toduppuṇḍāy veṇṇeyai enṟukaiyaip pidittuk karai uralōdu ennaik kāṇavē kattiṟṟilaiyēseydana sollic cirittu angu irukkil sirīdarā! un kādu tūrumkaiyil tiriyai idugidāy inninṟa kārigaiyār siriyāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

solluvār – those who appear to say as if I had stolen butter; sollai – words; mey enṟu karudi – thinking that to be true; veṇṇeyai – butter; toduppu uṇḍāy enṟu – saying that you ate by stealing; kaiyaip pidittu – catching my hand; karai – having an edge; uralōdu – with a mortar; kāṇa – such that everyone could see; ennai – me, who had not stolen butter; kattiṟṟilaiyē – did you not tie? (when kriṣṇa said this); sirīdarā! – oh, śrīya:pati \[divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi\]!; seydana – whatever I had done like this; solli – speaking about that; sirittu – laughing; angu irukkil – if you remain there, delaying in coming to me; un kādu tūrum – your ears will get blocked (Hence); ninṟa – standing here; ikkārigaiyār – these girls; siriyāmē – such that they do not laugh, saying “Blunted ears; wasted ears”; kaiyil tiriyai – cotton thread, in my hand; idu kidāy – see that you wear it such that \[the holes in\] your ears grow larger

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa asks yaśōdāp pirātti “Did you not tie me down to a mortar, with a circumferential rim, to be seen by everyone, by believing the words of those who appear to say that I had stolen and eaten butter to be true, catching my hand, when I had not stolen butter?” yaśōdāp pirātti tells him “Oh, śrīya:pati! If you keep delaying coming to me, by speaking and laughing about what I had done, while being away from me, \[the holes in\] your ears will get blocked. See that you wear the cotton thread which is in my hand, such that the girls, who are here, do not make fun of you saying that your ears are blunted”**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**mey …** – When yaśōdāp pirātti said \[as in the previous pāsuram\] that she will speak only the truth, after inserting the cotton thread, kriṣṇa tells her “I do not have faith in your words. āren’t you the one who punishes me, listening to the words of others?” yaśōdāp pirātti asks him “Have I done like that?” to which kriṣṇa says *mey enṟu solluvār sollaik karudi* – believing the words of those who say “He had stolen and eaten butter”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai describes this, in his svāpadēśam, as a conversation between yaśōdāp pirātti and kriṣṇa.

yaśōdāp pirātti – I have heard from many people that you only have stolen.

kriṣṇa – Is what they say the truth?

yaśōdāp pirātti – What they say is not untruth; what you say is not the truth.

kriṣṇa – What did they say?

yaśōdāp pirātti – They said that you stole butter; I was wondering whether this is apt for you?

kriṣṇa – Did they see me stealing?

yaśōdāp pirātti – Yes, they said that they saw you stealing.

kriṣṇa – If they had seen me, śouldn’t they have caught me in the act and brought me to you?

yaśōdāp pirātti – Is it possible for them to catch you? Am I capable of catching you?

kriṣṇa – Did you remain without catching me? Without beating me? Did you not tie me, with all the people in the world, whether they are enemies or friends or the indifferent type, looking at me? Is it not for doing a similar act that you are looking for me?

yaśōdāp pirātti – Do not remind me of what I had done before.

kriṣṇa – Should I not say what you had done before?

**toduppuṇḍāy veṇṇeyai enṟu** – you were sustaining yourself on butter through stealing. t*hoduppu* – stealing.

**kaiyaip pidittu …** – “You held my hand and with everyone looking at me, tied me down to a heavy mortar which had a rim”, saying this, he smiled. *karai ural* refers to a mortar with a rim around its circumference.

**seydana …** – yaśōdāp pirātti tells him “If you keep telling my faults and smiling, wasting the time without coming to me”

**sirīdaranē** – \[the holes pierced in\] your ears will get blocked. You should come, at the least, for her \[śrī mahālakśmi’s\] sake. Despite that, since he did not come …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that however young he may be, without addressing him as *sirīdara*, he will not lend himself to be controlled.

**kaiyil tiriyai …** – these girls have the beauty which you desire, they have affection towards you and desire to be in your proximity, without leaving you. I shall insert the cotton thread to increase the hole in your ears so that these girls will not make fun of you saying “Your ears are blunted; they are wasted”.

We shall next consider the 10<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.3.10. Karigaiyarkkum

*kārigaiyārkkum unakkum iḻukkuṟṟu en? kādugaḷ vīngi eriyiltāriyādāgil talai nondidum enṟu vittittēn kuṟṟamē anṟēcēriyil piḷḷaigaḷ ellārum kādu perukkit tiriyavum kāṇḍiēr vidai seṟṟu iḷam kanṟu eṟinditta irudīkēsā! endan kaṇṇē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kādugaḷ – my ears; vīngi eriyil – if they swell and burn; kārigaiyārkkum – those girls who are laughing; unakkum – and for you, who had come to insert that thread; iḻukkuṟṟu en? – what is the damage? (when kriṣṇa said this); tāriyādu āgil – if you are unable to tolerate inserting the thread; talai nondidum enṟu – thinking that \[your\] head will get hurt; vittittēn – having not done it, when you were young; kuṟṟam anṟē – is it not a fault?; ēr vidai – the bull ‘ariśtanēmi’ which came opposing you; seṟṟu – killing it; iḷam kanṟu – monster who stood in the form of a young calf; eṟinditta – one who threw it on another monster who had taken the form of a wood-apple; irudīkēsā! – oh, hriśīkēśa!; en than kaṇṇē! – oh, one who is like my eyes!; cēriyil – in the herd-people’s village; piḷḷaigaḷ ellārum – all the children; kādu perukki – enlarging the holes in their ears, by inserting cotton threads; tiriyavum – as they roam around; kāṇḍi – you have seen

**Перевод:**

**\[kriṣṇa tells yaśōdāp pirātti\] How will it affect you and these girls who are laughing, if my ears swell and pain? yaśōdāp pirātti says “It was my fault that I had not done this when you were younger since I thought that you would be unable to bear the pain in your head if I had inserted the cotton thread then. Oh, hriśīkēśa, who had killed the monster who came in the form of a bull ‘ariśtanēmi’ when he came opposing! You threw the monster in the form of a calf on another monster, who had taken the form of a wood-apple, killing both. Oh, one who is like my eyes! You have seen all the children in this village, who are roaming around, after increasing the holes in their ears by inserting the thread”**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kārigai …** – kriṣṇa asked yaśōdāp pirātti “How does it affect these girls who are laughing and you, waiting to insert this thread in my ears when my ears swell and burn?” He went some distance away from her.

**tāriyādāgil …** – yaśōdāp pirātti blames herself, saying “I should have done this when you were much younger. Since your head would have pained if you were unable to tolerate the pain then, I had not done it. It was my fault”. Further, she says …

**cērilyil …** – “Don’t you see children of your age in the village, roaming around, inserting the cotton thread and enlarging the holes in their ears?” When kriṣṇa stood, appearing to agree to her inserting the thread in his ears …

**ēr vidai …** – just as it has been mentioned in periya tirumoḻi 10-7-13 “*vambaviḻ kānattu mālvidai*” (with the dark bulls in the forest which had fragrant breeze), you had killed the bull *ariśtanēmi* which came opposing you; you had thrown a monster who was in the form of a calf, in the grazing area, on another monster who was in the form of a wood-apple, killing both of them. Oh, one who has he divine name of *hriśīkēśa* since you control the senses of all those who behold you! Oh, one who is like my eyes!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that kriṣṇa had killed the monstrous bulls which came opposing him. Just as periyāḻvār had mentioned in his periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3-3-7 “*kanṟin uruvāgi mēy pulattē vanda kaḷḷa asurarai …*” (the deceptive monster who came in the form of a calf in the grazing field …), he had killed the monsters who came in the form of calf and wood-apple. *irudīkēsā* – Oh, one who controls the senses such that they do not engage with worldly pursuits, through your will and your beauty! Oh, one who is like my eyes! He says that for āḻvār, in all situations, kriṣṇa remains as his eyes.

We shall next consider the 11<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.3.11. Kannaik kulira

*kaṇṇaik kuḷirak kalandu engum nōkkik kadi kamaḻ pūnguḻalārgaḷeṇṇattuḷ enṟum irundu tittikkum perumānē! engaḷ amudē!uṇṇak kanigaḷ taruvan kadippu onṟum nōvāmē kādukku iduvanpaṇṇaik kiḻiyac cagadam udaittitta paṟpanābā! ingē vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

kadi kamaḻ – emitting fragrance; pū kuḻalārgaḷ – women having locks donned with flowers; kaṇ kuḷira – with their eyes to remain cool; kalandu engum nōkki – looking at the overall beauty of your divine limbs, while looking at each limb separately; eṇṇattuḷ – with the thought of uniting with you; enṟum irundu – fitting always; tittikkum – being enjoyable for them; perumānē! – oh, one who has the eminence!; engaḷ amudē! – oh, one who is like a nectar for us!; sagadam – śakatāsuran \[a monster\]; paṇṇaik kiḻiya udaittitta – kicked such that he was blown to smithereens; paṟpanābā! – oh, padmanābha!; uṇṇa – for you to eat; kanigaḷ taruvan – I will offer fruits; onṟum nōvāmē – not being even a little bit painful; kādukku – for your ears; kadippu iduvan – I will don ornaments; ingē vārāy – come here, accepting that

**Перевод:**

**Women, who have locks adorned with flowers emitting fragrance, will look at your overall beauty and think of uniting with you. Oh, one who has the eminence of being constantly in their thoughts, and who is enjoyable for them! Oh, one who is like nectar for us!  Oh, padmanābha, who kicked the monster śakatan such that he was blown to smithereens! I will offer you fruits and apply ornaments for your ears such that there is absolutely no pain. Accepting this, come here.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kaṇṇai …** – Since you \[kriṣṇa\] will look into the eyes of the young herd-girls,

**kaṇṇaik kuḷirak kalandu** – looking at them with your eyes in a cool manner, mingling with their eyes. This implies union of eyes.

**engum nōkki** – looking at the overall beauty of their forms

**kadikamaḻ pūnguḻalārgaḷ** – \[herd-girls having\] locks decorated completely with flowers emitting fragrance

**eṇṇattuḷ enṟum irundu tittikkum perumānē** – oh, the eminent one, residing in their hearts forever, enjoying them!

Alternatively, keeping the second case in *kaṇṇai* as dormant \[viz. treat the verse as *kaṇ kuḷirak kalandu*\], the meaning would be – the herd girls, who have decorated their locks with fragrant flowers, would look at you such that their eyes become cool; they would look at your overall beauty, recalling their union with you. Since you do not go beyond the thoughts of those who are affectionate towards you, you remain within their thoughts aptly, as their enjoyable entity. Oh, the eminent one, who is like this!

**engaḷ amudē** – Oh, one who is the most enjoyable entity for us and who is the reason for our existence! When yaśōdāp pirātti called him for enlarging the holes in his ears such that those who are affectionate towards him \[the cow-herd girls\] and those who worry about what would happen to you \[yaśōdāp pirātti and other herd-women\] would feel happy, he tells her “I will come; what would you give me?”

**uṇṇak kanigaḷ taruvan** – “I will offer you the fruits which you consume desirously”. He says “However, if you insert the thread, it would hurt my ears”

**kadippu onṟum nōvāmē kādukkiduvan** – when she tells him that she would apply the thread such that there is absolutely no pain in his ears, he appeared to agree to this.

**paṇṇai …** – she praises him saying “When I left you under the protection of a wheel, a monster had pervaded the wheel with the intention of harming you. Did you not kick that wheel such that it broke into smithereens! You should come here”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam – by kicking the monster śakatan, oh, one who had protected yourself, the cause for all the worlds! Oh, one who has the lotus in your divine navel! You should come here.

We shall next consider the 12<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.3.12. Vavenru solli

*vāvenṟū solli en kaiyaip pidittu valiyavē kādil kadippainōvattirukkil unakku ingu iḻukkuṟṟu en kādugaḷ nondidum killēnnāvaṟpaḻam koṇḍu vaittēn ivaiyāṇāy nambī! mun vanja magaḷaiccāvap pāluṇḍu sagadiṟap pāynditta dāmōdarā! ingē vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

vā enṟu solli – calling me “Come”; en kaiyai – my hand; pidittu – catching hold, fast; valiya – forcefully; kādil – in my ears; kadippai – ear-rings; nōva – to hurt; tirikkil – if you apply; unakku – for you; ingu – presently; iḻukkuṟṟu en – is there any loss?; kādugaḷ nondidum – my ears will hurt (hence); killēn – I will not (come); nambī! – oh, one who is complete!; nāval paḻam – blue berries (which you desire); koṇḍu vaittēn – I had brought and kept; ivai āṇāy – look at these; mun – earlier; vanja magaḷ – the deceptive fiend; sāva – such that she died; pāl uṇḍu – drinking milk from her bosom; sagadu – śakatam \[wheel\]; iṟa – to break into smithereens; pāynditta – one who jumped over him; dāmōdarā! – oh, dāmōdara! Come here

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa tells yaśōdāp pirātti “Catching hold of my hand, after asking me to come, if you forcefully apply the ear-rings in my ears and it hurts me, is there any loss for you? My ears will get hurt; hence, I will not come”. She tells him “Oh, one who is complete! I have brought and kept blue berries, which you like. Look at them. Earlier, you had killed the deceptive fiend by consuming milk from her bosom such that she died. You had jumped on the monster who had pervaded a wheel in such a manner that he broke into smithereens. Oh, dāmōdara! You should come here”**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vā …**– When yaśōdāppirātti called him “Oh, paṟpanābhā, come here!” \[as in the previous pāsuram\],

**vā enṟu solli en kaiyaip pidittu** – \[kriṣṇa tells her\] “you would call me to come near you and if I come near, you will catch hold of my hand firmly

**valiyavē kādil kadippai nōvattirukkil unakku ingu iḻukkuṟṟen** – If you forcefully apply the ear rings by twisting them in my ears, is there any loss for you?

**kādugaḷ nondidum killēn** – My ears will get hurt. I will not come”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that kriṣṇa tells her that these are your words. My ears will hurt. I will not come.

**nāval paḻam koṇḍu vaittēn ivai āṇāy nambī** – For you to come, I have kept blue berries, which you desire. Look at these. Seeing them, kriṣṇa stood as if he was inclined to come

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa that she has brought blue berries for both him and for nappinnaip pirātti \[who was to become his consort in later years\]. *nambī* – one who has become complete, by not having any expectation!

**mun …** – Earlier, hiding her fiendish form, pūtanā had come deceptively in the form of your mother. You consumed her milk such that her life ebbed out. When śakatāsuran \[a monster\] came pervading a wheel to harm you, you kicked him such that he was broken to smithereens. You protected yourself such that you did not fall in their hands. When you had such strength, you allowed to be caught by me at my hands as if you were powerless, and allowed me to tie you with a rope. āren’t you the one who had the simplicity to be tied down by me and attained the name of *dāmōdara* \[one who has the marks of a rope on your stomach\]! Come here.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that by killing pūtanā and śakatāsuran, kriṣṇa established his quality of supremacy and by remaining with the marks of the rope on his stomach, he established his quality of simplicity.

We shall next consider the  last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.3.13. Varkadu tala

*vārkādu tāḻap perukki magarak kuḻaiyida vēṇḍiseerāl asōdai tirumālaic conna sol sindaiyuḷ ninṟu tigaḻappārār tol pugaḻān puduvai mannan panniru nāmattāl sonnaārāda andādi panniraṇḍum vallār accudanukku adiyārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vār – being long, naturally; kādu – ear; tāḻa – to come down further; perukki – enlarging; amaittu – making it; magarak kuḻai – ear-rings in the shape of crocodile; ida vēṇḍi – desiring to apply; seerāl – with eminence; asōdai – yaśōdāp pirātti; tirumālai – consort of śrī mahālakśmi; sonna – mentioned; sol – words; sindaiyuḷ – in his divine mind; ninṟu – to remain forever; tigaḻa – radiantly; pār Ar – spread throughout the world; tol – natural; pugaḻān – having fame; puduvai – for śrī villibuttūr; mannan – periyāḻvār, who is the controller; pattu iraṇḍu nāmattāl – with the twelve divine names, starting with kēśava; sonna – mercifully mentioned; ārāda – that which could not be enjoyed to the full extent; andādi – andādi \[class of poems \[pāsurams\] where the last word / syllable of previous pāsuram becomes the first word / syllable of next pāsuram\]; pattu iraṇḍum – these twelve pāsurams; vallār – those who are capable of reciting; accudanukku – for the one who never lets slip his followers; adiyār – will become his confidential servitors

**Перевод:**

**yaśōdāp pirātti wanted to lengthen the naturally long ears of kriṣṇa by applying crocodile-shaped ear-rings. With the eminent words of that yaśōdāp pirātti shining in his divine mind forever, periyāḻvār, who is the controller of śrī villibuttūr, and who has natural fame throughout earth, composed twelve pāsurams with the divine names of emperumān, starting with kēśava, which could not be enjoyed to completion. Those who are capable of reciting these twelve pāsurams will become the esoteric servitors of emperumān, who doesn’t let slip his followers.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In this final pāsuram, āḻvār mentions the benefit to those who learn this decad and brings it to an end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vār …** – kriṣṇa’s ears were, by themselves, long. yaśōdāp pirātti desired to lengthen them further, by applying crocodile shaped ornaments on his ears, properly.

**seerāl …** – the words mentioned by yaśōdāp pirātti about *śrīya:pati* \[divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi\], without any shortcoming to his eminence.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that these words were spoken by yaśōdāp pirātti without any shortcoming in the eminence and without kriṣṇa getting angry.

**sindaiyuḷ ninṟu tigaḻa** – to shine forever in āḻvār’s divine mind.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that it is only in āḻvār’s divine mind that yaśōdāp pirātti’s words will remain forever, shining. For yaśōdāp pirātti, the attention will be equally divided between kriṣṇa and her regular chores while for āḻvār, being focussed only on kriṣṇa is his pastime.

**pār Ar …** – periyāḻvār, who is the controller of śrī villibuttūr and who had ancient fame such that he would remain completely, in the minds of all those who are on earth

**pannirunāmam …** – Those who are capable of reciting these twelve pāsurams with the pathos of āḻvār, which are enjoyable without any limit, mercifully composed with the twelve divine names of emperumān, which are the symbols of śrī vaiṣṇavam, and which could never be enjoyed fully by the followers of emperumān, to their complete satisfaction.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that even if followers were to enjoy these twelve pāsurams until the entity called as time remains, they will not get satisfied. This is just like emperumān himself who is ārāvamudan, the nectar who could never be enjoyed completely to one’s satisfaction.

**accudanukku adiyārē** – for the one who doesn’t ever let slip his followers, they will become servitors forever.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *accudan* refers to emperumān who does not slip from any of his distinguishing features.

We shall next consider the  pravēśam of next tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.4.1. Venney alainda

*veṇṇey aḷainda kuṇungum viḷaiyādu puḻudiyum koṇḍutiṇṇena ivvirā unnait tēyttuk kidakka nān ottēneṇṇeyp puḷippaḻam koṇḍu ingu ettanai pōdum irundēnnaṇṇal ariya pirānē! nāraṇā! nīrāda vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

veṇṇey aḷainda – resulting from wallowing in butter; kuṇungum – peculiar smell of butter; viḷaiyādu – resulting from playing; puḻudiyum – dirt too; koṇḍu – carrying these; ivvirā – tonight; unnai – you; tēyttu – rubbing your body on the mattress, due to itching; kidakka – to remain; nān – I, who am affectionate in matters related to you; tiṇṇena – certainly; ottēn – will not agree; eṇṇey – protective oil (to apply on your body); puḷip paḻam – protective tamarind, to remove that oil; koṇḍu – taking in the hand; ingu – in this place; ettanai pōdum – for a long time; irundēn – I have been standing; naṇṇal ariya – difficult to approach for anyone, with one’s effort; pirānē! – oh, one who is the benefactor!; nāraṇā! – oh, nārāyaṇa!; nīr Ada – to mercifully carry out bath; vārāy – you should mercifully come

**Перевод:**

**I will not certainly agree to your sleeping on the mattress tonight, rubbing your body on it, to remove the itching resulting from wallowing in butter, carrying its peculiar smell, and having dirt on your body, resulting from playing in it. I have been standing here for a long time, carrying oil, to apply on your body to remove that smell and dirt, and tamarind, to remove that oil. Oh, one who is difficult to attain by those with their efforts! Oh, one who is the benefactor! Oh, nārāyaṇa! You should mercifully come to carry out your bath.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**veṇṇey aḷainda kuṇungum** – while eating butter, due to his desire, just as it has been mentioned in [siṟiya tirumadal](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/category/iyarpa/siriya-thirumadal/) “*tārār tadandōḷgaḷ uḷḷaḷavum kai nītti*” (extending his hand such that the shoulders, with the garland on them, would touch the rim of the vessel containing butter), due to his childish ignorance, thinking that his stomach would get filled up till the level to which his hand would go inside the pot containing butter, kriṣṇa put out his divine hand into the pot containing butter fully. This is also similar to [perumāḷ tirumoḻi 7-8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/08/perumal-thirumozhi-7-8/) pāsuram “*muḻudum veṇṇey aḷaindu*” (wallowing in butter with his divine hand, reaching till the bottom of the pot).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that the terms *veṇṇey* and *puḻudi* refer to m*umukśus* \[those who are desirous of getting liberated from samsāram (materialistic realm) and in attaining mōkśam (spiritualistic realm)\] and *samsāris* \[those who are happy, residing in samsāram forever\] respectively; if that is so, can they be got rid of? \[in the pāsuram, yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa that he should have a bath to get rid of *veṇṇey* and *puḻudi*\]. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that *mumukśus* are those who have rejected any desire in *ahankāram* \[mistaking the physical body for ātmā and ensuring that the body’s desires are always met\] and in *mamakāram* \[possessiveness; considering consort, children, relatives, wealth and so on as one’s own and not belonging to emperumān\] which come about while in samsāram. They reject desire in *kaivalyam* too \[ātmā, after getting liberated from samsāram, crosses vrajā river and enjoys itself, instead of carrying out servitude to emperumān\]. This term \[mumukśus\] refers to those who are deeply engaged with *prapatti* \[surrendering themselves to emperumān\] and with *bhakti* \[choosing the path of devotion to attain emperumān\], even though the divine abodes of emperumān \[divyadēśams\] are present here. They consider emperumān and *bhāgavatas*, the followers of emperumān, as their possession. He further says that *samsāris* are those who take a pledge to enjoy all the pleasures in samsāram, and being *pāratantryars* \[those who are totally dedicated to such pleasures\] they are servitors of *indriyam* \[sensory organs\], saying that *this is mine*, *this is me*. Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 1-4-5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/07/thiruvaimozhi-1-4-5-nalgith-than/) “*poḻilēḻum tān nalgik kāttaḷikkum nāraṇan*” (emperumān, on his own, due to his exclusive relationship with everyone, protects everyone and fulfils their desires in all the worlds), emperumān fulfils the desires of all, irrespective of whether they are *mumukśus* or *samsāris.* emperumān desires *samsāris* more than *mumukśus* \[since it is tougher to correct them and make them engage with him\]. When such is the case, is it correct to say that *veṇṇey* and *puḻudi* \[viz. *mumukśus* and *samsāris*\] should be removed under the pretext of having a bath? tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai answers this himself saying that for periyāḻvār \[who has composed this pāsuram\], anyone who is not interested in praising emperumān through the path of *mangaḷāśāsanam* is apt to be removed. While āḻvār runs after kriṣṇa to make him take a bath in order to get rid of the smell of butter and all the dirt from his divine form, kriṣṇa tries to escape.

**viḷaiyādu puḻudiyum –** further, playing in dirt such that dirt also got stuck to butter on his divine form.

**koṇḍu** – with the peculiar smell of butter due to putting his divine hand in the pot containing butter and dirt which came about due to playing with dirt.

**tiṇṇena** – surely.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *tiṇṇam* refers to āḻvār’s pledge that without giving kriṣṇa a bath, in order to remove butter and dirt from his divine form, he will not remain quiet. It is also telling kriṣṇa “Why are you so certain that you will not have a bath? We should carry out what I have decided to do. I will get this done soon”. Unless your body is rubbed well, the itching will not stop. Unless itching stops, you will not be able sleep well. Hence, āḻvār tells kriṣṇa “Unless I rub these off your form, I will not remain quiet”

**ivvirā …** – I will not allow you to lie down in your bed, tonight, and to rub your divine form on the mattress due to itching.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *ivvirā* refers to samsāram \[*irā* refers to darkness; samsāram always creates ignorance in us; hence, *irā* is samsāram\]. For both the person who does not have any taste in it and for the person who has taste in it, it is only samsāram which creates ignorance. emperumān gives commonly to both, without any distinction. Could āḻvār fight with emperumān like this \[compelling him to have a bath\] and serve him? Yes, he could, since it is good for kriṣṇa \[to have a bath\] and it is expected to be done.

**tiṇṇena – ottēn** – Certainly, I will not allow you, like this. I will surely give you a bath.

When kriṣṇa asked her “Have you brought all the materials required to give me a bath?” she says…

**eṇṇey …**– I have brought oil which needs to be applied first on your divine form and also tamarind, to later remove the residual oil from your form. Have I not been waiting here for a long time?

**naṇṇal ariya pirānē** – Oh, one who is the benefactor, who is not attainable for anyone with one’s own efforts!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār tells kriṣṇa that he is a great benefactor since despite āḻvār calling him several times to come for a bath, kriṣṇa is not coming \[he will come on his own and not because he has been called\]. He tells kriṣṇa that he should not have this much of independence.

**nāraṇā** – This divine name is universally known for both his eminence and his simplicity \[eminence comes out of emperumān being the abode for all the other entities, both *cit* (those with thinking ability) and *acit* (those without thinking ability), while simplicity comes out of emperumān residing inside all entities, both *cit* and *acit*\]. For yaśōdāp pirātti, the target now is in his quality of simplicity.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa’s manifestation of *svātantryam* (being totally independent) is his most common quality. āḻvār hints that being obedient to his followers is a distinguishing feature in emperumān.

**nīrāda vārāy** – Even though I had told you that I will not allow you \[to go to bed like this, with butter and dirt on your divine form\] out of my affection for you, there is no use for all these materials which I have gathered for your divine bath. They will have a use only if you come. Hence, you should come for your bath,

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says at the end that *eṇṇey* is *prakruti darśanam* (seeing the nature of prakruti, the primordial matter which is composed of the five sensory features and three qualities of satva, rajas and tamas) and *puḷi* is *dēha darśanam* (seeing the nature of body which keeps changing constantly). It is only through seeing the nature of *prakruti* and *dēham* that the dirt \[of *samsāram*\] will get removed.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.4.2. Kanrugal oda

*kanṟugaḷ ōdac ceviyil katteṟumbu pidittittāltenṟik kedum āgil veṇṇey tiratti viḻungumā kāṇbanninṟa marāmaram sāyttāy! nī piṟanda tiruvōṇaminṟu nī nīrādavēṇḍum empirān! ōdādē vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

kanṟugaḷ – calves; ōda – to run in fear; seviyil – in their ears; katteṟumbu – large, black ant; pidittu ittāl – if you drop; tenṟi – helter-skelter, such that one \[calf\] does not go in the same direction as the other; kedum āgil – if they run (then, you); veṇṇey tiratti – scooping up butter; viḻungum A – the way in which you swallow; kāṇban – I will see (the meaning hinted is: I will not see, since the cows will not give milk if; ninṟa – standing close to one another; marāmaram – seven ebony trees; sāyttāy! – oh, one who snapped and felled!; inṟu – this day; nī piṟanda – the day that you incarnated; tiru ōnam – it is the śravaṇa nakśatram (Hence); nī nīr Ada vēṇḍum – you should mercifully undertake a bath; em pirān! – oh, my lord; ōdādē – without running (deceiving me); vārāy – you should mercifully come

**Перевод:**

**If you drop large black ants into the ears of calves, they will run helter-skelter in fear. Without calves, the cows won’t give milk and you will not be able to scoop and consume butter. Oh, one who snapped and felled seven ebony trees which were standing close to each other! Today is tiruvōṇam star, your birthday. You should mercifully have a bath. Oh, one who is my lord! Do not run. You should mercifully come for your bath.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) Despite yaśōdāp pirātti calling him, instead of responding to that, kriṣṇa was engaging with the playful activity of dropping large, black ants into the ears of calves to see them running helter-skelter, in fear. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār tells kriṣṇa that even if he doesn’t come when āḻvār calls him out, he should come for his bath, at the least, on his birthday.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kanṟu …** – if you drop large, black ants into the ears of calves such that the ants bite them hard to make it painful for them…

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār tells kriṣṇa: while there are a thousand herd-boys like you, instead of playing with them, would you play with calves?

**tenṟi …** – if they run helter-skelter, out of fear, such that one does not run in the direction of another and they get scattered in various directions …

**veṇṇey tiratti viḻungumā kāṇban** – I would be pleased to see you scooping up butter in your hands and consuming it. However, only if calves are present, would the cows allow milking. Only if they allow milking could milk be gathered. Only if milk is gathered could butter be prepared.  Now, you would see that your existence itself is in question \[kriṣṇa would not exist without consuming butter\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: You are one who could not remain without butter even for a moment. For you, the smell of butter on your divine form is the cause for your existence. We are waiting to see your existence, without even taking a bath.

**ninṟa marāmaram sāyttāy** – Oh, one who pierced seven ebony trees which were standing close those together and felled them in order to remove the doubt expressed by one follower \[sugrīvan, during śrī rāmāvatāram\]!

**nī piṟanda tiruvōṇam inṟu** – see, today is śravaṇa nakśatram, when you had incarnated. This refers to the nakśatram of viṣṇu as well as to the nakśatram of his other incarnations \[such as vāmana\], since all the incarnations have a commonality, having incarnated from śrīman nārāyaṇa.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that this \[statement that today is your birth-star, tiruvōṇam\] is not showing any doubt unlike āḻvār’s earlier pāsuram “*attattin pattā nāḷ*” (tenth day from the star of hastam) and is not uncommon too. Even though this star has been seen in other incarnations \[of śrīman nārāyaṇa\], āḻvār is not explicitly mentioning that \[to prevent kamsan from knowing the identification of kriṣṇa\].

**nī nīrāda vēṇḍum** – is there anyone who would not bathe on his/her birthday? yaśōdā tells him to have a bath today, while he tries to run away saying that he would not have a bath.

**empirān odādē vārāy** – Oh, one who is my lord! You should not run. Come and have a bath.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says at the end that the term *kanṟugaḷ* refers to those who do not have any interest in their self-protection \[they depend on emperumān for their protection\]. The term *katteṟumbu* refers to the distinct instructions which are full of *tamas* \[ignorance and laziness\] given which will hurt the ears when listened to. The term *tenṟik kedum* refers to those who, after listening to such instructions, slip from their previous position of being dependent on emperumān for their protection and engage in activities to protect themselves \[moving away from emperumān\].

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.4.3. Peycci mulai

*pēycci mulai uṇṇakkaṇḍu pinnaiyum nillādu en nenjamāycciyar ellārum kūdi aḻaikkavum nān mulai tandēnkāyccina nīrodu nelli kadārattil pūrittu vaittēnvāytta pugaḻ maṇi vaṇṇā! manjanamāda nī vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

pēycci – pūtanā \[a fiend\]; mulai – milk from bosom; uṇṇa – while you consumed such that she died; kaṇḍu pinnaiyum – even after seeing that; en nenjam – my heart; nillādu – unable to bear due to affection (towards you); āycciyar ellārum – all the herd-women; kūdi – together; aḻaikkavum – (Fearing “Don’t you know of the fact that he has consumed milk from pūtanā’s; mulai tandēn nān – I gave you milk from my bosom, without any fear; nelliyodu – along with gooseberry; kāyccina – warmed-up; nīr – water; pūrittu vaittēn – I filled up fully; vāytta pugaḻ – having great fame; maṇi vaṇṇā! – oh, kaṇṇa who has the complexion of a bluish gemstone!; manjanam Ada – come to have a bath (such that dirt etc would get removed)

**Перевод:**

**Even after seeing you consuming milk from the bosom of the fiend pūtanā, my heart, due to overflowing affection towards you, would not stop giving you milk from my bosom, though all the herd-women were afraid and called out to me \[not to give milk to you\]. I have filled up warm water, along with gooseberry, fully in the vessel. Oh, one who has great fame and who has the complexion of a bluish gemstone! You should come for a bath.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**pēycci …** – Just as it has been mentioned in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/07/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-1-3-10/) “*vanjanaiyāl vanda pēycci*” (pūtanā, the fiend, who came deceptively in the form of kriṣṇa’s mother, yaśōdāp pirātti), pūtanā had hidden her fiendish form and taken over my \[yaśōdāp pirātti’s\] form. Despite seeing the manner in which you were suckling her such that she perished …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says the following: Upon hearing the wailing sound from the fiend, pūtanā, as she was falling, and seeing the manner in which she was lying on the ground, all the herd-men and herd-women in tiruvāyppādi \[śrī gōkulam\] became frightened and called out to me \[yaśōdāp pirātti\], as I was going towards you \[kriṣṇa\],  drinking milk from the bosom of that fiend. Despite that, I, seeing the way you were drinking milk from her bosom, went ahead, separated you from the fiend and went to another place, thinking, with fear “This fiend may still get up from its dead state and follow this little child” and tested my own bosom \[to check if that too had any poison on it\]

**pinnaiyum nillādu en nenjam** – while I should have got frightened upon seeing this and run away from that place, my heart was unable to bear any distress for you, due to overflowing affection.

**āycciyar ellārum kūdi aḻaikkavum** – Seeing the way the fiend was lying dead and the way that you \[referring to kriṣṇa\] were drinking milk from her bosom, all the herd-women gathered together and called out to me, out of fear \[that something terrible would befall me too\]. However, without feeling any fear, I came there, took you in my arms and gave you, my milk. This is the way my affection was towards you. Hence, you should listen to what I am telling you.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa that this is the way in which she had nurtured kriṣṇa and hence, he should listen to her.

**kāyccina nīr …** – To ensure that it would be apt for your divine form, I filled up water in the vessel, along with gooseberry, for your divine bath.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti had filled up water in the vessel such that it was neither hot nor cold and was apt for kriṣṇa.

**vāytta …** – Instead of getting trapped in the deceptive net of the fiend, rejecting her, you saved yourself, as a result of which you had great fame. Oh, one who has the divine form with the complexion of a bluish gemstone such that beholders would get attracted!

**manjanamāda nī vārāy** – you should come and take a divine bath to get rid of dirt etc which came onto your divine form, just like dust gets attached to a carbuncle gem.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa tells yaśōdāp pirātti “Bring the vessel in which you have filled up with warm water to the place where I am standing”. yaśōdāp pirātti tells him “I could only fill up water in that vessel. Is it possible for me to move the vessel?” and prays to him to come for a bath.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.4.4. Kanjan punarppinil

*kanjan puṇarppinil vanda kadiya sagadam udaittuvanjagap pēymagaḷ tunja vāy mulai vaitta pirānē!manjaḷum sengaḻunīrin vāsigaiyum nāṟu sāndumanjanamum koṇḍu vaittēn aḻaganē! nīrāda vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

kanjan – kamsan’s; puṇarppinil vanda – coming out of his incitement; kadiya – being cruel; sagadam – monster, who had pervaded a wheel; udaittu – snapping with divine feet; vanjagam – having deception; pēy magaḷ – pūtanā; tunja – to die; mulai – on her bosom; vāy vaitta – one who kept his mouth and drank; pirānē – oh, one who is my lord!; manjaḷum – protective turmeric powder; sem kaḻu nīrin vāsigaiyum – garland of red water-lily; nāṟu – fragrant, due to admixing with musk, rose-water etc; sāndum – sandalwood; anjanamum – black pigment (to decorate the divine eyes); koṇḍu vaittēn – I have brought; aḻaganē! – oh, kaṇṇa, who has beauty! Come for taking a bath

**Перевод:**

**Oh, my lord, who snapped the cruel śakatāsuran, who had come due to the incitement of kamsan, by kicking him with your divine feet and who killed the monster, pūtanā, by drinking milk from her bosom! I have kept protective turmeric powder, garland strung with red water-lily flowers and sandalwood which has become more fragrant due to mixing with musk, rose-water etc. Oh kaṇṇa, who is beautiful! Come for taking a bath.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kamsan …** – the cruel monster śakatāsuran was impelled by kamsan to kill kriṣṇa. He pervaded a wheel which was kept near kriṣṇa. Due to hunger caused by delay in getting bosom milk, kriṣṇa was crying and kicking his divine feet. The wheel came between the kicking divine feet of kriṣṇa and was crushed to smithereens.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that while the order of the verse should have been pūtanā – śakata \[kriṣṇa killed pūtanā before he annihilated śakata\], the order has been reversed by mentioning about śakata first and pūtanā, later. This implies that more than the deception manifested by pūtanā \[by taking the form of yaśōdāp pirātti\], the cruelty of śakata was greater. Alternatively, it could be said that since emperumān incarnates in every *yuga* \[epoch\], āḻvār would have seen the annihilation of śakata in the previous catur yugam \[encompassing all the four yugams\] and pūtanā in this catur yugam. Thus, he has mentioned killing of śakata ahead of that of pūtanā. It was not only because kamsan had impelled him to go after kriṣṇa, even by nature śakata was crueler than kamsan and hence he came to kill kriṣṇa. However, kriṣṇa killed him by kicking him such that he was dismembered to smithereens.

**vanjagam …** – Oh, one who became our benefactor by keeping your divine mouth on the poisoned bosom of the monster pūtanā, who deceptively came in the form of yaśōdāp pirātti and killed her! This implies that instead of getting caught at the hands of śakata and pūtanā, emperumān killed them and protected himself. This was the benefit which he showered on his followers.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa caused death to pūtanā, who had come with the intention of killing him.

**manjaḷum …** – I have brought turmeric powder which is appropriate for the complexion of your divine form, the garland of red water-lilies, which is appropriate to be donned on your divine crown, fragrant sandalwood paste which has been matured and cooled, and black pigment which has a colour much similar to your divine form., along with other ingredients which are required for your bath.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa knows the distinction in the quality of turmeric which is to be applied on one’s form. Hence, yaśōdāp pirātti says that she has selected the turmeric which is appropriate for his divine form. The colour of the garland of red water-lilies would reflect, in a shiny way, on his divine complexion. The dark pigment was of the same complexion as his divine form.

**aḻaganē nīrāda vārāy** – Oh, one who has a beauty which makes these materials to be superfluous! You should come for taking a bath.

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.4.5. Appam kalanda

*appam kalanda siṟṟuṇḍi akkāram pālil kalandusoppada nān suttu vaittēn tinnal uṟudiyēl nambī!seppiḷa menmulaiyārgaḷ siṟu puṟam pēsic ciripparsoppada nīrāda vēṇḍum sottam pirān! ingē vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

nambī – Oh, one who is complete!; nān – I, your mother; appam kalanda – along with the sweet dish appam; siṟu uṇḍi – light food; pālil – in milk; akkāram kalandu – mixing with sugarcane extract; soppada – well; suttu vaittēn – cooked; tinnal uṟudiyēl – if you desire to eat these; soppada – well; nīr Ada vēṇḍum – you should mercifully have a bath; seppu – having the form of copper; iḷa – being youthful; mel – being soft; mulaiyārgaḷ – those having bosoms; siṟu – mean words coming to them; puṟam pēsi – at unseen places; sirippar – will speak derisively; pirān! – oh, my lord!; sōttam – I worship you; ingē vārāy – you should come here (in order to neutralise their derision)

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who is complete! I, your mother, have cooked light food which contains appam along with milk in which sugar cane has been mixed well. If you desire to eat these, you should mercifully have a good bath. If you do not have a bath, girls, who have youthful, soft bosoms, with the form of copper, will speak derisively about you, in unseen places, using mean words. In order to annul their derisive words, you should come here and have your bath. Oh, my lord! I worship you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**appam …** – appam \[an eatable made with wheat flour and jaggery\] along with light food, containing other eatables.

**akkāram pālil kalandu** – mixing sugar cane extract with flour and adding milk to it

**soppada …** – very well

**tinnal uṟudiyēl nambi** – Oh, one who has completeness in your childish activities! If you have the desire to eat these foods … (she tells him further that he has to come for a bath).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *uṟudal* \[as in *uṟidiyēl\]* refers to having desire.

**seppiḷa men mulaiyārgaḷ** – those girls who have bosoms similar to the form of copper, and are youthful and soft.

**siṟupuṟam pēsic cirippar** – if they look at your form which hasn’t had a bath, they will talk in a mean way, derisively, at places which you have not seen. *siṟumai* – meanness. *puṟam pēsudal* – speaking at places where one doesn’t visit

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa has become complete in his qualities since young women have spoken derisively about him. *siṟupuṟam* – due to deep affection for him, the girls speak about his not having a bath, in lowly words.

**soppada nīrāda vēṇḍum** – you should have a bath such that you do not give them an opportunity to talk lowly about you.

Since he did not come, despite yaśōdāp pirātti telling him all these,

**sōttam pirān ingē vārāy** – Oh, one who is complete in all qualities! I worship you. You should come here.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.4.6. Enneyk kudattai

*eṇṇeyk kudaittai urutti iḷam piḷḷai kiḷḷi eḻuppikkaṇṇaip puratti viḻittu kaḻagaṇḍu seyyum pirānē!uṇṇak kanigaḷ taruvan oli kadal ōda nīr pōlēvaṇṇam aḻagiya nambī! manjanam āda nī vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

eṇṇeyk kudattai – pot, containing oil; urutti – rolling; iḷam piḷḷai – young child \[who is sleeping\]; kiḷḷi eḻuppi – pinching him such that the child wakes up, screaming; kaṇṇai – eye lids; puratti viḻittu – flipping them such that the inner reddish portion gets exposed \[appūcci, as seen in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2.1\]; kaḻagaṇḍu – intolerable misciefs like this; seyyum – one who carries out; pirānē! – oh, one who is independent!; uṇṇa – such that you consume; kanigaḷ taruvan – I will offer fruits; oli – belligerent; kadal – ocean’s; ōdam – having agitation; nīr pōlē – like its water; aḻagiya vaṇṇam – having a beautiful complexion; nambī! – oh, one who is complete, you should come for your bath

**Перевод:**

**Oh, the independent entity! You roll over oil pots; you wake up little children, who are deeply asleep, by pinching them hard such that they scream. You indulge in intolerable misciefs such as flipping your eyelids, exposing the inner reddish part of the eyelids, frightening the children further. Oh, one who is complete with the complexion of a belligerent ocean with agitating waves! I will offer you fruits which you could consume. You should come for a bath.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**eṇṇey …** – In order to make the people in their houses to engage with other activities \[instead of looking after sleeping children\], kriṣṇa would roll down pots containing oil. Once they see oil spilling, the people will run to stop it and to fill up the pots again with the spilt oil, feeling distressed

**iḷam piḷḷai kiḷḷi eḻuppi** – he would then pinch the sleeping children who will wake up screaming \[due to the pain suffered due to pinching\]. Once they hear the children screaming, the people, who were engaged earlier in scooping out the spilt oil, would come running to check on the children who are screaming.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that kriṣṇa would flip his eyelids, similar to his act in *appūcci*, frightening children who had just then got up from their sleep, and make them to scream. The purpose of doing this is to indulge in his favourite acts \[of stealing food\] due to the commotion which he had created. Oh, one who carries out such misciefs as your pastime!

**kaṇṇaip purātti viḻittu** – he would flip his eyelids by making the inner, red, fleshy part to get exposed and frighten people nearby, similar to his activity seen earlier in the *appūcci* padigam.

**kaḻagaṇḍu seyyum pirānē** – Oh, the completely independent entity who indulges in such intolerable mischievous acts! You appear to be outside anyone’s ability to control you. The implied meaning is that yaśōdāp pirātti wants him to be obedient towards her and to listen to her request.

**uṇṇak kanigaḷ taruvan** – I will give you fruits such as blue berry, which you consume desirously.

**oli kadal …** – Oh, one who is complete by having the complexion of the agitating waters, seen as waves in an ocean, which is belligerent!

**manjanamāda nī vārāy** – You should come for taking a bath such that the beauty of your divine form gets manifested.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.4.7. Karanda narpalum

*kaṟanda naṟpālum tayirum kadaindu uṟī mēl vaitta veṇṇeypiṟandaduvē mudalāgap peṟṟaṟiyēn empirānē!siṟanda naṟṟāy alar tūṟṟum enbadanāl piṟar munnēmaṟandum uraiyāda māttēn manjanam āda nī vāyāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

em pirānē! – oh, one who is my lord!; piṟandadu mudalāga – from the day when you were born; kaṟanda – milked at appropriate times; nal pālum – good milk; tayirum – and curd; kadaindu – churned; uṟi mēl vaitta – kept in a pot, hung from a network of ropes; veṇṇey – butter, too; peṟṟu aṟiyēn – I have never got them; siṟanda nal tāy – “An affectionate mother, expected to hide the offence even if her child had; alar tūṟṟum – blamed the son”; enbadanāl – following such words of people of the world; piṟar munnē – in the presence of strangers; maṟandum – even by mistake; uraiyāda māttēn – I will not let out words. You should come for a bath

**Перевод:**

**Oh, my lord! After you were born, I have not seen good milk, which had been milked at appropriate times, curd and butter, which had been kept inside pots, suspended from a network of ropes. In front of others who may say “An affectionate mother is expected to hide the offences of her child; but she is blaming her child” I will not let out words blaming you, even my mistake. Come, for taking a bath.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kaṟanda …** – Good milk which has been collected from cows, at appropriate times. Goodness for milk is that it is such rich that it will give plenty of ghee even with less quantity.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that it is not milk which has not been milked from cow. With effort, using my own hands, I have collected the good milk from cow.

**tayirum** – curd which has been set with that milk

**kadaindu uṟi mēl vaitta veṇṇey** – churning such curd and keeping the butter, obtained from it, in pots, suspended from *uṟi* \[a network of ropes suspended from ceiling, for safe-keeping\].

**piṟandu …** – Oh, my lord! From the day that you were born, I have not seen these materials.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *peṟudal* (as in *peṟṟaṟiyēn*) refers to the happiness that yaśōdāp pirātti would feel when kaṇṇan consumes milk offered by her \[Since kaṇṇan would consume these materials by stealing, yaśōdā laments that she did not get the happiness of offering the materials to him\].

**siṟanda** – People of the world would say “An affectionate mother is one who will hide the offences indulged in by her child. But she is blaming the child”. Thus, to prevent such words being said, even by forgetfulness, I will not let loose any such word.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the terms *siṟanda tāy* and *nal tāy* refer to mothers of princes. *nal tāy* is the mother who has given birth to the prince and *siṟanda tāy* is the foster mother who brings up the prince. If there is any shortcoming in the upbringing of the child, the two mothers could blame each other. However, in this case, yaśōdāp pirātti is common for both *nal tāy* and *siṟanda tāy*. Due to her overflowing affection, she would not give kaṇṇan to anyone else for bringing up since it could lead to lessening of his splendour. Since she is both *nal tāy* and *siṟanda tāy*, she would not blame him for anything.

For the term *piṟar* in the verse *piṟar mun maṟandum uraiyāda māttēn*, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says the following: Apart from those who keep focussing on the offensive qualities and shortcoming in good qualities, there are people such as śiśupālan who consider even eminent qualities of emperumān as offences.

**manjanam Ada nī vārāy** – to make me, who is affectionate towards you, feel happy, you should come for a bath.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.4.8. Kanrinai valolai

*kanṟinai vālōlai kattik kanigaḷ udira eṟindupin tudarndu ōdi ōr pāmbaip pidittukkoṇḍu āttināy pōlumnin tiṟattēn allēn nambī! nī piṟanda tiru nannāḷnanṟu nī nīrāda vēṇḍum nāraṇā! ōdādē vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

kanṟinai – a calf; vāl ōlai katti – tying a \[palm\] leaf to its tail; kanigaḷ udira eṟindu – throwing it against a tree such that fruits would fall scattering down; pin todarndu – subsequently; ōdi – running; ōr pāmbai – a snake; pidittuk koṇḍu – catching hold of it; āttināy pōlum – didn’t you shake it?; nambī! – oh, one who is an expert in carrying out misciefs!; nin tiṟattēn allēn – I do not know of any of your methods; nī piṟanda – the day you incarnated; nal – distinguished; tiru nāḷ – today is \[that\] divine star; nī nanṟu nīrāda vēṇḍum – you should have a distinguished bath; nāraṇā! – oh, nārāyaṇa!; ōdādē vārāy – come mercifully, instead of running

**Перевод:**

**Tying a palm leaf to the tail of a calf, you threw it against a tree such that fruits came scattering down. Subsequently, you ran behind a snake and shook it up. Oh, one who is an expert in indulging in misciefs! I do not have your capacity. Today is the day of the divine star under which you had incarnated. Do not run away. You should come here and have a distinguished bath.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kanṟinai …**– in order to look at calves running in a bewildered manner, you had tied palm leaves to the tails of these calves while you were grazing them. You had also thrown a calf, in which a monster had pervaded, with the intention of harming you, against a wood-apple tree, making the fruits to fall down in a scattering manner, leading to the annihilation of another monster who had pervaded a wood-apple.

**pin …** – subsequent to that, you ran behind a snake, caught hold of it and shook it up. By looking at your misciefs now, I believe that you would have carried out those misciefs too. The term *tūdarndu* refers to moving \[going behind the snake\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that kriṣṇa had jumped onto the hoods of the snake kāḷiyan and shaken him up. He says that yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa that he bewilders those who are favourable to them \[some calves\], annihilates those who are unfavourable to him \[monsters who had pervaded calf and wood-apple\] and drives away those \[such as kāḷiyan\] who are fearful of kriṣṇa, being unfavourable entities. She tells him that due to the misciefs that kriṣṇa was indulging in presently, she believes that he had done the earlier ones too \[as described above\].

**nin …** – I am not conversant with your methods \[of indulging in misciefs\]. Let that remain.

**nī piṟanda tiru nannāḷ** – today is the distinguished star under which you had incarnated.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *tiru* \[divine, as in the word *tiru nannāḷ*\] is *aupacārikam* (metaphorical). Alternatively, it could indeed refer to his actual birth-star. Thus, the day under that particular star when he incarnated, is a good day while the other days are inauspicious days. *nannāḷ* – since it is complimentary with his parents, relatives, friends and people of the world-at-large, it is a good day. There are also people who were born on a not-so-complimentary day. However, for kriṣṇa, it is a good day.

**nanṟu nī nīrāda vēṇḍum** – You should have a good bath. Even those, who do not have bath regularly, would take a bath on the day of their birth.

**nāraṇā ōdādē vārāy** – Oh, one who has an inseparable connection with all the *ātmās* (emperumān is the repository of all the ātmās and he resides inside every ātmā as the indvelling soul)! You should not run away, rejecting my words \[she tells him that she too has a connection with him\]. You should come for your bath.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *nāraṇā* also carries generic connection, apart from the distinguished connection with ātmās. In that case, just as everyone else, he \[kriṣṇa\] should come for a bath and fulfil his regular duties.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.4.9. Punit toluvinil

*pūṇit toḻuvinil pukkup puḻudi aḷainda pon mēnikāṇap peridum ugappan āgilum kaṇḍār paḻipparnāṇ ittanaiyum ilādāy! nappinnai kāṇil sirikkummāṇikkamē! en maṇiyē! manjanamāda nī vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

pūṇit toḻuvinil – in the barn where cattle are kept and released; pukku – entering; puḻudi aḷainda – wallowing in dirt; pon mēni – divine form, which is like gold; kāṇa – to see; peridum – to a great extent; ugappan – I would desire; āgilum – though I desire; kaṇḍār – those who see you; paḻippar – will ridicule (saying “Look at the manner in which she has given birth to and; ittanaiyum – even a little bit; nāṇ ilādāy! – oh, one who is without shame!; naṟ pinnai – nappinnaip pirātti; kāṇil – if she were to see your divine formsirikkum – will laugh; en – for me; māṇikkamē! – oh, one who is like a carbuncle!; maṇiyē – oh, one who is like a gemstone! You should come for taking a bath

**Перевод:**

**Entering the barn where cattle are kept safely and from which they are released, you wallow in the dirt there. I would very much desire to see your golden, divine form \[with that dirt\]. However, those who see you, will ridicule me (saying “What sort of a son has she sired and nurtured?”) Oh, one who is without even a little bit of shame! If nappinnaip pirātti were to see you like this, she will laugh at you derisively. Oh, one who is like a carbuncle for me! Oh, one who is like a gemstone for me! You should come for taking a bath.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**pūṇi …** – entering the barn where cattle are kept together \[during night\] and from where they are released for grazing \[in the morning\]. Since he belongs to the clan of herd-people, he would enter barn for playing.

**puḻudi aḷainda pon mēni** – in line with his childish stage, he enters and plays inside the barn. Since the dirt enters his divine form fully, it appears similar to dirt settling on a golden article.

**kāṇap peridum ugappan** – I would very much desire to see your form getting dirtied like this, in line with your stage of being a child, more than a clean form after taking a bath.

**āgilum kaṇḍār paḻippar** – Even though I may desire to see you like this, those who see your dirtied form will ridicule me, saying “Look at the manner in which she has given birth to and nurtured a son!”

**nāṇ ittanaiyum ilādāy** – Oh, one who is without even a little bit of shame!

**nappinnai kāṇil sirikkum** – If nappinnai \[who is your maternal uncle’s daughter\] were to see you with dirt all over your divine form, she will sneer at you, owing to your relationship with her. ṣouldn’t you feel shameful about her sneer, more than the ridicule of people of the village? The implied meaning is that he is without any sense of shame and hence remains that way.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that usage of the word *kāṇil* implies that yaśōdāp pirātti desires that he should come and have a bath before nappinnai looks at him. kriṣṇa appears to say “But, that is the one \[nappinnaip pirātti looking at my dirty form\] which I desire to see”

**māṇikkamē en maṇiyē** – Since there is no material which could be cited as an equivalent for his divine form, she is looking for words, to cite as analogy, just like picking foodgrains from the ground. The opinion expressed here is that his divine form is similar to carbuncle and to emerald.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti initially says that he looks like carbuncle. However, since even that was not sufficient to describe his divine form, she calls him “*en maṇiyē*”. Alternatively, she implies that she wishes to see him shine brightly like carbuncle and pearl, after taking a bath and ridding himself of all the dirt. *māṇikkam* – dark carbuncle. Alternatively, this could refer to an emerald on which carbuncle’s splendour reflects.

**manjanamāda nī vārāy** – You should come and have a bath such that all the dirt, which is not natural on your form but which came in between, would get removed and your form shines splendidly.

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.4.10. Karmali meni

*kār mali mēni niṟattuk kaṇṇa pirānai uganduvār mali kongai yasōdai manjanam āttiyavāṟṟaipār mali tol puduvaik kōn battar pirān sonna pādalsīr mali sendamiḻ vallār tīvinai yādum ilarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kār – dark, monsoon cloud, which has sprung up with plenty of water; malī – with abundance; mēni niṟam – having complexion of divine form; kaṇṇa pirānai – kaṇṇa pirān \[kriṣṇa\]; ugandu – cherishing; vār mali kongai – having rising bosoms which are uncontrolled by bodice; asōdai – yaśōdāp pirātti; manjanam āttiya – giving bath; āṟṟai – the manner of; pār mali – having eminence throughout earth; tol – belonging to ancient time; puduvai – for śrī villibuttūr; kōn – controller; battar pirān – periyāḻvār; sonna – composed mercifully; sīr mali – being with distinctive features; sem tamiḻ – in pure tamiḻ; pādal – (these) pāsurams; vallār – those who are capable of reciting; tī vinai yādum ilar – are without any sinful deed

**Перевод:**

**The complexion of kriṣṇa’s divine form is darker than the dark monsoon cloud which is filled up with water. yaśōdāp pirātti, whose bosoms cannot be controlled by bodice, spoke with affection about the manner in which she gave a bath to kriṣṇa. periyāḻvār, who is the controller of ancient śrī villibuttūr which has eminence throughout the world, mercifully composed those words into pāsurams in pure tamiḻ. Those who are capable of reciting these pāsurams, will be without any sinful deed.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In the final pāsuram of this decad, āḻvār mentions the benefit which will accrue to those who learn the pāsurams and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kār mali mēni niṟattu** – having a complexion which is darker than the dark monsoon cloud, brimming with water.

**kaṇṇa pirānai ugandu** – cherishing that kriṣṇa who is simple to approach for his followers and who is beneficial to them

**vār mali …** – yaśōdāp pirātti has rising bosoms which are not controllable by her bodice. The manner in which such yaśōdāp pirātti gave a bath to kriṣṇa …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that the bath given by periyāḻvār for kriṣṇa is not with the normal water which is used for bath. It is with *jñāna nīr* (the water of knowledge). What is this knowledge? It is knowledge matured with devotion, resulting in carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam \[praising emperumān and wishing well for him\].

**pār mali …** – śrī villibuttūr has an eminence which is much above that of earth and is also ancient. periyāḻvār is the controller of such śrī villibuttūr. The pāsurams mercifully composed by periyāḻvār…

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the eminence of periyāḻvār is not restricted up to brahmalōkam (the abode of brahmā), but it goes beyond that. It goes beyond śrī vaikuṇṭam too and culminates in the divine abode at śrī villibuttūr \[while we consider that there are only two vibhūtis, the leelā vibhūti (samsāram or materialistic realm) and nitya vibhūti (śrī vaikuṇṭam or spiritualistic realm), āḻvārs consider divya dēśams as the third vibhūti, superior to the other two\]. *tol* refers to the fact that this eminence is ancient.

**sīr mali sem tamiḻ vallār** – *seermali* refers to the beauty of pāsurams in tamiḻ language which is without any shortcoming in the seven defining features of pāsuram \[such as letter, word, meaning, metrics etc\]. Alternatively, pāsurams which are complete with the divine qualities of emperumān.

**sem tamiḻ** – tamiḻ which is honest. In other words, the language is such clear that the inner meanings in the pāsurams shine and reveal themselves on their own.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as a gemstone \[such as ruby etc\] lying at the bottom of an ocean is clearly visible from the top, despite the ocean depth, when the water is clear, the inner meanings of pāsurams would be clear to one who recites these pāsurams. This is the honesty referred to here, by which even while residing in samsāram, the ruby-like auspicious qualities of the son of dēvaki \[kriṣṇa\] are clear to us.

**pādal** – pāsurams

**vallār** – those who are capable of reciting with the pathos of periyāḻvār \[having affection towards kriṣṇa\]

**tīvinai yādum ilarē** – they will be without any sinful deed.  There will be no harmful deed for them.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *tīvinai* refers to deeds arising out of desire for *aiśvaryam* \[wealth\], *kaivalyam* \[ātmā enjoying itself instead of enjoying emperumān\] and means employed to attain these *puruśārtams* \[ultimate benefits\]. It also includes activities which are carried out in line with the nature of ātmā \[being servitor to emperumān and carrying out kainkaryams to him as a *śēśabhūtan* (one who is a servitor) \[this may appear bewildering, but from periyāḻvār’s point of view, carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam to emperumān is the only apt kainkaryam which is to be carried out. This assumes that emperumān is to be protected and we are the protector. Thus, any deed which does not lead to carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam is *tīvinai*\].

We shall next consider the pravēśam of the next tirumoḻi.

## 2.5.1. Pinnai manalanai

*pinnai maṇāḷanaip pēril kidandānaimunnai amarar mudal tani vittinaiennaiyum engaḷ kudi muḻudu ātkoṇḍamannanai vandu kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy! mādavan tan kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy!*

**Пословный перевод:**

pinnai – for nappinnaip pirātti; maṇāḷanai – beloved; pēril – in the divyadēśam called as “tiruppēr”; kidandānai – one who is mercifully reclining; munnai amarar – for nityasūris \[permanent dwellers of śrī vaikuṇṭam\]; mudal – as their lord; tani vittinai – as the unique causative factor; ennaiyum – me; engaḷ kudi muḻudu – all those who are in our clan, who have been without any fault for; āḷ koṇḍa – having as servitors; mannanai – one who is the king; vandu – oh, crow! Coming in proximity, comb his divine locks; mādavan than – oh, crow! Comb the divine locks of śriya:pati (divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi)

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa is the beloved of nappinnaip pirātti, mercifully reclining in the divyadēśam, tiruppēr. He is the lord of nityasūris and is their unique causative factor. He is the king who has me and all those who have come in our clan, in the last seven generations, without any fault, as his servitors. Oh, crow! Come, in his proximity and comb his divine locks. Oh, crow! Comb the divine locks of śrīya:pati.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**pinnai …** – one who is the beloved of nappinnaip pirātti. She alone is the principal consort of kriṣṇa, in this avatāram \[incarnation\]. Just as the term *śrīya*: *pati* denotes emperumān’s eminence, being the beloved of nappinnaip pirātti refers to his simplicity \[she was born in the clan of herd-people\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that being *puruśakāara bhūtai* (one who recommends an ātmā to emperumān for granting refuge\] precedes *prapatti* \[act of surrendering to emperumān\]. Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 1-7-8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-7-8-ennai-negizhkkilum/) “*pinnai nedum paṇāittōḷ magiḻ pīdudai*” (one who has the greatness of embracing the well-rounded shoulders of nappinnaip pirātti), this should be considered as being equivalent to the eminence of being *śrīya: pati.*

**pēril kidandānai** – this denotes further simplicity, beyond his being the consort of nappinnaip pirātti. The simplicity of *arcāvatāram* \[emperumān dwelling in idol form in samsāram\] is unlike his simplicity in incarnations \[incarnation is for a limited time while *arcāvatāram* remains forever\]. Just as tirumangai āḻvār mercifully said in his [periya tirumoḻi 5.9.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/04/periya-thirumozhi-5-9-8/) “*kombanār pinnai kōlam kūdudaṟku ēṟu konṟān – then tiruppēr mēvum empirān*” (the beautiful tiruppēr divyadēśam is the place where emperumān, who killed bulls in order to embrace the slender divine form of nappinnaip pirātti, dwells fittingly), there is a connection between being the consort of nappinnaip pirātti and reclining in tiruppēr. It was only to tiruppēr that kriṣṇa came, along with nappinnaip pirātti, after marrying her.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that it is due to nappinnaip pirātti’s desire that he is reclining in tiruppēr.

**munnai amarar …** – this speaks about his eminence, which is the exact opposite of his quality of simplicity, mentioned just now. Just as it has been mentioned in puruśa sūktam 18 “*yatra pūrvē sādyā santi dēvā*:” (He is the lord of nityasūris, who have been there since time immemorial), he is the lord of nityasūris, who have been at the forefront of *bhagavadanubhavam* (experiencing emperumān), being their lord and being the causative factor for their *sattā* (existence) as well as their *dāraka, pōśaka* and *bhōjñam* (sustenance, nurturing and enjoyment respectively).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that emperumān carries out tasks for nityasūris, much ahead of celestial entities. If he has to be the consort of nappinnaip pirātti, he has to carry out the tasks of nityasūris. This is his desire. For the term *mudal tani vittinai*, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that emperumān is the *trivida kāraṇam* for this *vibhūti* \[He is the *upādāna kāraṇam* (material cause)*, nimitta kāraṇam* (efficient cause) and *sahakāri kāraṇam* (expedient cause); in other words, just as a potter creates a pot using clay as the *upādanam* (material), himself as the *nimittam* (one who carries out the task) and wheel and stick as *sahakāri* (ancillaries), emperumān creates the world with himself as the material (without looking for any other material), with himself as the doer (without looking up to anyone else) and with himself as the *sahakāri*, without looking for any ancillaries\]. Alternatively, the term *trivida kāraṇam* could also refer to his role as *sruśti kāraṇam* (cause for creation), *stiti kāraṇam* (cause for existence) and *laya kāraṇam* (cause for destruction).

**ennaiyum …** – me, who cannot exist without being affectionate towards him and all the others who are in our clan for seven generations, carrying out servitude to him without any fault, in line with our *svarūpam* \[basic nature\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai explains here as to what is fault for the clan. In the first syllable of *tirumantram* (first among the three esoteric mantrams), three relationships are indicated – from the etymology, the first syllable ‘*a*‘ indicates protector. Thus, the first relationship between emperumān and us is that of protector – protected. The second relationship indicates one of cause and effect. He is the cause and we are the effect. The third relationship indicates one of *śēśi* and *śēśan* – he is the lord and we are the servitors. Thus, fault for the clan is to forget these three relationships between emperumān and us, and not carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam, befitting our basic nature.

**mannanai** – one who is the king.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that emperumān has the status of being the lord of the clan which behaves in line with nammāḻvār’s verse [*āḷumāḷār*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/02/thiruvaimozhi-8-3-3-alumalar/) \[he is the lord, but does not have anyone to carry out servitude to him\]. āḻvār’s clan is always looking forward to carrying out servitude to him and emperumān is the lord of that clan.

**vandu kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy** – this the manner in which those who comb the locks of their children, recite as a pāsuram.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that once bath has been taken, the next activity is to comb the locks. The reason for emperumān to make the samsāri to carry out *prapatti*, with nappinnai and nityasūris as puruśakāram, is to create the flavour of mangaḷāśāsanam in the samsāri. Instead of knowing this, and carrying this out, the samsāri has been engaged in desiring and acquiring wealth and other worldly pursuits. These actions create entanglements in emperumān’s divine locks \[he is not happy with the samsāri pursuing other benefits\]. āḻvār calls upon removing these entanglements by combing emperumān’s divine locks. For the term *akkākkāy*, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says the following: The term *kākkai* is a pretext. *kākkai* would refer both to the bird, crow, and the action, protection \[in tamiḻ, *kāttal* refers to protection\]. āḻvār transposes the action of protection onto a bird, crow, which has the ability to think and calls the bird to remove the entanglements in emperumān’s divine locks, caused by the samsāri’s desires in worldly pursuits. While being the causative factor is the prerequisite of being the lord, for emperumān, once the worlds are created, his engagement is focussed on protection only. Hence, āḻvār indicates a higher level of respect for the word ‘protection’ which comes out of the etymology for the syllable ‘*a*’ in tirumantram and calls out to the crow to come and remove the entanglements in emperumān’s divine locks. āḻvār says “It is only when the entanglements in emperumān’s divine locks get removed that the dirt in your \[reference here is to samsāris\] heads will disappear”. Thus, he calls all the samsāris, who are like crows, to remove the entanglements in emperumān’s locks, classify the three entities of *cit*, *acit* and *īśvaran* (entities which have ability to think, which do not have ability to think and the supreme entity of emperumān, respectively) knowing their true nature, analyse them till the end \[of his locks\], remove the faults in his locks and keep them on your heads \[here, the term *fault* refers to blaming emperumān for all our sorrows; instead of blaming emperumān for our sorrows, we have to take ownership for our actions and make us responsible for our actions and the resultant sorrows\].

**mādavan …** – just as he is the consort of nappinnaip pirātti, to manifest his quality of simplicity, he is the consort of śrī mahālakśmi, manifesting his quality of eminence. Oh, crow! Comb the divine locks of such mādavan.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that emperumān being *mādavan* (consort of śrī mahālakśmi) is the reason for his becoming *pinnai maṇāḷan* (the consort of nappinnaip pirātti). Since he is *mādavan*, he is without any fault. It is not only that he is without any fault, he is also full of all the auspicious qualities. āḻvār tells us not to look for faults in the auspicious qualities of emperumān. When lakśmaṇāḻvān said, as in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 4-18 “*sugrīvam nātam iccati*” (śrī rāma, who was earlier the lord of the entire world, is now accepting the lordship of sugrīvan) while introducing śrī rāma to hanuman, the presence of sītāp pirātti was missing for cementing the relationship. However, that fault was rectified earlier when śrī rāma accepted guha’s friendship in the presence of sītāp pirātti, as mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 5-8-1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/02/periya-thirumozhi-5-8-1/) “*un tōḻi umbiyembi*” \[accept this sītāp pirātti, who has the bewildered look of a doe, as your friend and my brother lakśmaṇa, as your brother). In the same way, āḻvār says that our fault will get removed if we surrender to emperumān as *pinnai maṇāḷan* (the consort of nappinnaip pirātti). With that fault removed, āḻvār tells us to come and remove the entanglement in emperumān’s divine locks.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.
