## 2.5.2. Peyin mulai

*pēyin mulai uṇḍa piḷḷai ivan munnammāyac cagadum marudum iṟuttavankāyā malar vaṇṇan kaṇṇan karum kuḻaltūydāga vandu kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy! tūmaṇi vaṇṇan kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy!*

**Пословный перевод:**

ivan – this little child; munnam – earlier; pēyin – pūtanā’s; mulai – milk from bosom; uṇḍa – one who consumed; piḷḷai – see, this child; māyam – dishonest; sagadum – wheel \[in which a demon had pervaded\]; marudum – twin arjuna trees, called as yamaḷārjuna; iṟuttavan – had snapped; kāyā malar – like the kāyām pū (purple water-lily); vaṇṇan – has the divine complexion; kaṇṇan – (one who is like these, such) kaṇṇan’s; karu kuḻal – dark, divine locks; tūydāga – oh, crow! Come and comb the locks well; tūmaṇi vaṇṇan – oh, crow! Comb the divine locks of one the who has the complexion of bluish gemstone which does not have any fault

**Перевод:**

**This little child, kaṇṇan, had earlier consumed milk from pūtanā’s bosom. He had snapped a dishonest monster who had pervaded a wheel as well as twin arjuna trees. Oh, crow! Come and comb well, the dark, divine locks of one who has the complexion of a dark purple water-lily. Oh crow, comb the divine locks of one, who has the divine complexion of a faultless, dark bluish gemstone.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**pēyin mulai uṇḍa piḷḷai ivan munnam** – earlier, the demon pūtanā had come, taking the form of yaśōdāp pirātti \[ to offer her poisoned milk to kriṣṇa\]. However, thinking that she was his mother yaśōdāp pirātti, kriṣṇa consumed her milk. He was such an innocent child. If there is no shortcoming in his childishness, how did she perish? His nature is such that if anyone approaches him with an unfavourable mind, that person will perish.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that āḻvār is warning us not to suffer like pūtanā who had seen a fault in kriṣṇa’s auspicious qualities and came with the intention of killing him. He further says that there is no boundary to his childishness.

**māyac cagadum marudum iṟuttavan** – subsequent to that, while he was reclining, a monster had pervaded in a dishonest manner, a wheel which was near kriṣṇa. \[Due to delay in arrival of milk\] kriṣṇa kicked his feet. The wheel got caught between his kicking feet and got snapped. When kriṣṇa was crawling, there were twin arjuna trees in his path, intending to harm him. kriṣṇa pushed the trees with his divine thighs, snapping them too.

**kāyā malar vaṇṇan** – his divine beauty is such that his qualities of ātmā become superfluous. With his beautiful, just then blossomed, purple water-lily like form, he would make the favourable entities to give in writing that they are his servitors.

**kaṇṇan** – even if his form had not been beautiful, his easy-to-approach nature was such that none could go away from him.

**karum kuḻal** – since āḻvār is unable to give an equivalent for the divine locks, he merely calls the locks as dark.

**tūydāga vandu kuḻal vārāy** – come and comb his divine locks well. Combing the divine locks well is to separate the locks, while combing.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that there is no fault in kriṣṇa’s divine locks. It is only we who, in our ignorance, have thought that he was responsible for our ills and transposed that as a fault on him.

**tūmaṇi vaṇṇan** – one, who has the complexion of a faultless bluish gemstone. The dark purple water-lily flower may not appear the same way, all the time. However, the bluish gemstone would have the same colour always. Thus, he has the divine complexion of such a bluish gemstone.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.5.3. Tinnak kalattil

*tiṇṇak kalattil tirai uṟi mēl vaittaveṇṇey viḻungi viraiyan uṟangidumaṇṇal amarar perumānai āyar tamkaṇṇanai vandu kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy! kārmugil vaṇṇan kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiṇṇam – being robust; kalattil – in a vessel; tirai – being strung with ropes and appearing big; uṟi mēl – on uṟi (suspended from ceiling with a network of ropes); vaitta – kept safely; veṇṇey – butter; viḻungi – swallowed; viraiyan – running fast; uṟangidum – lying, pretending to be asleep; aṇṇal – as the lord of all; amarar perumānai – one, who is the lord of nityasūris; āyar tam – for the herd-people; kaṇṇanai – oh, crow! Comb the locks of such kaṇṇan; kār mugil – like bluish cloud; vaṇṇan – oh, crow! Comb the locks of one who has the form of such cloud

**Перевод:**

**kaṇṇan would swallow butter which has been kept safely inside a robust vessel and kept in uṟi and lie down immediately as if he were sleeping. Oh, crow! Come and comb the divine locks of that kaṇṇan who is the lord of all, the lord of nityasūris as well belonging to the herd-people. Oh, crow! Comb the divine locks of kaṇṇan who has the form of a bluish cloud.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tiṇṇak kalattu** – in a sturdy vessel. Even if one were to repeatedly keep hitting the vessel with sticks, the vessel will not break.

**tirai uṟi mēl vaitta** – keeping the vessel on top, in a large *uṟi*. *tirai uṟi* – huge *uṟi*, made with thick ropes which have been intertwined well.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that the ropes have been intertwined such that none can even move it. Even the person who had strung the ropes would not be able to undo them. Alternatively, using many ropes and using them to create a dense structure.

**veṇṇey viḻungi** – swallowing butter, which has been safely kept \[inside that *uṟi*\], without disturbing the marks made on the ropes, making one to wonder “Was the butter taken away by any deity?”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that since the vessel has not been disturbed when the butter kept inside it has been found missing, it would appear that in his stress to eat the butter fast, before anyone could see him, butter has got spilt and spread out. This would make those who had seen it to surmise that he had swallowed the butter.

**viraiyan uṟangidum** – running hurriedly, before those who had kept the butter safely in that manner could see him, and sleeping as if he did not know anything which had happened. Is it possible to sleep when one runs in hurriedly, under stress, more than the stress experienced while swallowing the butter? He will see, with half-opened eyes, shadows of people moving here and there in such a manner that those who see him will accost him, saying “What sort of a pretending sleep is this?”

**aṇṇal** – lord. He would make the favourable entities, who hear about this narrative of stealing and eating butter, to give in writing that they are his servitors.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *aṇṇal* refers to kaṇṇan being the lord of the divine clan of herd-people.

**amarar perumānai** – the lord of nityasūris who have no bewilderment at all. This is the upper limit for his eminence.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kaṇṇan is the controller of nityasūris. Controlling them refers to his quality of mingling with them and experiencing together with them.

**āyar tam kaṇṇanai** – this speaks about his quality of simplicity, which is the exact opposite of the eminence mentioned earlier. He is the controller of herd-people who do not know the distinction between left hand and right hand.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that he is the protector of herd-people. He is one who is easy to approach. He is one who is the object of their vision.

**kaṇṇan** – this could also be considered as being their (herd-people’s) eyes.

**kārmugil vaṇṇan** – He has the form of a cloud which is about to pour down rain \[that dark\]. This implies that his form is such that it would remove the ennui of beholders. Oh, crow! Come and comb the divine locks of such kaṇṇan.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.5.4. Pallattil meyum

*paḷḷattil mēyum paṟavai urukkoṇḍukaḷḷa asuran varuvānaittān kaṇḍupuḷ idu enṟu podukkō vāy kīṇḍittapiḷḷaiyai vandu kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy! pēy mulai uṇḍān kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy!*

**Пословный перевод:**

paḷḷattil – in lower regions of water bodies; mēyum – searching for prey; paṟavai – bird, crane; uru koṇḍu – taking the form; varuvān – one who came; kaḷḷa asuranai – dishonest monster (bakāsuran); tān – he \[kaṇṇan\] who was grazing calves, and playing outwardly; kaṇḍu – seeing him; idu puḷ enṟu – superficially considering it as a bird and not thinking deeply that it is a monster; vāy – its mouth; podukkō – suddenly; kīṇḍitta – oh, crow! Comb the divine locks of the child who tore its mouth; pēy – pūtanā’s; mulai uṇḍān – oh, crow! Comb the hair of the one who consumed \[milk from\] her bosom

**Перевод:**

**A dishonest monster, bakāsuran, had taken the form of a crane, which was searching for its prey in lower regions of water bodies. kriṣṇa was grazing calves nearby, and playing outwardly. Thinking that it is a bird and not a monster, kriṣṇa suddenly tore the mouth of that bird. Oh, crow, comb the locks of that child kriṣṇa. Oh, crow! Comb the locks of the one who consumed milk from the bosom of the monster pūtanā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**paḷḷattil …** – taking the form of a bird, crane, which searches for prey in small ponds.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the demon looked at the auspicious qualities of kriṣṇa as faults, and hid himself in the form of a crane. He started looking for desired prey \[fish\] in low lying water bodies, along with lot of other cranes which were also looking for their favourite food. Though all the cranes looked similar, the difference could be seen. This is the reason why āḻvār calls him as “*kaḷḷa asuran*” (dishonest monster)

**kaḷḷa asuran** – dishonest monster. Hiding his form \[of a monster\], he took the form of a bird, due to his dishonesty.

**varuvānait tān kaṇḍu** – kriṣṇa, who was engaged with grazing calves, saw the monster, who had come hiding himself in the form of a bird, in order to harm kriṣṇa.

**puḷ idu enṟu** – not thinking of it as a monster, but considering it as a lowly bird.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that he could see the two forms \[form of monster and form of bird\] in that crane, just like a calf which is not desirous of eating. Even though it appeared like other birds, its distinction from the rest was evident.

**podukkō vāy kīṇḍitta** – the crane came opening its mouth to swallow kriṣṇa. However, kriṣṇa suddenly tore its mouth, without giving it any thought of carrying out what it had intended. *podukkō* – suddenly.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that even though the monster came as a crane, he appeared to be the king \[leader\] among the cranes. *podukkō* is a single word, with the meaning of ‘suddenly’.

**piḷḷaiyai** – one who has no limit for his childishness. Despite doing all these activities \[of killing a monster, consuming milk from another monster etc\], it appeared to him that these are playful activities.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa did not have any boundary to his activities of childishness. When children see a hole anywhere, they will insert their hand inside, without thinking about the result. In the same way, when the bird came, opening its mouth wide, kriṣṇa inserted his hand. Since it was a rare sight for him \[to see a crane coming with its mouth open\], he started growing, out of happiness. His hands too grew, as the result of which the mouth of the bird tore and the monster fell down. The child \[kriṣṇa\] was born in such a *muhurtam* \[auspicious time\] that any unfavourable entity, approaching him with evil mind, will perish. If this veren’t the case, the story would have been told as “Crane swallowed the child”. Since that did not happen, and kriṣṇa protected himself, āḻvār, remembering that benefit, tells the crow to comb the locks.

**pēy mulai uṇḍān** – Even when he consumed \[milk from\] her bosom, it appeared like a playful act for him, without limit to his childishness.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the child escaped both from the bird and the fiend. It is generally mentioned, in colloquial terms, that children would be affected by birds and fiends.

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.5.5. Karrinam meyttu

*kaṟṟinam mēyttuk kanikkoru kanṟinaipaṟṟi eṟinda paraman tirumudiuṟṟana pēsi nī ōdit tiriyādēaṟṟaikkum vandu kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy! āḻiyān tan kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kanṟu inam – herd of calves; mēyttu – grazing; oru kanṟinai – one calf, in which a monster had pervaded; paṟṟi – lifting it, catching hold of its leg; kanikku – in order to bring down a wood-apple in which another monster had pervaded; eṟinda – one who threw \[the calf on the fruit\]; paraman – benefactor’s; tiru mudi – beautiful, divine locks; uṟṟana – peculiar to your species; pēsi – speaking about; nī ōdit tiruyādē – without flying away; aṟṟaikkum – oh, crow! Come every day and comb his divine locks; āḻiyān than – oh, crow! Comb the divine locks of one who is holding the divine disc on his divine hand

**Перевод:**

**While grazing cows, kriṣṇa caught hold of the leg of one of the calves in which a monster had pervaded, and threw it against a wood-apple, in which another monster had pervaded \[with the intention of killing him\]. Oh, crow! Without speaking about matters relating to your species and flying away, come every day and comb the beautiful, divine locks of that benefactor. Comb the divine locks of one who is holding the divine disc on his divine hand.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kaṟṟinam …** – grazing the herd of calves. At young age, one has to graze calves. Only after growing older, could grown-up cows be grazed. Thus, kriṣṇa too started with grazing calves, initially.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that kriṣṇa doesn’t like going behind old cows. He prefers going behind young calves, grazing them. He would gently stroke their stomachs; only if their stomachs are filled, would he feel that his stomach is filled up. While he was going behind the calves which had their stomach filled up with grazing, he was playing with them and unable to leave them. Some monsters were waiting to harm him, wondering “When will he come?” One of them had taken the form of a calf and the other had taken the form of a wood-apple. kriṣṇa noticed both, seeing the difference between them and the other calves / wood-apple fruits. Just as one removes a thorn using another thorn, he threw the calf in which a monster had pervaded, on a wood-apple in which another monster had pervaded, killing them both. Thus, he became the benefactor, by protecting himself. His divine locks indicate that he is the supreme entity.

**kanikkoru kanṟinaip paṟṟi eṟinda** – In the places where he was roaming around, grazing the calves, he saw two monsters who had pervaded a calf and a wood-apple fruit, with the intention of harming him. Just as it has been mentioned in periya tirumoḻi 9.8.6 “*viḷam kanikku iḷam kanṟu visiṟi*” (throwing a young calf for making a wood-apple to fall), he threw a calf in which a demon had pervaded, by holding its foot and threw it on a wood-apple fruit, inside which too another demon had pervaded, to bring down both, killing them, similar to removing a thorn with the help of another thorn.

**paraman tirumudi** – Instead of getting caught at the hands of these two demons who had come to harm him, kriṣṇa annihilated them, thus protecting himself, who is the supreme lord for all the worlds, thus acting as a benefactor. The divine locks of such a supreme entity…

**uṟṟana pēsi nī ōdit tiriyādē** – Instead of flying away, speaking about matters related to your species, without staying in one place…

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār is addressing the samsāris here who are not paying heed to the true words of an ācāryan and carrying out servitude to him, but are discussing superficial meanings of certain matters which appear to be syncronised. He says that without looking at the topic which is being discussed, the explanations which are offered for proving that and the conclusion drawn at the end, and confirming that these are correct, samsāris would say what comes to their minds, affirming that this is what is mentioned in śāstrams. They will bewilder people of the world such that when a learned person comes to explain, they will turn their faces away and leave. āḻvār warns such people by addressing the crow and telling it not to roam around, speaking irrelevant matters.

**aṟṟaikkum vandu kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy** – You should come every day and comb kriṣṇa’s divine locks.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār tells the crow that even if it does not come on any other day, it should come at the least on that day when kriṣṇa had taken a bath in order to get rid of the faults which have come onto him on account of those who attempt to attain him through means other than himself \[means such as *karma yōgam, jñāna yōgam, bhakti yōgam* (the paths of deeds, knowledge, devotion) etc\] and is waiting for his divine locks to be combed. If the crow comes on that day and combs his divine locks, it would be equivalent to coming every day and combing his locks.

**āḻiyān** – One who has the divine disc. This implies that he has the means to control those who are unfavourable.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.5.6. Kilakkil kudimannar

*kiḻakkil kudimannar kēdu ilādāraiaḻippān ninaindittu avvāḻi adanālviḻikkum aḷavilē vēr aṟuttānaikkuḻaṟku aṇiyāgak kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy! gōvindan taṇ kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kēdu ilādārai – indra et al, who do not have any shortcoming, having taken refuge under kriṣṇa; aḻippān – to destroy; ninainditta – those who thought; kiḻakkil kudi – those who reside in prāgjyōtiśapuram; mannar – narakāsuran et al; viḻikkum aḷavilē – in a wink \[time it takes to close and open the eyes\]; ver aṟuttānai – one who uprooted; kuḻaṟku – for his divine locks; aṇi āga – oh, crow! Comb his divine locks as a decoration; gōvindan – one who grazes cows; taṇ kuḻal – oh, crow! Comb his distinguished locks

**Перевод:**

**Kings such as narakāsuran et al, who were residing in a place, prāgjyōtiśapuram, had thought of destroying indra et al, who had no shortcoming in them, having taken refuge under kriṣṇa. However, kriṣṇa uprooted such kings in the time that it takes to close and open the eyes. Oh, crow! Comb the divine locks of such kriṣṇa, as a decoration. Comb the distinguished locks of that kriṣṇa, who grazes cows.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kiḻakkil kudi mannar** – monster kings such as narakāsuran et al, who were residing in prāgjyōtiśapuram

**kēdilādārai** – those who thought that they did not have any shortcoming since they had strengths of boons and their shoulders

**aḻippān ninaindittu** – emperumān decided in his divine mind that he would destroy them since they were harming indra et al, who had taken refuge under him.

**avvāḻi adanāl** – divine disc of emperumān is such that it would go to the place, on its own, thought of by emperumān \[he doesn’t even have to tell it to go\]. Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.10.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-5-thiramudai-valaththal/) “*aṟamuyal āḻi*” (the divine disc which is engaged in the righteous act of protecting emperumān’s followers), the divine disc would engage with protecting the followers of emperumān more than emperumān himself. With that divine disc …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that the term *adanāl* refers to the divine disc which will not return to emperumān’s divine hands until the mission for which emperumān had set off the divine disc is completed, even if emperumān wishes to recall him.

**viḻikkum aḷavilē vēr aṟuttānai** – one who uprooted them even before one could wink \[close the eyes and open them\]. Alternatively, the verse could be rearranged as “*kēdilādārai aḻippān ninaindittu – kiḻakkil kudi mannar – viḻikkum aḷavilē, āḻi adanāl – vēr aṟuttānai*”. In this case, the meaning would be as follows: indra et al were thinking that īśvaran is there as our protector; hence, we do not have any shortcoming. The kings such as narakāsuran et al, living in prāgjyōtiśapuram, thought that they would destroy indra et al. Once indra conveyed this information to kriṣṇa, he mounted his vehicle, garuda, went to narakapuram, and with the divine disc, which goes to the place which he thinks of, he cut them down such that they could not come up again at all.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *viḻikkum aḷavilē* refers to emperumān thinking that this is the time to destroy \[the unfavourable entities such as narakāsuran et al, who reside in *prāgjyōtiśapuram*\], after deciding that they have to be destroyed. *kēdilāmai* \[being without any shortcoming\] refers to indra et al, getting engaged in *brahma bhāvanai* \[matters related to emperumān\] and dissociating from *karma bhāvanai* \[matters related to carrying out deeds\]. Thus, thinking of those entities who were thinking of harming such indra et al as well as the women related to them.

**kuḻaṟkaṇiyākak kuḻal vārāy** – such that the divine locks shine with beauty

**gōvindan** – one who has intense engagement in protecting cows

**taṇ kuḻal** – divine locks, which are excellent

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.5.7. Pindat tiralaiyum

*piṇḍat tiraḷaiyum pēykkitta nīrccōṟumuṇḍaṟku vēṇḍi nī ōdit tiriyādēaṇḍattu amarar perumān aḻagamarvaṇḍottu iruṇḍa kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy! māyavan tan kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy!*

**Пословный перевод:**

piṇḍam – balls of cooked rice, kept as offering for forefathers; tiraḷaiyum – collection; pēykku itta – offered for fiends; nīr sōrum – food, mixed with water; uṇḍaṟku vēṇḍi – desiring to eat them; nī – you, desiring to eat such offerings; ōdit tiriyādē – instead of roaming around, trying to find those; aṇḍam – remaining in nitya vibhūti \[śrī vaikuṇṭam\]; amarar – for nityasūris; perumān – one who is the lord; aḻagu amar – being beautiful; vaṇḍu ottu – like beetles; iruṇḍa – oh, crow! Comb the dark locks; māyavan than – oh, crow! Comb the divine locks of one who has amazing activities

**Перевод:**

**Crows roam around, looking for ball of cooked food, which is offered to forefathers as well as food mixed with water, which is offered to fiends. Oh, crow! Instead of roaming around for those types of food, comb the beautiful, divine locks of the lord of nityasūris, which are dark like beetles. Comb the divine locks of one, who has amazing activities.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**piṇḍat tiraḷaiyum** – the collection of ball-shaped, cooked rice, which is offered to forefathers.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says the following: The reason for adding “also” \[as in *sōṟum*, food also\] needs an explanation. (1) Apart from eating the food meant for it, crow will roam around for eating food which has been offered by someone for someone else \[food offered by people for their forefathers\]. (2) It will eat the food and excrements of others (3). Unlike dog, which also eats others’ excrements but shows gratitude, crow will not show any gratitude (4) It does not feel ashamed of earning the name that it eats food offered to others (5) Just as the saying goes “*paṟakkum kākkai irukkum kombu aṟiyādu*” (a crow which keeps flying will not distinguish between one stick and another), it does not have a regular place to live (6) It does not follow the rule of “Have a bath before eating”. After eating dirty food, it will wash of its head, to remove the fault of eating dirty food. (7) It will harm others \[such as sitting atop cattle and pecking them\] (8) It will eat the left-over food of those who have harmed others (9) It will eat the grains which have been kept for drying by those, who eat only grains which have got scattered around fields for their sustenance, when they are not standing guard over the grains (10) While it will bring up those who have sweet voices \[cuckoos\], it will drive them away later. Thus, the crow indulges in all these wrongful activities.

**pēykku itta nīr sōṟum** – food, which is mixed with water, and offered to fiends

**uṇḍaṟku vēṇḍi** – desiring to eat those

**nī ōdit tiriyādē** – don’t roam around, trying to locate those places.

**aṇḍattu amarar perumān** – the eminent entity \[emperumān\] who gives sustenance, nourishment and enjoyment to nityasūris, who dwell in śrī vaikuṇṭam

**aḻagamar vaṇḍottu iruṇḍa kuḻal vārāy** – Oh, crow! Comb the beautiful, divine locks of such entity, which are curled and dark, like beetles.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *vaṇḍu* refers to those who have taken refuge under emperumān. The term *ottu* also indicates that emperumān too takes refuge in them, just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.9.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/09/thiruvaimozhi-9-9-4-paviyen-manaththe/) “*deyva vaṇḍu*” (supreme lord who is like a beetle). emperumān had surrendered to sugrīvan, who had surrendered to emperumān \[in order to kill vāli and to get back his wife\], just as it has been said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 4-19 “*sugrīvam śaraṇam gata*:” ((such śrī rāma) is now taking shelter under sugrīvan) and in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 4-18 “*sugrīvam nātam iccati*” ((such śrī rāma) now accepts the lordship of sugrīvan). In the same manner, in order to make his follower to surrender to him, he surrenders to the same person ahead, just as he had done in the case of varuṇa et al \[samudra rājan, at the seashore, for asking him to give way for his army of monkeys to cross the ocean). How do he and his followers take refuge in each other? Just as it has been said in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/thiruvaimozhi-6-10-10-agalagillen-part-5/) “*alarmēl mangai uṟai mārbā – nigaril amarar*” (one who has a divine chest from which śrī mahālakśmi does not leave even for a moment and who is desired by the matchless nityasūris) or as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.7.8 “*pinnai nedum paṇaittōḷ magiḻ pīdu udai munnai amarar*” (emperumān has the greatness of enjoying the wide, well-rounded shoulders of nappinnaip pirātti and is the leader of nityasūris), they do so in the presence of pirātti or nityasūris. This is also mentioned in periya [tirumoḻi 5.8.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/02/periya-thirumozhi-5-8-1/) “*un tōḻi – umbi nī uganda tōḻan*” (sītāp pirātti is your friend, lakśmaṇa is your brother and you are my friend), when he became friends with guhap perumāḷ, in the presence of sītāp pirātti and lakśmaṇa \[a nityasūris\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai further says that the term *kuḻal* \[as in *iruṇḍa kuḻal*\] refers to *prapatti* \[act of surrendering\] and *irutci* \[darkness\] refers to the depth of the meaning \[of surrendering\] which is not fathomable in emperumān’s divine mind.

**māyavan …** – Comb the divine locks of one, who has amazing activities.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.5.8. Undi elunda

*undi eḻunda uruvam malar tannilcandac cadumugan tannaip padaittavankondak kuḻalaik kuṟandu puḷiyattitandattin seeppāl kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy! dāmōdaran tan kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy!*

**Пословный перевод:**

undi eḻunda – formed in the divine navel; uruvam – beautiful; malar tannil – in the lotus flower; candam – having candas (vēdic text) as his identity; cadumugan tannai – brahmā, who has four faces; padaittavan – one who created; kondam – being curled; kuḻalai – divine locks; puḷi kuṟandu – adding civet perfume; atti – applying it well; tandattin seeppāl – oh, crow! Comb with a comb made of ivory; dāmōdaran than – oh, crow! Comb the locks of dāmōdaran \[kriṣṇa\]

**Перевод:**

**emperumān created brahmā, who has four faces, and who constantly recites the vēdams, in the divine lotus flower, formed in his divine navel. Oh, crow! Comb his divine locks, after applying well the perfume of civet cat, to his divine locks! Comb the divine locks of dāmōdaran.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**undi …** – in the beautiful lotus flower which had formed in the divine navel. *uruvam* – beautiful.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that in the beautiful lotus flower formed in the divine navel, which is the starting point for the creation of all the worlds.

**candam …** – one who created brahmā during the time of creation such that one would have a doubt whether it was emperumān who created the worlds or brahmā who did that. brahmā was created with such distinguished knowledge and power. Here, the term *candam* would refer to beauty. Alternatively, the term could also refer to *candas*, reciting vēdam. Since brahmā has reciting of vēdams as an identity for him, this would refer to the second meaning.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as it has been said in mantra praśnam “*ātmāvai putra nāmāsi*” \[the father is reborn as the son\], due to the superficially close resemblance which brahmā has with emperumān at the time of creation, āḻvār says *candac cadumugan.* āḻvār remembers the earlier pāsuram \[in the first centum, 1.5.3\] *nāviyuḷ naṟkamala nānmuganukku* and follows that here too.

**kondak kuḻalaik kuṟandu puḷiyatti** – During the time of carrying out bath \[as seen in the previous decad\], it is customary to apply tamarind to remove the oil applied during bath. Due to this, the locks would get curled up and entangled. *kondam* – curling densely. Since this is not carried out during the time of combing the locks, it is certain that this had been done during the time of giving bath \[to kriṣṇa\]. We had seen that yaśōdāp pirātti had carried *eṇṇey puḷippaḻam* \[as in 2.4.1\] at the time of giving him a bath. Alternatively, *kondak kuḻalai* would refer to curled up locks which happen when the fragrant material from trumpet flower, obtained from plants grown in houses, is applied to the locks. Thus, it refers to *puḻugu*, a fragrant material. Instead of *kuṟandu puḷiyatti*, if the text were *kuṟandu puḻugatti*, this could be considered as the meaning.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai too says here that this follows the pāsuram mentioned in 2.4.1 *eṇṇeyp puḷip paḻam*, as accessories for giving bath.

**tandattin seeppāl kuḻal vārāy** – āppropirate to the distinction of the divine locks, comb the locks using comb made of ivory.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *tandattin sīppu* refers to the firm belief in knowledge arising out of distinction \[between what is to be carried out and what is to be avoided\]. By carrying out kainkaryam to ācāryan, one will get firm belief in the knowledge of *prapatti* \[surrendering to emperumān\]. \[tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his pravēśam for this tirumoḻi, had already stated that *sīppu* \[comb\] refers to *prapatti.*  It is through this comb \[*prapatti*\] that the fault \[curled entanglement of locks\] in emperumān’s locks \[our wrong belief that emperumān is responsible for our sorrows\] has to be removed. It is through this act that the faults in emperumān’s prapatti get removed \[the affection which emperumān shows towards one who surrenders to emperumān is referred to as emperumān’s *prapatti*. Why should there be any fault in emperumān’s *prapatti*? It is our reasoning that emperumān should grant mōkśam to all \[*sarvamukti praśangam*\], without our having to carry out anything, which is the fault that we heap on emperumān. Through the act of combing his locks, which is our prapatti to emperumān, this fault is removed\]. Since *kuḻal* results in bowing down of the head \[due to its weight\], this *prapatti* \[combing of the locks\] is over the neck.

**dāmōdaran …**– he is such an easy person to approach that he allowed a weak person such as me \[yaśōdāp pirātti\] to tie him down with a rope. Oh, crow! Comb the divine locks of such dāmōdaran.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that emperumān is *paramapadanilaiyan* (one, who is the most eminent, residing in śrī vaikuṇṭam). Having been tied down with a rope by a weak herd-woman \[yaśōdāp pirātti\], even after being released, he had the scar of that rope on his divine waist \[*dāmōdaran* refers to the mark of rope on his divine stomach; he carries that as the affection shown by yaśōdāp pirātti\]. This indicates that when yama removes our *pāśam* \[bondage\] from samsāram, we should get rid of all the bondage \[to worldly pursuits\]. While we listen to the instructions of our preceptors, we do not always lead our lives within those instructions. Though we claim that we have not transgressed those instructions, in their minds \[and in emperumān’s mind\], there will that thought that we have transgressed on occasions. Only then, when the final time times, could we remove ourselves from all the bondage. For āḻvārs, parrots are the most intimate \[they will repeat only that which has been said to them and will not say a word more or less\]. For us too, it should be like that.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.5.9. Mannan tan

*mannan tan dēvimār kaṇḍu magiḻvu eydamun ivvulaginai muṟṟum aḷandavanponnin mudiyinaip pūvaṇaimēl vaittupinnēyirundu kuḻal vāyāy akkākkāy! pērāyirattān kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy!*

**Пословный перевод:**

mannan than – the king of monsters, mahābali, his; dēvimār – consorts; kaṇḍu – looking at his garb and his language; magiḻvu eyda – to rejoice; mun – earlier; ivvulaginai muṟṟum – this entire word; aḷandavan – one who measured; pon mudiyinai – beautiful divine locks \[the term in (as in ponnin) is an augment. It doesn’t have any meaning\]; pū aṇai mēl vaittu – keeping on a soft mattress which is like a flower; pinnē irundu – oh, crow! Stand behind that mattress and comb his locks; āyiram pērān – oh, crow! Comb the divine locks of one who has a thousand divine names

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, as trivikrama \[and as vāmana, before that\] had measured all the worlds such that the consorts of king mahābali rejoiced, looking at emperumān’s outward appearance and the language which he used \[as vāmana\]. Oh, crow! Keep the divine, beautiful locks of that emperumān on a soft mattress and comb it, standing from behind. Oh, crow! Comb the divine locks of one who has a thousand divine names.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**mannan …**– \`the divine form of vāmana was such that it usurped all the senses of beholders, just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 1-8-6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-8-6-kalanthu-ennavi/) “*pulan koḷ māṇāy*” (great form which usurped all the senses). It was further decorated, just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 4.4.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/03/periya-thirumozhi-4-4-7/) “*pongu ilangu puri nūlum*” (radiantly shining sacred thread), with the radiantly splendorous *yajñōpavītam* (sacred thread), deer skin \[on his divine chest\], girdle made of sacred reed \[worn by bachelor brāhmaṇa children). Thus, vāmana walked to the arena where mahābali was conducting rituals, with a hurried walk, resembling the gait of an expert dancer. Looking at his handsome get-up and the gibberish manner of an ignorant child in which he said, as in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.8.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-9-kolvan-nan/) “*koḷvan nān*” (I shall accept the three steps of land which you offer), the consorts of king mahābali rejoiced. He first prayed to mahābali for three steps of land; as soon as water fell on his palm, symbolic of mahābali granting his wish, he measured all the worlds, which were always his, but which appeared as if he was getting now in an extraordinary way.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai adds, in his svāpadēśam, that the consorts of mahābali saw the way vāmana’s lips quivered when he said, as in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.8.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-9-kolvan-nan/) “*koḷvan nān māvali*” (Oh, mahābali! I shall accept your offering), the strangeness in his words \[emperumān is only used to giving to others; he doesn’t accept anything\], the way he came hurriedly to the arena and the way in which he took an oath “You could test my knowledge in vēdas. I shall answer your questions”. It could also be considered as having been seen both by mahābali and his consorts.

Further, for the term *mun kaṇḍu*, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that it was the garb of vāmana that was the reason for their unlimited happiness. When the feet of trivikrama, which they saw later, started expanding and went about measuring everything, they \[mahābali’s consorts\] had only fear and indifference.

For the term *ivvulaginai*, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that āḻvār, as soon as emperumān received his land as a donation, even before he had measured the worlds, says in anxiety, “*ivvulagu*”

**ponnin mudiyinai** – beautiful, divine locks. *pon* – beauty. The term *in* is an augment, added for poetic metrics and does not have any meaning.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here “*ipponmudi*” due to the desire which is manifested on pure gold. Since āḻvār says “*muṟṟum aḷandavan ponnin mudiyan*” he refers to the divine crown which is an indicator for emperumān being the supreme entity. It makes one to move away from being servitor to others and to remove one’s independence, and to be dependent on him, carrying out servitude to emperumān. Then, the crown will be splendorous.

**pūvaṇai mēl vaittu** – Keeping the divine locks, appropriate to its softness, on a soft mattress which was like a flower.

**pinnē irundu kuḻal vārāy akkākkāy** – Oh, crow! Comb his divine locks, by standing behind, which will facilitate the action of combing.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as it has been mentioned in taittirīya upaniśad *nārāyaṇavalli “satyam tapa: dama: śama: dānam dharma: prajnanam agnaya: agnihōtram yajña*: *mānasam nyāsa*:” (there are twelve types of penance) and “*tasmānnyāsam ēśām tapasām atiriktam āhu*:” (It is hence said that *nyāsa* \[prapatti or surrendering to emperumān\] is unequalled). Since *prapatti*, through the word *nyāsa*, has been mentioned right at the end, over all the rest of the types of penance, with each subsequent type being better than the earlier one, it stands at the head, after removing the rest. The same \[*prapatti*\] applies to emperumān’s divine locks, too. The various types of means to attain emperumān are “*karma jñāna bhakti prapatti*” \[attaining emperumān through the paths of deeds, knowledge, devotion and surrendering\] \[Mentioning *prapatti* here, along with *karma jñāna bhakti yōgams* is because when one surrenders to emperumān through the path of *prapatti*, it becomes one among the other *upāyams* \[means\]. We should attain emperumān through emperumān himself. The first *prapatti* is called as *upāya prapatti*, where the one, who surrenders, thinks that he is surrendering to emperumān by attaining his divine feet. Here, the doer is prominent. The other prapatti is called as *adikāri viśēśaṇa prapatti* when we consider emperumān as the *upāyam* and not our action of surrendering to him as the *upāyam*. Here emperumān is prominent. *adikāri* refers to the person who wishes to attain emperumān. *viśēśaṇam* refers to the quality which he should have to attain emperumān, viz. the thought that emperumān is the *upāyam* and not the action of surrendering to him\]. Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruneduntāṇḍakam 10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/11/thirunedunthandakam-10-part-1/) “*pinnānār vaṇangum sōdi*” (the splendorous entity who is vorśipped by those who came after his period of incarnations), he is the radiant entity who is attained by his followers. He has the splendour as his quality right from the beginning while his followers derive that radiance after attaining him. Thus, for both, *prapatti* is at the head \[for emperumān, *prapatti* refers to his attempts to get the ātmā under him forever; in physical sense, this refers to his divine locks. For us, attaining emperumān, considering him as the *upāyam* \[and not our act of surrendering to him\] should be at the top of our mind. Thus, for both, this is at the top\].

The term *pinnē* \[from behind\] has been explained by tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, as follows: yaśōdāp pirātti feels “If the crow comes in the front and combs kriṣṇa’s divine locks, he may get scared”. Hence, she says *pinnē*. āḻvār feels that even though persons who are like crows \[in terms of *tamō rajō guṇams*\] come after correcting themselves, they could not be trusted fully. Hence, he tells them to go back \[behind\]. Since these persons would have carried out *prapatti* before attaining noble qualities \[as seen earlier in the taittirīya upaniśad nārāyaṇavalli verse *satyam tapa*: *dama:* etc\] \[through an ācāryan\], they would be fearful, not having such noble qualities “Have we carried out the right activity? Is this sufficient for us”. They will hesitate to take shelter under their ācaryan’s affection too. It is for this reason that *prapatti* has been ordained for both the *ārta prapannan* \[one who is unable to tolerate remaining in samsāram and desires to attain emperumān at once\] and *drupta prapannan* \[one who is willing to wait to attain emperumān, enjoying his stay in samsāram\] as a means to get rid of the hurdles in attaining emperumān.

**pēr āyirattān** – for those who praise him, looking at his distinction, he appears like a bathing ghat for each of the divine names which they recite, just as it has been mentioned in mahābhāratam sabhā parvam 38.11 “*dēvō nāma sahasravān*” (he is the lord with a thousand divine names). Oh, crow! Comb the divine locks of such a distinguished emperumān.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here the following: even if his \[emperumān’s\] simplicity has been mentioned, his identification has to be established. āḻvār remembers the verse in 1.3.8 “*nārāyaṇā aḻēl*”. Even before identifying the entity, she \[yaśōdāp pirātti\] comforted him, offering him milk from her bosom and telling him not to cry. emperumān thinks “She considers me as her son and offers me her milk and tells me not to cry”. The other one \[pūtanā\] considered him as her enemy and offered him poisoned bosom. He drank from both. Only if āḻvār mentions *nārāyaṇa,* would the entity get established. It was this *mantram* \[nārayaṇa mantram\] which was referred to by prahlādan, as mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 2.3.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/08/periya-thirumozhi-2-3-8/) “*vāyil ōr āyira nāmam oḷḷīyavāgip pōda*” (from his divine lips, a thousand names came out beautifully). Here, the term *oḷḷiya* \[beautiful\] confirms that for both removal of undesired hurdles and for attainment of desired benefit, this *tirunāmam* \[divine name\] is the means. It is this divine name, which is referred to as thousand names, that yaśōdāp pirātti mentioned as *pēr āyirattān*. Mentioning this thousand is in alignment with āḻvār’s tiruppallāṇḍu pāsuram “*vandu adi toḻudu āyira nāmam*” \[āḻvār tells emperumān’s followers to come, worship emperumān’s divine feet and recite his thousand divine names\].

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.5.10. Kandar paliyame

*kaṇḍār paḻiyāmē akkākkāy! kārvaṇṇanvaṇḍār kuḻal vāra vā enṟa āycci solviṇ tōy madiḷ villibuttūrk kōn battan solkoṇḍādip pāda kuṟugā vinai tāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

akkākkāy – oh, crow!; kaṇḍār paḻiyāmē – “such that people do not blame; vaṇḍu Ar – settled upon by beetles; kuḻal – divine locks; vāra – to comb; vā enṟa – come”, one who called; āycci – yaśōdāp pirātti’s; sol – words; viṇ tōy – reaching to the sky; madiḷ – having compound walls; villibuttūr – for śrī villibuttūr; kōn – one, who is the controller; battan – periyāḻvār; sol – these pāsurams, mercifully given by him; koṇḍādi – praising the distinguished meanings of the words; pāda – when they sing; vinaigaḷ – those which are called as \[evil\] deeds; kuṟugā – will not even get in their proximity

**Перевод:**

**yaśōdāp pirātti had told the crow “Come and comb the divine locks of kriṣṇa, who has the complexion of a bluish cloud, such that none blames you”. periyāḻvār, who is the controller of śrī villibuttūr, where the compound walls reach to the sky, composed her words mercifully into these pāsurams. Evil deeds will not go anywhere near those who  sing these pāsurams, praising the distinguished meanings of the worlds.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In this final pāsuram, āḻvār mentions the benefit which accrues to those who recite these pāsurams and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kaṇḍār …** – once divine bath had been given, if the divine locks were not combed, those who saw this would have blamed. Such that they did not blame …

**akkākkāy kār vaṇṇan …** – kriṣṇa has a form which is dark like the bluish cloud. Beetles have settled on his divine locks. The words of yaśōdāp pirātti called the crow to comb the locks which were like beetles in their curliness and complexion.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that since āḻvār had already described kriṣṇa’s complexion as being dark, by using the term *vaṇḍār kuḻal*, he refers to the swarming of beetles on his divine locks since his locks will always be decorated with flowers \[and beetles will come swarming to those flowers to imbibe their honey\]. *akkākkāy vāra vā enṟa āycci sol* – the manner in which yaśōdāp pirātti had changed the crying of kriṣṇa and called the crow to comb his divine locks.

**viṇ tōy …** – these pāsurams have been mercifully composed by periyāḻvār, who is the controller of śrī villibuttūr, which has the tallest compound walls reaching the sky

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the words in these pāsurams are the *svāpadēśa mangaḷāśāsanam* \[in āḻvār’s opinion, these verses call upon people to carry out servitude to emperumān\] of āḻvār, who is the controller of the divine mansion, whose compound wall reaches the tallest, into the sky.

**koṇḍādi …** – evil deeds, which are termed as *vinai*, will not come anywhere near those, who sing these pāsurams, with affection, praising the distinction of the words and their meanings

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that for one who praises these pāsurams “How great is this word! How great is the meaning! How great is the *svāpadēśam* \[meaning in āḻvār’s opinion!” \[we have seen in these pāsurams, through tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai’s svāpadēśam that beetles refer to *prapannars* \[those who come to emperumān to surrender\], combing action of the crow refers to removing the entanglements which we have superimposed on emperumān through our words that emperumān alone is responsible for our plight, the comb made of ivory refers to instructions given by our ācāryan etc\], even if one were to sing these pāsurams as an outlet for one’s arrogance \[that he is singing āḻvār’s pāsurams\], since these are āḻvār’s mangaḷāśāsanam …

**kuṟugā vinai tāmē** – āḻvār considered those who have excess of *tāmasa guṇam* \[having characteristics of sleeping, postposing things etc\] and *tāmasa rājasa guṇam* \[apart from the previously said characteristics, having additionally the qualities of passion, anger etc\] as being equivalent to crows; he corrects such persons by telling them about the faults which they had not known; he removed the faults arising out of attaining emperumān through the paths of *bhakti* \[devotion\] and *prapatti* \[surrendering to emperumān, considering the act of surrendering as the reason for emperumān granting us *mōkśam*\]; he confirmed that it is emperumān who is the *pratama sukrutam* \[the one who primarily thinks good of us and wishes well for us\] and *taniyēn vāḻmudal* \[this is from nammāḻvār’s pāsuram, saying that emperumān is the reason for my life proceeding in the correct path\], by making the crow to comb the divine locks of kriṣṇa as a pretext and removing the faults which we have superimposed on emperumān. Since he has made the samsāris to be mangaḷāśāsanaparars by pointing out all these to the samsāris, he has manifested his affection too for them. For those who praise these ways of āḻvār, the evil deeds of hurdles which come in the way of carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam to emperumān will not come anywhere near them. Through the term *vaṇḍu*, āḻvār refers to *prapannan* and through the term *vaṇḍār kuḻal*, āḻvār refers to the bowing down of head by emperumān, as he attains the samsāri.

We shall next consider the pravēśam of the next tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.6.1. Velikkol vetti

*vēlikkōl vetti viḷaiyādu villēṟṟittālik koḻundait tadam kazuttil pūṇḍupeelit taḻaiyaip piṇaittup piṟagittukkālippin pōvāṟkōr kōl koṇḍu vā kadal niṟa vaṇṇaṟkōr kōl koṇḍu vā*

**Пословный перевод:**

vēli – grown in the fence; kōl – stick; vetti – cutting it; viḷaiyādu vil – making it like a bow, to play with; ēṟṟi – stringing it; tāli – palm tree’s; koḻundai – white tender leaves; tada kaḻuttil – in the huge neck; pūṇḍu – donning it like an ornament; peeli – peacock’s; taḻaiyai – feathers; piṇaittu – stringing them together; piṟagu – on the divine back; ittu – hanging them; kālip pin – behind calves; pōvāṟku – bring a stick for the one who goes, grazing; kadal niṟam – the complexion similar to an ocean’s; vaṇṇaṟku – to the one who has a form, bring a stick. (if the term is considered as aṇṇaṟku, it would mean ‘lord’)

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa has snapped a stick from the plants growing in the fence. He has made it into a bow, by stringing it, such that he could play with it. He has decorated himself with white tender leaves of palm tree around his neck, as an ornament, and has hung large number of peacock feathers on his divine back. Oh, crow! Get a stick for this kriṣṇa, to enable him to go behind calves for grazing. Get a stick for one who has the complexion of the ocean.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vēlikkōl vetti** – cutting the sticks from plants which are growing in the fence. Alternatively, *vēli* would refer to curved form. Hence, cutting curved sticks.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the term *vēr* refers to bamboo. Here, that term has got transformed to *vēl* and along with the addition of the syllable *i*, it now has become *vēli*, referring to a bamboo stick. Curving it in the form of a bow, in order to play with it and stringing it.

**viḷaiyādu villēṟṟi** – making the stick in the form of a bow, for the purpose of playing, and stringing it.

**tālik koḻundait tadam kaḻuttil pūṇḍu** – being appropriate for his clan, wearing a distinguished golden ornament, in the form of turtle, on his huge neck. Alternatively, the term *tāli* would also be read as *tāḷi*, referring to tender leaves of palm tree. Being white in colour, it would appear like a silver ornament. Herd-people will wear it on their necks.

**peeli …** – gathering the feathers of peacock, and hanging them from the divine back.

**kāli …** – Bring a stick for the one who goes behind calves, in order to graze them.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār tells the crow not to hide the stick \[sceptre\] meant for kriṣṇa and to bring it. Through this, āḻvār tells samsāris not to change his order \[*nitya* and *naimittika karmas* in following vēdams\] as one of *kāmya karma*. He tells them \[through the crow\] to bring the sceptre, which is symbolic of *sankalpa svasvātantryam* \[his will, derived out of his total independence\] with which he protects *paśuprāyars* \[those who are as good as animals in looking up to him for their protection\].

**kadal …** – Bring a stick for the one who has the form of an ocean, with its colour.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.6.2. Kongum kudandaiyum

*kongum kudandaiyum kōttiyūrum pērumengum tirindu viḷaiyādum en magansangam pidikkum tadak kaikkut takka nalangam koṇḍhadōr kōl koṇḍu vā arakku vaḻittadōr kōl koṇḍu vā*

**Пословный перевод:**

kongu – having fragrance (due to flowers etc); kudandaiyum – in tirukkudandai \[present day kumbakōṇam\] \[a divine abode\]; kōtti ūrum – in tirukkōśtiyūr \[another divine abode\]; pērum – in tiruppēr nagar \[another divine abode\]; engum – in other divine abodes too; tirindu – being active; viḷaiyādum – one who is playing; en magan – my son’s; pidikkum – holding; tada – broad; kaikku – for the divine hand; takka – being apt; nal angam udaiyadu – bring a stick which has an eminent form; arakku vaḻittadu – bring a stick which has been painted with lac

**Перевод:**

**My son plays actively in divine abodes such as tirukkudandai, tirukkōśtiyūr, tiruppēr etc, which have plenty of fragrance, arising from flowers. He is holding the divine conch, śrī pancajanyam, in his broad, divine left hand. Bring a stick which has an eminent form and will be apt for that divine hand. Bring a stick which has been painted with lac.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kongum kudandaiyum** – In tirukkudandai, which is having fragrance. The term *kongukkudandai* has got transformed to *kongum kudandai*. The fragrance from the orchards and streams in that place as well as the fragrance emanating from the divine form of the one who is reclining in that place \[emperumān\] make the entire town to be fragrant.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that tirukkudandai has orchards where the fragrance will never disappear. It is such a place where the flowers and their fragrance will never change. It is similar to periya tirumoḻi 10.10.8 pāsuram “*kongār tirukkudandai*” (the divine abode of tirukkudandai where the orchards are full of honey). The *um* syllable \[as in *kongum*\], could also be considered to be *E* \[*kongē*\], which would mean that it is fully permeated only with fragrance. Alternatively, the term *kongu* could be taken as referring to western direction, which is also the divine abode of emperumān \[as in *mēl tisai ninṟa aḻundūr*; emperumān who is dwelling in tiruvaḻundūr, which is in the proximity on the western side of *kudandai*\]. āḻvār is combining the eminence of *tiruvaḻundūr* with *tirukkudandai*.

**kōttiyūrum** – in tirukkōśtiyūr also

**pērum** – as well as in tiruppēr nagar

**engum** – in other divine abodes too, which have not been explicitly mentioned.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that out of affection towards *adiyārs* \[his followers\], emperumān goes to all the divine abodes. If the *adiyārs* do not surrender to him and attain him, he would consider that \[going to various divine abodes\] as a playful activity.

**tirindu viḷaiyādum en magan** – my son, who is playfully roaming around in all these places.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as protector-protected connection gets reversed \[āḻvār considers emperumān as the entity to be protected and himself as the protector of emperumān\], āḻvār reverses the cause and effect relationship too and calls emperumān as *en magan* \[emperumān is the creator and we are the created; however, āḻvār considers emperumān as his son\].

**sangam pidikkum tadakkaikkut takka** – apt for the huge divine hand, which is holding the divine conch, śrī pāncajanyam.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that śrī pāncajanyam, the divine conch of emperumān, is dear to him, and carries out mangaḷāśāsanam to emperumān from close quarters. It is through his divine disc and divine conch that emperumān carries out his orders, as mentioned in [tiruviruttam 33](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/01/thiruviruththam-33/) “*agal visumbum nilanum –  sengōl nadāvudir*” (you are ruling the expansive sky and earth through your divine disc). It is the divine conch, which is on his divine left hand, as mentioned in [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 71](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/01/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-71/) “*idangai valamburi ninṟārppa*” (the divine conch, standing on his divine left hand, blew vociferously), which blows, beyond emperumān’s control, towards those who do not listen to emperumān’s orders. It is such a divine conch that he is holding in his divine hand. āḻvār asks the people \[at large\] “The sceptre is his. Is it yours?” \[He is equating the stick, which yaśōdāp pirātti wants the crow to bring for kriṣṇa, to emperumān’s sceptre\]. It is only when he holds it that it would remain as a great entity, with distinction. When it remains on their hands, apart from looking ordinary, it would also look faulty in its form. He tells them that if they wish to be protected, just like animals, they should hand over the divine sceptre to him and live under the sceptre.

**nal angam udaiyadu ōr kōk koṇḍu vā** – bring a stick, which has an eminent form

**arakku vaḻittadu ōr kōl koṇḍu vā** – bring a stick, which has a good colour, painted with lac.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that periyāḻvār reminds all that it \[the stick\] is identified with lac. Understand that it is a stick which controls everyone. It appears spectacular to look at. If the identification disappears \[here, the identification referred to is emperumān’s svātantryam which comes with holding the sceptre in his hand\], it would lose its beauty. The sceptre not only refers to refuge. If the identification \[emperumān’s svātantryam\] is lost, it would lead to loss of protection for all of us \[it is only through his uncontrolled svātantryam that emperumān protects us all\].

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.6.3. Karuttittu edirninra

*kaṟuttittu edir ninṟa kanjanaik konṟānpoṟuttittu edir vanda puḷḷin vāy kīṇḍānneṟitta kuḻalgaḷai nīnga munnōdisiṟukkanṟu mēyppadōr kōl koṇḍu vā dēvapirānukku ōr kōl koṇḍu vā*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṟuttu – being full of anger; edirittu ninṟa – one who came to fight; kanjanai – kamsan; konṟān – one who killed; poṟuttittu – while \[bird was\] coming, kriṣṇa reduced the bird’s speed; edir vanda – one who came to harm; puḷḷin – bakāsura’s; vāy kīṇḍān – one who tore his mouth; neṟitta – hanging in the front, tightly; kuḻalgaḷ – divine locks \[the syllable ai in kuḻalgaḷai doesn’t have a meaning; it is a metric for the poem\]; nīnga – swaying on both sides while running; mun ōdi – running ahead of the calves; siṟu kanṟu – young calves; mēyppārkku – bring a stick, for the one who is going to graze; dēvar pirānukku – bring a stick for the one who is a benefactor for the celestial entities

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa killed kamsan who came, full of anger, to fight with him. He tore the mouth of bakāsuran who came to harm him, slowing him down a bit while coming. Bring a stick for the one who is running ahead of young calves, in order to graze them, with his divine locks swaying on either side. Bring a stick for the one who is the benefactor for celestial entities.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kaṟuttu …** – *kaṟuppu* – fury. kriṣṇa killed kamsan who came to fight him, with anger.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that just as tirumangai āḻvār had said in [periya tirumoḻi 7-7-7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/11/periya-thirumozhi-7-7-7/) “*kaṟuttuk kanjanai anja munindāy*” (kamsan became frightened of your anger; you killed him), kamsan was awaiting kriṣṇa’s incarnation, with a drawn sword to kill him as soon as he incarnated. Alternatively, in an earlier birth, kamsan had been born as *kālanēmi*. He came with anger, opposing emperumān. The scent of that anger was still lingering in this birth too, as kamsan. After seeing all his supporters getting killed by kriṣṇa, with none left to send, kamsan decided to bring kriṣṇa through akrūrar. When kriṣṇa came to maturā, with akrūrar, kamsan stood opposing him, for the first time, directly.

**poṟuttu …** – bakāsuran, came to harm kriṣṇa \[with the form of a crane\]. When he came flying fast, kriṣṇa slowed him down and tore his mouth.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that bakāsuran came in the form of a crane, with his mouth wide open, crying aloud to harm kriṣṇa. Effortlessly, kriṣṇa tore his mouth and protected himself.

**neṟitta …** – while running ahead of the calves, when he was grazing them, kriṣṇa’s divine locks, which were curled up tightly and were hanging in the front, swayed from side to side

**siṟukkanṟu …**– Bring a stick for one who is going to graze young calves.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the young calves were not only not involved in protecting themselves, they vouldn’t even know how to eat grass. Hence, kriṣṇa would take some grass in his hands, squeeze them well, and put them into the mouth of the calf. When the calf eats it, he would be happy. This is how he was grazing the young calves.

**dēva pirānukku** – since he destroyed monsters such as kamsan et al, he became a benefactor for celestial entities. Bring a stick for such an entity.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār says that kriṣṇa is the benefactor for both the entities in leelā vibhūti \[samsāram\] who look up to him for their protection and the nityasūris in nitya vibhūti, thus being the benefactor for both the realms.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.6.4. Onre uraippan

*onṟē uraippān oru sollē solluvāntunṟu mudiyān duriyōdanan pakkalsenṟu angup pāradam kai eṟindānukkukanṟugaḷ mēyppadōr kōl koṇḍu vā kadal niṟa vaṇṇaṟkōr kōl koṇḍu vā*

**Пословный перевод:**

onṟē – the only assurance that he will not let go of others; uraippān – as one, who says; oru sollē – the word by which he gives protection to everyone; solluvān – as one, who said; tunṟu – embellished with nine gemstones; mudiyān – having crown; duriyōdanan pakkal – to duryōdana; senṟu – going as the messenger of pāṇḍavas; bāradam – for mahābhārata war; angu – there; kai eṟindānukku – one, who came after placing his hands; kanṟugaḷ – calves; mēyppadōr – bring a stick which is apt for grazing; bring a stick for one, who has the complexion of an ocean

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is one who confirms through his words that he will not let go of others. He will say only one word of giving protection to everyone. He went as the messenger of pāṇḍavas, to duryōdana, who wears a crown embellished with nine gemstones. He confirmed that they will meet in the mahābhārata war. Bring a stick which is apt for one, who grazes calves. Bring a stick for one who has the complexion of an ocean.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**onṟē …** – duryōdana would convey only one meaning, saying “pāṇḍavas and we would not be able to live together”. If a few neutral persons asked “Even if you do not live together, should you not grant them a few entitlements?” he would say “We cannot grant them even that much of land where a pole could be grounded”. Alternatively, considering that these apply with emperumān, he would say only one word, just as it has been said in śrī rāmāyaṇam. yudda kāṇḍam 18-3 “*mithra bhāvēna samprāptam*” (even if a person comes in the guise of a friend, I will not let him down). He will give his word that he would protect all, just as he had mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18-33 “*abhayam sarva bhūtēbhyō*” (I grant protection from all entities).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, gives the meaning for this with respect to duryōdana. Whether duryōdana is having *rajas* and *tamas* characteristics or when he \[rarely\] has *satva* characteristics, he will only speak words of enmity. Even if one were to employ the methods of *sāma, dāna, bhēda* and *daṇḍa* \[to convince through conversation, gift, creating a difference of opinion and punishment, respectively\], it is only enmity which is deeply embedded in his heart. *satyavādis* \[those who speak only the truth always\], even when under the influence of the three characteristics of *satva, rajas* and *tamas* are expected to speak only one word, the truth. However, even they may, in order to protect a righteous entity, dither on occasions. śrī rāma, when he incarnated in the human species, carried out his activities in line with that. He always protected the righteous and did not change his words or his stance, based on the prevailing situation. duryōdana was like that. Whether the land sought was ten villages or five villages or one village, he had only one response, which was in the negative, even when said with different words \[conveying the same meaning\].

**tunṟu mudiyān** – one who has his crown embellished with closely strung gemstones. He is vorśipped by kings who have coronated with crowns.

**duriyōdanan pakkal** – to duryōdana, who is as stated above.

**senṟu angup pāradam kai eṟindānukku** – kriṣṇa went as pāṇḍavas’ messenger to that duryōdana, thinking whether he could bring about a compromise between the two sides. However, since duryōdana was not keen on making amends and was steadfast on engaging in war, kriṣṇa said “If that is the case, let it be so” and touched duryōdana’s hand, when he was steadfast on war, with his hand. Alternatively, when duryōdana was firm on war, kriṣṇa agreed to that; he then assisted pāṇḍavas in the war with his carioteering work and various formations of the army fronts. *eṟidal* – placing. Either of the two meanings could be considered.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa went to duryōdana and tried several times to convince him to agree to a peaceful existence. But since duryōdana was not agreeable for it and was firm on war, and since war is also a righteous act for a royal clan, duryōdana told kriṣṇa to accept war and as a symbol of kriṣṇa’s acceptance, told him to press his hands. Just as one tries through various means to know the inner thoughts of a person, kriṣṇa too employed similar tactics to confirm that it was only war which was in duryōdana’s mind and pressed his hand. After agreeing for war with duryōdana, kriṣṇa assisted pāṇḍavas through his carioteering and army formations, during the war.

**kanṟugaḷ mēyppadōr kōl koṇḍu vā** – kriṣṇa prefers grazing calves to cows \[since they look up only to him for protection\]. Bring a stick, which is appropriate for that.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that calves cannot even graze the grass. Someone has to pluck the grass, squeeze the grass in the hands and put that inside their mouths and see if that goes inside. emperumān’s divine mind would engage with such entities only, who could not protect themselves. Bring a unique stick for that kriṣṇa, such that his complexion, which matches an ocean’s, does not wear off.

**kadal niṟa vaṇṇaṟkōr kōl koṇḍu vā** – Bring a stick for one, who has a form with the complexion of an ocean.

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.6.5. Sironru tuday

*sīr onṟu tūdāy duriyōdanan pakkalūr onṟu vēṇḍip peṟāda urōdattālpār onṟip pāradam kai seydu pārttaṟkuttēr onṟai ūrndāṟku ōr kōl koṇḍu vā dēva pirānukku ōr kōl koṇḍu vā*

**Пословный перевод:**

sīr – the quality of being dependent on followers; onṟu – as part of being together; tūdāy – engaging with the activity of being a messenger; duriyōdanan pakkal – approaching duryōdana; Ur onṟu – “Give, at the least, one village to the pāṇḍavas”; vēṇḍi – despite requesting, from a lowly level; peṟāda – not having obtained, as requested; urōdattāl – with fury; pār onṟi – keeping his divine feet on earth; bāradam – in the mahābhārata war; pārttaṟku – for arjuna; kai seydu – being the support; onṟu tērai – a unique chariot; ūrndāṟku – bring a stick for one who mercifully conducted. Bring a stick for the benefactor of celestial entities

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa has the quality of being dependent on his followers. Exhibiting this quality towards pāṇḍavas, he went as a messenger to duryōdana. Lowering his status, he requested duryōdana to “Grant, at the least, one village for the pāṇḍavas”. With the fury of his request having been denied, he remained as a support for arjuna, planting his feet well, on the earth. Bring a stick for that kriṣṇa who mercifully conducted arjuna’s unique chariot and who is the benefactor for celestial entities.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**sīr onṟu tūdāy** – Just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 2-2-3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/08/periya-thirumozhi-2-2-3/) “*innār tūdan ena ninṟān*” (He stood as the messenger of pāṇḍavas), kriṣṇa engaged with the activity of going as a messenger, in order to establish the fact that he is dependent on his followers.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that emperumān’s auspicious quality of being dependent on his followers will hold true only if he acts in accordance with his incarnation in the human species. It is only if he is together with his divine quality could he share that with all. It is only to create such an eventuality that he went ahead as a messenger for the pāṇḍavas. It is because kriṣṇa went as a messenger that the pāṇḍavas too had their little bit of qualities intact with them. Had he refused to go as their messenger, the pāṇḍavas too could have spoken amongst themselves “Is he a proper royal person?” Alternatively, draupadi had surrendered to him during the game of dice between the pāṇḍavas and kauravas when she said as in mahābhāratam sabhā parvam “*dvārakā nilayācyuta*”. If that divine name \[*acyuta*, one who does not let go of his followers\] has to hold steadfast brightly, he has to go as a messenger. ānoterinterpretation – just as it has been said in [periya tirumoḻi 2-2-3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/08/periya-thirumozhi-2-2-3/) “*innār tūdan ena ninṟān*” (He stood as the messenger of pāṇḍavas), to align with his basic nature, he had to go as a messenger. His basic nature is one of *pāratantryam* \[being dependent\] based on *nirankuśa svātantryam* \[uncontrolled independence\]. It is only through this that he would fulfil his role. When he sets out on a task, there is none who could stop him. This is his nature of *āśrita pāratantryam* \[being dependent on his followers\]. While arjuna was a *sāparāda svatantryan* (independent entity, with faults) \[his faults were that he considered *adarmam* as *darmam* by telling kriṣṇa that he would abstain from engaging in battle when his *darmam*, as one belonging to the clan of warriors, was to engage in war; he showed qualities of friendship with people who were not appropriate to be friendly; he showed compassion towards people who were not to be shown compassion\], despite this, by surrendering himself to kriṣṇa, arjuna thought that he had auspicious qualities. kriṣṇa was also similar. While he was the most eminent entity, being the repository of the word *aham* \[I am the most independent\], he converted himself to say *mām* \[I am your dependent; I shall carry out your tasks\]. It is when he was said to be, as in [stōtra ratnam 20](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/sthothra-rathnam-20/) “*tvadāśritānām…*” (for your followers…) and *pāṇḍavadūtan* that he stood firmly on earth. Just as a person, who conducts a ritual with the permission of brāhmaṇas and with water as the symbol for offering wealth, feels happy that he has completed the ritual, even though he has lost his wealth, emperumān too, by offering his wealth \[vēdas etc\] to his followers \[such as brahmā et al\], feels happy on being a *pāratantryan* \[based on his *nirankuśa svātantryam*\].

**duriyōdanan pakkal Ur onṟu vēṇḍi** – duryōdana was *adārmika* \[not following the path of righteousness\]. He wanted to live with his strength, oppressing his relatives \[pāṇḍavas\]. kriṣṇa went to that duryōdana and told him “You could share the wealth which is there and live together”. When duryōdana refused, kriṣṇa told him “In that case, give them ten villages”. He declined this. When kriṣṇa told him “Give them one village”, refusing to give even this, duryōdana told kriṣṇa, harshly “They \[referring to pāṇḍavas\] have the path of righteousness. They have access to the lands of svargam \[heaven\] etc as a consequence of their righteous nature. We have only this much. There is nothing that we could offer from this”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here – we all know the activities indulged in by duryōdana when kriṣṇa went to him as pāṇḍavas’ messenger – reference here is to the false seat which duryōdana had set for kriṣṇa \[to kill him\], his pledge to arrest kriṣṇa etc. When duryōdana finally said that he would not offer anything to pāṇḍavas and that the victorious people can rule the earth, kriṣṇa was happy that the purpose for which he set out as a messenger had fructified \[to fulfil the pledge of draupadi\].

**peṟāda urōdattāl** – kriṣṇa was furious that he did not get even one village for the pāṇḍavas. He said “īsn’t *vasundarā* \[bhūmip pirātti, representative deity for earth\] the one who celebrates the victorious? Let the victor rule over the earth” duryōdana too agreed for the war.

**pār onṟi** – kriṣṇa was much pleased in his divine mind with the turn of events \[only if there is a war, could pāṇḍavas win it and draupadi could be made to plait her locks again\]. He stood firmly, on earth, with his divine feet.

**pārttaṟkut tēr onṟai ūrndāṟku ōr kōl koṇḍu vā** – Since kriṣṇa had given his word that he will not wield any weapon, he made arjuna to be the *rati* \[warrior\] and he took control of the unique chariot as *sārati* \[one who conducts the chariot\], killing the enemies through the wheels of the chariot itself. Bring a stick, for such kriṣṇa.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that arjuna was that capable person, who had also dropped his bow and arrows, just as it has been mentioned in [bhagavat gītā 1-47](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/1-47/) “*visrujya sa śaram cāpam*” (casting aside the bow, along with the arrows, arjuna sat on the chariot).

**dēvapirānukku ōr kōl koṇḍu vā** – He is also the controller of nityasūris, an eminence which is the exact opposite of the simplicity just mentioned \[as arjuna’s *sārati*\]. Thus, this speaks about his eminence even when he incarnated in the human species.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan
