## 2.6.6. Alattu ilaiyan

*ālattu ilaiyān aravin aṇai mēlānneelak kadaluḷ nedum kālam kaṇ vaḷarndānpālap pirāyattē pārtaṟku aruḷ seydakōlap pirānukku ōr kōl koṇḍu vā kudandaik kidandāṟku ōr kōl koṇḍu vā*

**Пословный перевод:**

Al ilaiyān – as one who is reclining on a tender banyan leaf (in the term ‘ālattu’, the term attu is present as a poetic metric and does not carry any meaning); aravu aṇai mēlān – as one who is reclining on tiruvanantāḻvān \[ādiśēśan\] \[here too, the term ‘in’ in aravin does not have a meaning; it is present for poetic metric\]; neelam – being dark (due to the shadow from the divine form); kadaluḷ – in the ocean; nedu kālam – until the time of deluge; kaṇ vaḷarndān – as one who is reclining; pālap pirāyattu – at young age; pārttaṟku – for arjuna; aruḷ seyda – one who showered his grace mercifully; kōlam – being beautiful; pirānukku – bring a stick for the one who is the benefactor for the world; kudandai – in tirukkudandai \[present day kumbakōṇam\]; kidandāṟku – bring a stick for one who is mercifully reclining

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is one, who is reclining mercifully on a tender banyan leaf. He is mercifully reclining on tiruvanantāḻvān. He is reclining on the ocean, which is dark \[due to the shadow cast by his divine form\], until the time of deluge. Bring a stick for one, who is beautiful, who showered his mercy on arjuna at his young age and who is the benefactor for the world. Bring a stick for one, who is mercifully reclining in tirukkudandai.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**ālattu ilaiyān** – when deluge came to destroy all the worlds, emperumān mercifully reclined on a banyan leaf. As seen earlier, the term *attu* is a *sāriyai* – it is added to keep with the metrics of the poem and does not carry any meaning.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says here that just as the incarnation of kriṣṇa, ādiśēśan too, as said in [mudal tiruvandādi 53](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/08/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-53/) “*senṟāl kudaiyām*” (when emperumān walks, ādiśēśan goes as the umbrella), incarnated, esoterically, as a banyan leaf, indicating the meaning for this pāsuram. periyavāccān piḷḷai would say that “poygai āḻvār prays to emperumān and asks him ‘*ālanṟu vēlai nīr uḷḷadō viṇṇadō maṇṇadō sōlai sūḻ kunṟu eduttāy sollu’*” (Oh emperumān! Only you should say as to how that banyan leaf came on that day. Did it come in the ocean, or did it come in the unsupported sky or did it come out of the \[dissolved\] earth?) In the term *ālattu*, the term *attu* is a sāriyai. If it is considered as a case \[as in *ālāna attinudaiya*\], it will be an indicative word, showing the reason for the leaf.

**aravin aṇai mēlān** – he also mercifully reclines on the mattress of tiruvanantāḻvān \[ādiśēśan\]. Just as the saying goes “*sahasra vadana*: *dēva*: *paṇāmaṇi virājita*: l *sa Eva vatavrukśō bhūt ananta*: *adbhuta rūpavān*” (ādiśēśan has a thousand faces through which he delivers thousand divine speeches; he is a nityasūri; he is resplendent with his spread hoods; he is also the banyan tree; such ādiśēśan is without an end and has an amazing form), it is only ādiśēśan who also is the banyan leaf. Since the pāsuram says *ālattu ilayān aravin aṇai mēlān* that meaning also holds good.

**neelak kadaluḷ nedum kālam kaṇ vaḷarndān** – Though the ocean is inherently white in colour, being the milky ocean \[where emperumān reclines\], due to reflection from emperumān’s divine form, the colour of the ocean appears to be blue. He reclined mercifully on that ocean, until the time of deluge. Just as it has been said in [periya tirumoḻi 3.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2022/05/periya-thirumozhi-3-1-1/) “*karum taṇ mākadal kaṇ tuyinṟavan*” (one who reclined on the dark, cool, expansive ocean) and in [mūnṟām tiruvandādi 37](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/04/munram-thiruvandhadhi-37/) “*uvarkkum karum kadal nīr uḷḷān*”(emperumān is mercifully reclining in the dark ocean which is salty), we could consider that emperumān is reclining on the salty ocean \[instead of the first meaning considered here, where due to his reflection, the milky ocean has acquired a bluish colour\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *neelak kadal* could refer either to the normal \[salty\] ocean or the milky ocean which has turned dark due to reflection from emperumān’s divine form, just as it has been said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.2.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/thiruvaimozhi-7-2-11-mugil-vannan/) “*mugil vaṇṇa vānam*” (due to the colour of emperumān’s divine form, the \[spiritual\] sky is also dark in colour). When milky ocean was churned \[during *krita yugam*\] many herbs were dropped in the ocean to get nectar. Due to these herbs, the colour of ocean had become blue. If one says that the colour which was manifested during *krita yugam* will not hold good during *kali yugam* \[when āḻvār had composed this pāsuram\], it could be said that since āḻvār had seen that blue colour \[due to emperumān’s causeless devotion-based-knowledge\], he is referring to that. Though good qualities and faults are incidental, they could be referred to, as long as the person who has those qualities and faults lives. In the same way, the ocean could be termed as blue, even now. If the reference is to the salty ocean, just as it has been said in periya tirumoḻi 3.1.1 “*karundaṇ mā kadal kaṇ tuyinṟavan*” and in mūnṟām tiruvandādi 37 “*uvarkkum karum kadal nīr uḷḷān*” \[we have seen above, the meanings for these pāsurams\], this is also true since emperumān reclines in all the oceans. In an ocean of this type, just as it has been said as *aravin aṇai mēlān*, he mercifully reclined, in *yōga nidrā* \[resting while reclining\], thinking about protecting the worlds.

**bālap pirāyattē pārttaṟku aruḷ seyda** – Since indra \[celestial head\] came and pointing out arjuna, told emperumān “He is my son; you should mercifully protect him”, right from young age, kriṣṇa was protecting arjuna. During later years, since arjuna became friendly with emperumān and lived under his protective care, kriṣṇa took extra care in the case of arjuna, unlike the others. Thus, that mercy grew up with time.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa had been supportive of arjuna for several reasons: (1) due to indra’s request to take care of him since arjuna was his son, (2) since he was biased towards arjuna, (3) since arjuna was listening to his words, (4) from the time when the pāṇḍavas were brought up along with servants of drutarāśtra in a shed, kriṣṇa was reminding the pāṇḍavas about what they had forgotten, and later, after they had grown up, due to draupadi’s pledge \[that she will plait her locks only with the blood of duśāsan\] and (5) with overwhelming mercy. It was for these reasons that kriṣṇa mercifully gave bhagavat gītā to kriṣṇa, on the chariot.

**kōlap pirānukku** – the beautiful benefactor. He manifested his unique, beautiful, divine form, which is beyond one’s sense organs, to arjuna, conducting his chariot, and thus became a benefactor.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that apart from all the above, kriṣṇa became a benefactor for arjuna by making his divine form, which is enjoyed by nityasūris, to be under the control of arjuna when he sat on arjuna’s chariot, conducting it, and protecting arjuna.

**kudandaik kidandṟku** – just as it has been said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.9.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/03/thiruvaimozhi-10-9-7-madandhaiyar-vazhththalum/) “*kudandai en kōvalan*” (kriṣṇa, who is mercifully reclining in tirukkudandai), it is in tirukkudandai where emperumān is mercifully reclining, manifesting his *saulabhyam* \[easy approacability\] during his incarnation as kriṣṇa. Just as he mercifully manifested himself as *kōlap pirān*, here \[in tirukkudandai\] he mercifully reclined, just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.8.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/08/thiruvaimozhi-5-8-1-aravamudhe/) “*ērār kōlam tigaḻak kidandāy*” (you are resting, exhibiting your abundant beauty, which is shining).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that apart from saying “*mōkśayiśyāmi*” (I shall relieve you from all your sins), kriṣṇa is mercifully reclining in tirukkudandai, to lend authenticity to the saying “*kumbakōṇē vinaśyati*” (sins will be destroyed in kumbakōṇam). He is one who, just as it has been said in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.8.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/08/thiruvaimozhi-5-8-10-vara-aruvay/) “*āvi agamē tittippāy*” (you trigger great taste in me, towards you, in my heart) is very sweet.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.6.7. Pon tigal

*pon tigaḻ cittirakkūdap poruppiniluṟṟa vadivil oru kaṇṇum koṇḍa akkaṟṟaik kuḻalan kadiyan viraindu unnaimaṟṟaikkaṇ koḷḷāmē kōl koṇḍu vā maṇivaṇṇa nambikku ōr kōl koṇḍu vā*

**Пословный перевод:**

pon – having the radiance due to the presence of orchards, streams etc; tigaḻ – being resplendent; cittirakkūdam – known as “citrakūtam”; poruppinil – on the mountain slopes; vadivil – in the divine form of pirātti \[sītāp pirātti\]; uṟṟa – due to perverse knowledge, out of two eyes with which \[you had\] looked at; oru kaṇ – one eye; koṇḍa – one who plucked; a – one who had such a nature; kaṟṟai – being dense; kuḻalan – having locks; kadiyan – this person, who has the cruelty of punishing, appropriate to the crime; unnai – you; maṟṟai kaṇ – the eye which remains; koḷḷāmē – without plucking; viraindu – bring a stick, immediately; maṇi vaṇṇan – one who has the form of a bluish gemstone; nambikku – bring a stick to one who is complete in all aspects

**Перевод:**

**On the slopes of the mountain in citrakūtam, which is resplendent with orchards and ponds, due to a perverse knowledge, you \[addressing the crow\] had looked at the divine form of pirātti. As a result, one of your eyes was plucked by one, who has dense locks and who has the cruel nature of punishing a person, appropriate to the fault committed. Bring a stick, immediately, so that your remaining eye too is not plucked. Bring a stick to the one who has the form of a bluish gemstone and who is complete in all aspects.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**pon tigaḻ …** – citrakūtam was resplendent with orchards, ponds, rocks and streams, just as it has been mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 98-12 “*subhagaścitrakūtō’yam girirāja upamōgiri*: l *yasmin vasati kākutsta*: *kubēra iva nandanē* ll” (This enchanting mountain of citrakūtam resembles the king of mountains; śrī rāma is residing here, just as kubēra is living in the garden called as nandana). śrī rāma was happier here than he would have been in śrī ayōdyā. It was then that the crow came and committed an offence. After having their divine bath, śrī rāma and sītāp pirātti would take turns in sleeping on each other’s lap, just as it has been mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 38-21 “*paryāyēṇa prasupta*:” (sleeping alternatively). After sītāp pirātti had taken her nap on śrī rāma’s lap, śrī rāma was napping on sītāp pirātti’s lap. jayanta, son of indra, due to his nature of a monster, hid his form of celestial entity, and took the form of a crow. Without knowing that she is *janani* (mother of the entire universe), looking at the divine form of pirātti, due to his perverse knowledge, he hurt her form. śrī rāma, with fury, shot off a grass as *brahmāstra* (a divine and powerful weapon). That weapon followed the crow, wherever the crow went, seeking protection. With none offering it protection, just as it has been mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 38-34 “*tamēva śaraṇam gata*:” (He surrendered to that śrī rāma himself), it surrendered to the divine feet of śrī rāma, to protect its life. As a result, it had to lose one eye since *brahmāstra* cannot remain without realising its purpose. This verse tells this narrative, briefly.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says the following: Just as it has been mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1-32 “*citrakūtam gatē rāmē*” (śrī rāma went to citrakūtam), śrī rāma went with *nāycciyār* \[sītāp pirātti\] to the slopes of citrakūtam mountain which was resplendent. jayantan \[son of indra\] had excess of *rajō guṇam* \[quality of passion and aggression\]. Instead of carrying out ordained rituals and attaining the benefit of *ahankāram* \[egoistic nature\], due to the emergence of *tāmasarājō guṇam* \[combination of passion along with ignorance, laziness etc\], he wanted to engage in worldly pursuits. Without looking at the relationship of *janya janaka* \[one who has given birth to and one who has been sired, mother and son\], he indulged in wrongful deeds arising out of his form of crow, which he considered to be superior to his celestial form. śrī rāma, looking at that, shot an *astra* \[weapon\] at him, in a delayed manner. It allowed him to go ahead, following him. Just as it has been mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 38-33 “*trīn lōkān samparikramya*” (going over all the paths in the three worlds), the crow went to all the places in the three worlds; not finding a place where he could take refuge, the crow, desiring his life, fell at the divine feet of śrī rāma, saying, as in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 38-34 “*tamēva śaraṇam gata*:” (surrendered to that śrī rāma himself). śrī rāma too, thinking that it is enough if he surrendered, let go of him, after removing one of the two eyes with which he had looked at pirātti. He \[such emperumān\] is one who has dense, divine locks and is also one who punishes for offences committed.

The *astram* was such that it will not go waste. The *astram* is known as *dēvēndra tanayākśihā* \[one which destroyed the eye of the son of indra\]. emperumān is of the type as mentioned in [tirumalai 15](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thirumalai-15/) “*poyyarkkē poyyanāgum*” (he is deceptive towards one who is deceptive) and [tiruvāimoḻi 4.8.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/04/thiruvaimozhi-4-8-6-arivinal-kuraivilla/) “*kodum kōḷāl nilam koṇḍa*” (one who took the land in a deceptive manner). When both eyes had performed offence by looking at pirātti in an offensive way, why was only one eye removed, when both should have been removed? It was to make the crow look at the one with dense locks, just as it has been mentioned in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.2.20](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/07/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-1-2-20/) “*kuḻalgaḷ irundavā kāṇīrē*” (look at the manner of his divine locks). For one who has surrendered, the punishment is light, just as it has been mentioned in “*lagurdaṇḍa*: *prapannasya*” \[for one who has surrendered, the punishment is light\]. āḻvār further tells the crow “You know the suffering of rāvaṇa et al at his hands. Before he takes your other eye, bring the stick quickly. When looking at the dense locks of emperumān, since one eye will not be enough, he would grant the other eye too. Without losing that eye too, do not go against his orders. Bring the stick, which is his order, and give it to his divine hand. His \[emperumān’s\] surrender \[attaining his followers due to his affection\] will not be half-hearted. This is the reason for which he called you to comb his locks \[as in the previous decad\]. There is very little difference between that crow and this”.

**uṟṟa vadivil oru kaṇṇum koṇḍa** – due to his perverse knowledge, the crow \[jayantan, the son of indra\] went and looked at the divine form of sītāp pirātti with his two eyes. śrī rāma plucked out one of the two eyes.

**akkaṟṟaik kuḻalan kadiyan** – being of that nature, emperumān has dense, divine locks. He also has the cruel nature of punishing, appropriate to the offence committed.

**viraindu …** – to ensure that you do not lose out your other eye too, due to his fury of not having got a stick, get a stick for him as soon as you could.

**maṇivaṇṇa nambikku** – one who has the form of a bluish gemstone; bring a stick for one who is complete on account of his *svātantryam* (total independence).

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.6.8. Minnidaic cidai

*minnidaic cīdai poruttā ilangaiyarmannan maṇi mudi pattum udan vīḻatannigar onṟu illāc cilai kāl vaḷaittittaminnu mudiyaṟku ōr kōl koṇḍu vā vēlai adaittāṟku ōr kōl koṇḍu vā*

**Пословный перевод:**

min – like lightning; idai – having waist; sīdai poruttā – for the sake of sītāp pirātti; ilangaiyar – for the demons, who are residents of lankā; mannan – head, rāvaṇa; maṇi – shining with ruby crowns; mudi pattum – ten heads; udan – at the same time; vīḻa – to fall down, after being severed; than – for self (bow); nigar onṟu illā – without a match; silai – bow; kāl vaḷaittu – drawing it, at its end; itta – one who shot; minnu – splendorous; mudiyaṟku – bring a stick for one who has divine crown; vēlai – ocean; adaittāṟku – bring a stick for one who built a dam with mountains

**Перевод:**

**Demons reside in lankā, under their king, rāvaṇa. For the sake of sītāp pirātti, who had a slender waist, like lightning, perumāḷ drew his bow, which had no match, and shot an arrow, simultaneously severing the ten heads of rāvaṇa, which were shining with ruby crowns. Bring a stick for that emperumān, who has a divine crown. Bring a stick for one who built a dam across the ocean, with mountains.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**min …** – sītāp pirātti had a waist which was like lightning. For the sake of pirātti, who had a soft, divine form and who did not incarnate through a womb.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that rāvaṇa was feeling proud about the strength of his boons, strength of his shoulders, the protection offered by the high compound walls built and the moats around his country. Not knowing what he was doing, he separated sītāp pirātti, who had lightning-like waist and who had not known anything about staying in a womb.

**ilangaiyar mannan** – rāvaṇa separated such sītāp pirātti \[from śrī rāma\] and imprisoned her in lankā; he was also the controller of demons living there.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that with that \[mentioned in the earlier verse\] as the reason, śrīrāma severed the heads of such rāvaṇa, who was the controller of demons \[residing in lankā\] and who had his ten heads covered with crowns made of ruby and other gemstones. However, since the heads were growing back again and again, despite being severed every time, he severed the ten heads all at the same time, such that they fell down together \[never to grow again\].

**maṇi mudi pattum udan vīḻa** – rāvaṇa’s ten heads were decorated with crowns made of ruby. When śrī rāma cut off each head, due to the strength of the boon which he had obtained, the heads grew back in their respective place. Hence, śrī rāma severed all the ten heads, simultaneously, such that all ten fell down together.

**tannigar …** – the divine bow \[held by śrī rāma\] had no match. He drew that bow, through its end.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that it was through that incomparable divine bow that he had a victorious crown for himself.

**vaḷaittu itta …** – he shot the arrow from that bow, after drawing it

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that it was through that same bow that śrī rāma built a dam across the ocean, just as it has been mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 21-22 “*cāpamānaya saumitrē*” \[Oh, lakśmaṇa! Bring my bow and arrows\].

**minnu mudiyaṟku** – the crown of śrī rāma shone as a result of annihilating rāvaṇa

**vēlai adaittāṟku** – it was for the sake of sītāp pirātti, described through verses such as [periya tirumoḻi 5.7.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/01/periya-thirumozhi-5-7-7/) “*surikuḻal kanivāy*” (having beautiful locks and reddish mouth like *kōvai* fruit) that śrī rāma had built a dam across the ocean.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.6.9. Ten ilangai

*tennilangai mannan siram tōḷ tuṇi seyduminnilangu pūṇ vibīdaṇa nambikkuennilangu nāmattaḷavum arasu enṟaminnalangāraṟku ōr kōl koṇḍu vā vēngadavāṇaṟku ōr kōl koMdu vā*

**Пословный перевод:**

then – located in the southern direction; ilangai – for lankāpuri; mannan – king, rāvaṇa’s; siram tōḷ – heads and shoulders; tuṇi seydu – severed; min ilangu – shining well; pūṇ – having donned ornaments; nambi – one, who is complete due to devotion towards śrī rāma; vibīdaṇanukku – for vibhīśaṇāḻvān; ilangu – “being resplendent; en nāmattaḷavum – until my name remains in this word; arasu – this kingdom will remain for you”; enṟa – one, who mercifully said this; min ilangu – radiant like lightning; āraṟku – bring a stick for one, who has a chain; vēngadam – in tiruvēnkata hills \[tirumala\]; vāṇaṟku – bring a stick for the one, who resides

**Перевод:**

**śrī rāma severed the heads of rāvaṇa, the king of lankā, which is located in the southern direction. He mercifully told vibhīśaṇāḻvān, who had donned shiny ornaments and who was complete with his devotion towards śrī rāma “Until my resplendent name remains in this world, this kingdom of yours will remain”. Bring a stick for that śrī rāma, who has a chain, which is radiant, like lightning. Bring a stick for one, who resides in the hills of tiruvēnkatam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**then …** – lankā was protected together by *durgatrayam* (three forts, viz. *giri durgam*, the fort of mountains, *jala durgam*, the fort of ocean, and *vana durgam*, the fort of forest), as a result of which it was indestructible. rāvaṇa was the controller of such lankā. *then* – beautiful

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that śrī rāma, having said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.3 “*mithra bhāvēna…*” (even if a person comes in the guise of a friend, I will not desert him…), did not look at vibhīśaṇa as *rāvaṇānujan* (younger brother of rāvaṇa) but protected him by saying “*na tyajēyam*” (I will not sacrifice him). āḻvār says that for such śrī rāma, what he had done for the sake of sītāp pirātti \[as mentioned in the previous pāsuram\] is not a great matter at all. It was before severing the heads and shoulders of rāvaṇa \[as mentioned in the previous pāsuram\] that śrī rāma welcomed vibhīśaṇa, who is described as one who is decorated with shiny ornaments \[in this pāsuram\]. The time spent by vibhīśaṇa as the younger brother of rāvaṇa, with all the decorative ornaments, was meaningless. When rāvaṇa drove him away, saying that he is *durvruttan* \[one with improper activities\], vibhīśaṇa came by the aerial route and became *śrīmān* \[one with wealth\], becoming complete \[with servitude to śrī rāma\]. It was only after coronating that vibhīśaṇa and telling him that “The kingdom will be yours until my resplendent name remains” that rāvaṇa’s heads and shoulders were severed.

**siram tōḷ tuṇi seydu** – severing the heads and shoulders, which, rāvaṇa thought, could not be destroyed ever.

**min …** – to vibhīśaṇāḻvān who had splendorous ornaments. vibhīśaṇāḻvān had left lankā \[and approached śrī rāma through the aerial route\]. He is referred to, in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 16-17 as “*antarikśagataś śrīmān*” (vibhīśaṇa who has wealth, approaching through the aerial route). He gave up the penury which he had due to his connection with rāvaṇa and gained the wealth, as a result of his connection with śrī rāma, due to which he became complete, and is hence called as *vibīdaṇa nambi*.

**ennilangu …** – mercifully told by śrī rāma “Until my resplendent name remains in this world, your kingdom too will remain”

**minnalangāraṟku** – one who has shiny decoration. If the text were *minnilangāraṟku*, it would refer to one who has a chain which shines like lightning.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that this refers to one who has his divine crown shining like lightning. \[If the text were *minnilangu āraṟku*\] *āram* – *muktāhāram* – pearl necklace. Alternatively, it is *rāmaguṇābharaṇam* \[the ornament of śrī rāma’s quality of granting refuge to vibhīśaṇa\] for vibhīśaṇa and *vibhīśanaguṇābharaṇam* \[the ornament of vibhīśaṇa seeking refuge under śrī rāma\] for śrī rāma. When brahmā said, as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 120-13 “*bhavān nārāyaṇō dēva*:” \[your highness is nārāyaṇa, the supreme entity\], śrī rāma considered that as *en nāmam* \[my name, nārāyaṇa\]. When śrī rāma responded to that saying “*ātmānam mānuśam manyē rāmam daśaradātmajam*” (I think of myself to be a human being, by the name rāma, the son of daśarata), “My name is rāma; my father’s name is daśarata. My identity is dāśarati” – his *ilangu nāmam* \[the shining name\] is rāma or dāśarati. This is similar to [periya tirumoḻi 2.2.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/08/periya-thirumozhi-2-2-4/) “*nandan maindanāga āgum nambi*” ((kriṣṇa) placing himself as the divine son of śrī nandagōpar) \[in śrī rāmāvatāram he desires to be called as the son of daśarata and in kriṣṇāvatāram, he desires to be called as the son of nandagōpar\]. Just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 6.8.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/08/periya-thirumozhi-6-8-5/) “*vibīdaṇaṟku….nallān*”, for śrī rāma, being distinguished for vibhīśaṇa is only when he is dāśarati \[son of daśarata\]. It appears that *nārāyaṇa* is a normal name. As an atonement for śrī rāma’s words addressed to him, brahmā bowed his head and said “*nama*:” \[I am your servitor and accept your words\].

**vēngadavāṇaṟku** – just as it has been mentioned in [tiruccanda viruttam 81](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/01/thiruchchandha-viruththam-81/) “*midainda ēḻ marangaḷum adanga eydu vēngadam adainda māl*” (piercing the seven ebony trees which were standing close to each other, emperumān attained tiruvēngadam), it is in tiruvēngadam that the qualities of *vibhavam* \[incarnations\] sparkle brightly. Bring a stick to the controller of tiruvēngadam.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as it has been said in tiruccanda viruttam 81 “*midainda ēḻ marangaḷum adanga eydu vēngadam adainda māl*” \[as seen above\], it is in tiruvēngadam that emperumān exhibits his quality of *nirankuśa svātantryam* \[uncontrolled independence\] when he showers his grace on the forest, monkeys, tribal people and everyone else. āḻvār tells the crow to bring such emperumān’s *sceptre* \[stick\].

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.6.10. Akkakkay nambikku

*akkākkāy! nambikkuk kōl koṇḍu vā enṟumikkāḷ uraitta sol villibuttūrppattanokka uraitta tamiḻ pattum vallavarmakkaḷaip peṟṟu magiḻvar ivvaiyattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nambikku – “For him who is an expert in misciefs; kōl koṇḍu vā enṟu – search and give a stick, apt for grazing calves”; mikkāḷ – yaśōdāp pirātti, who enjoyed the childish activities of kriṣṇa, as a result of which she had more eminence than dēvakip pirātti, who did not enjoy; uraitta – said; sol – words; villibuttūr – controller of śrī villibuttūr; battan – periyāḻvār; okka – just as she had said; uraitta – mercifully composed; tamiḻ – in drāvida \[tamiḻ\] language; pattum – (these) ten pāsurams; vallavar – those who are capable of learning; makkaḷai – disciples and children, who are engaged with emperumān; peṟṟu – attaining; ivvaiyattu – on this earth; magiḻvar – will get to enjoy

**Перевод:**

**yaśōdāp pirātti had higher level of eminence than dēvakip pirātti, having experienced the child-like activities of kriṣṇa, which dēvakip pirātti could not. She had told crow to “Search and bring a stick, which is apt for this kriṣṇa, who is an expert in misciefs, such that he could graze calves with that stick”. periyāḻvār, the controller of śrī villibuttūr, mercifully composed her words into ten pāsurams in drāvida language. Those who are capable of learning these pāsurams will get disciples and children, who engage with emperumān, and will be happy on this earth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In the final pāsuram of this decad, āḻvār mentions the benefit which will accrue to one who recites the pāsurams and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**akkāKkāy nambikku kōl koṇḍu vā enēu** – the words “Search and get a stick, apt for grazing calves” were spoken of as pāsurams when kriṣṇa started crying \[indicating that he wanted to go behind calves for grazing\], in order to change his crying.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says the following: What is the difference between the crow which combed kriṣṇa’s divine locks \[in the previous *tirumoḻi*\] and this? The context for the previous one was *prapatti* \[emperumān attaining the jīvātmā\] through his *saulabhyam* (easy to approach quality) while here the context is the eminence brought about by emperumān’s *nirankuśa svātantryam* (uncontrolled independence). Instead of calling both as *kākkai* \[crow\], the reason for calling it here as *akkākkāy* is because it is the object of protection of *akāra śabda vācyan* \[emperumān who is identified by the syllable ‘*a*’\].

**mikkāḷ uraitta sol** – while both dēvakip pirātti and yaśōdāp pirātti had observed similar penance to beget a son, dēvakip pirātti merely gave birth to kriṣṇa, without enjoying his child-like activities. Unlike dēvakip pirātti, who didn’t get to enjoy his activities, as mentioned in [perumāḷ tirumoḻi 7.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/08/perumal-thirumozhi-7-5/) “*tiruvilēn onṟum peṟṟilēn*” (I am without any fortune; I did not enjoy), yaśōdāp pirātti had the fortune of enjoying all the flavours of his child-like activities, as mentioned in the same pāsuram, perumāḷ tirumoḻi 7.5 “*ellām deyva nangai yasōdai peṟṟāḷ*” (yaśōdāp pirātti, who could be considered as a celestial person, enjoyed all those childish activities). The words mentioned by such fortunate lady, yaśōdāp pirātti …

This \[syllable, ‘*a*’\] is his prime name. Since the one which is protected is the object of protection, āḻvār is calling it as *akkākkāy*. Just as it has been said in taittirīya upaniśad ānandavalli “*vijñānam yajñam tanutē*” \[knowledge is carrying out ritual\], the term *vijñānam* \[knowledge\] will refer to the person who has that knowledge \[since he is the repository of that knowledge\]. Since that entity’s knowledge is desirous of attaining *jñēyam* \[emperumān, the object of knowledge\], it results in his carrying out the ritual. In the same way, the term ‘protected’ will refer to the ‘protector’ since the protected attains the protector for his protection. The protector’s act of protection will expect the ‘protected’, for carrying out the activity of protection. Due to this, āḻvār calls that \[the person who is protected\] as *kākkai*.

Our preceptors have given distinguished and regular meanings for terms such as “*pūvai, kiḷi, kuyil, mayil, annam, palli, kākkai*” \[myna, parrot, cuckoo, peacock, swan, lizard, crow respectively\]. The esoteric meaning for the term “*nambikku kōl koṇḍu vā*” is that when those, who are equivalent to crows, do not look at emperumān’s order \[to remind the readers: emperumān’s order is to get the stick, and the stick refers to his *svātantryam*, total independence\], they draw a limit to his *svātantryam* which is the basis for his *sankalpam* \[will\]. Unless the jīvātmā looks at emperumān’s svātantryam, there is no scope for his \[jīvātmā’s\] survival. āḻvār tells those, who are like the crow \[having two qualities which are to be rejected, *rajas* and *tamas*\], to recall the travails of the crow which incurred the wrath of his *sankalpam* when it did not look at his *svātantryam* \[reference here is to *jayanta*, indra’s son who lost an eye since he harmed pirātti\]. āḻvār tells them to understand that his *sankalpam* will never lose its sharpness; he tells them to know his *prapatti* \[desire to attain jīvātmā\], fall at his feet and carry out his instructions, just as arjuna had said in [bhagavat gītā 18.73](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-73/) “*kariśyē vacanam tava*” (I will carry out your order\]. If we look at his *svātantryam*, he will feel happy, thinking “Due to him, we have become *svātantryan*”. Instead of getting arrogant because he feels that we are the reason for his *svātantryam*, āḻvār tells us to rise up higher and higher \[in our nature of servitude\] with mangaḷāśāsanam and to join him in carrying it out.

**akkākkāy nambikku kōl koṇḍu vā enṟu mikkāḷ uraitta sol** – yaśōdāp pirātti had said a few words, in order to change his crying, on account of her affection towards him, since he is her son. This has to be united with the *svarūpānurūpam* (carrying out an activity in line with our basic nature), which is mangaḷāśāsanam.

**villibuttūrp pattan okka uraitta tamiḻ pattum vallavar** – periyāḻvār is the controller of śrī villibuttūr. With the pathos and connection which yaśōdāp pirātti had towards kriṣṇa, periyāḻvār composed these ten pāsurams, with her words, in drāvida language \[tamiḻ\]. Those who are capable of learning these pāsurams, with the same pathos of periyāḻvār \[of carrying out mangaḷāśānam for emperumān\] …

**makkaḷ …**– \[such people\] will get disciples and children, who are complete with knowledge and affection towards emperumān. Along with such disciples and children, these people will get to live happily on this earth.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that those who learn these ten pāsurams will beget disciples and children who will be steadfast in their *prapatti*, which leads up to carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam for emperumān. These people \[such disciples and children\] are the cause for their happiness.

We shall next consider the pravēsam of the next tirumoḻi.

## 2.7.1. Anirai meykka

*ānirai mēykka nī pōdi arumarundu āvadu aṟiyāykānagam ellām tirindu un kariya tirumēni vādappānaiyil pālaip parugip paṟṟādārellām sirippattēnil iniya pirānē! seṇbagap pūc cūtta vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

tēnil – more than honey; iniya – being sweet; pirānē – oh, my lord!; paṟṟādār ellām – those who are unfavourable to you; sirippa – to ridicule; pānaiyil – being inside pot; pālai – (fresh) milk \[which has not been heated yet\]; parugi – drinking; un – your; kariya – dark; tirumēni – divine form; vāda – to wither, unable to tolerate (the forest conflagration); kānagam ellām – throughout the forest; tirindu – roaming around; A nirai – herd of cows; mēykka – to graze; nī – you, who are of soft nature; pōdi – have gone; aru – difficult to obtain; marundu āvadu – that which is a medicine; aṟiyāy – do not know; seṇbagap pū – campaka flower; sūtta – such that I bedeck you; vārāy – should mercifully come

**Перевод:**

**Oh, lord who is sweeter than honey! Those who are unfavourable to you are ridiculing when you drink fresh milk, kept in pots. When you go roaming behind herds of cows, for grazing them in forest, your divine, dark form, which is like a difficult-to-get medicine, is withering. You are not aware of this. You should mercifully come such that I could bedeck you with campaka flowers.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**ānirai mēykka nī pōdi** – cows do not know your distinction. They will roam around to areas which are apt for them for grazing. However, you went after them, for grazing, with your tender form.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says: You are not looking at yourself \[your soft nature\] or at me \[who is affectionate towards you, not happy with your going into the forest, exposing yourself\]; you desire to go after the cows, to graze them with the help of the stick given by the crow.

**arumarundu āvadu aṟiyāy** – you do not realise that your divine form is a difficult-to-attain medicine. For people here \[in samsāram\], he is the medicine for removing their diseases. For nityasūris, who are in paramapadam, he is the medicine to give them happiness when they enjoy his divine form.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that emperumān does not realise that he is difficult-to-attain medicine. He is insatiable nectar. He is the nectar which has not been contained in the ocean \[unlike the nectar consumed by celestial entities when they were given by emperumān, after churning the ocean\]. Hence, he is rare-to-get nectar. *marundu* – nectar. When this medicine is in proximity, it is the source of enjoyment. When it leaves a place, it becomes the reason for one to regain existence.

**kānagam ellām tirindu** – roaming around the entire forest. Since cows would graze wherever the grass is verdant, over an expansive area, you have to go behind them wherever they go for grazing.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that since cows would roam around wherever they see verdant regions, kriṣṇa could not have a fixed path to go and return. He too has to roam everywhere, causing withering to his divine form, which is invigorating to the cows too.

**un kariya tirumēni vāda** – your divine form is such that it would make those who behold you to become cool and comfortable. However, you are exposing it to the conflagration in forest such that it would wither, just like a flower would, when exposed to heat.

**pānaiyil pālaip parugi** – you would drink milk, which has been just then milked and kept in pots \[without even heating it or adding sweeteners to it\], directly from the pots…

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when kriṣṇa drinks the freshly milked milk \[which has not been heated\], yaśōdāp pirātti will feel fearful as to what will befall his divine form. At the same time, when he drinks the milk from the pots, for those who are not favourable to kriṣṇa, even the little bit of good qualities in him will become cause for ridicule.

**paṟṟādār ellām sirippa** – … such that those who are unfavourable to you, will ridicule you, saying “He has drunk milk from pots kept in our house”

**tēnil iniya pirānē** – Oh, one who is the benefactor, who is sweeter than honey! When people enjoy you, they will not get satiated and would want to experience you even further. And, you offer yourself to others such that they could enjoy you \[this is the reason for calling him as benefactor\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: Did honey \[reference to kriṣṇa\] drink the milk? ōr did nectar, which is sweeter than honey, drink the milk? kriṣṇa is the honey and nectar, which will offer themselves for consumption. Hence, he is the *upakārakan* \[*pirān*\] – benefactor.

**seṇbagap pūc cūtta vārāy** – come such that I could bedeck you with campaka flowers, which blossom in the mornings, when they are still fresh. The pāsuram should be rearranged as *tēnil iniya pirānē – paṟṟādārellām sirippa – pānaiyiṟpālaip parugi – un kariya tirumēni vāda – kānagam ellām tirindu – ānirai mēykka nī pōdi – arumarundu āvadu aṟiyāy – seṇbagap pūc cūtta vāray* to get the sequential meaning.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when kriṣṇa does not don the flower, *sumanās* \[we have seen in the pravēśam of this decad that tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai refers to flowers as *sumanās*, those with noble hearts, viz. they know *ātmaguṇam*, which is to be subservient to emperumān\], on his head, the *sumanās* will wither.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.7.2. Karuvudai megangal

*karuvudai mēgangaḷ kaṇḍāl unnaik kaṇḍāl okkum kaṇgaḷuruvudaiyāy! ulagu ēḻum uṇḍāga vandu piṟandāytiruvudaiyāḷ maṇavāḷā! tiruvarangattē kidandāy!maruvi maṇam kamaḻginṟa malligaip pūc cūtta vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

karu udai – pregnant with water (rising with water); mēgangaḷ – clouds; kaṇḍāl – if seen; unnai – you; kaṇḍāl okkum – it appears like seeing; kaṇgaḷ – of the eyes; uruvu udaiyāy! – oh, one who has the beauty!; ulagu ēḻum – seven worlds; uṇḍāga – to gain existence; vandu – came to tiruvāyppādi \[śrī gōkulam\]; piṟandāy! – oh, one who divinely incarnated!; tiru udaiyāḷ – for pirātti, who has you as her wealth; maṇavāḷā! – oh, one who is the beloved!; tiru arangattu – in the huge temple in tiruvarangam \[śrīrangam\]; kidandāy! – oh, one who mercifully reclined!; maṇam – fragrance; maruvi – fitting aptly; kamaḻginṟa – wafting; malligaip pū – come to don jasmine flower

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who has the beauty of eyes such that when \[we\] look at water-laden clouds, they appear like seeing you. Oh, one incarnated divinely in tiruvāyppādi such that the seven worlds gained their existence! Oh, one who is the beloved of periya pirātti, who has you as her wealth! Oh, one who is mercifully reclining in the huge temple in śrīrangam! You should come and don the jasmine flower which has fragrance fitting well and wafting in it**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**karu …** – (*kaṇgaḷ – unnaik kaṇḍāl – karuvudai mēgangaḷ kaṇḍāl okkum – uru udaiyāy*) – Oh, one who has the cool, divine form such that when (our) eyes look at you, it appears like looking at dark clouds which are laden with water! Alternatively, when eyes look at water-laden clouds, it would appear that we are looking at you.

**kaṇgal uru udaiyāy** – this could also be considered to mean that emperumān’s divine eyes have the beauty of his divine form.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that this term is to be split as *kangaḷ udaiyāy* \[one who has divine eyes\] and *uruvu udaiyāy* \[one who has divine form\]. Oh, one who has divine eyes which do not have anything which can be termed as equivalent! Oh, one who has beauty which is also of the same nature \[does not have anything which is an equivalent\]!

**ulagēḻum uṇḍāga vandu piṟandāy** – Oh, one who came and incarnated such that all the worlds got uplifted, by gaining their existence!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that emperumān incarnated in order to uplift the worlds which he had created, such that they would behave as per his divine mind and not get atrophied, as per their *karma* \[past deeds\]. emperumān is one who establishes righteous activities and looks after the well-being of the worlds. Since it is he who incarnates as the *darmaśabdavācyan* (He is the identity for the word ‘righteousness’) enhancing existence of the worlds and instructs through preceptors to carry out mangaḷāśāsanam, āḻvār refers to this as *piṟandāy*. However, there are entities such as śiśupālan et al \[he was kriṣṇa’s cousin\] who would speak disparagingly for this reason \[that kriṣṇa was born just like anyone else and that there is no need to give any prominence to kriṣṇa\]. This earth, very patiently, puts up with people like pauṇḍraka vāsudēvan \[he was a contemporary of kriṣṇa, who told everyone that he was the real kriṣṇa\] as well as others who thought of their birth, their wealth, other *dēvatās* as being supreme.

**tiru udaiyāḷ maṇavāḷā** – just as it has been mentioned in [stōtra ratnam 12](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/12/sthothra-rathnam-12/) “*ka*:*śrī*: *śrīya*:” (one who is periya pirāttiyār’s wealth), in śrī guṇaratna kōsam 9 “*śriya*:*śrī*:” (wealth of periya pirāttiyār) and [periya tirumoḻi 7.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/11/periya-thirumozhi-7-7-1/) “*tiruvukkum tiruvāgiya*” (embodiment of wealth for periya pirāttiyār (śrī mahālakśmi) who is the cause for the wealth of everyone), oh, one who is the beloved of periya pirāttiyār, who has you as her wealth!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that this term gives the reason for his incarnation. Since emperumān is referred to as “*ka*:*śrī*:*śrīya*:”, “*śrīya*:*śrī*:”, “*tiruvukkum tiruvāgiya*” \[we have seen all these just now\] and in [periya tirumoḻi 4.9.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/05/periya-thirumozhi-4-9-2/) “*sindai tannuḷ nīngādirunda tiruvē*” (Oh, one who is the wealth, always residing in my heart, without every separating), he becomes her wealth. Since he is her wealth, she is at liberty to enjoy him or play with him or appropriate him, the way she pleases. Just as it has been mentioned in śrī guṇaratna kōśam 22 “*kēvala krupā nirvāhya vargē vayam śēśitvē parama*: *pūmān*” (\[addressing śrī mahālakśmi\] We are under your control, looking up to your mercy while emperumān remains as your lord), since he is her beloved, he has to recline in the place where she tells him to.

**tiruvarangattē kidandāy** – Oh, one who is reclining mercifully in kōyil \[the huge temple in śrīrangam\] for her happiness of protecting the *samsāri cētanas* \[ātmās in samsāram\]!

**maruvi …** – you should come to don the jasmine flower, in which fragrance is wafting, without leaving it.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here as an alternative interpretation that yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa that he should sit on her lap and don the jasmine flower.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.7.3. Maccodu maligai

*maccodu māḷigai ēṟi mādargaḷ tam idam pukkukaccodu pattaik kiḻittuk kāmbu tugil avai kīṟiniccalum teemaigaḷ seyvāy! neeḷ tiruvēngadattu endāy!paccait tamanagattōdu pādirip pūc cūtta vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

maccodu – along with middle storeys; māḷigai – higher storeys too; ēṟi – climbing; mādargaḷ tam idam – places where women are present; pukku – entering; kaccodu – along with their bodices; pattai – silk cloth worn over the bodice; kiḻittu – tearing them; kāmbu tugil avai – saris which have distinguished borders; kīṟi – tearing; niccalum – every day; teemaigaḷ seyvāy! – oh, one who indulges in misciefs!; neeḷ – being tall; tiruvēngadattu – one who has mercifully taken residence in tiruvēngadam malai; endāy! – oh, one who is my lord!; paccai – without any reduction in freshness; tamangattōdu – tavanam \[a variety of fragrant shrub, also called as Southern Wood\]; pādirip pū – come for donning fragrant trumpet flower

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who indulges in misciefs every day! You would enter places where women reside, whether in the middle or in the upper storeys. You would tear the bodices as well as the silk cloth covering the bodices of the women there. You would also tear their saris which would have beautiful borders. Oh, one who has mercifully taken residence in the tall hills of tiruvēngadam! Oh, one who is my lord! You should come and don the fragrant shrub, tavanam, along with trumpet flower.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**maccu …** – *maccu* – middle storeys; *māḷigai* – upper storeys*.* Climbing top storeys through the middle storeys.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says the following: Should you, who incarnated in order to uplift the seven worlds, indulge in carrying out misciefs by climbing the middle and higher storeys? m*accu* – middle floor; *māḷigai* – top floor. He went to the third floor, where women were present.

**mādargaḷ tam idam pukku**– entering places where women were present.

**kaccodu pattaik kiḻittu** – Tearing their bodices along with silken cloth, worn over the bodices.

**kāmbu tugil avai kīṟi** – Tearing saris which had borders. *kāmbu tugil* – sari which has a border at the end.

**niccalum teemaigaḷ seyvāy** – Oh, one who is indulging in carrying out misciefs every day. As he was growing up every day, his misciefs were growing more rapidly.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that indulging in more and more of misciefs, with each day, had become kriṣṇa’s identity.

**neeḷ tiruvēngadattu endāy** – Oh, one who is my svāmy, who is residing in tirumalai, which is in the northern direction, and which has tall hills! He is showering his mercy on the forest, monkeys and tribal people who live in that forest, as a result of being the lord.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here as an alternative meaning that just as tirumalai hills is the place to which people in leelā vibhūti \[samsāram\] go up \[to worship emperumān\], it is also the place to which entities in *tripād vibhūti* \[paramapadam, which is three times larger than leelā vibhūti\] go to, in order to worship one who is greater than all.

**paccai …** – You should come in order to don the fragrant shrub, which has not lost its green colour \[not dried up\] along with the trumpet flower, which has a complementary colour to that shrub, and which is still fresh.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says at the end, the following: Through the term *maccodu māḷigai*, the distinguished entities in the third vibhūti \[those who live in divyadēsams, the divine abodes of emperumān in leelā vibhūti, who have *ātma jñānam*, that they are servitors of emperumān\] are shown. Through the term *kaccodu pattu*, emperumān’s disinterest in *svarūpa jñānam* \[basic knowledge of ātmās, that they are servitors of emperumān and are totally dependent on him\], leading to devotion, is shown \[emperumān does not always enjoy the servitude of ātmās. On occasions, he desires to carry out service to ātmās. Since the *svarūpa jñānam* of ātmās would not allow them to accept service from emperumān, he is tearing off that knowledge\]. Through the term *niccalum teemaigaḷ seydu*, it enquires whether emperumān could play with those who are in divine abodes. Through the term *kāmbu tugil*, it enquires whether he could show disinterest in those who have gained discerning knowledge about one’s form and ātmā \[sari denotes form and the border, ātmā\] and whether he could have bias towards them.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.7.4. Teruvinkan ninru

*teruvin kaṇ ninṟu iḷavāyccimārgaḷai tīmai seyyādēmaruvum tamanagamum sīr mālai maṇam kamaḻginṟapuruvam karunguḻal neṟṟi polinda mugil kanṟu pōlēuruvam aḻagiya nambī! ugandu ivai sūtta nī vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

puruvam – eye brows; karu – being dark; kuḻal – divine locks; neṟṟi – (shining between these two) forehead too; polinda – shining; mugil kanṟu pōlē – like a calf begot by cloud; uruvam aḻagiya – being beautiful due to the divine form; nambī! – oh, one who is complete in all aspects!; teruvin kaṇ ninṟu – standing in the street; iḷa – young, by age; āyccimārgaḷai – towards herd-girls; tīmai seyyādē – do not carry out mischief; maṇam kamaḻginṟa – wafting fragrance; maruvum – marjoram, a fragrant herb; tamangamum – strung together with the fragrant shrub; sīr mālai ivai – these beautiful garlands; ugandu sūtta – such that I bedeck you, with joy; nī vārāy – you should mercifully come

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who is complete in all aspects, with the beautiful, shining form of a calf given birth to by a cloud, having unmatched eye brows, dark divine locks, beautiful forehead etc! Do not indulge in misciefs towards young herd-girls who are standing by the street. You should mercifully come such that I joyously bedeck you with beautiful garlands strung together with fragrant marjoram and fragrant shrub.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**teruvin kaṇ ninṟu** – After yaśōdāp pirātti had told kriṣṇa \[as in the previous pāsuram\] that he was doing mischief with herd-women by climbing atop houses, he asks her “Did I climb the middle and top storeys? Did I not stand in the street? When I am like that, why are you saying like these?” yaśōdāp pirātti tells him back “Are you not indulging in misciefs there?” Standing in the street …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that when kriṣṇa asked her as to what mischief he had done when he was quietly standing in the street, yaśōdāp pirātti tells him that he had carried out such misciefs earlier with these girls in the streets. She tells him not to indulge in such misciefs henceforth. Since his misciefs could not be counted out \[being innumerable\], she tells him through a single word, *tīmai*.

**iḷa āyccimārgaḷait tīmai seyyādē** – Do not indulge in misciefs with the young herd-girls, who are standing there. His activities of kicking the sand-houses built by these young girls in the streets, his grabbing their implements which they carry for playing among themselves, his pushing them after playing with them by locking hands etc are well known. Since his misciefs are beyond words, āḻvār says here through a single word *tīmai* (mischief)

**maruvum tamanagamum sīr mālai maṇam kamaḻginṟa** – garlands which have been strung together with marjoram and fragrant shrub are remaining, with fragrance being emitted from them continuously. The meaning implied here is that the fragrance, which should go to his divine locks from these fragrant flowers, is remaining on the flowers, without getting wasted.

**puruvam …** – you have unmatched eye-brows; dark, divine locks and divine forehead which is splendorous between these two. Oh, one who is complete in all aspects, shining like a resplendent calf, due to the beauty of these limbs, given birth to by a cloud!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, for the term *uruvam aḻagiya nambī* – Oh, one who is complete with your decoration, beauty of limbs and the qualities of indulging in misciefs!

**ugandu …** – You should come such that I would feel happy that “I have been able to bedeck you” with these fragrant garlands

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here for the term *ugandu* – it is my happiness that you would be happy with these fragrant flowers on your divine locks. The term *ivai* \[these\] includes the flowers mentioned earlier too such as *campaka, trumpet* flower etc.

Through this \[indulging in misciefs with those who are playing on the streets\], āḻvār is asking kriṣṇa “What do you have to do with those who are independent of your *sankalpam* (will), who are following other means to reach you \[than reaching through you\], who desire other benefits \[than you\] and who wish to play among themselves \[instead of being your paly-mate?\] ṣouldn’t you play only with those who are desirous of playing with you?”

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.7.5. Pullinai vay

*puḷḷinai vāy piḷandittāy poru kariyin kombosittāykaḷḷa arakkiyai mūkkodu kāvalanait talai koṇḍāyaḷḷi nī veṇṇey viḻunga anjādu adiyēn adittēnteḷḷiya neeril eḻunda sengaḻunīr sūtta vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

puḷḷin – bakāsuran’s \[a monster, who came in the form of a bird\]; vāy – mouth; piḷandittāy – oh, one who tore it!; poru – one that came against you, to fight; kariyin – the elephant, kuvalayāpeedam; kombu – tusk; osittāy! – oh, one who snapped!; kaḷḷam – one who came with a deceptive form; arakkiyai – demon, by the name sūrppaṇakhā; mūkkodu – along with her nose; kāvalanai – rāvaṇa, who is the protector of demons; talai koṇḍāy! – oh,one who severed his heads!; nī – you; veṇṇey – butter; aḷḷi viḻunga – when you consumed by scooping it; adiyēn – I, the servitor; anjādu – without fearing for the tenderness of your divine form; adittēn – beat you; teḷḷiya nīril – in clear waters; eḻunda – blossomed; sem kaḻunīr – you should come to don red water-lily flower

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who tore the mouth of the monster bakāsuran! Oh, one who snapped the tusk of elephant kuvalayāpeedam, which came to fight against you! Oh, one who had severed the nose of the deceptive demon sūrppaṇakhā and the heads of protector of demons, rāvaṇa! When you were consuming butter by scooping it, without fearing for your tender divine form, I beat you. Tolerating what I had done, you should come to don the red water-lily which has blossomed in clear waters.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**puḷḷinai …** – Oh, one who tore the mouth of bakāsuran who came in the form of a bird, with the intention of harming you when you were grazing calves, just as it has been mentioned in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2.5.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/11/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-2-5-4/) “*paḷḷattil mēyum paṟavai urukkoṇḍu*” (taking the form of bird which looks for prey in low level water-bodies)!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār says that the purpose for both incarnations \[śrī rāmāvatāram and kriṣṇāvatāram\] is to annihilate enemies. He says that kriṣṇa had effortlessly torn the mouth of bakāsuran.

**poru …** – kamsan had invited kriṣṇa to come for an auspicious function. However, he placed an elephant on the way, to harm kriṣṇa. Oh, one who effortlessly snapped the tusks of that elephant, which came upon you to fight!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the elephant had been kept in a deceptive manner \[kriṣṇa had been invited for an auspicious purpose but the elephant was made to stand in the way, with the intention of harming him\].

**kaḷḷa …** – the demon sūrppaṇakhā, came in a deceptive form, saying, as in siṟiya tirumadal 35 “*sīdaikku nērāvan*” (one who said “I am equal to sītā”) that she was equal to sītāp pirātti. Oh, one who severed her nose as well as the heads of rāvaṇa, her protector! Since rāvaṇa had told sūrppaṇakhā “Roam around wherever you wish”, he is termed as her protector. Alternatively, he could be termed as the protector, in general, for the clan of demons. The meaning hinted in all these \[destroying inimical entities\] is that emperumān effortlessly removes his famous enemies and offers himself to those who enjoy him.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the demon \[sūrppaṇakhā\] came with a deceptive form, just as pūtanā and śakata had done.

**aḷḷi …** – I had been waiting for you \[before you were born\], thinking “When will he consume butter, scooping it?” Having given birth to you, when you indeed consumed butter, scooping it, without caring for your tender form, *adiyēn* (the servitor), beat you. When one feels sorry for an improper action carried out, it is normal to say *adiyēn*. Instead of thinking about this \[his tender form\] before beating him, the reason for her beating him was in fear of having to listen to words of slander from others, when kriṣṇa would do this \[surreptitiously eating butter\] elsewhere.

**teḷḷiya …** – however, putting up with my action \[of beating you\], you should come such that I could bedeck you with red water-lily flowers, which are distinguished in terms of their colour and fragrance, having blossomed in fresh waters, before they lose their freshness.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.7.6. Erudugalodu porudi

*erudugaḷōdu porudi ēdum ulōbāy kāṇ nambī!karudiya teemaigaḷ seydu kanjanaik kāl kodu pāyndāyteruvin kaṇ teemaigaḷ seydu cikkena mallargaḷōduporudu varuginṟa ponnē! punnaip pūc cūtta vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

nambī! – oh, one who is complete in your infatuation towards nappinnaip pirātti!; erudugaḷōdu – with bulls, which have been pervaded by monsters; porudi – you were fighting (for the sake of nappinnaip pirātti); ēdum – in anything; ulōbāy kāṇ – behold, you were without any desire (the meaning hinted is that kriṣṇa was not concerned about protecting his divine form, his life); karudiya – \[acts\] which kamsan had thought of carrying out against you; teemaigaḷ – wrongful acts; seydu – you carried out against him; kanjanai – kamsan; kāl kodu – with your divine feet; pāyndāy – you had kicked; teruvin kaṇ – on the way to annihilating kamsan; teemaigaḷ seydu – carrying out acts against kamsan such as killing the vaśerman, snapping the bow; mallargaḷōdu – with wrestlers cāṇūra and muśtika; cikkena – permanently; porudu – waging a battle; varuginṟa – one who comes; ponnē! – oh, kaṇṇa, who has a divine form, like gold!; punnaip pū – you should come to don the punnaip pū (a fragrant flower, ālexandrian laurel)

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who is complete in your infatuation towards nappinnaip pirātti! You engaged in a battle with bulls, in which monsters had pervaded to harm you, for the sake of nappinnaip pirātti. You were without any desire in anything concerning you \[such as protecting your divine form or protecting your life\]. kamsan had thought of various activities to carry out against you. You did these against him and kicked him with your divine feet. On the way to annihilating him, you had indulged in acts such as killing the vaśerman and drawing the bow. Oh, one who has the divine form which is like gold, with which you had fought with wrestlers such as cāṇūra and muśtika! You should come and don the fragrant punnaip pū.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**erudugaḷōdu porudi** – Due to your desire of attaining nappinnaip pirātti, without looking at the tenderness of your divine form, you fought with the bulls, which had been pervaded by monsters. Even though the event \[fighting with the bulls\] had taken place a long time back, since it is shining as if it were taking place now, āḻvār is using the present continuous tense, *porudi* – fighting.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that yaśōdāp pirātti had beaten him \[as in the previous pāsuram\] since “She would not tolerate the blaming words of those who are in tiruvāyppādi”. Could such a person tolerate if he were to engage in a fight with bulls? Even an event which had taken place much earlier, would appear as if it were happening during present time.

**ēdum ulōbāy kāṇ** – Behold, you were standing without any desire \[*ulōpam* – desire; *ulōpāy* – without desire\]. In other words, kriṣṇa did not seem concerned about protecting his divine form or divine life.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that despite telling kriṣṇa to step back, he vouldn’t. *ulōbāy* – not looking after his divine form or his life. Even when sages, who knew events in all three times \[past, present and future\] told kriṣṇa “These are not mere bulls; these are monsters ordered to harm you, by kamsan” he would say “That is what I relish”. Behold, he has such boldness.

**nambī** – Oh, one who is complete with infatuation towards nappinnaip pirātti!

**karudiya teemaigaḷ seydu** – carrying out the wrongful acts, which kamsan had intended carrying out towards you, on him.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa carried out the wrongful acts which kamsan had intended to carry out on kriṣṇa. He pushed kamsan from his throne and kicked him with his divine feet. Alternatively, āḻvār thinks “Just as I had thought ‘He is capable of carrying out this too’ you had completed all these”. āḻvār is afraid that kriṣṇa could fall on other enemies too, who are like this.

**kanjanaik kāl kodu pāyndāy** – You kicked kamsan with your divine feet. Just as it has been mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5.20.26 “*tunga manja vyavastita*:” (kamsan was sitting on a high throne), you went and jumped up the steps to the throne where kamsan was sitting. Just as it has been mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5.20.84 “*kēśēśvākruśya vigaḷat kirītam avaneetalē* l *sa kamsam pādayāmāsa tasya upari papātaca* ” (that kriṣṇa, caught hold of kamsan’s locks such that kamsan’s crown fell on the ground. He pushed kamsan on the ground and fell upon him), kriṣṇa grabbed and threw the crown, pulled kamsan’s locks such that kamsan fell down on the ground and jumped on kamsan. This is how kamsan was killed.

**teruvin kaṇ teemaigaḷ seydu** – *teru*: way. On the way to annihilating kamsan, kriṣṇa killed kamsan’s vaśerman, entered the weapon storage area and broke the bow, which was kept there with decoration, since it was the festival with bow, creating wrath in kamsan and then killed kuvalayāpeedam, which was kamsan’s favourite elephant. These are the wrongful deeds which he carried out.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa would say “I am going to play in the street”, and while playing with his friends, he will carry out misciefs with them. Alternatively, while going on the streets of śrī maturā, he would make faces at the ladies who are walking there, frightening them fraudulently.

**cikkena mallargaḷōdu porudu** – just as it has been mentioned in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.2.6 “*ēviṟṟuc ceyvān ēnṟedirndu vanda mallar*” (The wrestlers who came, as ordered by kamsan, to oppose kriṣṇa), wrestlers such as cāṇūra, muśtika et al were ordered by kamsan to wrestle with kriṣṇa. However, kriṣṇa killed them all, as per his pledge.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that while the wrestlers were killed first and then only kamsan, āḻvār would have remembered that he had killed the wrestlers too and hence says this later. c*hikkena* – in line with his pledge \[of killing all of them\]. āḻvār says *ponnē*, looking at the radiance in kriṣṇa’s divine form after killing the enemies. This refers to the attractiveness which he had in his divine form.

**varuginṟa ponnē** – when you came, after annihilating all the enemies like this, oh, one who had an effulgent form, like gold, with an arrogance! Why did āḻvār narrate the destruction of kamsan first and the others, who had been annihilated before that, later? Since killing of kamsan was the objective, there is nothing contradictory in narrating about kamsan first and then these, which were a corollary to that.

**punnai …** – you should come such that you could don the *punnai* flower, which is a favourite one for you. Since she says “*ponnē punnaip pūc cūtta vārāy*”, just as gold is united with gold, one could see that she is calling him, who has a divine form like gold, to bedeck with the *punnai* flower, which has golden pollens.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.7.7. Kudangal eduttu

*kudangaḷ eduttēṟa vittuk kūttāda valla em kōvē!madam koḷ madi mugattārai māl seyya valla en maindā!idandittu iraṇiyan nenjai iru piḷavāga mun kīṇḍāy!kudandaik kidanda em kōvē! kurukkattip pūc cūtta vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

kudangaḷ – many pots; eduttu – carrying in the hands; ēṟa vittu – throwing in the sky; kūttu Ada valla – being an expert in dancing; em kōvē! – oh, one who is our lord!; madam koḷ – having ignorance; madi mugattārai – girls, who have their faces, which are cool, like full moon; māl seyya valla – to make them infatuated; en maindā! – oh, one who is my son!; mun – at an earlier time; iraṇiyan – the monster hiraṇya \[kaśyap\]’s; nenjai – chest; idandu – anchoring with divine nails; irup piḷavāga – into two pieces; kīṇḍāy! – oh, one who tore!; kidanda – mercifully reclining; em kōvē – oh, my lord!; kurukkattip pū – you should come to don the kuruakkattip pū \[fragrant flower, also known as white fig or hiptage\]

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who is our lord, who is an expert in dancing with pots, by holding them in your hands as well as throwing them in the sky! Oh, my son, who is capable of making girls, who have cool faces like a full moon and who are ignorant, to be infatuated with you! Oh, one who tore, at an earlier point in time, the chest of monster hiraṇya kaśyap, into two pieces, with your divine nails! Oh, one who is reclining in tirukkudandai! You should come and don the kurukkattip pū.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that in the previous pāsuram, āḻvār mentioned about the removal of enmity which occurred for good, virtuous people, due to kamsan et al; in this pāsuram, he mentions about the removal of enmity that occurred due to hiraṇya et al.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kudangaḷ …** – if brāhmaṇas get excessive wealth, they will celebrate by conducting *yajña*, *hōma* \[rituals, as mentioned in vēdams\] etc. Similarly, when herd-people get excessive wealth, they will celebrate, as an outlet for their pride, by performing *kudakkūttu*, dancing with pots. Unlike the wealth of the two vibhūtis \[leelā vibhūti, materialistic realm and nitya vibhūti, spiritualistic realm\], this wealth \[as a herd-person\] has been created after kriṣṇa had incarnated. Wealth for herd-people is having abundance of cows. That wealth is available for kriṣṇa, without any shortcoming. Since that wealth is only for him, he indulges in dancing with pots, as an outlet for that pride. While placing a stack of pots on the heads and shoulders, and carrying pots in the hands too, pots from the hand are thrown up in the sky and caught when they fall down. It is this, which has been mentioned through the term *kudangaḷ eduttēṟa vittuk kūttādavalla*.

Instead of saying pot, since the pāsuram says pots \[in plural number\], this refers to dancing with many pots. Since it has been mentioned as *eduttēṟavittu*, kriṣṇa will throw the pots from his divine hands into the sky and catch them when they fall down. Since the pāsuram says *kūttāda valla*, while there may be others who too could dance with pots, there is none who could dance as well as kriṣṇa does. In other words, the movements which kriṣṇa exhibits while dancing with the pots will not be seen in bharata śāstram \[treatise on bharatanātyam, a classical dance\] too.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when herd-people have excess wealth, as an outlet for their pride, they indulge in the dance called as *kudakkūttu*, dancing with pots. Since it is appropriate for kriṣṇa, he being from that clan, he has to carry this out. Just as *sandyā vandanam* \[paying obeisance to various entities during three times in a day\] has been ordained for brāhmaṇas, this \[dancing with pots\] is ordained for kriṣṇa. Since the pāsuram says *kudangaḷ* \[in the plural\], he is carrying many pots. Eyes could see when a pot is removed for throwing up in the sky. While the eye could see objects up to a particular distance, the eye could not see the pot when it is thrown in the sky.

In the pāsuram, we have only seen the terms *kudangaḷ eduttu* (taking the pots in the hands) and *ēṟa vittu* (throwing them in the sky). But we haven’t seen “*mīṇḍēṟa vitta kudangaḷ tirukkaiyilēyum vandadu*” (the pots which were thrown in the sky returned to the divine hands). While the pots were stacked on the divine head, while there was a movement of pots \[between the hands and sky\], since pots were stacked in the sky too, one could only guess that there has been a movement in this regard. Even if we could see those who go to *svargam* \[heaven\] return to earth, just as it has been said in [bhagavat gītā 9.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/periyazhwar-thirumozhi/://githa.koyil.org/index.php/9-21/) “*kśīṇē puṇyē martya lōkam viśanti*” (upon exhausting the results of their pious activities, people return to the mortal planet again), we could only guess that the pots which were thrown into the sky returned to kriṣṇa’s hands.

*kūttāda valla em kōvē* – even if one could see the pots which were thrown up, returning to kriṣṇa’s hands, the types of dances could not be fathomed. As far as dance is concerned, bharata nātya śāstram is the boundary. But kriṣṇa’s expertise goes beyond that. It could be said that he is the king of dances. In other words, he is the first to be counted, when it comes to expertise in dancing.

**em kōvē** – Oh, one who is our lord!

**madam koḷ …** – Oh, one who is my son, who is capable of making girls, who are ignorant and who have cool faces like full-moon, to become infatuated with you, through such activities!

For the verse *madam koḷ madi mugattārai māl seyya valla en maindā*, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that in that place \[śrī gōkulam\], apart from men, old women and children, there were young girls, who were affected because of him \[losing their hearts to him\], being obedient to him, sitting in the place where he tells them to sit, and on seeing his divine face, without any trace of drooping,  showing a cheerful face. Hence, they are referred to as *madi mugam*. Oh, my son, who is capable of making them infatuated like this! *maindu* – strength, youthfulness, childishness.

**idandittu …** – the term *nenju* refers to chest. Due to the strength of the boons given by celestial entities, hiraṇya’s chest had got strengthened further. Just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 1.7.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/05/periya-thirumozhi-1-7-2/) “*kolaikkaiyāḷan nenjidanda kūr ugirāḷan*” (emperumān has sharp divine nails with which he tore the chest of hiraṇyan who was killing people with his hands, as his nature), oh, one who tore the chest of hiraṇya at an earlier point of time, by ploughing it with your sharp divine nails! Through this, it says that emperumān looks at weak people, just like he saved prahlādan \[hiraṇya’s son\] from his danger.

Here, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that emperumān tore the chest of hiraṇyan into two. *mun* refers to earlier point in time. Alternatively, it could be taken as tearing hiraṇyan’s chest in front of prahlādan \[here, *mun* would refer to ‘in the presence of’ or ‘in front of’\]. *nenju* refers to chest. It is easy to tear the chest. āḻvār says that emperumān tore the heart, which does not have a form. There are those who explain that the meaning for the term *uḷam tottu* is that emperumān was analysing whether hiraṇyan has become favourable towards him. In this case, it would be against hiraṇyan’s earlier pledge \[that there is no emperumān, he is īśvaran and he would kill any other īśvaran, if existing\]. What is the meaning for the term *uḷam tottu*? The reason for the entity, who is omniscient, whose wish never goes waste and who is omnipotent to test hiraṇyan’s heart is this: when hiraṇyan saw the form of emperumān as narasimha, his earlier pledge \[of killing any other God\] disappeared and he turned his back to run away from that place \[in fear\]. However, just as it has been mentioned in the verse “*lōkatrayē sapatimānuśa simhagarbhē*” \[at that time, in all the worlds, the form of narasimha manifested\], since the form of narasimha countered him wherever he ran, with his \[hiraṇya’s\] pledge getting destroyed, emperumān was finding out whether his enmity was still firm. In other words, just as it has been mentioned in [periya tiruvandādi 35](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/11/periya-thiruvandhadhi-35/) “*anbudaiyan anṟē avan*” (emperumān is one with affection), emperumān felt hiraṇyan’s heart to check if he had given up his enmity and was going to die without showing enmity. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that it was not here that emperumān felt hiraṇyan’s heart. When hiraṇya had carried out an offence against emperumān in *kśīrābdi* (milky ocean) in an indirect manner, emperumān had decided. If emperumān had killed one who had given up enmity towards him, there will be a defect in emperumān’s bravery. Apart from this, emperumān had taken a pledge that “We will offer something to the celestial entities”. If he had let go of hiraṇyan, just as he had harmed the residents of *kśīrabdi*, he would have harmed celestial entities too. Since he is *āmāru aṟiyum pirān* \[the benefactor who knows the events which will happen later\], he annihilated hiraṇyan. emperumān had told the entities in samsāram, who do not have the ability to carry out emperumān’s orders and who desist from carrying out what emperumān had forbidden in his orders, to take refuge under him, as mentioned in [bhagavat gītā 18.66](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66/) ”*darmān parityajya mām ēkam śaraṇam vraja*” \[getting rid of other darmas \[all of which have been prescribed to be done\], surrender to me alone\]. Apart from touching his heart and finding out “Does he have at the least, this quality?” and killing hiraṇyan, there was no possibility for emperumān to take him under his refuge.

**kudandai …** – Oh, one who became my svāmy, by reclining in tirukkudandai in order to help those who came after your period of incarnation!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār is addressing emperumān as “My lord”, since he is the *prāpyam* \[ultimate benefit\] for āḻvār, who is reclining in tirukkudandai. More than emperumān’s divine activities of dancing with pots, making the herd-girls to be infatuated with him or analysing hiraṇyan’s heart, it is for the one who is reclining without engaging in any activity that āḻvār has to show his concern.

**kurukkatti …** – You should come such that I could bedeck you with *kurukkatti* flower, which I had searched and kept exclusively for you.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan
