## 2.7.8. Seemaligan avanodu

*seemāligan avanōdu tōḻamail koḷḷavum vallāy!sāmāṟu avanai nī eṇṇic cakkarattāl talai koṇḍāy!āmāṟu aṟiyum pirānē! aṇiyarangattē kidandāy!ēmāṟṟam ennait tavairttāy! iruvātcip pūc cūtta vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

māligan – having the name “māligan” (In the term seemāligan the term see is a courteous word. The samskrutam word śrī has become see in tamiḻ. Since he was kaṇṇan’s friend, this word reflects that relationship); avanōdu – with him, who is famous as being the chief among those with monster-like qualities; tōḻamai koḷḷavum – even to be friendly; vallāy! – oh, one who is capable!; avan – that monster (here, the syllable ai in avanai is for poetic metrics; it does not have any meaning); sām āṟu – the modes of killing him; nī eṇṇi – you had thought of; cakkarattāl – with the cakrāyudam (divine disc); talai koṇḍāy! – oh, one who severed his head!; Am āru – that which is going to happen; aṟiyum – capable of knowing; pirānē! – oh, my lord!; aṇi – being beautiful; arangattu – in the big town of śrī rangam; kidandāy! – oh, one who is reclining!; en – me, who is concerned for you (here again, ai (as in ennai), is a poetic metric); ēmāṟṟam – sorrow; tavirttāy! – oh, one who removed!; iruvātci pū – you should come to don iruvātci pū \[Tuscan jasmine flower\]

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who is capable of even being friendly with māligan, who is the chief among those with monster-like qualities! Oh, one who severed his head, with your divine disc, after analysing the modes in which you could kill him! Oh, my lord, who knows the events which are going to take place! Oh, one who is reclining in the beautiful town of śrī rangam! Oh, one who removed the sorrow of mine, who is concerned about you! You should come to don the Tuscan jasmine flower.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In the earlier pāsuram, āḻvār recalled about the annihilation of hiraṇyan. In this pāsuram, he recalls about the annihilation of māligan.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**seemāligan …** – A person, by name *māligan* was friendly with kriṣṇa. He learnt the usage of weapons from kriṣṇa. With this power, without fearing anyone, he started harming noble people in the world. kriṣṇa thought “He has become a friend, hence it is not possible to kill him” and was troubled in his divine mind. Once, kriṣṇa became angry with seemāligan \[due to his harming noble people\]. seemāligan started blabbering in response with words such as “*naṟugu muṟugu*” \[meaningless harsh words\]. Then, seemāligan told kriṣṇa “You had trained me in all the weapons; but you haven’t trained me in *āḻi* (divine discus)”. kriṣṇa told him “It is a distinct weapon for me; it is not something which is to be done for you”. However, seemāligan compelled kriṣṇa, saying “Is there any weapon which is not to be handled by me?” kriṣṇa thought “Due to his bad nature, he has to be annihilated”. Without any defect to his greatness, he started teaching seemāligan in handling the divine discus. With one divine finger, he spun the divine disc and let it into the sky. As the divine disc came down from the sky, he took it in his divine hand effortlessly. Seeing this, seemāligan said “Is it difficult for me?” Despite kriṣṇa telling him “This is not for you”, seemāligan took the divine disc in his hand, spun it and let it into the sky. As it came down spinning, aiming to take it in his finger, he kept the finger close to his neck. Since it is a sharp disc, and since it did not have enough space to spin from his finger, it severed seemāligan’s head. This narrative, which is mentioned in *itihāsam* \[epic\] etc, has been briefly stated in the earlier part of the pāsuram.

**seemāligan avanōdu tōḻamai koḷḷavum vallāy** – *sī* – a courteous word. Due to your eminent quality, you are capable of being friendly with even a person, named seemāligan, who has monster-like qualities.

**sāmāṟu avanai nī eṇṇi** – Once he started indulging in harming noble persons, you thought “If he is not killed, the world cannot tolerate”, analysing a way for him to die. In other words, the blame that “He had killed his friend” should not come on to him and that it should be said “He died due to his own deed”. In the term *avanai*, the syllable *ai* is a *sāriyai* (augment) and does not have any meaning.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa thought “What shall we do with him? We are not able to make him accept our words of advice. Due to friendship with us, he is harming people in the world. Moreover, he does not realise that any weapon, which is distinct for us will not be under his control, yet he is compelling”. Ultimately, kriṣṇa, who is such that he will enter one’s mind and be sweet, like nectar, thought of the modes by which he could destroy seemāligan, without getting blamed for it and did that in a manner which made āḻvār to celebrate by composing the verse “*tōḻamai koḷḷavum vallāy, sīr cakkarattāl talai koḷḷavum vallāy*” (you are capable of being even friendly and also capable of severing his head with the divine disc).

**cakkarattāl talai koṇḍāy** – Oh, one who severed his head with the divine disc, despite telling him “This is a distinct weapon for me; this is not for you”. Since māligan compelled you, with the garb of training him in that weapon, you had destroyed him through the divine disc as the means.

**āmāṟu aṟiyum pirānē** – Oh, one who is the benefactor, knowing the consequence of engaging with either annihilation of enemy or protection of followers.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār says “*āmāṟu aiyum pirānē*” since the divine disc severed seemāligan’s head. For āḻvār, it is not that emperumān became friendly with seemāligan and severed his head with the intention of killing him in the correct way, which made him to say “*āmāṟu aṟiyum pirānē*”. It is not even emperumān’s nature of being, as said in [tirumālai 15](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thirumalai-15/) “*poyyarkkē poyyanāgum*” (he would display falseness to those who are not interested in him as the ultimate benefit) or when he measured the worlds with his expanded foot, in a deceptive way \[when he went in a deceptive garb to mahābali\] that āḻvār says “*āmāṟu aṟiyum pirānē*”. It is when emperumān reclines in śrī rangam that āḻvār thinks in his divine mind “*aṇiyarangattē kidandāy, āmāṟu aṟiyum pirānē*”. It is due to this that emperumān too removed his sorrow. *ēmāṟṟam* – sorrow. It is the thought of “What will befall this \[most eminent\] entity?” Will it get removed? tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.3.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/03/thiruvaimozhi-8-3-11-uraiya-vennoy/) “*uṟaiyāvennōy tavira*” (removing the cruel disease of wondering “What will happen to bhagavān who is the lord of *ubhaya vibhūti*, the two realms \[materialistic and spiritualistic\]” by eradicating through his grace), emperumān will remove that sorrow. The basis for that is when emperumān makes āḻvār to see the time \[in śrī rangam, there is no threat from enemies\].

**aṇi arangattē kidandāy** – Oh, one who is mercifully reclining in the temple \[at śrī rangam\], which is the decoration for samsāram, thinking “If we remain here, we can attain mumukśus \[those who are desirous of attaining mōkśam\]”!

**ēmāṟṟam ennait tavirttāy** – Oh, one who removed my sorrow as to what will befall you due to your qualities of tenderness etc, by residing in a divine place such as śrī rangam, which is referred to as in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 11-5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/10/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-11-5/) “*nallārgaḷ vāḻum naḷir arangam* ” (divine abode where eminent people reside, not expecting any benefit from emperumān, other than himself)! *ēmāṟṟam* – sorrow

**iruvātcip pūccūtta vārāy** – You should come such that I bedeck your divine locks with this Tuscan jasmine flower, before it loses its freshness, since it has blossomed already at the right time.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.7.9. Andattu amarargal

*aṇḍattu amarargaḷ sūḻa attāṇiyuḷ angu irundāy!toṇḍargaḷ nenjil uṟaivāy! tūmalarāḷ maṇavāḷā!uṇḍittu ulagu ēḻinaiyum ōr ālilaiyil tuyil koṇḍāy!kaṇḍu nān unnai ugakkak karumugaip pūc cūtta vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṇḍattuḷ – in śrī vaikuṇṭam (the term uḷ as in ‘\[attāṇīy\]uḷ angu irundāy’ \[which appears at the end of the first line\] is added here); attāṇi – being together permanently; amarargaḷ – nityasūris \[permanent dwellers of śrī vaikuṇṭam\]; sūḻa – to surround and worship; angu – amidst them; irundāy! – oh, one who is mercifully sitting!; toṇḍargaḷ – of devotees; nenjil – in the minds; uṟaivāy! – oh, one who resides forever!; tū – sacred; malarāḷ – for periya pirāttiyār, who has lotus as her place of birth; maṇam āḷā! – oh, one who is the beloved!; ēḻu ulaginaiyum – all the seven worlds; uṇḍittu – keeping in the divine stomach (such that they are not destroyed during deluge); ōr Al ilaiyil – on a tender banyan leaf; tuyil koṇḍāy – oh, one who is mercifully reclining!; unnai – you; kaṇḍu – I, looking at; ugakka – to feel joyous; karumugaip pū – you should come to don the flowers of a kind of shrub, that yields fragrant flowers, karumugaippū \[also called as malabār jasmine\]

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who is mercifully sitting in śrī vaikuṇṭam, amidst nityasūris who are together with you all the time! Oh, one who residing forever in the minds of devotees! Oh, one who is the beloved of periya pirāttiyār, who was born on a sacred lotus! Oh, one who mercifully reclined on a tender banyan leaf, after keeping all the worlds safely in your divine stomach, such that they are not destroyed during deluge! You should come and don the kurumugaip pū such that I feel joyous, looking at you,**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that āḻvār recalls the way in which emperumān removes hurdles in all the worlds.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**aṇḍattu …** – periya tirumoḻi 10.2.10 “*iṟandāl tangum Ur aṇḍamē*” (after death, the place where all entities reach and stay permanently, is paramapadam). periya tirumoḻi 8.10.10 says “*aṇḍam pōy ātci avarkku*” (\[after getting liberated from samsāram\], they will reach paramapadam and rule all the worlds from there). Thus, the term *aṇḍam* would refer to śrī vaikuṇṭam here.

**aṇḍattuḷ attāṇi amarargaḷ sūḻa angu irundāy** – Oh, one who is sitting in śrī vaikuṇṭam ruling over all the seven worlds with your sceptre, surrounded by nityasūris, who remain in close proximity with you, vorśipping you. *attāṇi* – being in close proximity.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that just as it has been mentioned in [tiruppallāṇḍu 12](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/11/thiruppallandu-12-pallandu-enru/) “*paramātmanaic cūḻndu irundu ēttuvar pallāṇḍē*” (they will surround emperumān and recite mangaḷāśāsanam for him), *aṇḍattu attāṇiyuḷḷē amarargaḷ sūḻa irundāy* – in tripādvibhūti (śrī vaikuṇṭam, which is three times larger than samsāram), you were sitting, being praised by nityasūris, who are always close to you.

**toṇḍargaḷ nenjil uṟaivāy** – Oh, one who resides permanently in the minds of your followers, who live in samsāram, with a higher level of happiness than manifested in paramapadam, and who desire to attain paramapadam!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: Oh, one, who is residing forever in the minds of followers, who are residing in divine abodes of emperumān, such that they could carry out mangaḷāśāsanam!

**tūmlarāḷ maṇavāḷā** – Oh, one who is the beloved of periya pirāttiyār, who was born on a pure lotus flower! emperumān resides with periya pirāttiyār, whether it is in śrī vaikuṇṭam, just as it has been mentioned in Siva purāṇam “*vaikuṇṭētu parēlōkē śriyā sārdam*” (emperumān resides in the most eminent abode of śrī vaikuṇṭam with śrī mahālakśmi) or it is in the minds of his followers, just as it has been mentioned in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.2.10 “*aravindap pāvaiyum tānum agam padi vandu pugundu* ” (entering and staying in the mind, along with periya pirāttiyār who resides on a lotus flower).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: Oh, one who is the unique lord of periya pirāttiyār, which is the reason for residing in the minds of followers!

**uṇḍu …** – Oh, one who mercifully lay down on a tender banyan leaf, after keeping all the worlds safely in your divine stomach, such that they are not destroyed during deluge! The reason for exhibiting this protective quality is the *śrīya*:*patitvam* \[being the consort of śrī mahālakśmi) mentioned earlier. Just as it has been mentioned in śrī stavam 1 “*yasyā vīkśya mukham tadingita parādīnō vidattē’khilam* ” (emperumān executes all the tasks by taking hints from the divine face of periya pirāttiyār), everything is carried out, taking the cue from her.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: Oh, one who is mercifully reclining on a tender banyan leaf, which has still not blossomed fully, after keeping all those, who did not get into the *puruśakāram* \[recommendatory role\] of periya pirāttiyār, safely in your divine stomach during deluge.

**kaṇḍu …** – You should come and don your favourite flower of *karumugaippū* \[malabār jasmine\] such that I become joyous, looking at your divine locks and the garland.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār tells kriṣṇa that he should come such that āḻvār could carry out mangaḷāśāsanam for him and become joyous, bedecking him with *karumugaip pū*.

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.7.10. Senbaga malligai

*seṇbaga malligaiyōdu sengaḻunīr iruvātcieṇ pagar pūvum koṇarndēn inṟu ivai sūtta vā enṟumaṇ pagar koṇḍānai āycci magiḻndu urai seyda im mālaipaṇ pagar villibuttūrk kōn battar pirān sonna pattē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

seṇbagam – campaka flower; malligaiyōdu – along with this flower, jasmine; sengaḻunīr – red water-lily flower too; iruvātci – and Tuscan jasmine flower; eṇ pagar – mentioned as “such and such flower”, counting them; pūvum – all the flowers; koṇarndēn – I brought, searching for them; ivai – these flowers; inṟu – now; sūtta – to don; vā enṟu – saying that you should come; pagar – known famously in śāstram that it is his; maṇ – earth; koṇḍānai – regarding one who measured after taking water from \[king\] mahābali; āycci – yaśōdāp pirātti; magiḻndu – feeling joyous in her mind; urai seyda – mentioned; paṇ – to unite with tune (paṇ – tune); pagar – one, who mentioned; villibuttūrk kōn – the head of śrī villibuttūr; battar pirān – periyāḻvār; sonna – mercifully recited; im mālai – these, which are a garland of words; pattē! – are ten pāsurams!

**Перевод:**

**I have brought flowers such as campaka, jasmine, red water-lily, Tuscan jasmine etc, which have been identified as “such and such flowers” after searching for them. yaśōdāp pirātti had told, with joy in her mid, to emperumān, who had, after taking water from mahābali, measured earth which is famously mentioned in śāstrams as his, to come and don those flowers. periyāḻvār, the controller of śrī villibuttūr, recited these mercifully, with tune and these are the ten such pāsurams.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that in the final pāsuram, āḻvār mentions the benefit to those who recite the pāsurams in this decad and brings it to an end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**seṇbaga malligaiyōdu …** – along with campaka, which blossoms in the morning, and jasmine, which blossoms in the evening, I had searched and brought the morning flowers of red water-lily and Tuscan jasmine. Alternatively, the term *eṇ pagar pū* would refer to flowers which were counted as “Such and such flowers” and were established by śāstrams \[as being appropriate\]. Hence, there is no need to doubt whether a morning flower and an evening flower could be taken together with the same freshness.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, for the same doubt, explains in the following way: when it is for emperumān, there is no boundary with respect to time. When śrī gajēndrāḻvān \[elephant, which was snared by a crocodile in the pond when the elephant entered to pluck a flower to offer to emperumān\] was fighting with the crocodile for a thousand years, the flower which he held in his trunk did not wither at all. It could also be due to cillness. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai cites the following references to establish that when it comes to emperumān, all flowers would retain their freshness and all flowers are appropriate for him; it is only the qualification of the entity who approaches emperumān that is important and not of the offering : (1) [bhagavat gītā 9.26](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/9-26/) “*patram puśpam*” (Any leaf or flower is acceptable to me); (2) [tiruvāimoḻi 1.6.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-6-1-parivathil-isanai/) “*purivaduvum pugaip pūvē*” (submit some type of incense and flower); (3) periya tirumoḻi 11.7.6 “*kaḷḷār tuḻāyum*” (any wild flower and tuḷasi) – along with tuḷasi, which exists exclusively for emperumān, other flowers, even without fragrance, could be offered. It is appropriate for both the follower to offer such flowers and for emperumān to accept such flowers; (4) śrī viṣṇu darmam “*na kaṇḍakārika puśpam*” (flower with thorns are not acceptable) nanjīyar asked bhattar as to how emperumān could say that he will not accept a flower here, when he had said all along differently. bhattar told him that since thorns are present in the plant, they could hurt his followers; hence, emperumān forbids his followers from offering such flowers; thus there is no flower which is not of use to him; similarly, there is no need to look for time such as in [tiruppāvai 29](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/01/thiruppavai-29-chirram-chirukale/) “*siṟṟam siṟu kālē*” (I came to worship you, early in the morning) and in [tiruppallāṇḍu 5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-5-andakkulam/) “*andiyam pōdil*” (during the time of dusk); (5) cāndōjña upanishad “*sarva ganda*: *sarva rasa*:” (emperumān is the repository of all smells and all tastes) it is only when the flowers are taken near the supreme entity that they get their basic nature of smell; (6) [tiruvāimoḻi 1.9.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/10/thiruvaimozhi-1-9-7-tholinai-melum/) “*tōḷiṇai mēlum*” (having cool tuḷasi on his divine shoulders); (7) [periya tiruvandādi 37](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/11/periya-thiruvandhadhi-37/) “*taḻaikkum tuḻāy mārban*” (one who has the sprouting tuḷasi on his divine chest); (8) \[well known verse\] “*ahimsā pratamam puśpam*” (emperumān desires to don harmlessness as the primary flower); (9) [tiruvāimoḻi 1.4.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/07/thiruvaimozhi-1-4-9-nadatha-malar/) “*nādāda malar nādi*” (searching for and offering rare flowers); (10) [tiruvāimoḻi 4.3.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/thiruvaimozhi-4-3-2-pusum-sandhu/) “*pūsum sāndu – punaiyum kaṇṇi – vāsagam sey mālai*” (my heart is sandalwood paste for emperumān; my pāsurams are garlands which are donned); (11) periya tirumoḻi 8.1.10 “*kaliyan olisey tamiḻ mālai*” (the garland strung with the resounding tamiḻ words by tirumangai āḻvār) etc.

***eṇ pagar pūvum koṇarndēn*** – since it has been said that flowers, which were established by śāstrams, were brought with a count, this is representative of all the flowers. Thus, while āḻvār had mentioned nine flowers in the first nine pāsurams, he has cited only four in the final pāsuram \[*seṇbaga malligaiyōdu sengaḻunīr iruvātci*\], due to this reason. This is in line with śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 127.18 “*akāla palinō vrukśā*:” (trees blossomed with unseasonal flowers, when śrī rāma returned to ayōdyā), with śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam ślōkam “*puśpita kānana*:” (as soon as daśarata announced coronation for śrīrāma, all the trees started blossoming flowers) as well as with periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.6.9 “*malargaḷ vīḻum*” (upon hearing the tunes from kriṣṇa’s flute, flowers will fall down on their own).

**koṇarndēn** – I brought

**inṟu ivai sūtta vā enṟu** – you should come such that I could bedeck these on your beautiful, divine locks.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that since āḻvār has said *inṟu*, there is no rule that flowers should blossom in ”morning, noon or evening”. They could blossom any time. Just as it has been mentioned in [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 73](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/01/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-73/) “*ādi nadu andivāy vāynda malar tūvi*” (proffering flowers to emperumān with available flowers, without distinction among morning, noon and night), there is no rule that only specific flowers should be offered. Since āḻvār had said *ivai* (these) in plural count, this term would include flowers which had been left out when he mentioned the first four flowers. In other words, the first four flowers were not representative of all nine flowers.

**maṇ pagar koṇḍānai** – one, who took the land, which śāstram has said to be his. *pagardal* – emperumān’s assertion to grant him three steps of land; or, it could be mahābali’s assertion that he had granted; or, one who has land, which has been established by śāstras to be his.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that it was the land which emperumān had taken after mahābali had said “I have given” through water. It could also be taken as land which emperumān took, after requesting mahābali. This could also be taken as the land which emperumān took, which was established by śāstrams. Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruviruttam 61](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/02/thiruviruththam-61/) “*vēy agam āyinum*” (even land for bamboo), emperumān measured all the worlds with his two steps, not leaving even a little bit of land for a bamboo tree to grow. While mahābali had taken only three worlds, why is āḻvār saying “All the worlds”? āḻvār considers that mahābali has all the fourteen worlds, including the walls of universe. There is none who is inferior to mahābali in terms of being servitors to others \[instead of emperumān alone\] and being dependent on oneself for protection \[in other words, there are others like mahābali, who have other worlds, and emperumān measured everything, without leaving anything, to proclaim all as his\].

**āycci magiḻndu urai seyda** – the pāsurams recited joyously by yaśōdāp pirātti, asking kriṣṇa, who is like this \[as mentioned above\] to come and don them.

**paṇ pagar villibuttūrk kōn battar pirān sonna – immālai – pattē** – these pāsurams are such that even if someone were to say it in any particular manner, tune will come into that person’s recitation. Such is the garland of words, mercifully composed by periyāḻvār, who is the controller of śrī villibuttūr. The term *oru pattē* describes the eminence of the ten pāsurams. Instead of mentioning the benefit for reciting these pāsurams, mentioning its eminence is to make it apparent that the flavour of experiencing the pāsurams is the benefit which will accrue to one who recites them.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that whatever words are spoken by those who reside in villibuttūr and the response of others to such words, would all be in musical form. periyāḻvār is the controller of such śrī villibuttūr. *ōrtta ippattē* – āḻvār praises these ten pāsurams just as nammāḻvār had said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.2.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/05/thiruvaimozhi-1-2-11-serth-thadam/) “*ōrtta ippattē*” (well analysed ten pāsurams). These are the most trust-worthy words. It is only the flower garlands and word garlands which emperumān desires and the follower could carry out.

We shall next consider the pravēśam of the next tirumoḻi.

## 2.8.1. Indiranodu piraman

*indiranōdu piraman īsan imaiyavar ellāmmandira mā malar koṇḍu maṟaindu uvarāy vandu ninṟārcandiran māḷigai sērum sadurargaḷ veḷḷaṟai ninṟāy!andiyam pōdu iduvāgum aḻaganē! kāppida vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

candiran – candran (moon); māḷigai – mansions; sērum – such that it reaches; sadurargaḷ – those, who are capable of carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam, and who reside; veḷḷaṟai – in tiruveḷḷaṟai; ninṟāy – oh, one who is mercifully standing!; indiranōdu – along with dēvēndra (lord of celestial entities); piraman – brahmā too, with four faces; īsan – rudra, also; imaiyavar ellām – along with other celestial entities; mandiram – made pure, through chanting of puruśa sūktam etc; mā malar – distinguished flowers such as kalpakam \[celestial flowers\]; koṇḍu – bringing in their hands; maṟaindu – such that they are invisible to others; uvarāy – without being too near or too far; vandu ninṟār – came and stood; aḻaganē! – Oh, one who is having beauty (such that you have to be protected from evil eyes); idu – this time; andiyam pōdu āgum – is dusk (hence); kāppu ida – to carry out andikkāppu for your beauty; vārāy – you should mercifully come

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who is mercifully standing in tiruveḷḷaṟai, where candran is reaching the mansions and where those, who are capable of carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam, are residing! dēvēndra, brahmā,  rudra and other celestial entities have come, invisible to others, carrying distinguished flowers such as kalpaka, which have been made powerful through chanting of hymns such as puruśa sūktam etc and are standing, neither too far nor too near. Oh, one who is beautiful! This is the time of dusk. You should mercifully come such that I could carry out tiruvandikkāppu for your beauty.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that āḻvār tells kriṣṇa that indra and other celestial entities have come in order to worship him in the evening, asking him to come for andikkāppu.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**indiranōdu …** – indra, who is the protector of three worlds, brahmā, who is the creator of fourteen worlds and rudra, who is the destroyer of the worlds, along with their dependents, who are all celestial entities. Through this, it is made clear that along with the main celestial entities, their dependents too came, without any difference among themselves. While the order should have been brahmā, rudra, indra, what is the reason for mentioning indra first? The difference among them is only on account of the activity which they carry out and not because of any distinctive eminence, among them, of being the controller of all \[that feature is available only with emperumān\]. Moreover, these entities have been carrying out servitude to kriṣṇa, right from the time when he was in the cradle. Hence, āḻvār is including indra, who had given, as in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.3.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/07/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-1-3-3/) “*eḻil udaik kiṇkiṇi*” (beautiful anklet), brahmā, who had given, as in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/07/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-1-3-1/) “*vaṇṇac ciṟut tottil*” (beautiful, small cradle), rudra, who had given as in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.3.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/07/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-1-3-2/) “*udaiyār kaṇamaṇi*” (golden bells for the divine, beautiful waist), and all the other celestial entities, who had given as in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.3.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/07/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-1-3-4/) “*sēvadik kiṇkiṇi*” (anklets for the divine, reddish feet).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that brahmā, rudra, indra and other celestial entities came, invisible to others, standing neither too far nor too near to kriṣṇa. The reason for giving prominence to indra and then mentioning brahmā and rudra is that the pride, which comes due to difference in the levels of karma of individual entities, disappears first with indra \[since he has the shortest longevity \[among indra, brahmā and rudra\].

**mandira māmalar koṇḍu** – with flowers which have been purified by divine hymns. The term *mandiram* refers to śrī puruśa sūktam etc which have been mentioned in all the vēdams. The term *mā malar* refers to \[celestial\] eminent flowers such as kaṟpagam etc.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here \[for both this verse and the next verse\] that the mandirams referred to here are those contained in vēdams. Though they \[indran et al\] think that they are invisible, they are visible to āḻvār. *māmalar* – carrying flowers such as *kaṟpagam* etc, they stand with their faults too, awaiting kriṣṇa’s call. They were standing to carry out mangaḷāśāsanam with, mantrams which have been mentioned in *japa, hōma, dāna, tarpaṇam* \[these are rituals conducted either as nitya or naimittika karma, viz. ordained every day or for specific occasion respectively\]. There are some animals, which think that if they close their eyes, they will be invisible. The term *uvar* will not be applicable to those who have gone past the three qualities \[*satva, rajas* and *tamas*\] \[They would have been identified as *ivar*, these people; since they have been identified as *uvar*, they are less desirable entities\].

**maṟaindu uvarāy vandu ninṟār** – just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.7.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/10/thiruvaimozhi-7-7-11-katkariya-piraman/) “*katkariya piraman sivan indiran*” (entities such as brahmā, rudra, indra et al who are difficult to see for the eyes of humans), entities such as brahmā, rudra, indra et al, who are invisible to human beings, came and stood, waiting for their turn to be called out by you, neither too far away from you nor too near you. If the text has been *maṟaindu uvarā* \[instead of *maṟaindu uvarāy*\], the meaning for the term *uvarā* would be that they were neither too far nor too near.

**candiran …** – since the mansions are very tall, reaching up to the moon, candran could come and reach the mansions. Oh, one who is mercifully standing in the divine abode of tiruveḷḷaṟai, where people, who are capable of knowing your tender nature and who carry out mangaḷāśāsanam for you, reside!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mansions, in which śrī vaiṣṇavas dwell, and the temple \[in tiruveḷḷaṟai\] are such tall that candran reaches there. Through this, it is implied that those with deep, inner knowledge \[regarding ātma guṇams, viz. one is subservient to emperumān, dependent on emperumān etc\] reach there \[we have seen in the padigam 1.4 \[*than mugattuc cutti*\] that tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai refers to *madi*, *niṟaimadi*, *māmadi* etc as entities with knowledge of ātma guṇams\]. Knowledge born out of śāstrams \[sacred texts\] is like the radiance from a lamp. Those with this knowledge, and detached from worldly pursuits, are considered to be with knowledge like *āditya* \[sun\]. Knowledge gained through the instructions of an ācarya is like full moon. While there is parity among those with this knowledge \[leading to *ananyārhatvam*, existing only for emperumān\], who live in divine abodes \[such as tiruveḷḷaṟai\] and śrī vaikuṇṭam, it is a matter of honour for those in nitya vibhūti to descend to divine abodes to worship emperumān. *sadurargaḷ veḷḷaṟai ninṟay* – it is here \[tiruveḷḷaṟai\] that he \[emperumān\] also desires to reach. This is the reason that, just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 6.9.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/08/periya-thirumozhi-6-9-8/) “*nilaiyāra ninṟān*” (emperumān mercifully stayed forever), emperumān dwelt in tiruveḷḷaṟai. The term *sadir* \[derived from *caturargaḷ*\] refers to a tree, bearing fruits directly, without going through the stage of flowering. They are that capable. In other words, they will give response through their actions, as mentioned in the verse “*kriyā kēvalam uttaram*” (responding through action). They are similar to the followers of emperumān, as mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.7.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-7-6-alikkum-paramanai/) “*salippinṟi āṇḍu*” (engaging us firmly in service), capable of removing our connection with samsāram through their activities.

**andiyam pōdu idu āgum** – this is the time of dusk. Since you are indulging in playing, you are not aware that the sun has set.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that through the term *andiyam pōdu*, āḻvār, due to fear that it is the time when people with predominance of *rajō guṇam* \[characteristics of passion, aggression etc\] roam around, with high levels of *ahankāram* (egoistic tendencies) and who would not be able to bear the wealth of others, asks kriṣṇa to come \[so that he could carry out *andikkāppu*\]

**aḻaganē** – Oh, one who has the beauty such that you have to be kept protected from evil eyes due to fear from those eyes, constantly. Just as you are unaware of sun-set, you are unaware of your beauty too!

**kāppida vārāy** – you should come so that I could carry out *tiruvandikkāppu* \[protecting you from evil eyes\], for your natural beauty as well as the beauty from decorations \[with flowers etc\].

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.8.2. Kanrugal illam

*kanṟugaḷ illam pugundu kadaṟuginṟa pasu ellāmninṟu oḻindēn unnaik kūvi nēsamēl onṟum ilādāy!manṟil nillēl andippōdu madiḷ tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟāy!nanṟu kaṇḍāy endan sollu nān unnaik kāppida vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

pasu ellām – all the cows; kanṟugaḷ illam – in the place where calves stand; pugundu – entering; kadaṟuginṟa – were mooing aloud, since they \[owners of the cows\] neither let the calves to drink their milk nor let them be milked, leading to pain in the udder due to excessive secretion; unnaik kūvi – calling out to you; ninṟu oḻindēn – I stood; nēsam onṟum – not even a little bit of affection towards me (the syllable ēl in nēsamēl is for poetic metric; it does not have a meaning); ilādāy! – oh, one who is without \[that affection\]!; andip pōdu – at dusk; manṟil – at the junction of four streets; nillēl – do not stand; madiḷ – having fortified walls; tiruveḷḷaṟai – in tiruveḷḷaṟai; ninṟāy – oh, one who is standing and showering your mercy!; en than – your mother, my; sollu – word; nanṟu kaṇḍāy – will be good for you, you will see

**Перевод:**

**Calling out to you repeatedly, I have stood, doing nothing else. Cows have entered the area where calves are standing and are crying out, since they have pain in their udders due to excessive secretion of milk, which has not been removed either through the calves drinking or the cows being milked. Oh, one who is without even an iota of affection towards me! During the time of dusk, do not stand at the junction of four streets. Oh, one who is mercifully standing at tiruveḷḷaṟai! You would see that my, your mother’s, words are apt for you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kanṟu …** – Cows entered the place where calves have been kept; since there was none to let the calves to drink their milk or to milk them \[the cows\], with excessive secretion of milk, their udders became painful for them and they started mooing loudly. Alternatively, the term *kadaṟuginṟa* could be added to both the calves and the cows. In this case, the meaning would be: the calves entered the cattle-shed, and since they were not allowed to drink milk from the cows, were mooing loudly; the cows, standing outside, not able to nurse their calves or none to milk them, were mooing loudly due to pain in their udders.  When kriṣṇa asked her “They are mooing aloud since you have not let the calves to go and drink their milk. Why didn’t you do it?” yaśōdāp pirātti says …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says additionally that yaśōdāp pirātti asks kriṣṇa “If they do not give milk, how will you eat?

**ninṟoḻindēn unnaik kūvi** – I have stood here, calling out to you. Who will look after them there? Just as the cows keep mooing, thinking of their calves, I am standing here, calling out to you.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa “You are not coming when I call you” Is it only this much?

**nēsamēl onṟum ilādāy** – Oh, one who is without any affection towards me! ṣouldn’t you have the affection towards me, which the calves have towards their mothers who are mooing for them? You are without even a little bit of that affection. When kriṣṇa responds saying “Am I without any affection towards you? Is it not for playing, that I stood outside?” she tells him …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai continues here, from the previous verse: yaśōdāp pirātti further tells kriṣṇa “It is not that you do not have any affection towards me, thinking ‘We will not go to the place where she is calling me’. Apart from the affection that I should control you and make you carry out what I tell you, you do not have any affection for me. Beyond this, you do not have any affection for me”

**manṟil nillēl andippōdu** – Do not stand at the junction of four streets during dusk time when lowly deities roam around there. This is neither the place nor the time for playing.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says additionally here: The other boys, who were playing with you, have gone to their respective house. You may not know about yourself; should you remain without any care, not knowing about me too?

**madiḷ tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟāy** – Oh, one who is mercifully standing in tiruveḷḷaṟai, which has fortified walls such that those who carry out mangaḷāśāsanam for you, do not need to fear for you! Instead of going out repeatedly, if you stay within that protection, there is no need for me to fear for your well-being.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: yaśōdāp pirātti thinks that if kriṣṇa were to come inside the protective walls, she could, without any stress on her, look after the calves, ask the herd-men to milk the cows and look after her house chores. The protective walls in tiruveḷḷaṟai are such that the mangaḷāśāsanaparars \[those who wish well for emperumān and praise him\] could sleep without any care in the world.

**nanṟu kaṇḍāy endan sollu** – Despite her saying these worlds, since kriṣṇa did not heed her, she tells him “You would see that my words would do good for you. Heed them”. This is similar to her words, as mentioned in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2.2.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/10/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-2-2-5/) “*tāyar vāyccol karumam kaṇḍāy*” (children should necessarily listen to their mothers’ words).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: āḻvār tells kriṣṇa that these words are good for her, for him, for the calves which kriṣṇa desires and for the cows, which give milk.

**nān unnaik kāppu ida vārāy** – You should come such that I, who am having plenty of affection towards you, would be able to carry out *kāppu* \[protection\] continuously for you, when you have such *saukumāryam* (tenderness) etc.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār’s *nān* \[as in I will carry out *kappū* for you\] is as follows: he \[tiruvāimoḻi piḷḷai\] explains the terms *nān* and *unnai* with reference to *rahasya trayam* \[three esoteric mantrams\]. \[*nān* would refer to one who has ego, while *adiyēn* would refer to one who is a servitor. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai explains the background for āḻvār using the term *nān*\]. In tirumantram, the first word *Om* has three syllables, *a*, *u*, and *ma*, with a hidden case *āya* over the first syllable, *a*. Here, the syllable *a* refers to emperumān (1) who is *kāraṇam*, \[the cause of everything\], (2) who is *rakśakan* \[the protector\] and (3) who is *śēśi* \[lord of all\], the syllable *ma* refers to jīvātmā \[soul\], *u* refers to exclusive servitude of jīvātmā towards emperumān, and *āya*, the case hidden over *a*, refers to ‘for’. Thus, the meaning here is that jīvātmā is a servitor, exclusively for emperumān. In the third word of this *rahasyam*, there is a term *āya* \[*nārāyaṇāya*\], which refers to *prārtanā* \[praying to emperumān to accept service from jīvātmā for emperumān who is together with pirātti\]. The person who says *nān*, thus starts with knowing that he carries out servitude exclusively for emperumān \[as denoted by the third syllable *ma*, in *Om*, moves on to know that he is praying to emperumān to grant him that servitude, through *āya*, in the last syllable of tirumantram. Thus, āḻvār says that he is a servitor, exclusively to emperumān, constantly praying to him to grant him the opportunity to carry out mangaḷāśāsanam to both emperumān and pirātti \[Hence, there is nothing egoistic here, when āḻvār uses the term *nān*\]. Similarly, the term *unnai* \[kriṣṇa\] refers to *a,* the first syllable in the first *rahasyam* denoting emperumān as the causative entity, protector and lord of all.  In the third *rahasyam*, *carama ślōkam* \[ultimate hymn\], there is a term *aham*, which emperumān speaks of himself as one who is (1) *sarvajñan* \[omniscient\], (2) *sarva śaktan* \[omnipotent\], (3) *prāptan* \[one who is to be attained\] and (4) *pūrṇan* \[one who is complete in all aspects\]. Through the term *unnai*, the servitor starts with knowing that emperumān is the cause, he is the protector and is the lord, gradually going on to understand in the *carama ślōkam* that emperumān is the omniscient, omnipotent, goal to be reached and complete in all aspects. Thus, āḻvār refers to kriṣṇa as the entity who is the causative factor for all, who is the protector and who is the lord of all. He also says that kriṣṇa is the omniscient, omnipotent entity, who is to be attained and who is complete in all aspects. Thus, we can see here that even when āḻvār says *nān*, he knows that emperumān is the lord and that he \[āḻvār\] is the servitor. Also, he is an eminent entity \[emperumān, who denotes all the meanings as seen above in the syllables *a* and *aham*\] who is standing mercifully in tiruveḷḷaṟai.

Now, *unnai* should be transformed as *unakku*, ‘for you’ \[Hence, āḻvār says *nān unakkuk kāppida vārāy*,viz., come such that I could perform *kāppu* for you\]. This is similar to periya tirumoḻi 8.9.3 “*kaṇṇapuram onṟu udaiyānukku*” (for the one who has tirukkaṇṇapuram as his distinguished divine abode).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai further says that the term *manṟu* (as in *manṟil*) refers to the intersection of four streets, where many people will meet and go about their ways. He says that this is also the place where those who have predominance of *rajō guṇam* (with qualities of desire, passion, aggression etc), who follow the rituals mentioned in the first part of vēdam \[*karma kāṇḍam*, carrying out rituals which are ordained and also those which are done towards fulfilment of a desire {*kāmya karmam*)\] visit frequently. Since they desire other *puruśārtams* instead of emperumān, āḻvār too does not think about them. The term *kanṟu* refers to those who follow what has been ordained and who are incapable of protecting themselves. The term *pasukkaḷ* refers to those whose sorrow will not be removed unless they call those who are incapable of protecting themselves \[who are like calves\] and protect them.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.8.3. Seppodum menmulai

*seppōdu menmulaiyārgaḷ siṟu sōṟum illum sidaittittuappōdu nān urappap pōy adisilum uṇḍilai āḷvāy!muppōdum vānavar ēttum munivargaḷ veḷḷaṟai ninṟāy!ippōdu nān onṟum seyyēn empirān! kāppida vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

muppōdum – at all three times of morning, noon and evening; vānavar – by celestial entities; ēttum – as one who is praised; munivargaḷ – those, who constantly keep meditating on your qualities of eminence, reside; veḷḷaṟai – in tiruveḷḷaṟai; ninṟāy! – oh, one who is standing and showering your mercy!; empirān! – oh, one who is my lord!; āḷvāy! – oh, one who incarnated to rule over us!; seppu ōdum – being such that it could be called as golden bowl; mel – being soft; mulaiyārgaḷ – those who have bosoms; siṟu sōṟum – sand, which has been considered as rice and cooked as a playful act; illum – houses made of sand; sidaittittu – destroying them; appōdu – during the time when you destroyed them; nān urappa – when I uttered words in anger; pōy – running in fear; adisilum – even sweet rice; uṇḍilai – you did not eat; ippōdu – now; nān onṟum seyyēn – I will not indulge in catching or beating you. You should come such that I could carry out kāppu

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who is standing in tiruveḷḷaṟai and showering your mercy, where celestial entities keep praying to you on all three times of morning, noon and night and where those who keep meditating constantly on your eminence, reside! Oh, one who is my lord! Oh, one who incarnated in order to rule over us! You destroy the houses, built with sand, and rice, cooked with sand, by those who have bosoms which are soft and appear like a golden bowl. When I use words in anger, when you do such activities, you run away, without eating sweet rice kept for you. Now, I will not catch you or beat you. You should come and allow me to carry out kāppu for you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that kriṣṇa asks yaśōdāp pirātti  “āren’t you calling me in order to keep me inside the fortified walls instead of allowing me to play outside, after you have carried out your decorations, kāppu etc?” yaśōdāp pirātti says “I will not do anything”*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**seppu …** – those who have bosoms which have a form looking like copper, but being soft instead of being hard like that

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa “You have still not eaten the sweet rice which I have made for you, after I had scolded you not to play with girls, who have their bosoms which appear like copper and who have soft nature, by destroying their food and houses made of sand, despite my calling out to you repeatedly”. Is this the way you are ruling over me? This is similar to [periyāḻvār 1.6.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/09/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-1-6-11/) “*ātkoḷḷattōnṟiya āyar tam kōvinai*” (one who incarnated in the clan of herd-people as their head, in order to rule over them).

**siṟu sōṟum illum sidaittittu** – destroying the rice and houses, made by them with sand, as an outlet for their playing

**appōdu nān urappap pōy** – when I became angry then, telling you “Do not play with girls, holding their hands and fighting with them”, you were afraid to stand in my presence, thinking that I am going to catch you and beat you.

**adisilum uṇḍilai** – You have not consumed the sweet rice, which I had affectionately prepared for you.

**ennai āḷvānē** – Oh, who was born to rule over me! Is this the manner in which you wish to rule over me? For her, his ruling over her would happen when he listens to her words, consumes whatever she gives and behaves like a calf controlled through a stick.

**muppōdum …** – celestial entities worship you three times in a day, in the morning, noon and evening, when they have *brahma bhāvanai* in predominance \[*brahma bhāvanai* refers to engaging with thoughts about emperumān, as opposed to *karma bhāvanai* when one engages with carrying out rituals as mentioned in vēdams\], just like it has been mentioned in [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 73](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/01/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-73/) “*ādi nadu andi vāy*” (reciting the divine names of emperumān, during dawn, noon and dusk times); sages, who keep meditating upon your well-being constantly, reside in tiruveḷḷaṟai. Oh, one who is mercifully standing in such tiruveḷḷaṟai!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as it has been mentioned in [periya tiruvandādi 64](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/01/periya-thiruvandhadhi-64/) “*uranāl oru mūnṟu pōdum*” (thinking with their minds, on three occasions in a day), emperumān listens mercifully when celestial entities praise him, when *brahma bhāvanai* comes to the fore for them, and sages, who keep meditating constantly, desire the divine abode tiruveḷḷaṟai. Oh, one who is standing there and showering your mercy!

**ippōdu nān onṟum seyyēn** – Though I had spoken a few words then, having good intention for you, I will not do anything to you now.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār tells kriṣṇa “Apart from feeding you sweet rice, I will not control you”. But kriṣṇa runs away, saying “āren’t these your \[false\] words?” Even as he ran away, āḻvār kept chasing him. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai wonders at this turn of events \[emperumān is the most eminent entity and he is running away, and, periyāḻvār, who is his servitor, is running after him, hoping to catch him\]. He says that the pāsuram should be transposed as following, to get sequential meaning: *empirān ennai āḷvāy, seppōdu menmulaiyārgaḷ siṟu sōṟum illum sidaittittu nān urappappōy, muppōdum vānavargaḷ ēttum munivargaḷ veḷḷaṟai ninṟāy ippōdu adisilum uṇḍilai; ippōdu nān onṟum seyyēn; kāppida vārāy*

**empirān kāppida vārāy** – Oh, one who is my lord! You should come such that I could carry out *kāppu* for you.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.8.4. Kannil manalkodu

*kaṇṇil maṇal kodu tūvik kālināl pāyndanai enṟu enṟueṇṇarum piḷḷaigaḷ vandittu ivarāl muṟaippaduginṟārkaṇṇanē! veḷḷaṟai ninṟāy! kaṇḍārōdē tīmaigaḷ seyvāy!vaṇṇamē vēlai adu oppāy! vaḷḷalē! kāppida vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇṇanē – oh, one who is easy to approach!; veḷḷaṟai ninṟāy! – oh, one who is standing in tiruveḷḷaṟai and showering your grace!; kaṇḍārōdē – with strangers; tīmaigaḷ seyvāy! – oh, one who indulges in misciefs!; vaṇṇam – through colour (the syllable E in vaṇṇamē is for poetic metric; it does not have any meaning); vēlai adu oppāy! – oh, one who is like an ocean \[this refers to his matching the colour of ocean); vaḷḷalē! – oh, one who is magnanimous!; eṇ arum – countless; piḷḷaigaḷ – girls (who engaged with you, due to your activities); ivar – these people (the syllable Al (as in ivarāl) is for poetic metric. It does not have any; vandittu – coming in front of me; kaṇṇil – “in our eyes; maṇal – sand; kodu tūvi – had strewn; kālināl – with legs; pāyndanai – had kicked”; enṟu enṟu – saying separately, regarding you; muṟaippaduginṟār – they are complaining (Hence, instead of going to them hereafter, come to me so that I could carry out kāppu)

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who is standing in tiruveḷḷaṟai and showering your mercy! You are indulging in misciefs with strangers. Oh, one who matches ocean in the divine complexion! Oh, one who is magnanimous! Countless girls are coming in front of me and are complaining to me about you, individually, saying “You had strewn sand in our eyes and kicked us with your feet”. Hereafter, do not go to them. Come to me so that I could carry out kāppu for you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam says the following: in the earlier pāsuram, yaśōdāp pirātti had told kriṣṇa “Don’t’ run away. Come”. But he ran away. Some people came and complained to her “He strew sand in the eyes”. She says a few words, unable to tolerate their complaints.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kaṇṇil …** – yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa that the mothers of countless girls, who were engaged with him, came and complained to her “While we were playing with our eyes open, you had strewn sand in our eyes. When we asked you ‘Why did you strew sand in our eyes?’ you had kicked us”. They complained individually, you could see that.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that countless children, who were playing, came and complained to yaśōdāp pirātti “You had strewn sand in our eyes”; “You had kicked us”. Looking at them, yaśōdāp pirātti held kriṣṇa tightly, and was angry looking at them, thinking *ivarār muṟaippaduginṟār* (Who are these people, complaining?) In other words, she was telling them – You are many; he is a single person. And, you people are complaining. Immediately, kriṣṇa told her “They strew sand in my eyes; they kicked me”. It was this which appeared to be true, to her.

**kaṇṇanē veḷḷaṟai ninṟāy** – Oh, one who is standing in tiruveḷḷaṟai, being easily approachable for all, and showering your mercy!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa: “Do not stand near them such that they could see you. Come here”. Alternatively, “You are such an easy person to approach that you stood in a manner that they could carry out mischief towards you”. *veḷḷaṟai ninṟāy* – your standing here is even easier to approach you than in tiruvāyppādi.

**kaṇḍārōdē tīmai seyvāy** – Unlike those who have connection with you and are affectionate towards you, who would tolerate your misciefs, oh, one who is carrying out misciefs with strangers! You should see that you should not indulge in such misciefs.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa is engaging in misciefs with those who are unable to tolerate him.

**vaṇṇamē …** – Oh, one matches the ocean through your divine complexion! *vaṇṇam* – complexion. The syllable *E* \[as in *vaṇṇamē*\] refers to emphasis. *vēlai* – ocean. The term *adu* \[as in *vēlai adu oppāy*\] refers to ocean only. Through this, it is indicated that even if he carries out misciefs, he has such a beauty of his divine form that he could not be disregarded.

**vaḷḷalē**– Oh, one who gave that beauty of your divine form to me such that I could feel happy!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, at the end, that samsāris, without realising their faults, are shifting the blame on emperumān. For this, they say that emperumān made them to indulge in worldly pursuits. The term *kaṇṇil maṇal kodu tūvi* refers to hiding knowledge, which one gets through vēdam, by making those people to engage with sensory pursuits. Again, they indulge in the impure worldly pursuits on their own accord and try to attain emperumān through other means. While they have this fault, they say that emperumān kicked them into these, when they should have realised that it is emperumān’s divine feet which are the readily available means to attain him. Even though emperumān sees such people, he still resides close to them, in their hearts, and this is referred to as *tīmai* \[mischief\].

**kāppida vārāy** – you should come such that I could carry out *kāppu* for your divine beauty.

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.8.5. Pallayiravar ivvuril

*pallāyiravar ivvūril piḷḷaigaḷ teemaigaḷ seyvārellām unmēl anṟippōgādu empirān! nī ingē vārāynallārgaḷ veḷḷaṟai ninṟāy! jñānac cudarē! un mēnisollāra vāḻtti ninṟēttic coppadak kāppida vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

nallārgaḷ – inhabited by virtuous people; veḷḷaṟai – in tiruveḷḷaṟai; ninṟāy! – oh, one who is standing and showering your mercy!; jñānam – wisdom; sudarē! – oh, one who has as radiance!; em pirān! – oh, one who is my lord!; i ūril – in this place of herd-people; teemaigaḷ seyvār – carrying out misciefs; piḷḷaigaḷ – boys; pal āyiram – there are many thousands; ellām – all their misciefs; un mēl anṟi – apart from falling on you; pōgādu – will not go elsewhere; nī ingē vārāy – you should come here, instead of joining with them; un mēni – your divine form; sol Ara – to be fully apt with words; ninṟu ētti – praying (the word ninṟu does not have a meaning here; it is a pleasant word); vāḻtti – carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam (wishing well for you and carrying out servitude); soppada – come for carrying out kāppu, well

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who is standing in tiruveḷḷaṟai, where virtuous people reside, and who is showering your mercy! Oh, one who has the radiance of wisdom! Oh, one who is my lord! There are thousands of children in this place of herd-people, who are indulging in misciefs. All those activities, indulged in by these children, will fall only on you and will not be put on anyone else. Hence, you should come here instead of playing with them, such that I could carry out kāppu very well for you, praising your divine form with words which are fully apt and wishing well for you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that this pāsuram is a continuation of the earlier one, explaining similar features.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**pallāyiravar …** – among the five-lakh people who live in this place, there will be many thousands who would be indulging in mischief.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, additionally, that in the opinion of the mischief mongers and looking at kriṣṇa’s activities, those who do not know the happenings would tend to believe that kriṣṇa had caried out the misciefs.

**ellām un mēl anṟip pōgādu** – they shifted the blame due to misciefs carried out by them, on you. Hence, the misciefs indulged in by them, will come onto you only and will not go elsewhere.

**empirān nī ingē vārāy** – Oh, one who is my lord! You should move away from those who find fault with you and come here, where their thoughts and words will not be tolerated.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, additionally here, the following: Instead of staying in such places, you should come to those who do not tolerate the thoughts and words of those people. Just as it has been mentioned in mahābhāratam, when udanga maharishi \[sage udanga\] mentioned the meaning of this to kriṣṇa, kriṣṇa told him “Why did you come here? Why don’t you go, looking after your interests?” \[The narration here is that udanga maharishi wanted to tell kriṣṇa that he is responsible for pāṇḍavas’ victory and kauravas’ defeat in the mahābhāta war; his intention was to have the darśan of kriṣṇa in the viśvarūpa form, which kriṣṇa manifested to him. This example has been cited here to show how people would shift all the blame on kriṣṇa\]. In mahābhāratam, it has also been said that dritarāśtra \[head of kauravas\] et al said “*jānāmi darmam na ca mē pravrutti*: *jānāmi adarmam na ca mē nivrutti*: l *kēnā’pi dēvēna hrudi stitēna yatā niyuktōsmi tatā karōmi*” (I know what is the correct actions to be carried out, I am unable to engage with them; I know what are the incorrect actions that one should not carry out, I am unable to desist from engaging with them. There is a deity sitting inside me; I am doing as per his instructions). Thus, they claim that they are knowledgeable but the deity is responsible for my engaging and desisting actions. This was mentioned to sanjaya \[dritarāśtran’s charioteer\], who told dritarāhtra “I do not know deceits; let auspicious bodings come your way \[this example has been taken to stress the fact that people would blame emperumān for their actions \[just as dritarāśtra did\], not taking responsibility and there are people who would not tolerate those words \[just as śanjaya did\]\].

āḻvārs too, in some situations \[when they are in anguish and emperumān has not removed their hurdle\] have spoken like this, as mentioned by (1) nammāḻvār in [tiruvāīmoḻi 7.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/thiruvaimozhi-7-1-1-unnilaviya/) “*innum nalivān eṇṇuginṟāy*” (you are planning to torment me even after I have acquired the urge to reach you); (2) tirumangai āḻvār in periya tirumoḻi 11.8.1 “*āṟṟangarai vāḻmaram pōl anjuginṟēn*” (I am like the tree on the river bank, constantly in fear about the impending danger); (3) tirumangai āḻvār in periya tirumoḻi 11.8.2 “*sīṟṟam uḷa āgilum solluvan*” (even if I have the faults in me which will make you angry, I will still say); (4) kulasēkara āḻvār in [perumāḷ tirumoḻi 5.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/07/perumal-thirumozhi-5-1/) “*taru tuyaram tadāyēl*” (if you do not remove this sorrow called as samsāram, which you have given yourself); (5) nammāḻvār in [periya tiruvandādi 3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/10/periya-thiruvandhadhi-3/) “*ivai enṟu ivai aṟivanēlum – ennāl adaippu nīkku oṇṇādu*” (even though I know that it is right, not praising you or that it is not bad, not  praising you, it is not possible for me either to accept or reject these) and similar pāsurams. Instead of interpreting these pāsurams the way we wish, we should attain an expert ācārya \[preceptor\], pray to him and listen from him the activities carried out by our preceptors and their words about these in a detailed manner. Even if we are not able to practise the activities of our preceptors, if we regret our inability to do so and have the knowledge of carrying out the activities in the proper manner, it would be good for us.

**nallārgaḷ veḷḷaṟai ninṟāy** – Oh, one who is standing and showering your mercy in tiruveḷḷaṟai, where those who do not tolerate people who shift their blame on you, and who are affectionate towards you, carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam for you, reside!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the preceptors in tiruveḷḷaṟai are as good as the children in tiruvāyppādi \[śrī gōkulam\] who do not indulge in misciefs. These people will not indulge in any unjust act; even if they commit, by oversight, any fault, they will not blame emperumān for that. In the incarnations of emperumān, if it appears that he had indulged in any doubtful activities, they would set those right and instruct the people of the world accordingly, as a benefit for them. These people have such a wealth of *śrīviaṣṇavam* \[the principles of being a servitor to emperumān\]. The term *nallārgaḷ* refers to such people in tiruveḷḷaṟai. They are good to emperumān, to nityasūris, to themselves and to the people in leelā vibhūti, based on their capabilities.

**jñānac cudarē** – Oh, one who has the radiance of wisdom!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that emperumān’s divine form is such that it spreads the radiance of wisdom \[normally, it is the *ātmā* \[soul\] which is said to carry wisdom\]. One would think whether emperumān’s divine form is the repository of knowledge.

**un mēni** – your divine form which is the resplendent repository for that wisdom and your basic nature, on which the wisdom rests.

**sollāra – ninṟētti** – praising you such that the words, which are used to praise you, get their meanings. Words would get their meanings only when they engage with the entity who is the meaning of all the words. This is in line with [nānmugan tiruvandādi 69](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-69/) “*kavikku niṟai poruḷāy ninṟān*” (He remains as the complete meanings of all the praises sung on him by poets).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that emperumān is to be praised such that the words get fulfilment. The words would get fulfilment only when the meanings get fulfilled. This is possible only in the word *nārāyaṇa* \[which is called as the *vyāpaka* mantram, that which indicates permeation of emperumān everywhere\], which is different from the other two *vyāpaka mantrams* \[of vāsudēva and viṣṇu\]. This takes root in the *samāsa dvayam* \[*tatpurśa samāsam*, a compound word which indicates that all the jīvātmās reside in nārāyaṇan, thus highlighting his *paratvam* or eminence\] and *bahuvrīhi samāsam*, another compound word which indicates that nārāyaṇa resides in the jīvātmās, thus highlighting his *saulabhyam* or ease of approach\].This is also seen in the *dvaya mahāmantram* which highlights nārāyaṇa being the *upāyam* \[means to attain him\] and *prāpyam* \[the *puruśārtam* or the ultimate benefit\]. Since this word \[nārāyaṇa\] contains all the meanings, as mentioned above, only when he is praised, the words which are used to praise him, would get fulfilment. This gets completed when the emperumān, kaṇṇan, at tiruveḷḷaṟai is praised. This is also the reason why the people in tiruveḷḷaṟai are referred to as *nallārgaḷ*. Is so much required when āḻvār has to perform *kāppu* for kriṣṇa? Just as it has been mentioned in [perumāḷ tirumoḻi 2.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/09/periya-thirumozhi-2-4/) “*ētti vāḻttum en nanjamē*” \[my heart will praise and carry out mangaḷāśāsanam for the followers of emperumān\], singing *pallāṇḍu pallāṇḍu* \[carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam\] for emperumān is required to be carried out.

**vāḻtti** – carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam

**soppadak kāppida vārāy** – You should come such that I could carry out *kāppu* very well, for you. s*oppada* – very well.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *kāppu* refers to *sēvadi sevvi tirukkāppu* (there should be complete protection for the beauty of your reddish divine feet).

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.8.6. Kanjan karukkondu

*kanjan kaṟukkoṇḍu nin mēl karuniṟac cemmayirp pēyaivanjippadaṟku viduttān enbadōr vārttaiyum uṇḍumanju tavaḻ maṇi māda madiḷ tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟāy!anjuvan nī angu niṟka aḻaganē! kāppida vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

manju – clouds; tavaḻ – having a height such that they glide over; maṇi – embellished with the nine gemstones; mādam – mansions; madiḷ – and fortified walls; tiru veḷḷaṟai – in tiruveḷḷaṟai; ninṟāy! – oh, one who is standing and showering your mercy!; kanjan – “kamsan; nin mēl – on you; kaṟu(ppu)k koṇḍu – with anger; karu niṟam – having a dark complexion; sem mayir – and having reddish locks; pēyai – pūtanā; vanjippadaṟku – to kill you through deceit; viduttān – had sent”; enbadu – to this effect; ōr vārttaiyum – a narrative; uṇḍu – have heard, even when you were born; nī angu niṟka – for you to stand there; anjuvan – I am fearful; aḻaganē! – oh, one who has a beauty such that it has to be protected through kāppu! You should come, for me to carry it out

**Перевод:**

**tiruveḷḷaṟai has tall mansions, embellished with nine gemstones, and compound walls, such that cloud will glide over them. Oh, one who is mercifully standing there and showering your mercy! Even as you were born, we have heard of a narrative that “kamsan, with lot of anger on you, had sent pūtanā, with a dark complexion and reddish locks, in order to kill you deceitfully”. Hence, I am fearful when you stand there. Oh, one who has beauty which needs to be protected! You should come such that I could carry out kāppu for you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that in the previous pāsuram, āḻvār had told kriṣṇa not to stay with those who transpose their faults as kriṣṇa’s faults and to come to him. Since he did not come, āḻvār calls him with an urge, in this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kanjan …** – From the day that an *aśarīri* \[voice, without a form behind it\] was heard \[saying that the eighth son of dēvakip pirātti and vasudēvar would kill him\], kamsan was not only furious, he developed a total enmity in his mind; due to excessive doubt, he killed the first six children by smashing their heads against a stone, left the seventh when he was told that the foetus had collapsed and was awaiting the birth of the eighth, wondering as to “When will it be born?” in order to harm the child. Even as he was waiting, with none other than your \[kriṣṇa’s\] parents knowing, you were born in darkness. Through the words of durgai \[the girl child born to yaśōdāp pirātti, but changed places with kriṣṇa on the night that he was born\] and other sources, kamsan came to know that you had left that place \[maturā\] and shifted to tiruvāyppādi \[śrī gōkulam\] in that darkness itself. He became very furious in your matter. The word *kaṟuppu* has got shortened here as *kaṟu*. *kaṟuppu* – fury.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa found a way to be alive even after seeing six of his brothers getting killed by kamsan and had entered tiruvāyppādi with protection \[through vasudēvar and ādiśēśan\] and his intelligence. kamsan heard that kriṣṇa was growing up well there. kamsan thought that he could carry out the task of killing kriṣṇa through pūtanā. Hence, it is said that kamsan was furious with kriṣṇa.

**karu niṟam …** – pūtanā, the fiend sent by kamsan to kill you, had a form as if darkness had taken a shape. Her locks looked like flames from red hot fire. There is a narrative to the effect that kamsan told her “Do not confront kriṣṇa directly with this form; you will not be able to destroy him; go with a deceitful form and complete your task”. It is learnt that śrī nandagōpar \[kriṣṇa’s father\] had heard this from vasudēvar when he had gone to śrī maturā. It is also learnt that this news had come through hearsay from śrī maturā.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that it appeared that darkness had come together and taken a form, called as pūtanā. Her locks appeared as if fire had decided to emit cruel flames. It is heard that kamsan had told her “If you go like this, you would not be able to kill him. Go with a deceptive form and carry out the task”.  This narrative came from vasudēvar to śrī nandagōpar; it could have come through hearsay from maturā; or else, this could have been directly told by emperumān to āḻvār when āḻvār saw him.

**manju …** – Oh, one who stood firmly in tiruveḷḷaṟai, where the mansions, studded completely with gemstones, reach the sky such that clouds could glide over them and which has fortified walls for protection!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as we climb the hills of tirumalai with a huge effort, clouds would climb atop the mansions in tiruveḷḷaṟai, which were studded with gemstones, just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 4.10.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/07/periya-thirumozhi-4-10-8/) “*padiyidai mādattu adiyidait tūṇil paditta pal maṇigaḷin oḷiyāl*” (from the lustre of gems which have been embellished in the pillars erected inside mansions on the earth). The mansions were that tall. These were protected by the fortified walls in tiruveḷḷaṟai. Oh, one who is standing firmly in such tiruveḷḷaṟai!

**anjuvan nī angu niṟka** – Having heard that “pūtanā came in search of you to harm you was not due to her own accord but due to kamsan’s imploring her”, I was afraid as to “Who else he would send further and what else he would do”. Hence, I was afraid that you were standing in the place which is full of danger.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār is afraid when kriṣṇa stands amidst those who see faults in the auspicious qualities of emperumān, in the same way when he would be afraid of pūtanā \[approaching kriṣṇa\].

**aḻaganē kāppida vārāy** – Oh, one who has beauty beyond this world! Do not stand there. You should come such that I could carry out *kāppu* for your beauty.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa’s beauty was similar to the one as mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 3.29 “*pumsām driśti citta apahāriṇam*” (śrī rāma stole the eyes and minds of people with his beauty) and as mentioned in śrīmad bhāgavatam 10.32.2 “*sākśān manmata manmata*:” (kiṣṇa’s beauty was such that he would bewilder the mind of manmatan who would bewilder the minds of all). Even after seeing such beauty, there are people who would find fault with him. Hence, āḻvār tells kriṣṇa to come so that he could perform *kāppu* as a remedy for the evil eyes of such people. Through the term *manju*, it is said that those who have noble thoughts in their minds and corresponding activities, come to tiruveḷḷaṟai, since this noble place is that famous. Through the term *maṇi*, the distinguished knowledge about emperumān’s *svarūpa rūpa guṇa vibhūti* (basic nature, divine form, auspicious qualities and wealth respectively) which is splendorous, is shown. It also shows the efforts taken to protect such a distinguished entity.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.8.7. Kallac cagadum

*kaḷḷac cagadum marudum kalakkaḻiya udai seydapiḷḷai arasē! nī pēyaip pidittu mulai uṇḍa pinnaiuḷḷavāṟu onṟum aṟiyēn ōliyudai veḷḷaṟai ninṟāy!paḷḷi koḷ pōdu idu āgum paramanē! kāppida vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

oḷi udai – having beauty; veḷḷaṟai – in tiruveḷḷaṟai; ninṟāy! – oh, one who is standing and showering your mercy!; paramanē! – oh, one who is the supreme entity!; kaḷḷam – deceitful; sagadum – śakatam (wheel); marudum – yamaḷārjuna (yamaḷam – twin, arjuna trees); kalakku aḻiya – such that the spokes of the wheel were broken; udai seyda – one who kicked; piḷḷai arasē! – oh, one who has the fame of crossing all boundaries in your acts of childishness!; nī – you; pēy mulaiyai – the fiend’s bosom; pidittu – holding by your hand; uṇḍa pinnai – after consuming; uḷḷa āṟu – the way things are; onṟum aṟiyēn – I do not know anything; idu – this time; paḷḷi koḷ pōdu āgum – is the time to recline; you should come for me to carry out kāppu for you

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who stands in tiruveḷḷaṟai, which is beautiful, and showers your mercy! Oh, one who is the supreme entity! Oh, one who has the eminence of crossing all limits in \[your\] child-like activities, who broke the wheel such that its spokes fell apart and who kicked the twin trees of yamaḷārjuna! After you had held the bosom of the fiend \[pūtanā\] and consumed her life, I do not know about the true state of anything. This is the time to go to bed. You should come such that I could carry out kāppu for you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that āḻvār found the words, which were heard of when kriṣṇa was born, to be true.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kaḷḷam …** – Even as you were sleeping, a wheel, in which a monster had pervaded, came to harm you. Even as you were crawling, two trees stood, in which monsters had pervaded, in order to harm you. Just as it has been said in periya tirumoḻi 8.6.8 “*kālāl sagadam pāyndān*” (he kicked the wheel with his divine feet) and in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.5.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/08/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-1-5-5/) “*ūru karattinodum undiya*” (pushing with his divine thighs and divine hands), you had kicked them with your divine feet, divine thighs and divine shoulders such that they fell down, their forms crumbling.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār calls kriṣṇa *piḷḷai arasē* since his childish activities are without any signs of withering. He says that he doesn’t know of kriṣṇa after he had annihilated inimical entities such as śakatan et al. In other words, since kriṣṇa is carrying out activities which are beyond his age, āḻvār is worried as to what will happen further. āḻvār says “Even though I know of your abilities of *aghaditaghatanā* \[capability to bind things which cannot be bound together\], I do not know of your true nature”. Through this, it is opined that āḻvār says “I do not know as to which is the reason for your existence – is it annihilation of enemies of your followers or is it granting the wishes of your followers?” It is to make this clear splendorously that you are standing in the most radiant tiruveḷḷaṟai and showering your grace.

**piḷḷai arasē** – Even as you carried out these activities which were beyond the reach of human beings, oh, one who has the eminence of having no shortcoming in your childishness!

**nī pēyaip pidittu mulai uṇḍa pinnai** – after you had caught hold of the fiend, thinking her to be your mother, and consumed her bosom \[milk\]…

**uḷḷa āṟu onṟum aṟiyēn** – I do not know of anything which is happening. In other words, I am frightened, thinking, if you indulge in similar activities “One day or the other, danger would certainly come”.

**oḷi udai …** – Oh, one who is standing in tiruveḷḷaṟai which has the beauty of mansions and fortified walls and showering your mercy!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa is the most eminent of all entities, standing in tiruveḷḷaṟai and showering his mercy.

**paḷḷi koḷ pōdu iduvāgum** – this is the time for you to go to sleep. Apart from being the time of dusk, time is passing quickly.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *paḷḷi koḷdal* \[going to sleep\] is to keep aside his responsibility in *leelārasam* \[the flavour of playing with samsāris\].

The pāsuram has to be read as *pēyaip pidittu uṇḍa piḷḷai arasē*! *oḷi udai veḷḷaṟai ninṟāy, kaḷḷac cagadum marudum kalakku aḻiya udai seyda pinnai, unnai uḷḷavāṟu onṟum aṟiyēn* to get the sequential meaning.

**paramanē kāppida vārāy** – Oh, one who is without anyone above you in terms of beauty etc! You should come such that I could carry out *kāppu* for you so that there is no danger for you.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.
