## 2.8.8. Inbam adanai

*inbam adanai uyarttāy! imaiyavarkkku enṟum ariyāy!kumbak kaḷiṟu atta kōvē!kodum kanjan nenjinil kūṟṟē!sembon madiḷ veḷḷaṟaiyāy! selvattināl vaḷar piḷḷāy!kambakkabāli kāṇ anguk kadidu ōdik kāppida vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

inbam adanai – joy; uyarttāy – oh, one who gave me in abundance!; imaiyavarkku – for celestial entities; enṟum – for ever; ariyāy! – oh, one who is difficult to know!; kumbam – having a pot-like structure on its forehead; kaḷiṟu – elephant, kuvalayāpeedam; atta – killed; kōvē! – oh, one who is like a king!; kodu – having a cruel heart; kanjan – kamsan’s; nenjinil – in the mind; kūṟṟē! – oh, one who creates fear, like yama!; sem pon madiḷ – having fortified walls, which are desirable like reddish gold; veḷḷaṟaiyāy! – oh, one who has tiruveḷḷaṟai as your residence!; selvattināl – with the pride of wealth; vaḷar – growing up; piḷḷāy! – oh, one who is a child!; kambam – one who creates trembling in \[the minds of\] beholders; kabāli kāṇ – you would see that durgai, who has skulls on her form, is roaming around; kāppu ida – such that I could carry out kāppu; kadidu – at once; ōdi vārāy – come fast

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who gives me joy in abundance! Oh, one who is difficult to know for the celestial entities! Oh, one who is like a king, who killed the elephant, kuvalayāpeedam, which had a pot-like structure on its forehead! Oh, one who creates fear, like yama, in the cruel mind of kamsan! Oh, one who is having tiruveḷḷaṟai, which has fortified walls which are desirous like reddish gold, as your residence! Oh, one who is like a child, growing with the pride of wealth! Do not stand in places where durgai, who has skulls on her form, making those who behold her to tremble in fear, roams around, which you would see! Come at once to me such that I could carry out kāppu for you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār says “Is it only pūtanā et al that you annihilated? Was it not you who effortlessly annihilated kuvalayāpeedam too?”*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**inbam adanai uyarttāy** – Oh, one who created abundant joy for me through experiencing the activities of your divine incarnation and auspicious qualities! Just as it has been mentioned in [perumāḷ tirumoḻi 7-8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/08/perumal-thirumozhi-7-8/) “*toḻugaiyum ivai kaṇḍa asōdai tollai inbattu iṟudi kaṇḍāḷ*” (yaśōdāp pirātti, who saw you performing anjali to her \[cupping the palms together in salutation\] saw the boundary of unbounded pleasures), she felt more and more joyful on seeing his activities.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa, more than the joy which comes out of his being the *puruśārtam* \[ultimate benefit\], showed his activities as a result of his incarnation as well as his auspicious qualities such as simplicity etc to āḻvār splendorously. As a result, kriṣṇa made āḻvār to carry out mangaḷāśāsanam for him.

**imaiyavarkku enṟum aṟiyāy** – Oh, one who is out of bounds for celestial entities who try to attain you through their knowledge and power! Through this, his eminence, as opposed to the simplicity mentioned in the previous verse, has been narrated.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that this simplicity, which emperumān showed when he incarnated here, is difficult to see even for nityasūris \[permanent dwellers of śrī vaikuṇṭam\]. Alternatively, emperumān does not manifest this simplicity to celestial entities here.

**kumbak kaḷiṟatta kōvē** – Just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 4.1.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2022/11/periya-thirumozhi-4-1-9/) “*kumba migu mada yānai*” (the elephant kuvalayāpeedam which was in rut, and which had a huge forehead), oh, one who is like a king, having effortlessly annihilated kuvalayāpeedam, which had a huge forehead, with your valour!

**kodum kanjan nenjinil kūṟṟē** – Oh, one who appears like yama \[the deity of death\], creating fear in the mind of kamsan, who was always cruel towards you!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the cruel mind of kamsan is kriṣṇa’s yama \[since he keeps thinking of ways to harm kriṣṇa, constantly\]. Oh, one who became a crueller yama for kamsan, by annihilating that thought itself from kamsan’s mind!

**sem pon madiḷ veḷḷaṟaiyāy** – Oh, one who has tiruveḷḷaṟai, which has fortified walls glittering like pure gold!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: oh, one who has the divine abode of tiruveḷḷaṟai, which is surrounded by fortified walls which are regarded highly by mangaḷāśāsanaparars, as your identity!

**selvattināl vaḷar piḷḷāy** – śrī rāma, the son of emperor daśarata, was always under the control of many persons \[such as sages bharatvāja, agastya et al, sugrīva et al), doing as per their wishes. Unlike that, oh, one who was outside anyone’s control, who did as you wished, who ate as you desired and grew up with the pride of wealth!

**kambak kabāli kān angu** – the place \[where you are standing\] is frequented by durgai, who has skull and axe on her form, creating trembling in the minds of those who behold her. Alternatively, *kabāli* would refer to rudra too.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that it is the time when one, who creates fear in the minds of even followers through his cruel form and having a skull on his hand, roams around. Do not stand there. Come at once here such that I could carry out *kāppu* for you.

**kadidu ōdik kāppida vārāy** – Do not stand in places where such lowly deities keep roaming. You should come at once, to me, such that I could carry out *kāppu* for you.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.8.9. Irukkodu nir

*irukkodu nīr sangil koṇḍittu eḻil maṟaiyōr vandu ninṟārtarukkēl nambi! sandhi ninṟu tāy solluk koḷḷāy sila nāḷtirukkāppu nān unnaic cāttat tēsudai veḷḷaṟai ninṟāyurukkāttum adi viḷakku inṟu oḷi koḷḷa ēṟṟugēn vārāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

tēsu udai – having radiance; veḷḷaṟai – in tiruveḷḷaṟai; ninṟāy! – oh, one who stands and showers your mercy!; nambī! – oh, one who is an expert in carrying out misciefs!; sila nāḷ – for a few days more; tāy sollu – words of mother; koḷḷāy – you should follow; irukkodu – along with riks (hymns) such as puruśa sūktam etc; nīr – pure water; sangil koṇḍittu – carrying in conch; eḻil – distinguished; maṟaiyōr – brāhmaṇas, who follow vēdams; vandu ninṟār – have come, in order to apply protection for you; sandhi ninṟu – standing at the intersection of four streets; tarukkēl – do not feel proud; nān – I, your mother; unnai – for you; tiruk kāppu sātta – for the sake of carrying out beautiful protection; uru – your divine form; kāttum – such that it is manifested; andi viḷakku – the tiruvandikkāppu; inṟu – now; oḷi koḷḷa – to have light; ēṟṟugēn – I lit; vārāy – you should come such that you could mercifully see it

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who is standing in tiruveḷḷaṟai and showering your mercy! Oh, one who is an expert in carrying out misciefs! For some more time to come, you should follow the words of your mother. Distinguished brāhmaṇas, who follow vēdams, have gathered in order to apply protection for you, carrying pure water in their conces, and reciting hymns such as puruśa sūktam. Do not feel proud, standing at the intersection of four streets. I have lit the lamp in order to apply beautiful kāppu for you, now, which will manifest your divine form. You should mercifully come in order to see it.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that despite āḻvār telling kriṣṇa “See, this is the time that kāpāli roams and makes people to tremble in fear”, kriṣṇa did not come to him. In this pāsuram, āḻvār tells kriṣṇa “The junction of four streets is crueler than that. Come to me. śrī rāma listened to the words of his mother, only after he had matured \[into a youth\]. ḍidn’t you \[kriṣṇa\], on the other hand, listen to your mother, on the day that you were born?”*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**irukku …** – Distinguished brāhmaṇas, carrying pure water in their conces, along with hymns such as puruśa sūktam, just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.2.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thiruvaimozhi-5-2-9-mevith-thozhudhu/) “*vēdap punida irukkai*” (distinguished hymns in \[rig\] vēdam such as puruśa sūktam, śrī nārāyaṇa anuvākam etc which are purifying), have come in order to perform protection for you. We should carry out protection, with them. Your father too would do that. You should come. Without listening to her words, kriṣṇa, with pride, went to the junction of four streets in order to play with his friends.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the eminent brāhmaṇas, who are knowledgeable about *vēdāntam* \[that part of vēdam which deals with engaging with *brahmam*, the supreme entity\], have come with pure water in their conces and hymns in order to carry out *rakśai* \[same as *kāppu*, offering protection\] for you. Had your father been here, he would have welcomed them with distinction, offered them cows etc as gift and would have made them carry out *rakśai*. You should come such that they could carry out *rakśai*. This verse says that instead of listening to these words, kriṣṇa ran away, with pride. This also conveys the meaning that kriṣṇa gave response to yaśōdāp pirātti’s pleading and ran out. What was kriṣṇa’s response to yaśōdāp pirātti’s pleading? He said words such as “They have come for their own benefit. Did they come here for carry out something for me?”  “They have come to get some cows after carrying out protection for father. Have they not come for fulfilling their desires which would enable them to be protected?” cakravartit tirumagan \[śrī rāma, the son of emperor daśarata\], with auspicious qualities, would visit eminent people, paying them his obeisance. He would receive their *rakśai* and feel that he has been protected. kriṣṇa is unlike that śrī rāma.

**tarukkēl nambi sandhi ninṟu** – Oh, one who is complete with your misciefs! Do not stand, with pride, at the junction of four streets, where lowly deities roam. Even if those brāhmaṇas have not come for carrying out protection for you, do not stand in that place, come here.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *nambi* refers to kriṣṇa being complete with his responses, with pride. It also indicates that kriṣṇa was not interested in that *rakśai*.

**tāy solluk koḷḷāy sila nāḷ**– You should listen to the words of your mother, for some more time.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when yaśōdāp pirātti tells him that he should listen to mother’s words for some more time, kriṣṇa tells her “Are you compelling and calling me to come to you, only to do as you had done earlier \[as seen in the previous *tirumoḻis*\]?”

**tirukkāppu nān unnaic cātta** – In order for me to carry out beautiful protection for you

**tēsudai veḷḷaṟai ninṟāy** – Oh, one who is standing and showering your mercy at tiruveḷḷaṟai which has gained radiance due to distinguished people living there!

**urukkāttum andi viḷakku** – the *tiruvandikkāppu* (protection offered by driving way evil forces, through lighting camphor etc, during the time of dusk) will reveal your divine form. Looking at the divine form \[of emperumān\], which grants abundant enjoyment, is *puruśārtam* \[ultimate benefit\]. Those who carryout *tiruvandikkāppu* light the material only for this. Hence, the pāsuram says *urukkāttum* (revealing the divine form).

**inṟu oḷi koḷḷa ēṟṟugēn vārāy** – I have lit it, such that it is splendorous. You should come at once, in order to see this and shower your mercy. The pāsuram should be read as *tirukkāppu nān unnaic cātta – urukkāttum andi viḷaukku inṟu oḷi koḷḷa ēṟṟugēn vārāy* in order to get the sequential meaning.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa’s radiance is much higher than that of gemstones.

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.8.10. Podamar selvam

*pōdamar selvak koḻundu puṇar tiruveḷḷaṟaiyānaimādarkku uyarnda asōdai magan tannaik kāppitta māṟṟamvēdap payan koḷḷavalla vittu cittan sonna mālaipādap payan koḷḷa valla pattaruḷḷār vinai pōmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mādarkku – among all the women; uyarnda – one who is the most eminent; asōdai – yaśōdāp pirātti; pōdu – on a reddish lotus flower (pōdu – flower); amar – one who is fitting well; selvam – having the divine name śrī (deity for all the wealth); koḻundu – along with the primary consort, periya pirāttiyār; puṇar – one who is united for ever; tiruveḷḷaṟaiyānai – one who is standing in tiruveḷḷaṟai; magan tannai – regarding kriṣṇa, her son; kāppu itta māṟṟam – the pāsurams in which she had carried out rakśai \[protection\]; vēdam – vēdam’s; payan – true meaning; koḷḷa valla – one who is an expert in knowing; vittu cittan – periyāḻvār; sonna – mercifully composed; mālai – this tirumoḻi, which is a garland of words; pādam – mentioned in the last line of every pāsuram; payan – benefit \[viz. carrying out of kāppu mentioned in the fourth line of every pāsuram\]; koḷḷa valla – capable of absorbing; pattar uḷḷār – those who are with devotion; vinai – sins, which are hurdles for carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam; pōmē – will disappear, on their own

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa, who is the son of yaśōdāp pirātti, is standing in tiruveḷḷaṟai, being together always with periya pirāttiyār, who is known by the divine name śrī and who is fitting well on a reddish lotus flower. yaśōdāp pirātti, who is the most eminent among all women, carried out kāppu, for that kriṣṇa. periyāḻvār, who is capable of absorbing the true meanings of vēdams, mercifully composed pāsurams \[based on such yaśōdāp pirātti’s words\] with garland of words in this tirumoḻi. For those devotees, who are capable of absorbing the benefit mentioned in the fourth line of each of these pāsurams, sins, which are a hurdle for carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam for emperumān, would disappear on their own.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In this last pāsuram of the decad, āḻvār mentions the benefit which will accrue to one who learns it and brings it to completion.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**pōdamar selvak koḻundu** – periya pirāttiyār has lotus flower as her place of birth. Since she is known as *śrī*, she is the deity of all the wealth; she is also, the primary consort of emperumān. She is known by the name *pangayac celvi* \[name of the presiding deity in tiruveḷḷaṟai\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that periya pirāttiyār has such wealth that she has lotus flower as her dwelling place. It would appear that the fragrance from the flower has taken a form as her tenderness. Just as emperumān is the *sarva ganda*: *sarva rasa*: for her \[he is the repository of all the fragrances and all the tastes\], she is the same for him too. It is because emperumān has her as his wealth that he has the wealth of being the most supreme of all entities. Such a tender entity \[periya pirāttiyār\] took root in his divine chest. It was only after knowing the power of that chest that she let go of her place of birth. Hereafter, she would think of her place of birth only when sītāp pirātti would think of śrī mitilā \[after she had come along with śrī rāma to ayōdyā\] \[which means, that she will never think of her place of birth and would dwell only on the divine chest of emperumān forever\]. emperumān at tiruveḷḷaṟai is the supporting pole for this *koḻundu* (*koḻundu* refers to being the consort, *talaivi*). It was to denote her prominence that the place is called *tiruveḷḷaṟai* \[tiru refers to pirātti, she is mentioned first while referring to the place\].

**puṇar tiruveḷḷaṟaiyānai** – though born in lotus flower, periya pirāttiyār resides permanently in the divine chest of emperumān, just as it has been said in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/thiruvaimozhi-6-10-10-agalagillen-part-5/) “*agalagillēn iṟaiyum enṟu*” (saying that she will not separate from emperumān, even for a moment). emperumān resides in tiruveḷḷaṟai, united with such pirātti. Just as it has been mentioned in [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 27](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/10/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-27/) “*kōl tēdi ōdum kaḻundu adu*” (creeper going in search of a supporting pole), like a creeper which cannot sustain itself without leaning on a pole, pirāttiyār, who was born in a lotus flower and who is the deity of wealth, cannot sustain herself without leaning on emperumān in tiruveḷḷaṟai. Just as the pole stands as the support, with the creeper which spreads on it being the primary entity, in tiruveḷḷaṟai, pirāttiyār is the primary entity and *sendāmarakikkaṇṇan* \[puṇḍarīkākśan, the divine name of emperumān in tiruveḷḷaṟai\] is not prominent in that place.

**mādarkku uyarnda asōdai** – Just as it has been mentioned in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2.2.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/10/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-2-2-6/) “*enna nōnbu nōṟṟāḷkolō ivanaip peṟṟa vayiṟu udaiyāḷ*” (what penance did the one, who gave birth to kriṣṇa, carry out?) and in [perumāḷ tirumoḻi 7.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/08/perumal-thirumozhi-7-5/) “*ellām deyva nangai yasōdai peṟṟāḷ*” (It was yaśōdāp pirātti, who is like a celestial lady, who was fortunate to witness all the divine activities of kriṣṇa), it was yaśōdāp pirātti who had kriṣṇa as her son and who enjoyed all his activities starting with his childish ones. Thus, she is the most eminent among all the women in the world.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *mādu* refers to the prominence gained in the youthful state of that age. The eminence for women is on account of being the beloved of their respective spouse and being under their control \[and as a result, controlling the respective spouse\]. For yaśōdāp pirātti, the eminence comes on account of her higher affection towards kriṣṇa than towards śrī nandagōpar. It is due to this that she came under nandagōpar’s control. Just as it has been mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 12.68 “*yadā yadā hi kausalyā*” (kausalyāp pirātti was all entities for emperor daśarata, as a maid-servant, as a friend, as a wife et al), yaśōdāp pirātti was for nandagōpar. Since kriṣṇa is referred to as *asōdai magan* \[son of yaśōdāp pirātti\], śrī nandagōpar was similar to śrī vasudēvar \[a namesake parent\]. Only if she reiterates that kriṣṇa is her son would he be referred to as son of nandagōpar.

**magan tannaik kāppitta māṟṟam** – the pāsurams in which she carried out *rakśai* \[protection from evil eyes\] for her son kriṣṇa, manifesting all her affection towards him as her son; kriṣṇa’s *rūpa guṇa cēśtitam* \[divine form, auspicious qualities and divine activities\] were such that one has to keep carrying out *rakśai* for him all the time.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti called kriṣṇa many times in this tirumoḻi and praised him, revealing her affection towards him. *māṟṟam* – words \[pāsuram\]

**vēdap payan …** – periyāḻvār knew that the true meaning of vēdam is only to carry out mangaḷāśāsanam for emperumān. In this tirumoḻi, which is like a garland of words, he has mercifully mentioned this.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that those who gain the benefit of vēdam will be like periyāḻvār. Benefit \[of vēdam\] is mangaḷāśāsanam.

**pādap payan …** – followers of emperumān have total devotion towards him and are capable of knowing the benefit which has been mentioned in the last line of every pāsuram in this tirumoḻi. The sins of such followers, which are hurdles for their carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam \[the benefit mentioned in the last line of each pāsuram\] will disappear on their own.

We shall next consider the pravēsam of the next tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.9.1. Venney vilungi

*veṇṇey viḻungi veṟum kalattai veṟpidai ittu adan ōsai kētkumkaṇṇapirān kaṟṟa kalvi tannaik kākka killōm un maganaik kāvāypuṇṇil puḷippu eydāl okkum tīmai purai puraiyāl ivai seyya vallaaṇṇaṟku aṇṇānōr maganaip peṟṟa asōdai nangāy! un maganaik kūvāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

puṇ – in a wound; puḷi – tamarind (paste of tamarind); peydāl okkum – just as it irritates when applied; tīmai – intolerable misciefs; purai purai – in every house; seyya valla – being an expert in carrying out; aṇṇaṟku – for elder brother, balarāma; aṇṇān – one who is opposed to, in his activities (aṇṇān – one who is far away); ōr – being unique; maganai – son; peṟṟa – as one who gave birth to; nangai – one who is complete; asōdāy – oh, yaśōdāp pirātti!; veṇṇey – butter, which has been kept safely in pots; viḻungi – swallowing, through stealing, without leaving any residue; veṟum kalattai – vessel, which contained the butter; veṟpidai ittu – breaking it, by hitting it against stone; adan – during the time when it breaks; ōsai – sound; kētkum – one who listened; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa; pirān – benefactor (this is a word uttered in disgust; it is to be taken as one who gives troubles); kaṟṟa – learnt; kalvi tannai – art of making misciefs; kākka killōm – we are powerless to protect ourselves; un maganai – your son; kāvāy – you protect; un maganai – your son, who is roaming around, creating misciefs; kūvāy – call him

**Перевод:**

**After swallowing butter, kriṣṇa would relish the sound of the empty container which he hit against stone. We are unable to protect ourselves from the mischievous deeds carried out by kriṣṇa. You should keep your son, with you. Oh, yaśōdāp pirātti who is complete with all qualities! Your son is carrying out misciefs in every house, similar to pouring tamarind paste on a wound. Call your son, who you gave birth to and who is totally different from his elder brother.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) Some of the women in tiruvāyppādi (śrī gōkulam) come and complain to yaśōdāp pirātti, mother of kriṣṇa, about the misciefs which he has carried out in their houses during the previous night and request her to call him to her house. This pāsuram reflects this. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that yaśōdāp pirātti had thought that kriṣṇa was asleep. However, he had gone into the village and carried out misciefs in the night. Some people came on the next day morning and complained many times to yaśōdāp pirātti about his misciefs. āḻvār recalls those events in this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**veṇṇey viḻungi** – kriṣṇa, through stealing, swallows butter which has been prepared by churning \[curd\], without leaving behind anything. Is it only this much?

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa had swallowed butter which had been kept freshly in many containers, in each house. The people in those houses wanted to bring him with butter both in his mouth and hands and show him to yaśōdāp pirātti.

**veṟum kalattai veṟpidai ittu** – He breaks the container, in which the butter had been stored, by smashing it against stone. When yaśōdāp pirātti asks them in amazement “He had swallowed butter. But, why should he break the container? What benefit will he derive out of that?” They respond, saying …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says additionally that he broke the containers in order to distract them such that they would not follow him and bring him with butter in his mouth and hands.

**adan ōsai kētkum** – “The benefit which accrues to him out of this activity is that he hears the sound of the container being broken”. yaśōdāp pirātti tells them “If that were the case, lock your houses such that he cannot enter them”. They tell her …

**kaṇṇapirān kaṟṟa kalvi tannai kākka killōm** – “We are unable to protect ourselves from the mischievous activities learnt by kriṣṇa, who is the benefactor. We could protect ourselves from the misciefs of others, but not from kriṣṇa. The term *pirān* \[benefactor\] has been used with a negative connotation. It refers to one who steals everything and everyone. yaśōdāp pirātti tells them “If you could not protect your respective house, who will?” They say …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that upon hearing the complaints made by the women to yaśōdāp pirātti, kriṣṇa came there rubbing his eyes \[as he had been sleeping deeply\] and told yaśōdāp pirātti “They are telling lies”. When someone had said previously that butter is getting stolen in tiruvāyppādi, he had made a tantrum saying “They are blaming only me”

**un maganaik kāvāy** – “If you could keep your son safely, everyone’s property would get saved. Please do that”. yaśōdāp pirātti tells them “Would not little children indulge in misciefs? If he had done something unknowingly, śouldn’t you people put up with those activities? Could you blame him like this?” to which they respond …

**puṇṇil puḷippeydāl okkum tīmai** – Just as a wound on which, if a tangy material is poured, it will burn, when he carries out misciefs which cannot be tolerated by us, how could we put up with those? When yaśōdāp pirātti tells them “Are you people living in the same house? It is not possible for him to carry out such misciefs which you mention, in each of your houses”. They tell her “It is not only in our houses”

**purai puraiyāl ivai seyya valla** – He is capable of carrying out these misciefs in every house, you see. *purai* – house; repetition of this word \[*purai purai*\] is to emphasise that it is in every house; *Al* \[as in *purai puraiyāl*\] is for poetic measure. It does not have a meaning.

**aṇṇal kaṇṇān** – The term *aṇṇal* refers to being the lord. *aṇṇal kaṇṇān* refers to one having eyes which hint that he is the lord. Through this: the term lord here conveys the meaning that he is the lord of those carrying out misciefs. One who has eyes, highlighting this lordship. Alternatively, the term *aṇṇal* would refer to elder brother. The term *aṇṇān* refers to one who is totally distanced from that person \[one who is the opposite of the person\]. Just as it has been mentioned in periya tirumoḻi 10.7.4 “*than nambi nambiyum ingu vaḷarndadu avan ivai seydadu aṟiyān*” (balarāman \[elder brother of kriṣṇa\], too lived in tiruvāyppādi. However, he did not indulge in the misciefs which kriṣṇa was indulging in), kriṣṇa was one who had nothing congruent with balarāman, his elder brother and a quiet person.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa doesn’t come under his elder brother, balarāman’s, control too. He is uncontrollable.

**immaganaip peṟṟa asōdai nangāy** – Oh, one who has the completeness of having given birth to a son like kriṣṇa, who is unique!

**un maganaik kūvāy** – Instead of roaming around, carrying out misciefs like this, please ensure to keep kriṣṇa with you.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that even as these women were complaining to yaśōdāp pirātti, some more women came there, saying “Look at the misciefs which he is carrying out in our houses”.

Through this, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that the term butter refers to *mumukśus* \[those who are interested in attaining mōkśam, liberation from samsāram\], and the term containers refers to those who are not interested in mōkśam. Through his *sankalapam* \[pledge\], kriṣṇa destroys them by pushing them in samsāram repeatedly. This meaning is brought out in this pāsuram.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.9.2. Varuga varuga

*varuga varuga varuga ingē vāmana nambī! varuga ingēkariya kuḻal seyya vāy mugattuk kāgutta nambī! varuga ingēariyan ivan enakku inṟu nangāy! anjana vaṇṇā! asalagattārparibavam pēsat tarikka killēn pāviyunēkku ingē pōdarāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāmanan – as a dwarfish bachelor; nambī – oh, one who desired and became complete!; ingē – (leaving that place) to this place; varuga varuga varuga – come immediately; kariya kuḻal – having dark, divine locks; seyya vāy – along with reddish, divine lips; mugam – and a divine face; kāgutta – oh, one who makes the clan of emperor kakutsta to be splendorous!; ingē varuga – mercifully come here; nangāy – oh, one who is complete (in finding fault with me, by saying “You are calling your son; ivan – this child; enakku – for me; inṟu – now; ariyan – difficult to catch; anjanam – like black pigment; vaṇṇā – oh, one who has a divine complexion!; asal agattār – women from neighbourhood; paribavam pēsa – to talk ill of you, such as “He is a thief; he is a mischief monger”; tarikka killēn – I cannot tolerate; pāviyēnukku – for me, who has committed sins such that I have to listen to the despicable words of people in the neighbourhood about you; ingē pōdarāy – come here, to rid me of my worries

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who incarnated as vāmana, who is complete with qualities, you should come here. Oh, one who incarnated as śrī rāma, with all auspicious qualities, with dark locks and reddish mouth on the divine face! \[Speaking to the women who had come to complain about kriṣṇa\] Oh, one who is with all noble qualities! He is very dear to me. \[Turning to kriṣṇa\] Oh, kriṣṇa, who has a dark, divine form! I cannot tolerate the despicable words of people from other houses, spoken about you. Please come to me, who has the misfortune of hearing such words.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) After the women said \[as seen in the previous pāsuram\] regarding kriṣṇa’s misciefs, this pāsuram mentions the words spoken by yaśōdāp pirātti to her son. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that yaśōdāp pirātti is calling out to her son, being unable to tolerate when some more people came to complain to her.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**varuga varuga varuga ingē** – yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa to come to her, instead of remaining in other places, carrying out misciefs and hearing the scornful words of others. v*aruga* – come. Repeating it a few times over is to tell him forcefully to come at once.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti is calling out to him several times since he did not come when she called out to him once. She tells him that it is a disgrace for him, for her, for his father, for the entire village, while inimical entities such as kamsan and śiśupālan will rejoice. Hence, until kriṣṇa returns, yaśōdāp pirātti keeps telling him *varuga varuga varuga* …

**vāmana nambī varuga ingē** – Since he is *vāmana nambī*, one who has the completeness of auspicious qualities due to which he had protected his followers, she tells him to come to her. Since he did not come, despite saying these words …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that since kriṣṇa did not come to her despite her repeatedly telling him to come, she tells him “āren’t you one with completeness of auspicious qualities? You should listen to the words of your mother. Is it not said that one who does not listen to his mother will not be considered as a good person by people in that place? Hence, you should come”. Since he did not come to her commands, she is praising him to make him come to her.

**kariya …**– Oh, one who has dark, divine locks and reddish, divine lips, with a beautiful divine face in between these two, without any simile, and who has completeness of auspicious qualities with which you carried out the words of your mother and father! You should come here. When one of the women, who had come there to complain about kriṣṇa, told her, just as it has been mentioned in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 3.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/07/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-3-9/) “*anja urappāḷ aśōdai*” (yaśōdāp pirātti will not scold you, lest you get frightened), “Instead of ordering him to do what you say, since you allowed him to do as he liked, he is indulging in such misciefs. Even now, instead of controlling him, you are praising him to make him come to you” …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when yaśōdāp pirātti called out to him as *vāmana nambī*, kriṣṇa came a bit nearer. She looked at him from his divine foot to his divine crown. After looking at his dark, divine locks and reddish, divine lips, she forgot her position of controlling him, embraced him, feeling joyous “āren’t you the one who listened to your mother \[as śrī rāma\]?” She then looks at the women who had come to complain about him to her, and tells them despicably “Is it this person who you are calling as mischief-monger?”

**ariyan ivan enakku inṟu nangāy** – Oh, one who has the completeness of having given birth to a son and nurturing him! īsn’t he a rare person for me to get now? I will not control such a person harshly. After responding to the lady who spoke to her, yaśōdāp pirātti returns to her son, unable to tolerate the scornful words of the persons who had come to complain to her, and tells him to come to her, after telling him about her worries.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti tells the women “Just as your sons are rare to you all, kriṣṇa is a rare person for me to get”. She looks at them, who have gathered to complain now, while they used to carry kriṣṇa and feel joyous earlier, when he was an infant, and tells them “I am unable to tolerate this”. She looks at one person among those women, who has completeness of qualities and tells her the anguish that she has. She then catches kriṣṇa and takes him with her to go inside the house.

**anjana vaṇṇā** – Oh, one who has a dark, divine complexion, which is invigorating to beholders!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa’s divine complexion was such that she became blind due to her affection towards him. Through this pāsuram, the repeatedly beckoning term *varuga varuga* mentions about the dependence on followers. Where did this dependence manifest? This was brought out by āḻvār through the term *vāmana nambi* where, for the sake of his follower, indra, emperumān took on the garb of *vāmana* \[dwarf\] and went to mahābali, who was not his follower \[then\]. Similarly, through the term *kāgutta nambi*, āḻvār says that emperumān went out of his kingdom, using his mother’s words as a pretext, but truly for the sake of celestial entities and sages \[in the forests\], to the battlefield arena of rāvaṇa, an inimical entity, with the companionship of his bow and arrows and conquered rāvaṇa. The term *asalagam* \[as in *asalagattār*\], refers to those who wish to attain emperumān through other means \[and not through emperumān\]. The words of such people would certainly appear unfavourable to āḻvār, who is mangaḷāśāsanaparar. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai narrates an incident involving piḷḷai uṟangāvilli dāsar, one of rāmānuja’s disciples. Unable to tolerate the complaints of these women, he would ask, in a child-like manner “Which lock did kriṣṇa break? Which expensive material did he usurp? They are complaining only about him. He has all the entities for milking as well as churning in his house. Without differentiating between his house and other’s houses, and, without knowing the effect of his actions, he had entered someone else’s house. Why are they crying out that he stole milk, he stole butter?

**asalagattār paribavam pēsat tarikka killēn**– I am unable to tolerate scornful words such as “Deceitful person, mischievous person” which they say about you.

**pāviyēnukku ingē pōdarāyē** – I have to hear such despicable words, since I have committed sins. You should come here so that I could overcome my grief.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.9.3. Tiruvudaip pillaidan

*tiruvudaip piḷḷaidān tīyavāṟu tēkkam onṟum ilan tēsudaiyanuruga vaitta kudattodu veṇṇey uṟicci udaittittup pōndu ninṟānarugirundār tammai aniyāyam seyvadudān vaḻakkō asōdāy!varuga enṟu un magan tannaik kūvāy vāḻa ottān madusūdananē*

**Пословный перевод:**

asōdāy – oh, yaśōdāp pirātti!; tiru udai – without any shortcoming in opulence; piḷḷai – kaṇṇan, your son; tān – himself; tīya āru – in the modes of carrying out mischief; onṟum – even a little bit; tēkkam ilan – without any hesitation; tēsu udaiyan – he has that \[mischief-mongering\] as his radiance; uruga vaitta – kept for melting; veṇṇey – butter; kudattōdu – along with the container; uṟicci – sucking out; udaittittu – breaking the container too; pōndu – coming here; ninṟān – he stood; madusūdanan – one who had earlier annihilated the inimical entity, madu; vāḻa ottān – remaining now as the enemy himself, he is not allowing us to have our livelihood; arugu – in the neighbourhood; irundār tammai – we, who live; aniyāyam seyvadu – carrying out your wish, through your son; vaḻakkōdān – is it proper?; un magan tannai – kaṇṇan, your son; varuga varuga enṟu kūvāy – call him out “Come near me”

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa is wealthy, as a result of which there is no hurdle in his indulging in misciefs, He has radiance due to his mischief-mongering. He sucked out all the butter which we had kept in pots for melting and broke the pots too. Oh, yaśōdā! Is it correct to do injustice to those who live near you? Call your son to come near you. madusūdanan \[kriṣṇa\] will not allow us to earn our livelihood.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) Apart from the people who had complained earlier, some more people came to yaśōdāp pirātti and told her “Is it correct to do injustice to those who are near you? Please call your son and keep him with you”. This pāsuram mentions this incident. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that yaśōdāp pirātti had thought that kriṣṇa had gone into the house when she told him \[as in the previous pāsuram\] “pāviyēnukku ingē pōdarāyē”. She was not aware of the misciefs that he was indulging, in the village. Some other people came and complained to her.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tiruvudaip piḷḷai** – A wealthy boy; this hints that there is no shortage of wealth for him. Through this it is mentioned that he is not indulging in stealing and eating butter because there is shortage of butter in his house and that he could only eat butter from others’ places. He is indulging in misciefs due to the pride of his wealth.

**tān tīyavāṟu tēkkam onṟum ilan** – Looking at his birth \[born to the chief of that place\] and wealth \[his father is the richest in that place\], he does not hesitate when he sets out to indulge in misciefs, thinking “Why are we doing this?” He will indulge in all sorts of misciefs, without any hurdle.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that there is no limit to the misciefs which he indulges in, when looking at his activities. He was such that he was cited as an example for referring to people who were indulging in misciefs. *tēkkam* – hurdle.

**tēsu udaiyan** – Is it only that he does not have any hesitation? He will think that it is only when he indulges in carrying out misciefs that he gains a radiance. This infers that he does not fear the ridicule of others. When yaśōdāp pirātti asks them as to what kriṣṇa had done for them to say all these, they mention one among the many misciefs which he has done.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that apart from not fearing when someone tries to control kriṣṇa \[from indulging in misciefs\], he would recall the mischievous activities which he had carried out, think that those activities give him a radiance, consider that as a wealth and indulge in further mischievous activities.

**uruga …** – We had kept butter in pots, for melting \[into ghee\]. He tilted the vessels, ate up all the butter, broke the pots and is standing here as if he had not done any of these.

**arugu …** – Oh, yaśōdā! Is it correct on your part to carry out what you want, through your son, on us, who are living close to you?

**varuga enṟu un magan tannaik kūvāy** – Call your son so that he comes to you and keep him with you, instead of coming to our places and indulging in further misciefs.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when he heard the people complaining about him, kriṣṇa started running away from that place. Looking at the way in which he was running, those who came to complain about him, started running behind him, saying “He will not allow us to earn our livelihood”, fearing that he was going to enter their houses again in order to eat the remaining butter too, there.

**vāḻa ottān madusūdananē** – If you do not do this, he will not allow us to live in this place and earn our livelihood. Usage of the term *madusūdanan* hints that while earlier he \[kriṣṇa\] was removing enemies of his followers, now he has become inimical through his nature, and is harming his followers.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says at the end that “Stealing” became radiance for emperumān. When thieves, in the world, take umbrage when being called as “Thief”, kriṣṇa was focused on “Stealing”, taking over the name of “Thief”. This appeared acceptable to him and became his radiance. Since the pāsuram says that he recognized butter as an enjoyment and broke the vessel which contained that butter, it is clear that he is the *mōkśapradan* \[one who grants complete liberation\], which is the ultimate removal of bondage with samsāram for a jīvātmā. Through the term *tēkkam onṟum ilan,* it is clear that he cannot be controlled by anyone.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.9.4. Kondal vanna

*koṇḍal vaṇṇā! ingē pōdarāyē kōyil piḷḷāy! ingē pōdarāyēteṇḍirai sūḻ tiruppērk kidanda tirunāraṇā! ingē pōdarāyēuṇḍu vandēn ammam enṟu solli ōdi agam puga āycci tānumkaṇḍedirē senṟeduttuk koḷḷak kaṇṇa pirān kaṟṟa kalvi tānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

koṇḍal – like a monsoon cloud; vaṇṇā – oh, one who has a form!; ingē pōdarāy – come here; kōyil – residing in the śrīrangam huge temple; piḷḷāy – oh, one who is like a son!; ingē pōdarāy – come here; teḷ – clear; tirai – having waves; sūḻ – surrounded by; tiruppēr – in tiruppēr nagar \[a divine abode\]; kidanda – one who is reclining; tiru nāraṇā – oh, śrīman nārāyaṇa!; ingē pōdarāy – come here, to have food; ammam uṇḍu vandēn – “See, I have eaten food”; enṟu solli – saying like this; ōdi – running quickly; agam puga – as he entered the house; āycci tānum – yaśōdāp pirātti, his mother, too; kaṇḍu – looking at his arrival; edirē senṟu – going towards him; eduttuk koḷḷa – to make her carry him on her waist; kaṇṇa pirān – kaṇṇan; kaṟṟa – learnt; kalvidān – āḻvār rejoices, saying “How his tactics are!”

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who has the complexion of clouds! Come here. Oh, one who is reclining in śrī rangam temple! Come here. Oh, tirunārāyaṇa, who is reclining in tiruppērnagar, which is surrounded by clear waters with waves! Come here. When kriṣṇa ran into the house, saying that he has already eaten, yaśōdāp pirātti went towards him and held him in her arms. What an amazing activity has kriṣṇa done!**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) When the women told yaśōdāp pirātti “Call out for your son to come to you”, yaśōdāp pirātti praised kriṣṇa and asked him to come to her. When kriṣṇa ran into the house with affection, she took him in her arms. This pāsuram describes that. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that since yaśōdāp pirātti was told to call her son, she said “Come here”*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**koṇḍal …**– Oh, one who has the form which is like a monsoon cloud, full with water! You should come here, from there, to have your food. The meaning of the term *pōdarāy* is “come”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti is telling kriṣṇa “Oh, one who has a divine form which is like a monsoon cloud, filled with water!”

**kōyil piḷḷāy ingē pōdarāyē** – Just as it has been mentioned in amalanādipirān 10 “*koṇḍal vaṇṇan* – *kōvalanāy veṇṇey uṇḍa vāyan*” (One who has the complexion of a dark cloud, and a divine mouth with which he has eaten butter, as a herd-person; this pāsuram was sung on periya perumāḷ, reclining in śrī rangam), oh, one who is reclining in śrīrangam temple! You should come here.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti is telling kriṣṇa “Oh, one who is the complete controller, who does not have anyone to control you! Come here”. Instead of considering this way, it is more apt to consider that she is recalling the perumāḷ who is reclining in śrī rangam \[in our sampradāyam, the term *kōyil* refers to śrī rangam\] and is praising kriṣṇa as the one who is reclining in śrī rangam. He further refers to [tiruviruttam pāsuram 33](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/01/thiruviruththam-33/) “*aravaṇaiyīr* – *sengōl nadāvudir*” (Oh, one who is reclining on ādiśēśan as the mattress! You should rule from here with your sceptre) and says that when reference is taken to emperumān’s sceptre, his supremacy is clearly manifested in śrī rangam.

**teṇḍirai …** – Oh, śrīman nārāyaṇa, who is reclining in tiruppēr which is surrounded by rivers which have clear water, with waves! You should come here to have food.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai adds here that referring to kriṣṇa as śrīman nārāyaṇa brings out the first sentence of *dvaya mahāmantram* \[second among the three esoteric mantrams in our sampradāyam\].

**uṇḍu …** – When yaśōdāp pirātti called out to him like this, kriṣṇa came near her and said “See, I have consumed my food”. He ran inside the house. She too, feeling affectionate, looking at him coming towards her and the smile on his face, went towards him and took him in her arms. āḻvār feels joyous saying “What all does kaṇṇapirān do!” \[When people complained to yaśōdāp pirātti about kriṣṇa’s mischievous activities, asking her to control him, kriṣṇa had made her to forget all those and to take him in her arms. āḻvār is amazed with the turn of events\]. An alternative explanation – The term “*āycci tānum kaṇḍu edirē senṟu eduttuk koḷḷa*” could be construed as yaśōdāp pirātti referring to herself in the third person \[talking about herself\], asking kriṣṇa to come and have food. After coming near her, instead of saying “I will have food” or “I do not want food”, kriṣṇa said “I have eaten food” and ran inside the house. Feeling amazed with the way that he told her and the way that he ran into the house, yaśōdāp pirātti, who is his mother, forgot about his mischievous activities and took him in her arms. Thinking about all these, yaśōdāp pirātti appreciates his actions within herself, thinking “How one learns all these! How did he learn these, at his age!” When this explanation is considered, both the first part of the pāsuram and the second part could be considered as having been spoken by yaśōdāp pirātti herself \[instead of considering the first part as having been spoken by yaśōdāp pirātti and the second part by someone else \[āḻvār\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when kriṣṇa came inside the house, saying “I have eaten food”, yaśōdāp pirātti, who had called out to him to come for having food, forgot about his food, seeing the delight on his face and felt joyous herself. āḻvār celebrates the tactics employed by kriṣṇa in making her change her stance, exclaiming “What a way in which he has convinced her!”

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.9.5. Palaik karandu

*pālaik kaṟandu aduppēṟa vaittup pal vaḷaiyāḷ en magaḷ iruppamēlai agattē neruppu vēṇḍic cenṟu iṟaip poḻudu angē pēsi ninṟēnsāḷakkirāmam udaiya nambi sāyttup parugittup pōndu ninṟānālaik karumbin moḻi anaiya asōdai nangāy! un maganaik kūvāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

ālai – apt to be put in the mill; karumbu anaiya – matching sugar cane; in – sweet; moḻi – one who has speech; asōdai nangāy! – Oh, yaśōdāp pirātti who has completeness of femininity!; pal vaḷaiyāḷ – donning many bangles; en magaḷ – my daughter; pālaik kaṟandu – milking cow’s milk; aduppu – on top of the fire-place; ēṟa vaittu – keeping in a large pot; iruppa – as she stood as guard; mēlai agattu – in a house to the western side of your house; neruppu vēṇḍic cenṟu – to get fire \[to set fire to that fire-place\] to heat this milk; iṟaip poḻudu – for a moment; angē – in that house; pēsi ninṟēn – I was conversing; sāḷakkirāmam – śrī śāḷagrāmam; udaiya – having as his residence; nambi – one, who is without any shortcoming; sāyttu – tilting that vessel; parugittu – drinking the milk inside \[that vessel\]; pōndu ninṟān – came here, from that place; un maganai – kaṇṇan, your son; kūvāy – call out to him, to have him near you

**Перевод:**

**Oh, yaśōdāp pirātti who has words which are as sweet as the sugarcane which is apt to be fed into a mill \[for making sugar\]! My daughter, who wears many bangles, had milked the cow, kept that milk inside a pot, which she set on fire-place and stood guard over that milk. I went to the house, which is to the western side of your house, seeking fire, in order to set fire to that fire-place. I stood in that house, for a moment, speaking to the people there. Meanwhile, kriṣṇa, who has śāḷagrāmam as his residence, and who is without any shortcoming, tilted the vessel, which contained milk, drank the entire milk and stood here, getting out of my place. To ensure that he does not carry out further mischief in my house, call out to your son and keep him by your side.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) After entering the house and making yaśōdāp pirātti happy, kriṣṇa went to other’s houses, just as he had done before, and carried out misciefs. A lady from one of those houses came to yaśōdāp pirātti and complained to her, saying “Call your son and keep him with you”. This pāsuram mentions this narrative.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**pālaik kaṟandu** – milking all the cows, which are as mentioned in [tiruppāvai 3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2014/12/thiruppavai-03-ongi-ulagalandha/) “*vāngak kudam niṟaikkum vaḷḷal perum pasukkaḷ*” (The cows in tiruvāyppādi are such that they will keep on giving milk, even after several vessels have been filled with milk, during milking).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the cows in tiruvāyppādi were obedient like the royal elephant, śatrunjayan \[this is the name of the elephant used by daśaratan for his procession\]. Milking such cows. The term *kaṟandu* \[milking\], refers to the effort required to complete the process of milking these cows. This work is similar to telling a person to empty out water from an ocean, using one’s hands.

**aduppēṟa vaittu** – keeping them in small and large containers in order to boil all that milk, by keeping them on top of the fire-place.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the fire-place was that high and the milk was that heavy that one had to lift the vessels, containing milk, to keep them on top of the fire-places.

**pal vaḷaiyāḷ en magaḷ iruppa** – my daughter, who was wearing many bangles, stood guard over all the milk.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa entered the house, after seeing the bangles on the hands of her daughter and the containers of milk. Not aware of his entering my house, I had gone to the house in the western direction, seeking fire, and was talking to them for a short duration, recounting his mischievous activities. Using this \[my absence from my house\] as a prop, he entered my house.

**mēlai agattē neruppu vēṇḍic cenṟu** – I had gone to the house which is to the west of your house, in order to request for fire to light the fire-place in my house.

**iṟaip poḻudu angē pēsi ninṟēn** – I was talking to them for a few moments. ūtilising this interval to his advantage …

**sāḷakkirāmam …** – \[kriṣṇa is\] one who is complete with all qualities, residing forever in śrī śāḷagrāmam \[a divine abode\]. He tilted the vessels, which contained milk, drank milk from all the vessels, as if he were incomplete, and stood aside \[here\] as if he had nothing to do with whatever had happened.

**ālaikkarumbu …** – Oh, one who has the feature of talking sweetly, just like sugarcane which is apt to be churned in the mill \[for extracting sugar\] and who is complete with auspicious qualities!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the words of yaśōdāp pirātti would be such sweet that it would engage even those who have come to complain about her son in her words, even when she is scolding kriṣṇa. The term *mēlai agam* refers to the place where knowledge is shining bright and *neruppu* \[fire, sought by the lady\] refers to the detachment that one should desire to have, as a result of having that knowledge \[about emperumān and ourselves\] \[Thus, she had used her knowledge in order to obtain detachment from samsāram\].

**un maganaik kūvāy** – Call out to your son such that he does not remain in my house, carrying out misciefs, but comes to your side.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.9.6. Podar kanday

*pōdar kaṇḍāy ingē pōdar kaṇḍāy pōdarēn ennādē pōdar kaṇḍāyēdēnum solli asalagattār ēdēnum pēsa nān kētka māttēnkōdu kulam udaik kuttanēyō! kunṟam eduttāy! kudamādu kūttā!vēdap poruḷē! en vēngadavā! vittaganēī ingē pōdarāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōdu kulam udai – having auspicious qualities which are celebrated by everyone; O kuttanē – come, my dear son!; kunṟu – gōvardana hill; eduttāy – oh, one who lifted as an umbrella!; kudam ādu – lifting pots; kūttā – Oh, one dances!; vēdam – for all vēdams; poruḷē – Oh, one who is expounded!; en – apt to be considered as mine; vēngadavā – Oh, one who is standing on the hills of tirumalai!; vittaganē – Oh, one who has amazing powers!; ingē – (leaving that place) here; pōdar kaṇḍāy pōdar kaṇḍāy – Come fast (the word pōdaru has got shortened as pōdar here); pōdarēn ennādē – without saying that I will not come; pōdar kaṇḍāy – come; asal agattār – people in the neighbourhood; ēdēnum – faults about you, which cannot be spoken of; solli – to speak, amongst themselves; ēdēnum – words which I cannot hear or which I cannot speak; pēsa – to speak; nān – I, who am your mother; kētka māttēn – will not tolerate to hear; ingē pōdarāy – come here (yaśōdāp pirātti calls kriṣṇa, saying this)

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who has auspicious qualities which are celebrated by everyone, come! Oh, one who lifted the gōvardana hills as an umbrella! Oh, one who danced with pots! Oh, one who is expounded by vēdams! Oh, one who is apt to be called as mine, standing on the hills of tirumalai! Oh, one who has amazing powers! You should come here. Do not say that you would not come. I, your mother, cannot hear and tolerate words of people in the neighbourhood, who speak about your faults. Hence, come here.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) Since in the previous pāsuram yaśōdāp pirātti was told to call her son, she is calling out to him. This pāsuram describes that.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**pōdar kaṇḍāy ingē**– Do not carry out misciefs, standing there. Come here. The word *pōdaru* has got śortned as *pōdar* here.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that leaving that place \[where people complain about you\] and coming here is the apt activity for you. While I repeatedly call out to you to come, instead of repeatedly negating it saying that you would not come, you should come here. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that the word *pōgal* has got transformed to *pōdar*. The word *kaṇḍāy* is a word-filler used and does not have any meaning. It could also be construed as “You see, they are talking despicably about you”, in which case it has a meaning on its own.

**pōdar kaṇḍāy** – since kriṣṇa did not come when yaśōdāp pirātti called out to him the first time, she calls out to him a second time. Despite this, since he did not come …

**pōdarēn ennnādē pōdar kaṇḍāy** – Do not say “I will not come”. She tells him to come and see. When he asks her “For what purpose are you calling me?” she says …

**ēdēnum solli asalagattār ēdēnum pēsa nān kētka māttēn** – people in the neighbourhood would discuss amongst themselves about your faults, which could not even be mentioned through words, and then would come to me and tell me, which I cannot hear or speak about and which I cannot tolerate to hear.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that those people, apart from discussing amongst themselves, come to me and tell me “He is a thief”, words which are not proper for this clan and which I cannot tolerate,

**kōdu kulam udaiya kuttanē! O O** – “You are one, celebrated by everyone with your qualities. How could you be spoken of like this by everyone?” yaśōdāp pirātti feels saddened due to this. Due to that sorrow, she calls out “O O” \[Alas!).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here – “Oh, one who came as the son for the faultless clan!” The term *O* refers to excessive sorrow, felt by yaśōdāp pirātti.

**kunṟu eduttāy** – Oh, one who protected the cows and the herd-people by lifting the gōvardana hills!

**kudamādu kūttā** – Oh, one who danced with pots as an outlet for the pride of having opulence, due to cows! The term *kudamādu kūttan* refers to *kudam eduttu ādina kūttai udaiyavan* – one who performed dance by carrying the pots and dancing with them. Through these two features \[lifting the gōvardana hill and dancing with pots\], don’t you think that you are the protector for this clan and the opulence which came as a result of being born in this clan is your wealth? You should have your activities in line with this.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when herd-people get lot of wealth, they will engage in dancing with pots, just as brāhmaṇas will perform *hōmams* and *yajñams* \[vēdic rituals\] when they get excess of wealth.

**vēdap poruḷē** – Just as it has been mentioned in [bhagavat gītā 15-15](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/15-15) “*vēdaiśca sarvair ahamēva vēdya*:” (only I am known through the vēdams), oh, one who is expounded by all the vēdams!

**en vēngadavā** – Apart from knowing through vēdam, oh, one who had stood in tirumalai hills such that you could be seen through the eyes, both by nityasūris and by samsāris, to be called as “He is mine”!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that through the term *vittaganē* āḻvār asserts that emperumān is the cause for all the worlds \[the term *vittagan* is split into *vittu* and *agan*, in which *vittu* refers to seed, root cause for a tree\] and that he has the capability to control all the worlds \[when the word is considered as *vittagan*, instead of being split\].

**vittaganē** – Oh, one who is an amazing entity, since you are standing like this \[to be seen by both\]!

**ingē pōdarāyē** – Leaving the place where people, who speak ill of your qualities live, come here where I speak only about your good qualities.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.9.7. Sennel arisi

*sennel arisi siṟu paruppuc ceyda akkāram naṟu ney pālālpanniraṇḍu tiruvōṇam attēn paṇḍum ippiḷḷai parisu aṟivaninnam ugappan nān enṟu solli ellām viḻingittup pōndu ninṟānun magan tannai asōdai nangāy! kūvik koḷḷāy ivaiyum silavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

asōdai nangāy – oh, yaśōdāp pirātti, who is complete with auspicious qualities!; sem nel arisi – reddish paddy and rice; siṟu paruppu – small, green gram; seyda – made, by concentrating, without any fault; akkāram – jaggery; naṟu ney – fragrant ghee; pālāl – with milk, all these; pattu iraṇḍu tiruvōṇam – twelve tiruvōṇam \[days of śravaṇam star\]; attēn – I had prepared, pāyasam \[combination of rice, jaggery, green gram and milk\] and apūpam \[round objects made with rice and green gram, along with jaggery\] as part of nōnbu \[ceremony\]; paṇḍum – earlier too; i piḷḷai – this boy’s; parisu – nature; aṟivan – I knew; ellām – all the food cooked for the tiruvōṇa vratam (fasting observed on the day of śravaṇam star); viḻungittu – after swallowing them, without leaving anything behind; innam – “further; nān ugappan – I desire”; enṟu solli – saying this; pōndu ninṟān – leaving that place, he stood innocently; un magan tannai – your son; kūvik koḷḷāy – call him out; silavē – is this the way to bring up a child? (thus complain the women in the village)

**Перевод:**

**Oh, yaśōdāp pirātti, who is complete with auspicious qualities! Along with reddish paddy and rice, green gram, jaggery, fragrant ghee and milk, I had prepared dishes such as pāyasam and apūpam for observing śravaṇa vratam, for the last twelve months. I knew the quality of this boy, earlier too. He swallowed all the food stuff which I had prepared for the vratam, without leaving behind anything and says “I would like to eat more”. He had left our place, as if he had nothing to do with whatever had happened. Call your son to your side. Is this a way of bringing up a child, allowing him to engage in carrying out misciefs?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) When yaśōdāp pirātti told him \[as in the previous pāsuram\] “vittaganē ingē pōdarāyē” (Oh, one who is an amazing entity, you should come here), instead of coming to the place where she called him to come, kriṣṇa entered someone else’s house, ate food stuff which they had made for a vratam \[a ceremonial fast\]. A lady came to yaśōdāp pirātti and complained to her. This pāsuram describes this narrative. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that it is customary in the clan of herd-people to observe fast on the day of śravaṇam star. A lady comes to yaśōdāp pirātti, mentions the preparations which she had made for the ceremony, kriṣṇa’s misciefs at her house and tells yaśōdāp pirātti to control her son.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**sennel …** – reddish, pure rice, grown from fertile, hard soil; green gram which has been obtained from crops grown on similar soil; jaggery obtained after heating sugar cane extract, without any fault; milk from cows heated to one fourth of original measure, setting resultant milk to curd, churning the resultant curd and obtaining ghee, milk obtained from healthy cows; with all these …

**panniraṇḍu tiruvōṇam attēn** – I had been preparing *pāyasam* and *apūpam* (appam) during for the last twelve *tiruvōṇam* (*śravaṇam* star).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says further here that kriṣṇa would not wait for the *vratam* to be completed and take the food stuff offered. He would eat even before it is offered to deities. *parisu* refers to offering desired materials apt for one’s form.

**paṇḍum ippiḷḷai parisu aṟivan** – I knew the nature of this child \[kriṣṇa\] earlier too. In other words, even as I prepared the food stuff for *śravṇa vratam*, this boy would start his misciefs and eat up the food stuff even before offering the prepared food to deities. This time too, he has done the same mischief.

**ellām viḻingittu** – gathering all the food stuff, prepared for this *tiruvōṇam vratam,* and swallowing them, without leaving anything behind.

**innam ugappan nān enṟu solli** – not being satiated even after eating all the food stuff, during this *tiruvōṇam vratam*, he said that he would desire to have some more food

**pōndu ninṟān** – he left that place and came here, as if he had nothing to do with whatever had happened.

**un magan tannai asōdai nangāy kūvik koḷḷāy** – Oh, yaśōdāp pirātti! Call your son to your vicinity such that he would not be able to indulge in any mischief there

**ivaiyum silavē** – ṣouldn’t one, who had given birth to a child, bring up the child in a protective way such that he would not indulge in misciefs? Is this the way that one would bring up a child?

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when the lady complained to yaśōdāp pirātti about kriṣṇa, he became furious and told yaśōdāp pirātti “They are telling only lies about me”. yaśōdāp pirātti, believing his words, asked the lady who complained “Should I believe your words? ōr, should I believe his words?” The lady told her “It is not only that he had carried out misciefs. The way that you are asking us, who have come to complain to you, is indeed a way!” \[in sarcasm\]

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.9.8. Kesavane inge

*kēsavanē! ingē pōdfharāyē killēn ennādu ingē pōdarāyēnēsam ilādār agattirundu nī viḷaiyādādē pōdarāyētūsanam sollum toḻuttaimārum toṇḍarum ninṟa idattininṟutāy solluk koḷvadu tanmam kaṇḍāy dāmōdarā! ingē pōdarāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kēsavanē! – oh, one who has beautiful locks!; ingē pōdarāy – come here; killēn ennādu – without saying “I will not come”, come here; nī – you, saying that you would come after playing there for sometime; nēsam ilādār – towards those who are not affectionate towards you; agattu irundu – staying in their houses; viḷaiyādādē – apart from not playing; tūsanam sollum – those who speak abusively about you; toḻuttaimārum – those who are servitors of herd-women; toṇḍarum – those who are servitors to herd-men; ninṟa – standing; idattil ninṟum – from the places \[where they are standing\]; pōdarāy – come here; tāy sollu – mother’s words; koḷvadu – following \[her vors\]; tanmam kaṇḍāy – see, it is righteous act; dāmōdarā! – oh, dāmōdarā \[having the scar of rope tied on the stomach\]! Come here

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who has beautiful locks! Instead of saying “I will not come”, come here. Do not play inside the houses of those who do not have affection towards you. Come from the place where those, who are servitors to herd-women and herd-men, stand and abuse you, and come here. You should see that following the words of your mother is the righteous act. Oh, dāmōdarā! Come here.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) After the woman, who came to complain to yaśōdāp pirātti about kriṣṇa, told her to call her son to her place, yaśōdāp pirātti called out to him. This pāsuram narrates that.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kēsavanē ingē pōdarāyē** – Oh, one who has praiseworthy locks! You should leave that place and come here such that I could see the beauty of your gait and the swaying of your locks as you walk. When she called out to him like this, kriṣṇa said “I will not come now”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that apart from having praiseworthy locks, due to which yaśōdāp pirātti is addressing him as “*kēsavanē*”, this is also a famous name for kriṣṇa. Hence, she is calling him by that name. When kriṣṇa tells her “If you call many times after hearing the words of those who tell you something, will I come without playing?” …

**killēn ennādu ingē pōdarāyē** – she tells him to come to her, without refusing. When he says “I will play here for some time and then come” …

**nēsam …** – She says “īsn’t there any other place for you to play? Do not play inside the houses of those who do not have affection towards you. Come here”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār tells kriṣṇa “Do not remain as *antaryāmi* (indvelling soul) of those who do not have devotion towards you or who do not like to get uplifted \[from samsāram\], but enjoy *leelārasam* \[flavour of samsāram\]” This manifests the meaning that while kriṣṇa could enjoy the *leelārasam* through an infinitesimal part of his *sankalpam* \[vow\], there was no need for him to play, by remaining inside \[as antaryāmi of\] those people referred to here.

**tūsanam sollum toḻuttaimārum toṇḍarum ninṟa idattil ninēum** – Is it only this much? There is no limit to the abuses which those who are servitors to the herd-women and herd-men speak about you. Do not remain in the places where they are present and come here. Despite her telling him this, since he did not come, she says further …

**tāy solluk koḷvadu tanmam kaṇḍāy** – she prays to him. You should know that following the words of a mother who has given birth to you is the rightful act. āren’t you one who had followed the words of your mother, when you were born? \[This is about kriṣṇa hiding his two extra hands when he was born as well as the divine disc and divine conch which he had held in those divine hands, when dēvakip pirātti told him to hide them and be like a normal child, lest kamsan harm him immediately\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti is telling kriṣṇa “Did you not listen to your mother even at the time of your birth? Unlike that mother \[here, the reference is to kaikēyi, who had asked śrī rāma to go to forest, in exile, for fourteen years\], did I justify your going to forest where inimical entities and wild animals live? For anyone, listening to mother’s words is the righteous activity to be engaged in”

**dāmōdarā** – Weren’t you obedient towards me earlier, allowing me to tie you with a piece of rope on your divine stomach?

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: this term refers to the fact that kriṣṇa was tied down with a rope by yaśōdāp pirātti. Alternatively, with *dāmam* referring to paramapadam and *udaram* referring to centre, this term *dāmōdara* could also refer to emperumān who is living at the centre of śrī vaikuṇṭam. The reason for her calling out to him s *dāmōdarā* here is to hint that yaśōdāp pirātti is thinking “Why did I let go of him, from his tied-down position?” Alternatively, it could also be considered that yaśōdāp pirātti is saying “If I get hold of that old mortar and that rope, I will ensure that he does not go out of that binding”. She feels sorry that she has to tie him at the same place where he had been tied \[on his stomach\] earlier.

**ingē pōdarāyē** – When such is the case, without going against my words, come here.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.9.9. Kannal ilattuvattodu

*kannal ilattuvattōdu sīdai kāreḷḷin uṇḍai kalattil ittuennagam enṟū nān vaittup pōndēn ivan pukku avaṟṟaip peṟuttip pōndānpinnum agam pukku uṟiyai nōkkip piṟangu oḷi veṇṇeyum sōdikkinṟānun magan tannai asōdai nangāy! kūvik koḷḷāy ivaiyum silavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

asōdai nangāy! – Oh, yaśōdāp pirātti, who is complete in all auspicious qualities!; kannal – mixed with jaggery concentrate; ilattuvattōdu – along with laddu; sīdai – sīdai too \[a type of foodstuff, in spherical form\]; kār eḷḷin uṇḍai – spheres of black sesame sweet; kalattil – in containers; ittu – keeping them; ennagam enṟu – thinking “This is my house. None will enter”; nān pōndēn – I came out; ivan – this boy; pukku – entered \[my house\]; avaṟṟai – all those eatables; peṟutti – making it appear that I had got (this is said in the contrarian manner. In other words, without leaving anything for me, he stole the entire lot); pōndān – he has come; pinnum – yet again; agam pukku – entering the house; uṟiyai nōkki – looking at uṟi \[a holder for vessels, suspended from the ceiling, through a network of ropes\]; piṟangu oḷi – being very fresh; veṇṇeyum – is cow’s butter available?; sōdikkinṟān – he is checking; un magan tannai – your son; kūvik koḷḷāy – call out; ivaiyum – the manner of allowing him to indulge in misciefs; silavē – is this a way of nurturing a child?

**Перевод:**

**Oh, yaśōdāp pirātti, who is complete with all the auspicious qualities! I had prepared spheres of jaggery concentrate with laddu, sīdai and black sesame. Keeping them safely inside containers appropriate for each of those dishes, I left my house, thinking “It is my house; none will enter this place \[and steal them\]” This kriṣṇa entered my house as soon as I left, ate them all up, leaving nothing behind, making it appear as if I had eaten them all. He left the place, re-entered the house and looked at the uṟi to see if any freshly made cow’s butter is available too. I am unable to put up with such misciefs. Please call out to your son. Is this the way to bring up a child?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) Even after calling out to him “Oh, dāmōdarā! Come here”, kriṣṇa went to someone else’s house and carried out misciefs such as eating all the apūpam \[types of tasty dishes in round form\] which the people in that house had cooked for themselves. The lady of that house comes to yaśōdāp pirātti and complains to her to call kriṣṇa to her. This pāsuram mentions this narrative*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kannal …** – *kannal* – jaggery block. This is mixed with the three materials mentioned further. Food stuff made with jaggery will be tastier than mere jaggery block.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his vyākhyānam, that *ilattuvam* refers to appam \[a sweet dish made with jaggery and rice flour\].

**ilatutuvattōdu sīdai kār eḷḷin uṇḍai** – *ilattu* – a special preparation of *apūpam* \[round shaped object\]. Along with it, \[jaggery mixed\] *sīdai* and \[jaggery mixed\] black *sesame* spheres

**kalattil ittu** – storing them in vessels appropriate for each of these food stuffs

**ennagam enṟu nān vaittup pōndēn** – thinking “This is my house; none will enter here”, I went out.

**ivan pukku avaṟṟaip peṟuttip pōndān** – The moment that I left the house, he \[kriṣṇa\] entered the house and ate them all, leaving them for me. She is saying this in contrarian manner, viz. he didn’t leave anything behind for me to eat, and ate them all himself.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *peṟutti* conveys the meaning that kriṣṇa ate up all the dishes and considered that his eating the dishes is a favour to me. He considered them as living beings and ate them, considering that to grant them great life, uplifting me in the process.

**pinnum agam pukku uṟiyai nōkki** – not being contented with those, he entered the house again, looking at the *uṟi.*

**piṟngoḷi veṇṇeyum sōdikkinṟān** – He is checking to see if freshly made butter too would be available.

**un magan …** – Oh, yaśōdāp pirātti! Call out to your son such that he would not indulge in any mischief there and comes to you.

**ivaiyum silavē** – Is allowing a child to carry out misciefs, a way of bringing up the child? Alternatively, it could be considered that when the lady \[who had come to complain\] told yaśōdāp pirātti “Oh, yaśōdāp pirātti! You are complete in all auspicious qualities. You call him out to your side so that he too would become complete in all auspicious qualities”, yaśōdāp pirātti responded to her saying “You are crying about the fulness of my auspicious qualities and the faults of kriṣṇa. Little children will open the doors of houses, enter them, and eat whatever they could lay their hands on. Are your children fully under your control?” She turned away from that lady, in anger. The lady tells her “More than the misciefs carried out by him, this is also a manner of responding!” saying out of sadness.

We shall next consider the 10<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.9.10. Sollil arasi

*sollil arasip padudi nangāy! sūḻal udaiyan unpiḷḷaidānēillam pugundu en magaḷaik kūvik kaiyil vaḷaiyaik kaḻaṟṟik koṇḍukollaiyil ninṟum koṇarndu viṟṟa avvoruttikku avvaḷai koduttunallana nāvaṟpaḻangaḷ koṇḍu nān allēn enṟu sirikkinṟānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nangāy! – oh, yaśōdāp pirātti, who is complete with your auspicious qualities!; sollil – if I tell you the misciefs carried out by your son; arasip padudi – you become angry; un piḷḷaidān – your son; sūḻal udaiyan – has many deceitful activities; illam pugundu – entering my house; en magaḷai – my daughter; kūvi – called, by her name; kaiyil – from her hand; vaḷaiyai – bangle, which she wore for identity; kaḻaṟṟik koṇḍu – removed it; kollaiyil ninṟum – from the orchard; koṇarndu – brought to the street; angu – in that place; viṟṟa – one who was selling blue berries; oruttikku – to a lady; avvaḷai – that bangle; koduttu – gave her; nallana – beautiful, matching his divine form; nāval paḻangaḷ – blue berries; koṇḍu – bought; nān allēn – saying “It was not I who gave her the bangle”; sirikkinṟānē – he laughed

**Перевод:**

**Oh, yaśōdāp pirātti, who is complete with all the auspicious qualities! If I tell you the truth, you become angry. Your son is full of deceitful activities. He entered my house, called out my daughter, by her name, removed the bangle which she was wearing for her identity, from her hand, went to the orchard and entered the street there. He gave that bangle to a fruit-seller there, who was selling blue berries and received blue berries, which matched his divine form. When I asked him whether he had given that bangle to the fruit seller, he said “I did not give” and laughed.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) Before one lady completed her complaint, saying “Oh, yaśōdāp pirātti, call your son”, another lady came there and started listing the misciefs which kriṣṇa carried out in her house. This pāsuram mentions this narrative.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**sollil arasip padudi nangāy** – more than the complaints listed out by the previous lady, another lady came and started her complaints, as if adding insult to injury. yaśōdāp pirātti became angry, saying “Oh, another mischief!” The lady said “Oh, one who is complete with all auspicious qualities! If I tell you your son’s misciefs, you become angry”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says here that the lady, who came to complain to yaśōdāp pirātti says “If we tell you about your son’s misciefs, you get angry and turn your face away; if we do not tell you, that will cause a fault to your completeness”

**sūḻal udaiyan un piḷḷai tanē** – it is only your son, who indulged in intolerable misciefs, which cannot be brushed aside and have to be told you. *sūḻal* – deceptive act, many types of misciefs, indulged in by him. There is nothing among these misciefs that he does not have. When yaśōdāp pirātti told her “What is the intolerable mischief that he has indulged in due to which you have to come to me like this? Tell me that” the lady says further …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *sūḻal* refers to many varieties of misciefs, of which kriṣṇa lacks none. yaśōdāp pirātti tells the lady “Does he indulge in mischievous activities? What did you see on his side?”

**illam pugundu en magaḷaik kūvi** – he entered my house, called out to my daughter, by her name.

**kaiyil vaḷaiyaik kaḻaṟṟik koṇḍu** – he removed the bangle, which was an identification for her, from her hand.

**kollai …**– he went to the orchard, gave the bangle to a lady who was selling blueberries

**nallana nāval paḻangaḷ koṇḍu** – knowing \[and choosing\] the blueberries which match his divine form, he was bargaining with her, saying that he needs more and she was saying that she had given sufficient fruits already. That’s when I went there and asked the fruit-seller as to how she obtained that bangle. She said “He only gave me”. When I asked him “Did you give her the bangle?”

**nān allēn enṟu sirikkinṟānē** – “It vasn’t I who did it. Did you see me with the bangle in my hand? Did you see me entering your house? Did you hear me calling out to your daughter, by her name? Did you see me removing the bangle from her hand? If you had seen, why did you not take back the bangle?” He posed so many questions to me, in such a manner that I could not respond to any of those. He laughed, on top of that. Is there any mischief which is more intolerable than this?

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the lady, who came to complain to yaśōdāp pirātti, says that kriṣṇa asked her all these questions, all of which were false and smiled at her. She forgot the bangle, forgot kriṣṇa and told him “I will tell her to control you such that you would not indulge again in misciefs”

He further quotes an incident from the life of one piḷḷai engalāḻvār, a disciple of nanjīyar \[one of our preceptors\]. One day, when he was about to sleep, kriṣṇa came in his dream as a young boy and told him “I want blueberries”. When he tried to sleep, kriṣṇa did not allow him to slip into his sleep. When piḷḷai engaḷāḻvār asked him “Who are you?” he said “I am jīyar’s son, *āyar kō* \[the head of herd-people\]”. He got up from his sleep, went to nanjīyar, fell at his divine feet and told him “Oh, jīyar! Your son does not allow me to live in my house; neither does he allow me to sleep”. jīyar heard him out mercifully, went to his *tiruppaḷḷi* \[place where he had mercifully placed his tiruvārādanap perumāḷ\] and told him “Oh, my svāmy! It is not proper on your part to do like this”, controlling him. This narration is very famous.

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan
