## 2.9.11. Vandu kalittu

*vaṇḍu kaḷittiraikkum varu punal kāvirit tennaranganpaṇḍu avan seyda kirīdai ellām battar pirān vittucittan pādalkoṇḍu ivai pādik kunikka vallār gōvindan tan adiyārgaḷ āgieṇḍisaikkum viḷakkāgi niṟpār iṇaiyadi en talai mēlanavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇḍu – beetles; kaḷittu – being joyous, having imbibed honey; iraikkum – humming loudly; poḻil – with gardens; varu – coming in abundance of flow, for the sake of those gardens; punal – having water; kāviri – through the divine kāviri river; sūḻ – being surrounded; then – beautiful; arangan – residing in śrī rangam; avan – one, who has such greatness; paṇḍu – during the time of incarnation; seyda – mercifully carried out; kirīdai ellām – all the playful activities; vittu cittan – one who has viṣṇu in his heart; battar pirān – sung by periyāḻvār, the most supreme among brāhmaṇas; pādal – songs; ivai koṇḍu – with these pāsurams; pādi – singing, in full, with their mouths; kunikka vallār – those who are capable of dancing, with their physical forms moving constantly; gōvindan than – for kaṇṇan, the protector of cattle; adiyārgaḷ āgi – being servitors; ettu dikkum \[eṇ disaiyum\] – such that darkness from all eight directions gets removed; viḷakkāgi niṟpār – those who remain as lamps; iṇai – having the beauty of being together; adi – divine feet; en talai mēlana – will remain on my head

**Перевод:**

**Beautiful śrī rangam is surrounded by gardens in which beetles, having imbibed honey, are humming loudly, as well as by the divine kāviri river, which flows with abundance of water for the sake of those gardens. emperumān, who is dwelling in such śrīrangam, had indulged in playful activities during the time of his incarnation \[as kriṣṇa\]. periyāḻvār, who has emperumān in his heart and who is the most supreme among brāhmaṇas, has composed those activities through songs. Those who sing these pāsurams in full, through their mouths and dance with their physical forms, will become servitors of kriṣṇa and will be the illuminating light in all eight directions such that darkness gets removed fully. periyāḻvār says that their feet, which have the beauty of being together, will remain on his head.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In this final pāsuram of the decad, āḻvār says that those who learn these pāsurams are his puruśārta bhūtars; in other words, they are his ultimate benefit.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vaṇḍu …** – śrīrangam is surrounded by gardens where beetles, after imbibing honey, hum in a loud manner; it is also surrounded by the divine kāviri, which brings in abundance of water to sustain those gardens. śrīrangam has divine compound walls, divine turrets, divine streets and divine mansions. It has a distinguished beauty due to all these. emperumān has the greatness of dwelling permanently in this divine abode. The divine, playful activities in which he had indulged in, in his incarnations …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai adds, in his svāpadēśam, that the beetles were humming at the top of their voices. The term *then* would refer both to the \[southern\] direction and to being beautiful. *paṇḍu avan seyda kirīdai ellām* – the divine activities indulged in by emperumān in his incarnation \[as kriṣṇa\] were the pretext for the world, through the means of fear, devotion and relationship with emperumān, to be united with the relationship and activities in line with that relationship \[being servitors to emperumān and carrying out kainkaryam \[mangaḷāśāsanam\] to him)

**battar pirān …** – periyāḻvār, who is the most supreme among the brāhmaṇas, has viṣṇu, who has pervaded everywhere, in his mind. He has sung songs on these activities of emperumān.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that periyāḻvār combined the distinguished, playful activities of emperumān with mangaḷāśāsanam which is the ultimate kainkaryam on attaining emperumān. periyāḻvār is the benefactor for brāhmaṇas who desire knowledge of emperumān and jīvātmā. He is capable of carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam for emperumān, keeping emperumān in his heart.

**pādik kunikka vallār** – Those who are capable of reciting these pāsurams, impelled by their love towards emperumān, and also who are also capable of dancing along with singing, such that their physical forms do not remain in one place, with changing emotions…

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that those who sing these pāsurams and dance as well, should exhibit their pathos of obedience \[being servitors to emperumān\].

**gōvindan …** – they will become servitors of *gōvindan* (one who protects cattle), who had indulged in these divine activities. Not only that, they will also, with their presence \[knowledge\], remove the darkness of ignorance in all the eight directions. Those who have such radiance, their ….

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *eṇ disai* refers to the eight directions \[those people will remove darkness from the eight directions\], to the distinguished situations which are thought of \[they will be able to say good bodings to people who may be in different situations, good and bad\] and to the eight meanings which are reflected through the distinguished *vyāpaka mantram* \[tirumantram\], the first of the three esoteric mantrams. These eight meanings come from the three terms seen in tirumantram. These meanings are: (1). emperumān is the causative factor for all the worlds (2) He is the lord (3) He is the protector (these three come from the first syllable ‘*a’* in the first term, praṇavam and to the hidden fourth case which is on top of “*a”*). (4) jīvātmā is the servitor existing exclusively for emperumān (this comes from the third syllable, ‘*ma’* and second syllable ‘*u’* in the first term). (6) jīvātmā is totally dependent on emperumān and should not engage with protecting himself (this comes from the second term *nama*🙂 (7) jīvātmā is related to emperumān (this is from the last term nārāyaṇa). (8) jīvātmā should carry out kainkaryam to emperumān (through the suffix *āya* which is suffixed to nārāyaṇa). Thus, these people will be the splendorous radiance in all situations.

**iṇaiyadi en talai mēlanavē**– āḻvār says that the divine feet of such people, which have the beauty of being together, will dwell forever on his head. Through this, just as nammāḻvār had said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.1.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/06/thiruvaimozhi-9-1-11-adhumillai/) “*ōdavalla pirākkaḷ nammai āḷudaiyār paṇḍē*” (benefactors, who are capable of reciting these pāsurams, will be our lords, from the time that they accept a physical body), periyāḻvār describes the greatness of such entities \[through their becoming servitors of emperumān\] and the respectful reverence which he has towards them \[through their ability to remove darkness of ignorance in all the directions).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that periyāḻvār says this verse \[*iṇaiyadi en talai mēlanavē*\] similar to tirumangai āḻvār in [periya tirumoḻi 7.4.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/10/periya-thirumozhi-7-4-1/) “*en talai mēlārē*” (those who worship the divine feet of emperumān will step on my head and roam around). This decad is periyāḻvār’s *payilum sudaroḷi* and *nedumāṟkadimai* \[these two decads, [tiruvāimoḻi 3.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-7-payilum/) and [tiruvāimoḻi 8.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/05/thiruvaimozhi-8-10-nedumarkadimai/) respectively, were sung by nammāḻvār, glorifying the servitors of emperumān\]. periyāḻvār says here that the dwelling place for such divine feet \[of emperumān’s servitors\] is his head.

We shall next consider the pravēśam of the next tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.10.1. Arril irundu

*āṟṟil irundu viḷaiyāduvōngaḷaiccēṟṟāl eṟindu vaḷai tugil kaikkoṇḍukāṟṟil kadiyanāy ōdi agam pukkumāṟṟamum tārānāl inṟu muṟṟum vaḷaittiṟam pēsānāl inṟu muṟṟum*

**Пословный перевод:**

āṟṟil irundu – from the sands, on the bank of river yamunā; viḷaiyāduvōngaḷai – on us, playing with our friends; sēṟṟāl eṟindu – throwing mud; vaḷai – our bangles; tugil – saris; kaikkoṇḍu – gathering; kāṟṟil – more than wind; kadiyanāy – galloping (very hurriedly); ōdi – running; aāgam pukku – entering house; māṟṟamum trānāl – due to kaṇṇan \[kriṣṇa\], who is not responding despite our pleading to him; inṟu muṟṟum – we will perish today (word spoken out of frustration, meaning that they will give up their lives today); vaḷaittiṟam – regarding bangles; pēsānāl – by the one who did not say “I will give” or “I will not give”, we will perish today

**Перевод:**

**We were playing among ourselves on the sands, on the bank of river yamunā. kriṣṇa threw mud on us, gathered our bangles and saris, ran away faster than wind and entered his house. Despite our calling out to him and pleading with him, since he did not respond, we will perish today. We will perish on account of the one who did not speak about whether he will or will not return our bangles.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**āṟṟil irundu** – Did we stay on the land which some could claim us “This is ours”? Wasn’t it on a land common to all, that we remained! The meaning conveyed here is that “We remained in a place where people were roaming about and not in a secluded place where he \[kriṣṇa\] could come and carry out mischief”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that the women say “We were in a place where people were coming and going; it was a common place where you would not come normally”. What is the connection between the place where we remained and your coming there?

**viḷaiyāduvōngaḷai** – we, who were playing. Were we not engaging in things other than him? Did we engage with him? Did we carry out any mischief on him earlier? Did we look at him through the corners of our eyes? There was none amongst us who thought of him.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: We were engaging with one another in that river. Did we enter it, expecting any benefit? Was it not for playing among ourselves? Is there any benefit for playing? īsn’t that, in itself, the benefit? When we were playing in the sand, building houses, cooking food with sand, building castles etc, kriṣṇa came there and asked us to include him in their game. When we refused, taking our Implements for playing and turned our faces away \[from him\], he threw mud on us. He gathered our bangles and dresses…

**sēṟṟāl eṟindu** – threw mud on us. Couldn’t he have touched out, directly with his divine hands, without anyone noticing? Should he throw mud on us such that others, who were seeing this, would ask “What is this?”

**vaḷai tugil kaikkoṇḍu** – gathering the bangles and saris which we had removed, prior to taking a bath \[in the river\]. Since they are herd-women, they remove their bangles and dresses before taking a bath.

**kāṟṟil kadiyanāy ōdi** – without getting caught, even when we ran behind him, running faster than wind. If he could take things which sustain his life, should he also take things which sustain us? For him, the sustenance is through their \[the girls’\] bangles and dresses. For them, sustenance is through his divine form.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the women say “We could have caught the blowing wind, but not kriṣṇa”

**agam pukku** – even while chasing him, he ran and entered his house, where we couldn’t enter. He stole things from a public place but went into a private place.

**māṟṟamum tārānāl inṟu muṟṟum** – despite our calling out to him by his name, he is not responding to any of our calls. Is his word too like the bangles and dresses \[not to be given\]? Due to the person, who did not respond with even one word, we will end our lives. They would survive if he had uttered a word.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that had kriṣṇa responded to their calls, they would have sustained themselves, after sensing the clarity and the bewilderment in his voice \[clarity on account of the fact that his followers have come to him and bewilderment due to feeling sad that he had not gone to them to help them out but that they had to come to him\].

**vaḷaittiṟam pēsānāl inṟū muṟṟum** – Since he did not respond with a word regarding the bangles, saying either that he will give or he will not give, we will perish today. The word *muṟṟudum* has got shortened here as *muṟṟum*. *muṟṟudum* refers to an end, viz. we will perish.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the herd-women say that despite their pleading with kriṣṇa many times, should he not respond even once? Since they say that kriṣṇa did not speak to them a word about returning the bangles, their focus is on his speaking to them more than on their bangles being returned to them. These women are expressing their desire \[for kriṣṇa to speak to them\] when they speak about bangles, dress etc. They say that even if they stood the whole day, calling out to him, it was rare to get even a word out of him. It is enough for them if he says “I will return your bangles”.  He could tell us “You return to your respective house. I shall enquire whose bangle belongs to whom, come to the respective house and return that bangle to that person”. Even if he doesn’t do one among these, they say that they will perish. *inṟu muṟṟum* – either they will sustain themselves at the end of the day or they will perish. Even if yaśōdāp pirātti had told them “You go to your houses; I shall get the bangles and dresses for you” they would not go. If she had gone to him and told him “Return these to them” he would have said “Is it for this that I had taken this much of efforts and brought all these here?” Listening to him, yaśōdāp pirātti would appreciate the logic in his words and tell them “See, there is truth in what he says”. śrī nandagōpar too would have agreed with his \[kriṣṇa’s\] sense of justice, saying that it is the most apt.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai summarises his svāpadēśam for this pāsuram, at the end, with the following: It is clear that emperumān engages with those who do not consider any benefit other than himself as their benefit and who do not consider any means other than himself as the means to attain him. Those, who have knowledge \[about emperumān\], think that not having anything with us \[to attain emperumān\] is the reason for emperumān’s infatuation with us. The term *sēṟṟāl eṟīndu* indicates that the women engaged with him because of his simplicity and easy approacability \[he came down to where they were playing\]. The term *eṟindu* affirms that he was not happy with them and hence threw \[mud\] at them \[he could have smeared it on them with his hands gently; he did not do that. Instead, he threw mud at them, since he was angry that they had come to the river, in the open and did not stay put in their respective house\]. He left behind a mark by taking away things from them. The term *vaḷai tugil kaikkoṇḍu* \[taking away their bangles and dresses\] refers to removing their \[lowly degrees of\] servitude and total dependence towards him \[lowly degree of servitude is when serving emperumān, we think of ourselves. Here, it refers to the herd-girls wearing bangles as a decoration for themselves. By removing the bangles, he removes their thought about themselves when serving him. Similarly, lower degree of dependence is when they dress themselves with saris; this indicates their efforts in protecting themselves. emperumān, by removing their dresses, removes this lower degree of dependence on him\]. Through the term *kāṟṟil kadiyanāyōdi* \[*kāṟṟu* – wind, could not be seen, but could be felt\], it is emphasised that emperumān is beyond the sense of touch too. The term *agam pukku* refers to emperumān reaching his abode where he enjoys the jīvātmā as the total *svatantran* \[totally independent entity\]. The term *māṟṟamum tārānāl* indicates that he is *avākyanātarāmruta bhōgi* \[he enjoys the jīvātmās as nectar, without the need to speak or the need to sustain\]. The term *vaḷaittiṟam pēsānāl* refers to his being the *viśyānurūpa prāpya prakāśakan* \[he shows the entity to be attained, based on the person who approaches him for enlightening; if the person who approaches emperumān is his follower, he offers himself to that person; if the person is inimical, he offers all the other wealth to that person, but does not offer him\]. In this case, he hints to the herd-girls that bangles are not the entity to be attained for them; they have to attain him. Hence, he removes the bangles from these girls and makes them to think of himself. The term *inṟu muṟṟum* indicates that there are only two stages when it comes to attaining emperumān – either one attains him or one goes on taking births repeatedly, in samsāram, and that there is nothing in-between these two stages. The herd-girls say that if emperumān does not shower his mercy on them, they will perish. This is in line with [tiruvāimoḻi 2.5.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-5-3-ennul-kalandhavan/) “*tannuḷ kalavādadu epporuḷum tān illaiyē*” (there is no entity which exists, which is not related to him)

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.10.2. Kundalam tala

*kuṇḍalam tāḻak kuḻal tāḻa nāṇ tāḻaeṇ disaiyōrum iṟainjit toḻudu ēttavaṇḍu amar pūnguḻalār tugil kaikkoṇḍuviṇ tōy marattānāl inṟu muṟṟum vēṇḍavum tārānāl inṟu muṟṟum*

**Пословный перевод:**

kuṇḍalam – ear rings; tāḻa – hanging down to the shoulders and swaying; kuḻal – divine bundles of locks; tāḻa – lowered to the same extent as the ear rings and swaying; nāṇ – the necklace donned on the divine neck; tāḻa – coming down to the level of his divine navel and swaying; ettu disaiyōrum – all the entities such as sages, celestial entities et al in the eight directions, prayed; iṟainji – falling, with the six limbs touching the ground; toḻudu – with the heads bowed down; ētta – praised; vaṇḍu amar – beetles settling upon; pū – decorated with flowers; kuḻalār – women, who had such locks; tugil – saris; koṇḍu – gathering them; viṇ tōy – reaching to the sky; marattānāl – we will perish on account of one who has climbed atop such a kurundam tree (a type of tree with fragrant foliage); vēṇḍavum – even if we beseech him, saying “Please give us our saris”; tārānāl – we will perish because of him, who is refusing to return

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa’s divine ear rings dropped down to the level of his shoulders and swayed. His divine locks too lowered to the same extent and swayed. The divine necklace, worn on the neck, reached down to his divine navel and swayed. All the entities such as sages, celestial entities et al in the eight directions, fell on the ground in front of kriṣṇa, and praised him, bowing their heads down \[in respect\]. kriṣṇa gathered the saris of women, who had decorated their locks with flowers such that beetles were constantly settling on them. He climbed atop a kurundam tree and sat. The women say that they will perish because of him. They further say that they will perish by the end of the day if he does not return their dresses, despite their pleading to him “Return us our dresses”**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the women, seen in the previous pāsuram, did not wish to move away from that place, until they hear the final word on their pleading \[that they will perish if kriṣṇa did not respond\]. What were they doing, standing like that? They were recalling his incarnations, his amazing activities in those incarnations and the qualities exhibited in those activities, to such an extent that these would form the basis for their complaints in the subsequent pāsurams.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kuṇḍalam tāḻak kuḻal tāḻa nāṇ tāḻa** – *kuṇḍalam* – ear rings. They came down to the shoulders and swayed; divine locks, which were complementary to those ear rings, also came down to the shoulders and swayed; the divine chain, adorned on the divine neck came down to the divine navel and swayed.

**eṇ tisaiyōrum irainjit toḻudētta** – sages, celestial entities et al, who were in the eight directions, looking at the beauty of this divine form \[of kriṣṇa\] and his distinguished divine activities, lost their pride \[that they were *īśvarans*\], bowed down to him and praised him.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that sages and celestial entities, in the eight directions, attracted by the divine beauty of emperumān, just as it has been said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 3.27 “*pumsām driśticittāpahāriṇīm*” (śrī rāma stole the eyes and minds of men), paid obeisance to kriṣṇa and praised him. They performed *anjali* (cupping the palms together, in salutation) and, in complete humility, offered mangaḷāśāsanam to him.

**vaṇḍamar pūnguḻalār tugil kaikkoṇḍu** – gathering the dresses left on the river bank by women who had decorated their locks with flowers on which beetles settle forever…

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that even though the women say that kriṣṇa has gathered their dresses, their expectation was also that only \[that he should gather their dresses\]. Their wish is that just as he gathered their dresses, he should gather them too.

**viṇ tōy marattānāl inṟu muṟṟum** – due to this person, who has climbed atop the *kurundam* tree which has reached to the sky, we will perish.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that though kriṣṇa had gone to the top of the *kurundam* tree which had grown tall to reach the skies, they will not leave until he converses with them.

**vēṇḍavum tārānāl inṟu muṟṟum** – we will perish on account of the one, who does not yield despite appealing to him “Return us our dresses mercifully”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that by using the term *tarānāl* instead of *kodānāl*, āḻvār joins himself with the group of herd-girls. He thinks that the pathos and connection which kriṣṇa and the herd-girls have for each other, are his benefits. The girls keep coming around kriṣṇa repeatedly because they think that it is because of his infatuation with them that he has gathered their dresses.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 2.10.3. Tadambadu tamarai

*tadam padu tāmaraip poygai kalakkividam padu nāgattai vāl paṟṟi īrttupadam padu paindalai mēl eḻap pāyndittuudambai asaittānāl inṟu muṟṟum ucciyil ninṟānāl inṟu muṟṟum*

**Пословный перевод:**

tadam padu – being expansive; tāmaraip poygai – pond with lotus flowers; kalakki – (jumping inside) agitating; vidam padu – as a result, rising with fury, spitting poison; nāgattai – snake, kāḷiyan; vāl paṟṟi iṟttu – pulling him by his tail; padam padu – having hoods; pai – spread out, in anger; talai mēl – on top of his head; eḻap pāyndittu – jumping in such a manner that the snake spat out poison; udambai – divine form; asaittānāl – we will perish today due to one who swayed his divine form and danced; ucciyil ninṟānāl – we will perish on account of one who stamped on that kāḷiyan until kāḷiyan grew tired and fell down at kriṣṇa’s feet, seeking refuge

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa jumped into the pond, which had plenty of lotus flowers and agitated it. Consequently, kāḷiyan, a snake, rose up in fury, spitting out poison. kriṣṇa pulled that kāḷiyan by his tail and jumped on top of his hoods which had spread out, due to his anger, making the snake to spit out poison. We will perish on account of the one who swayed his divine form, on top of that snake and danced. We will perish on account of the one who stamped that kāḷiyan such that the snake grew thin and fell down at kriṣṇa’s feet, seeking refuge.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that apart from attaining kriṣṇa or losing him, the herd-women were worried saying “He has jumped on kāḷiyan. What will befall him?” They are certain that they will exist only if he exists.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tadam …** – Before kāḷiyan entered it, the pond was famously known as “expansive lotus-pond”. Only later did it become fiery, poisonous pond. Just as it has been mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5-7-11 and 12 “*nipapāta hradē tatra sarpa rājasya vēgata*: l *tēnādipatadātatra kśōbhitassa mahāhrada*: ll” (Since he jumped into the pond with speed, after getting on top of the tree, waves formed in the centre of the pond and spread), kriṣṇa jumped with a high speed, into the pond, agitating it.

**vidam padu nāgattai vāl paṟṟi iṟttu** – kāḷiyan, who was lying inside the pond, got furious because it was agitated and rose up in anger, spitting poison. kriṣṇa, without considering the snake’s anger, pulled him by his tail.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kāḷiyan was malicious and kriṣṇa pulled him by his tail. He further says that kriṣṇa jumped on his spread-out hoods such that he spat out poison. Despite kriṣṇa jumping on to his spread-out heads, kāḷiyan, without becoming tired, moved his heads. The herd-women say that it was their fortune that kriṣṇa, without becoming tired, stood on top of kāḷiyan and danced.

**padam padu paindalai mēl eḻap pāyndu** – kriṣṇa jumped onto the expansive, spread-out hoods of kāḷiyan with a roar such that kāḷiyan spat out poison in anger.

**udambai asaittānāl inṟu muṟṟum** – Looking at kāḷiyan’s fury and agitation as well as kriṣṇa jumping on to his hoods, the favourable herd-men and herd-women, seeing from the bank of the pond, thought “kriṣṇa is going to get caught in the mouth of the snake; all of us will perish” and fell down, unconscious. They say that they will all perish on account of the one who was shaking his divine form on top of the snake.

**ucciyil ninṟānāl inṟu muṟṟum** – They say that they will all perish on account of the one who stood on the hoods, pressing it hard until the snake became weak and fell at his divine feet, seeking refuge. Through this, the women say that the one, who controlled the unfavourable one \[kāḷiyan\] and removed the worries of the favourable ones \[themselves\], by his activities \[of stealing their bangles and saris\] made them worried. Hence, they say that they will perish that day. The reason for saying a second time that they will perish is because of excessive anguish.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the pāsuram should be read as *padam padu paindalai mēl eḻap pāyndittup poygai kalakki, vidam padu nāgattai vāl paṟṟi īrttu, udambai asaittānāl inṟu muṟṟum, ucciyil ninṟānāl inṟu muṟṟum*. He says that kriṣṇa stood on top of its head and carried out *abhayap pradānam* \[giving refuge\] to his affectionate ones such that they did not fear. They say that on that day, their target will be realised \[viz. they will perish\].

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup>pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.10.4. Denugan avi

*dēnugan āvi seguttup pananganitān eṟinditta tadam perum tōḷinālvānavar kōn vida vanda maḻai taduttuānirai kāttānāl inṟu muṟṟum avai uyyak koṇḍānāl inṟu muṟṟum*

**Пословный перевод:**

dēnugan – the monster, dēnukan’s; āvi – life; seguttu – killing; panai kani – such that the fruits of the palm tree, which had been permeated by monster, shook and fell down (recall \[the ancient poem\] nannūl “panai mun … valivarin aipōyammum …”. In other words, if the word panai is followed by a surd such as ka, the syllable ai in panai will be replaced with the syllable am as mentioned in the ancient grammatical text of nannūl. Thus, panai + kani will become panam + kani, in other words, panangani); tān – he \[kriṣṇa\]; eṟinditta – threw (that dēnukan); tada peru – humongous; tōḷināl – with the shoulders; vānavar kōn – dēvendran \[head of celestial entities\]; vida – ordered; vanda – came to pour; maḻai – rain; taduttu – lifting a hill and preventing; A nirai – herds of cows; kāttānāl – we will perish on account of the one who protected \[the cows\]; avai – those cows; uyyak koṇḍānāl – we will perish on account of the one who uplifted them

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa threw the monster dēnukan on a palm tree which had been permeated by a monster, such that the life of that monster dēnukan ebbed. With those humongous shoulders, kriṣṇa lifted a mountain and prevented the pouring rain, which was ordered by dēvēndran to harm the herds and herd-folks, from harming them. We will perish today, on account of the one who protected those cows. We will perish today on account of the one who had uplifted those cows.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the herd-girls are manifesting their concern for the divine hands \[of kriṣṇa\], lifting the \[gōvardana\] hill.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**dēnugan …** – śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5.8.9 and 5.8.10 say “*gruhītvā bhramanēnaiva sō’mabarē gatajīvitam* l *tasminēva sacikśēpa dēnukam truṇarājani* ll *tata*:*palānyanēkāni tāḷāgrān nipatankara*: l *prutivyām pātayāmāsa mahāvātō kanāniva* ll” (that lord caught hold of the monster dēnukan, swirled him in the sky, due to which he lost his life in the sky itself. He fell on the palm tree and made the fruits which were on top of the tree to fall down, just as great wind makes dark clouds to pour rain). Just as it has been mentioned here, emperumān caught hold of a monster, dēnukāsuran, who had come to harm him, swirled him in the sky, killing him with that speed. He made the monster to fall on top of a palm tree which had been permeated by another monster, making the fruits which were on the tree to fall down. With such huge shoulders …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that dēnukan was totally dependent on kamsan and came to śrī gōkulam in order to harm kriṣṇa. kriṣṇa annihilated him and the palm tree in which another monster had pervaded, with his shoulders.

**vānavar …** – kriṣṇa had told the herd-folk to proffer food to \[gōvardana\] hill instead of to dēvēndran, the controller of celestial entities. Becoming angry on account of this, dēvēndran ordered puśkalāvartakam clouds to pour in śrī gōkulam such that all the herds of cows, along with the herd-men and herd-women would end up in the ocean. Since kriṣṇa had earlier told the herd-folk that gōvardana hill is their protector, he lifted the hill itself as an umbrella and protected the cows, which knew in their hearts the great benefit carried out by kriṣṇa on them. We will perish today on account of that kriṣṇa.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa thought “In the place where we live, there should be no scope for people to be servitors of other dēvatās”. Hence, he told the herd-folk “Offer these foods to gōvardana mountain, which provides grass and water to our cows”. The herd-folk were in agreement with this. śrī nandagōpar, hearing this, said “Look at his level of knowledge, when he is still a little child!” celebrating the wisdom of kriṣṇa. Once they offered the foods to the mountain, indran became extremely angry and ordered clouds such as puśkalāvartakam to ensure that “The village of herd-folk ends in ocean”. kriṣṇa lifted that mountain itself and protected the cows. Instead of saying that kriṣṇa protected the herd-men and herd-women, why is periyāḻvār saying that he protected the cows? kriṣṇa wanted to protect only those who had the intelligence \[to understand that kriṣṇa is the only protector\].

**avai …** – We will perish today, on account of the one who had uplifted those cows such that they did not have to engage with those rains. Through this, it is mentioned that the one who removed the danger which was to befall the entities to be protected, created pangs of separation in us and harmed us \[reference here is to the herd-women, whose bangles and saris were taken away by kriṣṇa\]. Hence, we will perish today.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here even after protecting the cows, since there was none who was appropriate to receive his mercy, he uplifted those cows themselves.

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.10.5. Aycciyar ceri

*āycciyar cēri aḷai tayir pāl uṇḍupērttavar kaṇḍu pidikkap pidiyuṇḍuvēyt tadam tōḷinār veṇṇey koḷ māttādu anguāppuṇḍu irundānāl inṟu muṟṟum adi uṇḍu aḻudānāl inṟū muṟṟum*

**Пословный перевод:**

cēri – village; āycciyar – herd-folk; aḷai – anchoring the churning staff; tayir – curd (kept for churning); pāl – milk (kept for heating); uṇḍu – consuming; pērttu – when going again for stealing butter; avar – those herd-women; pidikka – as they caught; pidi uṇḍu – getting caught in their hands; vēy – like bamboo; tada – having roundness; tōḷinār – having shoulders; veṇṇey – butter; koḷ māttādu – unable to steal; angu – in their houses; āppuṇḍu irundānāl – we will perish, on account of the one who remained tied down; adi uṇḍu aḻudānāl – we will perish, on account of the one who got beaten by them and cried

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa consumed curd, which was kept for churning, and milk, which was kept for heating, by herd-women in the village. When he tried to steal butter once again, he was caught by the herd-women, whose shoulders were rounded, like bamboo. We will perish today on account of the one, who was caught like that, and tied down in their houses. We will perish today, on account of the one who was beaten up by them and who cried.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**ācciyar cēri** – in the village of the herd-women

**aḷai tayir pāl uṇḍu** – they had kept churning staff inside curd, for churning it \[to take butter from it\]. They had also kept milk, in containers, for heating it. kriṣṇa would consume all these. Alternatively, the term *aḷai tayir* would also refer to curd in which, due to excessive desire, kriṣṇa had put his hand and started churning it.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that kriṣṇa would go to every street in that village, and enter every house, whether it had a gate or not, consuming food in all those houses. He would be wondering “Will they find me?” and keep going and coming. He would only keep seeing whether people are there but would not check whether his stomach is full or not.

**pērttu avar kaṇḍu pidikkap pidi uṇḍu** – When he tried to enter their houses once again, in order to steal butter, they caught him, by hiding themselves initially.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that due to repeatedly walking into their houses, the sounds of his footsteps as well as of the spherical balls from his waist cord falling down would be heard. Once the herd-women find out his presence, he would think “Even if we run, they would be able to find out from the sound of the spherical balls”. Instead of catching hold of the waist cord or closing their ears, he would close his ears and stand. When they catch him, he would remain caught, in their hands.

**vēy …** – being unable to steal butter from the houses of those herd-women, whose shoulders were fresh, rounded and long, like bamboo.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the herd-women would have kept the butter, high, close to the height of their shoulders. Unable to reach that height and not being satisfied with the curd and milk consumed already, kriṣṇa would look for a way to reach that butter. Even while being caught by them, due to his fondness for eating butter and looking for ways to get to that butter, he would remain without any movement. That would enable them to tie him down to a mortar.

**angu …** – we will perish today, on account of the one who was tied down by them.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa would be thinking that he could devise ways to reach that butter, when being tied down to the mortar since none will disturb him.

**adi uṇḍu …** – apart from being tied down, when they beat him \[for consuming their curd and milk\], he would start crying. We will perish on account of such kriṣṇa. Through this, they say that we will perish due to that kriṣṇa, who was obedient towards his favourable people such that they could tie him down, but was not obedient towards us and was acting in a difficult manner.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when the herd-women take a stick, he would start crying even if they say that they would not beat him with it. He would behave just the same way as he would, in his house \[when caught by yaśōdāp pirātti\].

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.10.6. Tallit talar

*taḷḷit taḷar nadai ittu iḷam piḷḷaiyāyuḷḷattin uḷḷē avaḷai uṟa nōkkikaḷḷattināl vanda pēycci mulai uyirtuḷḷac cuvaittanāl inṟu muṟṟum tuvakkaṟa uṇḍānāl inṟu muṟṟum*

**Пословный перевод:**

taḷḷi – being unsteady; taḷar nadai ittu – taking tentative steps \[like a child\], being unable to firmly keep the feet down while walking; iḷam piḷḷai āy – even while being a young child; uḷḷattin uḷḷē – in his heart; avaḷai – her (pūtanā); uṟa nōkki – looking at steadfastly, knowing that she is coming to harm; kaḷḷattināl vanda – one who came deceptively; pēycci – pūtanā’s; mulai – along with the milk from her bosom; uyir – her life too; tuḷḷa – such that she quivered; suvaittānāl – we will perish, on account of one who consumed it fully; tuvakku aṟa – without any connection with that poison \[that poison will not affect him in any way\]; uṇḍānāl – on account of the one who consumed, we will perish today

**Перевод:**

**Even when he was a little child, being unable to walk with firm steps, kriṣṇa, walking with tentative steps in an unsteady manner, looked at her \[pūtanā\] steadfastly, knowing that she had come to harm him. We will perish today, on account of the one who consumed the life fully, along with the milk. from the bosom of pūtanā, who came deceptively, such that she trembled. We will perish today, on account of the one who consumed her life, without any connection.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**taḷḷit taḷar nadai ittu** – being unable to take steps firmly, kriṣṇa took tentative steps, in an unsteady manner.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār is recalling the manner in which kriṣṇa annihilated pūtanā.

**iḷam piḷḷaiyāy** – as an innocent child; this says that he was such young that he did not even have the strength to walk steadily.

**uḷḷattin uḷḷē avaḷai uṟa nōkki** – looking at her steadfastly, knowing in his divine mind that “She is coming to harm me” without anyone knowing.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa decided in his mind that he will “Consume the milk along with the life of pūtanā, who came in a deceptive manner, such that she perishes, trembling and getting reduced to a skeleton” without anyone knowing about it. When he closed his eyes, as if he were sleeping, she took him in her arms and kept her bosom in his divine mouth. He carried out his task as he had planned.

**kaḷḷam …** – pūtanā hid her \[fiendish\] form and came deceptively in the form of kriṣṇa’s mother, yaśōdāp pirātti. We will perish today, on account of the one who consumed along with her milk, her life too, fully, without leaving behind anything such that pūtanā quivered.

**tuvakkaṟa …** – Even while he was consuming her poisoned milk, there was no effect of that poison on him. The herd women say “We will perish today, on account of such kriṣṇa”. Through this, it is clear that according to the herd-women, kriṣṇa, who protected himself from pūtanā such that his followers could exist, made himself rare for them, who are his followers. Hence, they say “We will perish today, because of him”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that while pūtanā came in a deceptive manner, with poison applied to her bosom, when kriṣṇa took that milk, will not the defect in the poison take effect? No, there was no effect on kriṣṇa, since he is the purest entity and did not have any shortcoming in his quality of being a child too. Since the pāsuram has also said that he had looked at steadfastly, knowing her intention of harming him, it could be interpreted that he was a grown up. No, there was no defect in his childishness in the incarnation that he had taken, while at the same time, being the supreme entity, he also knew as to what pūtanā’s intention was.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.10.7. Mavali velviyil

*māvali vēḷviyil māṇ uruvāyc cenṟumūvadi tā enṟu iranda immaṇṇinaiōradi ittu iraṇḍām adi tannilētāvadi ittānāl inṟu muṟṟum taraṇi aḷandānāl inṟu muṟṟum*

**Пословный перевод:**

māvali – mahābali’s; vēḷviyil – in the arena where he conducted the yāgam \[ritual, with agni, fire\]; māṇ uru āy – in the guise of a bachelor; senṟu – reaching; mū(nṟu) adi tā enṟu – saying ‘Grant me three steps of land with my feet’; iranda – seeking alms, and accepting water, symbolically; im maṇṇinai – this earth; ōr adi ittu – taking one step such that its \[earth’s\] entire area came under his control; iraṇḍām adi tannilē – with the second step; tāvu adi ittānāl – we will perish today, on account of the one who stretched such that all the upper worlds came under his control; taraṇi – worlds including earth; aḷandānāl – we will perish on account of the one who measured

**Перевод:**

**emperumān went in the guise of a bachelor, to the arena where mahābali, the emperor, was conducting rituals with agni \[fire\]. He sought alms from mahābali, saying “Give me three seps of land, measured with my feet” and accepted water as a symbol of mahābali’s acceptance. With one step, he brought the entire area of earth under his control. With the second step, which he took by stretching out his divine foot, he brought all the worlds in the upper regions, under his control. We will perish today, on account of the one who stretched like that. We will perish today, on account of the one who measured all the worlds, including earth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār says that that it is not only that kriṣṇa had annihilated his enemies, he had also carried out the activity of protecting his followers.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**māvali …** – mahābali seized the wealth of indra \[head of celestial entities\] through his strength; just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.8.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/09/thiruvaimozhi-9-8-7-kovagiya-mavaliyai/) “*kōvāgiya māvali*” (mahābali, who considered himself as he lord of all the three worlds), he thought that he is the king of all. He also had the indestructible quality of magnanimity. In such mahābali’s ritualistic arena …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *maṇ* includes all the fourteen worlds \[seven above the earth and seven, including earth, below\]. Through the term *ōradi ittu* emperumān severed the *anyaśēśatvam* \[being servitors to deities other than emperumān\] of those on earth \[and below\]. Through the term *iraṇḍāmadi* he removed the vanity derived out of *svātantryam* \[independent of others\] of those in the upper seven worlds.

**māṇ uruvāyc cenṟu** – Just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 5.1.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/07/periya-thirumozhi-5-1-2/) “*kaḷḷak kuṟaḷāy*” (going deceptively as a dwarf), in order to divest mahābali of all his wealth, emperumān took on the guise of a dwarf, stole the heart of mahābali through the beauty of his guise and his gait and made him do what he wanted.

**mūvadi tā enṟu iranda immaṇṇinai** – emperumān asked for three steps of land in order to make mahābali to grant immediately, without thinking, and in order to imprison him with the third step. The term *maṇ* is representative of all the worlds, including earth.

**ōradi …** – In the way he measured, he ensured that the entire expanse of earth \[including other words below it\] came under his first step. Through the second step …

**tāvadi …** – \[the herd-girls say\] We will perish today because of the one, who stretched his foot such that all the worlds in the upper regions came under his control.

**daraṇi …**– We will perish today on account of the one, who, notwithstanding the tenderness of his divine feet, measured all the worlds with those divine feet in order to fulfil the task of his follower \[indra\]. Through this, it is hinted that the one, who transformed himself in order to fulfil the expectations of his follower, did not carry out our expectations. Hence, we will perish today, because of him.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *daraṇi* is representative of all the worlds. *tāvadi* – the divine foot which went as per his divine mind. Alternatively, it refers to the divine foot which went with his divine mind following it.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.10.8. Talai tannambal

*tāḻai taṇṇāmbal tadam perum poygai vāyvāḻu mudalai valaip pattu vādippuṇvēḻam tuyar keda viṇṇōr perumānāyāḻi paṇi koṇḍānāl inṟu muṟṟum adaṟku aruḷ seydānāl inṟu muṟṟum*

**Пословный перевод:**

tāḻai – (on the bank of the pond) screw-pine (a type of plant); taṇ āmbal – (inside the pond) cool, water-lily; tada peru – being huge; poygai vāy – in the pond; vāḻum – being present; mudalai – crocodile; valai – in its net \[mouth\]; pattu – getting caught; vādippu uṇ – afflicted (vādippu – affliction); vēḻam – śrī gajēndrāḻvān’s; tuyar – mental agony; keda – to be removed; viṇṇōr – for nityasūris; perumān – being the controller; āy – conducting periya tiruvadi \[garuda\]; āḻi – through cakrāyudam \[divine disc\] (severed the crocodile and released from that imprisonment); paṇi koṇḍānāl – we will perish today, on account of the one who took the flower from gajēndran’s hand \[trunk\] and placed it on his divine foot; adaṟku – for that gajēndran; aruḷ seydānāl – we will perish today, on account of the one who showered his mercy like that

**Перевод:**

**Crocodile was inhabiting a huge pond, which had screw-pines on its bank and water-lilies inside. śrī gajēndrāḻvān got caught in the net of that crocodile \[net – crocodile’s mouth\] and suffered. To remove the mental agony of that gajēndrāḻvān, emperumān, who is the controller of nityasūris, went on garuda. He severed the head of crocodile with his divine disc, releasing gajēndran from his imprisonment, and placed the lotus flower, which gajēndran had carried in his trunk for a long time, on his divine feet. We will perish on account of such emperumān. We will perish on account of emperumān who showered his mercy on gajēndran like that.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār celebrates that even though emperumān had his sankalpam \[divine oath or pledge through which he carries out his orders\], unable to tolerate the sorrows of his followers, he protected śrī gajēndran \[an elephant\] on account of his purpose of activity and due to his overflowing mercy, though coming directly to protect gajēndrāḻvān may appear superfluous.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tāḻai …** – In a huge pond, which had plants such as *tāḻai* \[screw-pine\] on its banks and cool, water-lily inside, in the water. *tāḻai* is representative of all the plants which were growing on the banks of the pond. nammāḻvār too had mentioned in his [tiruvāimoḻi 3.5.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-5-1-moymmam-pumpozhil/) “*moymmām pūmboḻil poygai*” (in the pond, which had gardens having tightly packed, well-grown blossomed flowers) that the pond had gardens around, in which flowers were seen blossomed. *āmbal* – water-lily, is representative of all the flowering plants inside the pond. This is similar to [periya tirumoḻi 5.8.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/02/periya-thirumozhi-5-8-3/) “*vaigu tāmarai vāngiya vēḻam*” (śrī gajēndran plucked the lotus flower, present in the pond). Looking at the lotus flowers blossoming densely in the pond, in order to pluck the lotus \[and proffer to emperumān\], unaware that the wicked animal, crocodile, was present in the pond, the elephant entered the pond with affection.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here for *tadam perum poygai* that the pond had coolness due to the depth of the pond, *tadam* signifies expanse arising out of its breadth and *perum poygai* signifies greatness due to its length. Inside such a pond, a crocodile was roaming around and the elephant got caught by that crocodile.

**vāḻu mudalai valaippattu** – the elephant got caught in the net \[crocodile\] which was living there for a long time, with the thought “When will the elephant, which is going to release me from my curse, going to come?”

**vādip puṇ vēḻam tuyar keda** – Just as it has been said in śrī viṣṇu darmam 68-46 “*gaja ākarśatē tīrē grāha ākarśatē jalē*” (śrī gajēndrāḻvān was pulling towards the bank and the crocodile was pulling towards water), while the crocodile was pulling the elephant into water, gajēndran was pulling it towards the bank. This went on for a long time, as mentioned in śrī viṣṇu  darmam ślōkam “*divyam varśam sahasrakam*” (thousand years, as per the period of celestial count). In order that the mental agony of śrī gajēndrāḻvān that “We are unable to proffer the lotus at the divine feet before it loses its freshness” was removed …

**viṇṇōr perumānāy āḻi paṇi koṇḍānāl inṟu muṟṟum** – manifesting that he is the controller of nityasūris, emperumān went on his divine vehicle, garuda, killed the crocodile through his divine disc, as mentioned in śrī viṣṇu darmam 9-80 “*grāham cakrēṇa mādava*:” (śrīya: pati, consort of śrī mahālakśmi, tore the crocodile with his divine disc); he released śrī gajēndran from his prison, took the flower from his hand and placed it on his divine feet. The herd-girls say that they will perish on account of the one who carried out the above-mentioned activity.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that because emperumān was *viṇṇōr perumān*, his divine name of nārāyaṇa explains the reason for his being the causative factor for the worlds. Since the elephant called out to him, as said in siṟiya tirumadal “*nārāyaṇā oh maṇivaṇṇā nāgaṇaiyāy*” (Oh, nārāyaṇa! Oh, one with blue gemstone like complex! Oh, one who is lying on the serpent-bed!) emperumān rushed to the bank of the pond as said in [periya tirumoḻi 2.3.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/08/periya-thirumozhi-2-3-9/) “*ānaiyin tuyaram tīrap puḷḷūrndu senṟu ninṟu āḻi tottānai*” (emperumān, in order to remove the distress of gajēndrāḻvān, went on garuda, to the banks of the pond, stood and then severed the crocodile through his divine disc) and removed gajēndran’s agony. By saying *viṇṇōr perumānāy  āḻi paṇi koṇḍān*, āḻvār emphasises the enjoyability of nityasūris \[with emperumān\] and that the existence of all the entities in the worlds is because of his existence \[since he is the *antaryāmi* \[in-dwelling soul\] of all entities, existence of all the entities arises only if emperumān exists; without him, nothing will exist\]. Just as mentioned in śrī vaikuṇṭha stavam 36 “*iccāda Eva*” (everything is carried out through emperumān’s wish), gajēndran survived for such a long time, trapped by the crocodile in his net, only because of emperumān’s wish. Just as it is said in “*dig balam kśatriya balam*” \[this is from śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 56.23, when king viśvāmitra realises that his strength as a warrior is inferior to the strength of the spiritual power of sage vasiśta\], gajēndrāḻvān left the path of *bhakti* \[devotion\] and came into the path of *prapatti* \[act of surrendering to emperumān\]. He was capable enough to call out to emperumān to come and protect him. While draupadi surrendered to emperumān \[in the court of dritarāśtra, when pulled by duśśāsan\], since she did not say “*vārāy ennāridarai nīkkāy*” \[Please come and remove my great distress\] emperumān did not come in person \[unlike the case of gajēndrāḻvān who said these words, as mentioned in siṟiya tirumadal\]. nammāḻvār, in his [tiruvāimoḻi 3.1.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-1-9-mazhungadha/) had said “*maḻungāda vainnudiya cakkara nal …*” (having a beautiful divine disc, which is not blunt, which has a mouth and is sharp). When this pāsuram was being recited in the temple, when the last line was recited, where nammāḻvār asks whether emperumān’s radiance vouldn’t have disappeared if he had not come in person to save śrī gajēndrāḻvān, a śrī vaiṣṇava, siṟiya ātkoṇḍār said “It would have disappeared” twice. This has been cited to affirm that emperumān came when śrī gajēndrāḻvān called out to him to come and remove his agony while he did not come when draupadi too called out to him, since she did not ask him to come and remove her agony. Through the term *āḻi paṇi koṇḍān* \[emperumān killed the crocodile with the help of his divine disc\] it is clear that he did not take the help of one who was proffering flower daily to him \[reference here is to śrī gajēndrāḻvān who was proffering lotus to him every day; emperumān accepted servitude from him, but did not utilise him for annihilating crocodile\].

**adaṟku aruḷ …** – Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.5.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-5-1-moymmam-pumpozhil/) “*kaimmāvukku aruḷ seyda*” (one who bestowed his mercy on the elephant), the herd-girls say “We will perish today on account of the one, who showered his mercy on the elephant like that”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that through the term *adaṟku aruḷ seydānāl*, āḻvār says that śrī gajēndrāḻvān caried out *svagatasvīkāra prapatti* \[carrying out surrendering through one’s efforts and not through emperumān\]. Since he carried out surrendering through his efforts, he had to sink until only his trunk was visible. It was then that emperumān came and showered his mercy on the elephant \[in our sampradāyam, we should carryout *paragatasvīkāra prapatti*, viz. surrendering through emperumān’s effort. In other words, we should not think that we have surrendered to emperumān because of our effort, but that emperumān showered his mercy on us and made us to reach him\].

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.10.9. Vanattu elunda

*vānattu eḻunda maḻai mugil pōl engumkānattu mēyndu kaḷittu viḷaiyādiēnattu uruvāy idanda immaṇṇinaitānattē vaittānāl inṟū muṟṟum daraṇi idandānāl inṟu muṟṟum*

**Пословный перевод:**

vānattu – in the sky; eḻunda – rising with water; maḻai mugil pōl – like great rain bearing clouds; ēnam uru āy – with the form of a boar; kānattu – in the forest; engum – roaming in all the places; mēyndu – eating foods such as kōraik kiḻangu (sedge-tuber); kaḷittu – with pride; viḷaiyādi – playing; idanda – removing from the walls of the universe; immaṇṇinai – this earth; tānattē – in their respective place; vaittānāl – we will perish on account of the one who placed it; daraṇi idandānāl – we will perish on account of the one who uplifted it

**Перевод:**

**emperumān took the form of a great boar, which looked like a great rain-bearing cloud rising up in the sky. He roamed around, all over the forests, digging up and eating foods such as kōraik kiḻangu (sedge-tuber). With pride, he played merrily and dug out earth from the walls of the universe. We will perish on account of the one who kept the earth, with all its lands in their respective place. We will perish on account of the one who uplifted the earth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that āḻvār recalls the ability of śrī varāham \[the great boar\], which is beyond the abilities of human species.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vānattu eḻunda maḻai mugil pōl** – Like the rain bearing clouds, which rose up in the sky. Through this, the complexion of the divine form has been mentioned. *idanda* – removing from the walls of the universe.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that through the term *vānattu eḻunda maḻai mugil pōl*, the complexion of emperumān’s divine form was mentioned. Alternatively, it would refer to the eminence of the clouds which have risen. Through the term *pōl*, the equivalence is shown; through the term *eḻunda*, the greatness of great boar, over the clouds, is shown.

**engum kānattu mēyndu** – roaming around, in the forest, without any fear of enemies and sustaining on tubers such as *kōraik kiḻangu*.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *engum* implies that without the presence of any hurdle such as lions, tigers etc, the boar roamed around everywhere.

**kaḷittu viḷaiyādi** – playing, with the pride of the species \[of boar\]

**ēnattu uruvāy** – without stepping back from water or mud

**idanda …** – digging out the earth, which has got stuck to the walls of the universe, just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāīmoḻi 7.4.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/thiruvaimozhi-7-4-3-nanrila/) “*nānṟilavēḻ maṇṇum dānattavē*” (picking up the earth such that the seven islands within it did not move even a little bit). We will perish on account of the one who kept the earth with all its lands in their original places, without any movement.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the pāsuram should be rearranged as *vānattu eḻunda maḻai mugil pōlē ēnattu uruvāy tān idantānāl inṟu muṟṟum, idanda immaṇṇinai tānattē vaittuk kānattu mēyndu kaḷittu viḷaiyādinānāl inṟu muṟṟum* to get the sequential meanings.

Alternatively, he says  
*vānam …* – like the rain bearing clouds which rose up in the sky, like the monsoon clouds  
*engum* – in all the places  
*kānattu mēyndu* – grazing in the gardens  
*kaḷittu viḷaiyādi* – immersing in the deluge of ocean, playing with a huge pride

*ēnattu uruvāy idanda immaṇṇinai* – as a great boar which could not be contained in the upper worlds, digging out the earth from the walls of the universe, keeping them back in their respective position, just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.4.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/thiruvaimozhi-7-4-3-nanrila/) “*ēḻ maṇṇum – nānṟila tānattavē*” (the seven islands within earth did not move even a little bit; they were placed in their original positions)

*daraṇi idandānāl* – just as it has been mentioned as “*idanda immaṇ*” (this earth which has been dug out), the one who dug out earth.

In this interpretation, the pāsuram should be rearranged as *maḻaimugil pōl ēnattu uruvāy vānattu eḻunda kānattu engum mēyndu kaḷittu viḷaiyādit taraṇi idandānāl inṟu muṟṟum, idanda immaṇṇinai tānattē vaittānāl inṟu muṟṟum*, to get sequential meanings.

**daraṇi …** – We will perish on account of the one who uplifted the earth which had got immersed \[in the water of deluge\]

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 2.10.10. Angamalak kannan

*angamalak kaṇṇan tannai asōdaikkumangai nallārgaḷ tām vandu muṟaippattaangavar sollaip puduvaik kōn battan solingivai vallavarkku ēdam onṟu illaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mangai – youthful, by their age; nallārgaḷ tām – girls, who are friendly towards kriṣṇa; am kamalam – like a beautiful reddish lotus; kaṇṇan tannai – regarding kaṇṇan, who has divine eyes; angu vandu – coming to her house; asōdaikku – to yaśōdāp pirātti; muṟaippatta – complained; sollai – words; puduvai – for śrī villibuttūr; kōn – one, who is the controller; battan – mercifully composed by periyāḻvār; sol ivai – these pāsurams; ingu – even while they are in this samsāram; vallavarkku – those who are capable of reciting; ēdam – blemish; onṟu – even a little bit; illai – will disappear such that it is non-existent

**Перевод:**

**Young girls, who have affection towards kriṣṇa, came to yaśōdāp pirātti’s house and complained about kriṣṇa, who has beautiful, reddish-lotus like eyes. periyāḻvār, who is the controller of śrī villibuttūr, mercifully composed those words into these pāsurams. For those who recite these pāsurams, even while they are still present in this samsāram, even a little bit of blemish will not be present, disappearing fully.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) In this last pāsuram of the decad, āḻvār mentions the benefit which will accrue to those who recite the pāsurams and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**angamalak kaṇṇan tannai** – Regarding kriṣṇa, who has eyes which are reddish, blossomed and fresh, like a beautiful lotus flower.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says additionally, in his svāpadēśam, that kriṣṇa’s divine eyes hint at his supreme nature.

**aśodāikku** – to his mother, yaśōdāp pirātti

**mangai nallārgaḷ tām** – girls, who are young in terms of their age and who have affection towards kriṣṇa

**angu vandu muṟaippatta** – coming to her house and complaining to her, manifesting their total involvement

**avar sollai** – their words. The pāsuram should be rearranged as *mangai nallārānavargaḷ tām – angamalakkaṇṇan tannai paṟṟa – angu – vandu – asōdaikku – muṟaippatta sollai* to get the sequential meanings.

**puduvaikkōn battan sol-ivai** – their words of complaint. These pāsurams, which have been mercifully composed by periyāḻvār, who is the controller of śrī villibuttūr …

**ingu vallavarkku** – for those who are capable of reciting, in this world, with his pathos …

**ēdam onṟu illaiyē** – that which is considered as blemish, will disappear, without even a little bit being present.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says at the end that the pāsuram should be rearranged as *mangai nallārgaḷ avar tām angamalak kaṇṇan tannai asōdaikku angu vandu muṟaippatta sollai puduvaikkōn battan sollivai ingum vallavarkku ēdam onṟū illai* to get the sequential meanings.

This brings us to the end of the second centum.

We shall next consider the pravēsam of the next tirumoḻi.

## 3.1.1. 3.1.1 -Tanner ayiram

*tannēr āyiram piḷḷaigaḷōdu taḷar nadai ittu varuvānponnēy neyyodu pāl amudu uṇḍu oru puḷḷuvan poyyē tavaḻumminnēr nuṇṇidai vanja magaḷ kongai tunja vāy vaitta pirānēannē unnai aṟindu koṇḍēn unakku anjuvan ammam taravē*

**Пословный перевод:**

than – for him; nēr – matching; āyiram piḷḷaigaḷōdu – with a thousand boys; taḷar nadai ittu – taking tottering walk; varuvān – one who comes; pon ēy – having the complexion of gold; neyyodu – along with ghee; pāl amudu – enjoyable milk too; uṇḍu – consuming; oru – unique; puḷḷuvan – as a mischievous child; poyyē – falsely; tavaḻum – as one who is crawling; nuṇ – subtle; vanja magaḷ – the deceptive pūtanā; tunja – to die; kongai – on her bosom; vāy vaitta – one who kept the divine mouth and consumed; pirānē – oh, the benefactor; annē – ammē! (a word which is mentioned in fear); unnai – you, who I had considered as my son all along; aṟindu koṇḍēn – I know today that you are the difficult-to-attain lord; unakku – for you; ammam tara – to give milk; anjuvan – I am afraid

**Перевод:**

**You had come with a tottering gait, along with a thousand herd-boys, who matched you. You had consumed ghee, which has the complexion of gold, along with enjoyable milk, crawling in a falsified manner, with unique mischievous nature. pūtanā, the fiend, had come in a deceptive way with a waist as thin as lightning. You killed her, keeping your divine mouth on her bosom. Oh, my lord! ammē! I considered you as my son, but I know today that you are the difficult-to-attain lord. I am afraid to give you \[my bosom\] milk.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tannēr …** – It is well known that “When kriṣṇa incarnated in tiruvāyppādi, a thousand children, matching him, were born at the same time”. \[*arumpada viḷakkam* \[explanatory notes for the vyākhyānam\] says the following: Just as it has been mentioned in paramasamhitā “*yēna yēna dātā gaccati tēna tēna sahagaccati*” (wherever emperumān goes, the nityasūris too go, carrying out kainkaryam), it is possible that nityasūris too incarnated in tiruvāyppādi at the same time\]. It was with those thousand children, who were matching him in their birth, upbringing, age, knowledge and mutual friendship that kriṣṇa would take tottering steps. As mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 18.27 “*bālyāt prabruti susnigda*:” \[lakśmaṇa was very friendly with śrī rāma right from his childhood\], just as lakśmaṇa couldn’t sustain himself without śrī rāma, these thousand children, right from the time of their birth, could not sustain themselves without kriṣṇa. Since they were friendly all the time and roaming around together all the time, it could be said that kriṣṇa took tottering steps with these thousand children. This verse should be considered as yaśōdāp pirātti calling out to kriṣṇa “Oh, one who comes with tottering steps with a thousand children!”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, additionally that even though the place, day and time of birth may be the same for these thousand children, as those of kriṣṇa, it is only when they too walk with tottering steps that they could be termed as *tannēr āyiram* \[a thousand children who matched him\].

**ponnēy ney pālodu amudu uṇḍu** – ghee was golden coloured since it was prepared with freśy made butter. Along with that, consuming tasty milk too…

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that along with ghee, which was having golden colour, kriṣṇa consumed normal milk.

**oru puḷḷuvan poyyē tavaḻum** – *puḷḷuvam* refers to a lie which appears as if it were the truth. When a person had taken food, if he says that he has not had food, it would appear like truth. The term *oru puḷḷuvan* refers to kriṣṇa who is unique in indulging in stealing \[milk, curd, butter etc\].

**poyyē tavaḻum** – When a child has already started taking tottering steps, if the child crawls, it would appear like a mischievous act. Hence, the pāsuram says *poyyē tavaḻum* \[even when he has started walking, kriṣṇa is crawling now, due to his mischievous act\]. Here too, yaśōdāp pirātti is calling out to kriṣṇa “Oh, one who is crawling mischievously!”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa could be, just as it has been mentioned in tiruvāimoḻi 10.4.5 “*mey pōlum poy vallan*”, truthful to his followers while at the same time, he could be untruthful to the others.

**minnēr …** – Since pūtanā came in the guise of yaśōdāp pirātti \[in order to nurse kriṣṇa\], she came with a slender waist, which appeared like lightning. Oh, one who became our benefactor by keeping your divine mouth on her bosom and consuming her life! Here, the term ‘benefit’ refers to kriṣṇa’s act of protecting himself, who is the life for all the worlds, by killing pūtanā who had come to kill him.

**annē** – This is a variant of *ammē*, a word which is used in order to express fear.

**unnai aṟindu koṇḍēn** – Earlier I considered you as my child and thought that the milk etc, which I gave you, was nurturing you. Since your activities are beyond the capabilities of human species, just as it has been said in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.1.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/06/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-1-1-7/) “*āyar puttiran allan arum deyvam*” (He is not the son of śrī nandagōpar; he is the most-difficult-to-attain sarvēśvaran), I now know very well that you are not a herd-boy and that the food stuffs which I had given you are not those which sustain you.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār was afraid as to whether kriṣṇa was *anaśnan* \[one who does not eat\], just as it has been mentioned in muṇḍaka upaniśat. Even though kriṣṇa himself had said in [bhagavad gītā 9.24](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/9-26/) “*aśnāmi*” (I eat), he is not able to accept that.  āren’t nectar and milk ordained for celestial entities and humans, respectively? Will one, who takes nectar, not take milk? Since kriṣṇa’s eminence was fully manifested, his supremacy was also manifested. It is pertinent to recall [tirunedundāṇḍakam pāsuram 21](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/10/thirunedunthandakam-21-part-1/) “*avarai nām tēvar enṟū anjinōmē*” (We were afraid that he is the supreme entity}. In the earlier pāsuram \[2.10\], his supremacy was indicated through the verse “*āḻi paṇi koṇḍānāl*” \[emperumān killed the crocodile through his divine disc\].

**unakku anjuvan amman taravē**– I will be scared to give you, who are like this, my milk. Though the word *ammam* is not normally used with grown up children, she repeats the word which he has used, just as using the word *tavaḻugai poy* \[his act of crawling is a false act\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says at the end that the pāsuram should be rearranged as *tannēr āyiram piḷḷigaḷōdu taḷar nadai ittu varuvān, ponnēy neyyodu – poyyē tavaḻum oru puḷḷuvan vāy vaitta pirānē annē unnai aṟīndu koṇḍēn, unakku anjuvan ammam tara* to get the sequential meaning. He further says that the verses which are in third person are to be considered to have been spoken in the second person \[such as yaśōdāp pirātti telling kriṣṇa in the third person that he was crawling mischievously, along with a thousand friends of his etc\].

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.1.2. Pon pol manjanam

*pon pōl manjanam ātti amudu ūttip ponēn varum aḷavu ippālvan bārac cagadam iṟac cādi vadakkilagam pukkirundumin pōl nuṇṇidaiyāḷ oru kannigaiyai vēṟṟu uruvam seydu vaittaanbā unnai aṟīndu koṇḍēn unakku anjuvan amman taravē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pon pōl – like gold (such that the divine form is manifested splendorously); manjanam ātti – giving a divine bath; amudu ūtti – making you to consume food; pōnēn – I had gone to yamunā river, to take a bath; varum aḷavu ippāl – before I could return; val – being strong; bāram – being heavy; sagadam – śakatam (wheel); iṟa – to be destroyed such that it was in smithereens; sādi – kicking it with your divine feet; vadakkil – to the north of this house; agam – house; pukku irundu – entering; min pōl – like lightning; nuṇ – being subtle \[that thin\]; idaiyāḷ – one who had waist; oru kanniyai – a youthful girl; vēṟu uruvam seydu vaitta – one who changed the form, through the marks of finger nails etc; anbā – oh, one who has affection such that you would fall head over heels on any entity who you like!; unnai – you, who I had considered as my son all along; aṟindu koṇḍēn – I know today that you are the difficult-to-attain lord; unakku – for you; ammam tara – to give milk; anjuvan – I am afraid

**Перевод:**

**I had given you a bath such that you were shining like gold. I had given you food and then left for yamunā river in order to tale a bath. By the time I returned, you had kicked a wheel, which was strong and heavy, with your divine feet such that it was broken to smithereens. You had entered a house, which is to the north of our house and changed a girl, who had a waist which was like lightning, by uniting with her. Oh, one has the affection to fall head over heels on anything which you like! I know today that you are the difficult-to-attain lord. I am afraid to give you \[my bosom\] milk.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**pon …** – I \[yaśōdāp pirātti\] had, after giving kriṣṇa a divine bath such that the beauty of his divine form shines, and giving him milk from my bosom, went to the banks of river yamunā, in order to have a bath. Before I returned …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that yaśōdāp pirātti had given him a bath with pure gold, which was splendorous without any dirt.

**van bārac cagadam iṟac cādi** – kriṣṇa, realising that there was a delay in getting milk from yaśōdāp pirātti, started crying and kicking his feet. A strong, heavy wheel, got caught between the divine feet which were kicking, and broke into smithereens.

**vadakkil agam pukku irundu** – entered a house, which was located to the north of yaśōdāp pirātti’s house.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *vadakku* refers to devotion, viz. those who attempt to attain emperumān through the path of devotion, with their efforts.

**min pōl nuṇṇidaiyāḷ oru kanniyai** – a girl, who was young and who had a slender waist, like lightning.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the girl was friendly towards kriṣṇa, had slender waist and was without any match.

**vēṟṟuruvam seydu vaitta** – changing her form due to indulging in playful activities with her. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa had changed her form by scratching her with his finger nails.

**anbā** – Oh, one who has affection such that when you see anything, you fall head-over-heels on it. This indicates his mischievousness,

**unnai aṟindu koṇḍēn** – I knew truly about you that “You are not one among us, in the clan of herd-people and that you are different from us”

**unakku anjuvan ammam taravē** – Hence, I am scared to give you milk.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.1.3. Kummayattodu venney

*kummāyattodu veṇṇey viḻungik kudattayir sāyttup parugipoymmāya marudāna asuraraip ponṟuvittu inṟu nī vandāyimmāyam valla piḷḷai nambī unnai en maganē enbar ninṟārammā unnai aṟindu koṇḍēn unakku anjuvan ammam taravē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kummāyattodu – along with lentils which had been cooked to a soft state; veṇṇey – butter; viḻungi – swallowing them; kudam – filled up in pots; tayir – curd; sāyttu – tilted with the pots; parugi – consuming; poy māyam – even falsified state to appear amazing; marudu Ana – stood as maruda \[arjuna\] trees; asurarai – monsters; ponṟuvittu – making them to snap and fall down; inṟu – now; nī vandāy – you came, like one who hasn’t done anything; immāyam – such amazing activities; valla – capable of doing; piḷḷai nambī – Oh, one who is complete with your qualities of being a child!; unnai – you, who are like this; ninṟār – those who are neutral; en magan enbar – will say that you are my son \[here, the term “my”refers to yaśōdāp pirātti\]; ammā – oh, one who is the lord for all!; unnai – you, who I had considered as my son all along; aṟindu koṇḍēn – I know today that you are the difficult-to-attain lord; unakku – for you; ammam tara – to give milk; anjuvan – I am afraid

**Перевод:**

**You \[yaśōdāp pirātti, addressing kriṣṇa\] had swallowed butter along with well-cooked lentils. You had tilted pots containing curd and consumed the curd. You had snapped and felled two maruda trees pervaded by monsters, who had made \[their\] false \[state of being tress\] to appear as amazing. You have come now, as if you had done nothing. Oh, one who is complete with the activities of a child, like these! Those who are neutral will say that you are my son. Oh, one who is the lord of all! I know today that you are the difficult-to-attain lord. I am afraid to give you \[my bosom\] milk.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kummāyam …** – Swallowing butter along with lentils which had been cooked very softly.

**kudat tayir …** – tilting curd which had been filled up in pots, along with the pots and consuming the curd too

**poy …** – two monsters had pervaded two *maruda* trees \[Indian laurel trees\], making it appear that they were indeed trees, in an amazing manner. You had gone through them, snapping them and making them to fall down, killing them.

**inṟu nī vandāy** – You had come, as if you had not done anything.

**immāyam valla piḷḷai nambī** – Oh, one who is complete with your qualities of being a child, capable of carrying out such amazing activities!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that kriṣṇa is complete with the qualities of such mischievous acts and his child-like activities.

**unnai en maganē enbar ninṟār** – Those who do not know about your capabilities, will say that you are my son

**ammā unnai aṟindu koṇḍēn** – Unlike those people, I know truly that “You are not my son” and that “You are the lord of all”

**unakku …** – Hence, I am afraid to give you milk.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.
