## 3.1.4. Maiyar kan

*maiyār kaṇ mada āycciyar makkaḷai maiyanmai seydu avar pin pōykoyyār pūndugil paṟṟit tani ninṟu kuṟṟam pala pala seydāypoyyā unnaip puṟam pala pēsuva puttagattukkuḷa kēttēnaiyā unnai aṟindu koṇḍēn unakku anjuvan ammam taravē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mai Ar – decorated with black \[eye\] pigment; kaṇ – having eyes; madam – having the quality of simplicity; āycciyar makkaḷai – herd-girls; maiyanmai seydu – making them infatuated; avar pin pōy – going behind them; koy Ar – being full of folds; pū – beautiful; tugil – saris; paṟṟi – holding on; tani ninṟu – standing alone; pala pala – countless; kuṟṟam – misciefs; seydāy – you had carried out; poyyā – oh, one who is mischievous!; unnai – regarding you; pēsuva – words spoken by others; puṟam pala – wicked details; puttagattukku – to write a book; uḷa – being appropriate; kēttēn – I heard with my ears; aiya – Oh, one who is the lord of misciefs!; unnai – you, who I had considered as my son all along; aṟindu koṇḍēn – I know today that you are the difficult-to-attain lord; unakku – for you; ammam tara – to give milk; anjuvan – I am afraid

**Перевод:**

**You had made herd-girls, who have eyes decorated with black pigment and who are simple, to be infatuated with you. You had gone behind them, held on to their saris which were full of folds and carried out countless misciefs, being alone. Oh, one who is mischievous! I have heard with my ears, wicked details regarding you from others, which are appropriate to write as a book. Oh, one who is the lord of misciefs! I know today that you are the difficult-to-attain lord. I am afraid to give you \[my bosom\] milk.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**maiyār …** – women who have their eyes decorated with black pigment, who have simplicity which is primary among the qualities of *ātmā* and who have taken birth in the herd-clan

**maiyanmai seydu** – making them infatuated such that they are friendly with you \[reference to kriṣṇa\] through your beauty and that they are not under the control of \[their\] mothers et al.

**avar pin pōy** – going behind them

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that gazing at the beauty of their dress and the beauty of their gait, kriṣṇa went behind the herd-girls, holding on to their pleats. *pūndugil* – soft dress.

**koyyār pūndugil paṟṟi** – catching hold of their dresses which have plenty of pleats. Through this, it is stated that kriṣṇa went behind the girls, holding on to the pleats of their saris.

**tani ninṟu kuṟṟam pala pala seydāy** – standing in secluded places, you indulged in activities in countless numbers, which cannot be spoken of. When kriṣṇa asked yaśōdāp pirātti “What is this? I did not do any mischief. Did you see?” she says …

**poyyā …** – Oh, one who indulges in misciefs! I have heard from others about all the wicked details indulged in by you, which would be enough to write as a book.  When kriṣṇa counters this, saying “Is whatever that they say and whatever that you hear the truth and what I say, lies?” she says …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa retorts saying “I have not committed any mischief”. yaśōdāp pirātti calls him “*poyyā*” \[one who tells lies\]. kriṣṇa says “Is what you say as *liar*, the truth?” she says “Is it only I who am saying this? I have heard from others such a lot about you that they cannot be contained even in a book” to which he says “Is it only what you say and what the others say which are to be taken as truth? Is what I say alone, false?” she says …

**aiya** – She celebrates him saying “What a clarity of thoughts you have!” Alternatively, this could also mean that she says that he is the lord of misciefs.

**unnai aṟindu koṇḍēn** – I have learnt that you are one, having activities which are beyond this world.

**unakku …** – Hence, I will be afraid to give you milk.

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.1.5. Muppodum kadaindu

*muppōdum kadaindu īṇḍiya veṇṇeyinōdum tayirum viḻungikappāl āyargaḷ kāvil koṇarnda kalattodu sāyttup parugimeyppāl uṇḍu aḻu piḷḷaigaḷ pōla nī vimmi vimmi aḻuginṟaappā unnai aṟindu koṇḍēn unakku anjuvan ammam taravē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mūnṟu pōdum – at all three times of morning, noon and evening; kadaindu – churned; īṇḍiya – accumulated; veṇṇeyinōdu – along with butter; tayirum – curd too; viḻungi – consumed; āyargaḷ – herd-people; kappāl – on shoulders; kāvil – pole, with vessels hung from the ends, for carrying burdens; koṇarnda – milk, brought; kalattodu – along with the vessel; sāyttu – tilted; parugi – consumed; mey pāl – bosom milk, secreted in the body; uṇḍu – consuming, for sustaining; aḻu – crying, when that \[bosom milk\] is not obtained; piḷḷaigaḷ pōla – like children; nī – you; vimmi vimmi – sobbing repeatedly; aḻuginṟa – crying for my bosom milk; appā – oh, my lord!; unnai – you, who I had considered as my son all along; aṟindu koṇḍēn – I know today that you are the difficult-to-attain lord; unakku – for you; ammam tara – to give milk; anjuvan – I am afraid

**Перевод:**

**You \[referring to kriṣṇa\] had consumed butter, which had been accumulated by churning curd, three times a day, along with curd. You had tilted vessels containing milk, carried on their shoulders, through poles, by herd-people, by tilting the vessels. When you do not get to consume my \[yaśōdāp pirātti, referring to herself\] bosom milk, secreted in my body, you sob and cry like children who have been denied it. Oh, my lord! I know today that you are the difficult-to-attain lord. I am afraid to give you \[my bosom\] milk.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**muppōdum …** – In tiruvāyppādi \[śrī gōkulam\], the activities of milking \[the cows\], setting \[curd\] and churning \[to get butter\] would be continuous. kriṣṇa would consume the butter which had accumulated during churning, in the morning, noon and evening times, along with the thick curd  which had got set during those times.

**kappāl …** – he would also consume milk, brought by herd-men on their shoulders with the help of poles, with milk contained in vessels hung from the ends of the poles, by tilting the vessels.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that the fact that herd-men brought it on their shoulders with the help of poles makes it evident that it is milk which they had brought \[though the pāsuram does not explicitly mention that it is milk\].

**meyppāl …** – you would also consume the bosom milk, secreted in my body, as your sustaining material. If that milk is not available, you would cry, sobbing, just like children who have not had milk.

**appā unnai aṟindu koṇḍēn** – Oh, the eminent one who has these activities which are beyond human levels of capabilities! I have come to know that “You do not belong to the species of human beings”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that earlier \[in the first pāsuram\], āḻvār had said *annē* \[which is the same as *ammē*, mother\]. Here, he calls kriṣṇa as *appā* \[father\]. Thus, it is clear that emperumān is āḻvār’s mother as well as father. Earlier \[in the first pāsuram\], he had spoken about *poyppāl* \[the false milk (poisoned milk)\] from the fiend. āḻvār remembers that and speaks about *meyppāl* \[milk secreted by the body\] here.

**unakku …** – Hence, I will be scared to give you \[my bosom\] milk.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.1.6. Karumbar neelvayal

*karumbār neeḷ vayal kāy kadirc cennelaik kaṟṟānirai maṇḍit tinnavirumbāk kanṟu onṟu koṇḍu viḷangani vīḻa eṟinda pirānēsurumbār men kuḻal kanni oruttikkuc cūḻvalai vaittut tiriyumarambā unnai aṟindu koṇḍēn unakku anjuvan ammam taravē*

**Пословный перевод:**

neeḷ vayal – in the expansive fields; karumbu Ar – rising like sugarcane \[plants\]; kāy – tender grains; kadir – having ears \[crops\]; sennel – grains of paddy; kanṟu A nirai – herds of cows, with calves; maṇḍi – falling over \[kneeling down\]; tinna – even as they were grazing; virumbā – not interested in eating; onṟu – one; kanṟu koṇḍu – with a calf; vīḻa – to scatter and fall down; eṟinda – one who threw \[that calf\]; pirānē – oh, the benefactor!; surumbu Ar – settled upon by beetles \[due to desire on honey present in flowers\]; mel kuḻal – having soft locks; kanni oruttikku – for a young girl; sūḻ – snaring, without failing; valai – divine eyes, which are the net; vaittu – keeping; tiriyum – one who is roaming around; arambā – oh, the mischievous one!; unnai – you, who I had considered as my son all along; aṟindu koṇḍēn – I know today that you are the difficult-to-attain lord; unakku – for you; ammam tara – to give milk; anjuvan – I am afraid

**Перевод:**

**Herds of cows, with their calves, were bending and eating the ears of reddish paddy crops, which look like sugar cane plants \[they were that tall\] and had grown on an expansive field. One calf was not interested in grazing the field. Holding that calf in your \[reference here is to kriṣṇa\] hands, you had thrown it on the fruits of wood apple such that the fruits fell down in a scatter. Oh, the benefactor! Oh, the mischievous one, who is roaming around, with the intention of ensnaring a young girl through your divine eyes, which are like a net! I know today that you are the difficult-to-attain lord. I am afraid to give you \[my bosom\] milk.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**karumbu …** – reddish paddy crops which had grown as tall as sugar cane plants in an expansive field, with tender grains.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that this term could refer to either that the paddy crops had grown tall like sugar cane or that there was no distinction between the two. They both looked alike

**kaṟṟānirai** – cows, together with calves.

**maṇḍittinna** – even as they desirously started eating, falling over one another

**virubāk kanṟu onṟu koṇḍu** – taking hold of a calf, which was not desirous of eating, though it was acting as if it were also eating.

**viḷangani vīḻa eṟinda pirānē** – oh, benefactor, who threw \[the calf\] at attractive fruits of wood apple such that they fell down in a scattered way! One monster had stood like a calf while another monster appeared like a wood apple fruit. Knowing this, kriṣṇa threw one on the other, killing them both. It is this benefit \[of protecting himself from inimical entities\] which is narrated here.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that through this, it is clear that those who hide themselves could be seen in all situations. He says that in śrī rāmāyaṇam, when mārīca \[a demon, rāvaṇa’s uncle\] came in the form of a deer, the other deer, after going near him, smelt his real nature, and became bewildered. It was because the seven bulls appeared to have been pervaded by monsters that kriṣṇa too annihilated them \[at the time of marrying nappinnaip pirātti\]. This calf was not grazing the fields, unlike the other calves. There was no necessity for the *sarvajñan* \[omniscient entity, viz. emperumān\] to annihilate it. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai now refers to [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi pāsuram 19](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/10/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-19/) \[*vaḻakkanṟu kaṇḍāy…*\], where this incident has been mentioned “*kuḻakkanṟu teeviḷavin kāykkeṟinda tīmai*” (Was it appropriate for you to throw a calf on a wood apple, in which another monster had pervaded? bhūdattāḻvār is worried as to what would have happened if both the calf and wood apple, in which monsters had pervaded, had fallen on top of kriṣṇa). He refers to this act as *tīmai* – mischievous act. Now, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai raises several questions – you \[addressing emperumān\] had determined that the wood apple fruit is *tī viḷavu* \[cunning wood apple\]. Is there any cunningness in the wood apple, which the calf had? Did it not become a fruit, after flowering and becoming an unripened fruit? Did it graze like the saintly cows? Did it remain without grazing? Did it nurse from the cow? ōr, did it now nurse from the cow? Was such contrarian behaviour seen in the wood apple? Hence, that \[wood apple\] was in a hidden state \[with some degree of doubt\]. This \[calf\] is in a well-hidden state. Thus, those who hide themselves could be present in any situation. emperumān tells bhūdattāḻvār “We had to do this after knowing that this is not correct”; bhūdattāḻvār, realising that it is emperumān’s duty \[to annihilate evil entities\] says that he had said incorrectly that this \[act of killing the calf and the wood apple\] is unjustified and that it is a fault. Feeling remorseful for his questioning kriṣṇa’s act of killing the calf and wood apple, bhūdattāḻvār says in the next pāsuram \[[iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 20](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/10/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-20/)\] “*paḻipāvam kaiyagaṟṟi …… vāḻvār vāḻvārām…*” (those who remove blame and sin, and worship you as ordained in śāstrams, will live without any trouble). Thus, those who do not impose a fault on emperumān’s auspicious qualities and worship him, will live without any trouble. periyāḻvār too, in this narrative, praises those who do not impose fault on emperumān’s qualities and removes the remorse, calls emperumān as *pirānē* \[oh, benefactor!\], recalling the benefit carried out by emperumān \[protecting himself and thus, protecting all the worlds\].

**surumbār …** – a young girl had soft locks on which flowers remained fresh always. Beetles settled on the flowers permanently, in order to take in the honey from those flowers.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the beetles, foregoing the honey in the flowers, have settled on the soft locks of the herd-girl since they enjoy the fragrance of the locks. This is the reason for saying *Ar* \[as in *surumbār*\]. Softness refers to the quality of the locks; it also refers to the tenderness of the girl who is unable to tolerate the beetles.

**sūḻ valai vaittut tiriyum arambā** – Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.3.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thiruvaimozhi-5-3-6-annai-en-seyyilen/) “*vāsudēvan valai*” (being caught in the web (of attractive activities) of the one who is the son of śrī vasudēvar), in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.2.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/11/thiruvaimozhi-6-2-9-ugavaiyal-nenjam/) “*tāmarait tadam kaṇ viḻigaḷin agavalai*” (trapping in the net of the glance of expansive eyes which are like lotus) and in nācciyār tirumoḻi 14.4 “*kārttaṇ kamalakkaṇṇennum nedum kayiṟu*” (trapped with eyes, which are like blossomed lotus on a dark cloud and which are like a long rope), kriṣṇa was keeping his divine eyes which are like a snare, on that young girl in order to trap her. Oh, the mischievous person, who was roaming around, engaging in other activities, while waiting for her to get trapped in that net!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: Oh arambā \[mischievous person\], who is keeping a snare for the girl who is both unique \[*oruttikku*\] and who has femininity in her \[*kanni*\]! He refers to the divine eyes of kriṣṇa, which surround her heart, as snare. This is similar to [nācciyār tirumoḻi 14.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/11/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-14-4/) “*kamalakkaṇ ennum nedum kayiṟu padutti*” (trapped with eyes, which are like blossomed lotus on a dark cloud and which are like a long rope). *arambu* – ability to win over an entity which one desires.

**unnai aṟindu koṇḍēn** – I have known about you, who are like all these.

**unakku …** – Hence, I will be afraid to give you \[my bosom\] milk.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.1.7. Maruttar menkulal

*maruttār men kuḻal koṇḍu poḻil pukku vāy vaittu avvāyar tam pādiccuruttār men kuḻal kanniyar vandu unnaic cuṟṟum toḻa ninṟa sōdiporuttu āyam ilēn emperumān unnaip peṟṟa kuṟṟam allāl maṟṟu inguarattā unnai aṟindu koṇḍēn unakku anjuvan ammam taravē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maruttu Ar – making one to be bewildered; mel – having soft sounds; kuḻal koṇḍu – with the flute; poḻil pukku – entering a garden, which is secluded for enjoying; vāy vaittu – keeping that flute on the divine mouth and playing it; a āyar tam pādi – in that village of herd-folks; suruṇḍu – coiled; Ar – decorated with flowers; mel – soft; kuḻal – having locks; kanniyar – girls; vandu – coming there, propelled by the sound of flute; unnai – you, playing on the flute; suṟṟum toḻa – vorśipping on all the sides; sōdi ninṟa – standing, resplendently; em perumān – oh, my lord!; unnai – you, the most mischievous; peṟṟa – begetting as son; kuṟṟam allāl – apart from the fault; maṟṟu – any other; ingu – among those in this village; poruḷ tāyam ilēn – I have no other dispute with reference to any property; arattā – oh, the mischievous one!; unnai – you, who I had considered as my son all along; aṟindu koṇḍēn – I know today that you are the difficult-to-attain lord; unakku – for you; ammam tara – to give milk; anjuvan – I am afraid

**Перевод:**

**\[addressing kriṣṇa\] You had gone into a secluded garden, with flute, which raises soft sounds, making those who hear them to be infatuated with you. You played on that flute, by keeping it on your divine mouth. Girls, with soft locks decorated with flowers, who are in the village of herd-folks, propelled by the sound of the flute, come there and worship you from all four sides. Oh, my lord, who is resplendent! Apart from the fault of giving birth to you as my son, I do not have any dispute on property with the people in this village. Oh, the mischievous one! I have known today that you are the difficult-to-attain-lord. I am afraid to give you \[my bosom\] milk.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**maruttu …** – when kriṣṇa plays on his bamboo flute, the soft tune emanating from it will make those who hear it to be bewildered such that they would not know of anything else. It would drag the ears of the person to where kriṣṇa is standing. Taking such a flute, you reached a garden which was secluded from the rest of the place such that it was apt for indulging in enjoyment, and placed your divine mouth on the flute.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that this would mean that kriṣṇa would enter a garden where beetles would settle down on flowers and keep his divine mouth on a flute which was capable of playing *maruḷ indaḷam* tune \[a type of tune\]. It would also refer to the flute which was capable of making girls to be bewildered.

**avvāyar …** – in that village, where the herd-folk would say “Look, kriṣṇa is here. Look after the girls carefully”, and would roam around, keeping a protective eye on the girls.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the village was such that kriṣṇa’s divine friends would bring any girl who was not propelled towards him on hearing him play on his flute. The girls in the village had locks which were decorated with soft flowers. This says that the girls were capable of bewildering even kriṣṇa with the beauty of their locks and attracting him towards them.

**suruttār …** – the girls, who have curly. soft locks, decorated with flowers, propelled by that tune from the flute, would come, surround you and worship you. Oh, one who stood with such acquired splendour!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *suṟṟum* refers to surrounding. He says that kriṣṇa’s splendour was on account of his dishonest method of bringing the girls to him.

**poruḷ tāyam …** – Oh, one who is my lord! Apart from the mistake of giving birth to a mischievous person such as you, I do not have any connection with the people of this village where they would come and shout at me, in anger.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that apart from hearing the scoldings of the people of the village on account of kriṣṇa, yaśōdāp pirātti says that she does not have any dispute with the people there on account of any land or property issue. She tells him that apart from the blame of having given birth to him, she had the misfortune of not having her relatives coming to her place, because of him. *āyam* – relatives who are dear, through their hearts.

**arattā unnai aṟindu koṇḍēn** – Oh, one who is mischievous like this! I have come to know about you well.

**unakku …** – Hence, I will be afraid to give you \[my bosom\] milk.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.1.8. Vala agilum

*vāḷā āgilum kāṇagillār piṟar makkaḷai maiyanmai seydutōḷāl ittu avarōdu tiḷaittu nī sollappadādana seydāykēḷār āyar kulattavar ippaḻi kettēn vāḻvillai nandankāḷā unnai aṟīndu koṇḍēn unakku anjuvan ammam taravēWord-by-Word Meaningsvāḷā āgilum – even if you remain quiet (te meaning conveyed is tat even if you are notindulging in any miscief)kāṇa killār – (tose vho do not like your splendour) vould not like to see you (even vhen tingsare like tis)piṟar makkaḷai – girls from oters’ housesmaiyanmai seydu – making tem infatuated vit your beautytōḷāl ittu – hugging teir śouldersavarōdu – standing togeter vit tose girlstiḷaittu – playing vit temsollap padādana – misciefs vhic cannot be recounted vit one’s moutnī seydāy – you had carried outāyar kulattavar – tose vho are in te herd-people clanippaḻi – tis blasphemykēḷār – vill not tolerate to hearkettēn – \[tis is a vord vhic is said, out of frustration, meaning ī have lost everyting!\]vāḻvu illai – ī cannot live in tis villagenandan – te virtuous person, nandagōpar’skāḷā – oh, one vho is te son!unnai – you, vho ī had considered as my son all alongaṟindu koṇḍēn – ī knov today tat you are te difficult-to-attain lordunakku – for youammam tara – to give milkanjuvan – ī am afraid*

**Пословный перевод:**

**Перевод:**

**There are people who do not like to look at you \[addressing kriṣṇa\] even when you remain without doing anything (since they do not like your splendour). You had made girls from others’ houses to become infatuated with you, hugged their shoulders, played with them and engaged in activities which cannot be mentioned by anyone with the mouth. Those who are in the clan of herd-people will not tolerate to hear this blasphemy. Oh, my bad! Now, I cannot live in this village. Oh, one who is the son of virtuous person nandagōpar! I have known today that you are the difficult-to-attain-lord. I am afraid to give you \[my bosom\] milk.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vāḷā …** – Even when you are not indulging in any mischief, those who do not tolerate your splendour, would not like to see you. When such is the case …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa “Even if you remain without doing anything, my relatives do not like to see you”.

**piṟar makkaḷai maiyanmai seydu** – you create bewilderment on girls from others’ houses, through your signals \[such as winking, whistling etc\] \[making them infatuated with you\]

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when kriṣṇa goes with other girls, embracing their shoulders and indulging in playful activities with them, none says “I did like this’’” \[kriṣṇa admitting what he did\] or “You did this…”’\[the girls accusing kriṣṇa of some activities\] or “He did this…” \[others, who had seen them saying what he did\]. However, you had done some activities beyond the limit of righteous activities in our clan.

**tōḷāl ittu avarōdu tiḷaittu** – embracing their shoulders and indulging in playful activities with them

**nī sollappadādana seydāy** – you carried out activities which cannot be mentioned about with the mouth.

**kēḷār āyar kulattavar ippaḻi** – those who are in the clan of herd-folk would not tolerate to hear these activities.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti says that even if the person tells nandagōpar \[the head of the clan\], he would say “Could you blame my son like this?” and would not listen to the blasphemy.

**kettēn vāḻvillai** – I am totally dejected. I cannot live in this village. In other words, yaśōdāp pirātti says that she cannot inhabit the place. The term *kettēn* refers to excessive sorrow or dejection, with one making a gesture with the hands, indicating losing everything.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti says that if nandagōpar does not listen to her and his relatives, who are also the controllers of herd clan, do not control kriṣṇa, how could she live in that place, with kriṣṇa? *vāḻdal* – to reside. *kettēn* – excess of dejection.

**nandan kāḷāy** – śrī nandagōpar is one who would not even step on a blade of grass, hard \[he is such a noble person, not injuring even a blade of grass\]. Being his son, could you behave like this? Alternatively, this indicates that kriṣṇa became a mischievous child because śrī nandagōpar did not control him while nurturing him.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti says that only śrī nandagōpar would consider kriṣṇa’s faults too as auspicious qualities. His countenance would be such that it would be similar to saying *dōśāguṇā*: \[faults too are good qualities\]. *kāḷāy* – I know that your activities are inappropriate to your age.

**unnai aṟindu koṇḍēn** – I have known that you are ”Not like the people of this place” when your age is like this and your activities are like these.

**unakku …**– Hence, I am afraid to give you \[my bosom\] milk.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.1.9. Taymar mor

*tāymār mōr viṟkap pōvar tagappanmār kaṟṟānirap pin pōvarnīyāyppādi iḷam kannimārgaḷai nērpadavē koṇḍu pōdikāyvārkku enṟum ugappanavē seydu kaṇḍār kaḻaṟat tiriyumāyā unnai aṟindu koṇḍēn unakku anjuvan ammam taravē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tāymār – mothers; mōr viṟka – to sell buttermilk; pōvar – would go to other villages (keeping their daughters to guard the houses); tagappanmār – fathers; kanṟu ānirai pinbu – behind herds of young cattle; pōvar – would go; nī – you, looking for that moment; āy pādi – in the herd-village; iḷam kannimārgaḷai – young girls in the village of herd-folk; nēr pada – to places you think of; koṇḍu pōdi – would take; kāyvārkku – for people such as śiśupāla et al, who are furious with you; enṟum – always; ugappanavē – only those which are joyous; seydu – carrying out; kaṇḍār – those who see your activities; kaḻaṟa – (with their minds in anguish) to say irritably; tiriyum – one who is roaming around; āyā – oh, one who is the son of the herd-clan!; unnai – you, who I had considered as my son all along; aṟindu koṇḍēn – I know today that you are the difficult-to-attain lord; unakku – for you; ammam tara – to give milk; anjuvan – I am afraid

**Перевод:**

**Mothers \[from various houses in the herd-village\] will go to other villages in order to sell buttermilk \[keeping their daughters to guard the respective house\]. Fathers will go behind young cattle, to graze them. You, waiting for the apt moment, would take the young girls to places which you think of. Oh, the young son of herd-clan, who roams around, being abused by those who see your activities, and making entities such as śiśupāla et al, who are furious towards you, to be always happy! I know now that you are the difficult-to-attain lord. I am afraid to give you \[my bosom\] milk.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tāymār …** – Keeping their daughters to look after the houses, the mothers will go out to sell buttermilk. Though the herd-people had enough wealth, they consider that they have to earn their livelihood by selling buttermilk. Selling buttermilk inside the herd-village is difficult, since in all the five-lakh houses in that village, milking and churning would be a continuous affair. Hence, they have to go to surrounding villages to sell. This delay in their returning \[to their houses\] would be a reason for getting enough time, for kriṣṇa.

**tagappanmār …** – when the mothers go out to sell buttermilk, if the fathers were to remain in the houses, kriṣṇa would not be able to carry out what he had thought of. To negate this, the fathers would have to go behind the herds of cattle. The cattle herds will go far away for grazing; these people, instead of controlling them, will go behind them, wherever they go. The cattle will return only when their stomachs are full. The fathers will return, only when the cattle return. Thus, this delay in their returning also gives kriṣṇa the time that he needs.

**nī āyppādi iḷam kannimārgaḷai nērpadavē koṇḍu pōdi** – You would take the young girls of tiruvāyppādi to the locations which you think of. In other words, to the places which you desire. While the mothers and fathers have already left, though their houses could be the desired places for kriṣṇa, since “Someone could return by carelessness”, you have to seek other locations.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says here that the girls were young on account of their age, their hands and their acts of righteousness in-line with the herd-clan. Through your activities of hinting to them, you would take them to the places which you desire.

**kāyvārkku enṟum ugappanavē seydu** – By indulging in such activities, you provide fodder to those, such as śiśupāla et al, who find fault with your auspicious qualities, who always have hatred towards you, to make them feel happy that “We have got enough space to despise kriṣṇa”.

**kaṇḍār kaḻaṟat tiriyum āyā** – Apart from those who find fault with you, there are also those who are good \[favourable\] towards you. Oh, the son of the herd-clan, who roams around, being controlled by such people who are unable to tolerate your mischievous deeds! This affirms that kriṣṇa is not mindful of the limits of righteousness for the herd-clan.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that apart from kamsan and those who are totally dependent on him \[his monster-friends\], there are those who abuse you, treating your auspicious qualities as faults, such as śiśupāla et al. You make them happy through your activities such that they will forever keep ridiculing you.

**unnai aṟindu koṇḍēn** – You are roaming like this, and after seeing your activities which are beyond the capabilities of human species, I have to come to know that “You are not one among the human species”.

**unakku …** – Hence, I will be scared to give you \[my bosom\] milk.

We shall next consider the 10<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.1.10. Tottar pungulal

*tottār pūnguḻal kanni oruttiyaic cōlait tadam pukkumuttār kongai puṇarndirā nāḻigai mūvēḻu senṟa pin vandāyottārkku ottana pēsuvar unnai urappavē nān onṟum māttēnattā unnai aṟindu koṇḍēn unakku anjuvan ammam taravē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tottu – bunch; Ar – together; pū – decorated with flowers; kuḻal – having locks; kanni – young girl; oruttiyai – a person; tadam – having space; sōlai – garden; koṇḍu pukku – taking her; muttu – with pearl garland; Ar – decorated; kongai – in bosoms; puṇarndu – embracing; irā – yesterday night; mūnṟu ēḻu nāḻigai senṟa pin – after the passing of three yāmams \[a yāmam is a measure of; vandāy – you returned home; unnai – regarding you; ottārkku ottana – those who are interested \[in a negative connotation\], as they like; pēsuvar – will speak ill; urappa – to speak angrily; nān – I, who am your mother; onṟum māttēn – am without any strength; attā – oh, my lord!; unnai – you, who I had considered as my son all along; aṟindu koṇḍēn – I know today that you are the difficult-to-attain lord; unakku – for you; ammam tara – to give milk; anjuvan – I am afraid

**Перевод:**

**You \[referring to kriṣṇa\] had taken a girl, who had decorated her locks with a bunch of flowers, to a place in the garden. You united with her, in her bosoms, which were decorated with a pearl necklace. You returned home yesterday night, after three yāmams. Those who are not favourable to you, will say whatever they want, regarding you. I, you mother, do not have the strength to get angry with you. Oh, my lord! I have come to know that you are the difficult-to-attain lord. Hence, I am scared to give you \[my bosom\] milk.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tottār …** – a girl, whose locks have been decorated with a bunch of flowers and who is distinct from all the other girls in tiruvāyppādi such that she could be identified as “This girl”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam that the term *tottu* refers to a bunch of flowers.

**sōlait tadam koṇḍu pukku** – taking her to a garden which was expansive

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the garden had a pond in it \[*tadam* – pond\]. *koṇḍu pukku* – enchanting \[her\] and entering with her. Since it says *pukku* \[entering\] it appears that he did not have a thought of leaving it. The word *pukku* is in present tense. It says that it is “A good place”.

**muttār kongai puṇarndu** – embracing her bosoms which were decorated with a necklace of pearls.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the pearl necklace, by reflecting moonlight, drove away the darkness from the garden such that it enabled him to see her face clearly. *puṇarndu* – Embracing her made that place to become dark. It was dark to such an extent that she did not have to hide her face, out of shyness, in her fingers.

**irā nāḻigai mūvēḻu senṟa pin vandāy** – you returned after three *yāmams* had passed in the night.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as kriṣṇa had bewildered girls, time had bewildered him. This is the reason for saying that “He returned after the passing of three *yāmams*”.

**ottārkku ottana pēsuvar unnai** – With your activity being like this, those who speak regarding you, to those who are interested in hearing \[about your mischievous activities\]. Through this, it is opined that you are engaging in activities which give rise to loose-talk among those who speak ill about you.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when kriṣṇa says “I was overcome by sleep; hence I was delayed”, those who are not favourable to him, forgetting all the good deeds which kriṣṇa had carried out earlier, thinking that he was just like themselves \[being lowly\], will talk ill of him.

**urappavē nān onṟum mātten** – Even if I have to get angry with you, who are like this, I do not have even a little bit of strength for it. When children become mischievous, vouldn’t mothers scold them?  I am unable to do that since “Your face will wither”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa “Since you are without faults, I will not get angry with you. Since you have come late, I will not control them”.

**attā** – Oh, my lord!

**unnai aṟindu koṇḍēn** – After seeing your activities which are beyond the realm of human species, I have to come to realise that “You are beyond control”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa “By coming late, you have made me to not respond to their words”. With sadness, she says that she has come to know that he is a mischievous person.

**unaqkku …** – Hence, I will be afraid to give you \[my bosom\] milk.

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.1.11. Karar meni nirattu

*kārār mēni niṟattu empirānaik kadi kamaḻ pūṇguḻal āycciārā innamudu uṇṇat taruvan nān ammam tārēn enṟa māṟṟampārār tol pugaḻān puduvai mannan battar pirān sonna pādalērār innisai mālai vallār irudīkēsan adiyārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kār Ar – matching clouds; mēni niṟam – having the complexion, for his divine form; em pirānai – for my benefactor; kadi kamaḻ – wafting fragrance; pū – donning flowers; kuḻal – having locks; āycci – yaśōdāp pirātti; ārā – never being satiated; in – being enjoyable; amudu – food \[milk\] from bosoms; uṇṇa – such that kriṣṇa consumes; taruvan – one who gives; nān – I; ammam tārēn enṟa māṟṟam – the pāsurams where she said “I will be afraid to give you milk”; pār – throughout the expanse of earth; Ar – being filled up; tol – having as nature; pugaḻān – having fame; puduvai – for śrī villibuttūr; mannan – controller; battar pirān – periyāḻvār; sonna – mercifully composed; pādal – pāsurams; ēr Ar – filled with beauty of iyal \[literary tamiḻ\]; in – sweet; isai – together with tune; vallār – those who are capable of reciting; irudīkēsan – for hriśīkēśan; adiyār – will get to be his servitors

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa, who has the complexion of his divine form similar to cloud, is my \[āḻvār’s\] benefactor. yaśōdāp pirātti, whose locks are decorated with flowers from which fragrance is wafting, usually gives kriṣṇa from her bosoms, milk, which is enjoyable for him and which is insatiable. periyāḻvār, who is the controller of śrī villibuttūr, and who has a natural fame which has pervaded throughout earth, mercifully composed her words, in which she told kriṣṇa that “I will be afraid to give you my bosom milk” into songs with sweet tunes in beautiful iyal tamiḻ. Those who are capable of reciting these words of garland, will get to be the servitors of hriśīkēśan.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kārār …** – one who is having the complexion of cloud for his divine form; one who is my benefactor.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that for the insatiable sweet nectar, who has the complexion of cloud and who is the benefactor, for the one who has insatiable enjoyment and who is the sustenance for our existence, the manner in which yaśōdāp pirātti, who normally gives him beautiful food from her bosom, now said that “I will be afraid to give”

**kadi kamaḻ pūnguḻal āycci** – yaśōdāp pirātti, who has beautiful locks which always emit fragrance.

**ārār …** – I, who had all along given you sweet milk, which is insatiable, from my youthful bosoms and who would give that to you in the future too. The words which she said “I will not give you milk, I will be afraid”, after knowing about you …

**pārār …** – periyāḻvār has a natural fame, which is celebrated by both those who have distinguished knowledge and by those who do not have any distinguished knowledge. He is also the controller of śrī villibuttūr. The pāsurams, mercifully composed by such periyāḻvār …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār has fame which fills up throughout the world. Alternatively, the word *pār* could be taken to represent both the vibhūtis (leelā vibhūti, the materialistic realm and nitya vibhūti, the spiritualistic realm). Thus, āḻvār has fame which spreads through both the vibhūtis. leelā vibhūti is a realm which prays only for itself \[here, the term leelā vibhūti refers to people who inhabit it\]. When such a realm is pervaded with the fame of \[āḻvār\] carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam for the well-being of the supreme entity, there is no need to say that the \[nitya\] vibhūti, which constantly carries out mangaḷāśāsanam for the supreme being, is also pervaded by his fame. *tol pugaḻān* – fame from a long time. What is long time for fame? nityasūris are termed, as in [tiruviruttam 2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/11/thiruviruththam-2/), as “*kaṇṇan mūduvarām viṇṇāttavar*” (the divine feet of emperumān are constantly vorśipped by nityasūris, who came ahead of all others). muktātmās (those who have been liberated from samsāram and have attained emperumān) surround emperumān and sing mangaḷāśāsanam to emperumān, as mentioned in [tiruppallāṇḍu 12](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/11/thiruppallandu-12-pallandu-enru/) “*sūḻndirundu ēttuvar pallāṇḍē*”. Along with such nityasūris and muktātmās, those in leelā vibhūti, who take refuge under the affection of periyāḻvār and who recite the pāsurams of periyāḻvār, with his pathos and also follow the activities \[carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam\] as mentioned by periyāḻvār, will carry out mangaḷāśāsanam to emperumān. This is the reference of *tol* as in *tol pugaḻān*. In other words, nitya-muktātmās are such esoteric servitors of emperumān that they will keep praising him and ensure that emperumān’s *nirankuśa svātantryam* \[uncontrolled independence\] does not rear its head \[they will make emperumān happy such that he will abide by their wishes\]. These people \[who are in leelā vibhūti and who recite these pāsurams, with āḻvār’s pathos\] carry out mangaḷāśāsanam for emperumān’s *āsrita pāratantryam* \[being dependent on his followers\], just as it has been mentioned in [perumāḷ tirumoḻi 7.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/08/perumal-thirumozhi-7-8/) “*tollai inbattu iṟudi kaṇḍāḷē*” \[yaśōdāp pirātti saw the boundary of unbounded pleasures when kriṣṇa kept quiet when she tied him with a rope and beat him, crying out in fear\]. This quality \[of carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam\] has been with periyāḻvār right from the beginning \[for seven generations, āḻvār’s clan has been carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam for emperumān\] and in the second line of *dvaya mahāmantram* \[second among the three esoteric mantrams in śrī vaiṣṇava sampradāyam\], this is the ultimate benefit mentioned. This is the reason that he has said in [tiruppallāṇḍu 2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-2-adiyomodum/) “*adiyōmōdum*” (āḻvār refers to himself first and then refers to emperumān, to signify that emperumān is āsrita paratantran) and in [tiruppallāṇḍu 3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-3-vazhatpattu/) “*ēḻātkālum paḻippilōm*” as well as in [tiruppallāṇḍu 6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/10/thiruppallandu-6-enthai-thanthai/) “*endai tandai tandai tandai tam mūttappan ēḻpadigāl todangi vandu vaḻi vaḻi ātseyginṟōm*”(starting with the predecessors in his clan, āḻvār says that they have been vorśipping emperumān without any fault of carrying out servitude to emperumān for his happiness). Thus, through both in the ascending manner \[when he starts with himself\] and descending manner \[when he starts with his predecessors\], when one analyses his servitude, it would be clear that he has been carrying this out for a long time. This is the reason for āḻvār saying “*pārār tol pugaḻān*”

**ērār …** – those who can recite these pāsurams, which have been strung together, with the beauty of *iyal* \[literary tamiḻ\] which is together with sweet tunes, with āḻvār’s pathos.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that these pāsurams have been mercifully composed by āḻvār who is the controller of śrī villibuttūr and who is the benefactor for the distinguished brāhmaṇas there, who are constantly meditating on emperumān. Apart from having depth of meanings in them, these pāsurams, which are like garland of words, have sweetness for the mere sounds of the words. Those who recite these pāsurams, which are full of beneficial qualities and are garlands of sweet words, with the pathos of periyāḻvār \[with his devotion\], taking refuge under his affection …

**irudīkēśan adiyārē** – they will get to be the servitors of one who, instead of allowing the senses to graze without any control, makes them to act in line with their basic nature \[to be emperumān’s servitors\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that only such people will be servitors. *irudīkēśan* – composed of two terms, *hriśīkam* which refers to senses and *īśan*, one who is the controller. Thus, apart from controlling the senses of those who are here \[in leelā vibhūti\], emperumān controls the senses of those who are there \[in nitya vibhūti\] too through his *ātma guṇas*. In other words, by exhibiting his quality of *pāatantryam*, emperumān makes them to be his *paratantras* \[they are his exclusive dependents\]. That exclusivity will extend to the extent to which he \[emperumān\] desires, viz. they will be servitors up to his followers. Only those, who have such depth in servitude, will be his servitors.

We shall next consider the pravēsam of the next tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.2.1. Anjana vannanai

*anjana vaṇṇanai āyar kōlak koḻundinaimanjanam ātti manaigaḷ tōṟum tiriyāmēkanjanaik kāynda kaḻal adi nōvak kanṟin pinen seyap piḷḷaiyaip pōkkinēn ellē pāvamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

anjanam – like pigment \[decorative, for eyes\]; vaṇṇanai – having divine form; āyar kōlam – having the guise of herd-people; koḻundinai – kaṇṇan, the head of the herd-folk; manjanam ātti – after giving a bath; manaigaḷ tōṟum – in others’ houses; tiriyāmē – instead of roaming (like his house); kanjanai – kamsan; kāynda – kicked; kaḻal – having the valorous anklet; adi – divine feet; nōva – to feel the pain; kanṟin pin – behind calves which go running, after seeing grass; piḷḷaiyai – my son; en seya – for what reason; ellē pāvamē – how sad! What sin have I committed (says she, in disgust)!

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa, who is the leader of herd-folk, has a divine form which is like black pigment \[applied to eyes\]. Instead of giving him a bath and allowing him to roam around in others’ houses, just like he roams around in his own house, for what reason did I send him, my son, to go behind calves, which jump towards lands which have grass, such that his divine feet, which had kicked kamsan, and which have valorous anklets, became painful? How sad! What sin have I committed!**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*(Introduction) There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**anjana vaṇṇanai** – one who has a divine form which is dark like black pigment, soothing to the eyes of the beholder. *anjanam* – black pigment, applied for decorating eyes of women.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that even any trace of whiteness which could have been present in the black pigment had been removed. kriṣṇa’s divine form was that black.

**āyar …** – Even as kriṣṇa goes behind the calves, he has an urgency in his gait, perspiration from the divine body, swaying of divine locks, golden stick on his divine hand, all pointing to his beautiful costume of a herd-person, who goes ahead of herd-folks, being their head. Alternatively, if the root gets a bit heated, the effect will be seen in the tender shoots on top, which will wither. Thus, if any of the herd-folks has any pain, it is kriṣṇa’s face which will droop first, hence he is termed as *koḻundu*. nammāḻvār too referred to emperumān, in [tiruvāīmoḻi 1.7.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-7-3-ayar-kozhunthay/) “*āyar koḻundāy*” (being the leader of cow-herd boys).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the herd-boys need not even say “kriṣṇa, control the calves and graze them carefully”. Even before that, kriṣṇa would take care of grazing of the calves such that even their celebration would be considered as superfluous. He felt that it was his benefit to graze the calves and that if they do not eat properly, it was his loss.

**manjanam …** – Instead of giving him a divine bath such that the beauty of his divine form is splendorous, just as it has been mentioned in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.1.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2026/03/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-3-1-2/) “*pon pōl manjanam ātti*” (giving him a divine bath such that his body glitters like gold) and making him to roam around in various houses, just like his own, and seeing that activity…

**kanjanaik kāynda kaḻal adi nōva** – the tender divine feet of kriṣṇa had kicked the hardened form of kamsan, due to which they had become a bit sore. Since he went on top of stones and hard surfaces on the way to the forest, they became very sore.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa had jumped onto the upper storey, a protective place, where kamsan was sitting on his throne and kicked on his hard chest with his tender foot. His divine feet became very sore when he walked on the hard surfaces on the way to the forest, behind the calves.

**kaḻal adi** – divine feet adorned with valorous anklets

**kanṟin pin en seyap piḷḷaiyaip pōkkinēn** – calves do not stay put in one place but keep hopping hither and thither. For what purpose did I send my young son, who has a tender form, behind those calves? Even though kriṣṇa had matured and is capable of annihilating enemies, she considers him as an infant.

**ellē pāvamē** – In a dejected manner, she says “What cruel sin have I committed?”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *ellē* is equivalent to *alas*, mentioned in dejection. yaśōdāp pirātti, saying *ellē pāvamē*, is similar to bharatāḻvān, in śrī rāmāyaṇam, saying “*math pāpamēva*”, (it was only due to my sin) blaming himself for śrī rāma having to go the forest.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.2.2. Parru manjal

*paṟṟu manjaḷ pūsip pāvaimārodu pādiyilsiṟṟil sidaittu engum tīmai seydu tiriyāmēkaṟṟut tūḷi udai vēdar kānidaik kanṟin pineṟṟukku en piḷḷaiyaip pōkkinēn ellē pāvamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paṟṟu – to get stuck well; manjaḷ – turmeric; pūsi – smearing on the divine form; pādiyil – present in tiruvāyppādi; pāvaimārodu – with girls; siṟu il – small sand houses built, disregarding him \[kriṣṇa\]; sidaittu – destroying with divine feet; engum – in all places; tīmai seydu – carrying out misciefs like this; tiriyāmē – instead of roaming around; kanṟu – calves’; tūḷi udai – dust, pervading everywhere; vēdar – roamed about, by hunters; kān idai – in the forest; en piḷḷaiyai – my kriṣṇa; eṟṟukku – for what purpose; pōkkinēn – did I allow, to go?; ellē pāvamē – how sad! What sin have I committed (says she, in disgust)!

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa, after applying turmeric, which will stick well on his divine form, would go to the girls who are in tiruvāyppādi. When they build houses with sand, disregarding him, he would destroy them by kicking with his divine feet. Instead of roaming around, carrying out misciefs like this, why did I send my son, kriṣṇa, behind calves, to the forest, which is pervaded by dust coming from the movement of calves and where hunters roam? How sad! What sin have I committed?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**paṟṟu manjaḷ pūsi**– When the girls in tiruvāyppādi grind turmeric for applying on themselves, they would test the efficacy of turmeric sticking to the body, on kriṣṇa’s divine form. Since each girl will test on separate regions on his form, his entire form would appear as if it had been smeared completely with turmeric. Alluding to this, yaśōdāp pirātti says in the pāsuram *paṟṟu manjaḷ pūsi*.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says the following: All the girls in tiruvāyppādi will grind turmeric. kriṣṇa would go to all those places. They will invite him, saying “Oh, kriṣṇa, come”. kriṣṇa would think “In a place where everyone says ‘kriṣṇa is a mischievous imp’ we have been fortunate to be called by them”. He will go near them. Since they grind turmeric, with effort, such that it would last a few baths, they will say “If we test on our bodies, since turmeric trace will not stick, even after taking bath, it would not be sticking to the places where we have applied”. Hence, they will test the efficacy of turmeric on kriṣṇa’s divine form. Since one girl will not test her turmeric on the same portion of kriṣṇa’s form where another girl had tested, his divine form would appear with turmeric everywhere. kriṣṇa will feel happy thinking “We have been fortunate that they have applied turmeric on our form with their hands and we have been given a bath by them to test the efficacy of turmeric sticking on our form”. When they go together for taking a bath, he would tell them “Let me also come along with you people. I will also have a bath along with you all. Take me also with you”. They will tell one another “He is a mischievous person; he should not come with us”. People in the village say “Look, kriṣṇa is here. Take care, girls” Thus, fearing fault-finding by the village people, they will leave him behind when going for a bath. Due to the dejection of not being taken by them when they went for bathing, kriṣṇa will think “Small girls will be playing, building small houses with sand. Let me also go to them and play with them”. When he goes to them, they will say “He is a mischievous boy who will kick sand in our eyes and destroy our houses” and will not allow him in their play. Since they did not allow him to take part, kriṣṇa will destroy their little houses of sand and roam around. yaśōdāp pirātti feels dejected that apart from not seeing such mischievous activities of kriṣṇa, she had sent him behind calves which kick up a sand storm while going into the forest, where hunters would be hiding under the sand storm, to waylay the people coming behind the calves and rob them of their belongings.

**pāvaimārodu pādiyil**– along with girls in tiruvāyppādi.

**siṟṟil sidaittu** – destroying small houses made with sand by girls, disregarding him.

**engum tīmai seydu tiriyāmē** – instead of roaming around everywhere, carrying out misciefs like these. It appears that yaśōdāp pirātti will be happy, seeing such activities carried out by kriṣṇa.

**kaṟṟut tūḷi udai vēdar kānidai** – when the calves run into the forest region, looking for appropriate places to graze, the dust kicked up by them would spread everywhere, making it difficult to see anyone coming from the opposite direction. Hunters would roam around in the forest, utilising this feature and steal materials from people coming behind the calves.

**kanṟin piṇ eṟṟukku en piḷḷaiyaip pōkkinēn** – Calves will not allow those coming behind them to look in any direction, other than themselves. For what purpose did I send my son behind these calves?

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti is asking herself in anguish, “What did I gain by sending him to the forest? What did the calves gain? What did kriṣṇa gain? What did his father or the people in the village gain? īsn’t there anyone apart from kriṣṇa to go behind the calves for grazing? Had I seen him when he left, I could have controlled him and prevented him from going. I was not fortunate to have done like that. Alas! It is all due to my sin”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says in the end “We have seen the divine daughter of āḻvār \[āṇḍāḷ nācciyār\] applying turmeric on mannār \[rangamannār, divine name of deity present in śrī villibuttūr\] and giving him a divine bath”. The reason for not saying “*sāṟṟit tirumanjanam seyya*” in the pāsuram \[after the first line *paṟṟu manjaḷ pūsi*\], is because these words could be uttered only by confidential servitor \[āṇḍāḷ\] \[and not by the girls in tiruvāyppādi\]. āḻvār too, when the situation demands, will be in the assembly of āṇḍāḷ nācciyār.

**ellē pāvamē** – In a dejected manner, she says “What cruel sin have I committed?”

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.2.3. Nanmani megalai

*nanmaṇi mēgalai nangaimārodu nādoṟumponmaṇi mēni puḻudi ādih tiriyāmēkanmaṇi ninṟadir kānadar idaik kanṟin pinenmaṇi vaṇṇanaip pōkkinēn ellē pāvamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en – such that I could enjoy; maṇi vaṇṇanai – one, who has a from like bluish gemstone; nal – most eminent in the world; maṇi – embedded with nine gemstones; mēgalai – having waist-cord; nangaimārodu – with girls who had completeness in their beauty; pon – beautiful; maṇi – like a bluish gem; mēni – divine form; nāḷ tōrum – every day; puḻudi ādi – wallowing in dirt; tiriyāmē – instead of roaming; kal – mountain; maṇi ninṟu adira – to raise an echo (due to his sounds of calling calves and their sounds of calling); kān adaridai – in the path inside forest; kanṟin pin – behind calves; pōkkinēn – I allowed to go; ellē pāvamē – how sad! What sin have I committed (says she, in disgust)

**Перевод:**

**My son, kriṣṇa, has a divine form like a bluish gemstone and is enjoyable for me. Instead of allowing him to play with girls who are complete with their beauty and who have the best waist-cords in the world, embedded with nine gems, and roaming around, with his beautiful form wallowing in dirt, every day, why did I send him behind calves in the forest paths, with mountains echoing sounds raised by kriṣṇa calling calves as well as of calves calling him back? How sad! What sin have I committed?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**nanmaṇi …** – with girls who were having a waist cord, embedded with faultless gems, and who were having qualities appropriate for their clan, kriṣṇa would play every day, instead of one or two days.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the girls were wearing waist-cords which were beautiful and auspicious; they also had qualities, in line with their clan.

**pon …** – while playing with them, as well as having dispute with them, kriṣṇa’s divine form, which was like a beautiful bluish gemstone, would be full of dirt. Instead of allowing him to have dirt on his divine form and roaming around… More than seeing his divine form after giving him a bath and making him to roam around various houses \[as we had seen in the first pāsuram of this tirumoḻi\], it was in seeing his divine body wallowing in dirt that yaśōdāp pirātti seems to enjoy.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as it has been mentioned in [tirunedundāṇḍagam 1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thirunedunthandakam-1/) “*ponnuruvāy maṇi uruvil bhūdam aindāy*” (having the nature of gold \[brightness, desirable etc\], in the form having the nature of gemstone, and being composed of five primary elements), periyāḻvār mercifully describes emperumān’s divine form as *ponmaṇi mēni*, like a bluish gemstone. He further days that the term *nāḷ toṟum* refers to a time equivalent to thousand deluges for periyāḻvār when he has to wait to see kriṣṇa returning home, after playing with the girls.

**kanmaṇi …** – Just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 2.5.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/10/periya-thirumozhi-2-5-3/) “*kanṟu mēyttu viḷaiyāda vallānai varaimī kāṇil*” (kriṣṇa incarnated to tend to calves and play with them in forests, atop hills), since he was grazing calves atop hills inside forests, he would call out to them with sounds. They too would respond to his calls, making sounds. These sounds would create echo in the hills, just like sounds from a bell. In such paths inside forest…

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the hills in the forest were without bushes and trees. As a result, they were capable of raising an echo for every sound made by kriṣṇa, when he was calling out to the calves or the sounds made by the calves, when they were responding to his calls. Alternatively, the sounds of bells tied to kriṣṇa’s waist cords made sounds which were echoed by the hills there.

**kanṟin pin en maṇi vaṇṇanaip pōkkinēn** – calves are such tender entities that they will run in fright if they see anything unusual. I allowed kriṣṇa, who has a form like a bluish gemstone and who is enjoyable for me, behind those calves. How sad! What sin have I committed (says she, in disgust).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the bluish gemstone was indicated as a simile for the limited scope of its colour.

**ellē pāvamē** – In a dejected manner, she says “What cruel sin have I committed?”

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.2.4. Vannak karungulal

*vaṇṇak karunguḻal mādar vandu alar tūṟṟidapaṇṇīp palaseydu ippādi engum tiriyāmēkaṇṇūkku iniyānaik kānadar idaik kanṟin pineṇṇaṟku ariyānaip pōkkinēn ellē pāvamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇṇam – being beautiful; karu – being dark; kuḻal – having locks; mādar – women; vandu – come running, with their dresses and locks diśevelled; alar tūṟṟidap paṇṇi – indulging, such that they calumniate; pala seydu – carrying out unlimited misciefs; ippādi engum – throughout this village; tiriyāmē – instead of roaming; kaṇṇukku – for the eyes; iniyānai – one who is enjoyable; eṇṇaṟku – to think “He is like this”; ariyānai – one who is difficult; kān adaridai – in the path inside forest; kanṟin pin – behind calves; pōkkinēn – I allowed to go; ellē pāvamē – how sad! What sin have I committed (says she, in disgust)

**Перевод:**

**Women in tiruvāyppādi have beautiful, dark locks. kriṣṇa would carry out many misciefs such that the women would come running helter-skelter, with their dresses and locks in a diśevelled manner and calumniate against him. Instead of roaming around the village, indulging in such misciefs, I allowed him, who is enjoyable for the eyes and who is beyond one’s thoughts, to go behind calves, in the forest path. How sad! What sin have I committed?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vaṇṇam …** – *vaṇṇam* – beautiful. Women, who were having beautiful, dark locks, came running with their dresses and locks diśevelled and blamed kriṣṇa for his misciefs.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that this verse refers to women who had decorated their locks with different types of ornaments made of gems. *vaṇṇam* – being colourful, typical of the clan of herd-women. *vandu alar tūṟṟida* – If children, in their own houses, indulge in misciefs, they \[the women\] would scold them and quieten after that. If women from other houses come to their houses, they will tell these women about the misciefs carried out by their children and leave it at that. However, when kriṣṇa indulges in mistakes, they will tell one another about his mistakes. Further, kriṣṇa has indulged in such misciefs that they will come to where I am \[reference to yaśōdāp pirātti\] and read out a litany of faults on him. However, making it difficult for me to tell them “Is he capable of indulging in all those?” and making it impossible for them to complete complaining about him, instead of allowing him to roam around the village, indulging in many mistakes, I have become the unfortunate one in not seeing all these.

**pala seydu ip pādi engum tiriyāmē** – his misciefs have been mentioned as “many” hinting that it was beyond one’s capability to count. He was roaming around the village, after indulging in his misciefs. It appears that yaśōdāp pirātti enjoyed his misciefs and their \[the affected herd-girls\] running in and blaming him.

**kaṇṇukku iniyānai** – Though they were hurt by his misciefs, his divine form was such enjoyable that people would look at him, without turning their attention away from him.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that “*manattukku iniyānai*” (being dear to the heart) comes later. First, he is dear to the eyes, with his divine form like dark cloud, and as mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇa ślōkam “*driśti cittāpahāriṇam*” (śrī rāma steals the eyes and hearts of those who behold him). Medicines such as *iḷanīr kuḻambu* \[a herbal medicine, applied to eyes to clear the vision\] would have his divine complexion. Since heart follows the path of eyes, his faults would appear like auspicious qualities, just as mentioned in the verse “*dōśā guṇā*:” (faults are auspicious qualities).

**eṇṇaṟku ariyānai** – He is beyond even the thoughts of those who wish to attain him through their efforts.

**kānadar idaik kanṟin pin pōkkinēn** – I allowed one, who is difficult to attain, to go behind calves, to the forest.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa had to go behind calves on single track paths inside forest, treading on his most tender, divine feet.  *eṇṇaṟku ariyānaip pōkkinēn*– There are people who think that by taking efforts on their own, those efforts will enable them to attain emperumān, instead of attaining him through his mercy. However, kriṣṇa will not be approachable for those who think that way. Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruccanda viruttam 45](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/11/thiruchchandha-viruththam-45/) “*eṇṇum eṇṇagappadāy kol*” (āren’t you outside the thoughts of those who remain on the earth?) and in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.10.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/10/thiruvaimozhi-1-10-2-kannulle-nirkum/) “*eṇṇilum varum*” (emperumān will present himself before those who accept his existence and think about him always), he is difficult to attain for those who think of reaching him on their own while he is easy to approach for those who leave their sustenance to him.

**ellē pāvamē** – In a dejected manner, she says “What cruel sin have I committed?”

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.2.5. Avvavvidam pukku

*avvavvidam pukku āyar peṇḍirkku aṇukkanāykkovvaik kanivāy koduttuk kūḻaimai seyyāmēevvum silai udai vēdar kān idaik kanṟin pindeyvattalaivanaip pōkkinēn ellē pāvamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

deyvam – for celestial entities; a a idam – in places such as middle or upper storey etc; pukku – entering, alone; a āyar peṇḍirkku – for those herd-girls; aṇukkanāy – being a confidante; kovvaikkani – looking like kovvaip paḻam \[a reddish coloured fruit\]; vāy – divine lips; koduttu – giving them as sustenance for their lives; kūḻaimai seyyāmē – instead of caressing and roaming around; evvum – frightening; silai udai – having bow in their hands; vēdar – roamed around by hunters; kānidai – in the forest; kanṟin pin – behind calves; pōkkinēn – I allowed to go; ellē pāvamē – how sad! What sin have I committed (says she, in disgust)

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa, who is the controller of celestial entities, would enter places such as upper storeys or large mansions, all alone, engage with the herd-girls present there as a confidante, offer them his divine lips which are reddish like the kovvaip paḻam, and engage in misciefs with them. Instead of roaming around like this, I had allowed him to go behind calves, to forests, where, hunters, holding bows in their hands, roam around. How sad! What sin have I committed?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**avvavvidam pukku** – \[kriṣṇa\] entered places such as upper storey, middle storey, cellar etc, without anyone knowing about that.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that kriṣṇa would enter places such as courtyard, streets where little girls are building sand houses, middle storeys, upper storeys, ponds, streams where people take a bath in the month of *mārgaḻi* (*danur māsam*), gardens, places where they churn curd to get butter, cellars etc, and be a confidential servitor to those girls in each of those places.

**avvāyar peṇḍiṟku aṇukkanāy** – being a servitor of herd-girls, who were present in those places. In other words, behaving in the way that they had thought of him to behave with them.

**kovvaik kanivāyk koduttu** – offering his divine lips, which were reddish like the *kovvaip paḻam*, to them as their life-sustaining entity

**kūḻaimai seyyāmē** – instead of roaming around, carrying out misciefs with those girls. *kūḻmai* – telling the girls “I do not know of anyone other than you”. “I cannot sustain myself without you” etc, making it appear that he exists only for that particular girl.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti is lamenting that instead of seeing kriṣṇa roaming around and carrying out misciefs with those girls… viz. instead of entering and roaming  around in those places, just as it has been mentioned in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.7.5 “*nāraṇan pōmidam ellām*” (in places where kriṣṇa roams around) and in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.5.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/02/thiruvaimozhi-6-5-5-kuzhaiyum-val/) “*ivaḷ nuḻaiyum sindaiyaḷ*” (she has a heart which is immersed in kriṣṇa’s beauty) \[In these two pāsurams, jīvātmās will follow wherever emperumān goes whereas in the pāsuram under discussion, emperumān goes, following girls, wherever they go\]. The term *kūḻaimai* refers to speaking words to various girls, to satisfy each of them, as mentioned in [perumāḷ tirumoḻi 6.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/07/perumal-thirumozhi-6-3/) “*karumalark kūndal*” (glancing at a girl who has flowers in her dark locks)

**ervvum silai udai vēdar kān idai** – *evvum silai* – just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 1.7.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/05/periya-thirumozhi-1-7-4/) “*evvum vevvēl*” (having spear which causes sorrow), this refers to a bow which gives sorrow to those who see it, due to its frightening appearance. Alternatively, the word *ēvum* \[arrow\] has got shortened as *evvum*, referring to a bow together with arrows. In the former case, the word *evvum* refers to causing sorrow on account of the frightening appearance of the bow; in the latter case, it refers to bow with arrow. To syncronise with the earlier lines, the word *evum* has got reinforced as *evvum*, with an additional ‘*v*’ syllable. In the forest, where hunters, carrying such bow, inhabit.

**kanṟin pin deyvat talaivanaip pōkkinēn** – I allowed the lord of celestial entities to go behind calves, which go as they like, without any control.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti says that she sent kriṣṇa, who is the head of nityasūris, as the head of herd-boys.

**ellē pāvamē** – In a dejected manner, she says “What cruel sin have I committed?”

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.2.6. Midaru melumeluttu

*midaṟu meḻumeḻuttōda veṇṇey viḻungippōypadiṟu pala seydu ippādi engum tiriyāmēkadiṟu pala tiri kānadar idaik kanṟin pinidaṟa en piḷḷaiyaip pōKkinēn ellē pāvamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

veṇṇey – butter; midaṟu – in the throat; meḻumeḻuttu ōda – to go in smoothly (without causing any irritation); viḻungi – consuming; pōy – going out; pala – unlimited; padiṟu – misciefs; seydu – carrying out; ippādi engum – throughout this village \[of tiruvāyppādi\]; tiriyāmē – instead of roaming; pala kadiṟu – many wild elephants; tiri – roaming; kān adar idai – in the path to the forest; kanṟin pin – behind calves; idaṟa – to go about in distress; en piḷḷaiyai – my kriṣṇa, who is of a tender nature; pōkkinēn – I allowed to go; ellē pāvamē – how sad! What sin have I committed? (says she, in disgust)

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa would consume butter such that it would go in smoothly, through his throat, without causing any irritation. He will then go out and carry out unlimited misciefs, roaming throughout this village. Instead of allowing him to do this, why did I send him behind calves, to go in distress, to the forest, where wild elephants roam about? How sad! What sin have I committed? (says she, in disgust)**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**midaṟu meḻumeḻuttōda veṇṇey viḻungi** – this describes the effortlessness with which kriṣṇa consumed butter. In other words, when eating rice or foodstuff such as *apūpam* (vadai etc), they should be taken in a limited quantity, kept in the mouth and pushed down. Unlike those foodstuffs, as mentioned in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.5.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/08/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-1-5-9/) “*tāḻiyil veṇṇey tadam kai Ara viḻungiya*” \[kriṣṇa consumed butter from the pot, extending his large hand into the pot) and in periya tirumoḻi 10.7.3 “*tadā niṟainda veḷḷimalai irundāl otta veṇṇeyai vāri viḻungittu*” (scooping and swallowing butter from the pot, in which it had been filled up, looking like *mēru* \[a celestial\] mountain,) looking at the abundance of butter available, with affection, with overflowing desire, kriṣṇa would take butter, spreading his hands fully, as mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.8.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-8-5-vaigalum-venney/) “*kai kalandu uṇḍān*” (\[kriṣṇa\] ate butter, stretching his hands fully). Butter was such that, when he took it in both his left and right hands, it would go into the mouth and through the throat, without any hurdle, in a smooth manner. Hence, this material would be the most apt for his tender nature too. It was butter which kriṣṇa liked, more than the other materials obtained from cow \[such as milk, curd, ghee etc\]. It was for eating this that he had incarnated too, as mentioned in [tiruviruttam 21](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/01/thiruviruththam-21/) “*īttiya veṇṇey todu uṇṇa…*” (to consume butter which has been churned and gathered). The term *viḻungip pōy* would refer to his eating butter; it would refer to his eating butter and slipping out of that place and going to some other place, as if he had nothing to do with butter disappearing; it would also refer to his eating butter in his house and going out \[to indulge in misciefs\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that kriṣṇa’s throat was such spacious \[he had swallowed all the worlds at the time of deluge\] that butter slipped into it smoothly, just as it has been mentioned in periya tirumoḻi 10.6.1 “*pon midaṟu attanaip pōdu angāndavan*” (kriṣṇa had opened his mouth wide to let all the entities to go in, for his protection). He had swallowed a large quantity of butter such that he could gargle with it. If there is any trace of butter on the hand, it would have to be cleaned by washing \[with soap-nut powder and water\] or by wiping it on the head. However, stickiness due to butter in the throat will not be visible. Thus, he could indulge in misciefs every day. The term *ōda* refers to the butter, not being controlled by the throat. Even if he eats to his mouthful, it will slip in without any trouble.

**padiṟu pala seydu** – *padiṟu* – mischief; since it says “*pala*”, this indicates that there is no limit to the misciefs which he indulged in. Just as it has been mentioned in periya tirumoḻi 10.7.5 “*pandu paṟīttut tugil paṟṟik kīṟip padiṟan padiṟu seyya*” (indulging in misciefs such as snatching the ball from the hands of girls, tugging at their dress etc), he would snatch the playing materials from the hands of girls who are playing with them; he would tug at their dresses and tear them; he would destroy the little sand-houses which they would have built; there is no limit to the misciefs which he would indulge in, fighting and arguing with them, as mentioned in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 2.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/07/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-2-8/) “*tottu udaittu naliyēl* ” (don’t harm us by touching and kicking us) and in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 2.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/07/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-2-9/) “*emmaip paṟṟi meyppiṇakkittāl*” (If you grasp us and embrace us, what will people nearby say?) Since his misciefs are unspeakable and uncountable, āḻvār mentions them as *padiṟu* \[mischief\] and *pala* \[many\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the misciefs indulged in by kriṣṇa could not be mentioned as “such and such misciefs”. They cannot even be spoken of. Hence, āḻvār says “*pala padiṟu*”.

**ippādi engum tiriyāmē** – it was not one house or two; it was not one street or two; kriṣṇa would go around all the five-lakh houses in the tiruvāyppādi village, where each house was twenty-four feet long. If he had indulged in these countless misciefs, yaśōdāp pirātti too would have been happy, as mentioned in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 3.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/07/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-3-9/) “*anja urappāḷ asōdai āṇāda vittirukkum*” (yaśōdāp pirātti would not scold him to frighten him; she would have allowed him to grow to indulge in more misciefs). When he indulges in misciefs, instead of controlling him to frighten him, she would think “We have been fortunate to have got a son like kriṣṇa who is capable of doing thee misciefs”. It is because of this that yaśōdāp pirātti felt sad that she had allowed him to go to the forest, instead of roaming around and indulging in misciefs like these.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *engum* would not be restricted to one or two houses, one or two streets, one or two corners. After kriṣṇa incarnated, tiruvāyppādi was home to five-lakh houses, with each house being twenty-four feet long.

**kadiṟu pala tiri** – in the forest where many elephants are roaming. Just as a type of fish, called as *keḷiṟu* \[in tamiḻ\], is referred to as *kediṟu*, elephant, which is called as *kaḷiṟu*, is referred to here as *kadiṟu*. Just as *garuda* is referred to as *garuḷa* (replacing the syllable *La* with the syllable, *da*), *kaḷiṟu* has been referred to as *kadiṟu*. Since the pāsuram refers to many elephants, yaśōdāp pirātti is afraid that “Wild elephants will chase people when they are seen in the forest and kill them”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa had to go the forest where wild animals were roaming. Alternatively, *kadiṟu* would refer to *kaḷiṟu*, elephant

**kānadar idai** – in the forest path. In other words, since it is a single-track path, there will not be space on the left or right side, even to step out.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the path in the forest was such narrow that kriṣṇa could not move to the side and control the calves from going out of line. Also, he was at that stage of an innocent child when he did not know the means of controlling them. He would follow the calves. These features make yaśōdāp pirātti to fret about his safety.

**kanṟin pin** – even here, instead of roaming around as he pleased, kriṣṇa will have to go behind calves, which will enter wherever they see grass for grazing, and will have to control them.

**idaṟa en piḷḷaiyaip pōkkinēn** – I allowed my son, who is very tender, to go like this, in a distressful manner.

**ellē pāvamē** – In a dejected manner, she says “What cruel sin have I committed?”

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan
