## 3.2.7. Valli nudangidai

*vaḷḷi nudangidai mādar vandu alar tūṟṟidattuḷḷi viḷaiyādit tōḻarōdu tiriyāmēkaḷḷi uṇangu vem kānadar idaik kanṟin pinpuḷḷin talaivanaip pōkkinēn ellē pāvamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaḷḷi – like a young creeper; nudangu – trembling; idai – having waist; mādar – women; vandu – coming, with an urgency; alar tūṟṟida – such that they calumniate; tuḷḷi – hopping (such that the divine feet do not step on land); viḷaiyādi – playing; tōḻarōdu – with friends; tiriyāmē – instead of roaming; kaḷḷi – cactus (which is greenish, even when there is no rain); uṇangum – to become withered, with milk \[latex\] drying out; vem – having excessive heat; kān adar idai – in the path to forest; puḷḷīn talaivanai – one, who is the lord of garuda; pōkkinēn – I allowed to go; ellē pāvamē – how sad! What sin have I committed? (says she, in disgust)

**Перевод:**

**Women, who have waists which are slender and trembling like a young creeper, will come hurriedly and calumniate kriṣṇa. He would go with his friends, hopping, with pride. Instead of allowing him to do this, why did I send the lord of garuda, behind calves, to forest, where due to excessive heat, even cactus plant, which is normally green even when there is no rain, withers, with its milk drying up? How sad! What sin have I committed? (says she, in disgust)**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vaḷḷi …** – *vaḷḷi* – creeper. Women, who had slender waists which were trembling like a creeper, came and complained about the misciefs which kriṣṇa did to them. Will they not complain if he breaks their possessions \[destroying the sand-houses built by them, grabbing ball from their hands, tugging at their dresses, tearing them etc\]?

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that since a regular creeper would not be an exact match for the waist of women, it has to be qualified as *nudangu idai*, trembling creeper, to make it more acceptable. Just as it has been said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 14.5 “*tulya śeela vayōvruttām*” (śrī rāma and sītāp pirātti were an exact match for each other, in terms of their qualities, age, activities etc), these girls were an exact match for kriṣṇa. *nudangidai* – they had the eminence of starving kriṣṇa for days on end \[by denying his wishes\]. *vandu alar tūṟṟida* – how strange is this behaviour of theirs where, while being affectionate towards kriṣṇa, they came and complained about him! Even if kriṣṇa were to do as per their bidding, they will not reciprocate, since they are many and he is alone. Since they are of the type who cannot sustain separation from him even for a moment, his qualities will appear as faults to them. This is the sustenance for them.  Since the tiruvāyppādi village will blame them if they are seen with kriṣṇa, they come and complain about him, to make it appear that there is no connection between them. In [periya tirumoḻi pāsuram 3.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2022/09/periya-thirumozhi-3-7-1/) “*vaḷḷi marungul en than mada māninai*” (\[kriṣṇa came in the middle of the night to take\] my daughter, who has a slender waist), kriṣṇa’s coming to the girl was accepted. Unable to accept \[the separation\], these girls came and complained. nappinnaip pirātti and śrī janakarājan’s divine daughter waited until emperumān came, to conquer “Bulls” and “Bow” respectively \[kriṣṇa killed the seven bulls to marry nappinnaip pirātti; śrī rāma broke the bow to marry sītāp pirātti; they waited for the arrival of emperumān. These girls could not wait for kriṣṇa to come. Hence, they came and complained\].

**tuḷḷī viḷaiyādit tōḻarōdu tiriyāmē** – If they come like this and calumniate him, without having any fear \[as to what they or his mother will do\], considering their complaints as an eminence for him, kriṣṇa would jump around, like young calves will do with pride, not keeping his divine feet on land, indulging in strange activities, along with his thousand friends, who are like him.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa felt proud that the girl listed his faults and lack of qualities, treating that as their sustenance, and complained. Just like a calf, after taking milk from its mother, goes around with other calves and plays, kriṣṇa, went with his thousand friends, who are like him, after this incident.

**kaḷḷi uṇangu vem kān adaridaik kanṟin pin** – even when there is no rain at all, cactus type of plants will retain their freshness. But even those plants were withering, with their milk drying out, due to excessive heat inside forest. I sent kriṣṇa, behind calves, to those forest paths.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumadal 50](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/category/iyarpa/periya-thirumadal/) “*tunnu veyil vaṟutta vem paral mēl*” (sītāp pirātti walked in the forest, with her divine feet stepping on small stones which were fried in the heat), kriṣṇa went over stones in the forest. The stones not only got heated during sunshine; when the sunshine reduced, they had enough heat with them to return it to the sunshine. It was through such a forest that yaśōdāp pirātti feels sad for having sent kriṣṇa. If janakarājan’s divine daughter could walk on those stones, is it required to state that kriṣṇa and the calves too could go over them?

**puḷḷin talaivanaip pōkkinēn** – I sent kriṣṇa, who is the lord of *periya tiruvadi* \[garuda\], and who goes around only atop that garuda, not stepping on land.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that garuda is the epitome of vēdams and has a speed matching the mind. yaśōdāp pirātti says that she sent kriṣṇa, whose mind garuda knows and acts as per his mind \[it could also be taken that kriṣṇa knows garuda’s mind and conducts him as per that\] to go on foot. He quotes from [tiruvāimoḻi 1.10.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/10/thiruvaimozhi-1-10-6-niyum-nanum/) “*putpāgan*” (controller of garuda) and [tirunedundāṇḍagam 6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/09/thirunedunthandakam-6-part-1/) “*anjiṟaippuḷ tanippāgan*” (unique controller of garuda who has beautiful wings) to reinforce that kriṣṇa is the lord of garuda.

**ellē pāvamē** – In a dejected manner, she says “What cruel sin have I committed?”

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.2.8. Panniru tingal

*panniru tingaḷ vayiṟṟil koṇḍa appānginālenniḷam kongai amudam ūtti edutti yānponnadi nōvap pulariyē kānil kanṟin pinenniḷam singattaip pōkkinēn ellē pāvamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pattu iraṇḍu tingal – twelve months; vayiṟṟil koṇḍa – keeping inside the stomach (without any distress to the child); appāngināl – through the affection of carrying very well; yān – I, the mother; en – my; iḷa – being soft; kongai amudam – milk from the bosom; ūtti eduttu – nurturing; ēn – for me; iḷa singattai – one who is like a young lion; pon – being tender and beautiful; adi – divine feet; nōva – to hurt; pulari – during the time of dawn; kānil – to the forest; kanṟin pin – behind calves; pōkkinēn – I allowed to go; ellē pāvamē – how sad! What sin have I committed? (says she, in disgust)

**Перевод:**

**Due to the affection of carrying the child in my stomach for twelve months, such that no harm befell the child, I, the mother \[of kriṣṇa\] offered milk from my soft bosom and nurtured him. I sent my son, who was like a young lion, behind calves, to the forest, such that his tender, beautiful, divine feet hurt. How sad! What sin have I committed? (says she, in disgust)**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**panniru tingaḷ** – just as it has been mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 18.8 “*tadaśca dvādaśa māsē*” (after the passing of twelve months), śrī rāma was born after being in his mother’s womb for twelve months. In the same way, kriṣṇa too was in the womb for twelve months. Pregnant women, with overflowing love, will move around without the foetus feeling any distress when the women sit or move or lie down. Since yaśōdāp pirātti too had carried kriṣṇa in her womb for twelve months, without causing any distress to him, she mentions the distinguished manner in which she had carried her son, through the verse *panniru tingaḷ vayiṟṟil koṇḍa appāngināl*.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that while people carry foetus in their womb for ten months, impelled by *karma* \[deeds\], in the case of emperumān, since he is impelled by his mercy, he stays in the womb for twelve months. yaśōdāp pirātti too thinks that she had carried him for twelve months in her womb. Neutral people too, after doubting, as in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2.1.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/10/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-2-1-7/) “*tānē peṟṟāḷ kolō*” (did she give birth to him?) have affirmed as in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2.2.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/10/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-2-2-6/) “*ivanaip peṟṟa vayiṟū udaiyāḷ*” (what penance did yaśōdāp pirātti, who has the divine stomach which gave birth to kriṣṇa, carry out?) It is said that the one who gave birth \[to kriṣṇa\] did not see \[kriṣṇa’s activities\] and the one who did not give birth, saw everything. dēvakip pirātti too said, as in [perumāḷ tirumoḻi 7.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/08/perumal-thirumozhi-7-3/) “*nandan peṟṟanan nangaḷ kōn peṟṟilan*” (nandagōpar was fortunate to have had you as his son; vasudēvar, my lord, did not have that fortune). *appāngināl* – yaśōdāp pirātti had carried kriṣṇa in her stomach, taking distinguished care of him during the twelve months. Since she had endured the pain herself, she adds two months \[to the normal ten months\]. This was done in order to make her “Bring up the child protectively, thinking of him as her son” as well as for the world to say in a renowned manner that he was her son. She says this as if she had given birth to him and that he was born to her \[when vēdams says that he does not have a birth, due to karma\]. The reason for periyāḻvār to mercifully say about yaśōdāp pirātti kept kriṣṇa in her stomach in a distinguished way is because when he had said, as in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.1.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2026/03/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-3-1-3/) “*immāyam valla piḷḷai nambi unnai en maganē enbar ninṟār*” (Oh, one who is complete in your auspicious qualities as a child! Seeing your amazing activities, people, who are neutral, will say that you are my son only) that neutral persons would say that he is her son only, he expressed his *bhakti pāravaśyam* \[being under the control of devotion towards kriṣṇa\] through yaśōdāp pirātti’s pathos. Though kamsan was long dead and gone and the time was also a totally different *yugam* \[epoch\], periyāḻvār would not reveal details of kriṣṇa’s birth, due to fear of kamsan \[as to what he would do to kriṣṇa\]. The ones who mentioned this to kamsan were durgai \[who slipped out of kamsan’s hands when he was about to smash her head against a stone and told kamsan that the one who was born to kill him is now in śrī gōkulam\] and śrī nārada bhagavān, who told kamsan not to spare the first seven children too when they are born and to kill them all. Even nammāḻvār, who had said, as in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.10.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/09/thiruvaimozhi-5-10-1-pirandha-arum/) “*periya bhāradam kaiseydu aivarkkut tiṟangaḷ kāttiyittuc ceydupōna māyangaḷum*” (the way in which kriṣṇa had arranged the armies for the five pāṇḍavas, revealing the means for their victory and the amazing ways by which he completed the purpose of his incarnation and returned to śrī vaikuṇṭam), merely said “*piṟandavāṟum vaḷarndavāṟum*” (the way in which kriṣṇa was born and the ways in which he grew up), without explicitly mentioning details of his birth. While he had mentioned about the amazing manner in which he had made the five pāṇḍavas to be victorious, the reason for nammāḻvār too, not to reveal details of his amazing birth is that in the former case \[with pāṇḍavas, during mahābhārata war\], kriṣṇa was at an age when he was powerful while during the time of his birth, he was not powerful \[this is in āḻvārs’ thinking, when they have overflowing affection and have the protective nature of a mother towards emperumān\]. They \[āḻvārs\] hide what is revealed by emperumān too; hence they will not reveal any detail about his birth \[at the time of his birth, kriṣṇa had manifested the divine weapons and four shoulders to vasudēvar and dēvakip pirātti\]. Just as it has been mentioned in manusmruti “*satyam bhrūyāt priyam bhrūyāt na bhrūyāt satyam apriyam*” (speak truth; speak what is good for one; do not speak even if it is a truth, if it hurts someone), āḻvārs will not speak if it would hurt emperumān. Even if emperumān carries out activities which are good for mankind as a whole, if he does not want it spoken about, āḻvārs would not speak about it. How then did people like durgai and nārada bhagavān speak about it? This is because, just as it has been mentioned in the same manu smruti, “*satyam bhūta hitam prōktam*” (for the sake of the well-being of some people, truth should be spoken), they would reveal the truth for the sake of some followers of emperumān. āḻvārs would look at *prakruti* \[primordial matter, which hides emperumān from samsāris\] and behave as if they have been under its control. This is similar to *riśis* \[sages\], who, while enjoying emperumān who is their antaryāmi, will not speak about it.

**enniḷam kongai amudam ūtti eduttiyān** – When she had taken care of her child inside her stomach for twelve months, without causing any distress to the child, she will not allow the child to get distressed when she brings up and nurtures the child. Thus, she explains the manner in which she had nurtured him appropriate to his age and carried him. Out of overflowing love, she nursed him and carried him. When he came to her to take in her milk, instead of dry bosom, she offered him soft bosom from which he could drink her milk. This is referred to in the word *iḷa koṇgai*. Since the pāsuram says *kongai amudam*, it refers to milk from the bosom \[*amudam* refers to nectar\]. Through the verse *ūtti eduttiyān*, she says that after nursing him with her bosom milk, she carried him on her waist and did not let him down on the floor. Thus, she roamed around, attending to her chores, carrying kriṣṇa on her waist.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that even though the milk from her bosom is full of strength, her bosom will be tender to enable him to suckle without feeling affected by it.

**ponnadi nōvap pulariyē kānil kanṟin pin** – just as is has been mentioned in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.7.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/09/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-1-7-9/) ”*taṇ pōdu koṇḍa tavisin mīdu*” (kriṣṇa would take tender steps on a mattress of soft flowers), kriṣṇa had completely soft divine feet which were attractive. yaśōdāp pirātti feels sad that she had allowed him to go, early in the morning, behind calves which go hopping to grasslands in forest, with his divine feet hurting on account of the hard surface in the forest.

**enniḷam singattaip pōkkinēn** – I allowed my son, who, due to being nurtured by me with care, went with the pride of a young lion.

**ellē pāvamē** – In a dejected manner, she says “What cruel sin have I committed?”

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.2.9. Kudaiyum seruppum

*kudaiyum seruppum kodādē dāmōdaranai nānudaiyum kadiyana ūnṟu vem paraṟgaḷ udaikadiya vem kānidaik kāladi nōvak kanṟin pinkodiyēn en piḷḷaiyaip pōkkinēn ellē pāvamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kudaiyum – umbrella (as protection from sun); seruppum – sandals (for protection from the heat etc on land); kodādē – without giving; dāmōdaranai – kaṇṇan, who has scar on his divine stomach, from rope; nān – I, his mother; udaiyum – being split (due to sun’s heat); kadiyana – being sharp; ūnṟu – pricking on the feet; vem – unable to keep the feet; paraṟgaḷ udai – having pebbles; kadiya vem – being excessively hot; kānidai – in the forest; kāl adi nōva – such that the soles of feet hurt; kanṟin pin – behind calves; kodiyēn – I, the hard-hearted person; pōkkinēn – I allowed to go; ellē pāvamē – how sad! What sin have I committed? (says she, in disgust)

**Перевод:**

**Without giving umbrella and sandals, which will protect him from sunlight above and from the heat etc on land, under the feet, I had sent dāmōdaran to the forest, where pebbles split due to the heat from sun and their sharpness hurt the soles of feet. I, the hard-hearted person, sent him behind calves, to such forest. How sad! What sin have I committed? (says she, in disgust)**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kudaiyum seruppum kodādē** – without giving umbrella, which protects from sunlight, and sandals, which protect from heat from earth, thorns etc.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that yaśōdāp pirātti sends kriṣṇa usually with umbrella, which protects from rain, wind and heat, and sandals, which protect from thorns, hot sand, hot dust and hot pebbles. She offers these to the entity who is served by ādiśēśan, as mentioned in [mudal tiruvandādi 53](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/08/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-53/) “*senṟāl kudaiyām…ninṟāl maravadiyām*” (ādiśēśan serves as the umbrella for emperumān wherever he goes and as sandals, whenever he stands). But, today, she did not send him with those protective materials.

**dāmōdaranai nān** – He was obedient to me, not untying himself free from the binding which I made with a mortar, using a rope. Such a son …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti calls him as dāmodāran since he is obedient and simplicity personified for her when she ties him with a rope or beats him. One who is at the centre of paramapadam and who does not move a bit, is seen here as simplicity personified.

**udaiyum kadiyana ūnṟu vem paraṟgaḷ udai** – pebbles which are broken due to excessive heat, and which are sharp, piercing the foot when placed over them, and hot enough such that foot could not be placed over them.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the pebbles break under the intense heat from sun, retaining their sharpness even when they break. Even if one were to carefully step aside from them and step onto the land, it would be similar to stepping over a heated metal plate. There would be no means for overcoming the heat inside the forest, which has lost its water resources. Alternatively, the term *udai* could be read with “*kudaiyum seruppum*”. This would then convey the meaning that yaśōdāp pirātti had sent kriṣṇa without umbrella, sandals and the dress specifically worn by the herd-people.

**kadiya vem kān idai** – in the forest which does not have any shade, where one could take cover, due to the cruel heat

**kāladi nōva** – such that the soles of the divine feet hurt

**kanṟin pin kodiyēn en piḷḷaiyaip pōKkinēn** – I, who did not take these into account, and who am cruel, sent my son, who is most tender, behind calves, which will go hopping wherever they see green grass for grazing.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that calves do not know the place where they should go to and return from. They will hop from one place to another, in search of green pastures. kriṣṇa would know about how their feet will hurt, but will not look after his divine feet, which are tender, as mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.2.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/06/thiruvaimozhi-9-2-10-koduvinaip-padaigal/) “*pidikkum melladi*” (tender, divine feet, which are gently massaged by periya pirātti and bhūmip pirātti) and as in [tirunedundāṇḍagam 1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thirunedunthandakam-1/) “*taḷir puraiyum tiruvadi*” (the divine feet which become fresh). He further says that yaśōdāp pirātti says that compared to her cruel nature, the forest could be termed as “That forest has water and shade”. It appears that she sees him after removing his eminence, his greatness, his good behaviour and the affection on account of being her son \[since she is sending him to the forest, with a cruel heart\].

**ellē pāvamē** – In a dejected manner, she says “What cruel sin have I committed?”

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.2.10. Enrum enakku

*enṟum enakku iniyānai en maṇi vaṇṇanaikkanṟin pin pōkkinēn enṟu asōdai kaḻaṟiyapon tigaḻ mādap puduvaiyar kōn battan solin tamiḻ mālaigaḷ vallavarkku idar illaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

enṟum – “forever; enakku – for me, the mother; iniyānai – being affectionate; en – such that I could enjoy; maṇi vaṇṇanai – one who has the form of a bluish gemstone; kanṟin pin – behind calves; pōkkinēn – allowed to go to the forest”; enṟu – saying so; asōdai – yaśōdāp pirātti; kaḻaṟiya – words, spoken with anguish; pon – made of gold; tigaḻ – being splendorous; mādam – having mansions; puduvaiyar – for those who reside in tiruppuduvai (śrī villibuttūr); kōn – one, who is the controller; battan – periyāḻvār; sol – having been mercifully composed; in – being enjoyable; tamiḻ mālai – these, which are garlands in tamiḻ; vallavarkku – for those who are capable of reciting; idar – sorrow; illaiyē – will disappear

**Перевод:**

**yaśōdāp pirātti had spoken with anguish about her having sent kriṣṇa, who is always dear to her and who has a complexion like a bluish gemstone, which she could enjoy. periyāḻvār, the controller of those who live in śrī villibuttūr, which has mansions which are splendorous, being made of gold, mercifully composed those words of yaśōdāp pirātti into pāsurams, which are enjoyable and are like garlands in tamiḻ language. For those who are capable of reciting these pāsurams, hurdles will disappear.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the last pāsuram of this decad, āḻvār mentions the benefit which will accrue to those who recite it and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**enṟum enakku iniyānai** – unlike a flower, which will close its petals after a period of time, kriṣṇa is forever enjoyable for me.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that unlike a river which will flow for a long time and become dry for a short time, before flowing again \[in other words, it has periods when it will change from its nature of flowing\], emperumān has affection towards periyāḻvār forever, as a result of which periyāḻvār considers himself as the protector and emperumān as the protected entity. It is because of this that overflowing affection is created in periyāḻvār towards emperumān.

**en maṇi vaṇṇanai** – one who has a form like a bluish gemstone, which is always enjoyable for me.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that due to his \[kriṣṇa’s\] distinction of divine form, which is like a bluish gemstone, emperumān steals periyāḻvār’s mind.

**kanṟin pin pōkkinēn enṟu asōdai kaḻaṟiya** – words spoken with anguish by yaśōdāp pirātti, who said “I had sent him behind calves, without knowing the effects”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that there is a huge difference between the way yaśōdāp pirātti said “*enṟum*” \[forever\] and āḻvār said the same. This is because, for āḻvār, emperumān is an entity to be protected always, not only when he is a child; for yaśōdāp pirātti, kriṣṇa has to be protected only until the time that he remains as a child. Similarly, for the word “*enakku iniyānai*”, there is a huge difference between yaśōdāp pirātti and āḻvār. Irrespective of where he is, emperumān is sweet for āḻvār while for yaśōdāp pirātti, kriṣṇa is sweet only till the time that he is with her.

**pon tigaḻ mādap puduvaiyar kōn battan sol** – mercifully composed by periyāḻvār, who is the controller of those who live in śrī villibuttūr, which has mansions which are splendorous, having been made of gold.

**in tamiḻ …** – These pāsurams, composed in tamiḻ language, have the distinction of being like garlands, with the flavour of both the sounds \[of the words\] and meanings. For those who are capable of reciting these ten pāsurams, with the pathos of periyāḻvār, there is no sorrow.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai explains here as to what is sweetness for tamiḻ language. He says that in samaskrutam, for example, with reference to the root of the word as well as the case \[*vēṟṟumai urubu*\], meanings beyond what was intended could be assumed. Similarly, due to the root, the intended meaning itself may not be present. However, with tamiḻ language, by merely hearing the word, the intended direction of the composer as well as the meaning of the word will become very clear. This is the sweetness of tamiḻ language. For the term *idar illaiyē*, he says that for the one who recites the pāsurams, unlike periyāḻvār, the sorrow which comes due to separation from emperumān will not be experienced.

We shall next consider the pravēśam of the next tirumoḻi.

## 3.3.1. Seelaik kudambai

*seelaik kudambai oru kādu oru kādu senniṟa mēl tōnṟip pūkkōlap paṇaik kaccum kūṟai udaiyum kuḷir muttin kōdālamumkālip pinnē varuginṟa kadal vaṇṇan vēdattai vandu kāṇīrjñālattup puttiranaip peṟṟār nangaimīr nānē maṟṟu ārum illai*

**Пословный перевод:**

oru kādu – on one ear; seelaik kudambai – a roll, made of cloth \[to enlarge the hole in the ear\]; oru kādu – on the other ear; senniṟam mēl tōnṟip pū – reddish glory lily \[also called as malabar lily\]; kūṟai udaiyum – cloth adorned, appropriate for his divine form; kōlam – being beautiful; paṇai – being large; kaccum – a type of belt \[made of cloth\] to keep the cloth \[worn on the waist\] in place; kuḷir – being cool; muttin – strung with pearls; kōdu – curved like the crescent \[of moon\]; ālamum – having a chain; kālip pinnē – behind calves; varuginṟa – one who comes; kadal – like an ocean; vaṇṇan – having divine complexion; vēdattai – the way he has attired; vandu kāṇīr – come and have a look; nangai mīr – oh women, who are without any shortcoming!; jñālattu – on this earth; puttiranai – son; peṟṟār – among those who have given birth to; nānē – only I (who could be called as “Sired a good son”\]; maṟṟu ārum illai – there is no one else

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa is wearing a roll of cloth on one ear and a red glory lily, on the other ear. He has a cloth on his waist, held in place by a beautiful, large belt. He has a curved chain, strung with cool pearls. Oh, women, who are without any shortcoming! Come and have a look at the attire of kriṣṇa, who has the complexion of an ocean. Among those who have given birth to a son on this earth, only I could be called as having given birth to good son. There is none else.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says in his svāpadēśam that yaśōdāp pirātti sees the way that she had decorated kriṣṇa as well the way in which he had \[subsequently, in the forest\] decorated himself. She fees happy and shows that to others who too, who are also happy.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**seelai …**– kriṣṇa had a cloth roll on one of his ears and a red glory lily flower, on the other ear; though yaśōdāp pirātti had applied cloth rolls in the holes of both ears \[in order to enlarge them\], he had removed cloth roll from one of the ears and placed the reddish lily flower in its place and came with that.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that looking at the way in which kriṣṇa has decorated one ear with the reddish lily flower, yaśōdāp pirātti would feel both happy and sad. In other words, when he removed the cloth roll from one ear and inserted the reddish flower, it would have given him pain, due to which she would have felt sad. She would have felt happy, enjoying the beauty of the contrast in the decoration of his two ears.

**kōlap paṇaik kaccum kūṟai udaiyum** – dress which had been adorned on him, appropriate to his divine form and a belt \[again with cloth\], which was attractive and large, adorned over it at the waist in order to keep the cloth under it, to be in place without slipping.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that even his dress and the belt, donned over it, would have slipped when kriṣṇa had to run behind the calves. Hence, he would have had to wear those again, in a diśevelled condition. Alternatively, he would have returned with the dress draped in the same manner \[in which yaśōdāp pirātti had donned for him in the morning when he had set out to go behind the calves\], without any change in the appearance.

**kuḷir muttin kōdāḷamum** – chain, strung with cool pearls \[cool and pleasant to the eyes\], and with a curve. The term *āram* \[chain\] has got transformed here as *ālam*, in line with the rule *ralayōrabhēda* \[the sounds *la* and *ra* are interchangeable\]. Alternatively, the text could be *āram* itself.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the chain would have swayed from left side to right side when kriṣṇa went behind the calves. Some people would call the ear rings too as *kōdālam*. However, that meaning is not applicable here since kriṣṇa has decorated both his ears with two different materials \[cloth and flower\].

**kālip innē varuginṟa kadal vaṇṇan vēdattai vandu kāṇīr** – While the term *kāli* would refer to cows, as a species, here it refers to calves. yaśōdāp pirātti calls women, who are nearby, to come and have a look at the attire of kriṣṇa, who is allowing the calves to go first and comes behind them, and who has the complexion of ocean.  Here, the term *vēdam* \[attire\] refers to kriṣṇa decorating himself with the cloth roll in one ear and the reddish lily flower, in the other ear. The term *kāṇīr* refers to her inviting the women to see with their eyes, to realise the purpose of having been provided with eyes.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *kāli* would refer to calves here; alternatively, it could also refer to the herd of both cows and calves which kriṣṇa would have allowed to mix, as his mischief \[normally, cows would come separately and calves, separately to prevent calves from getting hurt when cows walk by their side\].

**jñālattu …** – Oh, those who have the quality of knowing the distinction of having good children! Among the women in the world, who have given birth to children, it is only I, who could be termed as “having given birth to a good child”. This implies the meaning that there is none who has been celebrated as I have been, as mentioned in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2.2.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/10/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-2-2-6/) “*enna nōnbu nōṟṟāḷ kolo ivanaip peṟṟa vayiṟu udaiyāḷ*” (What penance did the one, who has the divine stomach which gave birth to him, who is distinguished in this world, carryout?) for having given birth to a good son.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, for the verse *jñālam* … that in the fifty crore yōjana \[around 500 crore miles\] universe \[from pātāḷam to satya lōkam\], is there anyone who has begotten a son like yaśōdāp pirātti? Repeatedly, didn’t I alone beget him? \[first, as priśṇi and sutapā, they had begotten emperumān as priśṇigarbha; second time, as atiti and kaśyapa, they had begotten emperumān has vāmana; now, as dēvaki and vasudēva (or, as yaśōdāp pirātti and nandagōpa\], they had begotten kriṣṇa\]. Oh, those who are complete in your quality of having begotten good sons! Is there anyone who is apt to be celebrated as “*ivanaip peṟṟa vayiṟu udaiyāḷ*” other than me? This is unlike the śrī rāmāyaṇa ślōkam āraṇya kāṇḍam 15.15 “*tvayā putrēṇa*” \[śrī rāma tells lakśmaṇa “Oh, lakśmaṇa! emperor daśarata was fortunate to have had you as his son. Since you have carried out tasks for me which he would have carried out, had he been alive, I consider that my father has not died”\] \[There, śrī rāma celebrated lakśmaṇa as his father; here, yaśōdāp pirātti celebrates kriṣṇa as her son. The latter is more eminent than the former. Thus, yaśōdāp pirātti feels proud, for having given birth to kriṣṇa\].

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.3.3. 3.3.3 -Kadugaludu poy

*kādūgaḷ ūdu pōyk kanṟugaḷ mēyttu maṟiyōdik kārkkōdal pūccūdi varuginṟa dāmōdarā! kaṟṟut tūḷi kāṇ unnudambupēdai mayil sāyal pinnai maṇāḷā! nīrātti amaittu vaittēnādi amudu sey appanum uṇḍilan unnōdudanē uṇbān*

**Пословный перевод:**

kādugaḷ ūdu pōy – going through the forest; kanṟugaḷ mēyttu – grazing the calves; maṟi ōdi – running ahead of them to control them such that they do not stray; kār kōdal pū – huge kāndaḷ \[black glory lily; also called as malabar lily\] flower \[kār – black as well as eminent\]; sūdi – donning on the divine locks; varuginṟa – one who is coming; dāmōdarā – oh, dāmōdara!; un – your; udambu – throughout the divine form; kanṟu – induced by the calves; tūḷi kāṇ – dust has settled, see that; mayil pēdai – like a peahen; sāyal – having a form; pinnai – for nappinnaip pirātti; maṇāḷā – oh, the beloved!; nīrāttu – required for a bath; amaittu vaittēn – I have kept \[all the materials\] ready; ādi – after having a bath; amudu sey – you should eat; unnōdudanē – along with you; uṇbān – in order to eat; appanum – your father too; uṇḍilan – has not eaten till now. Without any delay, come soon

**Перевод:**

**Oh, dāmōdara! You have come back, after grazing the calves through the forest, running ahead of them to ensure that they do not go astray from the herd, by controlling them. See, your divine form is full of dirt which had settled on you, due to the running of calves, induced by their hoofs. Oh, one who is the beloved of nappinnaip pirātti who has the form of a peahen! I have made all the preparations for your bath. You should have a bath and have your food. In order to eat along with you, your father too has not eaten so far. Without any delay, come soon.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that yaśōdāp pirātti had earlier fed kriṣṇa and sent him behind calves. Now, to get rid of his tiredness of having grazed the calves and to ensure that the dust from calves, which had settled on his divine form get removed, she prays to him to have a bath and to have his food.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kādugaḷ …** – going through several forests, which are unlike one another, in order to find if they have sufficient water and grass for the calves to graze and also to tend to them.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that though kriṣṇa goes along the path of the calves, he also goes out looking for green pastures, with availability of water such that the calves could graze there. At the same time, he also has to go ahead of the calves and control them such that they do not go astray of the herd and get harmed by wild animals. Once the calves have had their stomachs full, kriṣṇa feels a load off his chest and becomes happy. As a result of that happiness, he decorates himself with flowers such as malabar lily etc. yaśōdāp pirātti, knowing his time of return, looks out for him closely, celebrates his arrival and calls out to him as *Oh dāmōdarā,* who is returning! She feels happy, recounting the relationship with kriṣṇa, who is under her control, and who is obedient to her.

**kanṟugaḷ mēyttu maṟi ōdi** – grazing the cows; going ahead of them in order to control them such that they do not go away from the herd.

**kārkkōdal pūccūdi varuginṟa** – After the calves have had their stomachs full \[with grass\], when they return home, kriṣṇa is pleased \[that the calves have eaten well\]. Hence, he dons huge malabar lily flowers on his divine locks and comes.

**dāmōdarā** – yaśōdāp pirātti reminds him about the way that he was obedient to her, as a child \[by allowing her to tie him to a mortar with small pieces of rope, tied together\]. Also, she wants him to be obedient to her now also.

**kaṟṟut tūḷi kāṇ un udambu** – Since you were running amidst the calves, the dust induced by their movement has settled on your entire divine form, see that.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that while his divine form, with the dust induced by the calves, is attractive to yaśōdāp pirātti, she feels that if nappinnaip pirātti were to see him, she will laugh at him derisively.

**pēdai mayil sāyal pinnai maṇāḷā** – Oh, one who is the consort of nappinnaip pirātti who has the form of a peahen! Through this, yaśōdāp pirātti hints that even though the dust has settled on him as a result of carrying out an activity in line with clan and that it appears beautiful to her just like the encasing around a gemstone, he still has to have a bath if he wishes to embrace his beloved, nappinnaip pirātti.

**nīrāttu amaittu vaittēn** – I have kept ready, all the materials required for a bath, viz. oil, tamarind, warmed up water in a vessel and gooseberry, as mentioned in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2.4.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/11/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-2-4-3/) “*kāyccina nīrodu nelli kadārattil pūrittu vaittēn*” (I have filled up the vessel with warm water along with gooseberry fruits).

**ādi amudu sey** – Instead of coming in immediately to eat, since you are tired, you should have a bath and only after that should you come for eating.

**appanum uṇḍilan unnōdudanē uṇbān** – Desiring to eat with you, your father has also not eaten. Hence, without wasting time, you should come soon, after a bath, for eating.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa that his father is waiting for him to have his food with him. Both *cētana* (jīvātmā, who has ability to think) and *paramacētana* (supreme entity, emperumān) eat from the same vessel. The meaning of taittirīya upaniśat ānandavalli 1 “*sō’śnutē sarvān kāmān saha*” (jīvātmā attains paramātmā and the two enjoy the auspicious qualities of paramātmā together) could be seen here.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.3.4. Kadiyar polil

*kadiyār poḻil aṇi vēngadavā! karum pōr ēṟē! ni ugakkumkudaiyum seruppum kuḻalum taruvikkak koḷḷādē pōnāy mālē!kadiya vem kānidaik kanṟin pin pōna siṟukkuttac cengamalaadiyum vedumbi un kaṇgaḷ sivandāy asaindittāy nī empirān*

**Пословный перевод:**

kadi Ar – full of fragrance; poḻil – having gardens; aṇi – being beautiful; vēngadavā – oh, one who resides in tiruvēngadam!; karu – having a dark form; pōr – ready for battle; ēṟē – oh, one who is prideful like a bull!; māl – oh, one who is infatuated with calves!; nī ugakkum – the ones which you desire; kudaiyum – umbrella; seruppum – sandals; kuḻalum – flute; taruvikka – even when brought; koḷḷādē – without taking (them); pōnāy – oh, one who went to graze calves!; kadiya vem – in the unbearably hot; kānidai – forest; kanṟin pin – behind calves; pōna – one who followed; siṟu kuttan – a little child, your; sengamalam – like reddish lotus flower; adiyum – divine feet; vedumbi – became hot; un – your; kangaḷ – eyes too; sivandu āy – became red; asaindittāy – you became thin; nī em pirān – She says with anguish “āren’t you, my lord?”

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who is dwelling in the beautiful hills of tiruvēngadam, which has gardens, which are full of fragrance! Oh, one who is like a proud, dark bull, which is ready for battle! Oh, one who has love towards calves! Oh, one who went behind the calves, without taking umbrella, sandals and flute, despite bringing them for you! Your lotus-like, divine feet have become hot, since you followed the calves into the hot forest. Your eyes have become reddish and you have become lean. āren’t you my lord?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that it has become a daily routine for yaśōdāp pirātti to allow him to go for grazing the calves, to await his arrival and to affectionately engage with him when he returns.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kadi …** – Oh, one who is permanently dwelling in tiruvēngadam which has gardens having fragrance fully!

**karum pōrēṟē** – Oh, one who roams around tiruvāyppādi \[śrī gōkulam\], with the form of a dark, prideful bull, ready for battle! When kriṣṇa talks to a girl in tiruvāyppādi and someone opposes that, he would fight with that person and drive him away. He would be similar to the way that it has been said in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 14.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/11/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-14-1/) “*patti mēyndōr kārēṟu*” (A dark bull, roaming around as he liked, without any restraint).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that in tiruvāyppādi, there is no need to live under the watchful eyes of sages such as vasiśta et al \[reference here is to śrī rāma who had to be under the constant watchful eyes of vasiśta, viśvāmitra et al\]. In tiruvāyppādi, people are such simple that they would not even know the difference between the left hand and right hand. He could roam wherever he liked, like a huge bull, roaming as it pleased, with pride. In this case, the word *karum* would refer to eminence. Alternatively, *karum* would also refer to dark complexion. In this case, it would refer to kriṣṇa being like a dark bull, ready to fight. This would be apt for saying *porudu nī vandāy* (you came ready to fight). He has, indeed, fought with the wrestlers \[such as cāṇūra, muśtika et al\].

**nī ugakkum** – I was going to bring the ancillaries which you like such as umbrella, which protects from rain and sunlight, sandals for the divine feet, which protect from thorn etc, and flute, which is instrumental in keeping the herd of calves in an orderly way, for grazing them and for calling them back. Oh, one who went behind the calves due to your deep affection for them, without waiting to take these!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as it has been mentioned in [stōtra ratnam 40](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/sthothra-rathnam-40/) “*nivāsa śayyā …*” (ādiśēśan functions as the throne, as the mattress etc for emperumān) and in [mudal tiruvandādi 53](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/08/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-53/) “*senṟāl kudaiyām ..*” (ādiśēśan becomes umbrella when emperumān moves), it could be said that ādiśēśan becomes the flute in kriṣṇa’s hand too. Since kriṣṇa desires to be with the calves, he went urgently behind them, without even waiting for umbrella, sandals and flute. This is the reason for addressing him as *mālē* (one who has excessive affection towards his followers).

**kadiya vem kānidaik kanṟin pin pōna** – you went behind the calves wherever they went, in the forest, which was hot.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that even as yaśōdāp pirātti has kept kriṣṇa on her lap and has embraced him, she thinks of the urge with which he had gone behind the cattle \[in the morning\]. Since the forest is said to be very hot, it would appear like a desert. Oh, the little child, who went to such a forest!

**siṟukkuttac cengamala adiyum vedumbi** – you are a little child; your divine feet, which are like reddish lotus, became heated up. Since it is mentioned as *sengamala adi*, this refers to the qualities of softness, coolness etc associated with lotus flower, for the divine feet. When the divine feet are like this \[soft and cool\], is there a need to speak about them getting heated up when going without umbrella and sandals, in the hot forest?

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that since yaśōdāp pirātti was fearful of the heat in the forest, even though she likens kriṣṇa’s divine feet to lotus flower, the divine feet appear hot even now, to her hands.

**un kangaḷ sivandāy** – when the feet are heated up, it would certainly lead to reddish eyes. Beyond this, kriṣṇa has to look out for (1) areas where the calves could graze \[which have green pastures and water\], (2) the calves to check if their stomachs are full or not, (3) proximity of wild animals, which may harm the calves, (4) checking the calves to see if any calf has gone astray from the herd. Due to looking for these constantly, the eyes will become red.

**asaindittāy nī empirān** – Oh, my lord, you have become thin! Is it only that your divine feet became hot and the divine eyes became red? When you roam around inside tiruvāyppādi, your form would be like a dark bull, ready to fight, with a form which was strong and healthy. yaśōdāp pirātti says, despising herself, that kriṣṇa has become thinned down considerably now.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as tirumaḻisai āḻvār had said in tiruccanda viruttam “*eḻundirundu pēsu*” (Looking at the reclining form of ārāvamudan in tirukkudandai, tirumaḻisai āḻvār wanted emperumān to stand up from his reclining posture and tell him the reason for his lying down), yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa that due to walking continuously in the hot forest, he has thinned down. *nī* – you, not knowing your own eminence. *empirān* – you are our protector and our benefactor. How could you become thin like this?

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.3.5. Parrar nadunga

*paṟṟār nadunga mun pānjasanniyattai vāy vaitta pōrēṟē ensiṟṟāyar singamē sītai maṇāḷā siṟukkuttaccengaṇ mālēsiṟṟādaiyum siṟuppattiramum ivai kattilin mēl vaittup pōykaṟṟāyarōdu nī kanṟugaḷ mēyttuk kalandu udan vandāy pōlum*

**Пословный перевод:**

paṟṟār – enemies such as duryōdana et al; nadunga – to tremble; mun – during mahābhārata war; pānja sanniyattai – śrī pāncajanyam \[divine conch\]; vāy vaitta – one who kept in the divine mouth and blew; pōr ēṟē – oh kaṇṇa, who is like a battle-ready bull!; en – being obedient to me; siṟu āyar singamē – oh, one who is a lion-cub for the herd folk; sītai maṇāḷā – oh, one who is sītāp pirātti’s consort!; siṟu kuttan – as a young child; sem kaṇ – having divine eyes which are like reddish lotus flowers; mālē – oh, one who is the lord for everyone!; siṟu ādaiyum – divine dress, which is appropriate for your age; siṟu – apt for your divine hand; pattirumum ivai – knife, for playing, all these; kattilin mēl – on top of the cot; vaittup pōy – kept, but forgetting; kanṟu – those who are grazing calves; āyarōdu – with herd-boys; nī – you; kanṟugaḷ mēyttu – after grazing the calves; udan kalandu – along with them; vandāy pōlum – she is happy, saying “Haven’t you come!”

**Перевод:**

**Oh, kriṣṇa, who is like a bull which is ready for battle, who kept the divine conch śrī pāncajanyam on your divine mouth, during the mahābhārata war, and blew it such that enemies such as duryōdana et al trembled! Oh, one who is obedient to me, and who is like a lion-cub for the herd folk! Oh, one who is the consort of sītāp pirātti \[during the time of śrī rāmāvatāram\]! Oh, one who is the lord for everyone even when you are a little child! While I kept your divine dress, apt for your age and a small knife, which is apt for your divine hands, with which you could play, on the cot, forgetting to take them, you had gone with the herd-boys in order to graze the calves and now, you have returned with them.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**paṟṟār …** – duryōdana et al, who became your enemies since they harmed pāṇḍavas and pāṇḍavas are dear to you, as mentioned in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam 90-32 “*mama prāṇāhi pāṇḍavā*:” (pāṇḍavas are my life); you had even refused to eat in their palaces saying, as in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam 74-27 “*dviśadannam nabhōktavyam*” (food from enemies is not fit to be eaten). Oh, one who kept the divine conch, śrī pāncajanyam on your divine lips, during the mahābhārata war and blew it such that the hearts of enemies tore apart, as mentioned in [bhagavat gīta 1-19](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/1-19/) “*sagōśō dārtarāśtrāṇām hrudayāni vyadārayat*” (the sound of that divine conch tore apart the hearts of the sons of dritarāśtra), and one who stood like a proud bull, ready for battle!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that kriṣṇa had a prideful look on his divine face when he sounded the divine conch śrī pāncajanyam, standing as the best among all the people, protecting the favourable followers and annihilating the unfavourable enemies.

**en siṟṟāyar singamē** – Oh, one who is obedient to me and who is like a lion cub to the herd-boys, roaming around with pride, along with the thousand herd-boys who are like you!

**sītai maṇāḷā**– Oh, one who is the beloved consort of sītāp pirātti, who would embrace you well, just as it has been mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 30-39 “*bhartāram pariśasvajē*” (she tightly hugged her husband), when she sees the annihilation of unfavourable entities and protection of favourable entities by śrī rāma!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti addresses kriṣṇa as *sītai maṇāḷā*, just as janaka maharāja had told śrī rāma, as in [śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 73-29](https://granthams.koyil.org/2025/07/24/sri-ramayana-thani-slokam-9-english/) “*sahadarmacarī tava*” (She will walk in the path of righteousness, along with you) and as said in [śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 30-39](https://granthams.koyil.org/2025/12/20/sri-ramayana-thani-slokam-31-english/) “*bhartāram pariśasvajē*” (She tightly embraced her divine consort). The reason for bringing sītāp pirātti here is to manifest the union, *śrīya*:*pati* (consort of śrī mahālakśmi). In an earlier pāsuram too, yaśōdāp pirātti had addressed him as *pinnai maṇāḷā* (consort of nappinnaip pirātti)

**siṟuk kuttac cengaṇ mālē** – even while remaining as a little child, oh, one who had manifested your quality of *sarvasmātparan* (superior to all) through your lotus-like eyes!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa “Oh, one who has reddish divine eyes, which hint your simplicity as well as your eminence!”

**siṟṟādaiyum …**– just as those who forget to take things kept on the mat on which they lie down, in your urgency to go behind the calves, you had forgotten to take your little dress, apt for your divine form, and the divine knife, which you use while playing, kept on your cot.

**kaṟṟāyarōdu nī kanṟugaḷ mēyttu** – grazing the calves, along with the herd boys

**kalandu udan vandāy pōlum** – yaśōdāp pirātti feels happy, seeing him returning with the herd boys, such that he could be said as “One among them”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says additionally here that yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa that he has gone with the herd-boys, taking the calves with them, and ensuring that the calves are separated from the cows while grazing.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.3.6. Anjudar ali

*anjudar āḻi un kaiyagattu ēndum aḻagā! nī poygai pukkunanjumiḻ nāgattinōdu piṇangavum nān uyir vāḻndirundēnen seyya ennai vayiṟu maṟukkināy? ēdum ōr accam illaikanjan manattukku ugappanavē seydāy kāyām pū vaṇṇam koṇḍāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

am sudar – having beautiful radiance; āḻi – divine chakra; un – your; kaiyagattu – on the divine hand; ēndum – holding; aḻagā – oh, one who has beauty!; nī – you; poygai – in the poisonous pond; pukku – immersing; nanju umiḻ – spitting poison; nāgattinōdu – with the snake, kāḷiyan; piṇangavum – when you were engaging in a battle; nān – I, your mother; uyir vāḻndirundēn – was holding my breath; ennai – me; en seyya – for what purpose; vayiru maṟukkkināy – churned the stomach; ēdum – even a little bit; ōr accam – fear; illai – you don’t have; kāyām pū – purple coloured flower; vaṇṇam – complexion; koṇḍāy – oh, one who has!; kanjan – kamsan’s; manattukku – for mind; ugappanavē – liked; seydāy – you were doing

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who has the beauty of holding the beautifully radiant divine disc on your divine hand! When you entered the poisonous pond and engaged in a battle with the snake kāḷiyan, I was holding my breath. Why did you frighten me? You do not have even a little bit of fear. Oh, one who has the complexion of a purple-coloured flower! You were engaging in activities which were pleasant to kamsan’s mind.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that yaśōdāp pirātti, recalling a peril, which happened in the past, imagines it as happening in the present, and tells kriṣṇa “You did what made your unfavourable ones happy”*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**anjudar …** – your divine hand is beautiful, as it is, such that one has to ward off evil spirits. On top of that, you are holding the divine, beautifully radiant disc on your hand. Oh, one who is holding the divine disc which complements the complexion of your divine form!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says additionally here that the entity \[divine disc\], which is meant for protection, is the cause of beauty too.

**nī poygai pukku** – You had entered the pond, not considering your tenderness, as if you had none to help you, while still having the divine disc, which reaches the place that you think of, on your divine hand.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa entered the pond, which is mentioned as in [tiruccanda viruttam 86](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/02/thiruchchandha-viruththam-86/) “*salam kalanda poygai vāy*” (it appeared that water had been added to the poisonous pond)

**nanju umiḻ nāgattinōdu piṇangavum nān uyir vāḻndirundēn** – the poisonous snake, *kāḷiyan*, was spitting poison in a furious state. When you entered the pond, he tried to tie you down with his form. You broke free from his attempts, stood atop his spread-out heads, took hold of his tail and danced on him such that he became weak and spat out blood from his mouth. Even when you were engaging in a battle with him like this, I was still alive.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that one had to guess that water was present in the pond while outwardly it appeared as if it had only poisonous liquid.

**en seyya ennai vayiṟu maṟukkināy** – Why did you frighten me like this?

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *maṟukkudal* refers to getting frightened on account of an event which took place in the past, even as yaśōdāp pirātti was keeping kriṣṇa on her lap and thinking repeatedly of his entering the poisonous pond and fighting with *kāḷiyan.*

**ēdum ōr accam illai** – if you indulge in a daring act like this, it could (1) lead to harm for you, (2) make me feel frightened, (3) make it unbearable for the world. You did not have even a little bit of fear for any of these.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa did not fear about any harm to himself, about any harm to others, about the world being unable to bear the result of his daring act, and about the fright that it would cause yaśōdāp pirātti. However, this daring act would have caused happiness to kamsan et al.

**kanjan manattukku ugappanavē seydāy** – you indulged in an action which would have made kamsan feel happy since he is waiting to see “When will a calamity befall you?”

**kāyāmbū vaṇṇam koṇḍāy** – Oh, one who has the complexion of a purple-coloured lily flower! yaśōdāp pirātti prays to kriṣṇa, feeling happy that she is alive seeing that no shortcoming came to kriṣṇa’s beautiful divine form.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa “Oh, one who stole the fresh colour from the purple-coloured lily flower!” She further says that looking at the beauty of his divine form \[coming from the colour of the flower\] and the tenderness of his divine form \[coming from the soft nature of that flower\], due to her fortune, she was able to remain alive.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.3.7. Panriyum amaiyum

*panṟiyum āmaiyum mīnamum āgiya pāṟkadal vaṇṇā! un mēlkanṟin uruvāgi mēypulattē vanda kaḷḷa asurar tammaiccenṟu pidittuc ciṟukkaigaḷālē viḷangāy eṟindāy pōlumenṟum en piḷḷaikkut teemaigaḷ seyvārgaḷ anganam āvargaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

panṟiyum – incarnating as the great boar; āmaiyum – incarnating as the tortoise; mīnamum – incarnating as the fish; pāṟkadal – like the milky ocean; vaṇṇā – oh, one who has the divine complexion!; un mēl – to harm you; kanṟin uru āgi – taking the form of a calf; mēy – where calves graze; pulattu – in the land; vandu – coming and mixing with the calves there; kaḷḷam – having deceptive acts; asurar tammai – monsters; senṟu – going to them, knowing through their actions that they are monsters; siṟu kaigaḷālē – with small hands; pidittu – catching hold of the monster, who stood in the form of a calf; viḷa – wood-apple, in which also a monster had pervaded; kāy – such that the fruit fell down; eṟindāy pōlum – haven’t you thrown!; en piḷḷaikku – towards my son; temaigaḷ – harmful acts; seyvārgaḷ – those who attempt to indulge in; enṟum – at all times; anganam āvargaḷ – let them die like that, says yaśōdāp pirātti, cursing them

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who has the divine complexion of the milky ocean, and who incarnated as the great boar, the tortoise and fish! Intending to harm you, monsters, who indulge in harmful acts, came to the land where the calves were grazing. One took the form of a calf and the other, the form of a wood-apple fruit. Knowing that they are monsters, you went to them; with your small hands, caught hold of the monster who had pervaded a calf and threw him against another, who had pervaded the wood-apple fruit. yaśōdāp pirātti says, furiously, with a curse, that those who intend to harm her son would always meet the same fate as these monsters did.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**panṟiyum āmaiyum mīnamum āgiya** – emperumān incarnated as *varāha* \[the great boar\] to lift earth \[from the demon hiraṇyākśa\], as *kūrma* \[tortoise\] to support mantara mountain \[during churning of milky ocean\] and as *matsya* \[fish\] to help during the time of deluge. This narrates his simplicity in transforming his *aprākruta* \[not made of five primordial elements, like us\] divine form and protecting the world, by taking the forms of animals. While the order of incarnations was *matsya, kūrma* and *varāha*, the reason for mentioning *varāha* first is due to the fact that apart from lifting earth, when earth had got immersed in the deluge of oceans, he had also given instructions to śrī bhūmip pirātti for uplifting *cētanas* \[those who have the ability to think\] from the ocean of *samsāram* \[materialistic realm\], by mentioning the means to attain him, in line with their basic nature. nammāḻvār too had mentioned in his [tiruviruttam 99](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/04/thiruviruththam-99/) “*ēnattu uruvāy idanda pirān – jñānappirān*” (the benefactor who lifted the earth in the form of a great boar and the benefactor who gave knowledge\]. tirumangai āḻvār too, after saying as in [periya tirumoḻi 2.6.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/11/periya-thirumozhi-2-6-2-part-1/) “*ēnattu uruvāgi nila mangai eḻil koṇḍān*” (Being in the form of the great boar, he freed the connection of śrī bhūmip pirātti (from the walls of the universe), without disturbing her beauty), had said “*jñānattin oḷi uruvai*” (one who has a luminous form, revealing knowledge). This āḻvār, in a subsequent pāsuram, periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.2.3, had said “*eyiṟṟidai maṇ koṇḍa endai irāp pagal ōduvittu*” (emperumān, who had lifted śrī bhūmip pirātti on his tusks, instructed night and day).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that āḻvārs, having been showered with knowledge and devotion, without any doubt, know the secrets of emperumān’s incarnation. This is the reason that while it is well known that *matsya* etc were the normal line of incarnations, they have composed pāsurams such as [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.5.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/08/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-1-5-11/) “*annamum mīn uruvum āḷariyum kuṟaḷum āmaiyum ānavanē*” (Oh, one incarnated as *hamsa* \[swan\], fish, *narasimha* \[lion-man\], *vāmana* \[dwarf\] and *kūrma* \[tortoise), [tiruvāimoḻi 1.8.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-8-8-anan-anayan/) “*ānānānāyan mīnōdu ēnamum*” (emperumān incarnated as kriṣṇa, as fish and as boar), this pāsuram “*panṟīyum āmaiyum mīnamum āgiya*”(incarnated as boar, tortoise and fish), changing the order in which emperumān incarnated as well as pāsurams such as periya tirumoḻi 8.8.10 “*mīnodu āmai kēḻal*” (incarnating as fish, tortoise, boar), in the regular order. This is in line with the rule “*yugē yugē sambhavāmi*” \[in every epoch, I incarnate\], which is different from [bhagavat gītā ślōkam 4.8](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/4-8/) “*sambhavāmi yugē yugē*” (I incarnate in every epoch) and as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.3.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/thiruvaimozhi-7-3-11-uzhithoruzhi/) “*vaiyam kākkum uruvum pērum seygaiyum – ūḻidōṟ ūḻi vēṟavan*” (To protect the universe, emperumān assumes a variety of forms, divine names and activities in every epoch), where it has been mentioned that emperumān takes different forms, names and activities in different epochs. Thus, āḻvārs compose their pāsurams depending on the epoch in which emperumān has shown them his activities.

**pāṟkadal vaṇṇā** – Oh, one who has a whitish divine form, like the milky ocean! During the first yuga \[epoch\], *kruta yuga*, people will have predominance of *satva guṇa* \[noble qualities\] and desire white colour. emperumān too, makes his divine form to appear white in colour, as mentioned in [tiruccanda viruttam 44](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/11/thiruchchandha-viruththam-44/) “*pālin nīrmai*” (emperumān appears white), gives refuge to the people who have *satva* *guṇa*. If the text were *pārkkadal vaṇṇā* \[instead of*pāṟkadal vaṇṇā*\], it would mean – oh, one who has the complexion of ocean which surrounds earth. It is this divine form that you transform and take the forms of animals in order to protect the worlds.

**un mēl …** – While you are the protector in all manner for the worlds, in order to harm you, monsters had taken the form of calves which you were grazing, mingling with the herd in the green pasture.

**senṟu pidittuc ciṟū kaigaḷālē** – Knowing the distinction in their activities \[these calves were not eating grass, they were looking here and there, waiting for a suitable opportunity etc to harm you\], you held them with your small hands.

**viḷangāy eṟindāy pōlum** – It appears that in order to bring down the wood-apples, a form which too the monsters had taken in order to harm you, you had thrown the calf, which one monster had taken the form of, against the wood-apple, which another monster had taken the form of, bringing both down, killing them. When kriṣṇa responded, saying “Yes, I threw that way”, …

**enṟum …** – With anger in her heart, yaśōdāp pirātti says “Those who intend to harm my son, will always end up like that”. The meaning for the term *anganam āvārgaḷ* is that they will end up like that, viz. they will get annihilated like the calf and the wood-apple.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that from the emotions in her heart, one could understand the tone in which she says these words. Those who approach \[emperumān\] with unfavourable mind-set will meet the end of their lives, not getting anywhere near him.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.3.8. Kettu ariyadana

*kēttaṟiyādana kētkinṟēn kēsavā! kōvalar indiraṟkukkāttiya sōṟum kaṟiyum tayirum kalandu udan uṇḍāy pōlumūtta mudal ilēn unṟannaik koṇḍu oru pōdum enakku ariduvāttam ilāp pugaḻ vāsudēvā! unnai anjuvan inṟu tottum*

**Пословный перевод:**

kēsavā – Oh, kēśava!; kēttu aṟiyādana – in matters regarding you, whatever has not been heard of, before this; kētkinṟēn – I am hearing now; kōvalar – herd-folk; indiraṟku – for indra \[head of celestial entities\]; kāttiya – sent; sōṟum – food; kaṟiyum – and, vegetables, appropriate for that; tayirum – curd too; kalandu – mixed together; udan – without leaving anything behind; uṇḍāy pōlum – it appears that you have eaten; ūtta – to feed every day; mudal ilēn – I do not have any means with me; un tannaik koṇḍu – keeping you; oru pōdum – even for one time in a day; enakku – for me; aridu – it is difficult for me; vāttam ilā – never fading; pugaḻ – having fame; vāsudēvā – oh, the divine son of vasudēvar!; unnai – regarding you; inṟu tottum – from today, whatever I heard about you, which I have not heard of before; anjuvan – I am afraid

**Перевод:**

**Oh, kēśava! I am hearing about you, which I have not heard of before. Herd folks had sent food, along with suitable vegetables and curd, mixed together, as offering for indra, the head of celestial entities. It appears that you have eaten them all, without leaving anything behind. I do not have the wherewithal to feed you. It is difficult for me to feed you, even once in a day. Oh, one who has fame which does not fade at all, and who is the divine son of vasudēvar! I am afraid of you, from now.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that when unfavourable entities show enmity towards kriṣṇa, he would annihilate them. When favourable entities show enmity, due to the issue with annihilating them, he had to let go of them after putting down their pride.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kēttu aṟiyādana …**– yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa “Oh, one who, being the causative factor for the birth of brahmā and rudra, has the divine name of *kēśavan*! I am hearing everything about you today, which I have not heard until now” When kriṣṇa asked her, in turn, ”What is it?” she says …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa “What shortcoming is there for you in this place? Many people have come and told me ‘Your son has taken a gigantic form and eaten up all the food there, which had been brought in many carts’. They said ‘Your son, your son’. I have not heard like this any time before this. Only today, I am hearing like this”. For the term *kēsavā*, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai quotes yaśōdāp pirātti – Apart from being the causative entity for brahma and rudra, should you be the causative entity for such a blame too?

**kōvalar …** – Herd folk have cattle as their wealth. Hence, to nurture them, they pray to indra every year for rain, and offer him food. When they were about to offer to him this year, by bringing the food in a cart, drawn by wheels, along with vegetables and curd, you had argued with them for not proffering that food to indra and had told them “Offer the food to this gōvardana hill, which protects us in all ways”, making them to offer the food in front of the hill. Just as it has been mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam, “*gōvardanō’smi*” (I am gōvardana hill), you had taken a huge form, mixed all the food together and ate up the entire lot. Many people came and told me this, as mentioned in periya tirumoḻi 10.7.7 “*pāsana nallana paṇḍigaḷāl pugappeyda adanai ellām pōyirundu angu oru bhūda vadivu koṇḍu un magan inṟu nangāy māyan adanai ellām muṟṟa vāri vaḷaittu uṇḍirundān*” (food had been brought in good vessels, in many carts; today, your son, who is capable of engaging in amazing activities, went there, took the form of a huge entity, scooped up all the food together and ate them all up). Did you do that way? Since kriṣṇa stood there, without any response …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the food was collected from each of the five lakh families of herd-folk in tiruvāyppādi as well as those who have moved in newly to that place. All the food had been loaded in many carts and taken for offering to indra. yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa, “It appears that you had asked them ‘For whom are you offering this?’ When they said that they are offering the food to indra, you had told them ‘You people do not know what is correct. īsn’t this mountain offering our cattle and us, materials such as grass, water, firewood, place to rest etc?’ On hearing this, the people there became happy and your father too praised you saying ‘He is speaking beyond his age; what a knowledge he has! What he has said should be done’ When the deity in charge of that mountain came there and ate up the food, the people there said that you had mixed up all the food, kept for one person \[indra\] and had eaten it all up” She further says “It is shameful to hear that one person ate up the food offered to another person. However, I do not have the means to feed you like this”

**ūtta mudal ilēn un dannaik koṇḍu oru pōdum enakku aridu** – I do not have any means with me to feed you food like this, which you are capable of eating. It is difficult for me to feed you even one time like this.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that in the term *un*, yaśōdāp pirātti thought of kriṣṇa’s small form and in the term *tannai*, she thought of the greatness of the food and says “It is not possible for me to feed you like this even once”. Alternatively, it could be said that she says that “I did not get to feed you food like this every day”. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai further says: Just as kriṣṇa had prevented the people of his village from offering food to another person, when he was there and thus removed their servitude to others, āḷavandār too had removed the servitude of others towards ākkiyāḻvān. It is well known that by winning over ākkiyāḻvān \[who had lorded over all the wise men in that place by making them to serve him constantly\], āḷavandār liberated all the wise people in the place from this servitude such that they could serve emperumān. It was only after removing servitude of tiruvāyppādi herd-folk \[towards others\] that kriṣṇa gained undiminiśing fame. yaśōdāp pirātti feels that one who had consumed such a large quantity of food, was nurtured by her with the quantity of food which she gave him every day without any withering on his part. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai further says that when we, who reside in divyadēsams, prevent any worship of other deities and make everyone to worship only emperumān, due to their ignorance, those deities may try and harm us. However, just like emperumān lifted the gōvardana mountain and protected the herd-folk, he would protect us too. When kriṣṇa held the mountain, indra overcame his anger of having been denied food, went into *brahmabhāvanai* \[seeking emperumān\] and told kriṣṇa to keep the mountain down. kriṣṇa told him “This is not possible. You are a strong person. These herd-folk are innocent people, who do not even know to build a house of their own and protect themselves. Your anger may rear its head again; at that time, I would have to lift the mountain and protect them again. I am comfortable in this position itself, without any tiredness”. Thus, thinking about kriṣṇa’s such strategies, we do not have to be fearful.

**vāttam ilāp pugaḻ vāsudēvā** – Oh, the son of vasudēvar, having fame which shines for ever, without diminishing! The opinion here is that due to such activities \[of eating such large quantities of food\] there should be no shortcoming to his fame.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa “Is there any shortcoming for the fame that you have, since your incarnation?” She says that hearing words about him which she hadn’t heard until then, makes her feel afraid of him. By changing the case, it could also be construed as yaśōdāp pirātti telling him that she is afraid for him \[instead of being afraid *of* him, she would be afraid *for* him\].

**unnai anjuvan inṟu tottum** – I am afraid from today, after hearing about you, who had carried activities beyond the realm of human species, which I have not heard until now, as to “What you are looking for, to do further? Will your fame diminish because of these?”

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.3.9. Tinnar vensangu

*tiṇṇār veṇsangu udaiyāy! tirunāḷ tiruvōṇam inṟu ēḻun āḷ munpaṇṇēr moḻiyāraik kūvi muḷaiyattip pallāṇḍu kūṟuvittēnkaṇṇālam seyya kaṟiyum kalattadu arisiyum ākki vaittēmkaṇṇā! nī nāḷait tottuk kanṟin pin pōgēl kōlam seydu ingē iru*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiṇ Ar – having the firmness of blowing, without slipping, in annihilating unfavourable entities; veṇ – having whiteness; sangu – śrī pāncajanyam \[the divine conch\]; udaiyāy – oh, one who has in your divine hand!; tirunāḷ – the day on which you were born; tiruvōṇam – the star, śravaṇam; inṟu ēḻu nāḷ – is the seventh day from today; mun – before that; paṇ – with tune; ēr – being beautiful; moḻiyārai – those who speak; kūvi – inviting; muḷai atti – applying divine sprout; pallāṇḍu – wishing to live for long; kūṟuvittēn – I carried out mangaḷāśāsanam \[to praise and to wish to live for long\]; kaṇṇālam – divine celebration; seyya – to conduct for śravaṇa star; kaṟiyum – cooked vegetables; arisiyum – mixed \[varieties of\] rice foods; kalattadu ākki vaittēn – kept in vessels; kaṇṇā – oh, one who is like my eyes!; nī – you; nāḷait tottu – from tomorrow; kanṟīn pin – behind calves; pōgēl – do not go; kōlam seydu – decorating with ornaments etc; ingē iru – remain here itself, without leaving the house

**Перевод:**

**Oh, one who is holding on your divine hand, the white śrī pāncajanyam, which, with firmness, blows, without slipping from its task of annihilation of unfavourable entities! Your birth-star of śravaṇam occurs on the seventh day from today. Before that, I have invited people who speak sweetly with musical tones, prepared sprouts and carried out mangaḷāśāsanam. I have prepared cooked vegetables and varieties of rice preparations for celebrating \[your birthday\] on the divine star of śravaṇam. Oh, one who is like my eyes! From tomorrow, you do not go behind the calves. Decorating yourself with ornaments etc, stay in the house itself, without leaving the house.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that yaśōdāp pirātti forbids kriṣṇa from going behind the calves.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tiṇṇār veṇ sangu udaiyāy** – Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruppallāṇḍu 2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-2-adiyomodum/) “*padaipōr pukku muḻangum appāncasanniyamum pallāṇḍē*” (May the divine conch, śrī pāncajanyam, which enters battlefields and blows, live for long), when it comes to annihilating the unfavourable entities, without slipping from that task, with firmness, śrī pāncajanyam carries out the task. Oh, one who holds such śrī pāncajanyam, which complements the complexion of your divine form, as mentioned in [tiruppāvai 26](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/01/thiruppavai-26-male-manivanna/) “*pālanna vaṇṇattu un pāncajanyam*” (the divine conch which has the colour of milk) in your divine hand!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa has the firmness resulting from annihilation of unfavourable entities and protection of favourable entities. Also, he has śrī pāncajanyam. Alternatively, he says that kriṣṇa has śrī pāncajanyam which has this firmness \[of annihilating unfavourable and protecting favourable entities\] and has the nature of being pure.

**tirunāḷ tiruvōṇam inṟu ēḻu nāḷ mun** – tiruvōṇam star, under which you were born, comes on the seventh day from today.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that this verse implies that today is the star of viśākham which is splendorous with *bhaktirūpāpannajñānam* (knowledge derived out of devotion to emperumān) and its *anuśtānam* (implementing it) \[The reference here is to the star of nammāḻvār, who has been showered *bhaktirūpāpanna jñānam* by emperumān\]. He says that just as periyāḻvār had earlier said “*attattin pattām nāḷ*” (tenth day from the star of *hastam*), here too he is hiding kriṣṇa’s divine star under which he was born.

**mun …** – Hence, in preparation for that, I had invited those who speak sweetly in a musical voice, made out sprouting seeds in pots \[this is an auspicious activity carried out before any auspicious function such as birthday, wedding day etc or carrying out annual celebrations in temples\] and carried out mangaḷāśāsanam.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that there are entities who, even when they say words such as “You” or “I” \[which are common words\], will say it with a musical note and their words would be full of *tatvajñānam* \[knowledge about the truths – mainly about emperumān\]. He says that āḻvār invited such people, carried out mangaḷāśāsanam for them and kept the sprouting seeds ready, just as he had said in [tiruppallāṇḍu 3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-3-vazhatpattu/) “*vāḻātpattu uḷḷirēl vandu maṇṇum maṇamum koṇmin*” (If you are fully engaged with servitude to emperumān in order to uplift yourselves, come and take part in the temple celebrations by carrying the divine soil). tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai further says that when the function of keeping the sprouting seeds ready for namperumāḷ’s *utsavam* \[annual celebration\] is to be held, araiyars \[scholars who sing āḻvārs’ nālāyira divya prabandam in temples in the traditional method established by nātamunigaḷ\] such as tiruvarangapperumāḷ araiyar, piḷḷai tirunaṟaiyūr araiyar, āppān tiruvaḻundūr araiyar would be invited and, along with them, our preceptors would recite tiruppallāṇḍu and make ready the sprouting seeds’ pots to signal the start of *utsavam*.

**kaṇṇālam …** – In order conduct your marriage \[birthday\] on that day, I have prepared vegetables and rice foods, storing them in vessels.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti, recalling the time when she had made dishes such as *sennel arisi siṟu paruppu* etc earlier for the divine day of śravaṇam star, recalls that here.

**kaṇṇā** – Oh, one who is like my eyes!

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as people say *kaṇṇā*, *karuttē* etc \[oh, one who is like my eyes, one who is like my treasure\], kriṣṇa is the eyes and treasure for āḻvār.

**nī nāḷait tottu kanṟin pin pōgēl** – Do not go behind calves, from tomorrow, saying that “It is my duty, in line with my clan”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa need not go behind the calves, knowing kriṣṇa’s eminence and the calves’ simplicity. Simplicity for calves comes out of remaining quiet when tethered; standing aside, during milking of the cow; during the time of grazing, obeying the tunes of kriṣṇa played by him on is flute. Since kriṣṇa has already completed grazing task for the day, yaśōdāp pirātti ordered him not to go \[permanently\] from the next day.  Since he did not agree for that, she tells him not to go for the next seven days.

**kōlam seydu ingē iru** – yaśōdāp pirātti tells kriṣṇa, in an ordering manner, to decorate himself with ornaments and other such entities \[such as sandalwood paste, flowers etc\], and stay inside the house itself.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that yaśōdāp pirātti, after telling kriṣṇa to remain after decorating himself, starts decorating him immediately.

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.
