## 3.3.10. Purrara algul

*puṟṟaravu algul asōdai nallāycci tan puttiran gōvindanaikkaṟṟinam mēyttu varak kaṇḍu ugandavaḷ kaṟpitta māṟṟam ellāmseṟṟam ilādavar vāḻ taru tenpuduvai vittu cittan solkaṟṟu ivai pāda vallār kadal vaṇṇan kaḻal iṇai kāṇbargaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

puṟṟu – growing inside an ant-hill; aravu – matching the hood of a snake; algul – waist; asōdai – having the name of yāsōdā; nal – having deep affection towards her son; āycci – herd-woman; than – her; puttiran – son; gōvindanai – one who has the divine name gōvinda resulting from his act of protecting cows; kanṟu – calves’; inam – herd; mēyttu – grazing, till their stomachs became full; vara – and returning; kaṇḍu – looking to her eyes’ satisfaction; ugandu – feeling joyous in her mind; avaḷ – she; kaṟpitta – telling him to “Do like this”, “Do like that” etc; māṟṟam ellām – all the words; seṟṟam ilādavar – those who do not have any jealousy in periyāḻvār’s activities; vāḻ taru – inhabiting; then – being beautiful; puduvai – being the controller of śrī villibuttūr; vittu cittan – mercifully composed by periyāḻvār; sol ivai – these verses; kaṟṟu – learning from an ācāryan \[preceptor\]; pāda vallār – those who are capable of reciting \[due to its sweetness, to get the benefit of having been provided tongue\]; kadal – like an ocean; vaṇṇan – kriṣṇa, who has a divine complexion, his; iṇai – matching each other; kaḻal – divine feet; kāṇbargaḷ – they will get to see and enjoy

**Перевод:**

**yaśōdāp pirātti has a waist which is similar to the hood of a snake inhabiting an ant-hill. She has deep affection towards her son, gōvindan \[kriṣṇa\]. Looking at kriṣṇa, returning from grazing calves, which have had their stomachs full due to grazing, she joyously told him words such as “Do like this” “Do like that”. periyāḻvār is the controller of beautiful śrī villibuttūr, inhabited by those who do not have any jealousy in his activities. He composed yaśōdāp pirātti’s words into these pāsurams. Those who learn these from their ācāryan and recite them, will get to see and enjoy the divine feet, which are match for each other, of kriṣṇa, who has a divine complexion similar to an ocean.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In this last pāsuram of the decad, āḻvār mentions the benefit which will accrue to one who recites all the pāsurams of this tirumoḻi \[divine verses\] and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**puṟṟara …**– herd-woman, who has the name, yaśōdāp pirātti, who has deep affection towards her son and who has a waist similar to the spread hood of a snake, which lives in its regular land \[ant-hill\], due to which it has a splendour and richness.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that yaśōdāp pirātti is referred to as *nal āycci*, not only because of the affection that she had towards kriṣṇa, as one belonging to the same clan, but because of her overflowing affection towards him.

**than puttiran gōvindanai** – her son, *gōvindan* \[protector of cows\]. It is because he was born as her son that he got the divine name, *gōvindan*.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa is referred to as her son, just like it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 2.2.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/08/periya-thirumozhi-2-2-4/) “*nandan maindan āgum nambi*” (placing himself as śrī nandagōpar’s divine son, with completeness in auspicious qualities).

**kaṟṟinam mēyttu varak kaṇḍu ugandavaḷ** – kriṣṇa would feel happy if the calves, without missing even one, ate to the fullness their stomachs. yaśōdāp pirātti would feel happy looking at such joyous kriṣṇa.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *kaṟṟinam* refers to the herd of calves. kriṣṇa made himself as one among the herd, being always with them with his heart, just as they do not separate from one another. *mēyttu* – it is not only when grown-up calves eat to the fullness of their stomachs, even for the young calves, which do not know how to graze, kriṣṇa would pluck the grass, squeeze the grass in his hands and feed that to the young ones; he would feel joyous when they eat to the fullness of their stomachs. Only then would he feel that he has grazed them well. *mēyttu varak kaṇḍu* – even if he had not grazed them in this manner, his mere returning would make yaśōdāp pirātti happy.

**avaḷ kaṟpitta māṟṟam ellām** – All the words, with which she told him “Do this” “Do that”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that all the words through which she had ordered him many times not to go behind the calves for grazing.

**seṟṟam …** – periyāḻvār, who carries out mangaḷāśāsanam, taking in favourable people with him and leaving out unfavourable ones, is the controller of the attractive śrī villibuttūr, which is inhabited by those who do not have any jealousy in the activities of periyāḻvār.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the people in śrī villibuttūr will not feel jealous of the activities of periyāḻvār when he carries out mangaḷāśāsanam, in line with all the *pramāṇams* \[authentic texts\], leaving out some people with detachment, just as he had said in [tiruppallāṇḍu 3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-3-vazhatpattu/) “*engaḷ kuḻuvinil pugudal ottōm*” (we will not allow those who serve others for food etc to enter our assembly). They will be like mentioned in [bhagavat gītā 9.1](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/9-1/) as “*anasūyavē*” (I will instruct those who do not feel jealous). Since these people, who do not have the quality of intolerance towards āḻvār, live there, the abode of śrī villibuttūr itself got uplifted. āḻvār says this verse, thinking of his pāsuram, as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.4 “*irunda ūril irukkum mānidar*” (the noble people who inhabit divine abodes) and as mentioned in [perumāḷ tirumoḻi 10.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/09/perumal-thirumozhi-10-5/) “*tiridalāl – tavamudaittu*” (since noble people keep moving from place to place, this word is fortunate). Since the term *taru* (as in *vāḻ taru*) is in the present tense, just as the verb of the first person in the first line of *dvaya mahāmantram* \[which is *prapadyē*, which means “I take refuge”, which is also in the present tense\] this indicates that with maturity, the people reach higher and higher levels of knowledge and gain appropriateness for that. It is this quality which uplifts that divine abode. This is the reason that āḻvār says *then puduvai vittu cittan*. The divine mansion \[of the presiding deity *vataperum kōyil udaiyān* there\] is the prominent place in the southern direction. Since it is the abode where nācciyār \[āṇḍāḷ\], who is the divine daughter of all the āḻvārs, incarnated and since it is the abode where *vataperum kōyil udaiyān*, who had taken āḻvār under his refuge and mercifully showered āḻvār with knowledge and devotion without any shortcoming, reclines, it is the prominent place in the southern direction, just as periya perumāḷ had looked at, with affection, the divine place \[of āṇḍāḷ\]. The term *vittucittan* refers to one who keeps viṣṇu in his divine mind. This is due to the fact that āḻvār carries out mangaḷāśāsanam constantly to various distinguished *arccā vigrahams* \[forms of emperumān in divine abodes\], to the distinguished and auspicious qualities of emperumān, to nitya vibhūti (śrī vaikuṇṭam) which is superior to taking residence as *antaryāmi* (indvelling soul) in all entities and to emperumān’s *svarūpa vyāpti* (pervading everywhere through his basic nature).

**kaṟṟu – pādavallār** – learning from an ācāryan, and reciting these pāsurams, induced by the sweetness of the pāsurams.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that for those who approach an ācāryan, learn from his divine feet these words of mangaḷāśāsanam \[divine verses of periyāḻvār\], know the inner meanings of these verses due to that learning from ācāryan, and recite the pāsurams with the pathos of periyāḻvār…

**kadal vaṇṇan kaḻal iṇai kāṇbargaḷē** – kriṣṇa’s divine complexion matches the colour of ocean, just as it has been mentioned in the 1<sup>st</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi “*kālippinnē varuginṟa kadal vaṇṇan*” (one who comes behind the calves, with the complexion of ocean\]. Those who recite these pāsurams will get to see the divine feet of kriṣṇa, which match each other, and enjoy them, just as periyāḻvār had enjoyed.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *kadal vaṇṇan* refers to emperumān who has the complexion of his divine form, similar to the ocean; it also refers to emperumān who has the nature of ocean \[unfathomable, inestimable\]. *vaṇṇam* – nature. They will get to see the divine feet of emperumān, just as āḻvār had seen and recited mangaḷāśāsanam for those divine feet in t[hiruppallāṇḍu 1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-1-pallandu/) “*sēvadi sevvit tirukkāppu*” \[protection for the beautiful, reddish divine feet\].

We shall next consider the pravēsam of the next tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.4.1. Talaigalum tongalum

*taḻaigaḷum tongalum tadumbi engum taṇṇumai ekkam mattaḷi tāḻ peelikkuḻalgaḷum gīdamum āgi engum gōvindan varuginṟa kūttam kaṇḍumaḻaigolō varuginṟadenṟu solli mangaimār sālaga vāsal paṟṟinuḻaivanar niṟpanarāgi engum uḷḷam vittu ūṇ maṟandu oḻindanarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

taḻaigaḷum tongalum – different types of umbrellas made with peacock feathers; engum tadumbi – filling up everywhere; taṇṇumai – a kind of drum (percussion instrument, typically mrudangam); ekkam – instrument with a single string; mattaḷi – another kind of drum; tāḻ peeli – wind instrument, decorated with peacock feathers; kuḻalgaḷum – different types of flutes, made with leaves, bamboo etc; gīdamum – songs, apt for the clan; engum āgi – only these, being present everywhere; gōvindan – kaṇṇapirān \[kriṣṇa\]; varuginṟa – coming together with a thousand children like him; kūttam – crowd; kaṇḍu – looking \[at them\]; maḻai kol O – “Is it an assembly of clouds; varuginṟadu – walking on the land?”; enṟu – like this; mangaimār – young girls; solli – saying joyfully; sālagam vāsal paṟṟi – holding on to windows; nuḻaivanar – entering (out of infatuation, falling head over heels); niṟpanar āgi – standing (out of fear for elders, teachers et al); engum – throughout the path in which he \[kriṣṇa\] went; uḷḷam vittu – letting their hearts go; ūṇ – food; maṟandu oḻindanar – forgot

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa, along with a thousand children who were like him, returned, with different types of peacock umbrellas present everywhere, with musical instruments such as different types of drums, instruments with single  strings, flutes, and singing songs apt for their clan. Looking at this crowd, young girls said joyfully “Is it an assembly of clouds coming on land?” They went near windows, holding on to them, looking at kriṣṇa. They were entering, going head-over heels, standing, out of fear of elders et al, losing out their hearts to the way in which kriṣṇa was going. They even forgot to eat their food.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**taḻai …** – taḻai, tongal are different types pf umbrellas made with peacock feathers. divākaran lexicon classifies these umbrellas as *taḻai, tongal, sāpālam, piccam, kuḷiri.* Though all these are types of peacock umbrellas, since there are differences in their forms, they are called as *taḻai, tongal* etc. Since the verse says *taḻaigaḷ* in the plural number, it is evident that *tongal* too are many.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that *taḻai* refers to umbrella, *tongal* refers to umbrella made of peacock feathers.

**tadumbi engum** – filled up everywhere.

**taṇṇumai** – a distinguished type of auspicious musical instrument. *ekkam* – instrument with a single string. *mattaḷi* – another type of drum. Alternatively, *ekkammattaḷi* could be considered as a single instrument, referring to a type of drum.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *taṇṇūmai* is a small drum tied to the waist and played. *ekkam* refers to a drum with the skin on only one side. *mattaḷi* refers to a drum which makes loud noise.

**tāḻ peeli** – a type of wind instrument \[like a trumpet\], decorated with peacock feathers. The peacock feathers could be either on top or below the instrument.

**kuḻalgaḷum** – different types of flute, made with leaf or bamboo.

**gīdamum** – singing songs, apt for the herd-clan

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that apart from singing, they were also dancing. Alternatively, *taḻai* would refer to tender leaves supported with sticks. Also, decorated with peacock feathers. *tongal* – garland atop umbrella. Garland made of leaves.

**āgi engum** – wherever one looked, only these could be seen.

**gōvindan varuginṟa kūttam kaṇḍu** – kriṣṇa has coronated himself as protector of cattle. Looking at the crowd of kriṣṇa coming along with a thousand children, who are just like him.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *gōvindan* refers to one who protects cattle; it also refers to one who has cattle. One who is capable of stealing the eyes and hearts of beholders, instead of letting the senses to go after worldly pursuits.

**maḻai koḷo varuginṟadu enṟu solli mangamār** – young girls, joyously ask “Is it an assembly of clouds walking on land?”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the girls were saying joyously “How amazing is this!”

**sālaga vāsal paṟṟi** – approaching windows

**nuḻaivanar niṟpanar āgi** – due to infatuation with kriṣṇa, they are hitting against one another. Due to hurdles such as the window, or fear of elder relatives in the room or their own pride of being a woman, they stand, without going further.

**engum uḷḷam vittu** – losing their hearts behind the path in which kriṣṇa went

**ūṇ maṟandu oḻindanar** – They forgot their food. Don’t they need their hearts to think of food? However, their hearts have followed kriṣṇa. How could those, without hearts, think of food? Hence, instead of saying *maṟandanar* \[forgot\], the verse says *maṟandu oḻindanar* \[they have completely forgotten about the entity called as food\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here – Could they recall that they have eaten in the past, if they do not have their hearts? For those who have eaten now, is it possible to eat? \[looking at kaṇṇan itself is equivalent to eating. Thus, once they have looked at him, is it possible to eat again?\] *oḻindanarē* – they have changed to such an extent that it would appear that forever hereafter, they will not expect to eat.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.4.2. Vallinun idal

*valli nuṇ idaḻ anna ādai koṇḍu vasaiyaṟat tiruvarai virittu uduttuppalli nuṇ paṟṟāga udai vāḷ sāttip paṇaikkaccu undip pala taḻai naduvēmullai anna naṟū malar vēngai malar aṇindu pallāyar kuḻām naduvēelli am pōdāgap piḷḷai varum edir ninṟū inavaḷai iḻavēnminē*

**Пословный перевод:**

valli – creeper kaṟpagam \[a celestial plant\]; nuṇ – tender; idaḻ anna – soft complexion, like petal; ādai koṇḍu – with dress; vasai aṟa – without any damage (very well); tiru arai – in the divine waist; virittu uduttu – donning, in a spread-out manner; paṇaikkaccu – a huge belt; undi – raising; palli – lizard; nuṇ paṟṟāga – just like it holds on a wall, without any gap; udai vāḷ – divine dagger; sātti – donning it; pala taḻai naduvē – amidst many umbrellas made of peacock feathers; nal – being beautiful; naṟu – wafting fragrance; mullai malar – jasmine flowers; vēngai malar – yellow coloured flower \[marsupium, from kino tree\]; aṇindu – stringing and donning them; pal – many; āyar – herd-boys; kuḻām naduvē – amidst their assembly; elliyam pōdu āga – during the time of dusk; piḷḷai – kaṇṇan \[kriṣṇa\], son of nandagōpar; varum – he will come; angu – in that path; edir ninṟu – standing opposite him; inam vaḷai – solid bangles (lying on your hands); iḻavēnmin – do not lose (this pāsuram is in the words of friends who warn one another)

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa had worn a dress, which was soft, like the tender petals of kaṟpagam creeper, and having its complexion too. He had donned it, without any fault, on his divine waist, spreading it well. On top of that, he had worn a big upper cloth too, like a belt, taking it up. Just like a lizard holds on firmly to the walls, without any gap, he had kept a divine short sword, inside the upper garment. āmidst many umbrellas, made of peacock feathers, he had donned a garland, strung together with beautiful, fragrant jasmine flowers and vēngai flowers. He will come in the midst of many herd-boys, during the time of dusk. Do not go in front of him, in the path through which he comes and lose your bangles.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that those who lost their hearts out when they saw kriṣṇa returning \[from grazing\], now forbid, saying “Do not stand in front of him”*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**valli …** – taking a cloth which was as soft as the tender petal of *kaṟpaga* creeper, having its colour too.

**vasaiyaṟat tiruvarai virittu uduttu** – wearing that dress well, on his divine waist, spreading it well. The term *vasaiyaṟa* refers to being without any blemish. Even if the dress is good, one needs a capability to wear it well. Just as it has been mentioned in śrī rangarāja stavam 10 “*kauśēya puśpita katī tatam*” (the divine waist itself appears to have blossomed), he had worn it well.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *valli* refers to a creeper which has taken the support of *kaṟpaga* tree to nurture itself. kriṣṇa’s dress was as soft as the flower from this creeper. The way he had donned the dress on his divine waist appeared as if the divine waist had blossomed.

**palli …  paṇaikkaccu undi – palli nuṇpaṟṟāga udaivāḷ sātti** – on top of the cloth worn on the divine waist, kriṣṇa had worn an upper garment \[like a belt\], without any crumpling in it, spreading it over the top and pulling it up firmly. In between, he had kept a divine, small sword \[like a dagger, as a safety to take care of wild animals, while going with the cattle for grazing, inside forests\], which was tucked in, just like a lizard holds firmly onto walls, without any gap. It did not appear as if the sword had been placed inside the upper garment. It appeared as if it had been born with the cloth and found its place when the cloth was worn by kriṣṇa.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *palli* would refer to a plant whose root has blended well with the soil. kriṣṇa had kept the short divine sword on his waist, below the upper garment, just like the root of the plant had blended well with the soil. Alternatively, *palli* would refer to a lizard.

**pala taḻai naduvē** – amidst many umbrellas of peacock feathers.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa was walking in the midst of herd-boys who were holding umbrellas of peacock feathers; alternatively, he was walking amidst herd-boys who were holding foliage of plants.

**mullai …** – wearing a garland, strung with fragrant jasmine flowers, which hadn’t lost their freshness, along with *vēngai* flowers, in line with the custom of his clan.

**pallāyar kuḻā naduvē** – Just as it has been said [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2026/03/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-3-1/) “*tannēr āyiram piḷḷaigaḷ*” (a thousand boys matching him), kriṣṇa came in the midst of an assembly of herd-boys, who were like him in their capabilities, and who were constantly vorśipping him.

**elliyampōdāgap piḷḷai varum** – During the time of dusk, the divine son of śrī nandagōpar will come.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as emperumān wears the *vanamālai* \[a divine chain\] as a distinctive identification for him when he is with nityasūris, kriṣṇa was donning the garland of jasmine and *vēngai* flowers, as a distinct identification, while coming amidst herd-boys.

**edir ninṟu angu inavaḷai iḻavēnminē** – Do not go opposite him, when he comes in his path, stand there and lose all your bangles. The actions of standing in his path and losing the bangles are not two different actions \[the moment they stand opposite him in the path when he comes, the bangles will disappear\]. Since the pāsuram says *inavaḷai iḻavēnmin*, it says that there is none who could save even one bangle.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.4.3. Surigaiyum terivillum

*surigaiyum teṟivillum seṇḍu kōlum mēlādaiyum tōḻanmār koṇḍu ōdaoru kaiyāl oruvan tan tōḷai ūnṟi ānirai inam meeḷak kuṟitta sangamvarugaiyil vādiya piḷḷai kaṇṇan manjaḷum mēniyum vadivum kaṇḍāḷarugē ninṟāḷ en peṇ nōkkik kaṇḍāḷ adu kaṇḍu ivvūr onṟu puṇarkkinṟadē*

**Пословный перевод:**

surigaiyum – short sword; teṟivillum – catapult; seṇḍu kōlum – stick with bunch of flowers; mēl ādaiyum – upper garment; tōḻanmār – friends (who cannot tolerate separation from him, even for a moment); koṇḍu – carrying in their hands; ōda – as they followed (to give him when required, without any delay); oruvan than – a dear friend’s; tōḷai – shoulder; oru kaiyāl – with one divine hand; ūnṟi – firmly supporting; A nirai – cattle; inam – herd; meeḷa – in order to return; kuṟitta – blew; sangam – holding conch; varugaiyil – during the time of return; vādiya – wilting; piḷḷai – being young; kaṇṇan – kaṇṇan’s; manjaḷum – turmeric; mēniyum – complexion of the divine form; vadivum – the beauty of individual limbs and of the collective divine form; arugē – near the path, by which he returns; ninṟāḷ – one who stood; en peṇ – my daughter; kaṇḍāḷ – saw (like everyone else) (moreover, since it was a rare sight); nōkkik kaṇḍāḷ – looked at him desirously, with her eyes; adu kaṇḍu – looking at the manner in which she looked at him; i Ur – those in this village; onṟu puṇarkkinṟadu – are creating a connection between kriṣṇa and my daughter

**Перевод:**

**Friends of kriṣṇa, who would not tolerate any separation from him, went behind him, carrying his short sword, catapult, stick with a bunch of flowers and his upper garment, in order to give him when he required. kriṣṇa supported his divine hand on the shoulders of one dear friend, and held the conch, with which he would gather the cattle by blowing on it, in order to return home. As the young kriṣṇa came in this fashion, looking at his wilting form, the fresh turmeric, the complexion of his divine form, beauty of his individual limbs and of the collective divine form, my daughter stood in the way, by which he was returning. She saw him, just like everyone else. Since it was a rare sight to behold, she looked at kriṣṇa with desirous eyes. As a result, the people in the village are creating a connection between my daughter and kriṣṇa, says the mother of the girl.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that this pāsuram is in the words of a mother, negating the words of blame heaped on her daughter.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**surigai …** – When kriṣṇa goes behind cattle for grazing, he goes with necessary implements for annihilating enemies as well as for playing. In the earlier pāsuram, there was mention about “*udaivāḷ sātti*” (keeping a short sword). Here, *surigai* refers to another type of short sword, thus implying accessories for annihilating enemies. Since they \[herd-folk\] go and engage with enemies in fighting, weapons are required. *teṟivil* refers to catapult. This and *seṇḍukōl* (stick with a bunch of flowers tied at one end\] are implements for playing. These and …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *surigai* would refer to a weapon. However, it could also be considered as an implement for playing since the next two words *teṟivillum* and *seṇḍukōlum* refer to implements for playing.

**mēlādaiyum** – while going out for grazing cattle, apart from the dress worn on the waist, apt for it, for the upper dress \[like a belt\] worn over the dress on the waist, another upper garment is worn, covering that and the upper part of the divine form.

**tōḻanmār koṇḍu ōda** – kriṣṇa’s friends, who are of his age, who are his friends, who cannot tolerate separation from him even for a moment, carry these \[weapons, implements for playing and upper garment\] in their hands, going a step behind kriṣṇa, such that when required, they could hand it over to him immediately.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 5.8.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/02/periya-thirumozhi-5-8-1/) “*ugandu tōḻan nī*” (\[śrī rāma tells guhap perumān\] affectionately that you are a friend), apart from kriṣṇa being affectionate towards his friends, his friends were also affectionate towards him. They considered these materials \[weapons, implements for playing, upper garment etc\] as *puruśārtam* (ultimate benefits)

**oru kaiyāl oruvan than tōḷai ūnṟi** – unlike the friends mentioned in the previous term, this person is a dear friend for kriṣṇa, and who would counsel kriṣṇa with what is good for him. kriṣṇa keeps one hand on the shoulder of this friend.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai adds here that even when that friend tells things which are good for kriṣṇa, he would tell them in a manner which will make them to be desirous for kriṣṇa.

**ānirai inam meeḷak kuṟitta sangam** – with the other hand, kriṣṇa holds the conch with which he blows, to gather the cattle to return to where he is standing. While blowing the conch, there is a way for getting them ready to go for grazing, a way for calling them back for returning, a way to ensure that they do not go astray while walking \[for grazing or returning\]. The cattle would know the distinction among these calls. Since it is dusk time, the pāsuram says “*meeḷak kuṟitta sangam*” (sounding the conch to gather the cattle for returning home\]. This sound is also a signal to the girls in tiruvāyppādi, to tell them that he is returning, just as he had blown his pāncajanyam to send a message to rukmiṇip pirātti \[śrī mahālakśmi\] about his arrival.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa was returning, holding the divine conch in his divine right hand. It would also refer to kriṣṇa returning, with the conch with which he had called all the cattle to gather and return home. The cattle know the purpose for which he blows the conch. The sound of the conch also told people to not lose themselves in lowly pursuits such as going after women, but to uplift themselves to attain emperumān, as mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.10.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-2-sadhirila-madavar/) “*sadir iḷa madavār tāḻcciyai madiyādu…*” (not getting attached to damsels who are intelligent and mesmerising, through their youthfulness). Through this, it is said that in order to correct and uplift those who are as good as animals \[in terms of their knowledge about emperumān and their activities in attaining and serving emperumān\], emperumān takes the help of an ācārya. Here, ācārya is considered as being similar to conch – being pure white in heart, knowing the words of emperumān, being servile to his ācārya, having the qualities to help others, always interested in the vellness of disciples, such that without the ācāryan, even emperumān would find it difficult to correct and uplift the samsāris, despite various methods employed earlier – giving the samsāris bhagavat gītā, carrying out *abhayapradānam* \[giving refuge to vibhīśaṇa at seashore near tiruppullāṇi\], reciting śrī varāha carama ślōkam, instructing śrī pāncarātram etc. It is for this reason that nammāḻvār said, as in [tiruviruttam 96](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/04/thiruviruththam-96/) ”*vētkai eḻuvippan*” (Though you \[referring to emperumān\] have created many different paths for people to attain their goals, created many philosophies due to differences in the levels of knowledge of people, created many deities for all those philosophies, I will create desire in the minds of samsāris towards you). It is for a similar reason that parāśara bhattar said in bhattar mugdakam “*mrujña madyastvatvam*” (searching for a neutral person to establish emperumān’s supremacy).

**varugaiyil vādiya piḷḷai kaṇṇan** – due to his tender nature, kriṣṇa was tired, having to go behind the cattle throughout the day. He was also showing fatigue, having separated from the herd-girls through the day. Such kriṣṇa’s …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother is calling kriṣṇa as *piḷḷai* \[child\] though he is *yuvākumāra*: \[adolescent, entering the stage of youth\], since she is concerned about her daughter and wants to negate the damaging words of the people in the village.

**manjaḷum mēni …** – herd-girls would use kriṣṇa’s dark divine form to check the quality of turmeric. Hence, his form would be full of yellow marks. When he returned from grazing the cattle, the yellow marks as well as the dark form, which was complementing the yellow marks, the beauty of his individual limbs as well of the collective form as a whole, were attractive enough for everyone to see him. The narrator’s \[of this pāsuram\] daughter too saw him returning, with these features.

**nōkkik kaṇḍāḷ** – she was on her way to playing; looking at the rare-to see sight of kriṣṇa returning with all these features, she looked at him with a little bit more of focus.

**adu kaṇḍu ivvūr onṟu puṇarkkinṟadē** – looking at the way that she looked at kriṣṇa, the people of this village are imagining that she looked at him with affection. *onṟū puṇarttal* – refers to creating a connection between the girl and kriṣṇa, when there was none between them.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says at the end that the mother is wondering whether kriṣṇa and her daughter are the cause for the people of the village to imagine a link. He further says that this is the reason for āḻvār composing the pāsuram *aiya puḻudi*, which we will learn about in a subsequent pāsuram. Through this, it appears that for those who are involved completely with their ācāryas, involving with the distinguished sighting of emperumān too is not acceptable.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.4.4. Kunru eduttu

*kunṟu eduttu ānirai kātta pirān kōvalanāyk kuḻal ūdi ūdikkanṟugaḷ mēyttut tan tōḻarōdu kalandu udan varuvānait teruvil kaṇḍuenṟum ivanai oppārai nangāy! kaṇḍu aṟiyēn ēdi! vandu kāṇāyonṟu nillā vaḷai kaḻanṟu tugil ēndu iḷa mulaiyum en vasam allavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōvalan āy – as one born in the clan of herd-folk; kunṟu – gōvardana hill; eduttu – taking it as an umbrella; A nirai – herds of cattle; kātta – one who protected (when rain poured for seven days); pirān – benefactor; kuḻal – flute; ūdi ūdi – playing on it, repeatedly; kanṟugaḷ mēyttu – grazing the calves; than tōḻarōdu – with his friends, who went with him; kalandu – along with; udan varuvānai – one who came together; teruvil kaṇḍu – seeing on the street; nangāy – oh, one who is complete with the qualities of femininity!; enṟum – forever; ivanai oppārai – those who are like him; kaṇḍu aṟiyēn – I have not seen; ēdi – oh, my friend!; vandu kāṇāy – Come and see; tugil – dress; kaḻanṟu – slipping such that it would not remain on the waist; vaḷai – bangles on the hand; onṟum nillā – none is staying; ēndu – being raised; iḷa – youthful; mulaiyum – bosoms too; en vasam alla – are not under my control

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa, born in the clan of herd-folk, is the benefactor, who protected the herds of cows when he lifted the hill gōvardana when it poured for seven days. Oh, one who is complete with the qualities of femininity! I have not seen people like him, playing continuously on the flute and coming together along with friends who had gone with him, for grazing calves. Come and see him. After seeing him, my dress is not staying on my waist and the bangles too are not remaining on my hands. My young bosoms, which are raised, are not under my control.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that this pāsuram describes the people of the village calling one another and pointing out to kriṣṇa returning \[home\].*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kunṟu enduttu ānirai kātta pirān** – indra, the lord of celestial entities, was angry since he was denied food by kriṣṇa. He showed his anger by making rain to pour hailstorm on śrī gōkulam. Just as it has been mentioned in [tirunedundāṇḍakam 13](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/11/thirunedunthandakam-13-part-1/) “*kal eduttuk kalmāri kāttāy*” (one who lifted the mountain to protect the herds and herd-folk from hailstorm), kriṣṇa, being the benefactor, lifted the mountain gōvardana itself, which he had earlier identified as the protector, like an umbrella, ensuring that not a drop of rain fell on either the cattle or the people.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: *kunṟu … – kōvalanāyk kuḻal ūdi – kunṟeduttu ānirai kātta pirān* – kriṣṇa played on the flute, without showing any trace of tiredness, while carrying out the activities of lifting the mountain \[gōvardana\], playing on the flute, protecting the cattle, grazing the cattle etc, as one who cares for them. If it were not this way, what is the connection between lifting the mountain and playing on the flute? For one who cares, lack of tiredness will be manifested in the way that one is playing the flute. The reason for lack of tiredness is because of lack of blemish in the entities to be protected, viz. among the five lakh families \[living in śrī gōkulam\], not erecting gates for their houses \[and leaving the responsibility of protecting them with kriṣṇa\].It is worth recalling here the verse in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.8.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-8-4-verpai-onreduththu/) “*veṟpai onṟeduttu oṟkam inṟiyē niṟkum ammān*” (the lord, who is standing, without feeling tired, after lifting up the gōvardana hill). It is only because he is a herd person that he could lift the hill and play on the flute. This would not have been possible for *cakravartit tirumagan* \[śrī rāma\]. Since the verse is repeated (*ūdi ūdi*), in the present tense, it is clear that it was not to feign that kriṣṇa did it \[He was really playing on the flute repeatedly\].

**kōvalanāy** – It is his birth in the clan of the herd-folk which is the reason for his action in the previous verse and the succeeding verse. The term *āy* \[in *kōvalan āy*\] conveys the meaning that in his nature as a herd-person, there was no blemish. It is for this reason that, deciding that “cows, which are to be protected, should not be harmed in any way”, he kept the mountain aloft for seven days continuously. During this period, he did not have even a little bit of tiredness. The reason for this is that among the entities to be protected \[cattle as well as herd-folk\], none made any attempt on their own, in protecting themselves.

**kuḻal ūdi ūdi** – this is also an activity on account of having been born in the clan of herd-folk. The reason for repeating the word \[*ūdi ūdi*\] is on account of the fact that he had to play on the flute with different tunes to get the cattle to prepare for going for grazing at the time of dawn, to keep them without going astray while going or grazing and to gather them at the time of dusk to return home.

**kanṟugaḷ …** – when he returned in the evening after ensuring that the calves had eaten to their fill, he appeared as one among his friends without any distinction.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that calves do not look alike. Even when they graze as a herd, their forms will be distinctly known. Since he is returning together with a thousand other herd-boys who are like him, to emphasise on the difficulty in identifying him from the rest, the verse says “*kaṇḍu*” (saw). This is like getting back a material which had been lost. t*heruvil kaṇḍu* – This is the blemish with the girl. She only saw him; she did not tell him “Come to my house”.

**enṟum …**– Oh, one who is complete in all qualities \[a herd-girl addressing her friend\]! I have not seen anyone who matches him, ever. Apart from seeing kriṣṇa herself, she is calling her friend to come and have a look at him. Through the term *nangāy* \[one who is full in all the qualities\], she is specifically referring to the friend’s quality of ensuring fulfilment of an errand that she had thought of. The term *ēdi* refers to addressing a friend. According to tamiḻ lexicon, words such as *ellē*, *ēdi* are terms referring to addressing a female-friend who is near one. Though kriṣṇa has been coming every day like this, since the girl says *enṟum ivanai oppārai …*, that she has not seen someone like kriṣṇa ever, this clearly states that he is forever a rare person to see. This also confirms that there is nothing analogous to equate with kriṣṇa. The words *nangāy* and *ēdi* show that the friend is an acceptable person and that she is in close proximity. *vandu kāṇāy* shows that she is asking her friend to come and see kriṣṇa for her sake.

**onṟu …** – She refers to the changes \[in her form\], soon after seeing kriṣṇa.

**tugil-kaḻanṟu-vaḷai-onṟum-nillā** – The dress, not fitting on the waist, got loosened from it. Even one among the bangles on the hands, despite trying to stop from slipping, did not stay put on the hands.

**ēndiḷa mulaiyum en vasam allavē**– Even the bosoms, which are raised and young, are not under my control. Just as it has been mentioned in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 5.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/08/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-5-7/) “*kongai kiḷarndu kumaittuk kudugalittu āviyai āgulam seyyum*” (the bosoms swelled, and becoming joyous, will melt and make my life distressed), the bosoms, on their own, swelled and troubled me.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the herd-girl says that even if kriṣṇa stands in the street, my dress and bangles are not remaining in their positions. She says that even if an elephant, which has brought down its *mahout* \[keeper\] stands, my bosoms, which have gone beyond their holding bodice, are not under my control.

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.4.5. Surri ninru

*suṟṟi ninṟu āyar taḻaigaḷ idac curuḷ pangi nēttirattāl aṇindupaṟṟī ninṟu āyar kadait talaiyē pādavum ādak kaṇḍēn anṟippinmaṟṟoruvarkku ennaip pēsal ottēn mālirum sōlai em māyaṟku allālkoṟṟavanukku ivaḷām enṟu eṇṇik kodumingaḷ kodīr āgil kōḻambamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āyar – herd-boys, who are kriṣṇa’s friends; suṟṟi ninṟu – remaining in a surrounding manner; taḻaigaḷ – umbrellas with peacock feathers; ida – as they held, aptly for his divine form; suruḷ – curled; pangi – divine locks; nēttirattāl – with peacock feathers; aṇindu – decorating; āyar – herd-folk’s; kadaittalai – in front of herd-folk’s houses; paṟṟi ninṟu – keeping their hearts; pādavum ādavum kaṇḍēn – I saw them, singing and dancing; anṟippin – apart from him \[kriṣṇa\] who is like this; maṟṟu oruvarkku – for someone else; ennai – me; pēsal ottēn – I will not allow to speak about; mālirum sōlai – in tirumālirum sōlai; en – one who made me as existing for him; māyarvarkku allāl – apart from emperumān, who is with amazing powers; koṟṟavanukku – he, who is victorious; ivaḷ Am – she is apt; enṟu eṇṇi – thinking this way; kodumingaḷ – give; kodīr āgil – if you do not give this way; kōḻambam – confusion for you all

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa was surrounded by his friends, holding umbrellas made of peacock feathers, to protect his divine form. They decorated his curled divine locks with peacock feathers. I saw him singing and dancing in front of the houses of these herd-boys. Apart from him, I will not allow you people to look for a suitable consort for me. Think in your minds and give me in marriage to the victorious one who is the amazing emperumān, residing in tirumālirunjōlai, who made me as his. If you do not give me this way, it will lead to confusion for you all.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**suṟṟi ninṟu āyar taḻaigaḷ ida** – herd-boys, who are kriṣṇa’s divine and dear friends, surround him, holding umbrellas made of peacock feathers, to prevent rain and sunshine from falling on him.

**suruḷ pangi nettirattāl aṇindu** – combing the divine locks and decorating the locks with the eyes of peacock feathers.

**paṟṟī ninṟu āyar tam kadait talaiyē pādavum ādavum kaṇḍēn** – I saw kriṣṇa, with his heart fitting well, standing near the houses of herd boys, singing and dancing. *paṟṟi ninṟa* – standing near the houses of herd-folks. *āyar kadait talai* – our houses

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that tiruvāyppādi is the dwelling place for kriṣṇa, who severs the servitude of the people living there, to any other deity.

**anṟīppin maṟṟoruvarkku ennaip pēsal ottēn** – apart from him, who is \[eminent\] like this, I will not allow you people to speak about my marriage with anyone else. If you think about someone, I cannot do anything. However, if you speak about that, I will perish. She speaks in a manner which is similar to āṇḍāḷ in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 1.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/06/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-1-5/) “*mānidavarkku enṟu pēccup padil vāḻagillēn*” (I will not survive if you speak about marrying me to a person in human species). In order to hear from her mouth as to who she is referring to you, when she was asked “Who is that person, apart from whom you will not marry anyone else?” she says…

**mālirum sōlai em māyarkku allāl** – The reason for saying this way, instead of saying “Apart from kriṣṇa” is to trace the lineage of kriṣṇa. When speaking about lineage, the gōtram \[starting point of a clan\] has to be mentioned. She says that she is referring to the one who is with amazing power, who made her as exclusively his own, just as he made tirumālirum sōlai as exclusively his. More than tiruvāyppādi, it is tirumālirunjōlai which is exclusive for emperumān. It is only during the time of incarnation that he chose tiruvāyppādi whereas his permanent residence is only in tirumālirunjōlai.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when tracing the origin of kriṣṇāvatāram, instead of saying *paramapadam*, āḻvār is saying tirumālirunjōlai. It is in tirumālirunjōlai that emperumān has completeness of his auspicious qualities, as mentioned in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 9.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/09/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-9-3/) “*tiru viḷaiyādu tiṇ tōḷ tirumālirunjōlai nambi*” (the one, who has completeness of auspicious qualities, has firm shoulders which are the playing arena for śrī mahālakśmi). She tells the people nearby to unite her with the one who resides in tirumālirunjōlai, an entity who āṇḍāḷ too, spoke about in her [nācciyār tirumoḻi 9.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/09/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-9-6/) “*mālirunjōlai nambikku – vāy nērndu parāvi vaittēn*” (for the one who has completeness of qualities and who resides in tirumālirunjōlai, I proffered through my words…). While the herd-girls live for kriṣṇa only, āḻvār mercifully speaks about tirumālirunjōlai only.

**koṟṟavanukku** – *koṟṟam*-victorious. Even if you do not give me \[in marriage\] to him, he is one who will not let go of one who is “his”. He is one who took rukmiṇip pirātti \[śrī mahālakśmi\] as his when arrangements were being made for marrying her to śiśupālan, as mentioned in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 11.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/10/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-11-9/) “*aṇṇāndirukkavē āngu avaḷaik kaippiditta*” (when śiśupālan was looking at the sky, emperumān took hold of rukmiṇip pirātti’s hand\].

**ivaḷām enṟu eṇṇik kodumingaḷ** – give me in marriage to him such that people do not say that “she went on her own”. Just as hanuman had said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16.5 “*tulya śeelā vayō vruttām*” (sītāp pirātti has her nature, age and activities matching those of śrī rāma), one who is similar. Give me in marriage to him, as mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 73.24 “*sahadarma carī tava pratīccacainām*” (She is capable of carrying out righteous activities with you, accept her).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the herd-girl \[who is speaking these verses in the pāsuram\] thinks of herself as being the daughter born in the clan of janaka and as the daughter of periyāḻvār. After seeing kriṣṇa in tiruvāyppādi, she has forgotten that she was born in tiruvāyppādi.

**kodeeṟāgil kōḻambamē** – If you do not give me like that, it would lead to confused state of mind for you all. I cannot step back from going ahead \[with him\]. She is like cintayanti \[cintayanti was living in tiruvāyppādi; one day, while she was inside the house, she heard the music from the flute played by kriṣṇa. She wanted to go out to where he was; however, her in-laws and teachers were sitting in her path. She stood there, happy hearing his flute; she stood there, sad that she could not go to him. Happiness that she felt removed all her *puṇya* (virtues) and sadness removed all her *pāpas* (sins); with her sins and virtues removed, she attained *mōkśam* (śrī vaikuṇṭam)\]. She says that their confusion does not have any purpose. With her death, everything will come to an end, she says.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the herd-people will have confusion only, if they do not give the herd-girl in marriage to kriṣṇa. He quotes from śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 16.19 “*sarvān bhōgān parityajya*” (abandoning all the comfort \[in palace\], sītāp pirātti, impelled by her love towards her consort, śrī rāma, went to the forest) and śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 30.18 “*nirayōyastvayā vinā*” (where I am not with you is hell for me, says sītāp pirātti to śrī rāma) to say that the herd-girl will go with kriṣṇa irrespective of anything else. Their \[herd-folk’s\] confusion will end with perishing only.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.4.6. Sinduram ilanga

*sinduram ilangat tan tiruneṟṟī mēl tiruttiya kōṟambum tirukkuḻalumandaram muḻavat taṇ taḻaikkāvin kīḻ varum āyarōdu udan vaḷai kōl vīzaandam onṟillāda āyap piḷḷai aṟīndu aṟīndu ivvīdi pōdumāgilpandu koṇḍān enṟu vaḷaittu vaittup pavaḷa vāy muṟūvalum kāṇbōm tōḻi!*

**Пословный перевод:**

than – on his; tiru neṟṟi mēl – applied on the divine forehead; sinduram – vermillion powder; ilanga – to shine; tiruttiya – applied properly, over that; kōṟambum – ancient ornament for the forehead; tiruk kuḻalum – divine locks, which are complementary to that; ilanga – to be resplendent; andaram – throughout the sky; muḻavam – to reverberate with the sounds of musical instruments; taṇ – cool; taḻai – umbrella with peacock feathers; kāvin kīḻ – below the garden; varum – coming with him; āyarōdu udan – along with herd-boys; vaḷai kōl – curved sticks; vīsa – as they throw (shouting victoriously); onṟu – each of them (in terms of decoration); andam illāda – unable to see the boundary; āyap piḷḷai – one who is a herd-boy; aṟindu aṟindu – knowing that I couldn’t exist without him and knowing that he could; i vīdi – on this street; pōdum āgil – if he comes; pandu – “Our ball; koṇḍān – (when we were playing) he snatched and went”; enṟu – complaining this way; vaḷaittu vaittu – preventing him from going anywhere outside; pavaḷam – like coral; vāy – divine lips; muṟuvalum – smile; tōḻi – Oh, my friend!; kāṇbōm – let us see and enjoy \[this pāsuram is in the manner of friends speaking to one another, this way\]

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa has his divine forehead shining with the vermillion applied on it. Over that, he has the aptly applied divine ornament on his forehead, which too is splendorous. His divine locks, which are complementary to that golden ornament, too are resplendent. With the sounds of musical instruments reverberating throughout the sky, with his friends coming with him, holding the umbrellas made of peacock feathers like a garden, they keep throwing curved sticks at one another, along with shouts of victory, in a playful way. There is no limit to the decorations which kriṣṇa has. He knows that I could not survive without him and he also knows that he could survive without me. If such kriṣṇa comes through this street, we will surround him, such that he would not be able to go outside anywhere. We will complain “He has snatched our ball when we were playing”. Oh, friend! Let us enjoy the sight of his divine lips which are like coral and his smile.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that another girl says that she will not bother about her femininity hereafter.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**sinduram ilangat than tireneṟṟi mēl** – kriṣṇa has a beauty of his divine forehead, just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.7.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/10/thiruvaimozhi-7-7-7-kanmingal-annaiyargal/) “*nāḷ mannu veṇ tingaḷ kol nayandārgatku naccilai kol*” (Is the divine forehead of kriṣṇa like the faultless moon? ōr is it something which is not to be desired?) On top of that divine forehead, vermillion, which complements that \[dark\] divine forehead, has been applied and is shining.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the vermillion on his divine forehead would be similar to that mentioned in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 9.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/09/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-9-1/) “*sindurac chem podi pōl*” (butterflies are flying all over tirumālirunjōlai, like vermillion powder). On top of that, a divine golden ornament has been applied. His divine locks, which are like a garland of bluish gems, in colour, complement the golden ornament.

**tiruttiya kōṟambum tirukkuḻalum** – On top of these, a divine golden ornament has been applied aptly on his divine forehead and his divine locks are complementing the divine ornament. The word *ilanga*, which was seen in the earlier verse, has to be added here too.

**andaramuḻavam** – the entire sky is reverberating with the sounds of musical instruments. The term *muḻavam* refers to drum, a percussion instrument. Here, the meaning extends to refer to the sound made by the drum.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āṇḍāḷ had dreamt that kriṣṇa was coming with the drums playing resoundingly and that the conces blowing, as mentioned in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 6.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/08/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-6-6/) “*mattaḷam kotta varisangam ninṟūda*” (even as the drums were played and the conces with lines in them were blown for a long time). Here, the herd-girl saw the event unfolding in front of her eyes.

**taṇ taḻaik kāvin kīḻ** – under the garden of umbrellas, made with peacock feathers \[held by kriṣṇa’s friends to provide him protection from rain and sunshine\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that there is an alternative connotation to this: kriṣṇa was coming under a green canopy, which was cool.

**varum āyarōdu udan** – along with the herd-boys, who are coming with him

**vaḷai kōl vīsa** – as they keep throwing curved sticks on one another, shouting words of victory \[in a playful way\]

**andam onṟu illāda āyap piḷḷai** – he \[kriṣṇa\] is a herd-boy whose beauty of decorations, beauty of the manner in which he is returning \[from grazing the cattle\] and his playful \[mischievous\] activities cannot be estimated by even those who are capable of estimating anything.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that it is impossible to see the boundary of his childish activities. It may be possible to analyse emperumān’s various other incarnations as well as his eminence in various states such as *para* \[his state in śrī vaikuṇṭam\]*, vyūha* \[his state in the divine milky ocean\] etc. However, it is not possible to analyse the extent of his activities as a child in his kriṣṇāvatāram. This is due to the fact that his amazing activities are most liked by everyone. When he returns from grazing, the herd-girl thinks that he appears, as mentioned in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 6.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/08/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-6-3/) “*indiran uḷḷitta dēvar kuḻām*” (all the assemblies of celestial entities, including indra). This is her desire, just as it has been mentioned in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 12.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/10/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-12-2/) “*āyppādikkē ennai uyttidumin*” (carry me to tiruvāyppādi).

**aṟindu aṟīndu ivvīdi pōdum āgil** – Since he knows that I could not exist without him and that he could exist without me, he should not come through this street. Despite knowing this, if he comes through this street …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai adds here that even when she is desiring to see kriṣṇa going through her street, she is engaging with *praṇaya rōśam* \[a made-up pathos of anger, due to overflowing love\], due to her overflowing tender nature.

**pandu koṇḍānn enṟu vaḷaittu vaittu** – Do not think “How will we surround him when he comes in a large crowd \[of herd-boys\]?” We will stop him from going further by saying “He had snatched our ball when we were playing, and disappeared”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that they \[herd-girls\] will even speak about absurd things in order to stop him from proceeding further. She will say, as mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.2.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/11/thiruvaimozhi-6-2-6-kuzhagi-engal/) “*kaḻagam ēṟēl*” (Do not enter our assembly); she will say “When we were playing, you had snatched our ball and gone off”; this is a ruse for engaging in a conversation with him. Alternatively, she will throw the ball, which she is having in her hand, on his lap and accuse him of stealing their ball.

**pavaḷa vāy muṟuvalum kāṇbōm tōḻi** – When we accuse him like this, he will stop, without proceeding further, and smile gently. Oh, friend! When he does this, we will look at his divine lips, which are like coral and the smile, which is complementing his divine lips, and enjoy those. She desires to see this.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the girl says “We will see \[now\] whatever we had not seen before. We will get to see a rare sight. We will not look at his smiling face, directly”. She desires to tell him “Who do you think that we are that you are smiling at us? You should realise that this is our street. Are you bewildered?” Only if her desire fructifies would her pledge too get established \[to see his divine lips and the sweet smile\].

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.4.7. Salappal nirai

*sālap pal niraip pinnē taḻaikkāvin kīḻ tan tirumēni ninṟū oḷi tigaḻaneela naṟum kunji nēttirattāl aṇindu pal āyar kuḻām naduvēkōlac cendāmaraik kaṇ miḷirak kuḻal ūdi isai pādik kunittu āyarōduālittu varuginṟa āyap piḷḷai aḻagu kaṇḍu en magaḷ ayarkkinṟadē*

**Пословный перевод:**

\[sāla – to a great extent\] sāl pal – of many types; nirai pinnē – behind herds of cattle; taḻai – umbrellas made of peacock feathers; kāvin kīḻ – under the garden; than – his \[kriṣṇa’s\]; tirumēni – divine form; ninṟu – remaining \[the word ninṟu here is added as a sweet, pleasant word, without any additional meaning); oḷi tigaḻa – to shine brightly; neelam – having a blackish complexion; nal – having the advantages of curling and length; naṟu – having fragrance; kunji – divine bundles of locks; nēttirattāl – with peacock feathers; aṇindu – decorating; pal – many; āyar kuḻām naduvē – in the midst of the assembly of herd-boys; kōlam – being beautiful; sem – being reddish; tāmarai – like a lotus flower; kaṇ – the divine eyes; miḷira – to gleam; kuḻal – flute; ūdi – playing on it; isai – with appropriate music; pādi – singing; kunittu – and dancing; āyarōdu – with the herd-boys; ālittu varuginṟa – coming with pride; āyap piḷḷai – herd-boy’s \[kriṣṇa’s\]; aḻagu kaṇḍu – looking at his divine form; en magaḷ – my daughter; ayarkkinṟadu – is forgetting everything (says the mother of a daughter)

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa’s divine form was splendorous, as he came behind the cattle herds, under the umbrellas of peacock feathers. His divine locks, which are blackish and having the advantages of being curled and long, have been decorated with peacock feathers. As he came amidst herd-boys, with his divine eyes gleaming like beautiful reddish lotus, and playing on his flute, dancing and singing with herd-boys, my daughter saw the beautiful form of the prideful kriṣṇa, and is forgetting.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**sālappanniraip pinnē** – behind cattle which were of many types. The abundance of cattle in that place was such that even if they were to be counted in any manner that one chose to, it was impossible to completely count them. kriṣṇa let such cattle to walk in the front, and came behind them all.

**taḻaikkāvin kīḻ** – under the garden of peacock umbrellas.

**than tirumēni ninṟu oḷi tigaḻa** – his divine form was shining since the cattle had had their stomachs full and since he thought “The time has to come to be with the girls in tiruvāyppādi”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa’s divine form, which is as mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.7.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/05/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-4-govindhan/) “*tēvum tannaiyum*” (displaying aspects of his supremacy and simplicity), was splendorous. There was a contrast between his divine complexion and the complexion of the peacock feathers.

**neela nannaṟum kunji nēttirattāl aṇindu** – he decorated his divine locks which were blackish and fragrant and which had the advantages of both curliness and length, with the eyes of peacock feathers.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that he had decorated his divine locks, which were glistening and dark, and which had a fragrance.

**pallāyar kuḻā naduvē** – He came amidst the huge assembly of herd-boys.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that his divine eyes, which were attractive and reddish, were showering mercy on the assembly of his herd-friends, manifesting his relationship with them.

**kōlac cendāmaraik kaṇ miḷira** – His divine eyes, which were like attractive, reddish lotus flowers, were gleaming. This suggests that he was looking at the friends, coming to his left side and right side, feeling joyous, while returning.

**kuḻal ūdi isai pādik kunittu** – just as it has been said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/10/thiruvaimozhi-10-3-1-vey-maru-thol-inai/) “*āmaruvinanirai mēykka nī pōkku oru pagal āyiram ūḻi*” (In the daytime, when you go for the leelā \[playful pastime\] of tending to cows which are abundantly available, matching their species, it appears that it is like a thousand yugas), the herd-girls in tiruvāyppādi felt sorrowful since he had been away for a very long time, going behind cattle. In order to make those girls to feel exhilarated, in order to express his urge in seeing them, due to his affection for them, as well as to remove the anger in the hearts of those who felt the pangs of separation from him, he played on the flute, with suitable pāsurams, singing songs aligned with those tunes. Just as expert dancers would manifest movements of dancing even when they walk, kriṣṇa, through his gait, made it appear that he was dancing, as mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.1.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/10/thiruvaimozhi-10-1-6-kuththan-kovalan/) “*kūttan kōvalan*” (one who goes behind those who need protection \[cattle\] and protects them, walking beautifully like an expert dancer), while playing on the flute and singing.

**āyarōdu ālittu varuginṟa āyappiḷḷai** – he was returning with his friends, the herd-boys, with a look of pride on his face, on account of the incidents mentioned earlier.

**aḻagu kaṇḍu en magaḷ ayarkkinṟadē** – By merely looking at the beauty of such kriṣṇa’s divine form, my daughter is losing her mind, forgetting the clan in which she was born, forgetting her pride of being a girl and forgetting that she was under my control.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother says that the reason for her daughter losing her mind and forgetting is also the medicine for her disease.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.4.8. Sindurap podi

*sindurap podi koṇḍu senni appit tirunāmam ittu angu ōr ilaiyam tannālandaram inṟit tanneṟi pangiyai aḻagiya nēttirattāl aṇinduindiran pōl varum āyap piḷḷai edir ninṟu angu inavaḷai iḻavēl ennaccandiyil ninṟu kaṇḍīr nangai tan tugilodu sari vaḷai kaḻalginṟadē*

**Пословный перевод:**

senni – “in the divine locks; sindurap podi – with vermillion powder; appi – applying; angu – on the divine forehead; ōr ilai tannāl – with a leaf (in the verse ōr ilaiyam tannāl, the syllable am does not have any meaning; it is there for the poetic metrics); tirunāmam ittu – applying ūrdva puṇḍram \[the divine mark\]; than – his \[kriṣṇa’s\]; neṟi – dense; pangiyai – divine locks; aḻagiya – beautiful; nēttirattāl – eyes of peacock feathers; aṇindu – decorating; indiran pōl – like dēvēndran \[head of celestial entities\]; varum – one who is coming; āyap piḷḷai – for the herd-boy; edir angu – in the place opposite; ninṟu – standing; inam vaḷai – collection of bangles; iḻavēl – do not lose”; enna – even as I said, regarding my daughter; sandiyil – at the intersection of streets through which he is coming; ninṟu kaṇḍīr – stand there and see for yourself; nangai than – she, who does not have any blemish regarding the feminine qualities of shyness; tugilodu – along with the dress; sari vaḷai – bangles; kaḻalginṟadu – are slipping out, says the mother of a daughter, to her friends

**Перевод:**

**A mother tells her daughter “kriṣṇa is returning \[from grazing cattle\], applying vermillion powder on his divine locks, ūrdva puṇḍram on his divine forehead, decorating his dense divine locks with the eyes of peacock feathers. Do not stand opposite that kriṣṇa, who is coming like dēvēndran, at the intersection of four streets, through which he is coming and do not lose your bangles”. Even as I was telling her this, you would see that my daughter, who is without any blemish in her qualities of femininity such as shyness, simplicity, fear etc, is losing her dress and her bangles.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**sindurap podik koṇḍu senni appi** – applying vermillion powder on the divine locks. In the earlier pāsuram, it was mentioned “*sinduram ilangat than tiruneṟṟi mēl*”, applying vermillion powder on his divine forehead, to shine brightly. Here, since it says *senni appi*, it is clear that he had applied it on his divine locks, as a decoration.

**tirunāmam ittu angu ōr ilaiyam tannāl** – with a leaf, which was straight and long, which would create a distinct mark, he had applied the divine symbol \[*ūrdva puṇḍram*\], on his divine forehead. The term *angu* refers to the divine forehead, which is the apt place for applying the divine symbol of *ūrdva puṇḍram.* In the term *ilaiyam*, the syllable *am* is a poetic metric and does not have a meaning. Alternatively, it would also mean applying the vermillion using saliva from the mouth. In this case, the text would be *ōr ilayam tannāl*; *il* would mean *uḷ,* referring to inside and *ayam* would refer to water. Then, *ōr ilayam* would refer to water inside the divine mouth, viz. saliva. This would fit with *āyap piḷḷai*, having been born in the clan of herd-folk and his nature of being a child \[children would use their saliva for applying powder\].

**andaram …** – decorating his dense locks with the eyes of peacock feathers such that there was no gap in his locks.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai adds, in his svāpadēśam, that apart from the peacock feathers, kriṣṇa’s divine locks were also decorated by the eyes of young herd-girls.

**indiran pōl varum āyap piḷḷai** – just as indran, the controller of celestial entities, comes amidst celestial entities, showing his eminence, with the celestial entities vorśipping him, kriṣṇa came amidst a thousand herd-boys, who matched him, with the boys vorśipping him, manifesting his pride and eminence. Alternatively, for the word *indiran*, since it would refer to emperumān himself primarily, this could be taken as kriṣṇa coming, similar to emperumān, surrounded by nityasūris, who have equivalence with him in eight qualities, in paramapadam. Though *darmi aikyam* \[same entity\] is seen in both emperumān and kriṣṇa, considering that kriṣṇa is an incarnation, it could be said this way, just as it has been mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam “*viṣṇunā sadruśō vīryē*” \[śrī rāma was matching viṣṇu in his valour; here too, both śrī rāma and viṣṇu refer to the same entity, śrī rāma is an incarnation\]. The herd-boy, who was coming like this …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa matched indran in one manner: just as indran would not consume the *havis* \[offering in a ritual\] offered by samsāris when they carry out a ritual \[since he detests samsāram and its smell\], kriṣṇa too would not like those who sustain themselves without him. Alternatively, the term *indran* would refer to emperumān himself as a distinguished entity dwelling within indra and just as it has been mentioned in [mūnṟām tiruvandādi 38](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/04/munram-thiruvandhadhi-38/) “*tānē tanakkuvaman*” (emperumān could be compared only with himself since there is none who could be held as a metaphor for him) he is the lord of all, since he does not have anyone similar to him.

**edir ninṟu angu inavaḷai iḻavēl enna** – I told my daughter not to stand in the way by which he is coming and lose the *inavaḷai* \[a type of bangle\]. It appears that there are no two different events, such as standing in the way and losing the bangles. The moment she stood in the way, the bangles disappeared. Since it says *inavaḷai*, it appears that not even one herd-girl had even a single bangle remaining on her hand. Losing bangles is considered as losing one’s femininity.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother has told her daughter not to lose her femininity by standing in the way by which he comes; it was not possible for her \[the daughter\] to withstand the strong force of the waves of his beauty.

**sandiyil ninṟu kaṇḍīr** – You could see that this happened in the public way, when he was coming, with my daughter not listening to my words of caution.

**nangai than tugilodu sarivaḷai kaḻalginṟadē** – For her, who was complete in her femininity \[nangai refers to a girl who is complete with her femininity\], along with her dress, the bangles too slipped out. Just like there are bangles such as *kōl vaḷai, kaḻal vaḷai, vari vaḷai* etc, *sari vaḷai* is also a type of bangles. Just as it has been mentioned in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 11.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/10/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-11-3/) “*kaḻal vaḷaiyait tāmum kaḻal vaḷaiye ākkinarē*” (He made my *kaḻal vaḷai*, which was an arbitrary name, to become a slipping and disappearing bangle, a causative name \[*kaḻalhal*– to slip out\]), through his mere appearance, he made my *sarivaḷai* \[a type of bangle\] to become *sariyum* *vaḷai* \[that which slips and falls off\], and not hanging from my hand. Through this, the mother responds to those who came to enquire about her daughter’s change, the reason for the change and the distinct feature of the change \[kriṣṇa is the reason for the change in her daughter and the change in her was her bangles slipping and falling off\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother is telling those who came to enquire, about the distinguished changes in her daughter’s form. Even though the daughter is not doing what she had told her \[not to stand in the way by which kriṣṇa is coming\], she still calls her daughter as *nangai* \[one who is complete\]. This is because, even here, this word describes the completeness of her qualities. The effects of the shortcomings in kriṣṇa’s qualities are still a necessity \[here, the term ‘shortcomings’ refers to the positive features in kriṣṇa, such as his beauty, his decoration etc; if the girl had not bothered about kriṣṇa’s beauty and had not longed to be with him, her mother would not have called her as *nangai*\]. The addition of *than* to the term *nangai* \[*nangai than*\], refers to the eminence acquired by the girl \[by losing her bangles\].Along with her dress, the bangles too loosened. She could not protect either her femininity or her pride of having the quality of femininity. Instead of  swelling and breaking, the bangles slipped out of her hands due to kriṣṇa’s indifference. The bangles will not stay put, on her hands due to separation from kriṣṇa. When being united with him too, the bangles would not have stayed put on her hand \[since, out of sheer happiness of being together with him, she would have become larger in size, leading to the bangles being broken by the increased size of her hands\].

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.
