## 3.4.9. Valangadin mel

*valangādin mēḷ tōnṟip pū aṇindu malligai vana mālai mauval mālaisilingārattāl kuḻal tāḻa vittut tīnguḻal vāy maduttu ūdialangārattāl varum āyap piḷḷai aḻagu kaṇḍu en magaḷ āsaip pattuvilanginillādu edir ninṟu kaṇḍīr veḷvaḷai kaḻanṟu meymmeliginṟadē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vala kādil – in the right ear; mēl tōnṟip pū – sengāndaḷ flower (red species of malabar glory lily); aṇindu – donning; vanam – beautiful; malligai mālai – garland of jasmine flower; mauval mālai – wild jasmine garland; aṇindu – donning; silingārattāl – in a decorative manner; kuḻal – bundle of divine locks; tāḻa vittu – making it hang down on the back; tīm – giving sweetness to all; kuḻal – flute; vāy maduttu – keeping on the divine lips; ūdi ūdi – playing on it, repeatedly; alangārattāl – with this get-up; varum – one who came; āyap piḷḷai – herd-boy’s \[kriṣṇa’s\]; aḻagu kaṇḍu – looking at his beauty; en magaḷ – my daughter; āsaip pattu – with desire; vilangi nillādu – instead of stepping side (keeping the eyes elsewhere, instead of on him; edir ninṟu kaṇḍīr – looking at him, standing opposite him; veḷvaḷai – bangles made of conch; kaḻanṟu – slipping out (instead of staying put, on the hands); mey – form too; meliginṟadu – was emaciating; enṟu – says the mother of the daughter, to those who came to enquire about her

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa, the herd-boy, had donned the reddish malabar glory lily flower, on his right ear and garlands of beautiful regular jasmine and wild jasmine on his divine form. He had let bundles of his divine locks decoratively, to hang down on his back. He kept his flute, which gives sweet music to everyone, on his divine lips and played repeatedly on it. Looking at the decoration of the herd-boy, like this, my daughter, with desire, stood in his path, looking at him, instead of stepping aside, thinking “Looking at him like this will bring sorrow to beholders”. Her bangles, made of conch, slipped out of her hands and her form too became emaciated \[tells the mother of the girl, to her friends who came to enquire about her\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that this pāsuram too mentions about kriṣṇa’s decorations.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**valam kādil mēl tōnṟip pū aṇindu** – donning the reddish species of malabar glory lily flower, as a decoration, over the right ear. Since nothing has been mentioned about the left ear, it should be presumed that he came with this only, with the decoration on only one ear looking beautiful, in a way. After donning the flower on one ear, since he looked at the jasmine garland, he would have probably forgotten about the left ear and donned the jasmine garland \[mentioned next\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that decoration, apt for the clan, will look appealing for the eyes of people of that clan. kriṣṇa donned the reddish malabar glory lily, which was beautiful to the eyes, on his right ear. Looking at the jasmine flower, kriṣṇa forgot about decoration for the left ear. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai further says that looking at kriṣṇa’s flower decoration, the herd-girl too forgot about the left ear. He says that kriṣṇa desired the wild jasmine garland. Alternatively, just as it has been mentioned in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 14.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/11/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-14-2/) “*vanamālai minunga ninṟu viḷaiyāda*” (as kriṣṇa played with his friends, with the *vanamālai* shining) \[*vanamālai* is the distinguished garland worn by emperumān, on his chest, and is called as *vaijayanti*\], the jasmine garland became his distinguished *vanamālai*.

**malligai vana mālai** – The term *vanam* \[forest\] could be added to *malligai* \[jasmine\] and this would then refer to jasmine grown in forest areas. Alternatively, *vanam* could refer to being beautiful, thus referring to jasmine garland, which was looking beautiful.

**mauval mālai** – *mauval* refers to a variety of jasmine flower \[it is also referred to as wild jasmine flower\]. Just as in the term *pūvai kāyā* \[from periya tiruvandādi\], the flower *pūvai* is a variant of the flower *kāyā*, here too, a similar variation exists between *malligai* and *mauval* flowers. The term *vanam* \[beautiful\] is to be added here too, to make it beautiful *mauval* garland. Similarly, the term *aṇindu* \[donning\] in the first verse \[*mēl tōnṟip pū aṇindu*\] has to be added here to infer that kriṣṇa donned the garlands of *malligai* and *mauval* flowers.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *mauval vanamālai* refers to beautiful garland, with different colours.

**silingārattāḷ kuḻal tāḻa vittu** – *silingāram* – *śrungāram* \[decoration\]; through this, the decoration made to the divine locks with these garlands is mentioned. Along with those decorations, kriṣṇa had let his divine locks such that they came on to his back, hanging down.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the garlands were donned both on his divine locks and on his divine chest.

**tīnguḻal vāy maduttu ūdi** – the term *tīm* refers to sweetness. Since the pāsuram has not specifically mentioned that the sweetness is “For such a person”, this implies that the music from the flute was sweet for him as well as for others, without any distinction. Among the listeners \[of that music\], his ears are the nearest. Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.9.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/09/thiruvaimozhi-9-9-9-udhum-aththinguzharke/) “*pēduṟu mugam seydu nondu nondu*” (since his ears are closest to the music from the flute, he became distressed, thinking “If we are ourselves so immersed in it, how will the helpless girls feel about it?)” the music from the flute distressed him first, before going towards the others. Distressing others has been explained through the following pāsurams from periyāḻvār tirumoḻi, decad 3.6: (1) 3.6.7 “*aviyuṇā maṟandu vānavar ellām*” (\[the music went up to the celestial word such that\] the celestial entities forgot to consume the *havis* \[offering from ritual\] proffered by human beings\]); (2) 3.6.5 “*tumburuvōdu nāradanum tam tam vīṇai maṟandu*” (the music from the flute made tumburu \[a celestial sage\] and nāradan to forget their vīṇai \[a stringed instrument\]); (3) 3.6.1 “*kōvalar siṟumiyar* – *vandu kaviḻndu ninṟanar*” (young herd-girls, hearing the music from the flute, came to the place where kriṣṇa was, and with shyness, bowed down their heads and stood); (4) 3.6.8 “*paṟavaiyin kaṇangaḷ kūdu tuṟandu vandu sūḻndu*” (flocks of birds, hearing the music, came out of their nests, came to where kriṣṇa was, surrounding him) and (5) 3.6.10 “*marangaḷ ninṟu madu tāraigaḷ pāyum*” (trees, listening to his music, will stand in a focussed manner, and secrete a flood of honey). Thus, as seen in these examples, the music from kriṣṇa’s flute will affect all species, such as celestial, human, animals and plants, without any distinction. kriṣṇa will keep such a flute on his divine lips and keep playing repeatedly on it.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that since the music played by kriṣṇa on the flute was meant to alleviate the anguish of those who were affectionate towards him, it was sweet for them \[reference here is to the herd-girls who were wilting under separation from him from dawn to dusk\]. For the term *vāy maduttu*, he says that the herd-girl feels distressed that she is not like that flute, to be handled so affectionately by kriṣṇa. Why is it this slim? She wonders! \[Since he is constantly touching it and keeping it on his divine mouth, it should have become bulky, due to the resultant pride. But it is slim\]. This \[flute\] refers to the characteristic of an ācārya, who lets known the unknown \[just as emperumān instructs jīvātmās through an ācarya, here, kriṣṇa informs his instructions to the cattle or about his arrival to the people in tiruvāyppādi, through the flute\].

**alangārattāl varum āyap piḷḷai** – kriṣṇa, the herd-person, coming with the decorations as mentioned above. The term *piḷḷai* refers to kriṣṇa’s age which is between a boy’s and a youth’s, as mentioned in rig vēdam as “*yuvākumāra*:” \[between a youth and a boy\].

**aḻagu kaṇḍu en magaḷ āsaip pattu** – my daughter became desirous of such kriṣṇa, whose beauty was attracting the eyes and hearts of those who beheld him.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the herd-girl was overcome by the beauty of kriṣṇa’s divine, beautiful form. When an elephant, in rut, is coming, if one were to stand in its way, it will not only not allow to person to reach his destination, it will also throw the person down. In the same way, when one looks at kriṣṇa, with such decorations, his beauty will not only allow the person to attain him, by considering him as the means, it will also not allow the person to look at his qualities of protection etc. Will anyone desire to covert that beauty?

**vilangi nillā edir ninṟū kaṇḍīr** – Instead of stepping aside from his path, realising “This beauty will trouble those who see him”, she came looking at his beauty and came opposite him.

**veḷvaḷai kaḻanṟu mey meliginṟadē** – the bangles, made of conch, slipped out and her form too started emaciating. Will not the body become thin first and then the bangles slip out? Why then has the pāsuram mentioned about bangles slipping out first and then, the body becoming thin? For her mother, the bangles slipping out appeared first and then only she saw her daughter becoming thin. Alternatively, the daughter became thin just enough for the bangles to slip out; subsequently, the bangles could not be fitted back on the hands since she continued to become thin. The mother is mentioning this sequence. These words are also the response of the mother to those who came to enquire about her daughter’s condition.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother tells her friends that her daughter had not only gone out of her \[mother’s\] control, she had also lost respect for her own femininity. He asks whether the form \[of the herd-girl\] will become thin only after the shining, pure, bangles slip out. Will it not be sufficient to become slim until the bangles slip out? Since the term *meliginṟadu* \[slipping out\] is in the present tense, it appears that one would wonder whether there is any place for the bangles to get back on. *vaḷai* could also be considered as the bangles worn on the shoulder, which will keep dropping and would need to be pushed back up the arm. Since this would recur, the mother thought initially that the bangles had dropped down on their own. It was only when she found that despite being pushed up, the bangles were not staying in place, that she realised that her daughter had become thin. She tells the pāsuram in the manner in which she saw the events \[bangles slipping out first and then the realisation that the daughter’s form had become thin\].

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.4.10. Vinnin midu

*viṇṇin mīdu amarargaḷ virumbit toḻa miṟaittu āyarpādiyil vīdiyūdēkaṇṇan kālippinnē eḻuanhdaruḷak kaṇḍu iḷa āyk kannimār kāmuṟṟavaṇṇam vaṇḍu amar poḻil puduvaiyar kōn vittu cittan sonna mālai pattumpaṇṇinbam varap pādum pattar uḷḷār paramāna vaigundam naṇṇuvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

viṇṇin mīdu – in upper worlds such as svargam \[heaven\] etc; amargaḷ – celestial entities; virumbi – with desire; toḻa – to worship; miṟaittu – disregarding them; āyar pādiyil – in the village of herd-folk; vīdiyūde – in the middle of the streets; kāli pinnē – behind cattle; kaṇṇan – kaṇṇapirān \[kriṣṇa\]; eḻundu aruḷa – as he came mercifully; kaṇḍu – seeing that; iḷa – youthful; āy kanniyar – herd-girls; kāmuṟṟa vaṇṇam – the manner in which they desired; vaṇḍu – beetles; amar – settled; poḻil – having gardens; puduvaiyar – for those in śrī villibuttūr; kōn – controller; vittu cittan – periyāḻvār; sonna – mercifully composed; mālai – garland of worlds; pattum – these ten pāsurams; inbam vara – to feel the appreciation; paṇ – with music; pādum – singing; pattar uḷḷār – those who are devotees; paramāna – more eminent than the most distinguished; vaigundam – śrī vaikuṇṭam; naṇṇuvar – will attain

**Перевод:**

**While the celestial entities, inhabiting upper worlds such as svargam etc, were vorśipping emperumān with joy, disregarding them, kriṣṇa mercifully came through the streets in the village of tiruvāyppādi, behind cattle. Looking at him, the young herd-girls desired him. periyāḻvār, the controller of those who live in śrī villibuttūr, which has gardens where beetle have settled, mercifully composed their affection as garlands of words, into these ten pāsurams . Those, who are devotees of emperumān, who are able to appreciate these and sing them, will attain śrī vaikuṇṭam, which is more eminent than the most distinguished abodes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the last pāsuram of this decad, āḻvār mentions the benefit which will accrue to one who recites the pāsurams and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**viṇṇin mīdu amarargaḷ virumbitt toḻa** – in upper worlds such as svargam etc, celestial entities were vorśipping emperumān, with affection. Since they had prayed to him to reduce the burden on earth and made him to incarnate, right from the time of his incarnation, the celestial entities were seeing his amazing activities and were amazed. Hence, when emperumān, who is the lord of both *vibhūtis* \[*leelā vibhūti*, the materialistic realm, and *nitya vibhūti*, spiritual realm), incarnated in the clan of herd-people, engaged in protection of cattle, appropriate for that clan and roamed around, decorating himself apt for the clan, they vorśipped him with desire. Alternatively, the term *viṇṇin mīdu* could also refer to śrī vaikuṇṭam, which is above all the other worlds, referred to, as in taittirīya upaniśad nārāyaṇavalli “*nākasya pruśtē*” (seated above the sky). nityasūris, the permanent dwellers of śrī vaikuṇṭam, constantly worship his supreme nature of eminence. When they see his supreme nature of simplicity, as kriṣṇa, on earth, with the greatest affection, they worship him.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that celestial entities, who are in the upper worlds, desirously worship, due to the benefits gained by them while those, who are above them \[in śrī vaikuṇṭam\], worship, since the act of vorśipping itself is their benefit.

**miṟaittu** – disregarding. In other words, not looking at those who are vorśipping him from the upper worlds, and looking at the cattle and herd-folks in tiruvāyppādi, with affection.

**āyarpādiyil vīdiyūdē kaṇṇan kālippinē eḻundaruḷak kaṇḍu** – seeing kriṣṇa mercifully coming in the streets of tiruvāyppādi, behind cattle, with the decorations mentioned earlier and with a divine form, which would make those decorations to be superfluous.

**iḷa āyk kannimār kāmuṟṟa vaṇṇam** – starting with the first pāsuram of this decad “*sālagavāsal paṟṟi nuḻaivanar niṟpanarāgi*” and ending with the ninth pāsuram “*veḷvaḷai kaḻanṟu mey meliginṟadu*”, the young herd-girls looked desirously at kriṣṇa, leading to changes in their forms. The manner in which these incidents happened …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that periyāḻvār utilised the manners in which young herd-girls desired kriṣṇa, leading to changes in their forms, as a pretext and combined these with the mangaḷāśāsanam that he was carrying out. Will these combine with mangaḷāśāsanam? Since they \[the herd-girls\] lost out to kriṣṇa as a village, losing out their hearts to him, and he remained as the victor, without losing out his heart to them, since they, in essence, said “*tē jitam*” (victory to you), this will mingle with the manner of mangaḷāśāsanam. He is one who does not enjoy, as mentioned in vēdam as “*anaśnan*” (one who does not eat). Just as kriṣṇa had said in mahābhāratam “*yati mē brahmacaryam syāt*” (If I had observed the tenets of *brahmacaryam* \[being celebate\]) and as mentioned in śrī bhāśyam “*tatgata dōśairasamspruśta*:” (faults of the entities with whom emperumān comes into contact, do not rub on him), all these activities \[of indulging with herd-girls etc\] remain as *leelā rasam* (flavour of indulging in playful activities) for kriṣṇa. His enjoyment as *leelārasam* is acceptable to āḻvār. cintayanti and śiśupālan too were entities who played their part in his *leelārasam* \[cintayanti did not reach out to kriṣṇa fully. She stopped in her tracks. Hence, it was only *leelārasam* for emperumān and not *bhōgarasam* \[flavour of enjoyment, which he gets with nityasūris and muktātmās \[liberated souls\].

**vaṇḍu amar poḻil …** – śrī villibuttūr has divine gardens in which beetles, desiring to imbibe honey, have settled down permanently, not interested in anything else. Being the controller of the people who live in such a place, periyāḻvār has always kept sarvēśvaran in his divine mind, as mentioned in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.4.10 “*aravattu amaḷiyinōdum*” (with the mattress of ādiśēśan), as a result of which he is called as *viṣṇu cittar*. He has mercifully composed these ten pāsurams.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār is called as viṣṇu cittan since (1) he has *vataperum kōyil udaiyān* (the divine name of emperumān who has taken residence in śrī villibuttūr), who is viṣṇu, in his divine mind; (2) he is an entity who is dear to the divine mind of emperumān and (3) he holds on dearly to emperumān’s pervasive nature, in his divine mind \[the term *viṣṇu* refers to one, who has pervaded the entire universe\].

**paṇṇinbam varap pādum pattar uḷḷār** – those who have a deep devotion towards emperumān, singing these pāsurams with tunes, which bring joy to those who sing, more than the joy which they bring to the listeners of these pāsurams.

**paramāna vaigundam naṇṇuvarē** – Just as it has been mentioned in cāndōjña upanishad “*viśvata*:*pruśtēśu sarvata*: *pruśtēśu*” (paramapadam is above all the worlds which have been created by emperumān on his own and through brahmā, later on), it is more eminent than the most distinguished. Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruppallāṇḍu 12](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/11/thiruppallandu-12-pallandu-enru/) “*pallāṇḍum paramātmanaic cūḻndirundu ēttuvar pallāṇḍē*” (they will keep carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam to emperumān, surrounding him, forever), those people will attain such śrī vaikuṇṭam and carry out mangaḷāśāsanam to emperumān, until the entity ‘time’ exists \[viz. forever\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that such people will attain paramapadam which is described as an abode from which one does not return.

We shall next consider the pravēsam of the next tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.5.1. Attukkuvi sorru

*attukkuvi sōṟṟup paruppadamum tayir vāviyum neyyaḷaṟum adangappottatt tuṟṟu mārip pagai puṇartta porumā kadalvaṇṇan poṟutta malaivattat tadam kaṇ madamān kanṟinai valaivāyp paṟṟik koṇḍu kuṟa magaḷirkottait talaippāl koduttu vaḷarkkum gōvarttanam ennum koṟṟak kudaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

attu – cooked; kuvi – heaped; sōṟu – rice; paruppadamum – mountain; tayir vāviyum – stream of curd; ney aḷaṟum – muddled with ghee; adanga – all these; potta – immediately; tuṟṟu – consumed; māri – rainfall; pagai – enemy; puṇartta – one who created; poru – with belligerent waves; mā kadal – like a dark ocean; vaṇṇan – one who has a divine complexion; poṟutta – one who held; malai – mountain; vattam – round; tada – being huge; madam – having obedience towards its mother; mān kanṟinai – fawn; valaivāy – in a net; paṟṟik koṇḍu – catching it; kuṟa magaḷir – women of hill tribe; kottai – cotton roll; talai – with the head; pāl koduttu – feeding milk (the women will dip the cotton roll in milk and give the milk through one end of the roll to the fawn); vaḷarkkum – nurturing; gōvarttanam ennum – having the name ‘gōvardana’ on account of increase in cattle numbers; koṟṟam – being victorious over that rain; kudai – called as umbrella since it did not allow even a drop of rain to fall on anyone, by being inverted

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa ate up instantly, the heaped mountain of cooked rice, along with a stream of curd and muddled ghee, creating a fight as a consequence, through rain. He, having the divine complexion of a dark ocean with belligerent waves, held aloft the mountain. The mountain nurtured fawns which were having round, huge eyes, caught by tribal people through nets and given to their women, who fed them milk through rolls of cotton, dipped in milk. The mountain is named as gōvardana, since it helped in multiplying numbers of cattle. It emerged victorious in the fight with rains, since, by being inverted, it did not let even a drop of water to fall on anyone.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**attukkuvi sōṟṟup aruppadamum** – mountain of heaped cooked rice. Herd-people would traditionally worship indra, the lord of celestial entities, for getting rainfall. He too, being pleased with their offerings and worship, would enable clouds to rain in tiruvāyppādi. With the resultant water and well-grown grass, the herd-people would nurture their cattle, leading to abundance of milk and ghee, resulting in their well-being. This is the reason that this practice has been mentioned as traditional, as seen in [periya tirumoḻi 2.3.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/08/periya-thirumozhi-2-3-4/) “*eḻil viḻavil paḻanadaisey mandira vidiyil pūsanai*” (in the beautiful festival of sacrifice, chanting hymns, the herd-folk vorśipped). Since this was the custom, in order to worship indra, people in all the five lakh families of tiruvāyppādi cooked foods and loaded the cooked food on carts drawn by bulls, as mentioned in [periya tirumadal](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/07/periya-thirumadal/) “*tunnu sagadattāl pukka perum sōṟu*” (huge quantum of food carried in many carts). All the cooked food were spread out on a huge land and heaped, in order to look like a mountain. It is to emphasise this that the verse says *attukkuvi sōṟṟup paruppadamum*. The term *paruppadam* refers to mountain.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the herd-folk offer prayers to indra to give them rains and they believed that they were protected by indra. Hence, as done by their ancestors in tiruvāyppādi, they too vorśipped him, by cooking foodstuffs in their houses, as mentioned in periya tirumoḻi 2.3.4 “*mandira vidiyil pūsanai seyyakkadavōm*”, taking the foodstuffs in carts, as mentioned in periya tirumadal “*tunnu sagadattāl pukka perum sōṟu*”. They added other cooked vegetables and fresh fruits, poured curd and ghee over that heaped rice. *paruppadam* could also refer to *paruppu sōṟu* \[rice made with cooked lentils\]. They also made tamarind rice, sweet pongal rice etc.

**tayir vāviyum** – stream of curd

**neyyaḷaṟum** – muddled with ghee. On top of that mountain of cooked food, a container was placed, through which plenty of curd was let onto the cooked rice. In a similar vein, ghee was also poured through containers on top of the mountain of rice, such that ghee was seen everywhere, both on and around the rice mountain. This is the reason for referring to it as *ney aḷaṟu* (muddled with ghee). Mentioning these two \[curd and ghee\] is representative of all the other ingredients for making palatable food, such as vegetables and fruits.

**adanga** – all these

**pottat tuṟṟu** – instantaneously consuming all the foodstuff. All these foods were made, keeping in mind some other deity \[indra\]. Since emperumān is the in-dwelling soul of all entities, he decided to eat all that food stuff himself and did not want others, who exist solely for him in tiruvāyppādi, to have a taste of that food. Since the herd-folk could have a change of mind, saying “We would like to carry out the obeisance which we used to do earlier” \[of offering food to indra\], kriṣṇa instantaneously consumed all the food.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa did not want any residual food stuff to be consumed by other herd-folk and hence consumed the entire foodstuff immediately. kriṣṇa had already convinced the herd folk that compared to the *svatantra cētanas* \[entities such as indra et al, who think that they are independent and have thinking abilities\], it is better to offer food to the *paratantra acētana* \[totally dependent entity, which does not have thinking ability\], gōvardana mountain, and they too had accepted that. Lest they change their mind and offer the foodstuffs to indra, kriṣṇa, with an urgency, said *gōvardanōsmi* \[I am gōvardana\] and in a moment, consumed all the food. Since he has pervaded those independent entities and is their antaryāmi (in-dwelling soul), it was acceptable for him to consume the foodstuff. He decided that the foodstuff is not to be given to dependent entities and those who inhabit the village in which he had incarnated. This is the reason, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, that we do not partake of food which has been cooked and offered to other deities.

**mārip pagai puṇartta** – creating the enmity of rains. In other words, when food stuff was cooked, in order to proffer that to indra, kriṣṇa told the herd-folk not to proffer the food to indra but to gōvardana mountain. He then said “*gōvardanōsmi*” \[I am gōvardana\] and ate up all the foodstuff. This made indra to be starved of food. In the resultant anger, he ordered banks of clouds such as *puśkalāvartaka* etc to create a heavy downpour on tiruvāyppādi. Since kriṣṇa started the entire sequence, the verse says that kriṣṇa created the enmity.

**porumā kadal vaṇṇan** – one who has his divine complexion similar to a dark ocean, which has belligerent waves. This term describes the splendour which was seen on his divine form resulting from severing the dependence of herd-folk on other deities \[indra et al\] and the joy that was created in him as a result.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa has a divine complexion which is attractive, like the ocean. Since his action \[of consuming the foodstuff\] led to a fight, the pāsuram says “*porumākadalvaṇṇan*” \[ocean where the waves were fighting with one another\]. Alternatively, it could be considered as *mārip pagai puṇartta mā kadal vaṇṇan* \[one who caused the fight and who is like a huge ocean\]. Since he is *mā kadal vaṇṇan*, even if it is possible to estimate the depth of ocean, it is not possible to estimate the protective nature of his divine quality.

**poṟutta malai** – the mountain which he held. He had held it, continuously, for seven days.

**vattat tadam kaṇ madamān kanṟinai** – a fawn, which had rounded eyes, which were huge, and which was obedient towards its mother, being under the control of the mother-deer.

**valaivāy paṟṟikkoṇḍu** – trapping it in their net. The hunters in the tribes of hills would catch the fawn and hand it over to their womenfolk, to nurture it.

**kuṟa magaḷir kottait talaip pāl koduttu vaḷarkkum** – those tribal women would dip a roll of cotton in a container having milk, and feed the fawn with that milk by keeping the cotton roll on its mouth, similar to its mother’s udder, and nurture it. *kottai* – cotton roll

**gōvardanam …**– since the mountain had grass and water with it all the time, it was nurturing cattle, leading to plentiful of cattle. Hence, it was called “*gōvardanam*” \[that which nurtures and multiplies cattle\]. Since it inverted fully and prevented any drop of water to fall on anyone, when it rained heavily \[due to indra’s anger\], it is referred to as *gōvardanam ennum koṟṟak kudai* \[victorious umbrella called as gōvardanam\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that apart from rains, since the mountain protected the herd-folks and cattle against hail and fire too, enabling removal of undesirable for the entities to be protected \[distress created due to rains\] and fulfilment of desirable for them \[being close to kriṣṇa for seven continuous days, without a break\], the mountain is referred to as *koṟṟak kudai* \[victorious umbrella\]. He further explains the inner meaning of the second part of the pāsuram. *vattattadangaṇ* … this term refers to a young disciple who has attained an ācārya; this disciple, who is like the fawn which has large eyes, has sharp knowledge \[in our *sampradāyam*, eyes are equated to knowledge, bosoms are equated to devotion and waist, to detachment\], obedience towards ācārya and disinterest in protecting himself. Just as the tribal hunters catch the fawn in a net, the ācārya catches the disciple in the net of nārāyaṇa (nārāyana’s divine eyes are the net, for ensnaring the disciple here). The term *kadalvaṇṇan* refers to nārāyaṇa through *rūdyartam* \[generally accepted meaning\]. Through *yōgavyāpti* \[distinct quality\] of removing the ennui of beholder, the term *kadalvaṇṇan* also refers to nārāyaṇa, who removes one’s ennui. Thus, ācārya, who is bestowed with deep knowledge,  and who knows all three times \[past, present and future\], through his amazing faculty of speech, catches the disciple, telling him about the *svarūpa, rūpa, guṇa, vibhūti* characteristics of the term nārāyaṇa \[his *svarūpam* is that he dwells inside every ātmā, his *rūpam* is that all the ātmās reside in him, his *guṇa* is that he is the repository of all the auspicious qualities and his *vibhūti* is that he is the lord of both leelā and nitya vibhūti\]. All these meanings are derived from the single word *nārāyaṇa*. Just as the tribal people handover the fawn to their dependents \[the hill tribal women\], the ācārya hands over the śiśya to his dependents, the śiśyas already with him and tells them to enlighten the newly acquired śiśya. Just as the women feed the fawn with cotton roll, dipped in milk, the ācārya’s śiśyas enlighten the newly acquired disciple with nārāyaṇa’s *sauhardam* \[good heart, which is the equivalent of milk\], through the last term \[nārāyaṇa\] of tirumantram, which is the cotton roll, and which is the essence of all the vēdams. The term *nārāyaṇa* is similar to the roll \[of cotton\]; its shortened meaning, the first syllable ‘*a*’ in the first term of tirumantram, is the cotton \[which is dipped in milk while feeding the fawn\]. Thus, instructing the newly acquired disciple about nārāyaṇa’s *sauhardam* and protecting him through nārāyaṇa is the svāpadēśam for the tribal people catching fawn and nurturing it through milk.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.5.2. Valuvonrum illa

*vaḻuvonṟum illāc ceygai vānavar kōn valippattu munindu vidukkappattamaḻai vandu eḻunāḷ peydu māttadaippa madusūdanan eduttu maṟitta malaiiḻavu tariyādadu ōr īṟṟuppidi iḷam sīyam todarndu mudugudalumkuḻavi idaik kālittu edirndu porum gōvarttanam ennum koṟṟak kudaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

onṟum vaḻu illā – not having any flaw in the means carried out to get the position of indra; seygai – having activities; vānavar kōn – dēvēndran’s; valippattu – being under his control; munindu – in anger (with all his one thousand eyes becoming red); vidukkappatta – ordered; maḻai – clouds; vandu – coming; ēḻu nāḷ – seven days; peydu – pouring; māttadaippa – hindering the herds and herd-folks such that they did not have a way out; madusūdanan – kaṇṇan, who killed the monster, madu; eduttu – lifted effortlessly; maṟitta – held in an inverted manner; malai – mountain; iḷa sīyam – lion cub; todarndu – following (in order to harm an elephant calf); mudugudalum – on approaching; iḻavu – harm coming in the way of its calf; tariyādadu – unable to tolerate; ōr – a; īṟṟup pidi – female elephant, which has given birth to; kuḻavi – its calf; kālidai – within its four legs; ittu – keeping; edirndu – fighting with that lion cub; porum – it is the victorious gōvardana mountain, which is like an umbrella

**Перевод:**

**īndra, the head of celestial entities, had carried out all the means required to attain the position of indra, without any fault. Clouds are under the control of such indra. When indra ordered them, they came to tiruvāyppādi and poured rains for seven days to harm herds and herd-folk such that they could not find a safe place. madusūdanan \[kriṣṇa\], effortlessly lifted gōvardana mountain, upside down, to protect them. On this mountain, when a young lion approached an elephant calf, the mother elephant, which had just then given birth to the calf, unable to tolerate any harm coming in the calf’s way, protected the calf within its legs and drove away the young lion.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, says in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār thinks of poṟutta malai \[the mountain that kriṣṇa held\] and he says in this pāsuram that he held it for seven days.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vaḻuvu …**– indra, had carried out faultless means in order to attain the position of being indra, the head of celestial entities, as a result of which thirty-three crore celestial entities were under his control. Clouds were under the control of that strong indra. This implies that they were totally under his control and had to carry out whatever he ordains them to do.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here the following, to explain the faultless means carried out by indra in order to attain the position of indra. When carrying out the means, if he had not done any particular activity, he had to atone for it by carrying out further activities, in line with śāstrams \[sacred texts\]. Also, he had to carry out those activities, abandoning three thoughts: that he is the doer, that he expects a benefit out of it and that it is ordained for him to do so. Also, he had to carry out the activity without any shortcoming in the materials, in the hymns to be recited and in the activities performed. With all these, he had attained his position as indra. Even when he had to face the order of emperumān, for having crossed emperumān’s orders, he carried out the remedial action for those, without any shortcoming. It is this strength which he had, as the head of celestial entities. The clouds were under this strength of indra’s.

**munindu vidukkappatta** – Not only were they \[clouds\] under the control of his strength. When he was angry, having been denied food and prayer, which the herd-folk were offering him for a long time, he became angry with his thousand eyes becoming reddish, appearing like a thousand lotus flowers bursting out.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that more than that strength explained earlier, indra now had a huge hunger, having been denied his food. His thousand eyes became red, just as mentioned in periya tirumoḻi 10.7 “*āyiram kaṇṇudai indiranār*” (indran, who has thousand eyes).

**maḻai vandu** – Clouds such as puśkalāvartaka etc came \[to tiruvāyppādi\]

**ēḻu nāḷ peydu māttadaippa** – It was not for one or two days, the clouds poured heavily, in a syncronised manner, such that the herds, the herd-men and herd-women had nowhere to go.

**msadusūdanan eduttu maṟitta malai** – he \[kriṣṇa\], who is eminent in annihilating inimical entities \[such as madu, kaitaba et al\], lifted the mountain, gōvardana, and held it upside down such that cattle could stand in a widespread manner, for grazing.

\[What kind of mountain was it?\]

**iḻavu tariyādadōr īṟṟup pidi** – a female elephant, which had recently given birth to a calf, could not tolerate any harm coming in the calf’s way.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the female elephant, due to overflowing affection towards the calf that it had given birth to …

**iḷam sīyam todarndu mudugudalum** – a young lion came towards the calf, in order to harm it.

**kuḻavi idaikkāl ittu edirndu porum** – the mother elephant kept its calf within its legs and went to fight with the young lion.

**gōvardanam ennum koṟṟak kudaiyē** – since the mountain had grass and water with it all the time, it was nurturing cattle, leading to plentiful of cattle. Hence, it was called “*gōvardanam*” \[that which nurtures and multiplies cattle\]. Since it inverted fully and prevented any drop of water to fall on anyone, when it rained heavily \[due to indra’s anger\], it is referred to as *gōvardanam ennum koṟṟak kudai* \[victorious umbrella called as gōvardanam\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says at the end that the elephant calf is equated to a disciple, who approaches his ācārya. The ācārya takes care of the needs of the disciple and does not tolerate any separation from his disciple \[just like the mother elephant\]. The young lion which comes to harm the elephant calf is nothing but the scent of past deeds which come to harm the disciple if he moves away from his ācārya. Thus, just like the mother elephant keeps the calf within its legs and protects it, the ācārya also keeps the disciple under his tutelage and removes the effects of scent of past deeds.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.5.3. Ammait tadangan

*ammait tagangaṇ mada āycciyarum ānāyarum āniraiyumemmaic caraṇ enṟu koḷ enṟu irappa ilangu āḻikkai endai edutta malaitammaic caraṇ enṟa tam pāvaiyaraip punam mēyginṟa mān inam kāṇmin enṟukommaip puyam kunṟar silai kunikkum gōvarttanam ennum koṟṟak kudaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

am – being beautiful; mai – with decorative pigment; tadam – expansive; kaṇ – having eyes; madam – being obedient; āycciyarum – herd-women; An āyarum – herd-men, who have protecting their cattle as their work; A niraiyum – herds of cattle; alaṟi – calling with sadness, due to the harm wrought by rains; emmai – “us; saraṇ enṟu – ‘would protect’ taking a vow; koḷ enṟu – you should hold in your divine mind” saying so; irappa – as they prayed; ilangu – being splendorous; āḻi – divine disc; kai – holding in his divine hand; endai – one, who is my lord; edutta – who lifted (to protect them); malai – mountain; tammai – them; saran enṟa – took refuge, saying “You should protect us”; tam pāvaiyarai – their womenfolk; punam mēyginṟa – “grazing on our dry lands; mān inam – herd of deer; kāṇmin – look”; enṟu – pointing to one another; kommai – being round and huge; puyam – shoulders; kuṟavar – tribal people, inhabiting hills; silai – bow; kunikkum – (aiming to launch arrows at those people) drawing, it is the victorious mountain called as gōvardana

**Перевод:**

**Herd-women, who had their broad, beautiful eyes decorated with black pigment, along with the herd-men, whose work is to protect their cattle, and the herds, called out to kriṣṇa, being harmed by rains, praying “You should think in your divine mind ‘We shall protect them’” My svāmy, who has the splendorous divine disc on his divine hand, lifted  the mountain, gōvardana, to protect them. It is the mountain on which tribal hunters, who have firm, huge shoulders, to protect the womenfolk who took refuge under them, would point out to the deer which are roaming on their dry lands and tell their women folk “Look at them; they are the herd of deer which are out to destroy our dry lands”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**ammaittadam …** – herd-women, as such, have beautiful eyes. On top of that, they have decorated their broad eyes with black pigment; they have a natural quality of being obedient to their men-folk

**ānāyarum** – herd-men, who protect their cattle

**A niraiyum** – cattle, which look up to them for their protection

**alaṟi** – being troubled by the heavy rains, called out, just as it has been said in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5.11.13 “*gōgōpī janasankulam tīvārtam*” (when it rained heavily, herd-men, herd-women and herd were distressed).

**emmaic caraṇ enṟu koḷ enṟu irappa** – they prayed to kriṣṇa, saying “You should assume the role of our protector, saying ‘We shall protect them’”

**ilangāḻikkai endai edutta malai** – My svāmy \[lord\], who has the splendorous divine disc, which reaches the place thought of by my lord \[to destroy enemies\], on his divine hand, lifted the mountain in order to protect us. The reason for mentioning here about the divine disc is – while he had the implement to sever the head of indra \[who troubled the herd-folk and the herd\], he didn’t do that out of thinking “We had taken away his food; let us not take away his head too. He is our follower; due to his bewilderment, he has indulged in a wrongdoing. He will get clarity of mind”. This was mentioned here to indicate his simplicity in lifting the mountain such that the entities, dependent upon him for their protection, were not harmed.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that while kriṣṇa had the splendorous, divine disc in his divine hand, with which he could have dried up the entire waters, pouring through the rain, due to his overflowing urge to protect his followers, he lifted the mountain. It is pertinent for cakrattāḻvān (divine disc) to reach the place thought of by emperumān, in order to destroy his enemies. *endai* – it was only after kriṣṇa lifted the mountain that the entities to be protected were considered as having been born. *endai* – *kāraṇabhūtan*, one who is the causative entity.

**tammaic caraṇ enṟa tam pāvaiyarai** – their women folk, who have taken refuge under them \[the tribal hunters\] for their protection.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the women-folk are totally dependent on the men-folk among the tribal people; they took refuge under the men-folk.

**punam mēyginṟa mān inam kāṇmin enṟu** – they told one another, pointing out to some people who were roaming around in their dry lands “Look at the herd of deer, which is destroying our dry lands”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the tribal hunters tell their women “Stand here and look at us, making the deer, which are destroying our dry lands, to fall down with the grass still in their mouths”. The hunters, having firm, rounded shoulders, drew their bows, taking aim at the trespassers.

He says at the end that through this pāsuram, it is indicated that a śiśya \[disciple, equivalent to the tribal lady\] should not only attain an ācārya \[equivalent to the tribal hunter\], but should also take refuge under the ācārya’s affection, such that the ācārya thinks of the disciple as “He is ours”. ācārya instructs the disciple about matters unknown to the śiśya \[about matters relating to emperumān, śāstrams etc\]. It is not only that the śiśya has taken refuge under the ācārya, he also considers only the words of ācārya as apt to be considered. However, *bhāhyas* and *kudriśtis* \[these are people who do not believe in vēdams and who misinterpret vēdams, respectively\] will try to harm the śiśya through their expertise in words \[this is equivalent to those who roam around in the dry lands, trying to destroy the lands\]. Just like the tribal men drive away such people through their arrows, ācārya will drive away these *bhāhyas* and *kudruśtis* through references such as villibuttūr pagavar words “*yūyam …*” (We believe in emperumān and śāstrams while you people are different from us) and as said in [tiruppallāṇḍu 3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-3-vazhatpattu/) “*engaḷ kuḻuvinil pugadal ottōm* (We will not allow you to people to enter our assembly). If they keep coming to harm the śiśyas, despite these, the ācārya will drive them away through the arrow of knowledge born out of *dānta* (ability to control the mind, senses etc) of the śiśya, which will lead the śiśya to carry out mangaḷāśāsanam to emperumān \[this is equivalent to the arrows let off by the tribal hunters on the trespassers\].

**kommaip puyak kunṟar silai kunikkum** – the tribal hunters, who have rounded, firm shoulders, taking aim at the trespassers, draw their bows.

**gōvardanam ennum koṟṟak kudaiyē** – since the mountain had grass and water with it all the time, it was nurturing cattle, leading to plentiful of cattle. Hence, it was called “*gōvardanam*” \[that which nurtures and multiplies cattle\]. Since it inverted fully and prevented any drop of water to fall on anyone, when it rained heavily \[due to indra’s anger\], it is referred to as *gōvardanam ennum koṟṟak kudai* \[victorious umbrella called as gōvardanam\].

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.5.4. Kaduvayc cina

*kaduvāyc cina vem kaḷiṟṟinukkuk kavaḷam eduttuk koduppānavan pōladivāy uṟakkai ittu eḻap paṟittittu amarar perumān koṇḍu ninṟa malaikadalvāyc cenṟu mēgam kaviḻndu iṟangik kaduvāyppada nīr mugandu ēṟi engumkudavāy pada ninṟu poḻiyum gōvarttanam ennum koṟṟak kudaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kadu – being cruel; vāy – having mouth; sinam – having fury; vem – being angry; kaṇ – having eyes; kaḷiṟṟinukku – for an elephant; kavaḷam – spheres of food; eduttu – gathering; koduppān avan pōl – like the mahout \[elephant keeper\], who gives; adivāy – at the base of the mountain; uṟa – such that it holds; kai – divine hand; ittu – keeping it below; eḻa paṟittittu – uprooting; amarar perumān – kaṇṇan, who is the head of dēvas; koṇḍu ninṟa – sustaining; malai – mountain; mēgam – clouds; kadal vāy senṟu – going to the ocean; iṟangi – alighting on its shore; kaviḻndu – staying, upside down; kaduvāy pada – (ocean) floor becoming exposed; nīr – all the water present \[in the ocean\]; mugandu – taking it; ēṟi – climbing on to the sky; engum – in all the places; kudavāyppada ninṟu – remaining, with water pouring out of a pot full of water when inverted; maḻai poḻiyum – it is the victorious mountain gōvardanam, on which rain pours

**Перевод:**

**Just as a mahout (caretaker of an elephant) gives food, by rolling it into spheres, to the elephant which has a cruel mouth, which is in full fury and which has reddish eyes, kriṣṇa, the head of nityasūris, uprooted the gōvardana mountain by keeping his divine hand under the base of the mountain. He seized it and held it. Clouds go to an ocean, alight on its shore, imbibe the entire water from the ocean such that its floor could be seen, rise up with the imbibed water and pour it everywhere, like a pot of water pouring it out, when it is inverted.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that this pāsuram celebrates the effortlessness in lifting the gōvardana mountain.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kadu vāyc china vengaṇ kaḷiṟṟinukku** – for the elephant which had a cruel mouth, anger and eyes which were spitting fire

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *kaduvāy* refers to the elephant having the trumpeting sound and speed, which an elephant has. *vengaṇ* refers to eyes which were like lightning, and which were fiery like cloud having fire around it, coming from lightning.

**kavaḷam eduttuk koduppān avan pōl** – like the mahout, who rolls food in his hands and feeds the elephant. Through this, cloud has been placed in the status of elephant, mountain has been placed in the status of food and kriṣṇa, who lifted the mountain has been compared to the mahout, who feeds the elephant. The reason for comparing the elephant to cloud is due to its equivalence with the elephant. We could recall [nācciyār tirumoḻi pāsuram 8.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/09/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-8-9/) “*mada yānai pōl eḻunda māmugilgāḷ*” (Oh, the great clouds who have risen like the elephant in exultation). Since the pāsuram says *kaduvāyc china vengaṇ kaḷiṟu*, it is clear that it appears to be in exultation. This is explained as follows: *kaduvāy* – the elephant has a cruel mouth through which it was raising its trumpeting sound, and it also indicates its anger. The term *vengaṇ* refers to eyes which are spitting fire. These features are noticeable in the cloud too. It will raise a clattering sound, which will frighten those who hear it; it will pour \[rains\] obstinately. Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.7.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/08/thiruvaimozhi-9-7-5-theli-visumbu/) “*tī vaḷaittu minnilagum*” (Oh, clouds which are having increased beauty due to the presence of lightning which is like a ring of fire carried around!), it has the ring of fire brought about by lightning around it; due to its darkness, its huge form and height, it could be said that it looks like an “elephant in exultation” to those who see it.

**adivāy uṟakkai ittu eḻap paṟittittu** – kriṣṇa thrust his one divine hand under the base of the mountain, kept his other divine hand on top of the mountain and uprooted it.

**amarar perumān koṇḍu ninṟa malai** – the entity who is the lord of the indefatigable nityasūris, appearing as if he was without help from anyone, lifted and held the mountain, on his own.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *amarar perumān* refers to emperumān being the head of nityasūris. Alternatively, the term *amarar* would refer to celestial entities and *amarar perumān* would refer to their lord, indra. However, since indra has now become inimical, emperumān changed his \[indra’s\] name and assumed indra’s name for himself.

**kadalvāyc cenṟu mēgam kaviḻndu iṟangi** – clouds, going to the ocean, alighted near the shore of the ocean and inverted themselves \[with their mouths close to the ocean and their backs, pointing to the sky\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the clouds descended on the ocean and sucked in water, like an extremely thirsty person, and rose up the sky. Since indra, in anger, had ordained them to carry out a task, they rose up the sky to carry it out; since it was a fiery rain, all the places where they poured became hot.

**kaduvāyp pada nīr mugandu ēṟi** – the term *kaduvāyppada* refers to having a shortage. Through this, it is hinted that the clouds sucked in the entire water available with the ocean, such that the ocean felt that there was a shortage of water with it, and rose up in the sky. Alternatively, *kaduvudal* would refer to seizing with the mouth. In other words, having an affectionate mouth, and just as mentioned in [tirunedundāṇḍagam 24](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/10/thirunedunthandakam-24/) “*perum pauvam maṇḍi uṇḍa*” (entering the great ocean and sucking out the entire water from it), the cloud took in all the water from the ocean such that the ocean became hard floor, and rose up in the sky.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai adds here that the term *kadu* could be considered as a modification of the samaskruta term *kratu*, which means a ceremony or ritual, and the clouds poured out water such that it was flowing fully, as at the end of a ceremony.

**engum kudavāyp pada ninṟu maḻai poḻiyum** – just like a pot, when inverted, pours out the entire water held in it, the clouds remained for seven days and poured rains.

**gōvarttanam ennum koṟṟak kudaiyē** – since the mountain had grass and water with it all the time, it was nurturing cattle, leading to plentiful of cattle. Hence, it was called “*gōvardanam*” \[that which nurtures and multiplies cattle\]. Since it inverted fully and prevented any drop of water to fall on anyone, when it rained heavily \[due to indra’s anger\], it is referred to as *gōvardanam ennum koṟṟak kudai* \[victorious umbrella called as gōvardanam\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says at the end, the following explanation for the verse *kadalvāyc cenṟu mēgam kaviḻndu iṟangik kaduvāyppada nīr mugandu ēṟi* – just as the cloud descends onto the ocean and takes in water from it, great entities, such as our ācāryas \[preceptors\], also descended to the ocean of *samsāram* and carried out all activities which are befitting samsāram, without any taste in it. Instead of getting caught in the quagmire of samsāram, they ascend \[to śrī vaikuṇṭam\], without being affected by the faults seen in samsāram. Just as vibhīśaṇa, after spending considerable length of time in lankā, left it and went up the sky \[*antarikśa gata*: *śrīmān*\] while approaching śrī rāma, these ācāryas too, rise up. Similar to the clouds gathering only pure water from the salty ocean and distributing that good water to everyone, the ācāryas too, without considering the lowliness of samsāram, take up the good features from it \[such as *ācāram, anuśtānam, nityānusandhānam, nitya tiruvaradanam* etc, which are respectively good conduct, carrying out such activities, reciting hymns which are to be recited daily, carrying out divine worship to emperumān\] and spread those to their disciples. They realise that they are fully dependent on emperumān and instruct their disciples too accordingly. This is carried out as an example to *lōka sangraham* \[the people at large, as a whole\]. Just as the cloud carries the water for some time before giving it to others, the ācāryas too carry out the *anuśtānams* while instructing their disciples. Clouds were expected to help others. However, the clouds were harming the followers of kriṣṇa \[herd, and herd-folk\]. This is because of its *anyaśēśatvam* \[being dependent on others, instead of on emperumān\]. The reason for this \[being *anyaśēśatvam*\] is because in the previous yugam \[during śrī rāmāvatāram\], it had gone against the order of śrī rāma \[when śrī rāma surrendered to the ocean for giving way for his army of monkeys to cross the ocean and reach lankā\], it did not give way. The result in this yugam is that it became dependent on indra.

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.5.5. Vanattil ulleer

*vānattil uḷḷeer! valiyeer uḷḷeerēl aṟaiyō! vandu vāngumin enbavan pōlēnattu uruvāgiya īsan endai idavan eḻa vāngi edutta malaikānak kaḷiyānai tan kombu iḻandu kaduvāy madam sōrat tan kai eduttukūnal piṟai vēṇḍi aṇṇāndu niṟkum gōvarttanam ennum koṟṟak kudaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vānattil uḷḷeer – “Oh, those who are inhabiting the upper worlds!; valiyīr uḷḷeerēl – If you have strength; aṟai – shouting, as an indication of being victorious; vandu – coming to this place; vāngumin – lift this mountain and see”; enbavan pōl – as if saying, like one; ēnam uru āgiya – as one who had incarnated as the great boar, dug out earth from the walls of universe and lifted; īsan – being the controller of all; endai – one, who is my lord; idavan – like a block of mud; eḻa – to lift from the base; vāngi – taking; edutta – and stood, lifting; malai – the mountain; kānam – in forest; kaḷi – roaming with pride; yānai – elephant; than kombu – its tusk; iḻandu – losing it (since it roamed around unbounded, it struck with its tusk at one place and; kaduvāy – in the mouth from where the tusk snapped and it had got hurt; madam – liquid of rut; sōra – as it leaked; than kai eduttu – lifting its trunk; kūnal – curved; piṟai – third day after new moon \[crescent of moon\]; vēṇḍi – desirously; aṇṇāndu niṟkum – standing and looking up, the victorious mountain of gōvarttanam, which is like an umbrella

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa, who had taken the form of a great boar, dug up earth from the walls of universe and kept it on his tusks. Such an entity, who controls everyone and who is my svāmy \[lord\], lifted the mountain \[gōvardana\] as if it were a clod. “Oh, those who are inhabiting the upper worlds! If you think that you have the strength, come here, shouting cries of becoming victorious, lift this mountain and show your strength”. An elephant, roaming around in the forest, with pride, had lost one tusk, having hit it against some hard surface in the forest. At the place in its mouth, where the tusk snapped, the liquid of rut was coming out. The elephant lifted its trunk, and with desire, was looking at the crescent of moon \[thinking that the crescent is its broken tusk and it wanted to grab it and put it back\]. Such is the eminence of gōvardana mountain.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that this pāsuram too is an example of gōvardana mountain’s eminence.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vānattu …** – Oh, those who think that because you are living in the upper worlds, you have more strength than human beings! If you have the strength to carry out the tasks which you think of …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: “Oh, those who are living in the upper worlds, and have your strength through your boons and shoulders! If you have strength like I have, take this mountain from me and protect the herd and the herd-folk in this place”. It is obvious that there is no protector there, apart from kriṣṇa.

**aṟaiyō vandu vāngumin enbavan pōl** – Like a person who says “Victory is ours! Come, take this mountain and lift it”

**ēnattu uruvāgiya īsan endai** – Earth, consisting of seven parts and seven oceans had gone to the floor of the great deluge, sticking to the walls of the universe. Assuming the form of a great boar, which does not step back on seeing water or quagmire, just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.4.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/thiruvaimozhi-7-4-3-nanrila/) “*ūnṟiyidandu eyiṟṟil koṇḍa*” (the time when emperumān, as he great boar, pushed the earth, which had got submerged in deluge, dug it out and kept it on the tusk), he dug it out from the walls of universe, rising into the ethereal layer. He is the controller of every entity, making them to carry out tasks as he desires. He is the reason for their existence, being the causative factor for all.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that emperumān has the knowledge, strength and the connection \[relationship\] to dig out earth from the walls of the universe. For one who lifted that entity \[entire earth\], lifting this \[mountain\] will agree well.

**idavan eḻa vāngi edutta malai** – along with the base of the mountain, he \[kriṣṇa\] lifted it, as if it were a block of mud and stood. Instead of saying *idavan enap paṟitta malai* \[plucked the mountain\] or *idavan enap pērtta malai* \[cleaved the mountain\], since the verse says *idavan ena vāngi*, it confirms that he lifted it effortlessly. For the supreme entity who lifted the earth, which had sunk to the bottom of the universe with all its mountains, and kept it on his tusk, is lifting the mountain, which appeared like a clod, a difficult task?

**kānak kaḷiyānai than kombu iḻandu** – an elephant, roaming around in the forest with pride, was engaging in war-like activities. At a place where it had tried to hit against a hard surface, its tusk broke. Losing its tusk …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the elephant, which was roaming around in its own land, lost its tusk to a lion. Since blood was pouring down from that place in its mouth, all the waters would get dried up.

**kaduvāy madam sōra** – *kaduvudal* – secreting. In the mouth where the tusk broke, its rutting fluid was secreting and pouring down.

**than kai …** – due to its inability, without the lost tusk, it looked at the crescent of the moon, mistook it for its broken tusk, desired it and looked up at it.

**gōvarttanam ennum koṟṟak kudaiyē** – since the mountain had grass and water with it all the time, it was nurturing cattle, leading to plentiful of cattle. Hence, it was called “*gōvardanam*” \[that which nurtures and multiplies cattle\]. Since it inverted fully and prevented any drop of water to fall on anyone, when it rained heavily \[due to indra’s anger\], it is referred to as *gōvardanam ennum koṟṟak kudai* \[victorious umbrella called as gōvardanam\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that it had lost a single tusk and that is the reason that it was looking at the crescent \[if it had lost both tusks, it would not have looked at the moon’s crescent\]. He further explains in his svāpadēśam, at the end, that just like the elephant roaming in the forest, we pray to live in the forest of samsāram, through our desire; our *mamatā* \[considering everything related to us as ours, for example spouse, children, land etc\] is the tusk of the elephant. When our preceptors \[who are like the lion\], who are capable of defeating enemies \[of our sampradāyam\], such as *bāhyas* \[those who do not accept enunciations of vēdams\] and *kudruśtis* \[those who misinterpret the enunciations of vēdams\], establishing their philosophy \[viśiśtādvaitam\] remove these *mamatā* through rightful and logical arguments based on vēdams and through tirumantram \[primary among the three esoteric tenets of our sampradāyam\], the pride which we had earlier gets removed. They also take assistance of the meanings of *praṇavam* \[that emperumān is the protector, that he is the root cause of all entities, that he is the lord etc\], through the syllables *a, u* and *ma* along with the hidden fourth case, *āya* which is atop *a* \[through all these, we come to know that we are the protected, that we are the servitors, that we exist only for emperumān etc. When these concepts sink in, the concept of *mamatā* will disappear\]. Just like the elephant extending its trunk to get the crescent of moon, jīvātmā, after knowing the concepts mentioned above, may still try to reach up \[śrī vaikuṇṭam\] through his efforts \[means other than emperumān\]. ācāryas, by removing the elephant’s tusk \[mamatā\] will explain the full meaning of *prakrutyātma vivēkha jñānam* \[ātmā is different from dēham, the form\] through *padatrayam* \[*praṇavam, nama*: and *nārāyaṇāya*, which represent respectively *ananyārha śēśatvam*, being servitor only to emperumān, *ananya śaraṇatvam*, taking refuge only under emperumān and *ananya bhōjñatvam*, enjoying only emperumān by carrying out servitude to him and making him pleased\].

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.5.6. Seppadu udaiya

*seppādu udaiya tirumālavan tan sendāmaraik kai viral aindinaiyumkappāga maduttu maṇi nedum tōḷ kāmbākagak koduttuk kavitta malaieppādum parandu iḻi teḷḷaruvi ilangu maṇi muttu vadam piṟaḻakkuppāyam ena ninṟu kātci tarum gōvarttanam ennum koṟṟak kudaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

seppādu udaiya – having the quality of honesty; tirumāl – being the consort of śrī mahālakśmi; avan – one, who has that quality; than – his; sem tāmarai – looking like a reddish lotus flower; kai – in the divine hand; viral aindinaiyum – the five fingers; kappāga – as a handle, at the base of the mountain, which looks look an umbrella; maduttu – keeping closely; maṇi – having the complexion of a bluish gemstone; nedu – being long; tōḷ – divine shoulder; kāmbāga – as the support for that umbrella; koduttu – offering; kavitta – inverted; malai – the mountain; eppādum – on all the sides; parandu iḻi – remaining widespread; teḷ aruvi – clear streams; ilangu – shining well; maṇi – like a beautiful pearl chain; piṟaḻa – to shine individually; kuppāyam ena ninṟu – appearing as if that were a pearl dress for him; kātci tarum – it is the victorious mountain, gōvardana, which looks in that manner

**Перевод:**

**The divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi, tirumāl, who has the quality of being honest, made his five divine fingers, which looked like reddish lotus flowers on his divine hand, as the handle at the base of the mountain \[gōvardanam\], which looked like an umbrella; he gave his long divine shoulder, which has the complexion of a bluish gemstone, as the support for the umbrella and held the mountain, upside down. It is the mountain on which clear streams, which are seen shining on all the sides of the mountain, appear like a shining pearl dress for him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**seppādu udaiya tirumāl** – *seppādu* refers to the quality of honesty. Since the verse says *tirumāl* too, here the honesty refers to emperumān’s response to pirātti, as mentioned in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.9.2 “*sidaiguraittāḷ āgilum…..nanṟu seydār*” \[Even if śrī mahālakśmi complains about his devotees, he will argue with her saying ‘my devotees will not do anything wrong and even if they did anything, it is only for the good’\]. Alternatively, this could be construed as arising out of indra’s anger at having been denied food when he ordained clouds to pour down heavily in tiruvāyppādi. kriṣṇa had told the herd-people that the mountain gōvardana would protect them. When the herd and herd-people were suffering, instead of “Let them suffer”, kriṣṇa had protected them through the same gōvardana mountain, which he had told them earlier that it would protect, by lifting it as an umbrella over all of them. Since the reason for protecting is on account of his association with śrī mahālakśmi, the verse says here *tirumāl*.

**avan** – one who has a divine quality like that \[honesty\]

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says for the term *avan* that kriṣṇa is one who has infatuation towards his followers.

**than sendāmaraik kai viral aindinaiyum kappāga maduttu** – keeping the five fingers on his divine hand, which is like a reddish lotus flower, as the spokes of an umbrella , in a dense manner.

**maṇi nedum tōḷ kāmbāgak koduttuk kavitta malai** – giving his divine shoulder, which has the complexion of a bluish gemstone, and which is long, as the support for that umbrella, he held the mountain in an inverted fashion in order to prevent any harm coming in the way of the people who live in the five lakh houses in tiruvāyppādi, as well as to the herds of cattle such that they could get to feed on grass which had not been stamped upon by anyone’s feet and could get to drink water without any problem.

**eppādum parandu iḻi teḷḷaruvi** – just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.4.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/thiruvaimozhi-7-4-10-mey-nirai/) “*sunaivāy niṟai nīr piḷiṟīc coriya*” (ponds on the mountain gōvardana, having water filled to the brim, pour down with a tumultuous sound), clear streams of water were surrounding kriṣṇa on all sides, coming down.

**ilangu maṇi muttu vadam piṟaḻa** – each of those streams was shining like a beautiful pearl chain

**kuppāyam ena ninṟu kātci tarum** – they will give an appearance as if they were like a dress of pearl for kriṣṇa

**gōvarttanam ennum koṟṟak kudaiyē** – since the mountain had grass and water with it all the time, it was nurturing cattle, leading to plentiful of cattle. Hence, it was called “*gōvardanam*” \[that which nurtures and multiplies cattle\]. Since it inverted fully and prevented any drop of water to fall on anyone, when it rained heavily \[due to indra’s anger\], it is referred to as *gōvardanam ennum koṟṟak kudai* \[victorious umbrella called as gōvardanam\].

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.5.7. Padangal palavum

*padangaḷ palavum udaip pāmbu araiyan padar būmiyait tāngik kidappavan pōltadangai viral aindum malara vaittut tāmōdaran tāngu tada varai tanadangac cenṟu ilangaiyai īdaḻitta anuman pugaḻ pādit tam kuttangaḷaikkudangaik koṇḍu mandigaḷ kaṇ vaḷarttum gōvarttanam ennum koṟṟak kudaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

padangaḷ pala udai – having many hoods (in the term palavum, the syllable um does not have any specific meaning; it is there for the metrics); pāmbu araiyan – one, who is the king of snakes; padar – being expansive; būmiyai – earth \[here, the term earth refers to the entire universe\]; tāngik kidappavan pōl – just as remaining, supporting through his heads; tada – having space; kai viral aindum – five fingers on the divine hand; malara vaittu – spreading them out; dāmōdaran – one who is called as ‘dāmōdaran’; tāngu – standing, supporting; tada – huge; varai tān – the mountain; senṟu – attaining, through the path of sky; ilangaiyai – lankā; adanga – fully; īdaḻitta – destroyed; anuman – hanuman’s; pugaḻ – eminence; mandigaḷ – female monkeys; pādi – singing; tam – their; kuttangaḷai – baby monkeys; kudangai – on their palms; koṇḍu – lifting; kaṇ vaḷarttum – caressing them and putting them to sleep, occurs on gōvardana mountain

**Перевод:**

**ādiśēśan, who is the king of snakes and who has many hoods, supports the earth through his heads. Similar to that, dāmōdaran \[kriṣṇa\] spreads his five divine fingers and supports the huge mountain, gōvardana. This is the victorious mountain where female monkeys sing the praise of hanuman when he reached lankā through the path of sky and destroyed the city of lankā. The monkeys support their little ones on their palms, caressing them and putting them to sleep.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that ādiśēśan’s action of supporting the earth, became fruitful now \[āḻvār wanted to quote a simile for kriṣṇa holding gōvardana mountain; today, he quoted this as an example and thus, ādiśēśan’s activity bore fruit today\].*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**padangaḷ …** – like *nāgarājan* \[king of snakes, referring to ādiśēśan\] who has many heads, supports the expansive universe, through his heads

**tadam kai viral aindum malara vaittu** – \[kriṣṇa\] spreading out his fingers which are present on his expansive divine hand

**dāmōdaran tāngu tada varai than** – kriṣṇa was simple enough to be tied down \[to a mortar\] and beaten up by a person \[yaśōdāp pirātti\], who had no strength. He also acted as if he were without any strength to break free from that binding. It was the same kriṣṇa who held aloft the huge mountain, gōvardana. The mountain was such huge in its area that all the people living in the five lakh houses inside tiruvāyppādi, along with their cattle and calves, could take shelter under it. The term *tān* \[as in *tada varai tān*\] signifies the weight of the mountain, the trees which have grown on it, all the animals which were inhabiting it and all the people who were dwelling in it.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, additionally, here that ādiśēśan, who supports all the universe from down below, is a jīvātmā, in whom ādiśēśan has applied his strength. This jīvātmā has attained this status through his previously acquired *puṇya palam* \[fruit of his virtues\], emperumān’s ordainment and his \[emperumān’s\] support. Unlike that case, emperumān’s five fingers on their own held the mountain aloft \[there is no need for any of the three features which the jīvātmā, in whom ādiśēśan had pervaded, had\].

**adangac cenṟu ilangaiyai īdaḻitta** – lankā was a place which could not be easily entered into by anyone on account of the three protections which it had \[protection through ocean, protection through forest and protection through mountains\], the boons which had been granted to rāvaṇa by celestial entities as well as rāvaṇa’s strength of \[his\] shoulders. It could not be destroyed by anyone. It was such a place that hanuman, as mentioned in periya tirumoḻi 10.2.6 “*ōdamā kadalaik kadandu ēṟi*” (going past the huge ocean with belligerent waves), reached and destroyed as mentioned in the same periya tirumoḻi pāsuram 10.2.6 “*uyar koḷ mākkadikāvai iṟuttu*” (destroying the huge *aśōkavanam*, which was distinguished and fragrant). Singing the praises of such hanuman…

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that hanuman made some people in lankā to engage with him in a fight, he annihilated some in the fight, he made some people to come under his control through fear, using his strength in a just manner, through his quality of forgiving, through his power of speech. All these, which are śrī rāma *kainkaryam* \[servitude to śrī rāma\] brought him fame. This is termed as *anuman pugaḻ* \[hanuman’s eminence\]. Just as it has been mentioned in the dhyāna ślōkam of śrī rāmāyaṇam “*ullanka sindō*: *gōśpada kruta vā rāsīm*” \[hanuman crossed the ocean through a jump, making the ocean as the water under a cow’s hoof\], every act of hanumān’s brought him fame.

**tam kuttangaḷai** – their respective little monkey. Instead of saying *kutty* \[little one\], the reason for saying *kuttan* is due to affection.

**kudangaik koṇḍu** – keeping them on their palms

**mandigaḷ kaṇ vaḷarttum** – *mandi* – female monkey; the female monkeys will caress their little ones and put them to sleep \[recounting the eminence of hanumān\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai raises a query here. While many people had carried out servitude to śrī rāma, what is distinguishing about hanuman? Also, when female monkeys tell their younger ones about the eminence of their ancestors, instead of speaking about the king of monkeys \[sugrīva\], why are they speaking about a servitor, hanuman? He explains this saying that hanuman’s service was *niśkāraṇāya* \[without any underlying reason\]. While hanuman brought others to carry out servitude to śrī rāma, he did not need a reason for doing that. emperumān’s *anugraham* \[mercy\] brought him to emperumān. In [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.3.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2026/04/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-3-3-7/), āḻvār had said “*anganam āvargaḷē*” \[those who carry out harmful acts against my son will die like that\]. Why is he now praising hanuman, when hanuman had destroyed life and properties? tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that activities which bring auspiciousness to emperumān are eminent ones for āḻvār. Thus, he praises hanuman’s activities. Just as āḻvār says in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4<sup>th</sup> centum “*puḷḷaraiyan pugaḻ kuḻaṟum*” \[birds will speak about the eminence of garuda, the king among birds\], he says here that female monkeys tell their young ones about the eminence of hanuman and put them to sleep. If a person attains his ācārya and carries out servitude without any shortcoming, those born in that person’s lineage, those who live in the place where that person stayed, those who live in the place where he went, all these persons are acceptable to āḻvār. The term *kaṇ vaḷarttum* indicates that the ācārya tells his disciples the manner in which he was nurtured by his ācārya, viz. varying out servitude to emperumān and his followers. He says that this is termed as *mārbil kaivaittu uṟangap prāpti* \[in our sampradāyam, we do not engage in protecting ourselves. We leave our protection in the hands of emperumān and sleep without any worry about our protection\]. In the same way, the female monkeys put their younger ones to sleep by recounting about the eminence of the person in their ancestors \[hanuman\] who was involved in servitude to emperumān. ācāryas instruct their disciples about *tyaja, vraja* and *mā śuca*: \[All these three terms come from bhagavat gītā 18.66, *tyaja* – refers to giving up taking efforts on our own to attain emperumān, *vraja* refers to taking refuge under emperumān \[alone\] and *mā śuca*: refers to not grieving\]. This *nirbharatva anusandāna paryantam* \[completely leaving aside our protection\] is the essence of the term *kaṇ vaḷarttum*.

**gōvarttanam ennum koṟṟak kudaiyē** – since the mountain had grass and water with it all the time, it was nurturing cattle, leading to plentiful of cattle. Hence, it was called “*gōvardanam*” \[that which nurtures and multiplies cattle\]. Since it inverted fully and prevented any drop of water to fall on anyone, when it rained heavily \[due to indra’s anger\], it is referred to as *gōvardanam ennum koṟṟak kudai* \[victorious umbrella called as gōvardanam\].

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan
