## 3.5.8. Salama mugil

*salamā mugil palgaṇap pōrkkaḷattuc caramāri poḻindu engum pūsal ittunalivān uṟak kēdagam kōppavan pōl nārāyaṇan mun mugam kātta malaiilaivēy kurambait tavamā munivar irundār naduvē senṟu aṇār soṟiyakolaivāyc cina vēngai ninṟu uṟangum gōvarttanam ennum koṟṟak kudaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

salam – imbibing water and rising; mā mugil – monsoon clouds’; pal gaṇam – many groups; pōr kaḷattu – in the battlefield; saram māri poḻindu – pouring, as if raining arrows; engum – throughout tiruvāyppādi village; pūsal ittu – thundering and battling; nalivān – harming; uṟa – in a focussed manner; kēdagam kōppavan pōl – as if holding a shield; nārāyaṇan – one who is nārāyaṇan (holding \[the mountain\] in the divine hand); mun – coming, opposing; mugam – from the face of rains; kātta – protected; malai – mountain; ilai vēy kurambai – dwelling in hermitage; tavam mā munivar inrundār naduvē senṟu – going amidst sages who are carrying out penance; aṇār soṟiya – as they rub their necks; kolai – killing; vāy – having mouth; sinam – having anger; vēngai – tigers; ninṟu uṟangum – it is on the victorious gōvardana mountain where the tigers stand and sleep

**Перевод:**

**Groups of monsoon clouds, carrying water fully and rising, went all over tiruvāyppādi village, creating a thunderous noise as if they were in a battlefield, and poured out rains, as if arrows were raining in a battlefield. While they were focussed on harming \[herd and herd-folk\], nārāyaṇan held the mountain \[gōvardana\] like a shield against the rains which were coming opposite and protected \[the herd and herd-folk\]. It is the mountain where tigers, which have anger and have mouths which kill, go amidst sages, who dwell in their hermitages carrying out penance, stand and sleep, even as the sages rub their necks.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**salamāmugil …** – Huge clouds, in a large group, went to the ocean, drank up all the water in the ocean and rose up the sky. Just like arrows rain in a battle field, these clouds started pouring out water contained in them throughout tiruvāyppādi, without making any distinction between the place and the grazing lands. They thundered with a huge sound, engaging in a battle, focussed on harming everyone in their way, as if asking “Is there anyone who could escape from us?” When they did this, nārāyaṇan who is the protector of everyone, held up the mountain in his divine hand, just like one holds a shield to protect from the arrows raining in a battlefield.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that warriors such as arjuna et al, shoot arrows which will multiply themselves to many. In the same way, the water drops from clouds multiplied into many and started raining heavily. Just as a capable person holds up his shield to protect from such arrows, kriṣṇa held up the mountain such that the pouring rain did not affect anyone. Each droplet of water in that rainfall was like an arrow in the battlefield. When the clouds were focussed on harming him and the entities who were to be protected  by him, nārāyaṇan, who is the meaning of the root of the syllable ‘*a*’ in *praṇavam* \[root of the syllable *a* signifies that emperumān is the protector\], looking for the desire of the entities to be protected as an excuse, held the mountain such that the face of clouds darkened in shame since they could not cause any harm to anyone, despite pouring both fire and rain on them.

**ilai vēy kurambai** – hut, built with dried leaves. This refers to a hermitage. Great sages, who carry out penance, have made this as their dwelling place.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the sages are those who keep constantly meditating on emperumān.

**tava māmunivar** – Great sages, who are fully immersed in carrying out penance.

**irundār naduvē senṟu** – going amidst such sages who had assembled together at one place for carrying out penance.

**aṇār soṟiya** – Going to such people for getting their necks scratched. They \[sages\] are people who do not have any fear about anything, since they see every entity as *sarvamum bhagavat ātmakam* – every entity has emperumān as the in-dwelling soul.

**kolai vāyc china vēngaigaḷ ninṟu uṟangum** – Tigers, which have mouths which are accustomed to killing, and which are angry, will sleep due to the comfort of that rubbing.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the entities which look for footprints of elephants through the gaps between bamboo trees, will go amidst the sages in order to get their necks to be rubbed such that they could sleep. Would those, who are engaged in carrying out penance, stroke the necks of tigers? Sages carry out an experiment here to see if wild animals will exhibit their natural fury when they are with them and if they \[the sages\] will get attacked, in order to test whether they have reached a stage where they are able to look at anything with equanimity. Hence, it is possible that the tigers will settle down near them and that the sages will stroke their necks. *aṇār* – neck. *malai* – the victorious mountain, which is like an umbrella. The sages do not know that kriṣṇa would uproot the mountain and hold it upside down. If during the course of their penance, if the mountain is to be held upside down, they may fall down, along with the animals. In that case, they would have heard the sweet music emanating from kriṣṇa’s flute and see kriṣṇa’s divine form, as a fruit of their penance. But they had to fall down. After they fell down, whether they stood like the animals which heard kriṣṇa’s divine music from the flute or whether they closed their ears and eyes \[thus preventing the sweet music from kriṣṇa’s divine flute from reaching their ears and the great sight of his divine form from reaching their eyes\] resulting from the shock of falling down, wondering whether this is the fruit of their penance, we do not know, says tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, at the end.

**gōvarttanam ennum koṟṟak kudaiyē** – since the mountain had grass and water with it all the time, it was nurturing cattle, leading to plentiful of cattle. Hence, it was called “*gōvardanam*” \[that which nurtures and multiplies cattle\]. Since it inverted fully and prevented any drop of water to fall on anyone, when it rained heavily \[due to indra’s anger\], it is referred to as *gōvardanam ennum koṟṟak kudai* \[victorious umbrella called as gōvardanam\].

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.5.9. Vanpey mulai

*van pēy mulai uṇḍadōr vāy udaiyan van tūṇ ena ninṟadōr van parattaitan pēr ittukkoṇḍu daraṇi tannil dāmōdaran tāngu tada varai tānmunbē vaḻi kātta musukkaṇangaḷ mudugil peydu tammudaik kuttangaḷaikombu ēṟṟi irundu kudi payiṟṟum gōvarttanam ennum koṟṟak kudaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

van pēy – cruel pūtanā; mulai – bosom (smeared with poison); uṇḍadu ōr vāy udaiyan – one, who had a mouth, through which he had consumed; van parattai – heavy weight \[bearing it\]; ninṟadu ōr – one who stood; van tūṇ ena – like a strong pillar; than pēr – his name of gōvardanan; ittukkoṇḍu – giving to that mountaiun; daraṇi tannil – on this land; dāmōdaran – one who was obedient towards a herd-woman such that she could tie him down and beat him; tāngu – stood, holding; tada varai tān – the huge mountain; musukkaṇangaḷ – troops of \[a type of\] monkeys; munbē – already; vaḻi kātta – to show the manner of jumping from one branch to another branch; tammudaik kuttangaḷai – their little ones; mudugil – on their backs; peydu – taking them; kombu – top of tree; ēṟṟi irundu – hoisting up; kudi – to move from one part to another; payiṟṟum – it is the victorious mountain, called as gōvardanam, where they were training

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa has a divine mouth through which he consumed milk from the poisoned bosom of the cruel pūtanā. He is obedient towards a herd-woman \[his mother, yaśōdāPpirātti\] such that she could tie him down to a mortar and beat him up. He stood, bearing the mountain, which had his name of gōvardana, like a strong pillar which was holding up a heavy weight. On that mountain, troops of a type of monkeys, were training their little ones in jumping from one branch to another and from one part of a tree to another part, carrying their little ones on their backs.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**van pēy mulai uṇḍadōr vāy udaiyan** – one, who had a mouth with which he consumed the bosom of a cruel fiend. What is the cruelty for the fiend? Despite seeing his \[kriṣṇa’s\] infant age and his divine form, she had the cruelty of a hardened heart. Alternatively, the word cruelty could be considered as an adjective for the fiend’s bosom, due to the cruel nature of the poison on the bosom. It was the bosom on which poison had been loaded. The reason for saying *ōr vāy* is that it was a unique mouth that consumed milk, tolerating that poison and annihilating her, through that mouth.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that this verse refers to kriṣṇa having a mouth with which he consumed the bosom of the cruel fiend. It also refers to kriṣṇa having a cruel mouth with which he consumed the bosom of the fiend. Cruelty for the fiend comes from the context of coming to kill kriṣṇa herself, when kamsan could not harm kriṣṇa and having a cruel heart to accomplish that task. It also refers to the cruelty of the bosom which was loaded with poison. Cruelty of the poison comes out of the fact that even if a drop of this poison drops on another fiend, that fiend will get killed. Cruelty of the divine mouth \[of kriṣṇa\] is that if an unfavourable person gives even nectar, that person will get annihilated. That is his nature. Thus, when she came deveptively, in the garb of a favourable person \[she came in the garb of yaśōdāp pirātti, kriṣṇa’s mother\], even though he had thought in his divine mind that he too will drink it, deceptively, his divine mouth would not tolerate it. Since the mouth did not tolerate it, it could be said that it was cruel. *ōr vāy* – a unique, divine mouth. This distinguishes kriṣṇa from the one \[rudra\] who had also consumed poison, *kālakūta* poison. This is because, rudra had consumed different types of poison from a young age and it was at a mature age that he had consumed the *kālakūta* poison, while kriṣṇa consumed this poison when he was an infant, and this poison was such that even if a drop had fallen, it would have burnt a person.

**van tūṇ ena ninṟdōr van parattai** – Just like a strong pillar which sustains a heavy weight. The word *darittal*, which refers to sustaining, is not seen in the verse; it has to be assumed here, to get the meaning.

**than pērittuk koṇḍu** – giving his name of *gōvardanan*, to that mountain \[the word *gōvardanan* refers to one who nurtures cattle\].

**daraṇi tannil** – this term distinguishes this land from other lands. In other words, unlike satyalōkam, kailāśam etc, where only entities such as brahmā, rudra et al could see him, this incident happened on earth such that even lowly entities could see.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the place \[where kriṣṇa held the mountain\] was distinguished from other places since it was only here that entities starting from herd-men and herd-women and ending with brahmā, rudra et al could see it.

**dāmōdaran** – One who was obedient towards his mother such that she could tie him down. Since the verse mentions about *van pēy mulai uṇḍadōr vāyudaiyan* and *dāmōdaran*, this signifies that kriṣṇa annihilated one who came in the form of his mother and was obedient towards the mother who gave birth to him.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that there is a difference from other children who carried out the words of mother and were under mother’s control. yaśōdāp pirātti told kriṣṇa, as mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5.9.15 “*ati cancala cēstita*” (very disturbing activities), daring him to go out and steal from others’ houses. He had held the gōvardana mountain even before the wound on his divine stomach \[where yaśōdāp pirātti had tied him with a rope\] had healed. What a syncronisation is this with wound in the stomach, holding the mountain and at the stage of a child!

**tāngu tada varai tān** – it was a huge mountain, sustained by one who was like this.

**munbē …** – In order to teach their younger ones the manner in which one should jump from one branch to another, the monkeys had already taken their littles ones on their backs to the top of the tree. They will then demonstrate the way of jumping from one place to another and teach that to the younger ones.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the leader among the monkeys, who was famous, showed the way to jump from one place to another, for the younger monkeys. Alternatively, this species of monkeys showed the way for all the different species of monkeys.

In the end, he says that through this verse, it is shown as to how our pūrvācāryas adopted their disciples who they were affectionate with, making them to seek the *padatrayam* \[tirumantram, consisting of three words\] which is the essence of all the branches of vēdams. Within this *padatrayam*, they made the disciples to see the distinguished meanings of *mantratrayam* \[the three mantrams which establish the supremacy of śrīman nārāyaṇa, namely *aśtākśaram* \[mantram with eight syllables, praṇavam, nama: and nārāyaṇāya\], *śadakśaram* \[mantram with six syllables, praṇavam, nama: and viṣṇavē\] and *dvādaśākśaram* \[mantram with twelve syllables, praṇavam, nama: and bhagavatē vāsudēvāya\]\], through sacred texts such as *śruti* \[vēdams\], *smriti* \[texts such as manu smriti, yājñavalkya smriti etc, which were composed to explain the *śrutis*\], *itihāsa* etc \[epics , śrī rāmāyaṇa and mahābhārata, which were composed to show examples of the enunciations in vēdas\]. The pūrvācāryas, through the methods of *pravrutti* \[what is to be followed\] and *nivrutti* \[what is to be avoided\], demonstrated to their disciples to enable them to learn without any fault. It is this which is analogous to the activity of the monkeys in teaching their younger ones.

**gōvarttanam ennum koṟṟak kudaiyē** – since the mountain had grass and water with it all the time, it was nurturing cattle, leading to plentiful of cattle. Hence, it was called “*gōvardanam*” \[that which nurtures and multiplies cattle\]. Since it was inverted fully and prevented any drop of water to fall on anyone, when it rained heavily \[due to indra’s anger\], it is referred to as *gōvardanam ennum koṟṟak kudai* \[victorious umbrella called as gōvardanam\].

We shall next consider the 10<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.5.10. Kodiyeru sendamarai

*kodiyēṟu sendāmaraik kai viralgaḷ kōlamum aḻindila vādiṟṟilavadivēṟu tiru ugir nondumila maṇivaṇṇan malaiyum ōr sambiradammudiyēṟiya māmugil pal gaṇangaḷ munneṟṟi naraittana pōla engumkudiyēṟi irundu maḻai poḻiyum gōvarttanam ennum koṟṟak kudaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kodi ēṟu – having the flagstaff as a line on his divine hand \[there are many divine marks on the divine hands of emperumān; this refers to one such divine mark; flagstaff is present in all the temples at the entrance of the respective temple\]; sem tāmarai – like a reddish lotus flower; kai viralgaḷ – divine hands and divine fingers; kōlamum – natural beauty; aḻindila – has not got destroyed; vādiṟṟila – did not droop either; vadivu ēṟu – having considerable beauty; tiru ugir – divine nails; nondum ila – have not got damaged; maṇi vaṇṇan – the entity lifted by kaṇṇan, who has the complexion of bluish gemstone; malaiyum – gōvardana mountain; ōr sambiradam – it appeared like a legerdemain; mudi – on the peak of the mountain; ēṟiya – climbed; mā mugil – huge clouds; pal gaṇangaḷ – many banks; mun neṟṟi – the front portions of their foreheads; naraittana pōl – just as it had greyed; engum – in all places; kudi ēṟi irundu – dwelling; maḻai poḻiyum – it is the victorious mountain, called as gōvardana, where it was raining

**Перевод:**

**The natural beauty of kriṣṇa’s divine hands and the divine fingers on them, which appeared like reddish lotus flowers and which had flagstaff as a line, had not got destroyed. Neither did the beauty get faded. The divine finger nails, which had an abundance of beauty, had not got damaged. The manner in which kriṣṇa, who has the complexion of a bluish gemstone, lifted the gōvardana mountain, appeared like a sleight of hand. How did the gōvardana mountain appear? Many banks of huge clouds had climbed the peak of the mountain, with their foreheads appearing like grey hair, present everywhere and raining.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the second pāsuram of this decad, āḻvār had said “maḻai vandu eḻunāḷ peydu māttadaippa” (rains poured for seven days continuously, cutting off any escape for the herd and herd-folk). He had mercifully described in that pāsuram as to how kriṣṇa had held aloft the mountain such that no harm came in the way of herd or herd-folk. Despite holding it for seven days, finding that there was no pain in kriṣṇa’s divine hand, āḻvār is amazed and he joyously and mercifully sings mangaḷāśāsanam for kriṣṇa, in this pāsuram. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that after kriṣṇa had put the mountain down \[at the end of seven days when indra regretted his action and rains stopped\], āḻvār examined whether there was any agony for kriṣṇa in his divine hands, having held the mountain continuously for seven days, just like tirumaḻisai āḻvār had asked in tiruccanda viruttam 61 “nadanda kālgaḷ nondavō” (Since you walked for a long time \[in śrī rāmāvatāram\], are your divine feet hurting?) Since āḻvār did not find any wound, being a mangaḷāśāsanaparar \[one who carries out mangaḷāśāsanam\], he mercifully composes this pāsuram, with affection.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kodiyēṟu sendāmaraik kai viralgaḷ** – just as it has been said in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5.18.2 “*dvaja vajra abja kruta cinhēna pāṇiṇā*”(divine hands identified with symbols of flagstaff, diamond, lotus), kriṣṇa’s divine hands are identified with symbols of flagstaff, diamond etc, to indicate his wealth. Here, āḻvār has referred only to flagstaff, as a representative of all the rest. This verse refers to kriṣṇa having the flagstaff as a line on his divine hands, which, along with the fingers, look like lotus in terms of the reddish colour, beauty and tenderness.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that as per *sāmudrika lakśaṇa* \[identifications which are to be seen in a person’s form for distinction\], *dvaja* \[flagstaff\], *ankuśa* \[stick used for controlling elephants\], *śankha* \[divine conch\], *tāmarai* \[lotus flower\] are indicated. Since āḻvār had already seen these in kriṣṇa’s divine form \[in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.7.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/09/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-1-7-6/) “*oru kālil sangu oru kālil cakkaram*” (divine identification mark of conch on one foot and divine identification mark of divine disc on the other foot)\], after kriṣṇa had kept the mountain down, āḻvār goes to kriṣṇa, confirms that these marks are present and that they have not changed in any manner. He feels happy, with that. Alternatively, since *kodi* refers to creeper too, here it is taken as representing śrī mahālakśmi; kriṣṇa’s divine hands are like lotus flower, the place of birth of śrī mahālakśmi. *ēṟudal* \[variant of *ēṟu* seen in the verse\] refers to appearance. Alternatively, this would refer to the divine hands on which the creeper had spread and appeared. After seeing the tenderness of the divine hands, the tenderness of lotus flower would appear to be much inferior and to be given up. Since the divine hands and divine fingers appear like these even outwardly, āḻvār says that they have not lost their beauty. *vādiṟṟila* – Since the withering of lotus flower, taken as simile, is not seen in the object (divine hands), āḻvār says that they have not withered.

**kōlamum aḻindila vādiṟṟila** – with kriṣṇa holding the mountain continuously for seven days, the natural beauty \[of his divine hands and fingers\] had not got destroyed; they had not become weakened and had not withered since they had to bear the weight of the mountain for a long time.

**vadivēṟu tiru ugir nondumila** – the divine nails, whose beauty was increasing with time, had not got damaged either.

**maṇivaṇṇan malaiyum ōr sambiradam** – the manner in which kriṣṇa, who has a complexion like a bluish gemstone, lifted the mountain and the way in which he stood lifting it appeared like *indrajālam* – legerdemain. In other words, if he had really lifted and sustained the mountain, vouldn’t it lead to some change or the other in his divine hands? Since there was no change, it appeared that this was a sleight of hand. āḻvār says further that because there was no change in his divine hand, he is calling it as a sleight of hand, and that kriṣṇa lifting the mountain was indeed a fact.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that for those who keep asking for logic and proof for everything, this action \[of lifting the mountain continuously for seven days\] would appear like *sambiradam* – legerdemain. This \[sleight of hand\] happens when, for some people, only the faculty of sight functions, with the other faculties \[of the five senses\] and the inner mind, which controls all the senses, not in syncronisation. *sambiradam* – sleight of hand.

**mudi …** – different types of clouds, which were huge, had ascended the peak of that mountain.

**munneṟṟi naraittana pōla engum kudi ēṟi irundu maḻai poḻiyum** – the clouds will pour rain such that the entire world would have abundance of water; the clouds would appear as if their foreheads have greyed \[with white hair\]. Clouds would appear dark when they contain water. Once they release the water as rains, they will become white. Even when the clouds have emptied out the water and become white, the place where they come to stay is the mountain peak. Hence, the pāsuram says that the clouds would appear to be white in their forehead, while they dwell all over the mountain, surrounding it. Where does this happen? It is on the victorious mountain, called as gōvardana. Hence, this is a real event and not *indrajālam*.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says at the end of his svāpadēśam that there are people, referred to as *āntarāḷikars*, who are in between – they are neither *muktātmās* \[who have got liberated from samsāram and have reached śrī vaikuṇṭam\] nor *samsāris* \[those who inhabit samsāram, enjoying the pleasures seen in samsāram\]. They could be called as *mumukśus* \[those who desire śrī vaikuṇṭam\], have firm faith in emperumān and do not indulge in prohibited activities. They live in *divyadēśams* \[noble lands\]. Clouds, when they give off all the rain contained in them, become white in colour. This signifies that they do not have anything in their hands and look up to emperumān only. gōvardana mountain has allowed these clouds to rest on it. Clouds are like *āntarāḷikars*, without anything in their hands to attain emperumān. Clouds take residence on the mountain, just like the *āntarāḷikars* take residence in divyadēsams. Clouds manifest the magnanimous quality of gōvardana since gōvardana has allowed them to rest on it, having given up everything. This is the simile brought about in this pāsuram. It is the mountain, which receives rains under normal times, that also becomes the victorious umbrella when time becomes inimical.

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.5.11. Aravil pallikondu

*aravil paḷḷi koṇḍu aravam turandittu aravap pagai ūrdiyavanudaiyakuravil kodi mullaigaḷ ninṟu uṟangum gōvarttanam ennum koṟṟak kudai mēltiruvil poli maṟai vāṇar puttūrt tigaḻ battar pirān sonna mālai pattumparavu mana nangu udaip pattar uḷḷār paramāna vaigundam naṇṇuvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aravil – on top of tiruvanantāḻvān \[divine ādiśēśan\]; paḷḷi koṇḍu – reclining (in milky ocean); aravam – the snake, kāḷiyan; turandittu – driving him away; pagai – enemy for the entire clan of snakes; ūrdi avanudaiya – one who has \[garuda\] as his vehicle; kuravil – a type of tree; kodi – encircling that tree as a creeper; mullaigaḷ – jasmine flowers \[on the creeper\]; ninṟu – firmly; uṟangum – appearing as if taking rest; gōvarttanam ennum – having the divine name of gōvardana; koṟṟam – being victorious, as it stopped the rains; kudai mēl – regarding that mountain, which was like an umbrella; tiruvin – due to the wealth of their servitude; poli – shining; maṟai – for vēdam; vāṇar – those who live, having the capability to write treatise on vēdam, similar to vyāsa; puttūr – in śrī villibuttūr; tigaḻ – one who is splendorous; battar pirān – periyāḻvār; sonna – mercifully composed; mālai – garland of words; pattum – these ten pāsurams; paravum – to recite; manam – heart; nangu – very well; udai – having; pattar uḷḷār – those who are full of devotion; paramāna – that, which is the most distinguished; vaigundam – śrī vaikuṇṭam; naṇṇuvar – will get to attain

**Перевод:**

**emperumān reclines on ādiśēśan, in milky ocean. He left that and incarnated in tiruvāyppādi, where he drove away the snake, kāḷiyan. He has garuda, which is an enemy for the entire clan of snakes, as his vehicle. In this gōvardana mountain stands a kurava tree \[a type of tree\], with a creeper encircling that tree, with jasmine flowers on that creeper appearing to sleep firmly. About this mountain, which was victorious due to stopping rains from falling on herd and herd-folk, periyāḻvār has mercifully composed ten pāsurams, which are like garlands of words. periyāḻvār resides splendorously in śrī villibuttūr, where those, who have shining servitude towards emperumān, and who are capable of writing explanatory comments on vēdams, live. Those who have the hearts to recite these pāsurams very well, and who have devotion towards emperumān, will attain śrī vaikuṇṭam, which is the most distinguished.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In this last pāsuram of the decad, āḻvār mentions the benefit which will accrue to those who learn it and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**aravil paḷḷi koṇḍu** – reclining in tiruppāṟkadal \[divine milky ocean\] atop anantāḻvān, who has the nature of tenderness, coolness and fragrance.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that it is in the divine milky ocean, which is gently stirred by the breathing of tiruvanantāḻvān \[ādiśēśan\] which is like a hammock, that emperumān reclines.

**aravam turandittu** – just as it has been mentioned in harivamśam “*nāga paryankam utsrujya hyāgatō madurām purīm*” (emperumān left the mattress of ādiśēśan and came to incarnate in the divine abode of śrī maturā), emperumān incarnated in tiruvāyppādi \[śrī gōkulam\]. In that abode, kāḷiyan, a poisonous snake, had taken residence in a pond, which was used by the cows as well as the cow-herd people, as their source of drinking water. kriṣṇa drove away that snake, kāḷiyan, from that pond.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār recalls the time that kriṣṇa incarnated and grew up in tiruvāyppādi, when he drove away the kāḷiyan, a poisonous snake, which had poisoned the pond there, just as it has been mentioned in [tiruccanda viruttam 89](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/02/thiruchchandha-viruththam-89/) “*salam kalanda poigai*” (it was a poisonous pond in which water had been added), a pond which was the source of water for the herds of cattle grazed by the herd-folk, in line with the duties of their clan.

**aravap pagai ūrdi udaiya avan** – emperumān has garuda, which is the enemy of the clan of snakes, as his vehicle.

**kuravil …** – having the divine name of gōvardana, the mountain had on it, the tree called as *kuravu*, around which jasmine creepers had spread, with jasmine flowers in them sleeping. Regarding that mountain gōvardana, which was held as a victorious umbrella, to prevent rains from harming. If the text had been *kuravakkodi mullaigaḷ* – the meaning would change as: both the tree *kuravu* and the flowers on the creeper surrounding that tree, were standing and sleeping.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that it is natural for trees to wither away when there is no rain and to prosper abundantly, when it rains. It is due to lack of rains that the herd-folk in tiruvāyppādi were carrying out worship of *dēvatāntarams* \[divine entities other than emperumān\]. Thus, it was normal for the trees to nurture and to wither. It is due to this that the pāsuram says that the flowers on the creeper around the tree would blossom as well as wither and sleep. Even the term *aravappagai* \[inimical to snakes\] is associated with this world \[samsāram; the underlying fact is that in śrī vaikuṇṭam there is no enmity between snake and garuda\].

**tiruvil poli …**– śrī villibuttūr is an abode inhabited by those who were abundant with *śrī vaiśnava śrī* \[servitude towards emperumān and his followers\] and who are capable of writing treatise for vēdam, like sage vyāsa. periyāḻvār, who is the controller of such śrī villibuttūr, had strung a garland with words as flowers, into ten pāsurams.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār is the controller of śrī villibuttūr inhabited by those who shine with the *rahasya vēda śāstrams* \[esoteric texts in vēdams\] which explain that the ultimate benefit of attaining emperumān is to carry out mangaḷāśāsanam. s*onna mālai pattum* – the garland of words in tamiḻ language, mercifully composed by āḻvār. In other words, those who reside in śrī villibuttūr have the devotion which leads to mangaḷāśāsanam, who have the noble hearts to conduct themselves in the manner in which emperumān has mercifully spoken of in śāstrams such as śrī gītai etc \[where he had ordained that we should attain only him\] the moment they hear those and that reciting these ten pāsurams which mercifully say that emperumān would himself remove any harm wreaked by *dēvatāntarams* when those who worship them, stop their worship, is the *puruśārtam* \[ultimate benefit\].

**paravu mana nangudaip pattar uḷḷār** – those who are devoted towards emperumān and who have good hearts with which they speak, being full of affection towards emperumān.

**paramāna vaigundam naṇṇuvarē** – through the faculties of their knowledge and affection, they will engage in service experiencing emperumān and will get to attain the most eminent abode of śrī vaikuṇṭam, cohabiting with assemblies of followers of emperumān.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai gives here the sequence of events which happen in samsāram: (1) while remaining in samsāram, a person worships other dēvatās and carries out servitude to them (2) On acquiring knowledge about emperumān, the person starts rejecting these other dēvatās (3) Those other dēvatās, being impelled by their *karmabhāvanai* \[mode of engaging with deeds, as opposed to *brahmabhāvanai*, which is the mode of engaging with emperumān\] look for means to harm the person who engage with emperumān (4) emperumān comes to their rescue through his activities which are beyond the realm of human beings. Instead of remaining here, wallowing in sorrow, those, who recite these ten pāsurams, will attain the abode \[śrī vaikuṇṭam\] where his supremacy shines without any shortcoming, bowing to his divine feet, and will get to climb on to his divine lap. Through dialogue such as “*kōsi*” \[emperumān asking of the jīvātmā “Who are you?”\] etc, and with emperumān’s permission, the person will unite with those who surround emperumān constantly, carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam to him.

We shall next consider the pravēsam of the next tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.6.1. Navalam periya

*nāvalam periya teevinil vāḻum nangaimeergaḷ! idu ōr aṟpudam kēḷeertūvalamburi udaiya tirumāl tūya vāyil kuḻal ōsai vaḻiyēkōvalar siṟumiyar iḷam kongai kudugalippa udal uḷ aviḻndu engumkāvalaum kadandu kayiṟu mālai āgi vandu kaviḻndu ninṟanarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

periya – being huge; nāvalam teevinil – in jambhudvīpam (in the word nāvalam, the syllable ‘am’ does not have a meaning; it is present for poetic metric); vāḻum – living; nangaimeergaḷ! – oh, those who are without any shortcoming in anything!; idu ōr – this unique; aṟpudam – amazement; kēḷeer – do listen; tū – pure; valamburi udaiya – having śrī pāncajanyam \[divine conch\] on his divine hand; tirumāl – one who is the consort of śrī mahālakśmi; tūya – enjoyable; vāyil – playing, keeping on his divine mouth; kuḻal – flute’s; ōsai vaḻiyē – through the path of music; kōvalar – herd-people’s; siṟumiyar – young girls; iḷa – being mature; kongai – bosoms; kudugalippa – as they make merry, saying that they are going ahead in the front; udal – form; uḷ – heart; aviḻndu – losing control; engum – present everywhere; kāvalum – protection; kadandu – going past; kayiṟu mālai āgi vandu – just like garlands strung together in a rope, coming in huge numbers; kaviḻndu ninṟanar – stood, bowing their heads down (due to shyness of seeing kriṣṇa

**Перевод:**

**Oh, those who are living in the huge jambhūdvīpam, without any shortcoming in anything! Listen, to this amazing incident. One, who is the consort of śrī mahālakśmi, who is having the pure śrī pāncajanyam on his divine hand, is playing the flute, keeping it on his enjoyable divine lips. Through the path of that music, young girls from the clan of herd-folk, in large numbers, with their mature bosoms joyously going ahead, with their forms and hearts losing control, have crossed the protective barriers kept everywhere, and are coming, like garlands arranged properly on a rope, bowing their heads down.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**nāvalam periya teevinil** – in the huge land mass, called as a division, where *nāval* (blue-berry) is present. This distinguishes this division, called as *jambudvīpam*, from the others. The eminence of this division is not seen in the other divisions. The other divisions are for the purpose of experiencing the fruits of karmas \[deeds\] carried out while it is only in this division that one could earn, through one’s deeds \[virtues or vices or attain emperumān through himself\]. Even in this division, it is on the ninth continent, called as *bhārata varśam*, that one could earn deeds. All the other continents and other divisions are present only for experiencing the results of the deeds carried out here. For this reason, it is not inappropriate to call this division as being more eminent than the rest, since this alone contains *bhārata varśam*. It is only here that one could carry out *karmas*, the results of which could be experienced in the other divisions, as well as in the upper and lower worlds. For attaining mōkśam too \[śrī vaikuṇṭam\], it is only here that one could carry out deed \[surrendering to emperumān through an ācārya\]. Also, it is only in this division that divine abodes of emperumān \[*divyadēśams*\] as well as *mumukśus* \[those who are desirous of attaining mōkśam\] are present in large numbers. Due to all these reasons, āḻvār terms this division \[jambudvīpam\], which has *bhārata varśam* within it, as *periya tīvu* \[huge division\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that among the divisions of the universe, it is due to the ninth continent, *bhārata varśam,* present in the southern end of the *jambudvīpam*, that the *dvīpam* is referred to as huge land mass. It is due to this *bhārata varśam* that the other eight continents too got their eminence. It is here that *sākśātparars* \[those who had directly seen emperumān\], viz, āḻvārs, and *mumukśus* \[those who desire to attain mōkśam, śrī vaikuṇṭam\] are present. Also, the divine abodes, where emperumān’s distinguished divine forms could be seen, are present only here. *mumukśus*, who get liberated from here and reach śrī vaikuṇṭam, are cherished by nityamuktars \[nityasūris, the permanent dwellers of śrī vaikuṇṭam, and muktātmās, who had already reached śrī vaikuṇṭam\] as well as by emperumān himself. Hence, this is called as *periya dvīpam* \[huge land-mass\]. Being identified by blueberries, it is called as *jambudvīpam*, and is considered as a huge land-mass.

**vāḻum nangai meergaḷ** – \[the term *nangai* refers to a lady who is complete in all aspects; the term *vāḻvu* refers to flourishing\] Since these women have been born in the place where kriṣṇa has incarnated and have been witnessing the divine activities of his incarnation as well his auspicious qualities, these women are said to be flourishing. They are complete with respect to the knowledge required for understanding his divine activities as well as with respect to affection towards him. Since āḻvār considers himself to be one among the herd-folk, he is calling some of the women, present in tiruvāyppādi and is telling them mercifully. Alternatively, in line with the saying “*sa Eva vāsudēvō’sau sākśāt puruśa ucayatē* l *strīprāyam itarat sarvam*” (It is only that supreme entity, vāsudēvan \[emperumān\], who is considered as a masculine entity. All the others are considered as feminine entities only), considering everyone other than emperumān as feminine entities, devoid of any trace of independence, it could be assumed that āḻvār is calling out to those who are distinguished on account of their involvement with matters regarding emperumān as *nangaimīr*.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as it has been mentioned in [tiruppallāṇḍu 3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-3-vazhatpattu/) “*vāḻ ātpattu ninṟīr*” (if you are a servitor of emperumān), *vāḻvu*, which refers to living in a fit manner, is one where pursuing one objective leads the person to another objective \[carrying out one service to emperumān will lead the person to carrying out another service to emperumān or his followers etc\]. It is this which is the reason for the completeness of their qualities too.

**idōr aṟpudam kēḷeer** – Listen to this amazing incident.

**tū valamburi udaiya  tirumāl** – the divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi, having the sacred divine conch, curling to the right side. This implies that he has the necessary instrument to annihilate those who are unfavourable to him and to unite with him those who are favourable towards him. What is sacredness for śrī pāncajanyam? It is the purity of carrying out the task, thought of by emperumān. Through the sound of blowing, śrī pāncajanyam would be able to make the favourable entities to sustain themselves and the unfavourable ones to meet their end.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that sacredness of the divine conch lies in its having purity of qualities of form and purity of qualities of ātmā. The divine conch is pure white in complexion, reflecting purity of qualities of form. Since conch remains exclusively for emperumān and not for self, this reflects purity of the qualities of ātmā. Just as it has been mentioned in [2.10 decad of tiruvāimoḻi](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-1-kilaroli-ilamai/), the divine conch tells all “Leaving aside qualities of your intelligence, youthfulness, obedient attitude, hesitation, proudness etc, come and sing praises of this divyadēśam, tirumālirunjōlai”. It helps the favourable ones by signalling to them the arrival of emperumān \[as in the case of rukmiṇip pirātti, when she had requested kriṣṇa to come and marry her\] and it annihilates the unfavourable ones by blowing resoundingly in the battlefield \[just as it did in the kurukśētra battlefield to break the hearts of the hundred sons of king dritarāśtra\].

**tūya vāyil kuḻal ōsai vaḻiyē** – the sacredness of his divine mouth is that through the words spoken of by emperumān, it has the ability to sustain the favourable entities. Through the divine sound of the divine flute kept on such a divine mouth… In other words, in tiruvāyppādi where people warn of kriṣṇa’s presence through the words “Look, kriṣṇa is here; look after the girls”, with relatives erecting several layers of protection and keeping the girls safely, the sound emanating from kriṣṇa’s flute will put them to sleep, enter the ears of the girls, telling them “Come, now” and will lead them to kriṣṇa. It is due to the pull of that sound that the girls came to the place where kriṣṇa was playing the flute.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that sacredness of emperumān’s divine mouth is that through the flute it would attract everyone and convey the message that emperumān does not reject anyone and that he is firm in this. It is not that he had only said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 18.30 “*rāmō dvirna abhibhāśatē*” \[śrī rāma will not speak a second word. The reference here is to śrī rāmāyaṇa ślōkam where it is said that śrī rāma does not speak a second word. However, he had also said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.3 “*na tyajēyam katancana*” \[he will not let down his devotees\].

**kōvalar siṟumiyar** – the girls from the clan of people who are well versed in protecting cows.

**iḷam kongai kudugalippa** – the well grown bosoms, which were not under the control of the girls, went ahead of the girls, saying joyously “We are going ahead”. *iḷam kongai* – they do not listen to the girls. *kudugalittal* refers to rising up on account of the urge to reach kriṣṇa.

**udal uḷ aviḻndu** – it was not only the joy of the bosoms, even the substrate, their forms, on which the bosoms are located and the mind, controller of all the senses, lost control.

**engum kāvalum kadandu** – going past all the protective hurdles. In other words, the mothers have kept the girls inside, hugging them. The doors had been bolted from outside and relatives were standing guard outside the doors. Going past such protective layers, considering them as mere clod….

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the girls did not feel any shame in going past their fathers, mothers, brothers et al, when breaking their protective guard in order to reach kriṣṇa. They did not listen to their friends too who tried to control them from going.

**kayiṟu mālaiyāgi vandu** – the girls came together in large numbers, just like garlands which have been placed together in a rope properly.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just like the garlands in a rope will not slip, these girls let go of their friendliness, affection etc towards worldly people \[their relatives\] and were focussed on the music from the flute which made them to sever their links with worldly people. He says that kriṣṇa could attract people from a particular distance only whereas his music, from the flute, will attract people from much longer distances too.

**kaviḻndu ninṟanarē** – They stood, surrounding him. Alternatively, coming through the path of music from the flute, they came to the place where he was playing the flute, and out of shyness to see his face, they bowed down their heads; unable to look him on his face, they bowed down their heads.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that since they were young girls, coming out for the first time now, tracing the origin of the music, they saw kriṣṇa, felt shy throughout their forms and bowed their heads down. Alternatively, unable to look at kriṣṇa on his face, they bowed down their heads. In the end, he says that this incident reflects the instruction of *saptākśaram* (seven syllables) given by ācāryan. In tirumantram, which consists of eight syllables, if the first syllable \[praṇavam\] were to be removed, the resultant will be seven syllables. Flute, through which kriṣṇa played music to attract the herd-girls, has seven holes \[corresponding to *sapta svarams*, the seven notes\]. The second term of tirumantram, having two syllables \[*nama*:\], signifies *ananya pāratantryam* \[total dependence on emperumān\]. The last term of tirumantram, having five syllables \[*nārāyaṇāya*\], signifies *ananya bhōjñatvam* \[enjoying only the auspicious qualities of emperumān\]. Thus, these two terms, accounting for seven syllables \[corresponding to the seven holes in the flute\] signify total dependence on emperumān and enjoying only emperumān. What is the nature of the śiśyas who receive these instructions from ācāryan? \[Here, the herd-girls are the śiśyas, receiving musical notes from the flute\]. They will accept the words of ācārya fully and will not argue or look at logic etc. They are full of knowledge, devotion and detachment. Devotion is signified by their bosoms, which run ahead of them to receive the instructions. Detachment is signified by their loss of control over their form and mind. In other words, they have detached themselves from worldly matters and are focussed only on receiving the instruction from their ācārya.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.6.2. Idavanarai idattolodu

*idavaṇarai idat tōḷodu sāyttu iru kai kūdap puruvam nerindēṟakkuda vayiṟū pada vāy kadai kūdak kōvindan kuḻal kodu ūdina pōdumada mayilgaḷodu mān piṇai pōlē mangaimārgaḷ malarkkūndal aviḻaudai negiḻa ōr kaiyāl tugil paṟṟi olgi ōda arikkaṇ ōda ninṟanarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

gōvindan – kaṇṇan, who got to graze cows; ida aṇarai – region near moustace, on the left side; idat tōḷodu sāyttu – leaning towards the left divine shoulder; iru kai – both divine hands; kūda – to join with the flute; puruvam – divine eyebrows; nerindu ēṟa – to arch up; vayiṟu – divine stomach; kudam pada – to appear like a pot; vāy – divine lips; kadai kūda – at both ends, to close towards the hole in the flute; kuḻal kodu – with the bamboo flute; ūdina pōdu – when he blew; madam – having obedience; mayilgaḷodu mān piṇai pōla – like peacocks and does \[female deer\]; mangaimārgaḷ – women, who were young; malar – decorated with flowers; kūndal – locks; aviḻa – to loosen and sway; udai – dress; negiḻa – as it loosened; ōr kaiyāl – with one hand; tugil – the loosened dress; paṟṟī – holding on; ari ōdu – with red and black lines running; kaṇ – eyes; ōda – glancing towards kriṣṇa; ninṟanar – they stood, perplexed

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa tilted the left side of his face towards his divine left shoulder. Both his divine hands closed in, on the holes in the bamboo flute. His divine eyebrows arched up. His divine stomach, due to repeated sucking in of air \[for playing the flute\] and exhaling it, appeared like a pot. When he kept his divine mouth, with both sides of the lips close to the hole in the bamboo flute and played on the flute, young herd girls, who appeared like peacocks and does \[female deer\], came with their locks which were decorated with flowers, loosening and swaying. Their dress on the waist too got loosened \[due to coming in a hurry towards kriṣṇa\]. They held on to the loosened dress with one hand. With shyness taking over them, they stood perplexed with their eyes, having reddish and blackish lines running across, glancing towards kriṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**idavaṇarai idattōlodu sāyttu** – On the left side, tilting the location where moustace would grow, towards the divine left shoulder.

**iru kai kūda** – joining the two hands with the divine flute

**puruvam neṟindēṟa** – the divine eyebrows arching up

**kuda vayiṟu pada** – since kriṣṇa had to take in lot of air and release it slowly while playing on the flute, the divine stomach appeared like a pot

**vāy kadai kūda** – the corners of the divine mouth closed towards the hole in the divine flute

**gōvindan kuḻal kodu ūdina pōdu** – kriṣṇa is referred to as *gōvindan* since he was deeply involved in the protection of cattle, by modifying the tunes which he played with the flute in an eminent manner, to ensure that they do not go straying from the herd, they go for grazing at the proper time and they rejoin the herd in time for returning home. Since even a novice could play on the flute, creating tunes capable of attracting others, the verse says *kuḻal kodu ūdina pōdu*, instead of saying *kuḻal ūdina pōdu* \[the difference lies in emphasising that it was with the eminent flute that he played\]. This brings out at the same time the eminence of the person \[kriṣṇa\] who played on the flute and the distinction of the flute.

**mada mayilgaḷodu mān piṇai pōlē** – like peacocks which were obedient and like the doe, which was having a bewildering look. Just as the verse refers to the peacocks in the plural number, the deer too should be considered as plural number, though the verse does not specifically mention that.

**mangaimārgaḷ** – women, who were young.

**malark kūndal aviḻa** – with the locks, which have been decorated with flowers etc, loosening

**udai negiḻa** – the decorated dress too was loosening. They come hurriedly, with their locks and their dresses diśevelled, following the music from kriṣṇa’s flute.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that with their locks diśevelled and their dresses loosening, the girls, who were running towards the source of the music from flute, suddenly remembered their femininity and stood aside, in shyness.

**ōr kaiyāl tugil paṟṟi** – they held on to the dresses which had got loosened, when they came hurriedly.

**olgi** – since they remembered their characteristic of femininity, they stood aside, with shyness.

**ōdarikkaṇōda ninṟanarē** – even though they remembered their characteristic of femininity, could they stop their eyes, which were running towards kriṣṇa? They stood, with their eyes, which had blackish and reddish lines, going towards kriṣṇa. The term *mada mayil* is a simile for *malark kūndal aviḻa* \[just as the peacock loosens its feathers, the girls’ locks got loosened\]. Similarly, the term *mān piṇai* is a simile for *ōdarikkaṇōda* \[the eyes with reddish and blackish lines looked like the eyes of the deer\].

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.6.3. Van ilavarasu

*vān iḷavarasu vaigundakkuttan vāsudēvan madurai mannan nandakōn iḷavarasu kōvalar kuttan gōvindan kuḻal kodu ūdinapōduvān iḷam padiyar vandu vandu īṇḍi manam urugi malarkkanṇgaḷ panippatēn aḷavu seṟi kūndal aviḻac cenni vērppac cevi sērndu ninṟanarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vān – for paramapadam \[śrī vaikuṇṭam\]; iḷavarasu – as the prince; vaigundam kuttan – as a small child who has to be looked after constantly by those who are in that divine place \[it is also said that vaigundak kuttan refers to a small child who has the divine name of vaikuṇḍan); vāsudēvan – as the divine son of vasudēvar; madurai – for maturā, in the north; mannan – as the controller; nandar kōn – for nandagōpar (as the son); iḷa arasu – as the prince; kōvalar kuttan – as the entity who has to be looked by after herd-folk; gōvindan – when kaṇṇan, who got to graze cows, played on the flute; vān – inhabiting celestial world; iḷa – apt for enjoyment; padiyar – women, with forms; vandu vandu īṇḍi – gathering, coming again and again (impelled by the music from flute); manam – minds; urugi – melting like a liquid; malar – like flowers; kaṇgaḷ – eyes; panippa – to be cool with tears of joy; tēn aḷavu – with honey; seṟi – being in abundance; kūndal – locks; aviḻa – to loosen and to sway; senni – forehead; vērppa – to perspire; sevi – with ears; sērttu – hearing the music from the flute; ninṟanar – stood

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa is the prince of śrī vaikuṇṭam. He is like a little child, to be properly taken care of by those who inhabit that divine abode. He is the divine son of vasudēvar. He is the controller of maturā. He is the prince of nandagōpar, who has to be looked after by the herd-folk. When such kriṣṇa played on the flute, young women, who were inhabiting celestial worlds and who had forms apt for enjoyment, came in large numbers, with their minds melting like a liquid, with their eyes, which were like flowers, becoming cool due to tears of joy, with their dense locks, filled with honey, loosening and swaying. They stood, hearing his music, with their ears tuned to the music.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vān iḷavarasu** – One, who is the prince in paramapadam. He is like a young king who is nurtured by aging ministers. He has made the nityasūris as the prominent entities in paramapadam, as mentioned in [tiruviruttam 2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/11/thiruviruththam-2/) “*mūduvarām – viṇṇāttavar*” (making himself under nityasūris, who dwell in paramapadam, ahead of all the others, chronologically), and remaining as their lord. parāśara bhattar would often say “This entity \[emperumān\] sustains himself on the lap of tiruvanantāḻvān \[ādiśēśan\], under the cane of śrī sēnāpatiyāḻvān \[viśvaksēnar\] and under the wings of periya tiruvadi \[garuda\]”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that he is referred to as *vāṇiḷavarasu*, since the ancient entities in paramapadam had made him as the prince and were vorśipping him. He is referred to as *vaigundak kuttan*, since they consider him as a little child, all the time, carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam for him constantly, and he, in turn, is obedient towards them.

**vaigundak kuttan** – considering him as being protected by those in śrī vaikuṇṭam. He is of such an age \[*yuvākumāra*:, about 16 years of age\] that he has to be taken care of constantly, fearing about his safety in a place where one need not have any fear.

**vāsudēvan** – the divine son of śrī vasudēvar.

**madurai mannan** – One who is the king of śrī maturā. In paramapadam, since there is none who feels independent, āḻvār had referred to him as prince, in order to describe his *āśrita pāratantryam* \[being subservient to his followers\]. However, here \[in samsāram\], since everyone considers himself / herself to be independent, āḻvār refers to him as the king, in order to avoid having two kings in the same place.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that since he killed the king of maturā \[kamsan\], āḻvār refers to him as *madurai mannan*. Though kriṣṇa had coronated ugrasēnar \[father of kamsan\] as the king of maturā \[after kamsan’s death\], he was indeed the king of maturā.

**nandarkōn iḷavarasu** – This term refers to his even higher degree of simplicity than *vāsudēvan* \[from being the lord of nityasūris, he manifested his auspicious quality of simplicity by incarnating as the son of śrī vasudēvar\]. In the case of *vāsudēvan*, he was in a regal clan. However, here \[in tiruvāyppādi\],  it is the clan of herd-folk. He is the prince, being the divine son of śrī nandagōpar, who is the king of tiruvāyppādi, having five lakh families of herd-people.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that since nandagōpar is the king of five lakh families, and as mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 2.2.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/08/periya-thirumozhi-2-2-4/) “*nandan maindan āgu nambi*” (placing himself as the divine son of nandagōpar, with all the auspicious qualities), in [tiruppāvai 1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2014/12/thiruppavai-01-margazhi-thingal/) “*nandagōpan kumaran*” (as the dear son of nandagōpar) and in [perumāḷ tirumoḻi 7.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/08/perumal-thirumozhi-7-3/) “*nandan peṟṟanan nangaḷ kōn peṟṟilan*” (nandagōpan was fortunate to enjoy your divine activities whereas our lord, vasudēvar was not fortunate), kriṣṇa was the protector of herds and herd-folk. If any harm comes their way or if a thorn pierces their leg, it is kriṣṇa who would feel hurt. Hence, he remains as their prince, protecting them. kriṣṇa became complete with his auspicious qualities only after becoming the son of nandagōpar.

**kōvalar kuttan** – This term distinguishes him from *vaigundak kuttan*, mentioned earlier. He is at the age where he has to be taken care of, by the herd-folk.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that he is an equal to a thousand herd-boys who were like him. He was protected by them. They would even engage in a battle, if it comes to that, in order to protect him.

**gōvindan** – He was looking after the cattle, which is appropriate for his clan, as his occupation.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that he is gōvindan without any shortcoming \[*kuṟai onṟūm illāda gōvindā*, as mentioned in [tiruppāvai 28](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/01/thiruppavai-28-karavaigal-pin-chenru/)\].

**kuḻal kodu ūdina pōdu** – when kriṣṇa played on the flute, which attracts everyone.

**vān iḷam padiyar** – women, who inhabit the celestial worlds, not having the stages of aging and death until those worlds exist, as well as having forms which are apt for enjoying. *padi*– form \[body\].

**vandu vandu īṇḍi** – coming in large numbers, following the path of music from the flute.

**manam urugi** – With their minds melting, like liquid.

**malarkkaṇgaḷ panippa** – tears of joy flowing from their eyes, which are like flowers.

**tēnaḷavu seṟi kūndal aviḻa** – even if the flowers, which they had donned on their locks, had fallen down due to the speed with which came \[to the place where kriṣṇa was playing on his flute\], the trace of honey would still be present on the locks which the flowers had decorated, Thus, the dense locks, which were with honey, had loosened \[due to their speed\]

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when the flowers fell down when the celestial women came hurriedly to see kriṣṇa, they did not even realise that the flowers had fallen down. Only if they know that the flower has fallen would they pick it up and keep it back on their locks.

**senni vērppa** – With their foreheads perspiring. Will celestial ladies perspire? We could consider this as the transformation in the basic nature created by the music from flute on entities who / which were listening to the music.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that it was not clear whether they were perspiring or the drops of honey from their locks were dripping on their foreheads.

**sevi sērttu ninṟanarē** – They stood, with their ears tuned to the music.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that their ears will not go elsewhere. Each of the celestial ladies was saying “He was playing the flute, only for me”, filling their ears with the music, considering that as *puruśārtam* \[ultimate benefit\].

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.6.4. Denugan pilamban

*dēnugan pilamban kāḷiyan ennum tīppap pūdugaḷ adanga uḻakkikkānagam padi ulāvi ulāvik karum siṟukkan kuḻal ūdina pōdumēnagaiyōdu tilōttamai arambai uruppasiyar avar veḷgi mayangivānagam padiyil vāy tiṟappinṟi ādal pādal avai māṟinar tāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

dēnugan – monster, dēnukan; pilamban – monster, pralamban; kāḷiyan – snake, kāḷiyan; ennum – known by these identities; tīmba – cruel; pūdugaḷ adanga – all the bad elements \[the term pūdu stands for pūṇḍu, a type of shrub; uḻakki – annihilating them; kānagam – in the forest; padi – in a natural manner; ulāvi ulāvi – wandering around for a long time (out of his volition); karu – having a dark, divine form; siṟukkan – when kaṇṇan, the young person, played on the flute; mēnagaiyodu – along with mēnakā; tilōttamai arambai uruppasi – all these; aravar – apsaras, celestial women; veḷgi – feeling ashamed; mayangi – feeling fascinated (due to engaging with the music, played by him, on the flute); vānagam – in the celestial world; padiyil – and on earth too; vāy tiṟappu inṟi – without opening their mouths; tāmē – on their own (without being implored by anyone else); ādal pādal avai māṟinar – they avoided singing and dancing

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa, annihilating cruel elements such as the monsters dēnukan, pralamban, the snake kāḷiyan et al, was roaming around in the forest, as his nature. When he, who has a dark, divine form, played on his flute, celestial ladies such as mēnakā, tilōttamā, rambā and uṟvasi, felt ashamed \[that they too were singing, and he was playing such a divine music on his flute\]. Fascinated with his music, both in their celestial world and on earth, without uttering a word, without being implored by anyone, on their own, they stopped singing and dancing.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**dēnugan …** – The monster, dēnukan, came in the form of a donkey, inside the forest, with the intention of harming kriṣṇa; while kriṣṇa, balarāma and their friends were playing, the monster, pralamba, came in the form of one of the herd-boys and played with balarāma, with the intention of harming him \[he felt that balarāma was a huge protective entity for kriṣṇa and that by eliminating balarāma, he could then turn his attention of kriṣṇa and harm him too\]; kāliyan, the snake, made the water, used by the herds as well as herd-folk for their water needs, unfit for use by spitting poison in it. kriṣṇa annihilated the first two and drove away the third. The term *tīpapppūdu* refers to their nature of harming others. While each of them is individually strong, to term them collectively as “*pūdugaḷ*” \[a type of shrub\], in a lowly manner, is to indicate that compared to the strength of the one who annihilated/drove them, these are mere worms. This is the reason that āḻvār did not say *aḻittu* \[to destroy\] but as *uḻakki* \[to trample or to smash\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that kriṣṇa tried to bring the monsters under his control through his music. Since they did not get attracted to it and come under his control, he had to destroy them. Just like *kānjori* \[a type of plant, which, when contacted, will make sores on the skin, compelling the person to keep scratching\], *eripuḻu* \[a type of caterpillar, which also will lead to similar situation\], *sarpa* \[poisonous snakes, which will carry poison even when they get hatched and come out for the first time\], these monsters had the nature of harming others right from the time of their birth. Hence, they are termed as *viśappūdu* \[poisonous entities\]. *tīppappūdu* – in carrying out misciefs, they are fully focussed with all their three faculties of mind, words and deed.

**kānagam padi ulāvi ulāvi** – there were no experts inside the forest who could discern the manner in which one would walk and appreciate it. Thus, instead of having the objective of “Let me show the superior manner of my gait”, kriṣṇa roamed around the forest, out of his volition, and walked, in his natural manner. Even then, when he walked it appeared as if an expert was dancing.

**karum siṟukkan kuḻal ūdina pōdu** – kriṣṇa had a divine dark form, which was attractive and pleasant for the beholders \[explanation for the term *karum*\]. He was at a stage of youthfulness, which too was attractive \[explanation for the term *siṟūkkan*\]. When he was walking like this and played on his flute …

**mēnagai …** – Celestial *apsaras* \[eminent ladies\] such as mēnakā, tilōttamā, rambā and ūrvasi were famous as “There is none beyond these women who could dance or sing as well as these”. After experiencing the beauty of his gait and his music, they felt ashamed thinking “We think that we too dance and sing” \[and it is nothing compared to what kriṣṇa is doing\], and swooned, as the shame overtook them.

**vānagam …** – Determining “We shall henceforth not mention about dancing or singing, either in the upper worlds or on earth”, they avoided dancing and singing. The reason for avoiding this not on account of any neutral person, knowing the nuances of dancing and singing, telling them “Hereafter, you people need not dance or sing”.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *avai* \[as in *ādal pādal avai māṟinar*\] shows their expertise in these forms of art \[dancing and singing\]. They avoided even going to congregations where these are discussed and celebrated.

**tāmē** – On their own, they avoided dancing and singing.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here, the following: The celestial ladies did not give up dancing and singing because people, who were neutral and who knew the difference between kriṣṇa’s dancing / singing and these ladies’ dancing / singing told them “You have been attracting those who had given up attachments towards worldly pursuits \[such as sage viśvāmitra et al\] through your dancing and singing. Also, people in the celestial worlds were praising you all along on your accomplishments and you had taken those complements as recognition of your talent. Now, stop your dancing and singing”. They had given up their dancing and singing, on their own, out of their sense of shame. Those who know about *darmam* \[righteousness\] will consider the repository of such *darmam*, who is the *darmi* as *darmam* itself \[emperumān is the repository of all the *darmam*. Thus, he is referred to as *darmi*. However, such emperumān himself is referred to as *darmam* as in the saying in mahābhārata *kriṣṇam darmam sanātanam* \[know kriṣṇa as the *darmam*, traditionally\]. Now, kriṣṇa had said in [bhagavat gītā 18.66](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66/) “*sarva darmān parityajya*” \[give up all the darmams which you are following …\]. Even if *darmam* \[*darmi*\] himself says “Follow the other darmams which I had told you earlier to give up. If you do not follow those darmams, it will lead to accumulation of sins for you”, those who have given up everything and have attained emperumān alone as their refuge, will not go back to those other darmams. In the same way, if neutral people tell these celestial ladies to continue to dance and sing, they will not do so. There \[in bhagavat gītā 18,66\], it was after emperumān said to avoid other darmams, that those who surrendered to emperumān gave up those other darmams. For those who had received from emperumān knowledge, based on devotion, through his mercy, instead of saying “*tyaja; vraja; mā suca*:” \[terms from bhagavat gītā 18.66 where kriṣṇa had told arjuna to give up all darmams, take refuge only under him and not to grieve\], even if he had told them “Carry out those *darmams*” they would have said, as in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/08/thiruvaimozhi-5-7-1-norra-nonbilen/) “*nōṟṟa nōnbilēn*” (I have not performed karma yōgam to attain you), as in [tirumālai 25](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thirumalai-25/) “*oḷittittēn*” (I do not have the quality of carrying out karma yōgam, to attain you) and as in [stōtra ratnam 22](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/sthothra-rathnam-22/) “*na dharma niśtōsmi*” (I am not involved in practicing karma yōgam). It could be said that these celestial ladies are like those entities in this one aspect of changing themselves fully, after seeing him.

Even if emperumān, in order to carry out the proper manner of carrying out these activities \[dancing and singing\] for the sake of the worlds, had told them, through neutral persons, to engage with dancing and singing, they are capable of telling him “You could carry out these through those who you wish; we have forgotten even the names of those activities”. How did these women, who had avoided such activities, re-engage with them? This happens when their *karma bhāvanai* \[pathos of carrying out deeds\] rears its head. This is required for the sake of the world. When *brahma bhāvanai* \[pathos of engaging with the supreme entity, emperumān\] rears its head, they will say “*dāsōham*” \[we are your servitors\], melting in their hearts. However, when *karma bhāvanai* rears its head, the same people will say “*sōham*” (I am īśvaran), with total independence.

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.6.5. Mun narasingam

*mun narasingam adāgi avuṇan mukkiyattai mudippān mūvulagilmannar anjum madusūdan vāyil kuḻalin ōsai seviyaip paṟṟi vānganannarambu udaiya tumburuvōdu nāradanum tam tam vīṇai maṟandukinnara midunangaḷ tam tam kinnaram todugilōm enṟanarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mun – in an earlier point in time; narasaingam adu āgi – taking the form of narasimha \[half-man, half-lion\]; avuṇan – the monster, hiraṇya’s; mukkiyattai – eminence; mudippān – as one who destroyed; mū ulagil mannar – kings in all the three worlds; anjum – trembling in their hearts on looking at his eminence; madusūdan – kaṇṇan, who annihilated the monster, madu; vāyil – played, keeping on his divine mouth; kuḻalin – divine flute’s; ōsai – sound; seviyai – ears; paṟṟi vānga – as it pulled; nal narambu udaiya – having good strings in their musical instrument, vīṇai; tumburuvōdu – along with the sage, named tumburu; nāradanum – the great sage, nārada too; tam tam – their individual; vīṇai maṟandu – forgetting; kinnara midunangaḷum – those who are known as ‘kinnara mitunams’; tam tam – their individual; kinnaram – kinnaram \[a type of vīṇai\]; todugilōm enṟanar – they stopped playing, saying that they will not touch their musical instruments

**Перевод:**

**emperumān had earlier incarnated as narasimha, and destroyed the eminence of monster hiraṇya. He had annihilated the monster madu, who was such that kings in all the three words were frightened of. The sound from the divine flute, kept on the divine mouth of such kriṣṇa, pulled the ears of those who listened to it, towards it. Sage tumburu and the great sage, nārada, after hearing the music from kriṣṇa’s flute, said that they had forgotten about their respective musical instrument, vīṇai. Even kinnara mitunams \[celestial entities\], who play on kinnaram, a type of vīṇai, said that they will not touch their kinnarams anymore, after listening to kriṣṇa’s music.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that it is not only the ladies in celestial words, who did not have any strength in them, who were attracted to the sweet music played on his flute by kriṣṇa. This pāsuram speaks about the firmness of entities \[in a satirical manner\] who were experts in dancing and singing, who were capable of attracting all the worlds through their music and who were celebrated for their music.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**mun narasingam adāgi** – in an earlier time, when the monster hiraṇyan had obtained boons by which “I shall not be killed by anyone among the four species of dēvas \[celestial entities\], manuśyas \[human entities\], tiryak \[animals\] and stāvara \[botanical species\]” in order to kill him without being in conflict with the boons, emperumān had incarnated with half-human/half-animal form, as mentioned in the mahābhāratam ślōkam “*narasyārda tanum krutvā simhasyārda tanum tatā*” \[with a form composed of half-human and half-lion\]. The term *adāgi* refers to the amazing result that when the two halves were united, instead of appearing grotesque, due to the combination of two dissimilar forms, it appeared beautiful, as mentioned in [nānmugan tiruvandādi 22](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-22/) “*aḻagiyān tānē ari uruvan tānē*” \[emperumān, who is the boundary for beauty, took the form of narasimha, who looked beautiful).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that this term \[*mun*\] refers to the very beginning of emperumān’s incarnations. Even here, it is anachronistic in terms of the sequence of incarnations \[viz., annihilation of monster *madu* happened first and it was later that emperumān incarnated as *narasimha*; however, in this pāsuram, incarnation of narasimha has been mentioned first while annihilation of madu has been mentioned later\]. \[Since āḻvārs tend to mention incarnations in the way in which emperumān had manifested these to them, they mention in an anachronistic manner\], just as tirumangai āḻvār had mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 4.10.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/07/periya-thirumozhi-4-10-10/) “*paṇḍu mun ēnamāgi*” (in the beginning of varāha kalpam, emperumān took the form of a mahāvarāham, great boar) and tirumaḻisai āḻvār in [tiruccanda viruttam 22](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/10/thiruchchandha-viruththam-22/) “*paṇḍum inṟum mēlum*” (during the time prior to creation, during the time of creation and later, during the time of deluge \[emperumān protects all\]). Hence, this pāsuram also mentions *mun*, to refer to the earlier time. *adāgi* – this emphasises that even when emperumān incarnates in lower species \[such as humans and animals\], he does so without any deficiency in his knowledge \[omniscient\] and power \[omnipotent\].

**avuṇan mukkiyattai mudippān** – hiraṇyan, the monster, due to the \[boons of his\] unlimited, huge penance, had carried out many cruel acts; he had harmed the celestial entities; he considered himself as the most prominent entity in all the worlds; he could not tolerate hearing the names of emperumān; since prahlādan recited the names of emperumān, not considering that he was his son, he brought unspeakable misery on prahlādan. emperumān destroyed the eminence of that hiraṇyāsuran.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that hiraṇyan, having taken birth in the clan of monsters, thought that he had lot of power due to his boons; this was actually his ignorance. He also thought that he was very powerful. That was his lack of power. In order to destroy these \[which hiraṇyan considered as his eminence\], emperumān incarnated.

**mūvulagil mannar anja** – when the kings of the world looked at the eminence of his \[emperumān’s\] activities which were beyond the realm of human possibilities, they were trembling in their minds.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that emperumān annihilated the monster *madu*, who made the kings of all the three worlds to get scared of him. Since the kings surrendered to emperumān with their pride removed, as mentioned in [tiruppāvai 22](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/01/thiruppavai-22-anganma-gyalaththu/) “*abimāna bangamāy*” \[with their pride removed\], it could be said that they were frightened of him. Also, it was emperumān who incarnated through *āvēśam* \[pervading an entity with his characteristics\], as paraśurāma, and killed kings for twenty-one generations, with his weapon of axe. Thus, the kings were frightened of emperumān. When such paraśurāma confronted emperor daśarata, it was emperumān, as śrī rāma, who gave *abhayapradānam* \[granting protection\]. Is kriṣṇa, śrī rāma too? On account of *darmi aikyam* \[both are incarnations of the same emperumān\], they are the same. Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.3.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/thiruvaimozhi-7-3-11-uzhithoruzhi/) “*vaiyam kākkum uruvum pērum seygaiyum ūḻi dōṟūḻi vēṟavan engiṟa …*” (emperumān is the origin in every epoch for the forms, names and activities, protecting the worlds), since these incarnations are cyclic in nature, in every epoch, it is possible that there will be anachronism while describing the events, either with respect to different epochs or with respect to the activities taking place in the same incarnation \[sometimes, āḻvārs would speak of kriṣṇa killing kamsan, then the wrestlers and then the elephant kuvalayāpeedam, while in texts, the reverse order would be mentioned\].

**madusūdan vāyil kuḻalin ōsai seviyaip paṟṟi vānga** – the sound of music emanating from the flute, kept on the divine mouth of one who annihilated *madu*, the enemy of his followers, pulled the ears.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that emperumān had mercifully and wholeheartedly instructed śāstras \[sacred texts\] such as bhagavat gītā and abhaya pradānam \[śrī rāma giving refuge to vibhīśaṇāḻvān in tiruppullāṇi seashore\], instead of remaining quiet, as mentioned in cāndōjña upanishad 3.14.2 “*avākyanādara*:” \[emperumān, in śrī vaikuṇṭam, does not speak to anyone or sustain anyone\]. When he plays the flute from such divine mouth, is it possible for anyone not to get attracted to his music? \[when he speaks from his mouth, it is directly instructing jīvātmās; when he plays the flute, it is giving instructions through an ācārya. Instruction given by ācārya has a higher eminence than instruction given directly by emperumān, in our sampradāyam\]. Even if one remains without being attracted to the music, when the music comes on its own and occupies the ears, is it possible for anyone to sustain that and remain unmoved? \[No\].

**nannarambu …** – tumburu \[a sage\] and nārada \[another sage\] considered the strings on their vīṇā, which were capable of attracting those who had been provided with ears, as their benefit. They were famous throughout the worlds as “They are the people to listen to for their music”. Even these entities …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai adds here that it is the vīṇā that tumburu and nārada consider as their possession and have overflowing pride towards it.

**tam tam vīṇai maṟandu** – not only did they not take their vīṇās, which were forever prideful for them, they even forgot all about their vīṇās.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that even though tumburu and nārada are dear friends, since each claims the vīṇā as “This is mine; this is mine”, the pāsuram says *tam tam*.

**kinnaram …** – these entities were called as *kinnara midunangaḷ* on account of singing with their *kinnarams* \[a stringed instrument, looking similar to vīṇā\]. They too said that they will not get to touch their *kinnarams* \[after listening to the music from kriṣṇa\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says additionally here that even if someone reminds them about their kinnarams, they will say that they will never get to touch them and would go behind the music from the flute, being pulled by it. Alternatively, it could be said that they went on their own, desirously, behind that music. They will go to the source of that music \[kriṣṇa himself\] and will not return in between. Even if the one \[vibhīśaṇāḻvān\] who had said, as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 19.5 “*parityaktām* *mayā lankā*” (lankā has been given up by me), as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17.10 “*rāvanō nāma durvrutta*:” (\[I am the younger brother of\] rāvaṇa, who is of bad conduct) and as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 14.17 “*antarikśa gata*: *śrīmān*” (the one, who is a servitor, who went through the path of sky), returns midway, these entities will never return, until the time that they have ears. If they return at all, it will be due to rearing of their *karma bhāvanai* \[pathos of carrying out routine deeds, as opposed to *brahma bhāvanai* when one will be engaged with the supreme entity\].

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan
