## 3.7.6. Pattam katti

*pattam kattip pon tōdu peydu ivaḷ pādagamum silambumittamāga vaḷarttu  eduttēnukku ennōdu irukkal uṟāḷpottap pōy puṟappattu ninṟu ivaḷ pūvaip pū vaṇṇā ennumvatta vār kuḻal mangaimīr! ivaḷ māl uṟuginṟāḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vattam – being curly; vār – being long; kuḻal – having locks; mangaimīr! – oh, girls, who have youthfulness on account of your age!; pattam – ornament worn on the forehead; katti – donning it; pon tōdu – stud made with gold (for donning on the ears); pādagamum silambum – (suitable for the ankles) anklets \[one which does not make a sound and the other which makes a sound\]; peydu – donning them; ivaḷ ittamāga – the way she liked; vaḷarttu – nurtured; eduttēnukku – me, who roamed around, carrying her on my waist; ivaḷ – she, who was brought up in an eminent way like this; ennōdu – with me, who brought her up with affection; irukkal uṟāḷ – does not agree to reside with me; potta – suddenly; pōy – leaving me aside; puṟappattu ninṟu – going by the street, seen by everyone; pūvaip pū vaṇṇā ennum – will call out loudly “Oh, one who has the complexion of blue water lily!”; māl uṟuginṟāḷ – the mother says that she learnt that her daughter is fully infatuated

**Перевод:**

**Oh girls, who have long, curly locks and youthfulness on account of your age! I have donned my daughter with ornaments for her forehead, golden studs for her ears and anklets for her ankles. I nurtured her, the way she liked. I kept her on my waist and roamed around. However, she refuses to be with me, who had brought her up affectionately like this. She has gone on to the street, seen by everyone, shouting “Oh, one who has the complexion of a blue water-lily!” She is completely infatuated \[with kriṣṇa\]**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the mother is explaining to those who had come to inquire about her daughter’s condition.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**pattam …** – I had donned her with ornament, apt for her forehead, golden studs for her ears and anklets, for her ankles. These are representative of all the ornaments which I had adorned her with.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here: *pattam* – decoration for the head; *tōdu* – ornament for the ears; *pādagam* and *silambu* – those which are applied on the ankles. These are representative of all the other ornaments. I had nurtured her, without any shortcoming in any of these and had brought her up, the way she desired. Even though she did not have any affection towards me, considering that I am affectionate towards her, even if her heart had gone out to someone else, she could have stayed near me. We do not see even that. Even if she did not do that, she could have spent time with her friends. Even if she avoided doing that, she could have stayed in her place, awaiting his arrival. Instead of doing even that, when she went searching for him, she could have given up whatever had to be given up in the manner specified, by analysing and deciding \[as mentioned in [bhagavad gītā 18.66](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66/) “*sarva darmān parityajya..*”\]. She did not do that; she did not consider giving up what had been proscribed and what had been looked down upon. She even felt ashamed of the manner in which I had nurtured her. Should she go like this, suddenly, as if giving up harmful entities?

**ittamāga …** – instead of controlling her and nurturing her, I nurtured her the way she desired. I did not even allow her to walk, but carried her on my waist and roamed everywhere.

**ivaḷ ennōdu irukkal uṟāḷ** – She, who had been brought up in such an affectionate way by me, could have thought “Did she not nurture me like this!” and could have been obedient to me. Even if she had not been like that, she could have stayed with me, even if her heart had gone out towards someone else, so that I could have felt happy, enjoying her presence. She did not do that, either.

**pottap pōy …** – Without any of these, suddenly she left me. She went on to the street, having been seen by everyone around. Instead of keeping quiet, appropriate to her qualities of femininity, she called out “*pūvaip pū vaṇṇā*” (Oh, one with the complexion of a blue water lily), expressing her desire to enjoy the beauty of his divine form.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother is wondering whether anyone, while leaving suddenly, will engage with the beauty of the form of the person with whom one is intending to engage with, and call out “*pūvaip pū vaṇṇā*!”

**vatta vār kuḻal mangaimīr** – Oh, girls, who have curly and long hairs, and who are young, on account of your age! Are you people not obedient towards your respective mother? Should she \[my daughter\] too not be like that? Instead of doing that …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother says that the daughter is not staying with her, who is her controller; she is infatuated with him, who is not desirous of being with her. If he were desirous of being with her, the mother says that she would have stayed alone, as her righteous duty.

He says at the end that the pāsuram narrates the following: While the ācāryan decorates the disciple with all the ornaments \[here, the word ornament refers to providing knowledge etc\] and carries out that which is good for the disciple in a way that the disciple likes, the disciple avoids being under the control of the ācāryan and wishes to engage with emperumān directly. The ācāryan shares this with his other disciples. *pattam* refers to the completeness of being totally dependent on the ācāryan; *pon tōdu* refers to the strength provided to the faculty of hearing of the disciple \[through his ears\] to ensure firmness in the completeness of the total dependence mentioned above; *pādagam* refers to not having any other refuge \[considering ācāryan alone as the refuge\]; *silambu* refers to the brightness of that *pādagam*.

**ivaḷ māl uṟuginṟāḷē** – She is totally infatuated, in his regard.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.7.7. Pesavum teriyada

*pēsavum teriyāda peṇmaiyin pēdaiyēn pēdai ivaḷkūsam inṟi ninṟārgaḷ tam edir kōl kaḻindān mūḻaiyāykēsavā enṟum kēdilee enṟum kinjuga vāy moḻiyāḷvāsavār kuḻal mangaimīr! ivaḷ māl uṟuginṟāḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāsam – being fragrant fully; vār – being long; kuḻal – having locks; mangaimīr – oh, girls, who are complete with your innocence!; pēdaiyēn – I, who am unable to keep her under my control\|; pēdai – being \[my\] daughter; pēsavum teriyāda – none could utter a word; peṇmaiyin – having femininity; kinjugam – parrot’s; vāy moḻiyāḷ – having speech similar to \[the parrot’s\] speech; ivaḷ – this girl \[her daughter\]; ninṟārgaḷ tam – those who are firmly associated with qualities of accam \[fear\], madam \[innocence\], nāṇam \[modesty\] and payirppu \[aversion to being touched by strangers\]; edir – in their presence; kūsam inṟi – without any shyness; kōl kaḻindān mūḻiyāy – like a ladle which has come off the wooden handle; kēsavā enṟum – saying “Oh, one who has beautiful locks!”; kēdilee enṟum – saying “Oh, one who is without any fault” (one who does not let go of followers); māl uṟuginṟāḷ – she is infatuated

**Перевод:**

**Oh girls, who are having long locks which are always fragrant, and who are complete with your quality of innocence! I am unable to control my daughter, who cannot tolerate a word spoken by anyone about her femininity. She has sweet words just like a parrot. In the presence of those who are firmly rooted in feminine qualities of fear, innocence, modesty and aversion to strangers, without having any shyness, and \[severing her connection with me\] like a wooden ladle coming off its handle, she cries out “Oh, one who has beautiful locks! Oh, one who is without any faults!” She is completely infatuated with him \[kriṣṇa\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that apart from being unable to control her daughter by speaking about the faults in her qualities, the mother now finds that even if she praises her daughter, her daughter is not able to bear even for a moment \[separation from kriṣṇa\].*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**pēsavum teriyāda peṇmaiyin** – she has qualities of femininity such that none can speak a word about her. In other words, through her activities, she is steadfast in her femininity. Even if someone were to speak a word about her, which could appear as if it would make her slip from her qualities of femininity, she would hit back through her femininity. Femininity here is defined as having qualities of ātmā \[soul\], namely fear, innocence, shyness and aversion towards strangers.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *pēdai*, apart from referring to the feminine qualities of fear, innocence, shyness and aversion towards strangers, could also refer to a peacock; the mother says that her daughter is like a peacock.

**pēdaiyēn pēdai** – she is one who doesn’t know of any means, viz. she was born as a daughter to me, who doesn’t know of carrying out activities which are not apt for my femininity and my clan.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that her daughter became a *pēdai* since she was born to her \[the mother\], who herself is a *pēdai*. For the mother, the quality of *pēdai* refers to her not giving up on her daughter, who was apt to be given up after the daughter had given up on her mother.

**ivaḷ** – she, who is like this.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother looks pointedly at her daughter, thinking “Her thinking is not aligned to her age” \[she is thinking beyond her age\]

**kūsam inṟī ninṟārgaḷ tam edir** – those who are steadfast in their qualities of femininity and obedience towards their mothers. In their presence, without the shyness of thinking “In Your presence, how could I do this?”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that those daughters, who are obedient towards their mothers, are apt to feel shy etc. In svāpadēśam \[enunciating one’s own thoughts on a subject\], he says that this refers to those who feel that they cannot attain emperumān on their own; their responsibility ends with identifying the entity who they should attain. Alternatively, this refers to those who carry out the deed mentioned in the first part of *dvaya mahāmantram* \[second of the three esoteric mantrams in our sampradāyam; the deed referred to here is carrying out *śaraṇāgati*, act of surrendering, by saying ‘*prapadyē*’ (I hold on to your divine feet as my refuge)\]. This gets established when the dress is held on to \[we have seen in the earlier pāsurams that the girl does not even realise that her dress is loosening from the waist etc\]. This applies to other features allied to this \[we have seen words spoken by the mother, in earlier pāsurams, such as her daughter’s teeth have not sprouted, her locks have not grown such that they could be plaited etc\]. All these forbidden activities are carried out by the girl on account of her deep desire for kriṣṇa \[the entity whom she has to attain, irrespective of what others say\].

**kōl kaḻindān mūḻiyāy** – severing her connection with me, who is her refuge, similar to a ladle coming off its handle. This implies that the daughter is no more under the mother’s control.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother, in an earlier pāsuram \[3.7.4\], had said that the ladle does not know the taste of the foodstuff that it is serving. Now, she says that the ladle has come off the handle. The difference between the two is that the earlier incident was with reference to the quality of the girl \[she is unlike the ladle which does not know the taste of the foodstuff that it serves, viz she was too young to know the importance of emperumān and was still having the urge to attain him, somehow\]. Here, it is the fault which she is manifesting \[just as the ladle comes off the handle, she is severing her connection with her mother\]. The *An* \[as seen in the last syllable of the term *kōl kaḻindān*\] is a poetic metric and does not have any meaning. None benefits if the ladle comes off the handle. Alternatively, it could be said that her status was similar to the ladle which has come off the handle from the hands of the one who is serving a foodstuff. It has no use. Through this, it is implied that the mother has lost her control over the daughter and that the daughter is now going in line with her senses. This applies to an ācāryan too \[when the disciple goes outside the control of the ācāryan\].

**kēsavā enṟum** – She says “Oh, one who has eminent locks!”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that this term \[kēsavā\] refers to one who annihilates his followers’ enemy \[just as he killed the monster, *kēsi*\] as well as to one who has eminent locks.

**kēdilee enṟum** – She says “Oh, one who does not let go of those who are totally dependent on you!”

**kinjuga vāy moḻiyāḷ** – She has the complexion of a parrot’s beak on her lips and the sweetness of words, similar to the sweet words of a parrot. Even when the daughter is calling out to kriṣṇa, mentioning his name, without obeying her mother, the beauty of the daughter’s lips and the sweetness of her words are attractive to the mother.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that through these two \[lips being reddish like the parrot and words being sweet like the parrot’s\], it is inferred that unlike [tiruvāimoḻi 8.9.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/05/thiruvaimozhi-8-9-6-thiruvarul-muzhgi/) “*tiruvaruḷ oṇ kamugu paḻattadu*” \[her lips were like the reddish, well rounded areca fruit\], earlier, her lips were pale red and that she will not speak a word after her mother had told her anything.

**vāsavār kuḻal mangaimīr**– Oh, girls, who have fragrant and long locks, and who have youthfulness apt for your age!

**ivaḷ māl uṟuginṟāḷē** – She is totally infatuated towards him, like this.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.7.8. Karai punum

*kāṟai pūṇum kaṇṇādi kāṇum tan kaiyil vaḷai kulukkumkūṟai udukkum ayarkkum tan kōvaic cevvāy tiruttumtēṟit tēṟi ninṟu āyiram pērt tēvan tiṟam pidaṟṟummāṟil māmaṇi vaṇṇan mēl ivaḷ māl uṟuginṟāḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kāṟai – necklet made of gold \[necklet is similar to a bracelet, but worn on the neck\]; pūṇum – she wore on her neck; kaṇṇādi – in the mirror; kāṇum – she saw (her beauty of the necklet and her neck); than kaiyil – on her hands; vaḷai – bangles; kulukkum – she shook; kūṟai – sari; udukkum – she wore, properly; ayarkkum – she became forgetful; kōvai – like kōvaikkani \[a type of fruit, with reddish inner part); sem – being reddish; than vāy – her lips; tiruttum – made it to appear deep red; tēṟit tēṟi – becoming clearer; ninṟu – sustaining herself; āyiram pēr – one who has a thousand divine names; dēvan – supreme entity’s; tiṟam – regarding him; pidaṟṟum – she recited in a disorderly manner; māṟu il – unmatched; māmaṇi – like a bluish gem; vaṇṇan mēl – regarding kaṇṇan \[kriṣṇa\] who has a complexion like that; ivaḷ māl uṟuginṟāḷ – she became infatuated

**Перевод:**

**She donned a golden necklet, on her neck. She looked into the mirror to check the beauty of her neck and the necklet. She shook the bangles on her hands. She wore a sari, in a proper manner. Despite carrying out all these decorations, anticipating his arrival, since he did not come, she became forgetful. Gathering herself, starting to decorate herself further, she made her already reddish lips, to look further deep reddish. Becoming clearer \[in her mind\], she recited the thousand names of emperumān, in a disorderly manner. She became completely infatuated with kriṣṇa, who has the complexion of a bluish gem, without a match.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says the following: The daughter, due to her overflowing affection for kriṣṇa, was certain that he would come \[to see her\]. Thinking “He is one who likes to look at auspicious features. He should not look at my wizened state”, she decorates herself. What would happen if he had seen her pitiable state? He would have felt ashamed and sorrowful, taking responsibility for her condition, thinking “It is due to our thinking that she has not attained the state of maturity that we delayed coming to her and that has led to this condition for her”. As a remedial measure for that as well as to make her apt to be enjoyed by him, she decorated herself like this \[as mentioned in this pāsuram\]. In case he had not come, what would have happened to her decoration, which she made desirously? āccān piḷḷai, quoting nālūrp piḷḷai, would say “She would have thought that this auspicious decoration is one which had been carried out for a corpse”*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kāṟai pūṇum** – Due to her distress, thinking “I must attain him, by doing whatever it takes”, she started decorating herself, believing “If I decorate myself to attract him, he will come, head over heels”. She started with her neck since that is the first limb which he will hug upon seeing her. She wore a necklet. This is the ornament which will shine on the limb, which is between her top part \[head\] and the lower part \[body\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that if her neck were compared before and after donning the necklet, the necklet would appear to be superfluous \[her neck was that beautiful, even otherwise\].

**kaṇṇādi kāṇum** – Since the ornament worn on the neck, the necklet, could not be seen by her \[directly with her eyes\], in order to confirm “Is this apt for him or not?”, she would see the union of her neck and the necklet in a mirror. This ornament is representative of all the ornaments donned by her on her limbs.

**than kaiyil vaḷai kulukkum** – since her desire \[to see kriṣṇa\] results in a filling up of her form \[due to that happiness\], to confirm that it is indeed true, she would shake the bangles on her hands. Due to slimming down of the body on account of separation \[from kriṣṇa\], if the bangles fall down, it is she who picks them up and wears them again. Even when she wears them again, they will not stay on her hands \[since she has become that thin\]. Now that her form has filled up, anticipating kriṣṇa’s arrival, she would check if the bangles are in place, without falling down, by shaking the bangles.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when the bangles, which by themselves would fall down on their own, are shaken, it would be natural for them to fall down. \`The ones which fell down, had indeed fallen down. The rest would stay put on her hands due to the filling up of her form \[in anticipation of kriṣṇa’s arrival\]. Due to her thinking of his auspicious qualities, the bangles filled up as they were shaken up repeatedly. It would not do justice to her tenderness, if they fell down.

**kūṟai udukkum**– even her dress now fits aptly on her waist, since her body has got filled up. In normal times, part of the sari would be on her hand and the other part would be on her feet / on the ground. Both the bangles and the dress, like those who keep conversing with each other intimately, will stay in their respective place, together or will fall down from their respective place, together. She wore the sari only in order to search for a suitable, unmatched material beyond the necklet. In other words, to attract him only, did she wear the sari properly. He engages in her beauty only. Hence, she will keep removing and wearing the sari until the opportunity presents itself for him to come to her.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that it appears that her activities such as removing the bangles, wearing them, removing the necklet, wearing them, removing her sari, wearing it etc would continue until he comes.

**ayarkkum** – Thus, despite decorating herself for his arrival, since he did not come, she lost her thinking ability.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that due to the eminence of these decorations, she would even forget the time when she had called out to him as “*kēsavā*” \[as in the previous pāsuram\] and her desire of uniting with him. Alternatively, her desire would make her get bewildered; she would check whether she had worn the necklet and touch it to confirm it; she would look in the mirror, and touch the image of the necklet in the mirror and touch that to confirm whether she has worn it \[she was that bewildered\]. Thus, for every activity that she had indulged in \[while decorating herself\], this term *ayarkkum* \[to forget\] could be applied.

**than kōvaic cevvāy tiruttum** – She regains her knowledge and says “Let me make myself more attractive for him, by further adding to my decorations”. Hence, in order to make her lips, which, by their nature, are already reddish, to appear deeper in red colour, she will add a few materials which are reddish in colour. Unlike the other limbs, this limb \[her mouth\] is one which feeds him his food, just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 3.7.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2022/09/periya-thirumozhi-3-7-2/) “*toṇḍaiyam sengani vāy nugarndān*” (drank the nectar from her beautiful lips, which are like *kōvai* fruit).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that by repeatedly looking at her lips in the mirror, her lips would become darker \[they are such soft that if someone were to look at them, including herself, they would become deeper in their reddish colour\]. piḷḷai \[this could be nampiḷḷai or periyavāccān piḷḷai or nālūr āccān piḷḷai (our preceptors)\] would say that she would keep correcting his *amudu padi, sāṟṟup padi* \[*amudu padi* refers to the food proffered to emperumān; here, it refers to the nectar from her lips; *sāṟṟup padi* refers to the dress donned for emperumān; for him, her sari is his *sāṟṟup padi*\].

**tēṟit tēṟi ninṟu** – due to the benefit of her decorations and just as it has been mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 37.12 “*tasmin ca bahavō guṇā*:” (he has countless auspicious qualities), since she has firm faith in his qualities due to which he will come and help her, she avoids her forgetfulness, regaining clarity; due to that clarity, she sustains herself.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as she was earlier forgetting \[*ayarkkum*\] on account of not seeing kriṣṇa, she would regain clarity too. The desire in her mind was such that bewilderment and clarity would appear to take place when she is awake, and when she is asleep and getting dreams, respectively. Just as one, who is dreaming, does not realise that it is a dream, her desire in her mind too was unknown to her. *ninṟu* – that desire in her mind made her to regain composure.

**āyiram pērt tēvan tiṟam pidaṟṟum** – emperumān has a thousand divine names, reflecting his auspicious qualities and activities, as mentioned in mahābhāratam sabhā parvam 38.11 “*dēvō nāma sahasravān*”. She will recite those divine names, in a disorderly manner, being bewildered with the beauty of his form which usurps her mind and due to the involvement with those names.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that she recited his countless names, which reflected his splendorous, auspicious qualities, born out of his eminence and his simplicity, as well as the names of his divine servitors.

**māṟil …** – Thus, she became infatuated with the one who has an unmatched beautiful form, like a bluish gemstone.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that his divine form was similar to a unique, priceless bluish gemstone. The mother says that her daughter became infatuated regarding him.

In the end, he says the following: (1) *bhakti* \[devotion\] and *prapatti* \[surrendering, considering the act of surrendering as having been performed as a means to attain emperumān, called in our sampradāyam as *upāya prapatti*\], which are ordained in śāstrams, and which illuminate on what is to be given up and what is to be accepted \[every entity other than emperumān is to be given up and emperumān alone is to be accepted\], are not considered as significant in our sampradāyam. On the other hand, both *bhakti* and *prapatti*, which are *adikāra viśēśaṇam* \[attributes of one who has surrendered to emperumān and who does not consider that act of surrendering as a means to attain emperumān; *bhakti* is a prerequisite for carrying out *kainkaryam* \[servitude\] to emperumān and *prapatti* is the activity required by emperumān to shower his grace on the entity, who surrenders through an ācāryan\] and which lead to bowing down of the head, are considered as *ātma bhūśaṇam* \[decorations for the *ātmā*\]. It is this which is referred to by the term *kāṟai*, in the pāsuram \[when one bows down the head, it comes to the neck; *kāṟai* is an ornament for the neck\]. (2) Comparing this to the words and activities of *pūrvācāyars* \[preceptors\] is identified with the term *kaṇṇādi kāṇum* \[just as the daughter checks with the mirror regarding her necklet, the śiśya would check his qualities and activities of *bhakti* and *prapatti* with the words and actions of his ācāryan\]. (3) Due to the affection arising out of the words of ācāryan, desire towards other entities would disappear. The resultant affection towards the entity to be attained \[emperumān\] cannot be shaken either by her or by the ācāryan \[her mother\]. This is brought out by the term *kaiyil vaḷai kulukkum* \[just like the filling which she felt, in anticipation of the arrival of kriṣṇa, due to which the bangles will not fall, the instructions received from the ācāryan will create a fulfilment in us, due to which we will be strongly bonded with emperumān, and this bonding can never be shaken\]. (4) When we look at our *svarūpam* \[our basic nature, which is that we are servitors of emperumān\], in line with that, we should wait till we get approval from emperumān \[or ācāryan\] to carry out kainkaryam to emperumān. But, when we look at the *viśayam* (emperumān), we cannot wait and we will rush to carry out kainkaryam. Thus, we get caught between *svarūpānurūpa prāpyam* \[attaining emperumān based on our svarūpam\] and *viśayānurūpa prāpyam* \[attaining emperumān, based on emperumān’s distinction\]. This alternating thought is brought out by the term *kūṟai udukkum ayarkkum* \[when she waits for emperumān to come, she will wear the sari; when she wants to rush towards him, she will remove it\]. (5) The *bhakti* \[devotion\], which one should have just prior to carrying out kainkaryam, would take the person to divyadēśam to carry out kainkaryam. That devotion should gradually grow further, and it has to be tested for determining one’s level of maturity \[in carrying out kainkaryam\]. This is referred to by the term *kōvaic cevvāy tiruttum* \[one should test whether one has matured to the level of *bhakti* required to carry out kainkaryam\]. (6)  More than carrying out kainkaryam to him, reciting his divine names which manifest his auspicious qualities, and to his followers is brought out by the term *dēvan tiṟam pidaṟṟum* \[the term *tiṟam* refers to his followers\], just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.5.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/02/thiruvaimozhi-6-5-7-annaimir/) “*ivaḷ vāyanagaḷ tirundavē*” (emperumān’s symbols \[such as his divine ornaments etc\] and his divine names are becoming more glorious, on being spoken of by parānkuśa nāyaki). (7) These divine names will reveal the distinction of his divine form and enable her to engage with *bhakti* towards him. This is brought out by the term *ivaḷ māl uṟuginṟāḷē*.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.7.9. Kaittalattu ulla

*kaittalattu uḷḷa mādu aḻiyak kaṇṇālangaḷ seydu ivaḷaivaittu vaittuk koṇḍu enna vāṇibam nammai vadup paduttumseyttalai eḻu nāṟṟup pōl avan seyvana seydu koḷḷamaittada mugil vaṇṇan pakkal vaḷara vidumingaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaittalattu uḷḷa – available on hand; mādu aḻiya – all the wealth to get exhausted; kaṇṇālangaḷ – marriages; seydu – carrying out; ivaḷai – this girl, who is not under our control; vaittu vaittuk koṇḍu – keeping her under our control and keeping her under our protection; enna vāṇibam – what is the purpose?; nammai – for our clan; vadup paduttum – will bring slander; seyttalai – in the field; eḻu – growing up; nāṟṟup pōl – just as the owner \[of the crop\] has the liberty to do as per his wish, for her too; avan – he, who is desired by her; seyvana seydu koḷḷa – to do as per his wish; mai – being dark; tada – being huge; mugil – like cloud; vaṇṇan pakkal – in the proximity of one who has a form; vaḷara – to nurture; vidumingaḷ – leave her

**Перевод:**

**The mother says that she has spent all the wealth which was with her, in her marriage. She sees no purpose in controlling and protecting her daughter, who refuses to be under her control. She says that the daughter will bring slander to the clan. The relatives, on hearing these words of the mother, tell her that just as the owner of the crop, which is growing on his land, has the liberty to utilise the crop in the way that he desires, leave her too under the control of the one who desires her. Take her to the proximity of one, who has the complexion of a dark cloud, and allow her to grow up with him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that in the earlier pāsuram, āḻvār had mentioned through the words of the mother, the changes which happened in the daughter as a result of the desire which developed in her mind. In this pāsuram, he mentions through the words of the relatives, who had come to enquire about the changes in the daughter, as to what is to be done.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kaittalattuḷḷa …** – Due to affection, thinking “Appropriate to the status of relatives and appropriate to the wealth that we have, since we have only one daughter”, I spent all the wealth that I had and conducted her marriage such that all the people in the world praised me.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that starting from the day when she was born, on various occasions when there were distinctive celebrations, during the time when she came of age, the mother conducted functions appropriate to the clan such that people praised her “She has a daughter for whom she is celebrating appropriate to the status of her relatives and appropriate to her wealth”. Wealth here includes the wealth on hand and wealth in the earth \[could have been treasure or crops on land\]. The term *mādu*, apart from wealth, would also refer to cattle and calves, since they are herd-people, and would include cows which have calves, and cows which do not have calves.

**ivaḷai …** – Thinking “Could we allow her to do as she likes, when her age is such that she vouldn’t be under my control?” I had kept her under my control and protection. What is the purpose? There is no purpose either for her or for me, in line with our clan.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother is looking at her daughter, who is not under her control, sharply. She feels that in her younger days, she had kept her daughter on her lap and near her, nurturing her. Now, by keeping her under her control and protection, censuring her, she is not seeing any benefit for either. She sees that her daughter would only bring slander to the clan, which is trying to do good to her.

**nammai vadup paduttum** – We have not been blamed for anything until now. But, she will bring slander for us. The underlying opinion here is that she will bring in opprobrium to the clan, with people saying “With the relatives not agreeing to, she left on her own”

**seyttalai …**– just as the owner of a land on which crops are growing has the right over that crop, allow the one, who she likes, to do with her in the manner which he likes.

**mai …** – The relatives said ”He \[kriṣṇa\] has a complexion which is similar to a cloud which has imbibed water until its neck. Take her to him and leave her by his side”. The basis for this is that all these words have been mentioned by the mother, in all the pāsurams of this decad, just as it has been mentioned in the last pāsuram \[of the decad\] as “*tāy urai seyda adanai*” (the words spoken of by the mother). This applies to the pāsurams which come after this too.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that emperumān has the complexion of dark clouds which are filled with water. He has the firmness of utilising those who take refuge under him due to his auspicious qualities, in the manner that he desires. Those who know about the daughter, tell the mother “Take her to the one, who is capable of doing what he wishes, and let her grow up with him”.

In the end he says the following: An ācāryan instructs his disciple about *upāyam* \[means to attain emperumān\] and *upēyam* \[benefit that comes to the disciple after he attains emperumān, which is carrying out kainkaryam to emperumān in the manner liked by emperumān\], which has been coming down from one generation to the next over a long passage of time. The ācāryan sees the maturity in his disciple after he receives instructions from him. By instructing him further, what benefit will accrue? By making these meanings secretive, they have only been destroyed. The distinguishing meanings of these are known only to entities such as tirukkōttiyūr nambi \[one of the ācāryans of rāmānujar\], who instructed these meanings to rāmānujar, after making him walk many times and after testing him severely. The effect of such closely guarded secretive meanings do not go well with this clan of *prapannars* \[those who have taken refuge under emperumān\] who are unable to carry out *kainkaryam* \[service\] to emperumān \[this is similar to the mother, keeping the daughter with her, after marrying her off, and not letting her go the person of her choice\]. The verse says that instead of keeping her with you and blaming her, take her to the one, who has distinguishing form and who comes to take her under his refuge.

We shall next consider the 10<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.7.10. Perup perutta

*perup perutta kaṇṇālangaḷ seydu pēṇi nam illattuḷḷēiruttuvān eṇṇi nām irukka ivaḷum onṟū eṇṇuginṟāḷmaruttuvap padam neengināḷ ennum vārttai paduvadan munoruppaduttidumin ivaḷai ulagu aḷandān idaikkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

perup perutta – being grand; kaṇṇālangaḷ – marriages; seydu – carrying out; pēṇi – protecting established customs of a family; nam illattuḷḷē – inside our house; iruttuvān – to keep her \[the daughter\]; nām eṇṇi irukka – while we were thinking; ivaḷ – this girl; onṟu – opposite of our thinking; eṇṇuginṟāḷ – she is thinking; maruttuvap padam neengināḷ ennum – “When the medical practitioner prepares a medicine, when it is not properly matured, just as the medicine gets wasted, since we did not look at her level of maturity and carry out the necessary activity, she went out of our hands” – this; vārttai – word; paduvadan mun – before people in the world say this; ulagu aḷandān idaikkē – one who measured all the worlds, after receiving water symbolically; ivaḷai – this girl; oruppaduttidumin – they said “You reach her”

**Перевод:**

**After conducting her marriage in a grand manner, keeping the customs of the family in mind, we decided to keep her in our house. However, this girl is thinking the exact opposite. When the girl’s mother informed this to her relatives, they told her that when a medical practitioner prepares a medicine, just as the medicine gets wasted when it is not matured, \[people of the\] world may say that this girl has gone out of our hands since we engaged in an action without looking at her level of maturity. Before the \[people of the\] world say this, take her to the one who measured all the worlds by accepting water symbolically and leave her with him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that through this pāsuram, āḻvār says through the words of the mother that the relatives are urging her.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**perupperutta kaṇṇālangaḷ seydu** – carrying out marriage in a grand manner, beyond the grand marriages conducted by those who are wealthy on account of the vanity of their wealth.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother conducted her marriage beyond the grand marriages conducted by wealthy people, who did so due to their vanity. She was following the righteous acts prescribed for her clan as well as protecting her daughter.

**pēṇi** – keeping in mind, the customs followed by the clan

**nam illattuḷḷē …** – while we were thinking that we will keep her inside our house

**ivaḷum onṟu eṇṇuginṟāḷ** – she too is thinking of something which is the exact opposite of our thought.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the daughter thinks that her mother’s house is a prison and that the place where she should live is the place where he \[kriṣṇa\] was staying.

**maruttuvap padam …** – when a medical practitioner mixes a medicine, it would go waste if it is mixed before it has got matured. People of the world would say that “She has gone out of her hands since they carried out an action without looking at her maturity level”. Before such a situation develops …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother’s relatives tell her “Those who give birth to a daughter should watch constantly for signs of maturity in the daughter, just as a medical practitioner looks for the maturing of the medicines which he mixes. Before any mistake takes place in her case, take her to the one who measured all the worlds and protected all, without drawing any boundary, wholeheartedly.”

**oruppaduttidumin …** – while mahābali \[a king in the clan of monsters\] thought the world, which belongs to emperumān, was his, emperumān, through the means of taking alms from him, by accepting the water poured out symbolically by mahābali, took the land and kept it under his divine feet. You take this girl and keep her with such emperumān. If you do not carry out this, due to her nature and his nature, the two will unite on their own. Hence, they urge her to unite her with him, herself.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says at the end, the following: An ācāryan corrects a disciple through his instructions \[explaining the meanings of the three esoteric mantrams of our sampradāyam\] and joyfully celebrates when the disciple expresses desire to carry out kainkaryam to emperumān. The ācāryan keeps the disciple with him, in line with the disciple’s nature of being *paratantran* \[totally dependent on ācāryan\]. The ācāryan thinks that this is *puruśārtam* (ultimate benefit), coming out of his burden \[this explains the first line of the pāsuram, where the mother carries out marriage for her daughter and keeps the daughter with her, in her house\]. The disciple goes beyond this, thinking of *viśayānurūpam* \[the nature of emperumān\] and going out to attain emperumān \[this explains the second line of the pāsuram, when the daughter thinks of going out of the house, to emperumān\]. Seeing this firmness of the disciple, others say a few words, as mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.7.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-7-2-alum-paramanai/) “*āḷum paramanaik kaṇṇanai*” (emperumān has auspicious qualities such as sauśeelyam (disposition) etc, which he reveals during in incarnations such as in kriṣṇavatāram). They say that before the disciple goes outside of this *pāratantryam* and this becomes known to others, leave him with emperumān, after praying to him, as in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.9.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-9-4-enakke-atchey/) “*tanakkēyāga enaikkoḷḷum idē enakkē kaṇṇananai yān koḷ siṟappē*” (The only result that I desire from kriṣṇa is his saying mercifully “always exclusively serve me”) to grant exclusive servitude only for emperumān and not for others, not for the disciple and not for the disciple and emperumān together. They say that making the disciple to say as in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.3.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/10/thiruvaimozhi-10-3-2-thagavilai/) “*viyakka inbuṟudum*” (We become joyful when you are pleased), they should take him to the one who is looking for entities whom he could take under his refuge, as mentioned in [nānmugan tiruvandādi 60](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-60/) “*āḷ pārttu uḻi taruvāy*” (one, who goes searching “ Will I get anyone who will be under my refuge?”) That emperumān, utilising the battle between the celestial entities and monsters, had taken incarnation as trivikraman, taken back all his possessions through alms \[from mahābali\] and who, through that act, explained *anya śēśatvam* (carrying out servitude to others, instead of only to emperumān) and *svasvātantryam* (being dependent on oneself, instead of being totally dependent on emperumān). They finally say that one should affirm that *viśayānurūpa puruśārtam* \[benefit derived by considering emperumān’s nature\] is preferable to *svarūpānurūpa puruśārtam* \[benefit derived by considering our basic nature of being a servitor and dependent on emperumān\] and shift the status from *caramaparva stiti* \[status of being in the ultimate stage of carrying out kainkaryam\] to *pratama parva stiti* \[status of being the primary stage of carrying out kainkaryam\]. This may sound to be at loggerheads with our sampradāyam. The real meaning for this is that the term *caramaparva stiti* refers to engaging in kainkaryam with one’s ācāryan. ācāryan will tell the disciple to go and carry out servitude to emperumān, who is *pratmaparva stiti*. This is brought out by the last two lines of the pāsuram.

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.7.11. Jnalam murrum

*jñālam muṟṟum uṇḍu ālilait tuyil nārāyaṇanukku ivaḷmāl adāgi magiḻndanaḷ enṟu tāy urai seyda adanaikōlam ār poḻil sūḻ puduvaiyar kōn vittu cittan sonnamālai pattum vallavargatku illai varu tuyarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

jñālam muṟṟum – all the worlds, starting from earth; uṇḍu – keeping in his divine stomach such that they do not get destroyed during deluge; Al ilai – on a tender banyan leaf; tuyil – one who mercifully reclined; nārāyaṇanukku – she, in the matter regarding nārāyaṇan; māladāgi – being highly infatuated; magiḻndanaḷ enṟu – saying that she was joyous; tāy – divine mother; urai seyda adanai – described; kōlam Ar – being full of beauty; poḻil – by gardens; sūḻ – surrounded; puduvaiyar – for those who inhabit śrī villibuttūr; kōn – one, who is the controller; vittu cittan – periyāḻvār; sonna – mercifully composed; mālai – garland of words; pattum – the ten pāsurams; vallavargatku – for those who are capable of reciting; varu – that which comes as a hurdle to enjoying emperumān; tuyar – sorrow; illai – will not happen

**Перевод:**

**emperumān kept all the worlds, starting with earth, in his divine stomach, such that they would not get destroyed during the time of deluge. The divine mother recounted that her daughter became highly infatuated with that nārāyaṇan, becoming joyful. periyāḻvār, the controller of those who live in śrī villibuttūr, which is surrounded by beautiful gardens, mercifully composed those \[words of the mother\] into garlands of words. Those who recite these ten pāsurams will not have the sorrow of facing any hurdle in experiencing emperumān.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In this last pāsuram, āḻvār mentions the benefit which will accrue to those who learn this decad and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**jñālam …** – nārāyaṇan, who is the lord of all, has the quality of *aghatitaghatanam* (binding together entities which cannot ever be bound), just as the way he reclined on a tender banyan leaf after swallowing all the worlds during the time of deluge and protecting them, in his divine stomach.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says in his svāpadēśam that nārāyaṇan kept all the worlds, measuring 50 crore miles, inside his divine stomach, and reclined on a tender banyan leaf. This *aghatitaghatanā sāmartyam* \[ability to bind together entities which cannot be bound\] is typical of the name *nārāyaṇan*, coming from the *bahuvrīhi samāsam* \[compound word by which the word conveys the meaning that all the entities in all the worlds rest inside him; through the *tatpuruśa samāsam*, it would also mean that he resides inside all the entities\]. He resides inside the minutest entity, as brought out by the taittirīya upaniśat nārāyaṇavalli phrase “*aṇiyōr aṇīyān*” \[he resides inside the minutest particle\] and as mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/04/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-10-parantha-than-paravai/) “*idam tigaḻ poruḷ toṟum karandu engum parandu uḷan*” \[he pervades and remains hidden inside all the entities present in all the places\]. When he consumes all these, at the time of deluge, as mentioned in the same tiruvāimoḻi pāsuram 1.1.10 “*ivai uṇḍa karanē*” \[one who consumed all these and remained firm\], this becomes the *aghatita ghatanā* quality – one who resides inside all entities, yet swallows all the entities and reclines on a tender leaf.

**ivaḷ māl adāgi magiḻndanaḷ enṟu …**– she is a little child; she has become completely infatuated with that nārāyaṇan; as a result of her uniting with him, she became joyous. The words, spoken by the mother, regarding this …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *ivaḷ* refers to one who appears like an infant \[in the eyes of her mother\] and the term *māl adāgi* refers to the infatuation which is not seen even in those who have matured well into young girls. The term *adu* in *adu āgi* indicates absence of a metaphor for her infatuation with emperumān \[it is that eminent\]. *magiḻndanaḷ* – the mothers became satisfied that the infatuation which their daughters had, resulted in the ultimate benefit of carrying out kainkaryam to emperumān and that the daughters became joyous. *tāy* – though mentioned in singular number here, it refers to all the mothers. Terms seen in earlier pāsurams such as *vaḷara vidumin*, *oruppaduttirumin* refer to plural number. *ivaḷ* also refers to one who has had devotion, just before getting to carry out kainkaryam \[which is a prerequisite for carrying out kainkaryam\] and involving with kainkaryam, she attains emperumān, making herself enjoyable for him. Her status has matured to such an extent that her divine mother, who is her ācāryan, says “*ivaḷ māl adāgi magiḻndanaḷ*”.

**kōlam …** – śrī villibuttūr is surrounded by beautiful gardens. periyāḻvār is the controller of that place. For those who are capable of reciting these ten distinguished pāsurams, mercifully composed as a garland of words …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that āḻvār is the controller of śrī villibuttūr which is surrounded by gardens which are attractive, being complete with flowers and fruits. *vittu cittan* – one who has viṣṇu in his mind. ōr, one who is residing in viṣṇu’s mind. Similar to the divine name *nārāyaṇan*, this name *vittu cittan* is also a *samāsa dvayam* \[compound word with two terms, with complementary meanings\]. *sonna mālai* – the words used in these pāsurams will go until carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam, with words spoken by self \[*svāpadēśam*, as spoken by the mother\] and by others \[*anyāpadēśam*, spoken as the words of the relatives\]. For those who are capable of reciting these verses, with the pathos of periyāḻvār …

**illai varu tuyarē**– There is no sorrow which will come as a hurdle in experiencing emperumān etc.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that instead of saying *tuyar varuga illai*, since āḻvār has said *illai varu tuyar*, this is like *nama*: in the second term of tirumantram. In other words, *iśta prāpti* will come only after *aniśta nivrutti* \[viz. one can attain what one desires only after getting rid of undesirables, just as in tirumantram, the second term says that one is not dependent on oneself (*nama*:), which is elimination of undesirable, and then the third term says that one will carry out kainkaryam (*nārāyanāya*) which is getting the desirable). Here, the term *tuyar* refers to the transposition of *rakśya-rakśaka bhāvam* \[normally, emperumān is the protector and we, the jīvātmās, are the protected\] which is a prerequisite for carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam \[we consider ourselves as the protector and emperumān as the protected and wish well for him\]. When the transposition of the protector-protected roles takes place, there will be no sorrow. In the term in [tiruppallāṇḍu 3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-3-vazhatpattu/) “*paḻippilōm*” (We do not have any fault), *paḻippu* refers to this protector-protected role only \[āḻvār says that for seven generations in their clan, they have always considered emperumān as the protected and themselves as the protectors and do not have the fault of thinking on the contrary\]. It is only when we attain this status that we will truly know the meanings of *anyaśēśatvam* \[being a servitor to someone other than emperumān\] and *svasvātantryam* \[being dependent on oneself\].

We shall next consider the pravēśam of the next tirumoḻi.

## 3.8.1. Nallador tamarai

*nalladōr tāmaraip poygai nāṇmalar mēl pani sōraalliyum tādum udirndittu aḻagu aḻindāl ottadālōillam veṟiyōdiṟṟālō en magaḷai engum kāṇēnmallarai attavan pin pōy maduraip puṟam pukkāḷ kolō*

**Пословный перевод:**

nalladu – being beautiful; ōr – being unique; tāmaraip poygai – lotus pond; nāḷ – just then blossomed; malar mēl – on the flower; pani – dew, which is an inimical entity for that flower; sōra – as it condenses; alliyum – inner petals; tādum – and pollens; udirndittu – as they fall; aḻagu aḻindāl ottadu – just as the beauty of the pond gets destroyed; illam – house; veṟiyōdiṟṟu – has become empty; en magaḷai – my daughter; engum – in any place; kāṇēn – I am not seeing; mallarai – cāṇūra, muśtika \[wrestlers\]; attavan pin pōy – going behind the one who annihilated them; maduraip puṟam – to āyppādi, which is close to maturā; pukkāḷ kol O! – Have they entered! She is suspecting

**Перевод:**

**In a pond, which is beautiful and unique, with plenty of lotus flowers, when dew condenses, the inner petals and pollens from the flowers fall off, destroying the beauty of the pond. The house has become empty. I am unable to see my daughter in any of the places. Has she gone behind the one who had annihilated wrestlers such as muśtika and cāṇūra and entered tiruvāyppādi, which is close to maturā!**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that this pāsuram recounts the sadness of the mother, not finding her daughter in the bed.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**nalladōr tāmaraip poygai** – the pond looked beautiful and unique since lotus flowers had blossomed throughout the entire area of the pond.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that abundance of water and fertile soil are the eminence for a pond. It is because of such a pond that the lotus flower had got distinction. The word *ōr* \[as in *nalladōr*\] indicates absence of any metaphor for the pond.

**nāṇmalar mēl pani sōra** – while the lotus has qualities such as “ṟeddiśness, blossomed, freshness, coolness, fragrance and tenderness”, dew, which is of an inimical nature to lotus flower, was condensing in large quantity.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as the lotus flower has qualities of freshness, coolness, tenderness etc, her daughter too had qualities of birth in a good clan, good conduct etc, having been born to her. Now, with her leaving, the house looks totally empty. Is the pond, which is devoid of lotus, a metaphor for her house? Though the pond has lost its beauty since the lotus has lost its inner petals and pollens and has withered, this is a temporary phenomenon since the lotus will bloom again, as long as the reason for its existence \[pond\] remains. The mother says that this is not the case for her or for her house. Once rājariśi became brahmariśi, his quality of being a warrior did not follow him \[reference here is to sage viśvāmitra, who became *brahmariśi* (a supreme sage) from the status of *rājariśi* (a lower grade among the sages, referring to sages coming from regal background)\]. The divine daughter of janaka maharāja \[sītāp pirātti\] too did not think of śrī mitilā \[the town of mitilā, where she had spent her early years\] after leaving it \[the mother is quoting these examples to show that her daughter too would not return to her house\]. Thus, the usage of the term *ālō* \[as in *illam veṟiyōdiṟṟālō*\] signifies absence of any metaphor and the impossibility of her daughter coming back.

**alli …** – due to that, the inner petals and pollens lost their freshness and started withering. Since the flowers, which were a decoration to the pond, got destroyed, the pond lost its beauty. While dew helps most of the botanical entities, it has a nature of being inimical to lotus flower alone. The house has become just like the lotus flower which had been affected by dew. The syllables *Al* and *O* \[as in *aḻagu aḻindāl ottadālō*\] reflect the excessive sadness in the mother.

**illam veṟiyōdiṟṟālō** – house has become empty. It says that the house has become empty without anyone roaming around, inside. Only this girl was roaming around inside the house earlier. Even if others had been present, if this girl had left, it would appear to the mother that the house has become empty. She says *ālō* again, due to overflowing sadness.

**en magaḷai engum kāṇēn** – I am unable to see my daughter anywhere. It is not only inside the house, the mother has searched in all the places where the daughter used to go to, earlier and says that she is unable to see her anywhere.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that though the daughter has left, emphasising that “She is not my daughter”, the mother still looks for “My daughter”, everywhere. Even after not seeing her anywhere, even when she searches in the houses of others, she looks for “My daughter”, just like looking for her in her house. Despite tracking her movements, she did not see her daughter anywhere. When those, of whom she had enquired about the whereabouts of her daughter, responded in the negative, she became deeply saddened. Yet, due to her fickle-mindedness, due to the fact that she was born to her, due to her daughter’s natural quality \[of being a lady\], due to the mischief of gōvindan \[kriṣṇa, who tends to cattle\], due to his ability of annihilating his enemies as a measure of protecting his followers, just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 3.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2022/09/periya-thirumozhi-3-7-1/) “*aṇiyāli puguvar kolō*” (Will they enter the town, tiruvāli, which is like an ornament for earth?), the mother asks “Has she entered the vicinity of maturā, following him, who had annihilated wrestlers?”*puṟam* – tiruvāyppādi. Since the two of them are deeply infatuated with each other, they could even enter the town of kamsan, maturā. Alternatively, it could be said that the mother is suspecting whether “She has entered tiruvāyppādi, which is hers”. Though the wrestlers had been killed, kamsan had been destroyed, ugrasēna had been coronated as the king of maturā and the people of that place have become favourable towards kriṣṇa, āḻvār is still scared of maturā, due to the fear that in that place, even a corpse could get up and walk.

He says at the end, the following: Through this \[narrative\], it appears that an ācāryan, from whose residence a disciple has gone on his own \[in search of emperumān\], going past his *hita vacanam* \[instructions which bear good for the disciple\] due to cool and comforting words of emperumān, equates his residence to the pond. If a disciple leaves the divine abode of an ācāryan, the dwelling place for the disciple will be other abodes of emperumān, including śrī vaikuṇṭam. Similar to that, the mother too has got to search for her daughter in various places, including others’ residences and has to say that she is nowhere to be seen. However, the place to attain for the daughter is only the noble abode of gōvindan. His wish will be fulfilled only in his favourite abode of tiruvāyppādi. For the disciples of the ācāryan, who were separated from their apt residence of ācāryan’s dwelling place, and who were taken by emperumān, as well as for emperumān, the boundary is that only \[place to reside is emperumān’s noble abodes\]. Just as parānguśa nāyaki’s mother determined the place where her daughter has entered, as in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/03/thiruvaimozhi-6-7-1-unnum-soru/) “*pugum Ur*” (the place which she entered) through various guesses and suspicions, this mother too determined the destination for her daughter. When the explicit is supported by logical thinking, guess would also be supported by logical thinking.

**mallarai …** – since the mother did not find the daughter here, she concluded firmly that “He has taken her with him”. She wonders whether the daughter has gone behind the one who had annihilated the wrestlers and entered the vicinity of maturā. Vicinity of matuṟa refers to tiruvāyppādi \[śrī gōkulam\] which is next to maturā. The query “*maduraip puṟam pukkāḷ kolō*” is similar to tirumangai āḻvār saying in [periya tirumoḻi 3.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2022/09/periya-thirumozhi-3-7-1/) “*aṇiyāli puguvar kolō*” \[parakāla nāyaki’s mother wonders whether her daughter and emperumān would have entered tiruvāli\]. In other words, since the two of them \[her daughter and kriṣṇa\] are highly infatuated with each other, it is possible that they would have even entered maturā, ruled by kamsan. Instead of doing that, the mother is wondering whether her daughter has entered tiruvāyppādi.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.8.2. Onrum arivu

*onṟum aṟivu onṟu illāda uruvaṟaik kōpālar tangaḷkanṟu kāl māṟumā pōlē kanni irundāḷaik koṇḍunanṟum kiṟi seydu pōnān nārāyaṇan seyda tīmaienṟum emargaḷ kudikku ōr ēccuk kol āyidum kolō*

**Пословный перевод:**

onṟu – apt; aṟivu – knowledge; onṟum – even a little bit; illāda – being without; uru aṟai – being without good features; gōpālar tāngaḷ – herd-people; kanṟu kāl māṟumā pōlē – just as stealing calves which are good to look at, without the; kanni – girl; irundāḷaiī – my daughter, who was under my control; nanṟum – to a great extent; kiṟi seydu – realising his aim, through contrivance; koṇḍu pōnān – one, who took her; nārāyaṇan – one, who is known as nārāyaṇan; seyda – carried out; tīmai – mischief; emargaḷ kudikku – for our clan; enṟum – forever; ōr ēccu āyidum kol O – she is asking whether it would become a fault or a good quality

**Перевод:**

**Herd-people, who are without even a little of apt knowledge, and who do not have good looks, steal calves which are good to look at, without the owners of the calves knowing about their act. In a similar way, one, who is known as nārāyaṇan, spoke deceptive words to my daughter, who was under my control, and took her away. Will this deceptive act lead to fault for our clan or will it be considered as a good quality?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the mother is wondering whether the daughter leaving the house is a fault or a good quality.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**onṟum aṟivu onṟu illāda** – without having apt knowledge. Without having even a little bit of knowledge on *laukika* or *vaidika* (knowledge for living a life in samsāram (materialistic realm) or knowledge about vēdams). They are referred to, as in [tiruppāvai 28](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/01/thiruppavai-28-karavaigal-pin-chenru/) “*aṟivonṟum illāda āykkulam*” (we are from the covherd clan, without any *jñānam*, knowledge). When they enter forest for grazing their cattle, and if they lose their way, it is only the cattle which will show them the way to get back home. They have only that much knowledge.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, additionally says here that the herd-people do not have any knowledge about their *dēham* or *ātmā* \[about their physical forms or about their souls\]. When they eat food from their vessels and take water from freshly poured rains, due to their arrogance, when they assemble together in large numbers, they will say about kamsan, who has won over indra, “Who will be a citizen under him? Let us pull him down with the sticks which we have for controlling cows and kill him”. This reflects the strength in their hearts, when they do not have any knowledge about their abilities.

**uruvaṟaik kōpālar** – herd-people, who do not have good looks. Just as they do not have qualities of *ātmā* \[qualities of the soul such as being a servitor to emperumān, being totally dependent on him etc\], they do not have qualities of good looks too.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as they do not bother about sharpening their knowledge, they do not remove dirt too, from their physical forms. *gōpālar* – those who protect cattle; or, those who are protected by their cattle.

**tangaḷ** – the word, *tāngaḷ* has got shortened as *tangaḷ*. The word should be *gōbālar tāngaḷ* – when reference is made to the lack of apt knowledge and good looks, it follows as a corollary that their activities too would be wicked. Their wicket act is mentioned next.

**kanṟu kāl māṟumā pōlē** – this act refers to their fobbing off their calves, which do not look healthy, as someone else’s calves and taking healthy calves of others as their calves. Alternatively, this could also refer to their stealing the healthy-looking calves of others, without the knowledge of the owner of the calves. Of these two, it is the latter which is apt here \[reference is to kriṣṇa stealing the daughter of the mother, without the knowledge of the mother\]. Just as these herd-people indulge in such acts …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that while their calves will indulge in activities without knowing the result, they will keep their front legs behind and hind legs in the front and walk, as if walking on two feet. The  herd-men will protect their calves such that they do not step outside their protective places. In the same way, my daughter was protected, without stepping out of the house. But, kriṣṇa, showed his eminence to her and took her with him.

**kanni irundāḷai-nanṟum kiṟi seydu-koṇḍu-pōnān** – my daughter was a young, nubile girl, who did not know about the pleasures of worldly pursuits, and was under my control. He \[kriṣṇa\] took her under his control by manifesting his identifications, and, unknown to me, took her with him, in a contrived manner.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here for *nanṟum* … – carrying out deceptive deeds, utilising that as his nourishment, he took her with him. ūtilising sweet words etc, he made her to follow his steps. Alternatively, getting rid of unhealthy calves, just as the herd-people take away healthy calves which have long legs, gait like peacock, beauty of shining from a good clan etc, kriṣṇa too discarded girls who he had desired in the past, as unhealthy calves, and took my daughter, as a beautiful calf.

**nārāyaṇan seyda tīmai** – his name suggests that he is the repository of all the auspicious qualities. He is expected to carry out only beneficial acts, but he is indulging in deceptive acts, like this! The deception here is – while taking away an entity who is his possession, he could have done that publicly, known to all, instead of stealing her like this.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that while the term nārāyaṇan signifies one with all the auspicious qualities, the mother speaks as if the medicine is useless \[when one is not well, medicine is given to the person; but, the person rejects the medicine as being useless\].

**enṟum …** – will this deceptive act of his remain as a calumny on our clan forever? ōr else, instead of taking her, known to all, through the act of marriage, will his act of covertly taking her with him lead to a word of appreciation for this clan? Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.7.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/03/thiruvaimozhi-6-7-4-kollai-enbarkolo/) “*kollai enbargaḷō guṇam mikkanaḷ enbargolō*” (will the people of the town condemn my daughter for crossing all limits or will they praise her, saying that she has great qualities?), the mother is asking whether this deed would bring her clan slander or praise.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says at the end that this pāsuram reflects the state of an ācāryan, who recounts the way that *īśvaran* \[emperumān\] had taken one of his disciples, who was totally dependent on him, and how the ācāryan feels sad about this.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.8.3. Kumari manam

*kumari maṇam seydu koṇḍu kōlam seydu illattu iruttitamarum piṟarum aṟiyat tāmōdaraṟku enṟu sāṟṟiamarar padi udait tēvi arasāṇiyai vaḻipattutumilam eḻap paṟai kottit tōraṇam nāttidum kolō*

**Пословный перевод:**

kumari – maiden; maṇam seydu koṇḍu – carrying out functions prior to marriage; kōlam seydu – decorating with dress and ornaments; illattu – in the place where the marriage is held; irutti – making her to stay; tamarum – relatives; piṟarum – others too; aṟiya – such that they know; dāmōdaraṟku – for kaṇṇan, who is dāmōdaran; enṟu – saying “we are going to give her in marriage”; sāṟṟi – announcing, through beating of drums; amarar padi udai – dēvādirājan’s \[the king of all celestial entities, his\]; dēvi – she, who is his consort; arasāṇiyai – branch of peepal tree; vaḻippattu – circumambulating \[as per the customs of their clan\]; tumilam eḻa – in a boisterous manner; paṟai kotti – beating drums; tōraṇam – great arches etc; nāttidum kol O – will they decorate throughout the place and celebrate? ōr, will they say “Why celebrate to this extent”? She \[the mother\] suspects

**Перевод:**

**They \[the relatives of kriṣṇa\] will carry out functions before the marriage. They will decorate her \[daughter of the mother who is reciting this pāsuram\] with dress and ornaments, keep her inside the place where the marriage is held. They will announce to the relatives and others, by beating drums, that they are going to give her \[the daughter\], in marriage, to dāmōdaran. She, who is the consort of the king of all the celestial entities, will circumambulate a branch of peepal tree, in line with the customs of their clan. Will they beat drums in a boisterous manner and erect decorative arches throughout the town or will they say “Why celebrate to this extent?” wonders the mother.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the mother says that she does not know as to what her daughter did, at the place where she had gone \[along with kriṣṇa\].*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kumari maṇam seydu koṇḍu** – *kumari* – a maiden. Carrying out functions while in the state of a maiden. In other words, as a prelude to marriage, functions which are held.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that in line with the practice of their clan, they will decorate her with sandalwood paste and other fragrant materials, as well as with flowers etc. They will further decorate her with gold, gemstones, dresses etc.

**kōlam seydu** – Decorating with ornaments, dresses, sandalwood paste etc.

**illattu irutti** – keeping in the place where marriage is conducted.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai adds here that they will keep her inside the place where the marriage is held, not indulging in mischievous acts.

**tamarum …** – Making it known to relatives and others, by proclaiming publicly “We are going to offer her in marriage to dāmōdaran”. The term *dāmōdaran* signifies his simplicity such that he did not have the strength to get out of the binding which his mother \[yaśōdāp pirātti\] carried out on him and his being under her control.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that only undesirable activities are carried out without any publicity.  *dāmōdaraṟku* – kriṣṇa remained as one without any strength, when his mother, who did not have any strength, and whose word he wished to follow, tied him up with a rope and told him, as in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5.6.15 “*yadiśaknōśi*” (If you have the strength to come out of this binding). It was made known to all that she was going to be given in marriage to one with such auspicious qualities. If this had been done with one who is in śrī vaikuṇṭam, it would not have appeared as this eminent.

**amarar padi udait tēvi** – when taking a pledge that she is \[going to be the consort\] for the head of nityasūris and making an announcement about it, she became the consort of one, who is the controller of nityasūris, who do not have any ennui.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the consort of indra \[head of celestial entities\] is not vorśipped through the logic of “*sēndra*:” \[this has been taken from vēdam where emperumān is explained as the indvelling soul of all entities, including brahmā, Siva, indra and all the other entities\]. This girl \[the daughter of the mother, who is reciting this pāsuram\] is the consort of one who is the indra for all the indra \[the term indra refers to one who has wealth\], who is the controller of nityasūris and who is the consort of śrī mahālakśmi. She has the identification of being the consort of viṣṇu, as mentioned in śrī sūktam as “*viṣṇu patni*” (the consort of viṣṇu) and as in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 1.8.15 as “*anapāyini*” (one who does not ever separate from viṣṇu). She has emperumān as her identity. Her existence is derived from him. She identifies emperumān to the world. She is termed as “*un tiru*” (wealth for emperumān). She manifests his nature to the world. He is the *śēśi* (lord of all). That nature comes from the fourth case *āya* seen in the first syllable “*a*” of praṇavam, in tirumantram. This requires two entities, one in whom the quality of servitude will be present, namely the jīvātmā, and the one who receives servitude, namely emperumān. Thus, *śēśi* is the one who is identified here. a*marar padi udait tēvi* – śrī mahālakśimi is identified as *perundēvi* \[the senior consort\] while this girl \[the daughter\] is identified as “*en siṟut tēvi*” \[the little consort\]. Hence, the little consort has to worship the senior consort.

**arasāṇiyai vaḻippattu** – in line with the customs of their clan, circumambulating a branch of peepal tree, which has been placed as a pillar on the decorated dais. *arasāṇi* – branch of peepal tree, placed on the decorated dais.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *arasāṇi* refers to *ammi* \[a flat slab or stone for grinding materials\]. Just as it has been mentioned in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 6.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/08/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-6-8/) “*ammi midikka*” (he made me to step on the slab), worship is carried out by stepping on, here. The term *arasāṇi* is a modification of the term *arasāṇai*, which is the grinding slab \[the syllable *ai* in *arasāṇai* has got modified as *i*, as in arasāṇi\]. Since nitya vibhūti \[śrī vaikuṇṭam\] belongs to śrī mahālakśmi, and since the little consort has vorśipped the senior consort, the little consort could be referred to as *amarar padi udait tēvi*.

**tumilam eḻap paṟai kotti** – playing on the musical instrument to create a boisterous noise. This is similar to [nācciyār tirumoḻi 6.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/08/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-6-6/) “*mattaḷam kotta*” (Even as the percussion instruments were being played…).

**tōraṇam nāttidum kolō** – will they celebrate the marriage by erecting arches throughout the place, as decorations? ōr, will they say, as people who live their lives by borrowing money from others “What is the need for such grand celebrations for a marriage?”

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother is wondering whether the people will celebrate the marriage by erecting arches in all the streets of tiruvāyppādi, which houses five lakh families and in the intersections of the streets or whether the people, who are not that well-to-do will question the need for a grand celebration. He says at the end that this pāsuram expresses the worry and sadness experienced by the ācāryan \[mother\], from whom emperumān has taken the disciple \[daughter\] who was existing for the ācāryan all along, as to what the disciple is doing at emperumān’s place and as to how he is conducting himself.

We shall next consider the 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan
