## 3.8.4. Orumagal tannai

*oru magaḷ tannai udaiyēn ulagam niṟainda pugaḻāltirumagaḷ pōla vaḷarttēn sengaṇ māl tān koṇḍu pōnānperu magaḷāyk kudi vāḻndu perum piḷḷai peṟṟa asōdaimarumagaḷaik kaṇḍu ugandu maṇāttuppuṟam seyyum kolō*

**Пословный перевод:**

oru magaḷ tannai – only one girl; udaiyēn – I, who have; ulagam niṟainda – spread throughout the world; pugaḻāl – with fame; tirumagaḷ pōla – like śrī mahālakśmi; vaḷarttēn – nurtured, affectionately; sem kaṇ – having reddish eyes; māl – kaṇṇan \[kriṣṇa\], who has infatuation; tān – himself; koṇḍu pōnān – took her away; peru magaḷāy – as a distinguished lady; kudi vāḻndu – leading a familial life; peru piḷḷai – son, who is eminent; peṟṟa – one who begot; asōdai – yaśōdāp pirātti; marumagaḷaik kaṇḍu – looking at her daughter-in-law; ugandu – feeling affectionate; maṇāttuppuṟam – to be carried out for the daughter-in-law; seyyum kol O – will she carry out the activities? ōr, will she carry out whatever has to be carried out for life here, in a perfunctory manner?

**Перевод:**

**I, who have only one daughter, nurtured her affectionately, with her fame spreading throughout the world, like śrī mahālakśmi. kriṣṇa, who has reddish eyes and infatuation towards her, my daughter, took her away \[from me\], himself. Will yaśōdāp pirātti, who is leading a familial life as a distinguished lady, and who has sired an eminent son, feel happy with her daughter-in-law and carry out activities towards her, apt for her daughter-in-law or will she carry out perfunctory duties, in line with life on this earth?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**oru magaḷ tannai udaiyēn** – I have a daughter, who is unique. The term *oru magal* denotes a single daughter, the word *tannai* – denotes her eminence on account of her beauty etc, and the term *udaiyēn* denotes the eminence which the mother has, on account of having her as her daughter.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that the mother recounts the eminent manner in which she brought up her daughter. She says “My daughter is without any equivalent”. Through the word “*tannai*” she says that just as it has been mentioned of vēdavyāsa as *śukhatātam* \[father of sage *śukha*\], apart from the clan in which the daughter was born, due to the completeness of qualities of the daughter, such as beauty etc, she \[mother\] became eminent.

**ulagam niṟainda pugaḻāl** – the daughter had such a fame that all the people in the world, without any difference with regard to having significant knowledge or without any knowledge, praised her. recalling her qualities, from their respective place.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that starting with the controller of a little village and going beyond the controller of all the creations, just as she is called, as in śrī sūktam “*sarvabhūtānām īśvari*” (controller of all the entities), she has eminence beyond the nityasūris. The daughter is like śrī mahālakśmi, who has the pride of being the one who gives eminence to emperumān, as mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.6.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-6-parivathil/) “*tirumagaḷār tanikkēḷvan*” (emperumān has the eminence of the being the beloved consort of śrī mahālakśmi, who is the best among women). Since there is no metaphor to be compared for one beyond śrī mahālakśmi, the mother says that she brought up her daughter like śrī mahālakśmi. However, śrī mahālakśmi has shortcoming by way of her clan, whether it be samudram (tiruppāṟkadal, or milky ocean) \[since ocean did not immediately give way to śrī rāma when he surrendered to it, the king of oceans is not considered as eminent\] or king janaka \[when sītāp pirātti underwent all the tribulations, there was no help from king janaka; hence he too is not considered as eminent\]. The mother, hence, says “*oru magaḷ*”.

**tirumagaḷ pōla vaḷarttēn** – I nurtured my daughter such that she has equivalence with śrī mahālakśmi, who is held as an example for distinction for all, who has the quality of *puruśakāram* (recommendatory role, for acceptance of jīvātmās, with emperumān), who is the most distinguished among all women, and who is mentioned, as in [periya tirumoḻi 3.7.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2022/10/periya-thirumozhi-3-7-9/), as “*kadi māmalarp pāvai oppāḷ*” (one who matches śrī mahālakśmi, who resides on a very fragrant lotus flower).

**sengaṇmāl tān koṇḍu pōnān** – emperumān has naturally reddish eyes, as mentioned in cāndōjña upanishad 1.6.7 “*yatā kapyāsam puṇḍarīkam*” (\[emperumān’s divine eyes have\] the colour, which a blossomed lotus flower has, in the morning, under sunlight). On top of that, since he keeps looking at her \[the daughter\] constantly, without looking at any other entity, with infatuation, the divine eyes have become even more reddish. He has this infatuation as an identity for him. Instead of sending any messenger such as *ātivāhikar* \[eminent entities who reside in vidyut lōkam, the land of lightning and who guide muktātmās who proceed towards śrī vaikuṇṭam, by helping them to cross river virajā\] or *periya tiruvadi* \[garuda, emperumān’s vehicle\], he came himself to take my daughter with him, as mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 3.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2022/09/periya-thirumozhi-3-7-1/) “*kaḷvan kol*” (Is he a thief?) An incident is narrated here by the vyākyātā of this prabandam, maṇavāḷa māmunigaḷ: when āḻvān \[kūrattāḻvān\] attained śrī vaikuṇṭam, unable to bear the separation, udaiyavar \[rāmānujar\] famously said “*oru magaḷ tannai udaiyēn*”, “*ulagam niṟainda pugaḻāl tirumagaḷ pōla vaḷarttēn*”, “*sengaṇ māl tān koṇḍu pōnān*” \[same lines which are in this pāsuram\]. śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 1.15.156 says “*upamānam aśēśāṇām sādūnām yassadābhavat*” (he sired prahlādan, who was the metaphor always for all the wise people). Since kūrattāḻvān was held as the metaphor for all wise people in the world, it was his fame which had spread throughout the world.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai adds further to the above-mentioned narration explained by maṇavāḷa māmunigaḷ. He quotes a few pāsurams from the divine works of āḻvārs to show that it was kūrattāḻvān who had a fame which had spread throughout the world. The pāsurams quoted are: (1) [tirumālai 43](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/12/thirumalai-43/) “*sādi andaṇargaḷēlum*” (even if it is a highly informed brāhmaṇa, if he indulges in despising the followers of emperumān, such a person would be considered as lowly) \[kūrattāḻvān corrected one of his disciples, piḷḷaip piḷḷai āḻvān and made him to stop denigrating śrīvaiṣṇavas\]; (2) [tirumālai 7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thirumalai-7/) “*kalaiyaṟakkaṟṟa māndar*” (those who had learnt the deeper meanings of vēdams and other sacred texts) \[kūrattāḻvān’s father, kūrattāḻvār, himself praised kūrattāḻvān as having learnt all the vēdams and sacred texts\]; (3) [tiruvāimoḻi 7.10.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/11/thiruvaimozhi-7-10-5-malaradip-podhugal/) “*palar adiyār munbu aruḷiya pāmbaṇaip paḷḷiyappan*” (one, who is reclining on ādiśēśan, who showered his grace on me, in the presence of great followers) \[this incident is about periya nambi, the ācāryan of rāmānujar, who chose kūrattāḻvān, as the one without any ahankāram or mamakāram (ego and possessiveness), ahead of all the others, for carrying out a specific task\]; (4) [irāmānusa nūṟṟandādi 7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/ramanusa-nurranthadhi-7/) “*moḻiyaik kadakkum perum pugaḻān*” (one who has eminence which is beyond words, viz. indescribable) \[kūrattāḻvān had such eminence that it cannot be described through one’s words\], and (5) “*oṟppāl karuduvar*” (people will analyse the supremely auspicious qualities of kūrattāḻvān and consider him as befitting all the praise\]. Thus, it is only kūrattāḻvān who has fame which had spread throughout the world. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai further says that the term *lōkam* is synonymous with *śāstram*. Thus, kūrattāḻvān’s fame is widely spoken of by śāstram too.

**perumagaḷāyk kudi vāḻndu** – living a life as a distinguished lady, in the house. śrī nandagōpar is the controller of the five lakh families in tiruvāyppādi. Since she is his consort, she is referred to as *perumagaḷ* – distinguished lady. Just as he administers the town with affection, she administers the house, with affection. Hence, she is referred to as “*kudi vāḻndu*” \[living in the house\].

**perum piḷḷai peṟṟa asōdai** – one who gave birth to an eminent son. Since kriṣṇa is fully complete with *rūpaguṇam* \[qualities of his divine form\] and *ātmaguṇam* \[qualities of his divine soul\], and since he has made people say of his mother “*enna nōnbu nōṟṟāḷ kolō ivanaip peṟṟa vayiṟu udaiyāḷ*” (What penance did the one, who gave birth to him, carry out?) he is referred to as *perum piḷḷai*, eminent son. She is a distinguished lady; the one, who she gave birth to, is also a distinguished son.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai adds here that yaśōdāp pirātti became eminent only after giving birth to kriṣṇa.

**marumagaḷaik kaṇḍu ugandu** – being affectionate, after seeing her daughter-in-law. Even though the mother is sad that “He had taken her away” \[about her daughter\], since she has to identify her \[daughter\] with a relationship in the place where she has gone, she refers to her as \[yaśōdāp piātti’s\] daughter-in-law.

**kaṇḍu ugandu** – Looking at the qualities of beauty etc of her daughter and infatuation \[with kriṣṇa\], yaśōdāp pirātti should keep her daughter-in-law on her lap and feel happy, thinking “We have been fortunate to get such a person”.

**maṇāttuppuṟam seyyum kolō** – Will she carry out all the eminent activities with her, considering her as her daughter-in-law or will she do, without her heart in it, considering her to be one who “came on her own” in a perfunctory manner?

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother is wondering whether yaśōdāp pirātti will consider her daughter-in-law as an eminent person and decorate her with flowers, dresses etc, in a wholehearted manner, in line with the appropriate methods of her clan.

He says at the end that through this pāsuram, even if emperumān takes away the ācāryan’s disciple \[here, mother is ācāryan and daughter is disciple\] who is obedient and unique, the ācāryan will forget about his loss and consider emperumān’s benefit and loss, as his \[ācāryan’s\] benefit and loss. It is also apparent in this pāsuram that if the disciple leaves for śrī vaikuṇṭam, the divine consorts of emperumān and eminent women there will accept the disciple.

We shall next consider the 5<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.8.5. Tan maman

*tammāman nandagōpālan taḻeeikkoṇḍu en magaḷ tannaisemmāndirē enṟu sollic ceḻum kayal kaṇṇum sevvāyumkommai mulaiyum idaiyum koḻum paṇait tōḷgaḷum kaṇḍittuimmagaḷaip peṟṟa tāyar init tariyār ennum kolō*

**Пословный перевод:**

than – for the girl; māman – one, who is the father-in-law; nanda gōpālan – nandagōpar; en magaḷ tannai – my daughter; taḻeeik koṇḍu – hugging her and keeping her on his lap; semmāndu iru enṟu – saying “Sit straight”; seḻu – cheerful; kayal – like fish; kaṇṇum – eyes; sem – being reddish; vāyum – lips; kommai – well grown; mulaiyum – bosoms; idaiyum – waist; koḻu – flourishing; paṇai – like bamboo; tōḷgaḷum – shoulders; kaṇḍittu – looking \[at the limbs\] individually; i magaḷai – “this girl; peṟṟa tāyar – the mother, who gave birth to; ini – after separating from her; tariyār – will not sustain herself”; ennum kol O – would he say so or would he be without registering any change? The mother wonders

**Перевод:**

**nandagōpar, who is the father-in-law of this girl, would hug and keep my daughter on his lap. He would tell her “Sit straight”. He would look at her cheerful eyes, which are like fish, at her reddish lips, at her well grown bosoms, at her shoulders which are like flourishing bamboo. Looking at these limbs, separately, would he say “The mother, who gave birth to this girl, will not sustain herself, in separation from her” or would he remain without showing any change in his countenance?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the mother is wondering whether śrī nandagōpar will feel in his heart about her \[the mother’s\] loss.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tam māman nandagōpālan** – śrī nandagōpar, who is the father-in-law of the girl

**taḻeeik koṇḍu en magaḷ tannai** – manifesting that she is his “daughter-in-law”, hugging her and keeping her on his lap.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother says “*en magaḷ tannai*” \[my daughter\] only after saying “*tam māman”* \[her father-in-law\]. Going by the relationships seen in the world, only the relationship “*tam māman*” will sustain over a period of time. Since the mother has said “*en magaḷ*”, after that, it appears that only this will sustain, here. This is similar to [tirumālai 38](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/12/thirumalai-38-part-1/) “*meymmaiyai uṇarndu*” and “*meymmaiyai miga uṇarndu*” (meymmaiyai uṇarndu refers to the ātmā knowing that it is subservient to emperumān; meymmaiyai miga uṇarndu refers to the ātmā knowing that it is subservient to the followers of emperumān).

**semmāndirē enṟu solli** – while the girl put her head down, out of shyness, he told her to look up. *semmāppu* – to be with pride. Since he wanted to see her limbs such as her face etc and to see her overall looks, he tells her to sit erect.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when it is looked for the sake of others, for every limb or person, similes will also be thought of \[reference here is to śrī nandagōpar looking at each limb of his daughter-in-law and confirming that she is apt for emperumān\].

**seḻum kayal kaṇṇum** – beautiful eyes, which appear like fish.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the two eyes seem to be those of a fish which fight with each other, in a clear pond

**sevvāyum** – lips, which are naturally reddish

**kommai mulaiyum** – round bosoms which are larger than those which would befit her age. *kommai* – round

**idaiyum** – waist, which has grown thin and tight, due to the growth of the bosoms

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the waist does not have a metaphor.

**koḻum paṇait tōḷgaḷum** – her shoulders appear like a well-grown bamboo, due to their roundness, freshness and length; *koḻumai* – beauty and prideful.

**kaṇḍittu** – looking at the beauty of the individual limbs and at the overall form, thinking of her \[the mother’s loss\]

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that śrī nandagōpar saw all these limbs. *ittu* – her loss appeared in his mind, then.

**immagaḷai …** – Will he say that the mother, who had given birth to this girl, would not be able to live, after separating from her? ōr, would he remain without showing any change in his countenance?

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that śrī nandagōpar is thinking whether the mother, who gave birth to this, would be alive or whether she would feel joyous, knowing the benefits, which the daughter has got in his place.

In the end, tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says the following: \[here, the features of the daughter’s limbs are matched with corresponding features of the disciple of an ācāryan\] Looking at the knowledge of the disciple regarding emperumān \[corresponding to the eyes of the girl\], the ability to speak sweetly \[lips\], devotion towards emperumān \[bosoms\], detachment towards matters other than emperumān \[waist\] and feeling happy when others are flourishing \[shoulders\], emperumān, who is mentioned in cāndōjña upaniśad as *avākyanādara*: (one does not speak to anyone and who does not support anyone, in śrī vaikuṇṭam) recalls the benefits and losses of the ācāryan, who had sent the disciple to him \[similar to śrī nandagōpar wondering about the ability of the mother to sustain herself in separation from her daughter\] and how this \[praising of emperumān about the disciple\] was celebrated by viśvaksēnar et al. This is similar to our ācāryars praising tiruvadi \[hanuman\] based on the praising of hanuman by śrī rāma.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.8.6. Vedar marakkulam

*vēdar maṟakkulam pōlē vēṇḍiṟṟuc ceydu en magaḷaikūdiya kūttamēyāgak koṇḍu kudi vāḻum kolōnādu nagaramum nangu aṟiya nalladu ōr kaṇṇālam seydusādiṟap pāynda perumān takkavā kaippaṟṟum kolō*

**Пословный перевод:**

vēdar – people belonging to hunter tribe, who are lowly; maṟakkulam pōlē – people who belong to the clan of warriors; en magaḷai – my daughter; vēṇḍiṟṟu seydu – doing, the way that they desire; kūdiya kūttamē āgak koṇḍu – considering that the way the boy and the girl united is marriage; kudi vāḻum kolō – will they live their lives!; sādu – śakatam (wheel, in which a monster had pervaded); iṟa – such that it snapped; pāynda – one, who kicked; perumān – one, who is the lord; nādum – those lacking in knowledge; nagarum – those who are knowledgeable; aṟiya – such that they know; nalladu – distinguished; ōr – without any match; kaṇṇālam seydu – conducting the marriage; takka A – appropriate to the conduct of their clan; kaippaṟṟum kol O – will he hold her hand and marry her! The mother has a doubt

**Перевод:**

**People in the clan of tribal people, who are lowly, and people in the clan of warriors, would behave the way that they desire. In line with that, considering the union between the boy and the girl as marriage having been conducted, will they live their lives? ōr, will the lord, who kicked the śakatam (wheel) to make it break into smithereens, hold her hand, such that all the people, those with knowledge and those without knowledge come to know of it and marry her in a unique manner?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the mother expresses her doubt as to what the one, who has the pride of annihilating the monster śakatāsuran, will do.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**vēdar maṟakkulam pōlē** – the lowly clans such as hunter tribes and warriors. These are differences in the clans.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *vēdar* are those who inhabit mountains and *maṟakkulam* refers to those who live in forests, on earth. They do, as they desire.

**vēṇḍiṟṟuc ceydu** – without considering the clan of the two sides \[the daughter’s and kriṣṇa’s\] without any consideration for śāstrams, carrying out what one desired.

**en magaḷai** – the girl, who was born to me, who hails from a faultless clan.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that without considering that she was born to me and without considering his clan \[of birth\]

**kūdiya kūttamēyāgak koṇḍu** – considering that the union between the two of them, with their hearts in unison, as marriage having been conducted.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother is wondering whether kriṣṇa, considering the union of their hearts as the end result, will engage in a life which is inappropriate for their clans. She has this doubt since she feels that he would be feeling proud, having annihilated śakatāsuran and that he would not give eminence to birth in respectful clans. Through this annihilation of his enemy, he had protected himself and his parents, who had left him in an unattended place, from blame.

**kudi vāḻum kolō** – will they lead a life together?

**sādiṟap pāynda perumān – nādu nagarum aṟiya nalladōr kaṇṇālam seydu – takkavā kaippaṟṟum kolō** – when kriṣṇa was alone, in a place, a monster had pervaded a wheel which was nearby. kriṣṇa was kicking his feet in hunger, since yaśōdāp pirātti had delayed in nursing him. The monster \[who came running, with the intention of killing him\] got caught between the kicking legs of kriṣṇa and was broken to smithereens. Will the one, who protected himself through that action and saved his mother from the blame of “She caused harm to her son, by leaving him unattended in a place”, marry her in a distinguished manner, with the knowledge of those who live in the rural places surrounding tiruvāyppādi and those who live in the town of tiruvāyppādi, who would say “This has never been seen before”, holding her, in-line with the customs of the clan?

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *nādu* refers to rural places surrounding tiruvāyppādi and *nagaram* refers to the town of tiruvāyppādi itself. Since śrī nandagōpar is the head of tiruvāyppādi, it could be considered as a town. For the verse *nalladōr kaṇṇālam seydu*, he says that all the identifications which have been mentioned for a marriage should be followed, being famous throughout the world. He says that the pāsuram should be transformed as given below, for getting sequential meaning: *sādiṟap pāynda perumān en magaḷai vēdar marākkulam pōlē vēṇḍiṟṟuc ceydu kūdiya kūttamēyāgak koṇḍu tagādavar kudi vāḻumō* ? *nādu nagaram aṟiya nalladōr kaṇṇālam seydu takkavāṟu kaippaṟṟum kolō*?

In the end, he says that the term *vēdar* refers to *dēhātmābhimāni* (those who consider their physical forms as ātmā), holding on to their forms alone and not knowing anything else \[about emperumān\] and the term *maṟakkulam* refers to *svasvātantryars* \[those who know the difference between physical form and ātmā, but who consider themselves to be fully independent\]. They will indulge in carrying out activities as they like since they go by the diktats of their forms.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.8.7. Andattu amarar

*aṇḍattu amarar perumān āḻiyān inṟu en magaḷaippaṇḍap paḻippukkaḷ sollip parisaṟa āṇḍidum kolōkoṇḍu kudi vāḻkkai vāḻndu kōvalap pattam kavittuppaṇḍai maṇāttimār munnē pādugāval vaikkum kolō*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṇḍattu – residents of paramapadam \[śrī vaikuṇṭam\]; amarar – for nityasūris; perumān – as their head; āḻiyān – one, who has the divine disc in his hand; en – my; magaḷai – daughter; inṟu – now; paṇḍam paḻippukkaḷ solli – finding fault with her (this refers to finding fault with her limbs on her form or her qualities); parisu aṟa – to remove eminence; āṇḍidum kolō – will he rule over her? (ōr); paṇḍai maṇāttimār munnē – in the presence of his earlier consorts, who had been given title; koṇḍu – taking her; kudi vāḻkkai vāḻndu – enabling her to arrange for carrying out household chores; kōvalar pattam kavittu – manifesting that she is his consort, by calling her “The leader of the clan of herd-women”; pādu kāval vaikkum kol O – will he keep her safely in his private quarters?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the lord of nityasūris, who reside in śrī vaikuṇṭam; he has the divine disc in his divine hand. Will he now find fault with her form or qualities and rule over her, without acknowledging her eminence? ōr, will he take her to his earlier consorts, to whom he has granted titles, enable her to get the household chores carried out, by giving her the title of “Head of the clan of herd-women”, and keep her safely in his private quarters?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**aṇḍattu amarar perumān āḻiyān** – he is the head of nityasūris, who do not have any contact with samsāram \[materialistic realm\], and who live in śrīvaikuṇṭam. He has the eminence of donning the divine disc on his divine hand, as a symbol of being sarvēśvaran \[controller of all entities\]. Due to the pride of that eminence …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that he incarnated \[during kriṣṇāvatāram\] with all his divine weapons, as mentioned in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.2.12 “*upasamhara*” \[to hide; when he was born to dēvakip pirātti, she saw him with all his divine weapons; she told him to hide the divine weapons\]. Even on the day that he incarnated, he had fulfilled her words.

**inṟu en magaḷaip paṇḍap paḻippukkaḷ solli** – my daughter is one who is endowed with all the auspicious identifications \[of an eminent person\]. Will he make remarks belittling her? In other words, will he point out to some imperfections in her form or in her qualities?

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother says that if kriṣṇa, who had listened to his mother on the day that he incarnated, fulfilling her wish, had listened to her \[the mother’s\] words too, when she is on a level with dēvakip pirātti in terms of auspicious qualities, this separation \[between her and her daughter\] vouldn’t have occurred. Would the one, who separated my daughter from me, give her eminence and rule over her, without blaming her for imperfections in her? Even if imperfections are pointed out, there are people who respect eminence and rule over them. *paṇḍap paḻippu* \[imperfection in an entity\], which is mentioned here, refers to finding faults in the limbs of a lady, arising out of not supporting the person. *parisu* refers to giving oneself fully to that lady. If both are avoided, there is no hurdle in ruling over a person.

**parisaṟa āṇḍidum kolō** – due to his unpleasant intelligence, will he rule over her, removing her eminence? In other words, instead of carrying out personal services through her, will he make her to carry out household chores?

**koṇḍu kudi vāḻkkai vāḻndu** – with her, carrying out the requirements of a married life; viz. through her control, carrying the household chores.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that this term refers to carrying out *pāṇigrahaṇam* \[holding the hand, an event which occurs during the marriage\] and living, appropriately for the clan, with her.

**kōvalap pattam kavittu** – giving her an eminent title, such as “Head of the clan of herd-women”, manifesting that she is his consort.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother desires that kriṣṇa make her daughter as the prominent consort, like nappinnaip pirātti.

**paṇḍai maṇāttimār munnē** – in the presence of his consorts, on whom he had already conferred titles.

**pādu kāval vaikkum kolō** – Will he keep her safely, in his *anta:puram* (private quarters)?

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother wonders whether he would, with desire, keep her safely in his private quarters. He says at the end that if emperumān separates a disciple from his ācāryan and takes the disciple to śrīvaikuṇṭam, just as this āḻvār is going to say further in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.9.3 “*ēṟṟi vaittu ēṇi vāngi*” (after remaining as the means for uplifting a jīvātmā from samsāram to śrī vaikuṇṭam \[who now becomes a muktātmā\] , emperumān changes his stance of being the means \[and takes on the role of being the lord who takes service from the muktātmā\]), even if the disciple were to pledge something to emperumān, he will not be allowed to return. This shows emperumān’s desire \[and that the mother will not get her daughter back\].

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.8.8. Kudiyil pirandavar

*kudiyil piṟandavar seyyum guṇam onṟum seydilan andōnadai onṟum seydilan nangāy! nandagōpan magan kaṇṇanidai irupālum vaṇanga iḷaittu iḷaittu en magaḷ ēngikadai kayiṟē paṟṟi vāngik kai taḻumbu ēṟidum kolō*

**Пословный перевод:**

nangāy – Oh, one who is complete with all the auspicious qualities!; nandagōpan – śrī nandagōpar’s; magan – divine son; kaṇṇan – kaṇṇan \[kriṣṇa\]; kudiyil – in an eminent clan; piṟandavar – those who are born; seyyum – carrying out activities, which are apt for their clan; guṇam – in the qualities \[activities\]; onṟum – even one; seydilan – has not done; nadai – in the activities conducted by the people of the world; onṟum – even a little bit; seydilan – has not carried out; andō – alas! (feeling sorrowful); idai – waist; iru pālum – both the sides; vaṇanga – to curve; en magaḷ – my daughter; ēngi – languishing (unable to churn continuously, with breathlessness in between); iḷaittu iḷaittu – becoming very wizened; kadai kayiṟē – the rope, that is used for churning; paṟṟi vāngi – holding it and pulling; kai – \[her\] soft hand; taḻumbu ēṟidum kolō – will the hand get scarred?

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa, who is the son of śrī nandagōpar, is not carrying out activities which are carried out by those who are born in eminent clans. He is not even carrying out activities which are done by the people of the world. Alas! Oh, one who is complete in auspicious qualities! With her waist curving on either side \[as she churns the curd\], my daughter is languishing, due to breathlessness. She has become very weak. Will her soft hands get scarred since she is pulling the rope repeatedly?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the mother is lamenting as to whether kriṣṇa could not have carried out activities which are apt for śrī nandagōpar, who goes in the path of righteousness.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kudiyil piṟandavar seyyum guṇam onṟum seydilan** – he \[kriṣṇa\] is not carrying out any quality \[activity\], which, those who are born in eminent clans will carry out. In other words, \[after marriage\], he is not taking out my daughter with him, in a proper manner.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that if people, born in a clan, do not carry out the activities of that clan, then, these have to be carried out by others who are not born in that clan, for the welfare of the world. He \[kriṣṇa\] did not carry out any of these.

**andō** – alas! The mother becomes very sorrowful.

**nadai onṟum seydilan** – Even if one does not carry out the activities of those born in eminent clans, one could carry out the activities which are normally carried out by the people of the world. He is not doing even any of those. In other words, the mother says that there is none in the world who would do like this \[not doing anything\]

**nangāy** – She addresses one, who is her relative, who is near her, who knows the activities of eminent clans and the activities of the people of the world and who is complete in her knowledge about these.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother addresses the lady near her as one who was born in an eminent clan and who was carrying out the apt activities of that clan, being complete with all the qualities. This is applicable for all.

**nandagōpan magan kaṇṇan** – kriṣṇa, who came in the clan of śrī nandagōpar, as his son. After saying how he had taken her in an improper way, through the verse “*nangāy*! *nandagōpan magan kaṇṇan-kudiyil piṟandavar seyyum guṇam onṟum seydilan-nadai onṟum seydilan-andō*”, she recalls about the tenderness of her daughter and says in a hurtful manner …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that in terms of birth, even dāśarati \[śrī rāma, soon of emperor daśaratan\] is not a match for kriṣṇa. kriṣṇa is capable of offering both this world and śrī vaikuṇṭam. The mother says that despite all these, it was due to her sins that things have gone astray, as mentioned by bharatāḻvān in śrī rāmāyaṇam “*math pāpamēva atra nimittamāsīt*” \[the reason for śrī rāma going to forest was due to my sins\] and as mentioned by sītāp pirātti to hanuman in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 38.47 “*mamaiva duśkrutam kincit*” (it is due to some wrong activity of mine).

**idai irupālum vaṇanga** – since she is churning curd \[to get butter\] from left side to right side and back again to left side, her waist is curving on either side.

**iḷaittu iḷaittu en magaḷ ēngi** – my daughter, who is tender, due to her physical weakness, unable to churn further, became breathless, and further weakened, languishing.

**kadai kayiṟu …** – Completing the task \[of churning\] from the beginning till the end, by pulling the rope without a break. The mother wonders whether her daughter’s tender hands will get scarred due to this effort. Even if one were to become the head of the herd-women \[and being the consort of kriṣṇa\], for herd-women, pulling the rope and churning the curd cannot be given up. The mother is indicating the tenderness of her daughter.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says at the end, the following: when emperumān decides to make a disciple, who is totally dependent on his ācāryan, as an ācāryan, the new ācāryan vows that he will explain *prakrutyātma vivēkham* \[the distinction between one’s physical form and ātmā\] which comes from the syllable “*ma*” in the first word *praṇavam* in tirumantram \[the first of the three esoteric mantrams in our sampradāyam\]. Though he has been instructing this for a long time, since there is none who is willing to take this and engage firmly with it, the new ācāryan starts explaining the other means such as *jñāna* and *bhakti yōgams* \[the paths of knowledge about emperumān and devotion towards emperumān\], though the basic knowledge of difference between the physical form and ātmā is yet to sink in. Since he keeps doing this, he becomes leaner and leaner \[this is the equivalent of the girl churning curd repeatedly and becoming thin\]. The older ācāryan \[on whom, the new ācāryan was totally dependent, when he was the older ācāryan’s disciple\] thinks “As emperumān keeps taking his vow and teaches him, will the new ācāryan \[his earlier disciple\] get used to it? Will it yield result?” \[this is the equivalent of the girl holding the rope and churning, leading to formation of scars on her hand\]. Here, the older ācāryan is the equivalent of mother \[mentioned in the pāsuram\] and the new ācāryan is the daughter.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.8.9. Vennirat toy

*veṇṇiṟat tōy tayir tannai veḷvaraippin mun eḻundukaṇṇuṟangādē irundu kadaiyavum vallaḷ tān kolō?oṇṇiṟat tāmaraic cengaṇ ulagaḷandān en magaḷaipaṇṇaṟaiyāp paṇi koṇḍu parisaṟa āṇḍidum kolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

tān – my daughter, who has the quality of tenderness; veḷ niṟam – having white colour; tōy – set densely; tayir tannai – curd; veḷ varaippin mun – before the eastern sky becomes pale in colour \[dawn\]; eḻundu – waking up; kaṇ uṟangādē irundu – remaining awake, with eyes open; kadaiyavum – to churn \[the curd\], with effort; vallaḷ kol O – is she capable?; oṇ niṟam – having a beautiful colour; tāmarai – like a lotus flower; sem – reddish; kaṇ – having eyes; ulagu – all the worlds; aḷandān – one who measured, accepting water; en magaḷai – my daughter; paṇṇaṟaiyāp paṇikoṇḍu – engaging in mean tasks; parisu aṟa – removing her eminence; āṇḍidum kol O – Will he rule over her? The mother says that she doesn’t know

**Перевод:**

**Curd, with a whitish colour, has set well. Is my daughter, who is tender, capable of churning the curd with effort, after getting up in the morning, keeping her eyes wide open, before the eastern sky becomes whitish? Will the one, who has reddish eyes, like a beautiful lotus flower, and who measured all the worlds, engage my daughter in menial tasks, without considering her eminence, and rule over her?**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**veṇṇiṟat tōy tayir tannai** – Since the milk has been heated well, and set for curd, without lowering its freshness, the curd has set densely, with a whitish colour.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the milk was heated without reducing its original whiteness, to a matured level. It was then set with curd. Getting up in the morning such that the whiteness seen on the eastern side followed her waking up.

**veḷvaraippin mun eḻundu** – waking up before the eastern sky becomes pale in colour, as an indication of sun rise.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that she got up in anxiety. Herd-women too get up early, just like brāhmaṇas, who get up such that both dawn and dusk follow after they get up.

**veḷ varaippu** – eastern sky becoming pale. Just as brāhmaṇas wake up, before sun rise, in order to carry out *sandyāvandanam* \[vorśipping emperumān through various deities at the time of dawn\] , herd-women too wake up at this time, for churning curd.

**kaṇ uṟangādē irundu**– even when they wake up, sleep is an enemy. Remaining awake, instead of being under its \[sleep’s\] control…

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the urge in churning curd will prevent them from falling asleep again.

**kadaiyavum tān vallaḷ kolō** – is she, who is of a tender nature, capable of churning the curd, taking effort?

**oṇṇiṟam …** – He \[kriṣṇa\] has reddish, divine eyes, which appear like a lotus flower, which has just then blossomed. He had brought all the worlds under his divine feet \[as trivikrama, when he measured the worlds\]. Through this, the pāsuram says that he made her *ananyārhai* \[to exist exclusively for him\] through the beauty of his divine eyes and kept her under his divine feet.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the mother is wondering whether kriṣṇa will make her totally dependent on him and engage her in menial tasks, without considering her eminence or whether he will engage her, without lowering her eminence and offer himself to her.

In the end he says the following: śāstram has ordained certain tasks for us to carry out, in order to develop a taste in it \[śāstram\]. Instead of doing these for a personal benefit, we should carry these out as per the instructions received from ācāryan, such that we do not do these as a means \[to attain emperumān\] or with an end-benefit in our minds \[this is the equivalent of maintaining the colour in curd, as mentioned in the pāsuram\]. These activities could be aimed at those who are dependent on emperumān for their sustenance. However, the activity which we do towards them should not be considered as providing any brightness for them \[this is the equivalent of getting up before the eastern sky becomes bright\]. We should not feel that we are without any burden either \[this is the equivalent of being alert and not going back to sleep; sleeping is considered as an act of feeling without having any burden\]. We should be in the status of one who understands tirumantram, which has the syllable “*ma*” as the predominant factor \[tirumantram’s instruction is directed towards the jīvātmā\] and know the difference between the physical form and the ātmā \[this is the equivalent of the girl churning curd\]. emperumān looks everywhere to see if there are entities who are capable of creating exclusive servitude towards him and total dependence on him, cutting off the features of carrying out servitude towards other entities and being dependent on oneself. It was with those reddish, divine eyes which look like a just-then-blossomed lotus flower that he had measured the worlds too \[this is the equivalent of emperumān having reddish eyes and measuring the worlds, mentioned in the pāsuram\]. Here, the ācāryan wonders whether emperumān, without accepting servitude in line with the s*varūpānurūpam* of his \[ācāryan’s\] disciple \[*svarūpānurūpam* refers to the disciple’s status of being a servitor and being totally dependent on ācāryan; he has to wait for ācāryan to allow him to go to emperumān and carry out kainkaryam (servitude) to emperumān\] or whether he would accept kainkaryam from the disciple, based on *viśayānurūpam* \[this refers to the distinction of emperumān’s form, due to which instead of waiting for permission, the disciple falls head over heels and carries out kainkaryam to emperumān\]. He further wonders whether emperumān would share the happiness of accepting kainkaryam from the disciple, with the disciple \[this refers to the mother wondering whether kriṣṇa would engage her daughter in tasks befitting the daughter’s eminence or not befitting her eminence\].

**en magaḷaip paṇṇaṟaiyāp paṇi koṇḍu** – he engaged my daughter, who I had nurtured as śrī mahālakśmi, in menial tasks, not considering her eminence.

**parisaṟa āṇḍidum kolō** – the mother is unsure as to whether he will rule over her, lowering her eminence or keeping her eminence high.

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.8.10. Mayavan pin

*māyavan pin vaḻi senṟu vaḻi idai māṟṟangaḷ kēttuāyargaḷ cēriyilum pukku anguttai māṟṟamum ellāmtāy avaḷ solliya sollait taṇ puduvaip pattan soltūya tamiḻ pattum vallār tūmaṇi vaṇṇanukku āḷarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

māyavan – sarvēśvaran \[lord of all\] who has amazing activities; pin vaḻi senṟu – following him; vaḻi idai māṟṟangaḷ kēttu – querying about the strange entities/events seen on the way; āyargaḷ cēriyilum pukku – entering tiruvāyppādi too; anguttai – appropriate to those who are there; māṟṟamum ellām – all the words of her daughter; tāy avaḷ – mother; solliya – spoken to those who were in proximity; sollai – words; taṇ – cool; puduvai – controller of śrī villibuttūr; pattan – periyāḻvār; sonna – mercifully composed; tūya – sacred (since it is related to emperumān); tamiḻ – in tamiḻ language; pattum – ten pāsurams; vallār – those who are capable of reciting; tū maṇi – like a faultless bluish gemstone; vaṇṇanukku – one who has his form; āḷar – will get to carry out servitude

**Перевод:**

**The mother went behind sarvēśvaran, who has amazing activities. She queried about the strange entities/events which she saw on the way. She entered tiruvāyppādi too and learnt about the words spoken by her daughter about those who are present there, appropriate to each of them. The mother shared those words with those who were in her proximity. periyāḻvār, who is the controller of the cool śrī villibuttūr, mercifully composed those words into ten pāsurams in the sacred tamiḻ language. Those who are capable of reciting these pāsurams will get to be the servitors to one, who has a form resembling a faultless bluish gemstone.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the end, āḻvār mentions the benefit which will accrue to those who recite these pāsurams and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**māyavan pin vaḻi senṟu** – emperumān had manifested his *rūpa guṇa cēśtitams* \[his divine form, his auspicious qualities and his divine activities\] to my daughter and captivated her, through those amazing characteristics. She went behind him, just like it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 3.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2022/09/periya-thirumozhi-3-7-1/) “*kaḷvan kol*” (Is he a thief, who came and took my daughter away?)

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that with the owner taking his possession and not taking it with the permission of the one who has it now, he has manifested both his auspicious quality and his fault. The mother calls him as *māyavan* \[one with amazing activities\] since both these qualities are apt to be accepted. She follows the way in which he had gone, asking from people, who were coming opposite her, about their \[kriṣṇa’s and her daughter’s\] condition, their path, their rest etc.

**vaḻiyidai māṟṟangaḷ kēttu** – just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 3.7.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2022/09/periya-thirumozhi-3-7-2/) “*kiḷi pōl miḻaṟṟṟi nadandu*” (walking behind him, speaking some words like a parrot), as she went behind him, whenever she saw anything strange on the way, she would ask him about it.

**āyargaḷ cēriyilum pukku** – entering the divine abode to be attained, tiruvāyppādi. All these activities which happened …

**anguttai māṟṟamum ellām** – all the activities which her daughter had done and all the words which she had spoken to śrī nandagōpar, yaśōdāp pirātti, kriṣṇa et al, there, appropriate to their nature. Through the word *māṟṟamum* which is a word of aggregation \[meaning this along with others\], we have to consider the activities mentioned in earlier pāsurams too.

**tāy avaḷ solliya sollai** – the words spoken by the divine mother, from her house, feeling sorrowful as well as desirous \[sorrowful about the way the daughter left and desirous to know what happened further\], to other herd-women in her proximity.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *avaḷ* \[added to the mother here\] appears to convey the meaning that whatever she had said is very secretive and is *parama rahasyam* \[most concealed\]. ūtilising these as a reason, with his *bhaktirūpāpanna jñānam* \[knowledge maturing into devotion\], taking it to the limit of *mangaḷāśāsanam* \[carrying out kainkaryam, born out of that devotion\]

maṇavāḷa māmunigaḷ gives a second interpretation for the verse up to this part. ***māyavan*** … – emperumān had taken his possession \[her daughter\] as the owner takes the owned. He did not take that entity, in the way in which he should have taken. Thus, manifesting both his auspicious quality and fault, both of which are to be considered as acceptable, he left with her. The mother followed such an amazing entity. On the way, she enquired from people who were coming opposite her about the condition, the way in which they were going, their taking resting for sleeping etc. ***āyargaḷ cēriyilum pukku*** – She went into the town of tiruvāyppādi, to the street where śrī nandagōpar was living, enquiring from the people there about distinguishing activities taking place there. ***tāy avaḷ solliya sollai*** – she asked the people who came opposite her “Have they gone near maturā?” \[as in pāsuram 1\], “Will this activity be a matter of blame or auspicious quality for our clan?” \[as in pāsuram 2\], “Did you see decorative arches erected in tiruvāyppādi and the sound of auspicious music?” \[as in pāsuram 3}. She went to tiruvāyppādi and enquired about the support \[for her daughter\] or the lack of support from śrī nandagōpar, yaśōdāp pirātti etc. The responses given by them are to be considered as the words of the divine mother. maṇavāḷa māmunigaḷ says that the first narrative \[between these two\] appears more appropriate.

**taṇ puduvaip pattan sonna** – śrī villibuttūr appears as a cool place, removing the ennui from samsāram \[materialistic realm\]. Mercifully composed by periyāḻvār, who is the controller of such śrī villibuttūr.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that śrī villibuttūr is without any shortcoming in enjoyable materials and these are the aids for carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam. Hence, āḻvār mentions the coolness of the place, in the same breath as mentioning about himself.

**tūya tamiḻ pattum vallār** – unlike samskrutam words which are dark, without knowing the meaning, tamiḻ language, which is pure, has words whose meanings are bright, which ladies and ignorant people too could know. While each of these pāsurams is sufficient to uplift a person, those who are capable of reciting all the ten pāsurams, with āḻvār’s pathos …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that purity for tamiḻ comes due to the following: unlike śāstrams where emperumān is known through words, in tamiḻ, words are composed in a fluent style for a meaning; also, the words express empathy; through the root word, suffix and etymology \[root word is the primary part of the word, which denotes an action while suffix is the last part of the word, which denotes the tense, gender, number etc. As an example, in the word *padittān* (he read), *padi* is the root word (also called in tamiḻ as pagudi) which says that the person is indulging in the action of reading, while *An*, at the end is the suffix \[called in tamiḻ as *vigudi*\]; it reveals that it is in past tense, the person is male and is a single person\], the meanings become clear in tamiḻ while in samskrutam, there will be several interpretations for the same word. The words which define the action \[verb\] in tamiḻ are straightforward, such as “*ninṟanar, irundanar*” etc, while in samskrutam, there will be three different genders for every word \[male, female and neutral gender; for example, for the meaning wife, there are three words in samskrutam, one for each gender such as dārā: in masculine, kaḷatram in neutral and bhāryāḷ in feminine gender. Context will change based on the word used. In tamiḻ, there is only one word, *manaivi*\]. Our ācāryas, who were experts in all the śāstrams, cherished the pāsurams of āḻvārs, saying that they are indeed free from any fault. Hence, it is correct to say *tūya tamiḻ*. While one pāsuram alone is enough to uplift a person, the reason for saying “*pattum vallār*” \[those who could recite all ten pāsurams\] is because of its flavour. Those who are capable of reciting these ten pāsurams, till the stage of carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam.

**tūmaṇi vaṇṇanukku āḷarē** – They will get to carry out servitude to the one, who has the beauty of his divine form like a faultless bluish gemstone, as his servitor.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the purity in *pramāṇam* \[the language of pāsuram\] is extended to the *pramēyam* too \[subject of the pāsuram\]. Since the term is with fourth case \[*tūmaṇivaṇṇanukku*, where the last syllable *ku* is the fourth case, conveying the meaning, for him\], it is similar to periya tirumoḻi pāsuram 8.9.3 “*kaṇṇapuram onṟu udaiyānukku*” (for one, who has tirukkaṇṇapuram as his permanent dwelling). The syllable *E*, in *āḷarē* confirms that the fourth case is present in all the parts of *padatrayam* \[three parts of tirumantram, viz *praṇavam*, *nama:* and *nārāyaṇāya*\]. He further explains as to how this is treated as *mangaḷāśāsanam* \[carrying out servitude to emperumān, since the pāsuram is only expressing the sorrow of the mother regarding her daughter who has been taken by emperumān\]. emperumān has taken a disciple who was totally dependent on his ācāryan \[kriṣṇa, taking the daughter away from the mother\] since he \[emperumān\] had been taking efforts since time immemorial, to take this ātmā to mōkśam \[śrī vaikuṇṭam\]. ācāryan is wondering whether the disciple is capable of carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam to emperumān there. Thus, he follows them and asks people who come in the opposite direction and those in the town, about this \[mother asking people coming opposite her as well as those in tiruvāyppādi about her daughter\]. Hence, this is to be treated as mangaḷāśāsanam only. The term “those who came opposite” refers to those who propel the disciple towards emperumān and return to take more such disciples.

We shall next consider the pravēsram of the next tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.9.1. Ennadan devikku

*ennādan dēvikku anṟu inbappū eeyādāḷtannādan kāṇavē taṇ pū marattinaivannādap puḷḷāl valiyap paṟittittaennādan vanmaiyaip pādippaṟa empirān vanmaiyaip pādippaṟa*

**Пословный перевод:**

en – for me; nādan – sarvēśvaran \[lord of all\], who is the śēśi \[one who accepts kainkaryam\]; dēvikku – for satyabhāmaip pirātti, his consort; anṟu – at the time when she desired; inbam – attractive; pū – kaṟpagappū \[flower from kalpaka, a celestial tree\]; eeyādāḷ than – indrāṇi, who didn’t offer; nādan – indra, her consort; kāṇavē – even as he was looking on; taṇ – flourishing and being cool; pū – blossomed well; marattinai – kalpaka tree; nādam – having sāmavēdam as his form; val – bring strong; puḷḷāl – through periya tiruvadi \[garuda\]; valiya – forcefully; paṟittu – uprooting; itta – and planted in the palace of satyabhāmaip pirātti; en nādan – one, who made me as his servitor; vanmaiyai – ability to carry out the task that he had thought of; pādi – singing, with joy; paṟa – undi paṟa \[undipaṟattal – a literary game, in which two or more persons sing songs, extolling virtues of their chosen entity, in a competition\]; em – for us; pirān – sing, about the capability of one, who is my benefactor, says a girl, who is deeply immersed in kriṣṇāvatāram

**Перевод:**

**A girl, who is immersed in kriṣṇāvatāram, says the following: satyabhāmaip pirātti is the consort of sarvēśvaran \[kriṣṇa\]. On the day when she desired the flower of kalpaka tree, whey they had gone to svarga \[heaven\], indrāṇi, the consort of indra, the lord of celestial entities, refused to give the flower to her. Even as her consort, indra, was looking on, emperumān, through garuda, forcefully uprooted the tree, and had it planted in the palace of satyabhāmaip pirātti. Sing, with joy, about the capability of one, who made me as his servitor, and who has the ability to carry out the task that he has thought of. Sing about the capability of my benefactor.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that this pāsuram says about the manner in which those who are on one side, immersed themselves in kriṣṇāvatāram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**ennādan dēvikku** – for the consort of my lord. The term *nādan* refers to one who owns. When one is aware of one’s *svarūpam* \[basic nature of a jīvātmā is to be a servitor to emperumān\], the relationship with emperumān is such that each person could say “*ennādan*” “*ennādan*” \[my lord\], individually. The jīvātmā’s servitude is not merely restricted to only him, but to the two of them \[perumāḷ and pirātti\], together. This is the reason for saying “*ennādan dēvikku*”. Just as it has been mentioned in śrī sūktam “*viṣṇu patni*” \[consort of viṣṇu, emperumān\], her identification comes from her relationship of being his consort. Usage of the term *dēvi* manifests satyabhāmaip pirātti’s endearment to him, viz., she is his favourite consort.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the girl \[who sings this pāsuram\] considers herself to be on a par with kriṣṇa’s consorts \[through the six qualities of *ananyāarha śēśatvam* (being servitor exclusively to emperumān)*, ananya śaraṇatvam* (taking refuge of only emperumān)*, ananya bhōjñatvam* (being enjoyed exclusively by emperumān and in turn, enjoying emperumān, exclusively) etc\] and due to the eminence of *mitunam* \[perumāḷ and pirātti, together\]. Just as nammāḻvār had said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.5.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/thiruvaimozhi-4-5-8-namakkum/) “*namakkum pūvinmisai nangaikkum*” (emperumān gives bliss to us, who are very lowly, and to pirātti, who is the most eminent \[citing the jīvātmā first\], the girl speaks about her first and says *ennādan*. It is only after ascertaining her identification that she says *ennādan dēvi* \[consort of my lord\]. This is similar to saying, as in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.10.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/03/thiruvaimozhi-10-10-2-mayam-seyyel/) “*un tiru*” (pirātti is your wealth). Just as it is mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.10.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/03/thiruvaimozhi-10-10-7-kola-malarp-pavaikku/) “*āgiya anbē*” (due to the love that you have towards pirātti, you manifest that towards me too), the repository is mentioned in a concealed way and not directly \[the pāsuram says “*kōlamalarp pāvaikku anbāgiya en anbēyō*”, instead of *anbanāgiya en anbēyō*\]. The term *ennādan dēvikku* is similar to this, with the relationship not explicitly mentioned.

**anṟu** – on the day when satyabhāmaip pirātti had mercifully gone, along with kriṣṇa, after kriṣṇa had annihilated *narakāsura* \[a monster\] and provided a place for the celestial entities to live. It was the day, when, without the celestial entities  asking or desiring for it, a great treasure \[perumāḷ and pirātti, together\] visited them.

**inbappū eeyādāḷ** – when the enjoyable flowers from *kalpaka* tree were brought by indrāṇi’s maid, satyabhāmaip pirātti expressed a desire for it. indrāṇi, citing some unacceptable reasons, and due to her misfortune, refused to offer the flowers to pirātti.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says additionally here that while she should have offered the flowers to pirātti herself even before pirātti asked for them, she did not offer them, even when pirātti asked for them.

**than nādan** – indrāṇi thought that indra, being her lord, was a great strength for her.

**kāṇavē** – even as he, indra, who thought that he was the controller of thirty-three classes of celestial entities and had a vanity on account of that, was watching …

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that indrāṇi is unlike pirātti, who removes hurdles initially \[*aniśta nivrutti*\] and then gives that which is desired \[*iśta prāpti*\]. Her consort \[indra\] is a match for her. Just as emperumān is referred to as *śrīya*: *pati* \[consort of śrī mahālakśmi\], indra would have thought that he has indrāṇi as his consort, due to the emergence of *karma bhāvanai* \[when one engages with emperumān (through thoughts, speech or deeds\], it is referred to as *brahma bhāvanai*, and when one engages with samsāram, it is *karma bhāvanai*\]. He would have thought “Am I not indra? Am I not the lord of celestial entities?”

**taṇ pū marattinai** – the *kalpaka* tree, which was flourishing, was cool and was abundant with flowers

**vannādap puḷḷāl** – through periya tiruvadi \[garuda\], who has the form of *sāma vēdam*, which is predominantly musical in nature. yajur vēdam says that he has the three vēdams \[rig, yajur and sāma\], as his head and *gāyatri* \[an important mantram, recited often\], as his eyes. His form, being made of vēdams, has been clearly stated through these pramāṇams. For *nādam* \[vēdam\], *vanmai* \[strength\] comes from the fact that *bhāhyas* \[those who do not accept the primacy of vēdams\] and *kudruśtis* \[those who misinterpret vēdams\] cannot wish it away. The term *vanmai* could also be considered as a distinguishing qualification for garuda. The strength for garuda comes from his quality of completing a task that emperumān had thought of.

**valiyap paṟittitta** – uprooting \[the tree\] forcefully. kriṣṇa did not ask indra for the gift, indra did not offer it on his own, to emperumān, it was not done when indra was not present. Even as indra was looking and tried to prevent the action, garuda forcefully removed the tree.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says additionally here that indra came with his *vajrāyudam* \[a weapon\] to fight with garuda and followed him, in order to get back the tree. This was the same indra who had just a few moments earlier welcomed kriṣṇa and satyabhāmaip pirātti and was affectionate towards them. Through this it is inferred that for those with *ubhaya bhāvam* (pathos of engaging with emperumān and also with samsāram), the knowledge and firmness which they get through devotion to emperumān is not steady. Furthermore, for attaining one’s desire, the affection and hatred which one shows in action too, will not only not bring the desired result, but also make the person to feel ashamed of the action indulged in. This is applicable not only to indra, but all those who indulge in *karma bhāvanai.*

**ennādan vanmaiyaip pādip paṟa** – emperumān carried out the task as a *paratantran* \[being dependent\] om satyabhāmaip pirātti, who is his beloved. Through this quality of affection towards his beloved, he made me \[this refers to the girl who is singing this pāsuram\] as his servitor. Sing, with joy, about the quality of carrying out the task that he had thought of, through the concept of *undi paṟattal*.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the girl says *ennādan*, losing out to the favouritism shown by emperumān, towards his followers \[pirātti, in this case\]. When it comes to protecting his followers, he will not bother about *svasankalpa paratantrars* \[those who carry out tasks based on his thoughts; entities such as indra, sūriya, candra et al who carry out tasks based on what he had ordained them to carry out\]; he will not even look at his ordainment. tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai cites the example of [mudal tiruvandādi 8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-8/) “*mayanga valamburi vāy vaittu …*” \[kriṣṇa had taken a vow that he will not take to arms during the mahābhārata war; however, when arjuna was about to enter fire, to keep his word, he hid the sun with his disc and enabled arjuna to fulfil his vow of killing jayadratan, before sunset; to protect his follower, arjuna, he went against his own vow\]. Here, the term *svasankalpa paratantrars* refers to those who had carried out plenty of virtuous deeds and are dependent on their *kāmyadarmam* \[deeds carried out to fulfil their desires\], viz. celestial entities. emperumān himself has *svasankalpa pāratantryam* \[when he takes a vow, he has to be within the boundaries of that vow\]. The term *sankalpam* refers to carrying out a remedial action for preventing sin from accruing on account of not taking a specific action. He will keep to within his *sankalpam* so long as there is no threat to righteousness. If righteousness were to be threatened, he will take the role of upkeeping righteousness and become *nirankuśa svātantryan* (totally independent entity, with uncontrolled freedom) \[when there was a threat to arjuna’s life on account of unrighteous activities from kauravas’ side during the mahābhārata war, he utilised his weapon, disc, to hide the sun and enabled arjuna to fulfil his vow\]. He alone has this strength to carry out such tasks. This is his *vanmai*.

**empirān vanmaiyaip pādip paṟa** – āḻvār considers the benefit carried out to pirātti, as the benefit carried out for him. Thus, he says “*empirān*”. The reason for repeating the word *pādip paṟa* is due to the intensity of affection. The term *paṟa* refers to *undi paṟattal*.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that since this *vanmai* \[emperumān’s strength\] is of auspicious nature, she says *empirān*.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.9.2. En vil

*en vil vali kaṇḍu pō enṟu edir vandān tantan villinōdum tavattai edir vāngimun vil valittu mudu peṇṇuyir uṇḍāntan villin vanmaiyaip pādippaṟa dāsarati tanmaiyaip pādippaṟa*

**Пословный перевод:**

en – my; vil – bow’s; vali – strength; kaṇḍu pō – saying “Check this and go”; edir vandān than – parasurāma, who came opposite him \[śrī rāma\]; villinōdum tavattai – his bow and penance; edir – in his presence; vāngi – one who destroyed; mun – prior to this; vil – bow in his divine hand; valittu – drawing it; mudu peṇ – a woman demon, called tātaki; uyir – life; uṇḍān – consumed; pādip paṟa – sing about the strength of the bow of the divine son of cakravarti; dāsarati – the son of emperor daśaratan; tanmaiyai – auspicious quality; pādippaṟa – sing (this is from a girl, who is engaged with śrī rāmāvatāram)

**Перевод:**

**paraśurāma came opposite śrī rāma and told him “Check the strength of my bow and proceed”. śrī rāma destroyed paraśurāma’s bow as well as his penance, in his presence. Earlier, he had destroyed a woman demon, called as tātaki, by drawing the bow from his divine bow. Sing about the strength of the bow of the divine son of daśarata cakravarti. Sing about the auspicious qualities of the son of daśarata cakravarti.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that it appears that he \[emperumān\] has helped this way, for the mangaḷāśāsanaparar \[periyāḻvār\] and the daughter of king janaka \[sītāp pirātti\].*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**en …** – paraśurāma came opposite \[śrī rāma\] and told him “Examine the strength of my bow and proceed”. śrī rāma had broken the bow of rudra and married sītāp pirātti, the divine daughter of śrī janakarāja. While they were returning to ayōdyā, paraśurāma heard about this incident; with anger in his heart, he came on their way, with his bow. Emperor daśarata proffered golden flowers at his divine feet and prayed to him, as mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 75.7 “*bālānām mama putrāṇām abhayam dātum arhasi*” (My sons are children; you should shower your protection on them). However, disregarding his plea, showing harsh anger on his face, paraśurāma, with the thought running in his mind “You are going proudly, having broken a bow which was already broken at a few places and had been patched up; if you take the bow from me and draw it, I will accept that you are a capable person”, told him “Check the strength of my bow”, thinking of his earlier achievements and the penance, which was the reason for those achievements, and not regarding śrī rāma as the son of emperor daśaratan.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that even as perumāḷ \[śrī rāma\] was mercifully returning after marrying sītāp pirātti, paraśurāma came and told him a few words such as “Is it of any eminence to you to say that you had drawn or broken a damaged bow?” He was having the vanity of having been successful in his tasks due to the distinguished power of emperumān having pervaded him \[*āvēśa śakti viśēśam*\], derived from the results of his penances. He further said “I will accept your ability if you check my bow and proceed further”.

**than villinōdum tavattai vāngi** – śrī rāma took the bow from paraśurāma saying “In that case, give me your bow”. While taking the bow, he also took the cause of paraśurāma’s vanity, his penance, even as paraśurāma was looking. The term *edir vandān than* *vil* refers to the bow of paraśurāma, who came opposite śrī rāma. It would also refer to the bow, which is now in the hands of paraśurāma, but which was earlier with him \[the bow with paraśurāma was originally known as the bow of viṣṇu, and śrī rāma is the incarnation of viṣṇu\]. With such a bow, he took the penance of paraśurāma. What is the meaning of taking the penance? After taking the bow from paraśurāma and fixing an arrow in it, he told paraśurāma “If I could release this arrow, it would kill you, but I do not desire that since you are a brāhmaṇa. Instead, shall I make you immobile such that you would not reach your destination? ōr, shall I destroy the benefits of the penances which you had carried out?” paraśurāma told him “If you make me immobile, I would not be able to reach mahēndra parvam \[the mountainous region near present day tirukkuṟungudi\] where I wish to go to; hence, you destroy the benefits of my penances”. śrī rāma did just that. How did paraśurāma, who is considered as the *svarūpam āvēśa āvatāram* \[incarnation of viṣṇu, wherein emperumān pervades the divine form of a jīvātmā, with his svarūpam (his basic nature) and remains until the end of the divine form of the jīvātmā\], and who is counted among the incarnations of emperumān, lose out? Since a *sākśāt avatāram* (direct incarnation of emperumān\] is more powerful than a *svarūpa āvēśa avatāram*, there is no issue with paraśurāma losing out to śrī rāma, when the line of righteousness is crossed. Just as *svarūpāvēśāvatāram* is more powerful than a *śakti āvēśa avatāram* \[this happens when emperumān pervades a jīvātmā,  with his śakti (power), for achieving an objective and leaves, once the objective is fulfilled\], a *sākśāt avatāram* is more powerful than a *svarūpa āvēśa āvatāram*. It is because a *svarūpa āvēśa avatāram* is more powerful than a *śakti āvēśa avatāram* that kārtavīryārjuna lost out to paraśurāma, earlier.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that paraśurāma maintained that it was *than vil* \[his bow\], not realising that the one, standing in front of him, was the one who gave him the powers, utilising his penance as a pretext. He had thought that even the penance was his \[kriṣṇa says in bhagavat gītā that when carrying out any task, one should give up three facets: that he is the doer, that it is his duty and that the result is his\]. While śrī rāma should have taken the penance from paraśurāma before taking the bow from him, he reversed the order due to the vanity which paraśurāma had in the result of the penances, more than the penances. *edir vāngi* – he took it from paraśurāma, even as he was looking. emperumān gives, when he sees that it would be handled in a justified manner. If it is crossed, he would take it back. When a person receives anything from emperumān, during the time of enjoyment with it, whether at the beginning or in the middle or at the end, if the person crosses the limit of fairness, it could be taken back from him, by emperumān. Engaging with the beyond-human activities of emperumān, a person may engage in carrying out penance in order to get the fruits of emperumān’s *śakti āvēśam* \[emperumān pervading the person with his *śakti*, his power\]. However, once that *śakti* is withdrawn \[at the end of the time when the purpose for which the *śakti* was given had been fulfilled\], the person becomes responsible for the actions carried out by him and has to experience the results of wrongful deeds carried out by him. In order to get over this fear, paraśurāma desired *svarūpāvēśam* from emperumān \[pervading with his *svarūpam*, his basic nature\]. Here, even after destroying his enemy, he will not accumulate sins of his deeds; it is due to this that he had engaged with the difficult-to-carryout penance earlier, being counted as one among the incarnations of emperumān, as in the saying “*rāmō rāmaśca rāmasca*” (emperumān incarnated as paraśurāma, śrī rāma, balarāma). It was to explain this that tirumangai āḻvār said, in his periya tirumoḻi 8.8.10 “*munnumirāmanāyt tānāy pinnumirāmanāy*” (incarnating first as paraśurāma, then as śrī rāma and further as balarāma\]. In the case of *śakti āvēśam*, during the time of having the power from emperumān, if one indulges in wrongful activities, after the activity had been carried out, if one atones for it, by saying “īśvaran gave us, based on the penance that we carried out” one need not undergo the effect of sins committed. It was to negate this effect that paraśurāma had carried out penance for getting *svarūpāvēśam*. The difference between the two is that the latter lasts as long as the physical form remains in samsāram \[till the end\].  When such is the case, how did an impediment come in the middle? This is because he \[paraśurāma\] could not tolerate the activity of *cakravartit tirumagan* \[śrī rāma\] who has a distinguished, divine form. In the presence of emperumān, due to all such qualities, the *āvēśam* \[emperumān pervading with is svabhāvam\] will return \[to emperumān\]. rudra, who had taught him \[paraśurāma\] about the other features, had not taught him about intolerable activities in the presence of emperumān. Even if he had taught, āḻvārs would say “*aran aṟivānām*” \[rudra would have known, but would not have instructed\]. Since he spreads *mōhaśāstram* \[instructions he gives, which bewilder the world, at the behest of emperumān\], he could have told him too \[to bewilder paraśurāma\]. paraśurāma, realising that the task which he had undertaken \[challenging śrī rāma to take the bow from him and to draw it\] would not succeed, told śrī rāma “Target the arrow, which you have taken on the bow, at my penance”. śrī rāma too, aimed at his penance \[in essence, removing *āvēśam* from paraśurāma\], censuring him with shame, knowing that paraśurāma will not engage in penance again. Even if he engages in any penance, it would be of the penance as mentioned in taittirīya upaniśad nārāyaṇavalli “*ēśām tpasām atiriktamāhu*:” (listing twelve types of penance, śāstram says that the best among these is …\], which is the penance of *nyāsam* \[surrendering\], which is one of being without any power \[when we surrender to emperumān, we say that we are *akincanan* (not having anything with us, to reach him)\].

**mun vil valittu mudu peṇ uyir uṇḍān** – tātaki was a demon, who was habitually harming others, destroying the penance and rituals of brāhmaṇas as well as brāhmaṇas themselves. Sage viśvāmitra feared troubles from her when he wanted to undertake a ritual. Before this incident \[with paraśurāma\] , when śrī rāma had mercifully gone with the great sage viśvāmitra, in order to help him in fulfilling his rituals, tātaki came running, crying out loudly, with plenty of anger. Implored by sage viśvāmitra, śrī rāma drew the bow in his hand and killed her.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that this \[killing tātaki\] happened before taking paraśurāma’s penance; before he \[śrī rāma\] got married. Before both. Before he entered the forest, treating fulfilment of the words of his mother as an excuse, and killed his enemies \[kara, dūśaṇa, rāvaṇa et al\]. After taking his bow, śrī rāma showed the power of his bow on her \[tātaki\] first. *mudu perṇ uyir uṇḍān* – *mudircci* \[matured; aged\] refers to her quality of harming brāhmaṇas and their rituals, unlike the womenfolk among demons and monsters and unlike demons and monsters themselves. Sage viśvāmitra told śrī rāma “Do not consider her as a woman; kill her immediately”. To fulfil the words of the sage, he annihilated this matured woman, first.

**than villin vanmaiyaip pādippaṟa** – The girl \[who is reciting this pāsuram\] tells her competitor to sing about the strength of śrī rāma’s bow and carry out *undipaṟattal*. What is the strength of his bow? Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.4.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thiruvaimozhi-5-4-3-niyum-pangallai/) “*kāyum kadum silai*” (the divine, cruel bow, śrī śārngam, roasts the enemies of emperumān), even if emperumān desires to show compassion on his enemies, the divine bow will not show any compassion on them. It is very firm, in carrying out its task.

**dāsarati vanmaiyaip pādippaṟa** – this refers to the quality of emperumān, who, despite carrying out such deeds which are outside the limits of human beings, has the simplicity to address himself as the son of daśaratan, without thinking of even the trace of the quality of being the supreme being for all.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that though śrī rāma had the power of his bow, since he identified himself as the son of king daśarata, always, the pāsuram says this verse \[*dāśarati vanmaiyaip pādippaṟa*\]. This pāsuram describes the controller’s–controlled’s pathos which takes place when two incarnations \[primary incarnation of śrī rāma and permeated incarnation of paraśurāma\] meet. The word *tanmai* refers to auspicious qualities.

We shall next consider the 3<sup>rd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.9.3. Uruppini nangai

*uruppiṇi nangaiyait tērēṟṟik koṇḍuviruppuṟṟu angu ēga viraindu edir vanduserukkuṟṟān vīram sidaiyat talaiyaicciraittittān vanmaiyaip pādippaṟa dēvaki singattaip pādippaṟa*

**Пословный перевод:**

uruppiṇi nangaiyai – rukmiṇip pirātti; tēr – on the divine chariot; ēṟṟik koṇḍu – taking; angu – with that; viruppuṟṟu – desirously; ēga – even as he went; edir – to oppose and fight with him; viraindu vandu – one who came hurriedly; serukkuṟṟān – rukman, who had vanity; vīram sidaiya – to destroy the power \[of that vanity\]; talaiyai – head; siraittittān – sing about the strength of the one who tonsured his head with his arrow; dēvaki singattai – sing about the son of dēvakip pirātti, who has the valour of a lion

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa took rukmiṇip pirātti, on his divine chariot, and went desirously. Even as he was proceeding \[to marry her\], rukman \[the eldest brother of rukmiṇip pirātti\] came hurriedly to fight with him. Sing about the strength of the one who destroyed the power of that rukman’s vanity by tonsuring his head with his arrow. Sing about the strength of the son of dēvakip pirātti, who has the valour of a lion.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that the earlier pāsuram described emperumān’s affection for sītāp pirātti. This pāsuram recalls the benefit that he carried out for rukmiṇip pirātti.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**uruppiṇi nangaiyait tēr ēṟṟik koṇḍu** – just as it has been mentioned in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 11.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/10/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-11-9/) “*kaṇṇālam kōdittu*” (carrying out nicely, all the arrangements for the marriage), the wealth earned by king \[rukma\] was spent in the arrangements for the marriage \[of rukmiṇip pirātti with śiśupālan\]. Desiring to hold her hand in marriage and like one who desires to “smell the fresh flower”, śiśupālan had carried out all the preliminary functions preceding the marriage. He was firm that he had got hold of rukmiṇip pirātti. kriṣṇa went there and took the hand of rukmiṇip pirātti, such that śiśupālan’s radiance was completely destroyed; he felt ashamed to look at anyone’s face and looked upward. kriṣṇa took her on his chariot.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that rukmiṇip pirātti had tied the sacred protective thread around her wrist as a prelude to marrying śiśupālan. She had prayed to emperumān “At the time when śiśupālan comes to touch me, my life should have left me or kriṣṇa should accept me”. kriṣṇa, who is the supreme entity himself, thought in his divine mind about her prayer, kept śrī pāncajanya āḻvān \[the divine conch\] on his divine lips and blew on it, signalling his arrival to her and making her to sustain herself. He came there, took rukmiṇip pirātti’s divine hand in his divine hand, signalling that he will rule over her, making the radiance of śiśupālan and the assembly of kings there to disappear, and making them to feel ashamed. He took her on his chariot and mercifully left, uproariously. When the son of king rukman came there to oppose kriṣṇa and to retrieve his sister rukmiṇip pirātti, kriṣṇa, thinking that if he were to kill her brother, rukmiṇip pirātti;s divine mind will get hurt, kriṣṇa tied him to the wheels of his chariot and tonsured his head with his arrow. He carried out the remaining parts of the marriage function, considering the other functions conducted by śiśupālan as having been carried out by himself, since he is the antaryāmi \[indvelling soul\] of śiśupālan too. Just as it has been mentioned in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 11.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/10/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-11-9/) “*peṇṇāḷan pēṇum Ur pērum arangamē*” (tiruvarangam is the divine abode where that emperumān, who is famously known to help all women, has mercifully taken residence, with desire), \[the girl, who sings this pāsuram tells her competitor to\] sing the strength of one who placed rukmiṇip pirātti in the famous *bhōgamaṇḍapam* \[the centre which is for enjoying\], who helped women-folk, who tonsured the head of rukman, to remove the vanity of his valour and who destroyed his enemies. This is taken as an example of all his valour.

**viruppuṟṟu angu ēga** – even as he left, taking her desirously with him

**viraindu …** – rukman, the eldest brother of rukmiṇip pirātti, wondered “Why is this being done?” and came there, to oppose kriṣṇa and to retrieve rukmiṇip pirātti from him, with the vanity of his valour. kriṣṇa thought that if he killed rukman in the fight, rukmiṇip pirātti’s mind will get hurt. Hence, he caught him, tied him to the wheel of his chariot, and as a means of destroying his vanity, tonsured rukman’s head with his arrow. Sing about the strength of such kriṣṇa, impelled by your affection \[says the girl who sings this pāsuram, to her competitor\]. Alternatively, if the text had been *vanda serukkuṟṟān* \[instead of *vandu serukkuṟṟān*\], the meaning would be: sing about the strength of one who tonsured the head of one, who came hurriedly, with vanity, to retrieve rukmiṇip pirātti.

**dēvaki singattaip pādippaṟa** – sing about the one, who has the greatness of having been born from the divine stomach of dēvakip pirātti and who has the valour of a lion in annihilating enemies.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the reason for mentioning kriṣṇa as the son of dēvakip pirātti, more than the son of yaśōdāp pirātti who had the fortune of getting him and nurturing him, is to manifest his basic clan of royalty \[in order to marry rukmiṇip pirātti, who is from royal clan\] and to emphasise his fulfilling the words of his mother right at the time when he was born \[to hide the divine weapons with which he incarnated\].

We shall next consider the first part of 4<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.
