## 3.9.5. Panjavar tudanay

*panjavar tūdanāyp pāradam kai seydunanjumiḻ nāgam kidanda nal poygai pukkuanjap paṇattin mēl pāyndittu aruḷ seydaanjana vaṇṇanaip pādippaṟa asōdai tan singattaip pādippaṟa*

**Пословный перевод:**

panjavar – for the five pāṇḍavas; tūdanāy – taking the role of a messenger; bāradam – in the mahābhārata war; kai seydu – helping; nanju – poison; umiḻ – spitting; nāgam – snake, kāḷiyan; kidanda – lying down; nal poygai – on the banks of the cruel river; pukku – went and entered; anja – such that he was frightened; paṇattin mēl – on the hoods; pāyndittu – jumped, making him weak; aruḷ seyda – letting him go, without killing him; anjanam – like black pigment \[used for decorating eyes\]; vaṇṇanai – sing about the one, who has a complexion like that; asōdai than singattai – sing about the one who is like a lion cub for yaśōdāp pirātti

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa took on the role of a messenger for the five pāṇḍavas and helped them \[later\] during the mahābhārata war. He entered the shore of the river inside which kāḷiyan, the snake, was lying, spitting poison in the river. He jumped onto the hoods of the snake such that the snake was frightened. When kāḷiyan and his consorts surrendered to kriṣṇa, without killing him, he allowed him to go. Sing about such kriṣṇa, who has he complexion of a dark pigment. Sing about the one, who is like a lion cub, for yaśōdāp pirātti.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār is engaging with kriṣṇāvatāram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**panjavar tūdanāy** – as a messenger for yudiśtra et al. Among these five \[brothers\], it appears that there is none who does not ordain him \[kriṣṇa\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa incarnated only to become a messenger. It was only after he was identified as “*innār tūdan*” \[the messenger of pāṇḍavas\] that his incarnation established itself. He overcame the shortcoming of awaiting the result of sending a messenger, by going as a messenger himself \[reference here is to śrī rāmāyaṇam, where, śrī rāma had to wait until hanuman returned from lankā, to know about the condition of sītāp pirātti). The term *āy* \[as in *tūdanāy*\] indicates that being a messenger was natural for him and was not something which he had to take on.

**tūdanāy** – while he is the *sarvādikan* \[superior to everyone else\], he went as a messenger, tying a palm leaf around his neck \[to notify all, that he is a messenger\], without any fault. He thinks that this is a difficult-to-attain benefit for him, just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 2.2.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/08/periya-thirumozhi-2-2-3/) “*innār tūdan ena ninṟān*” (he stood, as the messenger of pāṇḍavas). It was only after becoming famous as the messenger of pāṇḍavas that he sustained himself and stood upon earth.

**bāradam kai seydu** – when kriṣṇa kept asking duryōdana to grant at the least, ten villages to pāṇḍavas, later scaling it down to one village, duryōdana refused even that. He made them engage in war, by saying “In that case, let the one who emerges victorious in the war, rule the world”. During the subsequent war, he helped the pāṇḍavas by arranging the battle formations and remaining as the charioteer for arjuna, conducting the war.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *bāradam kai seydu* refers to his partiality towards pāṇḍavas, after his role, as a messenger of pāṇḍavas, did not yield the desired result and he helped the pāṇḍavas to emerge victorious.

**nanjumiḻ nāgam kidanda naṟpoygai pukku** – kāḷiyan, a poisonous snake, had entered the river and spat poison inside the water such that all the tress and birds nearby started falling down, dying. He entered, as mentioned in periya tirumoḻi 10.7.12 *“naccaḻaṟ poygai*” (river where the snake was spitting poison), the poisonous river. What is the reason for calling it as *nal poygai*, when it is poisonous? This is similar to saying *nalla pāmbu* \[good snake, for cobra\], *nalla neruppu* \[good fire, for a destructive fire\] etc, through the symbolism of opposite enunciation. Alternatively, before kāḷiyan entered it, the river was a good river, hence it is mentioned even now as a good river.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as it has been mentioned in [tiruccanda viruttam 86](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/02/thiruchchandha-viruththam-86/) “*salam kalanda poygai*” (it appeared as if water had been added to a poisonous river), kāḷiyan had spat such an amount of poison in that river that cows were unable to drink any water. *nal poygai pukku* – before the entry of kāḷiyan, the river was indeed good. kriṣṇa jumped into that river, making kāḷiyan to surface. If he stood inside the water, it would not have been possible to jump onto the head of kāḷiyan; hence, he climbed a tree nearby \[*kurundam* tree\] and jumped on top of kāḷiyan’s hoods, by twisting his body while jumping, such that the snake was frightened. It was only after jumping atop kāḷiyan that he showered his mercy on it. It was only after that his natural complexion manifested itself \[shiny black\].

**anjap paṇattin mēl pāyndittu aruḷ seyda** – kriṣṇa agitated the river such that kāḷiyan surfaced. Then, he jumped onto the spread hoods of that kāḷiyan such that he was frightened. He danced on him, making him grow weaker. kāḷiyan pleaded with kriṣṇa, as mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5.7.70 “*krupāmātra manōvrutti*: *prasīdamē*” (you should shower only your mercy on me), and his consorts pleaded, as mentioned in śrī viṣṇupurāṇam 5.7.79 “*bhartru bikśā pradīyatām*” (You should mercifully grant us our husband, back to us). After their surrendering to him, he showered his mercy on them such that kāḷiyan went out, alive.

**anjana vaṇṇanaip pādippaṟa** – sing about the one whose divine form shone brightly, with black pigment, getting the splendour on account of granting them protection, after they surrendered to him.

**asōdai than singattaip pādip paṟa** – sing about the one who is like a lion cub, since yaśōdāp pirātti nurtured him eminently.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that more than the term *dēvaki singam*, it was this term, *asōdai than singam* that āḻvārs celebrated. Hence, āḻvār wanted this to be sung about.

We shall next consider the 6<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.9.6. Mudi onri

*mudi onṟi mūvulagangaḷum āṇḍu unadiyēṟku aruḷ enṟu avan pin todarndapadiyil guṇattup parada nambikku anṟuadi nilai īndānaip pādippaṟa ayōddiyar kōmānaip pādippaṟa*

**Пословный перевод:**

mudi onṟi – donning the divine crown; mū ulagangaḷum – the three worlds of bhūmi (earth), svarga (heaven) and pātālam (nether world); āṇḍu – looking after; un – your; adiyēṟku – servant, for me; aruḷ – you should shower your mercy; enṟu – praying like this; avan pin todarnda – one, who followed the divine son of daśarata cakravarti \[śrī rāma\]; padi il – unmatched; guṇam – having auspicious qualities; barada nambikku – for śrī bharatāḻvān; anṟu – during that time, when he was distressed in his mind; adi nilai – śrī pādukas \[divine sandals\]; īndānai – sing about him, who mercifully gave him; ayōddiyar kōmānai – sing about the one, who is the king of those who inhabit the divine ayōdyā

**Перевод:**

**śrī bharatāḻvān, who has unmatched auspicious qualities, followed the divine son of emperor daśarata and prayed to him “You should don the divine crown and rule over the three worlds, protecting them. You should shower your mercy on me, your servitor”. Sing about the one, who mercifully gave his divine sandals to that śrī bharatāḻvān, when he was distressed and prayed to him. Sing about the one who is the king of all who inhabit divine ayōdyā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*The day after carrying out the last rites for emperor \[daśarata\], after the sun had risen, all the royal entities, all the common people and the priests, headed by vasiśta et al, gathered together and told bharatāḻvān “perumāḷ \[śrī rāma\] has gone to the forest; emperor is no more; the country cannot remain without a king”. To make bharata as the king, auspicious music from musical instruments was being played. Upon hearing the music, bharata became very pained. To manifest his inability to bear the pain, he came to the gathering and, as mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 82.10 “vilalāpa sabhāmadyē jagarhēca purōhitam” (In the middle of the assembly, he lamented and reproached the head priest), cried out aloud, saying “You are coming as a huge gathering and stealing my quality of pāratantryam \[servitor to śrī rāma\]”. Without observing the rule stated in āpastamba sūtram “When the teacher crosses the boundary of justice, he should be told in confidence”, he accosted vasiśta bhagavān \[he is addressed here as bhagavān since he has been the head priest for the clan of ikśvāku kings for a very long time\], in that gathering, saying “You have very nicely carried out good bodings for this clan from the beginning”. Further, he said, as in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 82.12 “rājyam ca aham ca rāmasya darmam vaktumihārhasi katam daśaratāj jātō bhavēd rājyāpahāraka:” (The kingdom and I are śrī rāma’s possessions; mercifully ordain what is righteous in this matter. How could one, born of daśarata become the usurper of the crown?) He said “When two entities are the possessions of a person, would one of the two possessions rule over the other? Could the kingdom rule over me? When you say that the kingdom cannot remain without a king, should you not look at me, who is involved in this, and speak the words? If I usurp the kingdom, which śrī rāma had left behind, vouldn’t it be said as to how could I, born to that daśarata, take over the kingdom as soon as śrī rāma left?” When they all asked him “What should we do now?”, he told them “Let us all go to śrī rāma, fall at his divine feet, bring him back with us and coronate him; come with me”. This pāsuram mentions the manner in which bharatāḻvān took them all with him to citrakūtam, surrendered at the divine feet of perumāḷ, with his grief and submitted to him.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**mudi onṟi** – You, who had avoided the divine crown, who had matted your hair, left the country and entered the forest, should leave aside this forest and your *tāpasavēśam* \[the dress of penance\], mercifully enter divine ayōdyā and don the divine crown.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says in his svāpadēśam, that śrī bharatāḻvān tells śrī rāma “Unlike last time, without any hurdle, you should come and don the divine crown, forever. The reason for the hurdle last time was my staying away \[from ayōdyā\].” śrī rāma replied to him “It was due to me that the coronation ceremony was stopped. The kingdom is intact. Did not our father give that to you? You should look at his solemn words and his permission”. śrī bharatāḻvān said “He was father to you. I was born after you. Moreover, vasn’t I your disciple? Weren’t you the disciple of sage vasiśta? Am I only your brother and your disciple? Am I not your servitor too? īsn’t my nature such that I consider both the kingdom and me as your possessions \[on equal footing\]?” śrī rāma asked him “Do you have a separate perception, other than our father’s?” śrī bharatāḻvān told him “Please bear with my being in my uncle’s place when all these incidents happened and mercifully return to ayōdyā” and surrendered to perumāḷ.

perumāḷ told him “If you think that you are my younger brother, then do as per the wishes of the elder brother. If you think of yourself as a disciple, then carry out the ācāryan’s wishes. If you are servitor, then do as per the wishes of the lord. If you have surrendered to someone, then do as per the wishes of the person who has granted you refuge”. Stating a few convincing words mercifully, like these, perumāḷ made śrī bharatāḻvān to feel happy and granted his divine sandals to him. It was only after śrī bharatāḻvān accepted the sandals, considering them as his ultimate benefit \[*puruśārtam*\] that he became *padiyil guṇattup parada nambi* \[one who has unmatched auspicious qualities and who is complete with all the auspicious qualities\]. The term *padiyil guṇam* \[unmatched qualities\] infers that the qualities of one who said that he would fulfil the words of his father \[perumāḷ\] and the one who said that he does not consider emperor daśarata as his father \[iḷaiya perumāḷ\] are not a match for the qualities of śrī bharatāḻvān. It was after accepting the divine sandals that bharata became *adi sūdum arasan* \[the king who donned the divine sandals\]. It is because of this that he attained completeness \[*nambi*\]. This came about due to the thoughts of śrī śatrugnāḻvān \[śatrugna considered bharata as his lord and would serve only him; he would not even look at śrī rāma (for fear that he would change)\], and since he \[bharata\] did not say, like lakśmaṇa, that he could not live without śrī rāma. This is the explanation for the syllable “*u*” in praṇavam \[*ananyārha śēśatvam*, being exclusive servitor to emperumān and to none else\].

**mūvulagangaḷum āṇḍu** – just as it has been mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 2.13 “*trailōkyamapi nātēna yē nasyānnātavattaram* ” (through which lord the three worlds would shine, getting a great lord), you should rule over the three worlds, being their lord

**unnadiyēṟku aruḷ enṟu avan pin todarnda** – bharatāḻvān had gone, following the path of śrī rāma and prayed to him, as mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 101.12 “*bhrātuśśiśyasya dāsasya prasādam kartum arhasi*” (It is appropriate for you to shower your mercy on me, who is your younger brother, your disciple and your servitor), saying “Not only as your brother, since I had learnt all the esoteric meanings from you, you should treat me as your disciple; also, I am your servitor such that you could do as you deem fit with me. Hence, you should mercifully grant me”.

**padiyil guṇattup parada nambikku** – śrī bharatāḻvān has unmatched auspicious qualities since he revered the boundary of the clan which said “When the elder is there, none has known of a younger brother coronating, in this clan”; he was frightened of being coronated since it would make him *svātantryan* \[as an independent entity, while he was totally dependent on śrī rāma\]; he also looked at his *svarūpam* (basic nature of being a servitor to śrī rāma). He fell at the divine feet of śrī rāma, trembling from head to foot, and prayed to him “You should return mercifully and don the divine crown”.

**anṟu adi nilai īndānai** – when bharatāḻvān was standing, with anguish, in front of him, śrī rāma told him “If I return as requested by you now, I would have gone against the words of our father, due to involvement with ruling the country. If you take me back with you, people would say that you are capable of carrying out both deeds – of earlier sending a secretive message to your mother to send me to the forest and getting the kingdom for you;  now, once the people started speaking ill of you, you followed your brother, cried in his presence, fell at his feet and somehow, brought him back to ayōdyā. This blame will come on you. Hence, in the presence of those who said a few words to you which made you feel that you are independent, get back the quality of being totally dependent, which is aligned to your basic nature and return”. śrī rāma spoke these words which made śrī bharatāḻvān not to compel him further and to agree to his words. Just as it has been mentioned in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.9.1 “*maravadiyait tambikku vān paṇaiyam vaittu*” (pledging his divine wooden sandals to śrī bharatāḻvān to make him feel reassured), to ensure that śrī bharatāḻvān rids himself of his fear of independence as well as to assure him that he \[śrī rāma\] would mercifully return, he gave his divine sandals to him and made him as one who donned the sandals. Sing about such śrī rāma.

**ayōddiyar kōmānaip pādippaṟa** – the girl \[who sings this pāsuram\] tells her competitor to sing about the one who became the controller of those who are in divine ayōdyā, by making śrī bharatāḻvān to don his \[śrī rāma’s\] divine feet instead of the divine crown.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that since the divine sandals ruled ayōdyā, using bharata as a pretense, the one who gave the sandals could be termed as the king. Moreover, since he crowned himself subsequently, it could be said that he is the king.

We shall next consider the 7<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.9.7. Kaliyan poygai

*kāḷiyan poygai kalangap pāyndittu avannīḷ mudi aindilum ninṟu nadam seydumeeḷa avanukku aruḷ seyda vittagantōḷ vali vīramē pādippaṟa tūmaṇivaṇṇanaip pādippaṟa*

**Пословный перевод:**

kāḷiyan – where the snake kāḷiyan was lying; poygai – river; kalanga – such that it was agitated; pāyndittu – went and jumped; avan – his; neeḷ – rising to the sky; mudi aindilum – on the five hoods; ninṟu – keeping his feet alternatively; nadam seydu – danced; meeḷa – again (once he surrendered); aruḷ seyda – one who was compassionate in his divine mind; vittagan – one who is amazing, his; tōḷ vali – strength of his shoulders; vīramē – sing about his valour; tū – without any fault; maṇi – like a bluish gemstone; vaṇṇanai – sing about the one who has a beautiful form

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa went and jumped into the river where the poisonous snake, kāḷiyan, was lying, such that the river became agitated. On feeling the agitation in the river, kāḷiyan rose up, to the sky. Sing about the valour of the strength of the shoulders of one, who stood on that kāḷiyan’s five hoods alternatively and danced, and who later granted him freedom, with compassion in his divine mind, after that kāḷiyan surrendered to him. Sing about the one who has the complexion of a faultless, bluish gemstone.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kāḷiyan poygai** – it is enough to just say “*kāḷiyan poygai*” (the river in which the snake was lying) to speak about the cruelty of that snake. It is similar to saying ‘a snake pit’ . The cruelty of its poison was such that animals and trees, which were in its vicinity, fell down due to the extreme heat of that poison, and died. This is similar to saying, as in periya tirumoḻi 10.7.12 “*āyiravāy naccaḻal poygai*” (with a snake which was spitting poison, which was like fire, through its one thousand mouths).

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai, in his svāpadēśam, says that this pāsuram is together with 3.9.5 “*naccumiḻ nāgam*”. kriṣṇa had the capability to jump on to the hoods of kāḷiyan and when he surrendered, he gave him life, asking him to go the ocean and remain there.

**kalangap pāyndittu** – running and jumping into that river such that it was agitated fully.

**avan …**– once the river got agitated, kāḷiyan, who was lying inside that river, became angry and rose up to the sky, spreading his hoods widely, in fury. kriṣṇa got on top of those hoods and kept dancing, alternating his feet on those hoods.

**meeḷa avanukku aruḷ seyda vittagan** – just as it has been in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5.7.4 “*tam prabinnaśirōgrīvām asyēpya*: *śrutaśōṇitam*” (looking at that kāḷiyan whose heads and necks had been torn and who was bleeding), kāḷiyan, with his heads and necks torn and bleeding from the mouth, became weak. In order to survive, he surrendered to the divine feet of kriṣṇa. Earlier, kriṣṇa had intended to kill kāḷiyan; however, after kāḷiyan surrendered to him, he let go of his anger and mercifully showered his grace; he is one with amazing activity. Amazing activity is that while he intended to kill him, he showered his grace on the same entity, once he surrendered, and protected him.

**tōḷ vali vīramē pādippaṟa** – when kāḷiyan attempted to coil around kriṣṇa when kriṣṇa danced on his hoods, just as it has been mentioned in [periya tiruvandādi 18](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/10/periya-thiruvandhadhi-18/) “*pāmbāl āppuṇḍu*” (he was coiled around by the snake), instead of getting caught in that, he deftly removed the coiling, held the tail of the snake over his shoulders and danced on kāḷiyan. Sing about the strength of those shoulders and the valour which he manifested.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that just as snake *vāsuki* had coiled around *mandara parvatam* \[the mountain mandara, which was anchored in the milky ocean and used as a staff for churning it\], when kriṣṇa was dancing on the hoods of kāḷiyan, it coiled around him. He released himself from that, took hold of its tail and held it high over his shoulder. It is this, which is referred to in this pāsuram, as *tōḷ vali*.

**tūmaṇivaṇṇanaip pādippaṟa** – After driving away the snake, giving him life, he made the poisoned river as sweet water, like nectar, and enabled the cattle and the herd-people to drink water from it, like before. Due to this, his divine form was splendorous like a bluish gemstone. The girl, who sings this pāsuram, tells her competitor to sing about such kriṣṇa.

We shall next consider the 8<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.9.8. Tarkku ila

*tārkku iḷandambikku arasīndu taṇḍagamnūṟṟavaḷ soṟkoṇḍu pōgi nudangidaiccūrppaṇagāvaic ceviyodu mūkku avaḷārkka arindānaip pādippaṟa ayōddikkarasanaip pādippaṟa*

**Пословный перевод:**

tārkku – for ruling over the country, wearing a garland \[in olden days, kings wore garland while sitting on the throne\]; iḷa – not apt; tambikku – for \[śrī rāma’s\] brother, śrī bharatāḻvān; arasu īndu – offering the kingdom of bearing his \[śrī rāma’s\] divine sandals; nūṟṟavaḷ sol koṇḍu – as per the words of kaikēyi, who had analysed; daṇḍagam – towards daṇḍaka āraṇyam \[forest\]; pōgi – mercifully went; nudangu – quivering; idai – one, who had waist; sūrppaṇagāvai – demon sūrpaṇakhā \[sister of demon rāvaṇa\]; seviyodu mūkku – ears and nose; avaḷ ārkka – such that she screamed; arindānai – sing about the one who sliced; ayōddikku arasanai – sing about the one, who is the king of ayōdyā

**Перевод:**

**śrī bharatāḻvān considered himself as not being fit to rule over, as the king \[of ayōdyā\], wearing a garland. śrī rāma gave śrī bharatāḻvān, his divine sandals, which bharata kept on his head \[as a crown\]. śrī rāma went to the daṇḍaka forest, heeding to the words of kaikēyi, who had analysed her boons. There, he sliced the ears and nose of demon sūrpaṇakhā, who had come in disguise, with her slender waist quivering. Sing about such śrī rāma. Sing about the one, who is the king of ayōdyā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**tārkku iḷandambikku arasu īndu** – sages vasiśta et al as well as the key members of the court in ayōdyā told śrī bharatāḻvān “Emperor \[daśarata\] has allowed you to be the king; perumāḷ too agreed to it. This country \[of ayōdyā\] should not be without a king. You should wear the regal crown”. While there is a provision like this, śrī bharatāḻvān, considering that ‘It is not known in our clan that while the elder brother is there, the younger one would wear the crown’ told them “I do not qualify for wearing the crown, donning a garland. When elder brother, śrī rāma is there, I have no right to be the king”. He refused their pleading and went to citrakūtam, to bring back śrī rāma. śrī rāma gave him his divine sandals, in line with śrī bharatāḻvān’s nature \[of being a servitor\].

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār meditates on the pāsuram “*adinilai īndānai*” \[3.9.6\] and continues with that. śrī bharatāḻvān had countered the counsel of vasiśta et al, to make him he king, by saying that none in his clan had donned the crown when the elder brother was there. In the open, royal court, he was angry with vasiśta and refused to wear the crown. śrī rāma, by stating a principle, had made him to agree to his proposal of giving him his sandals and the kingdom which was befitting him \[to rule ayōdyā until śrī rāma returns, as his representative\]. The term *tār* also refers to the four divisions of the army \[chariots, elephants, horses and foot-soldiers\]. When the four divisions of the army requested him to don the garland and rule over them, he said a few words, with his heart getting softened \[here, *iḷa* stands for *nenju iḷagudal*, heart getting softened\]. Alternatively, *tār* would also refer to garland, and through that, it refers to the kingdom. *iḷandambi* refers to śrī bharatāḻvān, who is directly the immediate younger brother of śrī rāma \[*īḷam* – young; *tambi* – younger brother\].

**daṇḍaga nūṟṟavaḷ sol koṇḍu pōgi** – kaikēyi analysed her boons which she had received from emperor daśarata \[at an earlier point of time\] and told śrī rāma “We shall allow you to leave the kingdom and go to the forest”**.** Heeding her words, śrī rāma went to daṇḍaka āraṇyam. In an earlier pāsuram \[3.9.4\] too, it was mentioned as “*kūṟṟuttāy sollak kodiya vanam pōna*” \[one who went to the cruel forest, heeding the words of kaikēyi, who was like yama, the lord of death\]. It was only to heed her words that śrī rāma did not return to ayōdyā, despite \[eminent\] people such as vasiśta et al, who had gone with śrī bharatāḻvān, pleading with him to return to ayōdyā, but went ahead with daṇḍaka āraṇyam.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that he went against the words of sages such as vasiśta et al, his divine mothers and the people of the city of ayōdyā, heeding the words of kaikēyi alone, who had analysed her boons and told him to go to the forest. The word *pōgi* would refer to going as well as to the person who is going. Heeding her words, he went not only to the forest that she had indicated, but further beyond \[all the way to lankā\].

**nudangu idai …** – since she \[sūrpaṇakhā\] was driven by her lust, she hid her original form of a demon and took on the guise of a beautiful woman. \[She came to pancavati\] Displaying her beautiful form, with quivering waist, she told śrī rāma “You should accept me”.  Pointing out sītāp pirātti, śrī rāma told sūrpaṇakhā “She is there for us. You could go there”, pointing out to lakśmaṇa. When she went to him, he told her “I am his servitor. It is better for you to go to him”. Becoming angry, due to their taunting, sūrpaṇakhā took her original \[demonic\] form and tried to take sītāp pirātti with her. Sing about the one, who sliced her ears and nose. Though it was lakśmaṇa who disfigured her with his sword, since lakśmaṇa is said, as in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 34.14 “*rāmasya dakśiṇōbāhu*:” (lakśmaṇa is considered to be the right hand of śrī rāma\], lakśmaṇa was only the instrument and it was śrī rāma who was the doer.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when sūrpaṇakhā tried to abduct sītāp pirātti, knowing the signal from perumāḷ, lakśmaṇa, considering himself as only the implement \[carrying out the order of the doer, śrī rāma\], sliced her ears and nose, such that she screamed and fled the place. Instead of saying *aṟuttānai* \[one, who severed\], the reason for saying *arindānai* \[one, who sliced\] is that during the time of slicing, the pain will not be felt. However, a few moments later, the pain will hit the person, severely. The term *ārttal* \[as in *avaḷ* ***ārkka*** *arindānai*\], could also mean pride. In this case, lakśmaṇa sliced her ears and nose, even as sūrpaṇakhā was looking at śrī rāma’s divine form, fulfilling her desire to imbibe his looks fully. Later, while recounting this incident to her brothers kara and dūśaṇa, she said, as in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 19.14 “*taruṇau rūpa sampannau…*” (They are youthful and good-looking). Regarding lakśmaṇa acting as the implement for śrī rāma, while disfiguring her, this is fortified by the ślōkam in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 34.14 “*rāmasya dakśinōbāhu*:” (lakśmaṇa is the right hand of śrī rāma). tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that this is not to be considered as *sāmādikaraṇyam* but as *sāyujyam* \[*sāmādikaraṇyam* is one where the substrate is one, displaying different qualities, while *sāyujya* refers to two different entities, united with each other\].

He says at the end, the following: The physical form will not distinguish aspects such as knowledge, power etc among those who have taken *aprākruta* forms \[*aprākrutam* refers to one which is different from the five elements seen in the universe, viz. sky, wind, fire, water and earth. Any entity seen in śrī vaikuṇṭam is *aprākrutam* while any entity seen anywhere else, including brahma lōkam \[abode of brahmā\], rudra lōkam \[abode of Siva\] etc is *prākrutam*\]. In other words, their knowledge, power etc will always shine and nothing can hide them. It is only with *prākruta* forms, that differences will be seen \[since the *prākruta* form hides the knowledge of the entity, from knowing about emperumān\]. When differences are seen, at the time of getting a task done, when emperumān has to impel someone to carry out the task, *sāmānādikaraṇyam* will be seen. Otherwise, it is only *vaiyadikaraṇyam* which will be seen \[for example, when śrī rāma desires to slice the ears and nose of sūrppaṇakhā, he will act through lakśmaṇa, treating lakśmaṇa as an implement of himself. However, when lakśmaṇa carries out a task towards fulfilling his nature of a servitor to emperumān, such as building a hermitage etc, he will be a separate entity carrying out the task. This is termed as *vaiyadikaraṇyam*\].

**ayōddi …** – Since śrī bharatāḻvān did not wear the crown, and since śrī rāma had given his divine sandals to śrī bharatāḻvān \[as his representative\], it is śrī rāma, who is considered as the king of ayōdyā. The girl, who sings this pāsuram, implores her competitor to sing about such śrī rāma.

We shall next consider the 9<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.9.9. Mayac cagadam

*māyac cagadam udaittu marudu iṟuttuāyargaḷōdu pōy ānirai kāttuvēyinkuḻal ūdi vittaganāy ninṟaāyargaḷ ēṟṟinaip pādippaṟa ānirai mēyttānaip pādippaṟa*

**Пословный перевод:**

māyam – having deception; sagadam – śakatāsuran; udaittu – kicking with his divine feet such that it \[wheel, pervaded by śakatāsuran\] was blown to pieces; marudu – twin trees of yamaḷārjuna; iṟuttu – snapping them; āyargaḷōdu – along with herd-boys; pōy – going to the forest; A nirai – herds of cows; kāttu – protecting them; aṇi – beautiful; vēyin kuḻal – flute, made of bamboo; ūdi – blowing it; vittaganāy ninṟa – one who stood as an amazing entity; āyargaḷ ēṟṟinai – sing about the one, who is the leader of herd-people; ānirai mēyttānaip pādippaṟa – sing about the one, who grazed the cows and became joyful

**Перевод:**

**When kriṣṇa was an infant, a monster, śakatan, had pervaded a wheel. When he came towards kriṣṇa \[as the wheel\], with the intention of killing kriṣṇa, he got caught between the kicking, divine legs of kriṣṇa and was blown to smithereens. Later, when he was a toddler, kriṣṇa was tied down to a mortar by yaśōdāp pirātti. He went crawling with the mortar and snapped two yamaḷārjuna trees. When he had grown up further, he went along with the herd-boys, grazing cows and protecting them. Sing about such kriṣṇa, who is the leader of herd-folk. Sing about kriṣṇa, who grazed cows and became happy, due to that.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**māyac cagadam udaittu** – just as it has been mentioned in [tiruppāvai 6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2014/12/thiruppavai-06-pullum-silambina-kan/) “*kaḷḷac cagadam kalakkaḻiyak kālōcci*” (lifting his divine feet such that the deceptive wheel was blown to pieces), the wheel was kept as a guard for kriṣṇa, by yaśōdāp pirātti \[when she went to look after her chores\]. Demons pervaded the wheel and came running towards him with the intention of harming him; though it appeared to be a harmless wheel, with the monsters pervading it, it appeared deceitful. kriṣṇa was feeling hungry and when yaśōdāp pirātti had not come to nurse him, he started kicking his feet. The wheel got caught between his divine feet and was blown to smithereens.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that the monsters came in disguise, being sent by kamsan to harm kriṣṇa. They were annihilated by kriṣṇa.

**marudu iṟuttu** – when he started crawling, pulling the mortar, to which his mother had tied him, he went between two *maruda* trees, which were standing there, to harm him. He went past, between the two trees, but the mortar got caught between them. When he pulled the mortar towards him, it hit the trees such that they got snapped and fell on either side \[demons had pervaded these two trees too, with the intention of killing him\].

**āyargaḷōdu pōy ānirai kāttu** – when going along with the herd-boys for grazing cattle, he went as the primary person among them, scouting for grass and water, such that the cows were able to graze, eating till their stomachs were full. Thus, he protected the cattle.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says that kriṣṇa would choose forests where wild animals such as tigers etc were not present. He would not enter towns where no grazing land was available. He will choose places which had grazing land and water, and play on his beautiful flute to get the cows to assemble together.

**aṇivēyin kuḻal ūdi vittaganāy ninṟa** – unlike the cows seen in the land which nurture on grass and water, the cows from tiruvāyppādi nurture themselves primarily on the sound from kriṣṇa’s flute. He would play the flute for a variety of purposes, such as taking them \[cows and calves\] out in the morning for grazing, ensuring that they do not go astray, calling them back to assemble together, before returning to tiruvāyppādi etc. He stood, with his capability manifested, clearly.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa was the main person among the herd-boys; he was highly capable.

**āyargaḷ ēṟṟinai** – one who has the pride of being the leader of herd-folk

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that kriṣṇa had the eminence of carrying out tasks for the herd-folks before they even told them.

**pādippaṟa** – sing about such kriṣṇa.

**ānirai mēyttānai** – just as it has been said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/11/thiruvaimozhi-10-3-10-avaththangal-vilaiyum/) “*tivattilum pasunirai mēyppu uvatti*” (emperumān is more joyful in grazing cows than being in paramapadam), kriṣṇa is one who enjoys going behind cows and grazing them than being in śrī vaikuṇṭam.

**pādippaṟa** – the girl, who sings this pāsuram, tells her competitor to sing about such kriṣṇa.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the girl tells her competitor to sing about the one who grazed cattle like this, playing on the flute.

We shall next consider the 10<sup>th</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan

## 3.9.10. Karar kadalai

*kārār kadalai adaittittu ilangai pukkuōrādān pon mudi onbadōdu onṟaiyumnērā avan tambikkē neeḷ arasu īndaārāvamudanaip pādippaṟa ayōddiyar vēndanaip pādippaṟa*

**Пословный перевод:**

kār Ar – being very dark, due to its depth; kadalai – ocean; adaittittu – blocking, with the aid of mountains; ilangai pukku – entered lankā; ōrādān – rāvaṇan, who did not revere perumāḷ’s valour; ponmudi onbadōdu onṟaiyum – the ten beautiful heads, which had been decorated with golden crowns; nērā – severed them; avan tambikkē – to vibhīśaṇa, his \[rāvaṇa’s\] younger brother; neeḷ – to hold for a long time; arasu – kingdom; īnda – one, who gave; ārā – insatiable, despite enjoying for a very long time; amudanai – sing about the one who is the most enjoyable, like nectar; ayōddiyar vēndanai – sing about the one, who is the king for those in ayōdyā

**Перевод:**

**śrī rāma entered lankā, after blocking the ocean, which was dark in colour due to its depth. He severed the ten beautiful heads of rāvaṇa, who had not respected his valour and gave the kingdom to rāvaṇa’s younger brother, vibhīśaṇa, such that he could rule over for a very long time. Sing about the one, who is the most enjoyable, like nectar, and who does not give satisfaction even after enjoying for a very long time. Sing about the one, who is the king for the people in ayōdyā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*There is no specific avatārikai for this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**kārār kadalai adaittittu** – Ocean looks dark owing to its depth. When stones are dropped in the ocean, they will sink to the ocean-bed. However, due to his *aghatitaghatanā sāmartyam* \[ability to bind together entities which cannot ever be bound\], śrī rāma blocked the ocean, with the help of monkeys, by dropping mountains and boulders in the ocean.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that śrī rāma quickly blocked the ocean, which was dark due to its depth, got to the other side of the ocean, mercifully entering the northern side of lankā, ready to carry out battle. When rāvaṇa, thinking of himself as the king of demons, as mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 4.4.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/03/periya-thirumozhi-4-4-6/) “*arakkar tangaḷ kōn pōlum*” (that he is the king of all demons), with the itching in his shoulders to go for battle, believing “Am I not the king of all the demons!” went out to battle, śrī rāma severed his mother head, along with the other nine heads simultaneously.

**ilangai pukku** – just as it has been mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 1-39 “*lankām rāvaṇa pālitām*” (regarding lankā, which is ruled by rāvaṇa), the land of lankā was such that it is difficult to enter the place for anyone. Moreover, owing to the strength of one, who is ruling it from inside, it is almost impossible to enter the place. śrī rāma entered that lankā, along with his army of about seventy thousand monkeys.

**ōrādān ponmudi onbadōdu onṟaiyum nērā** – Despite seeing such a super-human effort on the part of śrī rāma \[in entering such a fortified lankā\], rāvaṇa did not consider śrī rāma’s strength. He believed the strength of his boons and his shoulder. He did not respect the strength of śrī rāma, which was as mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 4.4.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/03/periya-thirumozhi-4-4-6/) “*tān pōlum enṟu eḻundān daraṇiyāḷan*” (cakravartit tirumagan, who is the emperor of earth, arose, like a king, opposing), in a very superficial manner. rāvaṇa had decorated his beautiful heads with golden crowns. He had a boon by which, if a head is severed, it will reappear. As śrī rāma severed each head, it reappeared. Just as it has been mentioned in [periya tirumoḻi 2.4.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/09/periya-thirumozhi-2-4-5/) “*kālam idu enṟu ayan vāḷiyināl kadirnīṇmudi pattum aṟuttamarum*” (determining that this is the correct time, śrī rāma, who is to sit on the throne in ayōdyā, severed the ten splendorous heads of rāvaṇa, with brahmāstram \[a potent weapon\]), śrī rāma determined that “This is the time to annihilate him”, severed all the ten heads at the same time, with brahmāstram.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that *ōrāmai* (inability to accept) is śrī rāma killing vāli, then building a bridge across the ocean and setting lankā to fire \[through hanuman\].

**avan tambikkē neeḷ arasu īnda** – when vibhīśaṇāḻvān came to surrender to śrī rāma, he introduced himself, as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 19.42 “*anujōr rāvaṇasya aham*” (I was born after rāvaṇa), to indicate his low birth, and took refuge under the divine feet of śrī rāma. śrī rāma gave the kingdom \[of lankā\] to that vibhīśaṇa and told him, as mentioned in [periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2.6.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2026/01/periyazhwar-thirumozhi-2-6-9/) “*ennilangu nāmattaḷavum arasu*” (This kingdom will be yours until my resplendent name remains), giving him the wealth of the kingdom of lankā.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the term *avan tambikkē* refers to vibhīśaṇa being the younger brother of rāvaṇa. Earlier, sūrpaṇakhā had said that vibhīśaṇa does not possess the qualities of a demon \[since he was honest, righteous etc\]. Later, when śrī rāma asks vibhīśaṇa about the strength of the army in lankā, he tells him, as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 19.7 “*rākhasānām balābalam*” (tell me the strength and weakness of the demons) \[here, he is not asking him about “Your strength and weakness” but that of the demons; in other words, he does not consider vibhīśaṇa as a demon at all\]. He has all along considered vibhīśaṇa as his brother. However, after the death of rāvaṇa, he told vibhīśaṇa, as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 112.26 “*kriyatāmasya samskārō mamāpyēśatā tava*” (you should carry out the last rites for this rāvaṇa since I have the same relationship with him as you have\]. The reason for saying this is that he had already decided in his divine mind that he will hand over the kingdom to \[rāvaṇa’s\] brother, vibhīśaṇa, though vibhīśaṇa had come to him only for carrying out service to him as his *puruśārtam* \[ultimate benefit\]. Alternatively, it could be said that āḻvār had mercifully thought that when the demons come under the control of śrī rāma \[sine he had conquered lankā\], śrī rāma wanted to have a connection, hence he made vibhīśaṇa as the king, succeeding rāvaṇa. Also, it is difficult to get rid of the qualities of a demon. Unlike lakśmaṇa, who said that he will not leave śrī rāma and that he would carry out all the servitude to him, even when śrī rāma had told him to remain in ayōdyā, vibhīśaṇa followed the words of śrī rāma. Hence, āḻvār addresses vibhīśaṇa as the younger brother of śrī rāma.

Further, śrī rāma told vibhīśaṇa that he could remain the king of lankā until his divine name remains. Earlier too \[during the time of rāvaṇa\], the sounds of vēdams and rituals such as agnihōtram were heard in every house of demons, with the divine name of viṣṇu being recited. However, compassion, truth, sacredness etc were unknown to the demons. Now, śrī rāma says that vibhīśaṇa could remain as the king until śrī rāma’s divine name remains, signifying that his divine name is more splendorous that that of viṣṇu.

**ārāvamudanai** – sing about the one, who, through this quality, creates more and more involvement with him to enjoy him like nectar, and who is such that even after enjoying him for a long time, the person is insatiable.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that after the annihilation of rāvaṇa, a splendour was seen on the divine form of śrī rāma, since he had removed an inimical entity. āḻvār, carrying out mangaḷāśāsanam for this, calls him as *ārāvamudu*, the insatiable entity. Just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.6.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-6-5-kolgai-kolamai/) “*viḷgai viḷḷāmai virumbi uḷ kalandārkku ōr amudē*” (emperumān is the distinct nectar who approach him with the intention of serving only him, unlike those who come to him with a prayer and leave after getting what they had asked for), he is a unique *amudam*. He is every moment, *ārāvamudan*, as mentioned in the saying *dārāvāhika vijñānam* \[like a stream of oil flows without any disturbance, from one knowledge to another\]; emperumān is enjoyable, without one getting satiated. After comparing with a metaphor, *amudam*, nectar, āḻvār feels that it is nowhere near his nectar \[his nectar is śrī rāma\]. Hence, he mercifully calls his refuge as the nectar.

**ayōddiyar vēndanai** – after annihilating rāvaṇa, śrī rāma returned to ayōdyā and crowned himself as the king of ayōdyā. Sing about one, who thus became the king of ayōdyā.

**pādippaṟa** – the girl, who sings this pāsuram, tells her competitor to sing about him.

We shall next consider the last pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

## 3.9.11. Nandan madalaiyai

*nandan madalaiyaik kāguttanai navinṟuundi paṟanda oḷi iḻaiyārgaḷ solsendamiḻ ten puduvai vittucittan solaindinōdu aindum vallārkku allal illaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nandan madalaiyai – kaṇṇan \[kriṣṇa\], the son of nandagōpan; kāguttanai – the divine son of cakravarti, who is from the clan of emperor kakutsta; navinṟu – singing about them, as those from opposing sides; undi paṟanda – celebrating the flavour of undi paṟattal (this is a game played by tamiḻ women); oḷi – beautiful; iḻaiyārgaḷ – women, who have decorated themselves with ornaments, their; sol – words; sem – being honest; tamiḻ – in the tamiḻ language; then – beautiful; puduvai – controller of śrī villibuttūr; vittucittan – periyāḻvār; sol – mercifully composed; aindinōdu aindum – ten pāsurams, composed of five pāsurams regarding kriṣṇāvatāram and five pāsurams regarding śrī rāmāvatāram; vallārkku – for those who are capable of reciting; allal illai – there is no distress

**Перевод:**

**Women, who have decorated themselves with ornaments, have sung about kaṇṇan, the son of nandagōpan, and śrī rāma, who is the son of emperor daśarata, from the clan of emperor kakutsta, keeping them as opponents, in the style of undi paṟattal. periyāḻvār, who is the controller of beautiful śrī villibuttūr, has mercifully composed their words in the honest tamiḻ language. For those who are capable of reciting these ten pāsurams, composed of five pāsurams regarding kriṣṇāvatāram and five pāsurams regarding śrī rāmāvatāram, there is no distress.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*āḻvār mentions the benefit which those who recite this decad will get and brings the decad to its end.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**nandan madalayaik kākuttanai navinṟu** – keeping the divine son of śrī nandagōpar and the divine son of emperor \[daśarata\], who came in the clan of emperor kakutsta.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that women of tiruvāyppādi divided themselves into two groups, and played the game of *undi paṟattal*, sang alternately, with the quality of simplicity coming to the fore in the incarnation of kriṣṇa and the qualities of eminence as well as simplicity coming to the fore in the incarnation of śrī rāma.

**undi paṟanda oḷi iḻaiyārgaḷ sol** – the words of women who had decorated themselves with beautiful ornaments, celebrating the flavour of the game of *undi paṟattal*.

**sendamiḻ tenpudvai vittucittan sol** – mercifully composed by periyāḻvār, the controller of śrī villibuttūr, in the honest tamiḻ language.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that periyāḻvār, the controller of śrī villibuttūr, has carried out eminent servitude through tiruppallāṇḍu \[wishing emperumān well\], in the honest language of tamiḻ.

**aindinōdu aindum vallārkku** – for those who are capable of reciting these ten pāsurams, consisting of five pāsurams regarding kriṣṇāvatāram and five pāsurams regarding śrī rāmāvatāram

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that though the pāsurams appear to be of two kinds, due to the reason of *darmi aikkyam* (both śrī rāma and kriṣṇa are incarnations of the same śrīman nārāyaṇa), both appear of one type. For those who are capable of reciting these ten pāsurams, with the pathos of periyāḻvār, due to the mercy of periyāḻvār, the distress of living in samsāram, which arises due to *sankalpam* \[vow, of both emperumān, who creates samsāram for his play, and jīvātmās, who indulge in deeds of their volition\] will not come. *allal* – multitude of deceptive play in samsāram, which is composed of both happiness and sorrow, through which emperumān enjoys.

**allal illaiyē** – there is no distress arising out of samsāram \[materialistic world, this earth\].

We shall next consider the pravēśam of the next tirumoḻi.

## 3.10.1. Nerinda karum

*neṟinda karum kuḻal madavāy nin adiyēn viṇṇappamseṟinda maṇi mudiccanagan silai iṟuttu ninaik koṇarndaaṟindu arasu kaḷai katta arundavattōn idai vilangacceṟinda silai kodu tavattaic cidaittadum ōr adaiyāḷam*

**Пословный перевод:**

neṟinda – being dense; karu – being black; kuḻal – having locks; madavāy – Oh, pirātti, who is quivering, due to separation from perumāḷ!; nin – to your highness; adiyēm – my, the servitor’s; viṇṇappam – appeal is; seṟinda – tightly packed; maṇi – embedded with the nine gemstones; mudi – donning the crown; sanagan – king janaka; silai – bow, which was kept as the wager for marriage; iṟuttu – snapping; ninai – your highness; koṇarndadu – that he \[perumāḷ\] was taking, after marriage; aṟindu – after knowing; arasu – twenty-one generations of wicked kings; kaḷai katta – as one, who de-weeded; aru – impossible to perform for anyone; tavattōn – paraśurāman, who carried out penance; idai – in the middle; vilanga – as he stopped; seṟinda – apt, to remove his vanity; silai kodu – with the bow; tavattai – his penance; sidaittadum – removing it; ōr adiyāḷam – is an indication (for your highness to know this servitor, who is a servitor of perumāḷ)

**Перевод:**

**Oh, pirātti, who has dense, black locks and who is quivering on account of separation from perumāḷ! Please listen to the appeal of this servitor. śrī rāma had snapped the bow, which king janaka, who dons a crown studded with densely packed nine gems, had kept as a wager for marrying your highness. After hearing this, paraśurāma, who had weeded out twenty-one generations of wicked kings and who has strength of penance, which is impossible for anyone to carry out, stopped śrī rāma, in the middle of his journey \[to ayōdyā\]. Taking the bow, which was apt for ridding that paraśurāma of his vanity, śrī rāma removed the power of paraśurāma’s penance. This is one of the indications for you to believe this servitor, who is a servitor of that śrī rāma.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says, in his svāpadēśam, that āḻvār mentions about the first incident in this pāsuram.*

**vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

**neṟinda kuḻal madavāy** – Oh, one who as dense, dark locks and who is quivering on account of separation from perumāḷ! The eminence for locks is that they should be curled and soft, unlike elephant grass, which is stiff and straight, and that the locks should be dark until the end \[which, usually is below the waist\]. This describes the locks of pirātti, as they were in the past. At the moment, her locks appear, as mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam, sundara kāṇḍam 15.25 “*neela nāga ābhayā vēṇyā jaghanam gatayaikayā*” (with the radiance of a single, black serpent, reaching the hinder part), with a single plait, reaching her back. While she had the right to be together with her consort, perumāḷ, and feel proud, since she had been separated from him, due to her sorrow, she is now quivering. hanuman, looking at this, calls her as *madavāy*. Alternatively, *madappam* \[the root word for *madavāy*\] would also refer to not letting go of that which has been grasped. In pirātti’s case, while she is here \[in aśōka vanam, a long distance\] away from emperumān, as mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 15.52 “*asya dēvyāmanas tasmin*” \[the divine mind of sītāp pirātti is engaging only with śrī rāma pirān\], she is continuing to think of only śrī rāma and her mind is not involving in anything else.

**nin adiyēn viṇṇappam** – since hanuman is a servitor of śrī rāma, as mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 42.35 “*dāsō’ham kōsalēndrasya*” (I am the servitor of śrī rāma, the king of kōsala dēśam), as soon as he became the servitor of śrī rāma, he became the servitor of sītāp pirātti too; to emphasise this, he says of himself as the servitor of sītāp pirātti. Through this, it is implied that your highness \[addressing pirātti\] should listen to the appeal of this servitor.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that when one says a word, one has to stand at a lower level and say it. śrī rāma himself had told sage viśvāmitra, after the annihilation of tātakā and subāhu that he, along with lakśmaṇa, are the sage’s servitors and that he \[the sage\] could order them to carry out any activity, which they will do willingly. Later, while introducing śrī rāma to hanuman, lakśmaṇa had told him, as in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 4-18 “*sugrīvam nātam iccati*” (śrī rāma is willing to accept sugrīva as his lord) that śrī rāma will accept sugrīva as his lord. Just as tirumangai āḻvār had said in [periya tirumoḻi 2.2.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/08/periya-thirumozhi-2-2-3/) “*innār tūdan*” (kriṣṇa said proudly that he is the messenger of pāṇḍavas), hanuman said that he is the servitor to make sītāp pirātti to believe him firmly.

**seṟinda maṇi mudic canagan silai iṟuttu** – king janaka had a crown, embellished with gemstones, which were closely placed. He had kept a bow as a wager for anyone to draw it and tie the cord, in order to marry his daughter, sītāp pirātti. While there was none in the world, even to draw the bow, as soon as śrī rāma took it and drew it, even before he could tie the cord, being unable to sustain the power of his divine hand, the bow broke into two pieces.

**ninaik koṇarndadu aṟindu** – looking at the valour of śrī rāma, king janaka said, as mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 73.24 “*iyam sītā mama sutā sahadarmacarītava* l *pratīccainām bhadrantē pāṇim gruhṇīśva pāṇinā*” (This sītā, is my daughter. She is apt to be with you when you engage with righteous activities. Accept her. Let auspicious events happen to you. Hold her hand, with your hand) told śrī rāma to hold her hand. Hearing the information about śrī rāma marrying you …

**arasu kaḷai katta arundavattōn idai vilanga** – paraśurāma had weeded out wicked kings for twenty-one generations and he had carried out penance which none could carry out. While śrī rāma was proceeding, after his marriage, to ayōdyā, paraśurāma stopped him, on the way and told him “Check the strength of my bow and then proceed”. The term *vilanga* is a transformation of *vilakka* – to stop.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that paraśurāma spoke a few words, which crossed the limit \[of forbearance\] to śrī rāma \[while asking śrī rāma to prove his ability by drawing the bow, which was with paraśurāma\]. When paraśurāma tried to prevent śrī rāma from proceeding further, just as it has been said in [bhagavat gītā 16.19](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/16-19/) “*kśipāmi*” (I push them into low births), śrī rāma removed the power of paraśūrāma’s penance, thus making him unable to enjoy that power. *kaḷai katta* would also refer to killing.

**seṟinda …** – while it was a bow taken from the hands of paraśurāma, the bow fitted better, on the divine hands of śrī rāma, it being the bow of viṣṇu. With that bow, śrī rāma removed the strength of paraśurāma’s penance. Instead of saying “*tavattaic cidahittadu adaiyāḷam*” (removing the penance was identification), since hanuman said “*tavattaic cidaittadum ōr adiyāḷam*” (removing the penance was *an* identification), it appears that hanuman has decided to point out to several other identifications for pirātti to believe in him. He has to keep saying until her doubt is removed.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says here that the bow was very distinguished in the retinue of emperumān’s divine weapons, as mentioned in [tiruppallāṇḍu 12](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/11/thiruppallandu-12-pallandu-enru/) “*śārngamennum villāṇḍān*” (emperumān, who controls the divine bow, śrī śārngam). This is one of the identifications \[for sītāp pirātti to believe that hanuman is indeed śrī rāma’s servitor\]. Just as kriṣṇa kept telling arjuna “*mā suca*:” \[do not grieve\] until arjuna stopped grieving, hanuman too has to repeatedly point out to various identifications, until sītāp pirātti’s doubt was cleared.

tiruvāimoḻip piḷḷai says at the end that when *svarūpāvēśam* \[emperumān entering a jīvātmā , giving his powers to that jīvātmā\] meets the most distinguished emperumān, it cannot stand upright before emperumān. Once the purpose of that *āvēśam* has been completed, emperumān himself removes the results of the penance of that jīvātmā, making that jīvātmā to experience the results of past deeds \[since the base is a jīvātmā, in which emperumān has pervaded with his powers, once the purpose for which he had pervaded has been accomplished, the jīvātmā has to spend the remaining years, experiencing the results of its past deeds\]. emperumān also manifests the eminence for the *svarūpāvēśam* \[in this case, standing against emperumān himself\]. The difference between the most distinguished emperumān and the ordinary *svarūpāvēśam* will be clearly known only if it is demonstrated through an activity, as in this case.

We shall next consider the 2<sup>nd</sup> pāsuram of this tirumoḻi.

adiyēn kriṣṇa rāmānuja dāsan
